recs.facts: 100 minutes ÷ 20 km = 5 minutes per km.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 4 times older than him. How old is his sister?
recs.facts: 4 × 4 = 16 years.

recs.q: Ahmed is 10 years old and his brother is 5. What will his brother's age be after 3 years?
recs.facts: 5 + 3 = 8 years.

recs.q: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ?
recs.facts: Gaps increase by 1: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6 (O → U).

recs.q: Find the next number: 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
recs.facts: Differences double: +4, +8, +16, then +32 → 65.

recs.q: Find the next number: 66, 63, 57, 45, ?
recs.facts: Differences: −3, −6, −12, then −24 → 21.

recs.q: Complete the series: A, C, E, ?
recs.facts: Every alternate letter: A, C, E, G.
Letters move back by 2 (z, x, v, t, r) and numbers go up by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11).

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th?
recs.facts: 24 − 4 = 20 days; 20 mod 7 = 6 → Monday + 6 = Sunday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 12th?
recs.facts: 12 − 4 = 8 days; 8 mod 7 = 1 → Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday.

recs.q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 4th?
recs.facts: 14 − 4 = 10 days back; 10 mod 7 = 3 → Sunday − 3 = Thursday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th?
recs.facts: 12 − 2 = 10; 10 mod 7 = 3 → Monday + 3 = Thursday.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 27th?
recs.facts: 27 − 3 = 24; 24 mod 7 = 3 → Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

recs.q: Today is Monday. What day will it be 15 days later?
recs.facts: 15 mod 7 = 1 → Monday + 1 = Tuesday.

recs.q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: Today = Saturday; tomorrow = Sunday; day after tomorrow = Monday.

recs.q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you?
recs.facts: My brother's sister is my sister; she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother — your maternal uncle.

recs.q: A man walks north, then turns left, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing?
recs.facts: North → left = West → right = North again.

recs.q: Ali is shorter than Bilal. Umer is taller than Ali but shorter than Bilal. Who is the tallest?
recs.facts: Ali < Umer < Bilal, so Bilal is tallest.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Lahore, Rawalpindi, Karachi, Quetta
recs.facts: Lahore, Karachi and Quetta are provincial capitals; Rawalpindi is not.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda
recs.facts: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Circle, Angle
recs.facts: The others are shapes; an angle is not a closed shape.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: January, March, Friday, November
recs.facts: All others are months; Friday is a day.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Axe, Sword, Dagger, Fork, Knife
recs.facts: Axe, sword, dagger (and knife) are weapons/cutting arms; a fork is a table utensil.

recs.q: Hospital is to patient as school is to:
recs.facts: A hospital serves patients; a school serves students.

recs.q: Ink is to pen as blood is to:
recs.facts: Ink flows in a pen; blood flows in veins.

recs.q: Bird is to nest as human is to:
recs.facts: A nest is a bird's home; a house is a human's home.

recs.q: Brain is to think as heart is to:
recs.facts: The brain's function is thinking; the heart's function is pumping blood.

recs.q: Flower is to fragrance as food is to:
recs.facts: A flower is known for fragrance; food for taste.

recs.q: Carpenter is to wood as mason is to:
recs.facts: A carpenter works with wood; a mason works with bricks/stone.

recs.q: Arrange the letters of BEAUTY alphabetically. Which letter comes last?
recs.facts: Alphabetical order: A, B, E, T, U, Y → last is Y.

recs.q: Rearrange PARDLEO to make an animal.
recs.facts: PARDLEO → LEOPARD.

recs.q: Rearrange NMERGAY to form the name of a country.
recs.facts: NMERGAY → GERMANY.

recs.q: Arrange the letters of MANAGEMENT alphabetically. Which is the 3rd letter?
recs.facts: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T → 3rd letter is E (3rd last letter of the word is also E).

recs.q: Which word remains the same when reflected in a mirror (vertical mirror)?
recs.facts: T, W and M are symmetrical about the vertical axis; S, R and Q are not.

recs.q: Snake cannot hear and bat cannot ___?
recs.facts: Test answer: bats are (said to be) unable to see and use echoes; snakes cannot hear airborne sound.

recs.q: Why do we boil milk?
recs.facts: Boiling kills harmful bacteria and germs.

recs.q: Why do parents send their children to school?
recs.facts: School educates and grooms children for life.

recs.q: Antonym of WILD:
recs.facts: Wild means untamed; its opposite is tame.

recs.q: Antonym of PRECIOUS:
recs.facts: Precious = of great value; opposite = worthless.

recs.q: Synonym of TURBULENT:
recs.facts: Turbulent means violent, unsteady or stormy.

recs.q: Word closest in meaning to SELFLESS:
recs.facts: A selfless person thinks of others first — altruistic.

recs.q: Word closest in meaning to LUCID:
recs.facts: Lucid means clear and easy to understand.

recs.q: Word closest in meaning to EXCUSE:
recs.facts: An excuse is a reason offered to defend a fault — a pretext.

recs.q: 'To throw cold water on' something means:
recs.facts: The idiom means to dampen enthusiasm or discourage.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: You should call ___ your teacher.
recs.facts: 'Call on' someone means to visit them.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He complained ___ the manager about the noise.
recs.facts: We complain TO a person (and ABOUT a thing).

recs.q: Fill in the blank: I congratulate you ___ your success.
recs.facts: The correct collocation is 'congratulate (someone) on'.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: 'She writes a letter.'
opts: She is written by a letter.
A letter is written by her.
A letter was written by her.
recs.facts: Simple present passive: is/am/are + past participle.

recs.q: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am happy."
opts: He said that he is happy.
He said that he was happy.
He said that I am happy.
recs.facts: In reported speech, 'am' shifts to 'was' and 'I' to 'he'.

recs.q: Antonym of BRAVE:
recs.facts: Brave = courageous; opposite = cowardly.

recs.q: Synonym of RAPID:
recs.facts: Rapid means quick or fast.

recs.q: Antonym of ANCIENT:
recs.facts: Ancient = very old; opposite = modern.

recs.q: Synonym of COMMENCE:
recs.facts: Commence means to start or begin.

recs.q: Antonym of EXPAND:
recs.facts: Expand = become larger; contract = become smaller.

recs.q: Antonym of VICTORY:
recs.facts: Victory means winning; its opposite is defeat.

recs.q: Antonym of HONEST:
recs.facts: Honest = truthful; opposite = dishonest.

recs.q: Synonym of HUGE:
recs.facts: Huge and enormous both mean very large.

recs.q: Plural of CHILD:
recs.facts: Child has an irregular plural: children.

recs.q: Choose the correct sentence:
recs.facts: 'Senior', 'junior', 'superior', 'inferior' take 'to', not 'than'.

recs.q: Antonym of GENEROUS:
recs.facts: Generous = giving freely; opposite = stingy.

recs.q: Synonym of DILIGENT:
recs.facts: Diligent means hardworking.

recs.q: In which year did the Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
recs.facts: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

recs.q: Who was the first Governor General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Jinnah took oath as the first Governor General on 15 August 1947.

recs.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Justice Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice (Federal Court) in 1948.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
recs.facts: The SCO Secretariat is in Beijing.

recs.q: What is the length of Pakistan's coastline?
recs.facts: Pakistan's coastline is about 1,046 km (Sindh ≈ 270 km, Balochistan ≈ 770 km).

recs.q: In which direction is Afghanistan from Pakistan?
recs.facts: Afghanistan lies to Pakistan's west and north-west.

recs.q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution gives the right to education?
recs.facts: Article 25-A guarantees free and compulsory education for ages 5–16.

recs.q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution deals with freedom of speech?
recs.facts: Article 19 guarantees freedom of speech; 19-A gives the right to information.

recs.q: Article 19-A of the 1973 Constitution guarantees:
recs.facts: 19-A (18th Amendment, 2010) gives citizens the right to information.

recs.q: Under the 1973 Constitution, who is the head of state?
recs.facts: The President is the head of state; the Prime Minister heads the government.

recs.q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), which rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
recs.facts: The three western rivers went to Pakistan; the three eastern rivers to India.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan join the United Nations?
recs.facts: Pakistan became a UN member on 30 September 1947.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan join SAARC?
recs.facts: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in December 1985 with Pakistan as a founding member.

recs.q: In which year was the OIC founded?
recs.facts: The OIC was founded in Rabat in 1969 after the Al-Aqsa arson.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan after Liaquat Ali Khan?
recs.facts: Nazimuddin served as the 2nd Prime Minister (1951–53).

recs.q: The Lucknow Pact between Congress and Muslim League was signed in:
recs.facts: The Lucknow Pact (1916) accepted separate electorates for Muslims.

recs.q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place?
recs.facts: Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement after the 1922 incident.

recs.q: Pakistan's first direct general elections were held in:
recs.facts: The first general elections on the basis of adult franchise were in December 1970.

recs.q: The Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms were introduced in:
recs.facts: The Government of India Act 1919 was based on these reforms.

recs.q: 'Jinnah of Pakistan' was written by:
recs.facts: Stanley Wolpert authored 'Jinnah of Pakistan' (1984).

recs.q: The Karakoram Highway is also known as:
recs.facts: KKH (N-35) links Pakistan and China via the Khunjerab Pass.

recs.q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with:
recs.facts: Khunjerab Pass (4,693 m) is the Pakistan–China border crossing.

recs.q: CPEC is a project of which country in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The China–Pakistan Economic Corridor is a Chinese Belt and Road project.

recs.q: How many Nobel Prizes has Pakistan won (Malala Yousafzai and Dr Abdus Salam)?
recs.facts: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).

recs.q: Hafeez Kardar was a famous Pakistani ___ player.
recs.facts: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was Pakistan's first Test captain.

recs.q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan won in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.

recs.q: The city of flowers (Phulon ka Shehar) is:
recs.facts: Peshawar is known as the City of Flowers.

recs.q: Which city is known as the 'Manchester of Pakistan'?
recs.facts: Faisalabad is the textile hub, hence the nickname.

recs.q: Which city is called the 'Heart of Pakistan'?
recs.facts: Lahore is commonly called the cultural 'heart' of Pakistan.

recs.q: What was the old name of Karachi?
recs.facts: Karachi grew from the fishing village of Kolachi.

recs.q: Which was the old (first) capital of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Karachi was capital from 1947 until Rawalpindi/Islamabad.

recs.q: Which is the largest dam of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Tarbela on the Indus is the largest earth-filled dam.

recs.q: On which river is the Tarbela Dam located?
recs.facts: Tarbela is built on the River Indus.

recs.q: On which river is the Baglihar Dam built?
recs.facts: Baglihar (Indian-held Kashmir) is on the Chenab.

recs.q: Which is the largest river of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Indus (≈ 2,900 km) is the longest river of Pakistan.

recs.q: In which year did Swat join Pakistan?
recs.facts: The princely state of Swat was merged into Pakistan in 1969.

recs.q: What was the percentage of East Pakistan's population when One Unit was formed (1955)?
recs.facts: East Pakistan had about 56% of the total population (1951 census).

recs.q: Who mediated the Tashkent Agreement (1966)?
recs.facts: The Soviet Premier Kosygin hosted and mediated it.

recs.q: The Tashkent Agreement (1966) was signed between:
recs.facts: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it after the 1965 war.

recs.q: Who presented the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution in 1940?
recs.facts: Fazlul Haq (Sher-e-Bangal) moved the resolution on 23 March 1940.

recs.q: Who presented the Objectives Resolution in 1949?
recs.facts: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved it in the Constituent Assembly (March 1949).

recs.q: Who authored 'Now or Never' (1933)?
recs.facts: The pamphlet coined the name 'Pakistan'.

recs.q: In which year was the Simla Conference held?
recs.facts: Lord Wavell called the Simla Conference in June–July 1945.

recs.q: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
recs.facts: Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757.

recs.q: The 'Kargil War' between Pakistan and India took place in:
recs.facts: The Kargil conflict took place in 1999.

recs.q: East Pakistan separated from Pakistan in:
recs.facts: Bangladesh emerged on 16 December 1971.

recs.q: In which year did the Quaid-e-Azam join the Indian National Congress?
recs.facts: Jinnah joined the Congress in 1906 (and the Muslim League in 1913).

recs.q: Who made the 1973 Constitution (Prime Minister at the time)?
recs.facts: Under PM Z. A. Bhutto, the National Assembly adopted it unanimously.

recs.q: The Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa were written by:
recs.facts: They are well-known poems by Allama Iqbal.

recs.q: 'Umar Marvi' is a famous folk story of which province?
recs.facts: Marvi is a heroine in Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai's Sindhi poetry.

recs.q: What is the height of K2, Pakistan's highest peak?
recs.facts: K2 is 8,611 m — the 2nd highest peak in the world.

recs.q: What is the height of Tirich Mir?
recs.facts: Tirich Mir (Hindu Kush) is 7,708 m — the highest peak outside the Karakoram–Himalaya.

recs.q: Babusar Pass connects Chilas with:
recs.facts: Babusar Pass (4,173 m) links Kaghan Valley with Chilas.

recs.q: What percentage of the Senate members retire after every 3 years?
recs.facts: Half the Senate members retire every three years.

recs.q: How many Houses are in the Parliament of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Parliament consists of the National Assembly, the Senate and the President.

recs.q: The Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) post was created through which Constitutional Amendment?
recs.facts: The 27th Amendment (Nov 2025) created the CDF post. (Current affairs.)

recs.q: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic with the first Constitution in:
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic.

recs.q: Pakistan's 1973 Constitution was enforced on:
recs.facts: It was passed on 10 April and enforced on 14 August 1973.

recs.q: The Allahabad Address (1930) was delivered by:
recs.facts: Iqbal proposed a separate Muslim state in NW India.

recs.q: The All India Muslim League was founded in:
recs.facts: It was founded at Dhaka under Nawab Salimullah Khan.

recs.q: Pakistan came into being on:
recs.facts: Pakistan was created on 14 August 1947 (27th Ramadan).

recs.q: Which is the largest city of Pakistan by population?
recs.facts: Karachi is the most populous city.

recs.q: Which province of Pakistan is the largest by area?
recs.facts: Balochistan covers about 44% of Pakistan's area.

recs.q: Hazrat Hafsa (R.A.) was the daughter of:
recs.facts: Hafsa bint Umar was a wife of the Prophet ﷺ.

recs.q: Which daughter of Hazrat Umar (R.A.) married the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
recs.facts: Hafsa bint Umar became Ummul Mu'minin.

recs.q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.) was the father of which wife of the Prophet ﷺ?
recs.facts: Ayesha bint Abu Bakr.

recs.q: Who was the first woman martyred in Islam?
recs.facts: Sumayya bint Khayyat, mother of Ammar, was martyred by Abu Jahl.

recs.q: Which Sahabi is known as 'Zun-Nurain'?
recs.facts: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ (Ruqayya, then Umm Kulthum).

recs.q: The second battle of Islam was:
recs.facts: Badr (2 AH) was first, Uhud (3 AH) second.

recs.q: In which Ghazwa was the Prophet's ﷺ blessed tooth martyred (broken)?
recs.facts: At Uhud (3 AH) the Prophet ﷺ's tooth was broken and he was wounded.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought?
recs.facts: Badr took place on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Ghazwa Ahzab (Khandaq) fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of the Trench (Ahzab) was in 5 AH.

recs.q: Ghazwa Ahzab is also known as:
recs.facts: The Muslims dug a trench around Madinah on Salman Farsi's advice.

recs.q: Tauraat (Torah) was revealed on which Prophet?
recs.facts: Tauraat — Musa; Zaboor — Dawud; Injeel — Isa; Quran — Muhammad ﷺ.

recs.q: Zaboor was revealed on which Prophet?
recs.facts: Zaboor (Psalms) was given to Dawud (A.S.).

recs.q: 'Ruhullah' is the title of which Prophet?
recs.facts: Isa (A.S.) is called Ruhullah (Spirit of Allah).

recs.q: Who is the father of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.)?
recs.facts: The Quran names Ibrahim's father as Azar.

recs.q: Hazrat Ismail (A.S.) and Hazrat Ishaq (A.S.) are the sons of:
recs.facts: Both are sons of Ibrahim (A.S.).

recs.q: The prophet whose title was 'Israel' is:
recs.facts: Israel means 'servant of Allah' — the title of Yaqub (A.S.).

recs.q: Which is the last Surah of the Quran?
recs.facts: Surah 114, An-Nas, is the last.

recs.q: Which is the shortest Surah of the Quran?
recs.facts: Al-Kawthar has 3 verses and the fewest words.

recs.q: What is the minimum number of verses in a Surah?
recs.facts: Al-Asr, Al-Kawthar and An-Nasr each have 3 verses.

recs.q: How many Surahs are in the last Para (Juz 30)?
recs.facts: Surahs 78 to 114 are in Juz 30 = 37 surahs.

recs.q: How many verses (ayat) does Surah Al-Baqarah have?
recs.facts: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 verses.

recs.q: How many Surahs are named after Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
recs.facts: Only Surah Muhammad (47) is named after him.

recs.q: How many Manzils (stations) are in the Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran is divided into 7 manzils.

recs.q: How many Prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran?
recs.facts: 25 prophets are mentioned by name.

recs.q: How many pillars are in Islam?
recs.facts: Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj.

recs.q: How many Madni Surahs are in the Quran (commonly accepted)?
recs.facts: 28 Surahs are Madni; 86 are Makki.

recs.q: Over how many years was the Madni portion of the Quran revealed?
recs.facts: Madni revelation: from Hijrah (622 CE) until 632 CE ≈ 10 years.

recs.q: Which prayer is not preceded by Azan?
recs.facts: No Azan is called for the funeral prayer.

recs.q: What does 'Islam' mean?
recs.facts: Islam means submission to the will of Allah (and peace).

recs.q: 'Miraath' means:
recs.facts: Miraath (Mirath) = inheritance.

recs.q: Who appointed Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (R.A.) as Governor of Yemen?
recs.facts: The Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen in about 10 AH.

recs.q: The Prophet's ﷺ mother, Hazrat Amina, passed away when he was about:
recs.facts: She died at Abwa when he ﷺ was about six.

recs.q: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ receive the first revelation?
recs.facts: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira at age 40.

recs.q: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ migrate to Madinah?
recs.facts: Hijrah took place in 622 CE when he ﷺ was 53.

recs.q: In which Ghazwa did the Prophet ﷺ lead his last military expedition?
recs.facts: Tabuk (9 AH) was the last expedition he ﷺ personally led.

recs.q: Name the four daughters of the Prophet ﷺ — which of these is one of them?
recs.facts: Zainab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (R.A.).

recs.q: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.)?
recs.facts: His name was Abdullah; Abu Bakr was a nickname.

recs.q: Which battle is also called 'Yaum-ul-Furqan'?
recs.facts: Badr separated truth from falsehood.

recs.q: In which year of Hijrah was the Treaty of Hudaibiyah signed?
recs.facts: It was signed in 6 AH between the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh.

recs.q: Makkah was conquered in:
recs.facts: Fath-e-Makkah happened in Ramadan 8 AH.

recs.q: Who was the first Caliph of Islam?
recs.facts: Abu Bakr (632–634 CE).

recs.q: Who was the first Muazzin of Islam?
recs.facts: Bilal bin Rabah called the first Azan.

recs.q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ?
recs.facts: Khadija bint Khuwaylid.

recs.q: Which is the longest Surah of the Quran?
recs.facts: It has 286 verses.

recs.q: Which Surah is called 'Umm-ul-Kitab'?
recs.facts: Al-Fatiha is the Mother of the Book.

recs.q: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the year:
recs.facts: Born in Makkah on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
recs.facts: The UN HQ is in New York City.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of NATO?
recs.facts: NATO HQ is in Brussels, Belgium.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC (oil organisation)?
recs.facts: OPEC HQ is in Vienna, Austria.

recs.q: Which country is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'?
recs.facts: Finland has about 188,000 lakes.

recs.q: Who founded Apple (iPhone)?
recs.facts: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple.

recs.q: Who founded Facebook?
recs.facts: Zuckerberg founded Facebook in 2004.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Benazir became PM in 1988.

recs.q: Who said 'The only thing we have to fear is fear itself'?
recs.facts: FDR in his 1933 inaugural address.

recs.q: Which is the capital of Austria?
recs.facts: Vienna is Austria's capital.

recs.q: Which is the capital of Mongolia?
recs.facts: Ulaanbaatar is Mongolia's capital.

recs.q: Which is the capital of Kazakhstan?
recs.facts: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan.

recs.q: Which is the capital of Bahrain?
recs.facts: Manama is the capital of Bahrain.

recs.q: Which is the capital of Ghana?
recs.facts: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

recs.q: What is the currency of Egypt?
recs.facts: Egypt uses the Egyptian pound.

recs.q: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia?
recs.facts: Saudi Riyal (SAR).

recs.q: The Lira is the currency of:
recs.facts: The Turkish Lira.

recs.q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
recs.facts: Sri Lanka uses the Rupee (LKR).

recs.q: Who has taken the most wickets in Test cricket?
recs.facts: Muralitharan has 800 Test wickets.

recs.q: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
recs.facts: Jupiter is the largest planet.

recs.q: Which planet has the largest number of moons?
recs.facts: Saturn has the most confirmed moons.

recs.q: What is the world's fastest bird?
recs.facts: It can dive at over 300 km/h.

recs.q: Which is the longest river in Asia?
recs.facts: The Yangtze (≈ 6,300 km) is Asia's longest.

recs.q: FIFA was founded in 1904 in which country?
recs.facts: FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904.

recs.q: Which is the most populous country in the world (recent)?
recs.facts: India overtook China in 2023.

recs.q: Which is the largest desert in the world?
recs.facts: Antarctica is the largest desert (Sahara is the largest hot desert).

recs.q: Which gas is essential for human breathing?
recs.facts: Humans need oxygen for respiration.

recs.q: Why are trees important?
opts: They give oxygen and reduce pollution
recs.facts: Trees produce oxygen, absorb CO₂ and prevent erosion.

recs.q: Which strait lies between Oman and Iran?
recs.facts: Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

recs.q: Which country has the highest number of satellites in orbit?
recs.facts: The US (with Starlink etc.) operates the most satellites.

recs.q: India conducted its first nuclear test ('Smiling Buddha') in:
recs.facts: On 18 May 1974 at Pokhran.

recs.q: Which is the national fruit of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Mango is the national fruit.

recs.q: What does SUPARCO stand for?
opts: Space and United Pakistan Research Corporation
Space Union of Pakistan Research Committee
Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
recs.facts: SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency.

recs.q: What does HIT (Pakistan) stand for?
recs.facts: HIT is a defence production facility at Taxila.

recs.q: What is the length of the Pak–Afghan border (Durand Line)?
recs.facts: The border is roughly 2,640 km.

recs.q: Pakistan's economy mainly depends on:
recs.facts: Agriculture is the backbone, employing the largest share of the workforce.

recs.q: Which country is the Great Wall located in?
recs.facts: The Great Wall of China.

recs.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
recs.facts: The Pacific covers about one-third of the Earth.

recs.q: Which is the smallest continent?
recs.facts: Australia/Oceania is the smallest.

recs.q: Which is the tallest mountain in the world?
recs.facts: Everest is 8,848 m.

recs.q: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
recs.facts: Russia covers about 17 million km².

recs.q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Sindh? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Murad Ali Shah of PPP has been CM since 2016 (re-elected 2024). Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Balochistan? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Sarfraz Bugti became CM in March 2024. Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Pakistan? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Shehbaz Sharif became PM in March 2024. Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the Deputy Prime Minister of Pakistan? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Ishaq Dar has been Deputy PM since 2024. Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the Governor of Sindh? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Tessori was appointed Governor of Sindh in 2023. Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Kundi became KP Governor in 2024. Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Gilani was elected Senate Chairman in April 2024. Verify latest.

recs.q: Who is the President of Turkey? (current affairs)
recs.facts: Erdogan has been President since 2014.

recs.q: If i is an imaginary number, then i² equals:
recs.facts: By definition i = √−1, so i² = −1.

recs.q: The value of log 64 ÷ log 4 is:
recs.facts: log 64 = 3 log 4, so the ratio is 3.

recs.q: The value of log 100 (base 10) is:
The integral of 2x with respect to x is:
recs.facts: ∫2x dx = x² + C.

recs.q: The value of sin 0° is:
The eccentricity of a parabola is:
recs.facts: Ellipse e < 1, parabola e = 1, hyperbola e > 1.

recs.q: A triangular prism has how many faces?
recs.facts: Two triangular ends + three rectangular sides = 5 faces.

recs.q: A prism's side faces are called:
recs.facts: The side faces of a prism are lateral faces.

recs.q: A cube has how many edges?
recs.facts: A cube has 12 edges, 8 vertices, 6 faces.

recs.q: The sum of angles in a triangle is:
recs.facts: Always 180° in a plane triangle.

recs.q: The area of a circle with radius r is:
recs.facts: Area = πr².

recs.q: What is the square root of 144?
The speed of light is approximately:
The chemical formula of water is:
recs.facts: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

recs.q: If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 8th?
recs.facts: 28 − 8 = 20 days back; 20 mod 7 = 6 → Monday − 6 = Tuesday.

recs.q: Ahmad walks North, then turns left. In which direction is he now facing?
recs.facts: Turning left while facing North makes you face West.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 23rd?
recs.facts: 23 − 2 = 21 days = exactly 3 weeks, so the day is the same: Friday.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 13th?
recs.facts: 13 − 1 = 12 days; 12 mod 7 = 5 → Monday + 5 = Saturday.

recs.q: Rearrange RAPISS to form the name of a city.
recs.facts: RAPISS → PARIS (the capital of France).

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister Sidra is twice his age. When Ali is 11, how old will Sidra be?
recs.facts: Sidra is 5 × 2 = 10 now. Ali reaches 11 after 6 more years, so Sidra will be 10 + 6 = 16.

recs.q: A class has 500 students, of whom 340 are boys. What is the percentage of boys?
One dozen pencils cost Rs 60. What is the price of 5 pencils?
recs.facts: 1 dozen = 12 pencils, so 1 pencil = Rs 5; 5 pencils = Rs 25.

recs.q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How far does it go in 12 minutes?
recs.facts: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour; 120 × 1/5 = 24 km.

recs.q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct in May 1998?
opts: 6 (five on 28 May and one on 30 May)
recs.facts: Pakistan announced five tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I) and one on 30 May (Chagai-II).

recs.q: What is the chemical symbol of gold?
recs.facts: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum'. Ag is silver.

recs.q: Against whom was the Battle (Ghazwa) of Uhud fought?
recs.facts: Uhud (3 AH) was fought between the Muslims and the Quraysh of Makkah led by Abu Sufyan.

recs.q: In which city was the 1974 OIC (Islamic Summit) meeting held in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC was held in Lahore in February 1974.

recs.q: Who was the foster mother of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
recs.facts: Halima Sa'diyah nursed and raised him ﷺ in the desert as an infant.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan when the 1956 Constitution was adopted?
recs.facts: The first Constitution was adopted on 23 March 1956 under PM Chaudhry Muhammad Ali.

recs.q: In which year was the Bogra Formula presented?
recs.facts: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented it in October 1953 to settle representation between the two wings.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan acquire Gwadar from Oman?
recs.facts: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman on 8 September 1958.

recs.q: How many types of Sunnah are there?
recs.facts: Sunnah is of three types: the Prophet's ﷺ sayings (Qauli), actions (Fe'li) and tacit approvals (Taqriri).

recs.q: What is the capital of Australia?
recs.facts: Canberra is the capital; Sydney is the largest city.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks, so the day of the week is the same: Sunday.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What percentage are girls?
What is half of 1/8?
Which one is different from the rest: September, May, March, Tuesday?
recs.facts: September, May and March are months of the year, while Tuesday is a day of the week.

recs.q: Complete the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
recs.facts: The differences are consecutive even numbers: +4, +6, +8, +10, then +12. So 30 + 12 = 42.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 23rd be?
recs.facts: The 1st, 8th, 15th and 22nd are Mondays, so the 23rd is a Tuesday.

recs.q: The speed of an aircraft is 720 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
recs.facts: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so distance in 1 minute = 720 / 60 = 12 km.

recs.q: A car covers 60 km in 40 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
recs.facts: 60 km in 40 minutes means 30 km in 20 minutes, so in 60 minutes it covers 90 km: 90 km/h.

recs.q: Choose the odd one out: Cricket, Football, Hockey, Chess.
recs.facts: Chess is an indoor board game, while the others are outdoor field sports.

recs.q: He is strictly opposed ___ this new rule.
recs.facts: The adjective opposed takes the preposition to: opposed to something.

recs.q: She has been living here ___ 1999.
recs.facts: Since is used with a fixed starting point in time (1999), while for is used with a period of time.

recs.q: The prisoner was accused ___ theft.
recs.facts: The correct collocation is accused of (a crime).

recs.q: What is the synonym of 'Obsolete'?
recs.facts: Obsolete means no longer in use or out of date, which is the same as outdated.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'Transparent'?
recs.facts: Transparent means see-through; its opposite is opaque, which does not let light pass through.

recs.q: Choose the correctly spelled word.
recs.facts: The correct spelling has a double c and a double m: accommodation.

recs.q: What is 75% of 200?
If 20% of a number is 40, what is the number?
Solve for x: 3x + 5 = 20
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:2. If there are 15 boys, how many girls are there?
recs.facts: 3 parts = 15, so 1 part = 5. Girls = 2 x 5 = 10.

recs.q: The boundary line between Pakistan and India is called:
recs.facts: Sir Cyril Radcliffe headed the Boundary Commission in 1947 and drew the Radcliffe Line, the international border between Pakistan and India.

recs.q: In which year was the first Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza imposed the first martial law in October 1958 and appointed General Ayub Khan as Chief Martial Law Administrator.

recs.q: When did Balochistan officially become a province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: After the One Unit scheme was dissolved, Balochistan became a full province on 1 July 1970.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All-India Muslim League?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in 1913 (the League was founded in 1906).

recs.q: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Under the 1956 Constitution Pakistan became a republic and Iskander Mirza became its first President in 1956. Before that, Jinnah was Governor General.

recs.q: Who was Pakistan's first Foreign Minister?
recs.facts: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan served as Pakistan's first Foreign Minister from 1947 to 1954.

recs.q: The book "My Brother" was written by:
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah wrote "My Brother", a memoir about the life of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

recs.q: Which Surah is known as the Heart of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Surah Yaseen is called Qalb-ul-Quran (Heart of the Quran) according to a well-known tradition.

recs.q: Which angel is responsible for rainfall and sustenance?
recs.facts: Hazrat Mikael (A.S) is the angel in charge of rain and provision. Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Izrail takes souls.

recs.q: How many obligatory acts (Faraiz) are there in Wudu?
recs.facts: According to the Hanafi school, the four Faraiz of Wudu are washing the face, washing the arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head and washing the feet up to the ankles.

recs.q: On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations (UN)?
recs.facts: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, shortly after independence. The UN itself came into existence on 24 October 1945.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the OIC and how many members does it have?
recs.facts: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has its headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and 57 member states. It was founded in 1969 at Rabat after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.

recs.q: Which is the largest continent in the world?
recs.facts: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population.

recs.q: What is the longest river in the world?
recs.facts: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is traditionally regarded as the longest river. The Amazon carries the most water.

recs.q: What is the official currency of Japan?
recs.facts: The Japanese yen is the currency of Japan. The yuan is China's, the won is Korea's and the ringgit is Malaysia's.

recs.q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
recs.facts: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: What is the capital of Hungary?
recs.facts: Budapest, on the Danube river, is the capital of Hungary. Vienna is Austria's capital, Bucharest is Romania's and Prague is the Czech Republic's.

recs.q: Jahangir Khan is world-famous for which sport?
recs.facts: Jahangir Khan is a Pakistani squash legend who won 555 consecutive matches between 1981 and 1986 and six British Open titles in a row.

recs.q: Which country is the world's largest crude oil producer (2025/2026)?
recs.facts: The USA has been the world's largest crude oil producer since 2018, ahead of Saudi Arabia and Russia.

recs.q: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan in the Khyber region?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad region in Afghanistan. Khunjerab connects Pakistan with China, Bolan lies in Balochistan and Lowari lies between Dir and Chitral.

recs.q: What is the factorial of 4 (4!)?
What is the negative of iota (i), where i is the square root of -1?
recs.facts: Negative means multiplying by -1, so the negative of i is -i.

recs.q: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated on 27 December 2007?
recs.facts: She was killed after a rally at Liaquat Bagh in Rawalpindi.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Khadija (R.A.)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khadija (R.A.) was the daughter of Khuwaylid bin Asad of the Quraysh.

recs.q: Who married two daughters of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), one after the other?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman married Ruqayyah and, after her death, Umm Kulthum, so he is called Zun-Noorain.

recs.q: On which river is the Mangla Dam located?
recs.facts: Mangla Dam was completed in 1967 on the Jhelum River near Mirpur, Azad Kashmir.

recs.q: What does the word 'Ahzab' mean?
recs.facts: Ahzab means the confederate parties. It refers to the tribes that besieged Madinah in the Battle of the Trench (5 AH).

recs.q: Which is the largest port of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Karachi Port is the largest and busiest port of Pakistan.

recs.q: When was the Eiffel Tower built (completed)?
recs.facts: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair.

recs.q: Ayat-e-Bir (the verse of righteousness) is in which Surah?
recs.facts: Ayat-e-Bir is verse 177 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

recs.q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (People of the Cave)?
recs.facts: The Quran mentions the dog of the People of the Cave, who stayed at the entrance of the cave.

recs.q: Hazrat Hajra (R.A.) was the mother of which Prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S.).

recs.q: Which female companion of the Prophet (PBUH) narrated the most Hadith?
recs.facts: Hazrat Aisha (R.A.) narrated about 2210 Hadith, the most among women.

recs.q: What is the capital of Somalia?
recs.facts: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia.

recs.q: Who was Bulleh Shah?
recs.facts: Bulleh Shah (1680-1757) was a famous Punjabi Sufi poet buried in Kasur.

recs.q: Who was the second Khalifa of Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (R.A.) ruled from 634 to 644 CE after Hazrat Abu Bakr.

recs.q: Who is known by the title 'Abu Hafs'?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umar (R.A.) is called Abu Hafs because his daughter was Hazrat Hafsa (R.A.).

recs.q: What is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
recs.facts: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

recs.q: Who was the second Governor-General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Khawaja Nazimuddin took over in 1948 after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.

recs.q: In which year was the Simla Agreement signed between Pakistan and India?
recs.facts: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.

recs.q: On which date was the 2024 general election of Pakistan held?
recs.facts: The general election for the 16th National Assembly was held on 8 February 2024.

recs.q: Synonym of 'Eminent':
recs.facts: Eminent means famous and respected within a field, so distinguished is the closest word.

recs.q: Between which leaders was the Simla Agreement signed in 1972?
opts: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
recs.facts: It was signed at Shimla on 2 July 1972 by Pakistan's President Z. A. Bhutto and India's Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

recs.q: In which year did East Pakistan separate to become Bangladesh?
recs.facts: After the 1971 war, East Pakistan became Bangladesh on 16 December 1971.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'gracious'?
recs.facts: Gracious means courteous, kind and pleasant, so its opposite is rude, meaning impolite or lacking consideration for others.

recs.q: Where is Masjid an-Nabawi located?
recs.facts: Masjid an-Nabawi was built by the Prophet (PBUH) in Madinah after the Hijrah. It is one of the holiest mosques in Islam.

recs.q: In which year were Pakistan's first general elections held on the basis of adult franchise?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first general elections on adult franchise were held in December 1970. The Awami League won a majority of seats in the National Assembly.

recs.q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib passed away?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) was born around 570 CE and lost his mother at age 6. His grandfather Abdul Muttalib, who then cared for him, died when he was about 8.

recs.q: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a joint project between which two countries?
recs.facts: CPEC is a joint development initiative linking Gwadar Port in Pakistan with Kashgar in China's Xinjiang region through road, rail, energy and infrastructure projects.

recs.q: What does the word Pakistan mean?
recs.facts: Pakistan combines the Persian and Urdu word pak (pure) with the suffix -stan (land). The name was coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Dasht River located?
recs.facts: The Dasht River flows in southwestern Balochistan through the Kech and Gwadar areas towards the Arabian Sea.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q1) What will be the next number: 13, 15, 17, 19, ?
recs.facts: The series goes up by 2 each time, so after 19 comes 21.
recs.rel: Tip: first check the difference between neighbouring terms; a constant difference means an arithmetic series.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q2) What will be the next letters: BC, DE, FG, ?
recs.facts: Each pair starts two letters after the previous pair: BC, DE, FG, then HI.
recs.rel: Tip: write the letters as numbers (B=2, C=3 and so on) to spot the jump between groups.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q3) Subtract 7 from 25+3. If the answer is 10 then write X, otherwise write Y.
recs.facts: 25+3 = 28 and 28 - 7 = 21, which is not 10, so the answer is Y.
recs.rel: Tip: in condition questions, do the arithmetic first and only then choose the letter.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q4) Airplane is to Air as Whale is to:
recs.facts: An airplane travels in air, and a whale lives and travels in the ocean.
recs.rel: Tip: in analogies, name the relation (here: moving thing and its medium) and apply it to the second pair.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q5) Saleem was born in 1947. He is 21 years old. His brother was born in 1965. What is the age of his brother?
recs.facts: Saleem is 21 in 1947 + 21 = 1968. His brother was born in 1965, so he is 1968 - 1965 = 3 years old.
recs.rel: Tip: find the current year from the first person's data, then use it for the second person.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q6) 4+3=8. If the answer is right then write X, otherwise write Y.
recs.facts: 4 + 3 = 7, not 8, so the statement is wrong and the answer is Y.
recs.rel: Tip: check the statement itself; the printed total is a claim you must test.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q7) If sow is to seed then reap is to?
recs.facts: A farmer sows seed and reaps the crop, so the object that matches seed is crop.
recs.rel: Tip: in analogies the second word of the pair is the thing acted upon; sow acts on seed, reap acts on crop.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q8) 8, 10 and 6: divide the largest number by the difference of the two smaller numbers. Answer = ?
recs.facts: The largest number is 10 and the two smaller are 8 and 6, whose difference is 2. So 10 / 2 = 5.
recs.rel: Tip: identify the largest and smaller numbers first so you do not mix up which ones to subtract.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q9) Tight is to Loose as Hard is to:
recs.facts: Loose is the opposite of tight, so the opposite of hard is soft.
recs.rel: Tip: if the first pair are opposites (antonyms), choose the opposite of the third word.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q10) Fish is to swimming as Snake is to:
recs.facts: Swimming is how a fish moves, and a snake moves by creeping along the ground.
recs.rel: Tip: this is an animal-and-movement analogy; match the animal to its typical way of moving.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q11) Which word does not belong to this list: Foot, Inch, Yard, Acre, Mile?
recs.facts: Foot, inch, yard and mile measure length, but an acre measures area.
recs.rel: Tip: an acre is about 4047 square metres; in Pakistan land is also measured in kanal and marla.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q12) Cat is to Kitten as Dog is to?
recs.facts: A kitten is the young one of a cat, and a puppy is the young one of a dog.
recs.rel: Tip: animal-to-young analogies use the special word for the young of that animal (calf, lamb, cub).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q13) Which one is different from the others: Ship, Bus, Train, Car, Truck?
recs.facts: Bus, train, car and truck travel on land, while a ship travels on water.
recs.rel: Tip: group items by where or how they work, then pick the one that falls outside the group.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q14) If Light is to Eye, then Sound is to?
recs.facts: The eye senses light, and the ear senses sound.
recs.rel: Tip: sense-organ analogies pair a stimulus with the organ that detects it.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q15) Which is different in the following: Lion, Wolf, Leopard, Lamb, Tiger?
recs.facts: Lion, wolf, leopard and tiger are carnivorous predators, while a lamb is a gentle animal that eats plants.
recs.rel: Tip: carnivores hunt other animals, herbivores eat plants; this split is common in odd-one-out questions.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q16) Which one of the following is different: Mile, Kanal, Marla, Acre?
recs.facts: Kanal, marla and acre are units of land area, while a mile is a unit of length.
recs.rel: Tip: one kanal equals 20 marla, and a marla is about 272 square feet.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q17) Hand is to Touch as Nose is to?
recs.facts: The hand is the organ of touch, and the nose is the organ of smell.
recs.rel: Tip: the five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch, each tied to one organ.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from others: Shirts, Boots, Coats, Trousers, Necktie?
recs.facts: Shirts, coats, trousers and necktie are clothes worn on the body, while boots are footwear.
recs.rel: Tip: look for the item that belongs to a different category (footwear versus clothing).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q19) Easy is to Light as Rough is to:
recs.facts: Easy and light both mean not hard or heavy to deal with, and rough is closest to hard (a rough surface feels hard and coarse). The paper's answer key gives Hard.
recs.rel: Tip: when the analogy is not obvious, look for the option that is the antonym of the third word.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q20) Which of the following is different from others: Plate, Dish, Knife, Spoon, Sugar?
recs.facts: Plate, dish, knife and spoon are utensils, while sugar is a food item.
recs.rel: Tip: separate objects used for eating from things that are eaten.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q21) One third of one half is equal to?
recs.facts: One third of one half is 1/3 x 1/2 = 1/6.
recs.rel: Tip: the word 'of' between fractions means multiply.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q22) Hot is to Burn as Cold is to?
recs.facts: Excessive heat makes things burn, and excessive cold makes things freeze.
recs.rel: Tip: this is a cause-and-effect analogy; ask what the extreme does.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q23) Which number will come next: 6, 11, 12, 11, 18, ?
recs.facts: Take alternate terms: 6, 12, 18 goes up by 6, and the other terms stay at 11, 11, so the next is 11.
recs.rel: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q24) Which is different from others: Whisper, Shout, Sing, Tell?
recs.facts: Whisper, shout and tell are ways of speaking words, while singing involves music and a tune.
recs.rel: Tip: look for the action that uses a different skill from the rest.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q25) Which one is different from others: Selfish, Dishonest, Foolish, Ugly?
recs.facts: Selfish, dishonest and foolish describe character or behaviour, while ugly describes physical appearance.
recs.rel: Tip: separate qualities of character from qualities of looks.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q26) Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to?
recs.facts: A bird is kept in a cage, and a prisoner is kept in jail.
recs.rel: Tip: the relation is 'confined living thing and its place of confinement'.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q27) Which is different from other: Radius, Diagonal, Diameter, Circumference?
recs.facts: Radius, diameter and circumference are all parts of a circle, but a diagonal belongs to polygons such as squares and rectangles.
recs.rel: Tip: circumference = 2 x pi x radius, and diameter = 2 x radius.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q28) Which number is out of order: Four, Eight, Ten, Seven, Twelve?
recs.facts: Four, eight, ten and twelve are even numbers, while seven is odd.
recs.rel: Tip: check parity (odd or even) first when numbers are written as words.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q29) Which one of the following is different: 62, 31, 34, 17, 20?
recs.facts: Each of 62 and 31, and of 34 and 17, forms a pair where one is double the other. 20 has no partner (10 is missing), so it is different.
recs.rel: Tip: look for pairs related by doubling or halving; the leftover number is the odd one.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q30) Which one of the following is different: Cow, Goat, Sheep, Horse, Buffalo?
recs.facts: Cow, goat, sheep and buffalo are milk-giving farm animals, while a horse is not kept for milk.
recs.rel: Tip: think about the main purpose an animal is kept for.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q31) Which number will come next: 1, 4, 10, 22, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 3, 6, 12, which double each time, so the next difference is 24: 22 + 24 = 46.
recs.rel: Tip: if differences keep doubling, the series follows a doubling-gap rule.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q32) Which is different in the following: Speech, Lecture, Oration, Sermon, Gossip?
recs.facts: Speech, lecture, oration and sermon are formal talks given to an audience, while gossip is casual talk about other people.
recs.rel: Tip: formal versus informal is a common basis for odd-one-out questions.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q33) If A is to E then C is to?
recs.facts: A to E is a jump of 4 letters (A=1, E=5), so C (3) plus 4 gives G (7).
recs.rel: Tip: convert letters to positions to find a fixed jump.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q34) Which one is different in the following: Petrol, Oil, Water, Spirit?
recs.facts: Petrol, oil and spirit are flammable liquids, while water does not burn.
recs.rel: Tip: flammability is a quick test for fuels versus other liquids.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q35) Write the number that comes next: 5, 3, 6, 4, 7, ?
recs.rel: Tip: when the series zigzags, look for two alternating operations.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q36) Nib is to Pen as Blade is to?
recs.facts: A nib is the writing part of a pen, and a blade is the cutting part of a knife.
recs.rel: Tip: this is a part-to-whole analogy.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q37) Which number comes next: 3, 8, 14, 21, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 5, 6, 7, so the next difference is 8: 21 + 8 = 29.
recs.rel: Tip: when differences increase by 1, the series is built from consecutive added numbers.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q38) Which letters will come next: BY, CX, DW, EV, ?
recs.facts: The first letters go forward B, C, D, E, F and the second letters go backward Y, X, W, V, U, so the next pair is FU.
recs.rel: Tip: one letter moving forward while the other moves backward is a classic two-track pattern.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q39) A cake is cut so that one piece, which is half of the cake, is twice as large as one of the other pieces. How many pieces are there?
recs.facts: One piece is 1/2 of the cake, and each other piece is half of that, 1/4. The remaining 1/2 makes two pieces of 1/4, so there are 3 pieces in all.
recs.rel: Tip: draw the fractions out; the pieces must add up to one whole.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q40) Which is different in the following: Violin, Piano, String, Cutter, Banjo?
recs.facts: Violin, piano, string and banjo are all connected with music, while a cutter is a cutting tool.
recs.rel: Tip: the key word here is the category, musical instrument versus tool.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q41) Which number comes next in the following: 5, 9, 8, 12, 11, ?
recs.facts: The pattern is +4, -1, +4, -1, so after 11 comes 11 + 4 = 15.
recs.rel: Tip: write the differences between neighbours to find repeating operations.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q42) December is to October as June is to?
recs.facts: December is two months after October in reverse, so go two months back: June gives April.
recs.rel: Tip: count the months in the first pair and apply the same step.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q43) Which number will come next: 20, 15, 18, 13, 16, ?
recs.facts: The pattern is -5, +3, -5, +3, so 16 - 5 = 11.
recs.rel: Tip: alternate -5 and +3 gives two interleaved series: 20, 18, 16, 14 and 15, 13, 11.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q45) Which number comes next in the following: 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 22, ?
recs.facts: The pattern is multiply by 2, then add 1: 2x2=4, 4+1=5, 5x2=10, 10+1=11, 11x2=22, 22+1=23.
recs.rel: Tip: if the numbers jump up and then up slightly, test alternating multiply and add.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q46) Laugh is to Cry, so Weep is to?
recs.facts: Cry is the opposite of laugh, and the opposite of weep is smile.
recs.rel: Tip: antonym analogies pair opposite feelings or actions.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q47) Add all even numbers and divide it by its middle number: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
recs.facts: The even numbers are 4, 6 and 8, which add up to 18. The middle number is 6, so 18 / 6 = 3.
recs.rel: Tip: with an odd count of numbers, the middle one is the one with equal numbers on both sides.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q48) Which number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42.
recs.rel: Tip: these are products of consecutive numbers: 1x2, 2x3, 3x4, 4x5, 5x6, 6x7 = 42.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q49) Tobacco is to Pipe as Coal is to:
recs.facts: Tobacco is burned in a pipe, and coal is burned in an oven.
recs.rel: Tip: the relation is a material and the container or device where it is burned.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q50) Which number comes next in the following: 3/4, 6/8, 12/16, 24/32, ?
recs.facts: Each fraction doubles both numerator and denominator: 24 x 2 = 48 and 32 x 2 = 64.
recs.rel: Tip: all these fractions equal 3/4, only the numerator and denominator are scaled.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q51) If 2200 hours is 10 o'clock in the evening then write the answer as 4, and if not then write 5.
recs.facts: 2200 hours in the 24-hour clock is 22 - 12 = 10 in the evening, so the statement is true and the answer is 4.
recs.rel: Tip: for 24-hour times after 1300, subtract 12 to get the pm hour.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q52) The next number in the series is: 120, 108, 97, 87, 78, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -12, -11, -10, -9, so the next is -8: 78 - 8 = 70.
recs.rel: Tip: when differences shrink by 1 each step, continue the pattern.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q53) Finger is to Hand as Toe is to?
recs.facts: A finger is a part of the hand, and a toe is a part of the foot.
recs.rel: Tip: part-to-whole analogies are solved by naming the whole that holds the part.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q55) What will be the next letter: A, E, I, M, ?
recs.facts: Each letter is 4 places after the previous one: A(1), E(5), I(9), M(13), then Q(17).
recs.rel: Tip: convert letters to numbers to see equal jumps.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q56) If L comes before P then write 5, otherwise write 4.
recs.facts: In the alphabet L is the 12th letter and P is the 16th, so L comes before P and the answer is 5.
recs.rel: Tip: alphabet position questions are easiest if you remember A=1 up to Z=26.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q54) Which is different in the following: Ounce, Pound, Ton, Maund?
recs.facts: Ounce, pound and ton belong to the same Western (imperial) system, while the maund is a traditional South Asian unit.
recs.rel: Tip: a maund is about 40 kg in Pakistan today (37.3 kg in the older system).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q57) List is to Last as Fist is to?
recs.facts: List becomes Last by changing the vowel I to A, so Fist becomes Fast.
recs.rel: Tip: when the words look alike, compare letter by letter to find which letter changes.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q58) What letter comes next in the following series: A, C, F, J, ?
recs.facts: The letters are at positions 1, 3, 6, 10, whose gaps are 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5: 10 + 5 = 15, which is O.
recs.rel: Tip: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 are triangular numbers.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q59) Triangle is to Prism as Circle is to?
recs.facts: A prism is the three-dimensional solid built from a triangle, and a sphere is the solid form of a circle.
recs.rel: Tip: 2D-to-3D analogies pair a flat shape with its solid.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q60) Which word does not belong to this list: Less, Depart, Abate, Decrease?
recs.facts: Less, abate and decrease all mean to reduce, while depart means to leave.
recs.rel: Tip: look for the word whose meaning is not shared by the others.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q61) Tomorrow is to Yesterday as Thursday is to?
recs.facts: Yesterday is two days before tomorrow, so the matching day is two days before Thursday, which is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Tip: count the day gap in the first pair and apply it to the second.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q62) If 6 and 5 make 10 then write A, otherwise write B.
recs.facts: 6 + 5 = 11, not 10, so the condition fails and the answer is B.
recs.rel: Tip: evaluate the arithmetic, then pick the letter that matches the condition.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q63) If W precedes X then write the answer as 5, otherwise 6.
recs.facts: In the alphabet W comes right before X, so W precedes X and the answer is 5.
recs.rel: Tip: the alphabet order is ...U, V, W, X, Y, Z.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q64) Which number comes next: 6, 12, 9, 16, 12, ?
recs.facts: Alternate terms form two series: 6, 9, 12 (adding 3) and 12, 16, 20 (adding 4). The next term is 20.
recs.rel: Tip: when numbers go up and down, split them into odd-position and even-position series.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q65) A watch reads half past nine. The minute hand points toward North. In which direction does the hour hand point?
recs.facts: At half past nine the minute hand points to 6 and the hour hand lies between 9 and 10. If the minute hand (6) points North, the clock is turned half a turn, so the 9-10 position (about 3) points East.
recs.rel: Tip: turn the whole dial so that the minute hand matches the given direction, then read the hour hand.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q66) What will be the next number in the series: 5, 8, 9, 16, 13, ?
recs.facts: Odd-position terms go 5, 9, 13 (adding 4) and even-position terms go 8, 16, 24 (adding 8). The next term is 24.
recs.rel: Tip: when a series mixes slow and fast growth, it is probably two interleaved series.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q67) Bright is to Dim as Clear is to?
recs.facts: Dim is the opposite of bright, and vague is the opposite of clear.
recs.rel: Tip: antonym analogies: find the opposite of the third word in the answer options.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q68) P is to L as N is to?
recs.facts: P is the 16th letter and L is the 12th, which is 4 places back. N is the 14th, and 4 places back is J (10).
recs.rel: Tip: letter analogies depend on the fixed jump between the first pair.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q69) What will be the next number: 11, 21, 40, 77, 150, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 10, 19, 37, 73, and each difference is double the previous minus 1. The next difference is 145, so 150 + 145 = 295.
recs.rel: Tip: when each term is roughly double the previous, check for double plus or minus a small number.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q71) Write the fifth last letter of the alphabet.
recs.facts: Counting from the end: Z (1st last), Y, X, W, V (5th last), so the answer is V.
recs.rel: Tip: the last letter is 1st last, so the fifth last is the 22nd letter (26 - 5 + 1).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q72) Write the 4th letter before W, as counted from the end of the alphabet.
recs.facts: Going back from W: V, U, T, S, so the 4th letter before W is S.
recs.rel: Tip: the letter 4 places before W (23rd) is the 19th letter, S.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q75) If three oranges cost Rs. 9, how much will it cost to buy four and a half dozen?
recs.facts: Four and a half dozen is 54 oranges. One orange costs 9 / 3 = Rs. 3, so 54 x 3 = Rs. 162.
recs.rel: Tip: find the unit price first, then multiply by the quantity; one dozen is 12 items.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q74) Write the next letter in the series: A, C, D, H, K, ?
recs.facts: The letter positions are 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, with gaps +2, +1, +4, +3, so the gaps are +2, +1, +4, +3, +6, and the next letter is 11 + 6 = 17, which is Q.
recs.rel: Tip: when the gaps themselves form a pattern (here pairs rising by 2), write them out.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q77) Write the next number: 10, 30, 50, 80, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 20, 20, 30, 30, so the next difference is 30 (then 40, 40): 80 + 30 = 110.
recs.rel: Tip: repeated differences like 20, 20, 30, 30 are a common pattern.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q78) NECESSARY CUSTOM TO TRADE ROAD DEVELOPMENT. If one word is omitted from the above, the others could be arranged as one sentence. Write the second letter of the word to be omitted.
recs.facts: Without the word CUSTOM the rest forms the sentence 'Road development necessary to trade'. CUSTOM has U as its second letter.
recs.rel: Tip: try dropping each word in turn and see which remaining set makes a sensible sentence.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q80) How much distance will you cover in 3 and a half minutes if you are moving at the speed of 120 km/h?
recs.facts: 120 km/h is 2 km per minute, so in 3.5 minutes you cover 2 x 3.5 = 7 km.
recs.rel: Tip: dividing km/h by 60 gives km per minute.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q1) SICK is to SACK as LICK is to:
recs.facts: SICK changes its vowel I to A to make SACK, so LICK becomes LACK.
recs.rel: Tip: in word analogies compare the letters one by one to find which letter changes.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q2) What letter comes next in the following series: B, D, G, K, P, ?
recs.facts: The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6: P (16) + 6 = 22, which is V.
recs.rel: Tip: letter gaps that grow by 1 each step are very common.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q3) What number comes next in the following series: 34, 24, 16, 10, 6, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -10, -8, -6, -4, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.
recs.rel: Tip: when the differences fall by 2 each time, the next one is also 2 less.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q4) If 4 is more than 9 write 2 as your answer, otherwise write 3.
recs.facts: 4 is not more than 9, so the condition fails and the answer is 3.
recs.rel: Tip: check the condition first, then write the answer for the matching branch.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q5) Students go to school because:
opts: They want to be away from home.
They want to tease the teacher.
recs.facts: The main purpose of school is to gain knowledge; the other choices are minor or silly reasons.
recs.rel: Tip: in reasoning questions pick the most general and sensible cause.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q6) What number comes next in the following series: 18, 13, 9, 6, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -5, -4, -3, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.
recs.rel: Tip: shrinking differences mean the series is slowing down.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q7) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Car, train, aircraft and ship are machines with engines, while a cart is pulled by an animal or by hand.
recs.rel: Tip: the Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q8) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: February, December, June and September are months, while Monday is a day of the week.
recs.rel: Tip: February is the shortest month, with 28 days (29 in a leap year).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q9) What number comes next in the following series: 49, 36, 25, 16, ?
recs.facts: These are squares in reverse: 7 squared, 6 squared, 5 squared, 4 squared, so next is 3 squared = 9.
recs.rel: Tip: learn the squares up to 15 so square series are quick to spot.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q10) NORTH is to SOUTH as EAST is to:
recs.facts: South is the direct opposite of north, and west is the direct opposite of east.
recs.rel: Tip: the four opposite pairs of compass directions are north and south, east and west.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q11) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Brother, uncle, son and grandfather are male relatives, while a sister is female.
recs.rel: Tip: check gender first when the words are family relations.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q12) Girls wear glasses because:
recs.facts: The usual real reason for wearing glasses is weak eyesight.
recs.rel: Tip: in cause questions choose the practical and most common reason.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q13) In a group of 50 players, 30% play hockey and 80% play cricket. Are there any who play both hockey and cricket?
opts: One cannot say without further detail
recs.facts: 30% of 50 is 15 and 80% of 50 is 40. Since 15 + 40 = 55 is more than 50, at least 5 players must play both.
recs.rel: Tip: if the two groups add up to more than the total, they must overlap.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q14) What number comes next in the following series: 40, 30, 35, 25, 30, 20, ?
recs.rel: Tip: two alternating steps make a zigzag series.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q15) Engine is to Car as Cell is to:
recs.facts: An engine powers a car, and a cell (battery) powers a torch.
recs.rel: Tip: this analogy links a power source to the device it runs.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q16) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Tennis, hockey, cricket and football are outdoor games, while billiard is an indoor game.
recs.rel: Tip: split games into indoor and outdoor groups.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q17) If 7 and 6 make 19, write 5 as your answer, otherwise write 3.
recs.facts: 7 + 6 = 13, which is not 19, so the condition fails and the answer is 3.
recs.rel: Tip: do the sum first before choosing the branch.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Huge, great, fat and big all describe large size, while small is the opposite.
recs.rel: Tip: look for the antonym among a group of synonyms.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q19) What number comes next in the following series: 62, 32, 30, 16, 14, 8, 6, ?
recs.facts: Terms alternate between halving plus 1 and subtracting 2: 62 to 32, 32 to 30, 30 to 16, 16 to 14, 14 to 8, 8 to 6, then 6 halved plus 1 is 4.
recs.rel: Tip: in mixed series test each pair of neighbours for different operations in turn.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q20) If Arza is older than Munir and Munir is younger than Javaid, then Arza is:
recs.facts: Munir is below both Arza and Javaid, but nothing links Arza and Javaid directly, so their order cannot be known.
recs.rel: Tip: two people both older than a third cannot be compared with each other.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q21) If Asif is 12 years old and all boys over 10 are hockey players, then:
opts: It is not sure that Asif is hockey player.
Asif is likely to become hockey player.
recs.facts: Asif is 12, which is over 10, and the rule says all boys over 10 are hockey players, so he is one.
recs.rel: Tip: when a rule says all, apply it directly to anything that meets the condition.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q22) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Mango, lemon and orange are fruits, while tomato is generally treated as a vegetable in cooking.
recs.rel: Tip: botanically a tomato is a fruit, but in everyday classification it is a vegetable.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q23) Women go to market because:
opts: They have plenty of spare time.
They don't want to stay at home.
recs.facts: The practical purpose of going to a market is to buy things.
recs.rel: Tip: choose the reason that is the real purpose, not a general opinion.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q24) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Two, four, twenty and fifty are even numbers, while five is odd.
recs.rel: Tip: parity (odd or even) is a quick odd-one-out check for numbers.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q25) What number comes next in the following series: 27, 20, 14, 9, 5, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -7, -6, -5, -4, so the next is -3: 5 - 3 = 2.
recs.rel: Tip: differences falling by 1 give a smooth decreasing series.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q26) What letter comes next in the following series: J, H, F, D, ?
recs.facts: Each letter is 2 places before the previous one: J, H, F, D, then B.
recs.rel: Tip: going backward in the alphabet by a fixed step is as common as going forward.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q27) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Yard, foot, mile and kilometer are units of measuring length, while length itself is the quantity being measured.
recs.rel: Tip: one mile is about 1.609 kilometres.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q28) Forests are useful because:
opts: They help in building the economy.
recs.facts: Forests supply timber and other resources, so their main usefulness is to the economy.
recs.rel: Tip: Pakistan observes Tree Plantation Day to promote more forests.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q29) NEAR is to FAR as CLOSE is to:
recs.facts: Far is the opposite of near, and open is the opposite of close (shut).
recs.rel: Tip: close can mean near or shut; the first pair tells you to use the antonym of the word.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q30) What is the area of a square which is 8 feet long?
recs.facts: The area of a square is side times side: 8 x 8 = 64 square feet.
recs.rel: Tip: perimeter adds the sides, area multiplies them.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q31) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Cup, mug, glass and jug are containers, while a drink is what goes inside them.
recs.rel: Tip: separate containers from their contents.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q32) If 5 is subtracted from 30, what would be the square root of the remaining?
recs.facts: 30 - 5 = 25 and the square root of 25 is 5.
recs.rel: Tip: remember the perfect squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q33) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Sword, knife, fork and axe are sharp tools or weapons, while a cup is a container with no sharp edge.
recs.rel: Tip: look at the main property (sharp or pointed) shared by most of the items.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q1) Which of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Unearth, discover, find and locate all mean to come across something that already exists. Invention means to create something new.
recs.rel: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q2) What number comes next in the following series? 2413, 2420, 2434, 2462, 2518, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 7, 14, 28, 56, doubling each time, so the next difference is 112: 2518 + 112 = 2630.
recs.rel: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q3) Which one is different from the rest? Cow, Hen, Duck, Bull, Mare
recs.facts: Cow, hen and mare are female animals, while bull is the only male.
recs.rel: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q4) If Shoe is to Foot then Helmet is to ____.
recs.facts: A shoe is worn on the foot and a helmet is worn on the head.
recs.rel: Tip: in analogies, first state the relationship (here, worn on) and then apply it to the second pair.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q5) What number comes next in the following series? 3, 10, 4, 17, 5, ?
recs.facts: Alternate terms form two series: 3, 4, 5 (plus 1) and 10, 17, 24 (plus 7). The next term belongs to the second series: 24.
recs.rel: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences. The answer key lists 26 here, but 24 is what the pattern gives.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q6) Which one is different from the rest? QS, EH, IL, MP, AD
recs.facts: In EH, IL, MP and AD the second letter is 3 places after the first. In QS the gap is only 2.
recs.rel: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q7) If the second of the following numbers is added to the shortest number and divided by the third number, what will the answer be? 2, 14, 4
recs.facts: Second number 14 plus shortest number 2 is 16. Dividing by the third number 4 gives 4.
recs.rel: Tip: identify the numbers by position first (first, second, third), then apply the operations in order.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q8) What is the next number in the following series? 4, 8, 24, 96, ?
recs.facts: Each term is multiplied by 2, 3, 4 and then 5: 96 x 5 = 480.
recs.rel: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q9) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Town, city, village and township are all human settlements on earth. Heaven is not.
recs.rel: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q10) March is to 31/3 and June is to ____.
recs.facts: March has 31 days and is the 3rd month. June has 30 days and is the 6th month, so 30/6.
recs.rel: Tip: months with 30 days are April, June, September and November.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q11) Which one of the following is different from the rest? Infant, Adult, Child, Newborn, Baby
recs.facts: Infant, child, newborn and baby all describe young ones. Adult is a fully grown person.
recs.rel: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q12) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
recs.facts: Separation, split, divide and gap all involve parting. Union means joining together.
recs.rel: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q13) What number comes next in the following series? 63, 3, 44, 0, 91, ?
recs.facts: Each pair is the first digit minus the second digit: 6 - 3 = 3, 4 - 4 = 0, so for 91: 9 - 1 = 8.
recs.rel: Tip: when a series mixes two-digit and one-digit numbers, try operations on the digits.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q14) What letter comes next in the following series? E, J, N, Q, ?
recs.facts: The steps are +5, +4, +3, so the next step is +2: Q + 2 = S.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q15) Which one is different from the rest?
