recs.rel: Badr was in 2 AH and the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) in 5 AH.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 74) Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, real executive power lies with whom?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution created a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister is the chief executive.
recs.rel: The President is the ceremonial head of state, although the 8th Amendment later shifted powers temporarily.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 75) Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Armed Forces?
opts: Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
recs.facts: The President of Pakistan is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces under the Constitution.
recs.rel: The President is the constitutional Supreme Commander of the armed forces; the 27th Amendment (November 2025) created the post of Chief of Defence Forces.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 76) On which date was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot dead on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
recs.rel: The park was renamed Liaquat Bagh after him.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 77) Which was the first country to recognise Pakistan?
recs.facts: Iran was the first country to accept and recognise Pakistan after independence.
recs.rel: Afghanistan was the only country to vote against Pakistan's UN membership in 1947.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 78) How many sons and daughters did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) had three sons (Qasim, Abdullah and Ibrahim) and four daughters (Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima).
recs.rel: All sons died in childhood; of the daughters only Hazrat Fatima (RA) outlived him.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 79) For how many years did the British rule India, counting from 1857 to 1947?
recs.facts: 1947 minus 1857 gives 90 years of direct British Crown rule after the War of Independence of 1857.
recs.rel: Direct Crown rule began in 1858; counting from the war of 1857 to independence in 1947 gives about 90 years.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 80) Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan served as Pakistan's first Foreign Minister from 1947 to 1954.
recs.rel: He also later served as President of the UN General Assembly and a judge of the International Court of Justice.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 81) On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
recs.facts: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, as its 56th member.
recs.rel: Pakistan and Yemen were admitted to the United Nations together on 30 September 1947; the UN itself was founded on 24 October 1945.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 82) From which country did Allama Iqbal obtain his PhD degree?
recs.facts: Iqbal received his PhD from the University of Munich in Germany (his thesis was completed around 1907-08).
recs.rel: His thesis was The Development of Metaphysics in Persia.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 83) In which year was the Nehru Report presented?
recs.facts: The Nehru Report was drawn up by a committee led by Motilal Nehru in 1928.
recs.rel: Jinnah responded to it with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 84) In which year was the All India Muslim League founded?
recs.facts: The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka.
recs.rel: The founding session was presided over by Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk, and Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka proposed the party.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 85) Which angel brought Wahi (revelation) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jibrael (AS) conveyed the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira with the words Iqra (Read).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 86) Which gas is commonly used to extinguish fire?
recs.facts: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and does not support burning, so it smothers a fire.
recs.rel: CO2 extinguishers are suited to electrical and oil fires, but not to metal fires.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 87) What is the total area of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan covers about 796,096 square kilometres.
recs.rel: Balochistan is the largest province by area, making up about 44 percent of the country.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 88) How many seats does the Senate of Pakistan have at present?
recs.facts: After the 25th Amendment (merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018) the Senate was reduced to 96 members.
recs.rel: The notes give 104, which was the number before the 2018 merger.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 89) How many seats does the National Assembly of Pakistan have at present?
recs.facts: After FATA's merger the 6 FATA seats were abolished, so the National Assembly now has 336 seats (266 general, 60 women and 10 minorities).
recs.rel: Earlier it had 342 seats; 272 was the old number of general seats.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 90) Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
recs.facts: By area the order is Russia first, Canada second, then the USA and China close together.
recs.rel: Russia covers about 17 million sq km and Canada about 10 million sq km.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 91) In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (Aligarh) College established?
recs.facts: The school was begun in 1875 and upgraded to MAO College in 1877 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
recs.rel: The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 93) Which country won the 1998 FIFA Football World Cup?
recs.facts: France, the host nation, beat Brazil 3-0 in the 1998 final in Paris.
recs.rel: France won its second World Cup in 2018.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 94) Which angel is responsible for rain?
recs.facts: Hazrat Mikael (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.
recs.rel: Jibrael brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Azrael takes souls.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 95) In which year did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic?
recs.facts: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic on 23 March 1956 when the first Constitution came into force.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza became the first President under that Constitution.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 96) Who was the cousin of Hazrat Khadija (RA) and a Christian scholar who confirmed the Prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Waraqa bin Naufal, cousin of Hazrat Khadija (RA), told the Prophet (PBUH) that the angel of Moses had come to him.
recs.rel: He died soon after the first revelation.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 97) Tarbela Dam, near Haripur Hazara, is built on which river?
recs.facts: Tarbela Dam stands on the River Indus in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
recs.rel: Tarbela was completed in 1976 and Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 98) On which date was the United Nations Organization formally established?
recs.facts: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, which is celebrated as UN Day.
recs.rel: The Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 99) Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at present?
recs.facts: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq was elected Speaker in February 2024 after the general elections.
recs.rel: Dr Fehmida Mirza, named in the note, was the first woman Speaker (2008-2013).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 100) Who is the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at present?
recs.facts: Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah of the PPP was elected Deputy Speaker in March 2024.
recs.rel: Faisal Karim Kundi, named in the note, held the post earlier (2012-2013).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 101) Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan at present?
recs.facts: Khawaja Muhammad Asif is the Defence Minister (again since March 2024; he also held the post in 2013-2017 and 2022-2023).
recs.rel: Ch Ahmed Mukhtar, named in the note, held the post in 2008-2012.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 102) Who is the Interior Minister of Pakistan at present?
recs.facts: Mohsin Naqvi became Interior Minister in March 2024.
recs.rel: Rehman Malik, named in the note, was Interior Minister under the PPP government (2008-2013).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 103) Who is the Foreign Minister of Pakistan at present (also serving as Deputy Prime Minister)?
recs.facts: Ishaq Dar was appointed Foreign Minister in 2024 and also holds the office of Deputy Prime Minister.
recs.rel: Shah Mehmood Qureshi, named in the note, was Foreign Minister in 2008-2011 and 2018-2022.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 104) Who is the Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan at present?
recs.facts: Jameel Ahmad has been Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan since August 2022.
recs.rel: Dr Shahid Hafiz Kardar, named in the note, was Governor in 2010-2012.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 107) Who was elected President of Pakistan in 2008 and was elected to the office again in 2024?
recs.facts: Asif Ali Zardari became President in September 2008 and again in March 2024.
recs.rel: The notes call him the 15th President, but counts differ: he is usually the 11th (2008) and 14th (2024) President.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 108) How many seats does the Punjab Provincial Assembly have?
recs.facts: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats, the largest of the four provincial assemblies.
recs.rel: Sindh has 168 and Balochistan 65 seats.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 108) How many seats does the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly have at present?
recs.facts: After the 2018 merger of FATA the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly increased from 124 to 145 seats.
recs.rel: The note gives 124, which was the figure before the merger.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 110) How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan has five: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II.
recs.rel: The world has 14 peaks above 8000 m, and K2 at 8,611 m is the second highest.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 111) Who was the first Muslim to shoot an arrow in the way of Allah?
recs.facts: Hazrat Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA) was the first Muslim to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah.
recs.rel: The note names Zubair bin Awam (RA), who is known as the first to draw his sword in Islam.

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 112) In which year of Hijrah did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
recs.facts: Khalid bin Waleed (RA) embraced Islam in 8 AH, shortly before the Conquest of Makkah.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) gave him the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

recs.q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 113) Which is the smallest continent of the world?
recs.facts: Australia is the smallest of the seven continents, with an area of about 7.7 million sq km.
recs.rel: Asia is the largest continent and Africa the second largest.

recs.q: What is 90% of 90?
recs.rel: Taking 90% of a number 90 gives 81, which equals 9 x 9.

recs.q: Why do we boil milk?
recs.facts: Boiling heats milk enough to kill harmful germs and bacteria and makes it safe to drink and keep for longer.
recs.rel: Pasteurization, named after Louis Pasteur, is the industrial process of heating milk to destroy germs.

recs.q: Why do parents send their children to school?
recs.facts: Schools provide education, which develops knowledge, skills and character in children.
recs.rel: Education is a fundamental right of children under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is 2 + 2/2?
recs.facts: Division comes before addition (BODMAS), so 2/2 = 1 and 2 + 1 = 3.
recs.rel: BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

recs.q: Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 1200 / 1500 x 100 = 80%.
recs.rel: The absent students are 300, which is 20%.

recs.q: How many months of the year have 31 days?
recs.facts: The months are January, March, May, July, August, October and December, which makes 7.
recs.rel: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year).

recs.q: What is the antonym of wild?
recs.facts: Wild describes an animal or place not under human control. Tame means gentle and domesticated, its opposite.
recs.rel: Domestic is another common antonym of wild.

recs.q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
recs.facts: A triangular prism has two triangular bases and three rectangular side faces: 2 + 3 = 5 faces.
recs.rel: It also has 9 edges and 6 vertices. Candidates gave different answers (3, 4, 5, 6) because the paper did not name the prism type; the triangular prism is the usual one.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
recs.facts: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
recs.rel: The UN itself was founded in 1945.

recs.q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 120?
recs.facts: One tenth of 120 is 12, and a quarter of 12 is 3. Working in the other order gives 30 and then 3.
recs.rel: One quarter of one tenth equals 1/40, so the answer is 120/40.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.facts: Absent students = 500 - 340 = 160. Percentage absent = 160 / 500 x 100 = 32%.
recs.rel: The present students make up 68%, which is the number many people wrongly give.

recs.q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: If yesterday was Sunday, today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday. The day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
recs.rel: The day after tomorrow is always two days after today.

recs.q: If today is Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: Tomorrow is Saturday, so the day after tomorrow is Sunday.
recs.rel: The day after tomorrow means two days from today.

recs.q: What is the national drink (juice) of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sugarcane juice is regarded as the national juice or drink of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan is among the world's top producers of sugarcane.

recs.q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: If yesterday was Friday, today is Saturday. The day after tomorrow is Saturday plus 2 days, which is Monday.
recs.rel: The day after tomorrow is always three days after yesterday.

recs.q: In which year of the Hijri calendar was the Battle of Uhud fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (625 AD) near Mount Uhud, a year after Badr.
recs.rel: The archers left their post on the hill, which let the Quraish attack from behind.

recs.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
recs.rel: He was assassinated at Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

recs.q: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid (RA) married the Prophet (PBUH) about 15 years before the first revelation.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) did not marry again during her lifetime.

recs.q: If yesterday was Saturday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: If yesterday was Saturday, today is Sunday and tomorrow is Monday. The day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Candidates remembered Monday, which is tomorrow, not the day after tomorrow.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was a paternal uncle of the Prophet (PBUH). He was also close in age and a foster brother.
recs.rel: Hazrat Hamza was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.

recs.q: A pen is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage?
recs.rel: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
recs.facts: Jinnah formally joined the Muslim League in 1913, at the persuasion of Allama Iqbal, Wazir Hasan and others. He remained a member of the Indian National Congress at the same time.
recs.rel: He left the Congress in 1920 over differences with Gandhi's policies.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 90?
recs.rel: 1/10 of a number is the same as 10% of it.

recs.q: Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan was appointed the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan in 1947 and served until 1954.
recs.rel: He later served as a judge and President of the International Court of Justice.

recs.q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed?
recs.facts: Abu Jahl, a leader of the Quraysh, was killed in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH. He was struck down by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.
recs.rel: Abu Jahl's real name was Amr ibn Hisham.

recs.q: In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hamza (RA), uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH. He was killed by Wahshi, a slave of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.
recs.rel: Hazrat Hamza (RA) is known as Asadullah and Sayyid ush-Shuhada (Chief of the Martyrs).

recs.q: In which year was the OIC founded?
recs.facts: The OIC was founded in September 1969 at Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
recs.rel: Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: Which country lies to the east of Pakistan?
recs.facts: India shares Pakistan's long eastern border.
recs.rel: Pakistan borders Iran to the west, Afghanistan to the north-west, China to the north and India to the east.

recs.q: What is one third of one tenth of 90?
recs.facts: One tenth of 90 is 9, and one third of 9 is 3. The same value results from taking one tenth of one third of 90 or one third of 10% of 90.
recs.rel: Fractions of a number can be taken in any order because multiplication is commutative.

recs.q: What is 1/10 of 120?
recs.rel: One tenth is the same as 10 percent.

recs.q: What is the largest lake of the world by area?
recs.facts: The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 square km, is the largest inland body of water and is classed as a lake.
recs.rel: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest.

recs.q: What is the longest (largest) river of Asia?
recs.facts: The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest river in Asia.
recs.rel: It is the third longest river in the world.

recs.q: What is the length of the Indus River according to Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Pakistani textbooks give the length of the Indus as about 3,180 km.
recs.rel: Sources differ: some give about 2,880 km (Britannica) or 2,900 km.

recs.q: What is the national bird of the USA?
recs.facts: The bald eagle was chosen as the national bird and emblem of the United States.
recs.rel: It appears on the Great Seal of the United States adopted in 1782.

recs.q: A book is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit?
recs.facts: Profit = selling price - cost price = 40 - 30 = Rs 10.
recs.rel: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

recs.q: From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar?
recs.facts: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958 for about 3 million US dollars, and it joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958.
recs.rel: Prime Minister Feroz Khan Noon was in office at the time.

recs.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
recs.facts: The five pillars are Shahadah (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj.
recs.rel: Salah is the pillar performed five times daily.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
recs.facts: Pakistan became a member of NAM in 1979 at the Havana summit.
recs.rel: NAM was founded in 1961 at Belgrade.

recs.q: What is the length of the Canada-United States border?
recs.facts: The border is about 8,891 km (5,525 miles), the longest international land border in the world.
recs.rel: Note that 5,525 is the length in miles, not kilometres.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam become president of the All India Muslim League for the first time?
recs.facts: Jinnah was elected president of the Muslim League at the Lucknow session in December 1916. This was the session at which the Lucknow Pact was agreed.
recs.rel: He later served as president again in the 1920s and 1930s and led the League until Pakistan was created.

recs.q: Who among the following was a son-in-law of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
recs.rel: Hazrat Uthman (RA) was also a son-in-law, having married Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

recs.q: Who was the second Governor General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: After the death of Quaid-e-Azam in September 1948, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor General of Pakistan. He held the post until 1951.
recs.rel: Nazimuddin was followed as Governor General by Malik Ghulam Muhammad in 1951.

recs.q: Who wrote the Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha?
recs.facts: Waris Shah wrote the best known version of Heer in 1766.
recs.rel: Earlier versions of the story were written by Damodar Gulati.

recs.q: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
recs.facts: The permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China, each holding veto power.
recs.rel: Russia took the Soviet Union's seat in 1991 and China's seat passed from Taiwan to the PRC in 1971.

recs.q: In which battle did the Muslims dig a trench around Madinah?
recs.facts: The Muslims dug a trench around Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH on the advice of Salman Farsi. It stopped the Quraysh and their allies from attacking the city.
recs.rel: The Battle of Khandaq is also called the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab).

recs.q: Which is the highest pass of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Khunjerab Pass, at about 4,693 m on the Pakistan-China border, is the highest pass usually cited for Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sources differ because some lists name Mintaka Pass, also on the China border, as slightly higher; Khunjerab is the highest paved international border crossing.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of wild?
recs.facts: Wild means living or growing in nature, not controlled by humans, which is untamed. The other options are its opposites.
recs.rel: Its antonym is tame or domesticated.

recs.q: What was Fatima Jinnah's profession?
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah trained as a dentist and qualified from the University of Calcutta in 1923. She ran her own dental clinic in Bombay.
recs.rel: She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation) and contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.

recs.q: In which district is the Khewra salt mine located?
recs.facts: The Khewra salt mine is in Jhelum district, Punjab, in the Salt Range.
recs.rel: It is among the largest salt mines in the world.

recs.q: Who was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025, succeeding Ali Amin Gandapur?
recs.facts: Sohail Afridi of PTI was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025.
recs.rel: Since 11 October 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been under governor's rule (Governor Faisal Karim Kundi), so the province has no sitting Chief Minister at the moment. In 2021-22 the answer was Mahmood Khan.

recs.q: What is one tenth of 120?
recs.facts: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place left, so 120 becomes 12.
recs.rel: One tenth is the same as 10%.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan join SEATO?
recs.facts: Pakistan joined the South-East Asia Treaty Organization in 1954 when the Manila Pact was signed in September 1954.
recs.rel: Some sources give 1955 (ratification), and Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (CENTO) in 1955.

recs.q: In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty signed?
recs.facts: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Ayub Khan and Nehru, with the World Bank as a party.
recs.rel: It gave Pakistan the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India the eastern rivers.

recs.q: In which year was the Nehru Report presented?
recs.facts: The Nehru Report, drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru, was presented in 1928.
recs.rel: Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

recs.q: In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed?
recs.facts: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963.
recs.rel: It settled the border in the Karakoram region and led to the Karakoram Highway cooperation.

recs.q: What is the currency of Armenia?
recs.facts: Armenia uses the dram.
recs.rel: Georgia uses the lari and Azerbaijan the manat.

recs.q: What is the currency of Azerbaijan?
recs.facts: Azerbaijan uses the Azerbaijani manat.
recs.rel: Turkmenistan also uses a currency called the manat.

recs.q: What is the currency of Bangladesh?
recs.facts: Bangladesh uses the taka.
recs.rel: Pakistan, India and Nepal use rupees, while Bhutan uses the ngultrum.

recs.q: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab?
recs.facts: Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024.
recs.rel: She is the first woman Chief Minister of Punjab; her predecessor in 2021-22 was Usman Buzdar.

recs.q: Who was the first Governor General of independent India in 1947?
recs.facts: Lord Mountbatten became Governor General of the Dominion of India on 15 August 1947.
recs.rel: Sources differ because Warren Hastings and William Bentinck are also called the first Governor General in earlier British India, but for 1947 it is Mountbatten.

recs.q: Who wrote the novel Raja Gidh?
recs.facts: Bano Qudsia wrote Raja Gidh, a novel about the concept of haram and halal food and its effect on the mind.
recs.rel: She was married to the writer Ashfaq Ahmed.

recs.q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.
recs.rel: At about 4693 m it is among the highest paved border crossings in the world.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Safiyyah (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib was a sister of Hazrat Hamza and thus a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: She was the mother of Hazrat Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA).

recs.q: Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Isa (AS), who was born without a father by Allah's command.
recs.rel: Surah Maryam, the 19th surah of the Quran, is named after her.

recs.q: How many daughters did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) have?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters: Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA).
recs.rel: All of his daughters except Hazrat Fatima (RA) died during his lifetime.

recs.q: How many non-permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
recs.facts: The Council has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.
recs.rel: Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH (629 CE), before the conquest of Makkah. Some sources give 7 AH, so sources differ, but 8 AH is the common textbook answer.
recs.rel: He was later given the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

recs.q: On which prophet was the Injeel (Bible) revealed?
recs.facts: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (A.S). Zabur was given to Dawood, Taurat to Musa and the Quran to Muhammad.
recs.rel: Hazrat Isa (A.S) is also known as Ruhullah.

recs.q: On which river is Simly Dam (Simla Dam) built?
recs.facts: Simly Dam near Islamabad is an earthen dam on the Soan River. It supplies water to Islamabad.
recs.rel: It was completed in 1983; Khanpur Dam, by contrast, is on the Haro River.

recs.q: What is the value of sin 90 degrees?
recs.facts: On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1) and sine is the y-coordinate, which equals 1.
recs.rel: The value of cos 90 degrees is 0.

recs.q: On what date was the Nehru Report presented?
recs.facts: The Nehru Report was presented at the All Parties Conference at Lucknow on 28 August 1928.
recs.rel: Motilal Nehru headed the committee that prepared it.

recs.q: What is the largest district of Pakistan by area?
recs.facts: Chagai in Balochistan covers about 44,748 square km, the largest district of Pakistan by area.
recs.rel: Chagai is where Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998 (Ras Koh hills).

recs.q: Who was the first child to accept Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA), the cousin of the Prophet, accepted Islam as a boy of about 10 years old. He was raised in the Prophet's household.
recs.rel: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the first free adult man to accept Islam.

recs.q: Which is the biggest sea of the world by area?
recs.facts: The Philippine Sea covers about 5.7 million square km, the largest sea in the world. The South China Sea is about 3.5 million square km.
recs.rel: The Arabian Sea is the largest of the other options and lies next to Pakistan's coast.

recs.q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of a Jewish leader?
recs.facts: Hazrat Safiyya bint Huyayy was from the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir and married the Prophet (PBUH) after Khaybar.
recs.rel: She accepted Islam before the marriage.

recs.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of Pakistan in 1949.
recs.rel: Muhammad Munir succeeded him as Chief Justice in 1954.

recs.q: Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The lyrics of Qaumi Tarana were written by the poet Abul Asar Hafeez Jalandhari. It was officially adopted in 1954.
recs.rel: The music of the national anthem was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla.

recs.q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times: 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
recs.rel: Pakistan is the most successful team in Hockey World Cup history.

recs.q: In which battle was Hazrat Jafar Tayyar (RA) martyred?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) was one of the three commanders martyred in the Battle of Mutah in 8 AH. He is called Tayyar (the flyer) because he is said to have been given wings in Paradise.
recs.rel: The other two commanders at Mutah were Zaid bin Haritha and Abdullah bin Rawaha (RA).

recs.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit America?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the United States in May 1950, the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.
recs.rel: His visit came after he chose Washington over an invitation from Moscow.

recs.q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Khyber Pass is about 53 km long and has been an invasion and trade route for centuries.

recs.q: The Dorah Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: The Dorah Pass lies on the Chitral border and leads from Pakistan into Afghanistan (Badakhshan).
recs.rel: Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the Pakistani side of the Dorah Pass.

recs.q: Hazrat Hajra (Hajar) was the mother of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and gave birth to Hazrat Ismail (AS).
recs.rel: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates her search for water.

recs.q: How many original members did the United Nations have when it was founded in 1945?
recs.facts: The UN began in 1945 with 51 original member states (Poland signed later and is counted among them).
recs.rel: The UN now has 193 members.

recs.q: How many planets are there in the solar system?
recs.facts: There are eight planets since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
recs.rel: The planets in order from the Sun start with Mercury and end with Neptune.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
recs.facts: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim League reply to the Nehru Report.
recs.rel: They demanded safeguards for Muslims such as separate electorates and a federal system.

recs.q: Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan are famous players of which sport?
recs.facts: Both Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan of Pakistan were world champions in squash.
recs.rel: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times in a row and Jansher Khan won the World Open eight times.

recs.q: On which prophet was the Zabur (Psalms) revealed?
recs.facts: The Zabur was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (A.S).
recs.rel: Hazrat Sulaiman (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (A.S).

recs.q: What causes swine flu?
recs.facts: Swine flu is caused by influenza A viruses, most notably the H1N1 strain.
recs.rel: The 2009 H1N1 pandemic was declared by the WHO in June 2009.

recs.q: What is the capital of Austria?
recs.facts: Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria. Canberra is the capital of Australia, not Austria.
recs.rel: Austria and Australia are often confused because of their similar names.

recs.q: What is the capital of Bulgaria?
recs.facts: Sofia is the capital and largest city of Bulgaria.
recs.rel: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.

recs.q: What is the largest river of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan.
recs.rel: It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

recs.q: What is the length of the Suez Canal?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal is about 193 km, which is roughly 120 miles.
recs.rel: It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and opened in 1869.

recs.q: Which country is the largest producer of coffee in the world?
recs.facts: Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.
recs.rel: Vietnam is the second largest coffee producer.

recs.q: Which country is the largest producer of tea in the world?
recs.facts: China produces more tea than any other country, with India second.
recs.rel: Kenya and Sri Lanka are the next major producers.

recs.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by surface area?
recs.facts: Lake Superior in North America has a surface area of about 82,000 square kilometres, the largest among freshwater lakes.
recs.rel: Lake Baikal is the deepest freshwater lake and holds the most fresh water by volume.

recs.q: Which woman accepted Islam first?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khadija (R.A), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the first person and first woman to accept Islam.
recs.rel: Hazrat Sumayya was the first martyr of Islam.

recs.q: Who was the first president of the All India Muslim League?
recs.facts: Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was the first president of the All India Muslim League, founded in Dhaka in 1906.
recs.rel: The League was founded at Dhaka during the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

recs.q: Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'?
recs.facts: 'Friends Not Masters: A Political Autobiography' was written by Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan. It was published in 1967.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan was Pakistan's second President and ruled from 1958 to 1969.

recs.q: Zakat is which pillar of Islam?
recs.facts: The five pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj, so Zakat is third.
recs.rel: Candidates wrote 4, but in the standard order Zakat comes third.

recs.q: A bat cannot see; a snake cannot what?
recs.facts: Snakes have no external ears and cannot hear airborne sound well; they sense ground vibrations instead.
recs.rel: Bats find their way by echolocation using high-pitched sounds.

recs.q: What type of government was set up by the 1962 constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1962 constitution concentrated executive power in the President, so it created a presidential form of government.
recs.rel: The 1973 constitution replaced it with a parliamentary system.

recs.q: How many member states does the European Union (EU) have?
recs.facts: The EU has 27 member states, and the number has not changed since the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020.
recs.rel: Before Brexit the EU had 28 members; Croatia was the last to join, in 2013.

recs.q: In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located?
recs.facts: The Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir is buried in Lahore, in the Dharampura area.
recs.rel: Mian Mir is said to have laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple at Amritsar at the invitation of Guru Arjan.

recs.q: In which month did the 1965 Pakistan-India war take place and how long did it last?
recs.facts: The war began on 6 September 1965 when India crossed the international border at Lahore, and ended with a ceasefire on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days.
recs.rel: Pakistan celebrates 6 September every year as Defence Day.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress?
recs.facts: Jinnah left Congress in 1920 over the Nagpur session and its non-cooperation policy.
recs.rel: He joined the Muslim League in 1913.

recs.q: In which year was the Tashkent Agreement signed?
recs.facts: The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed on 10 January 1966 under Soviet mediation.
recs.rel: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri.

recs.q: Oil wrestling is the national sport of which country?
recs.facts: Oil wrestling (Yagli Gures) is the national sport of Turkey.
recs.rel: The Kirkpinar festival in Edirne, Turkey, is the oldest wrestling competition in the world.

recs.q: On which river is Warsak Dam built?
recs.facts: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar.
recs.rel: Warsak Dam was built in the 1950s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.

recs.q: Which is the fifth pillar of Islam?
recs.facts: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is fifth.
recs.rel: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are able to afford it.

recs.q: What is the capital of Azad Kashmir?
recs.facts: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
recs.rel: Muzaffarabad lies at the confluence of the Jhelum and Neelum rivers.

recs.q: What is the capital of Belarus?
recs.facts: Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus.
recs.rel: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe.

recs.q: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan?
recs.facts: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: Gilgit-Baltistan is home to K2, the second highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: What is the capital of Ukraine?
recs.facts: Kyiv (also spelled Kiev) is the capital of Ukraine.
recs.rel: Kyiv sits on the Dnieper river.

recs.q: What is the currency of Egypt?
recs.facts: Egypt uses the Egyptian pound.
recs.rel: Egypt controls the Suez Canal.

recs.q: What is the currency of Indonesia?
recs.facts: Indonesia uses the rupiah.
recs.rel: Malaysia uses the ringgit and Thailand the baht.

recs.q: On what date was the Tashkent Agreement signed?
recs.facts: India and Pakistan signed the Tashkent Declaration on 10 January 1966, ending the 1965 war.
recs.rel: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, who died in Tashkent the next day.

recs.q: What is the largest lake of Europe?
recs.facts: Lake Ladoga in Russia, about 17,700 square km, is the largest lake entirely within Europe.
recs.rel: The Caspian Sea is larger but is usually not counted as a European lake.

recs.q: What is the largest river of Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Helmand River, about 1,150 km, is the longest river wholly within Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border and is not entirely within Afghanistan.

recs.q: What is the length of the Pakistan-India border (including the Line of Control and Working Boundary)?
recs.facts: The combined length of the international boundary, Working Boundary and Line of Control is about 3,323 km.
recs.rel: The Radcliffe Line of 1947 defined the border between the two countries.

recs.q: What is the national bird of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Shaheen (falcon) is the national symbol of Pakistan's air force and a popular emblem, but not the national bird.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of attire?
recs.facts: Attire means clothes or dress, so clothing is the synonym.
recs.rel: Another synonym of attire is apparel.

recs.q: What is the title of Liaqat Ali Khan?
recs.facts: Liaqat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was given the title Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
recs.rel: He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

recs.q: In which year was SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) founded?
recs.facts: SAARC was founded at a summit in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. The idea was proposed by Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman.
recs.rel: SAARC has its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.

recs.q: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam located (on the Indus, in Mianwali district)?
recs.facts: Kalabagh is in Mianwali district of Punjab, on the Indus near the boundary with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: The dam has never been built because of political opposition from some provinces.

recs.q: Which country awards the Nobel Prizes (apart from the Peace Prize)?
recs.facts: The Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine and literature are awarded in Sweden, in line with Alfred Nobel's will.
recs.rel: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

recs.q: Which of the following countries is NOT a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
recs.facts: The SCO has ten full members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus. Turkey is only a dialogue partner.
recs.rel: Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024; Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.

recs.q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by population?
recs.facts: Punjab has more than half of Pakistan's population (about 127 million in the 2023 census).
recs.rel: Sindh is the second most populous province.

recs.q: Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar?
recs.facts: The Islamic year has twelve months and Dhul Hijjah is the twelfth and last.
recs.rel: Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah and Muharram is the first month.

recs.q: Which Sahabi married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (R.A) married Ruqayyah first and, after her death, Umm Kulthum.
recs.rel: He is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

recs.q: Which was the first mosque built by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the first mosque of Islam in Madina?
recs.facts: Masjid Quba was built by the Prophet (PBUH) on his arrival near Madina during the Hijrah.
recs.rel: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built soon afterwards in Madina.

recs.q: Who is the current Chairman of NAB (National Accountability Bureau)?
recs.facts: Lt Gen (retd) Nazir Ahmad became NAB chairman in 2023 and received a three-year extension from March 2026.
recs.rel: Earlier chairmen were Javed Iqbal (2017-22) and Aftab Sultan (2022-23).

recs.q: Who is the President of Turkey?
recs.facts: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been President of Turkey since 2014 and was re-elected in 2023.
recs.rel: The capital of Turkey is Ankara.

recs.q: Who was the brother of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA)?
recs.facts: Walid bin Walid (RA) was the brother of Khalid bin Waleed (RA) and accepted Islam before him.
recs.rel: Their father Waleed bin Mughirah was a leader of the Banu Makhzum of Quraish.

recs.q: Who wrote the Punjabi qissa (folk romance) Sohni Mahiwal?
recs.facts: The best-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal is attributed to Fazal Shah (Sayyid Fazal Shah). Waris Shah is known for Heer Ranjha.
recs.rel: Sources differ on tellers of this tale, but Fazal Shah is the usual textbook answer.

recs.q: A car travels at 60 km/h and a train at twice that speed (120 km/h). How far does the train travel in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: Which sea lies between Greece and Italy?
recs.facts: The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.
recs.rel: The Aegean Sea lies east of Greece, between Greece and Turkey.

recs.q: What is one third of 90?
recs.facts: 90 divided by 3 is 30.
recs.rel: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

recs.q: Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
recs.facts: Russia is the largest country and Canada, with about 9.98 million square km, is second.
recs.rel: China and the United States follow closely as third and fourth.

recs.q: According to the 1962 constitution, how was the President of Pakistan elected?
opts: By an Electoral College of Basic Democrats
By the Governors of the provinces
recs.facts: The 1962 constitution introduced indirect election of the President by an Electoral College made up of the elected Basic Democrats.
recs.rel: The Electoral College initially had 80,000 members, later raised to 120,000 (equally from East and West Pakistan).

recs.q: Against whom was the Battle of Khyber fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought by the Muslims against the Jewish tribes living in the fortresses of Khyber.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali conquered the fort of Qamus in this battle.

recs.q: Al Jazeera TV channel belongs to which country?
recs.facts: Al Jazeera is an Arabic news channel founded in 1996 and funded by the Qatari state, based in Doha.
recs.rel: Some candidates thought it was Egyptian, but it is Qatari.

recs.q: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of whom?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayesha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).
recs.rel: Her mother was Umm Ruman.

recs.q: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of whom?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA).
recs.rel: The first written compilation of the Quran was kept with her during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA) and later.

recs.q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (rightly guided caliphs) are there?
recs.facts: They are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).
recs.rel: Their combined rule lasted about 30 years (632 to 661 AD).

recs.q: How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) have?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (AS) and Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was born to Hazrat Hajra and Hazrat Ishaq (AS) to Hazrat Sarah.

recs.q: In which Ghazwa were the blessed teeth of the Prophet (PBUH) martyred?
recs.facts: The Prophet's (PBUH) front tooth was broken and he was wounded in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
recs.rel: The Battle of Uhud took place near Mount Uhud close to Madinah.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed?
recs.facts: The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraysh in Dhul Qadah 6 AH (628 CE).
recs.rel: The Quran calls it a clear victory (Fath-e-Mubin) in Surah Al-Fath.

recs.q: In which province is Khanpur Dam located?
recs.facts: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Khanpur in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

recs.q: In which year did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
recs.facts: The Hijrah took place in 622 AD, the 13th year of prophethood.
recs.rel: The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan join the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
recs.facts: Pakistan was a founding member of the OIC, which was formed in 1969.
recs.rel: The OIC was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.
recs.rel: He is buried at Mazar-e-Quaid in Karachi.

recs.q: Kaleemullah is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Kaleemullah means the one who spoke with Allah, the title of Hazrat Musa (A.S).
recs.rel: The Torah (Taurat) was revealed to Hazrat Musa (A.S).

recs.q: Which organism causes malaria?
recs.facts: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, spread to humans by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
recs.rel: The deadliest malaria parasite is Plasmodium falciparum.

recs.q: What is the area of Punjab (Pakistan) in square kilometres?
recs.facts: Punjab covers about 205,344 square kilometres.
recs.rel: Punjab is the second largest province by area but the largest by population.

recs.q: What is the capital of Chile?
recs.facts: Santiago is the capital of Chile.
recs.rel: Valparaiso, where the national congress sits, is a major port city but not the capital.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word alter?
recs.facts: To alter means to change something or make it different.
recs.rel: The related noun is alteration, meaning a change.

recs.q: What is the currency of Cuba?
recs.facts: Cuba uses the Cuban peso (CUP).
recs.rel: Cuba formerly had a second currency, the convertible peso (CUC), which was abolished in 2021.

recs.q: What is the currency of Russia?
recs.facts: Russia uses the ruble.
recs.rel: Ukraine uses the hryvnia and Kazakhstan the tenge.

recs.q: On what date did the War of Independence of the Subcontinent begin?
recs.facts: The 1857 War of Independence began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
recs.rel: The British call it the Sepoy Mutiny.

recs.q: On what date did the Chauri Chaura incident happen?
recs.facts: A mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh on 4 February 1922.
recs.rel: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after this incident.

recs.q: Which is the highest plateau in the world?
recs.facts: The Tibetan Plateau averages over 4,500 m above sea level and is called the Roof of the World.
recs.rel: The Pamir region is also known as the Roof of the World.

recs.q: What is the maximum length of a cricket bat under the laws of cricket?
recs.facts: The Laws of Cricket limit a bat to 38 inches (96.52 cm) in length.
recs.rel: The maximum width of the blade is 4.25 inches.

recs.q: What is the length of the coastline of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline is officially about 1,046 km.
recs.rel: It is shared between Sindh (about 270 km) and Balochistan (about 770 km).

recs.q: What is the national tree of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is the national tree of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Its name comes from Sanskrit and means timber of the gods.

recs.q: What is the relation of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) with Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
recs.facts: Both were sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), so they were brothers (half-brothers, by different mothers).
recs.rel: Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra and Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Sarah.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Abdul Muttalib with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Abdul Muttalib was the father of Abdullah, the Prophet's father, so he was the paternal grandfather. He looked after the Prophet after the death of his mother Hazrat Amina.
recs.rel: Abdul Muttalib was the chief of Quraysh and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.

recs.q: What is the range of the Pakistani surface-to-surface missile Ababeel?
recs.facts: Ababeel is a medium-range ballistic missile with a range of 2,200 km, as announced by ISPR after its first test.
recs.rel: Ababeel is stated to have MIRV (multiple warhead) capability and was first tested in January 2017.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of evident?
recs.facts: Evident means clearly seen or understood, which is obvious.
recs.rel: Another synonym is apparent.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of prevalent?
recs.facts: Prevalent means common or existing widely at a given time, which is widespread.
recs.rel: Its opposite is rare or uncommon.

recs.q: What is the total number of seats of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab?
recs.facts: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 reserved for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
recs.rel: The National Assembly has 336 seats, of which Punjab has 141 general seats.

recs.q: Where does the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961 belong, that is, which country was invaded?
recs.facts: The Bay of Pigs (Bahia de Cochinos) is on the southern coast of Cuba. In April 1961 CIA-backed Cuban exiles landed there to overthrow Fidel Castro and failed.
recs.rel: The failed invasion took place during the presidency of John F. Kennedy and pushed Cuba closer to the Soviet Union.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval in London on 18 June 2017 under captain Sarfraz Ahmed.
recs.rel: Pakistan has won the Champions Trophy only once; India won the 2025 edition.

recs.q: In which year did Swat merge fully into Pakistan?
recs.facts: Swat acceded to Pakistan in 1947 but remained a princely state. It was merged fully on 28 July 1969, when the state was abolished.
recs.rel: Swat is now part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

recs.q: In which year was the first constitution of Pakistan enforced?
recs.facts: The first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.
recs.rel: 23 March was celebrated as Republic Day until the 1962 constitution replaced it.

recs.q: In which province is Manchar Lake located?
recs.facts: Manchar Lake is in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus.
recs.rel: It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.

recs.q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque of Pakistan located?
recs.facts: The Shah Jahan Mosque was built in Thatta, Sindh, in the 17th century.
recs.rel: It is famous for its blue tile work and for having no minarets.

recs.q: Which country was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
recs.facts: Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17, signing its deal around 2015 and receiving aircraft from 2018.
recs.rel: The JF-17 is jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.

recs.q: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
recs.facts: Russia covers about 17.1 million square km, more than any other country.
recs.rel: Canada is the second largest country by area.

recs.q: Which is the month of Allah (Shahrullah) in the Islamic calendar?
recs.facts: Ramadan is commonly called the month of Allah in Pakistani textbooks, because fasting is observed in it.
recs.rel: Some sources also apply the title Shahrullah to Muharram or Rajab, so sources differ.

recs.q: Which is the outermost planet of the solar system?
recs.facts: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
recs.rel: Pluto was considered the ninth planet until 2006.

recs.q: Which is the smallest continent?
recs.facts: Australia (Oceania) has an area of about 7.7 million square km, the smallest of the continents.
recs.rel: Australia is the only continent that is also a single country.

recs.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a fish and stayed in its belly?
recs.facts: Hazrat Younus (A.S) was swallowed by a large fish and prayed to Allah from within its belly.
recs.rel: He is also called Dhun-Nun and Surah Younus is named after him.

recs.q: Who was the first man to embrace Islam?
recs.facts: Among adult free men, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first to accept Islam.
recs.rel: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Ali (RA) the first child to accept Islam.

recs.q: Who inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan in Karachi on 1 July 1948.
recs.rel: The first governor of the State Bank was Zahid Hussain.

recs.q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh?
recs.facts: Syed Murad Ali Shah of the Pakistan Peoples Party has been Chief Minister of Sindh since 2016 and won a third consecutive term in 2024.
recs.rel: He succeeded Qaim Ali Shah, who had held the post from 2008 to 2016.

recs.q: Who is the national poet of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet of Pakistan, called Shair-e-Mashriq.
recs.rel: His birthday, 9 November, is observed as Iqbal Day.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest?
recs.facts: Nazir Sabir reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1999 as the first Pakistani to do so.
recs.rel: Samina Baig became the first Pakistani woman to climb Everest in 2013.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Das Kapital?
recs.facts: Das Kapital, a critique of capitalism, was written by the German thinker Karl Marx. The first volume appeared in 1867.
recs.rel: Friedrich Engels edited and published the second and third volumes after Marx died.

recs.q: Who wrote The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal wrote this book, which is based on his lectures delivered in 1928-29.
recs.rel: It was first published in 1930 and expanded in 1934.

recs.q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you (taking me as male)?
recs.facts: My brother's sister is my sister, so your mother is my sister. I am therefore your mother's brother, that is your maternal uncle.
recs.rel: A mother's brother is called mamu in Urdu, and a father's brother is called chacha.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 120?
recs.rel: Taking 1/3 of 1/10 is the same as taking 1/30 of the number.

recs.q: Who was the commander of the Muslim army in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk?
recs.facts: The Ghazwa of Tabuk (9 AH) was a campaign in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself led the Muslim army of about 30,000. A Ghazwa is by definition a battle in which the Prophet personally took part.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) was left in charge of Madina during the Tabuk expedition.

recs.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Manchar Lake in Sindh is generally regarded as Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.
recs.rel: Keenjhar Lake near Thatta is the second largest and a major drinking water source for Karachi.

recs.q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed?
recs.facts: The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916. It was an agreement in which the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam was the main architect of the pact and was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity.

recs.q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 1300 / 1500 x 100 = 86.67%.
recs.rel: The absent students are 200, which is 13.33%.

recs.q: What is one tenth of 90?
recs.facts: 90 divided by 10 is 9.
recs.rel: One tenth of a number is the same as 10% of it.

recs.q: Abdul Qadir was a famous player of which sport?
recs.facts: Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler famous for his googly and wrist-spin.
recs.rel: Abdul Qadir played 67 Tests for Pakistan and died in 2019.

recs.q: The Khilafat Movement started after which event?
recs.facts: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire in World War I, which threatened the Caliphate.
recs.rel: Its leaders included Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali.

recs.q: Asadullah (Lion of Allah) is the title of which Sahabi?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was given the title Asadullah for his bravery. Hazrat Hamza is also called Asadullah.
recs.rel: Khalid bin Waleed is known as Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

recs.q: Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which place?
recs.facts: The Bolan Pass is a natural route in Balochistan linking Quetta with the plains of Sibi and Dadhar.
recs.rel: Khojak Pass, not Bolan, links Quetta with Chaman and Afghanistan.

recs.q: From which institution did Quaid-e-Azam obtain his law degree?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Jinnah studied at Lincoln's Inn in London and was called to the bar in 1896.
recs.rel: He was the youngest Indian to be called to the bar at that time.

recs.q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of ghusl are there (Hanafi fiqh)?
recs.facts: The three faraiz of ghusl are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole body.
recs.rel: The faraiz of wudu are four in Hanafi fiqh.

recs.q: How many Makki surahs are there in the Quran?
recs.facts: Commonly 86 surahs are counted as Makki (revealed before the Hijrah) and 28 as Madani.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly on the exact numbers, but 86 and 28 are the figures most Pakistani textbooks give.

recs.q: How many seats of the National Assembly of Pakistan are reserved for women?
recs.facts: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves 60 seats for women, filled by proportional representation.
recs.rel: Another 10 seats are reserved for non-Muslims.

recs.q: In which city of India is Jallianwala Bagh located?
recs.facts: Jallianwala Bagh is a public garden in Amritsar, Punjab, India. British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd there on 13 April 1919.
recs.rel: The massacre took place on Baisakhi day in 1919.

recs.q: In which country were the Olympic Games postponed from 2020 and held in 2021 hosted?
recs.facts: The Tokyo Olympics, scheduled for 2020, were postponed because of Covid-19 and held in Japan in July-August 2021.
recs.rel: The next Summer Olympics after Tokyo were held in Paris in 2024.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
recs.facts: The martyrdom of Hazrat Hussain (RA) at Karbala took place on 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE).
recs.rel: Yazid ibn Muawiya was the Umayyad ruler at that time.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).
recs.rel: The conquest followed the Quraysh breaking the Treaty of Hudaibiya.

recs.q: In which language did Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai write poetry?
recs.facts: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai (1689-1752) is the great Sufi poet of the Sindhi language.
recs.rel: His famous collection of poetry is called Shah Jo Risalo.

recs.q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Azha celebrated?
recs.facts: Eid ul Azha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
recs.rel: Eid ul Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.

recs.q: In which Islamic month was the Quran first revealed?
recs.facts: The Quran began to be revealed in the month of Ramadan, on Laylat ul Qadr, in the cave of Hira.
recs.rel: The first revealed verses are the opening of Surah Al-Alaq.

recs.q: In which province is Keenjhar Lake located?
recs.facts: Keenjhar Lake is near Thatta in Sindh.
recs.rel: Keenjhar is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan and a main water source for Karachi.

recs.q: In which year did India carry out its first nuclear test?
recs.facts: India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran in May 1974.
recs.rel: India carried out further tests, Pokhran-II, in May 1998.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Khyber (Khaybar) fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khaybar was fought in 7 AH (628 AD) against the Jewish fortresses of Khaybar.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus in this battle.

recs.q: Riyadh is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.
recs.rel: Saudi Arabia hosts the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah.

recs.q: Safiullah is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Safiullah means the chosen one of Allah and is the title of Hazrat Adam (A.S).
recs.rel: Other titles: Khalilullah for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Ruhullah for Isa (A.S).

recs.q: Tirana is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Tirana is the capital and largest city of Albania in the Balkans.
recs.rel: Albania's neighbours include Greece, North Macedonia, Kosovo and Montenegro.

recs.q: Tripoli is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Tripoli is the capital of Libya on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.
recs.rel: There is also a city named Tripoli in Lebanon, but it is not the capital.

recs.q: Turkey is surrounded by the Aegean Sea, the Black Sea and which other sea?
recs.facts: Turkey has the Black Sea to the north, the Aegean to the west and the Mediterranean to the south.
recs.rel: The Sea of Marmara lies entirely within Turkey and links the Black and Aegean Seas.

recs.q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) does Hajj have according to the Hanafi school?
recs.facts: The three faraiz are Ihram, standing at Arafat (Wuquf) and Tawaf-e-Ziyarat.
recs.rel: Schools of thought differ slightly in counting Hajj faraiz, but the Hanafi count of three is common in Pakistani textbooks.

recs.q: What does PEMRA stand for?
opts: Pakistan Education and Media Regulatory Authority
recs.facts: PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, which regulates TV and radio broadcasting.
recs.rel: PEMRA was established in 2002.

recs.q: What does POF stand for?
recs.facts: POF stands for Pakistan Ordnance Factories, which make arms and ammunition.
recs.rel: POF is headquartered at Wah Cantt.

recs.q: What is observed on 8 March every year?
recs.facts: 8 March is International Women's Day, celebrating women's achievements and rights.
recs.rel: International Labour Day is on 1 May.

recs.q: What is Pakistan's rank in the world by population (2026)?
recs.facts: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, after India, China, the United States and Indonesia.
recs.rel: Pakistan's population is estimated at over 250 million and may overtake Indonesia by around 2050.

recs.q: What is sin X divided by cos X equal to?
recs.facts: By definition, tan X equals sin X over cos X.
recs.rel: The reciprocal, cos X over sin X, is cot X.

recs.q: What is the product of the three cube roots of unity?
recs.facts: The cube roots of unity are 1, w and w squared, and w cubed equals 1. Their product is 1 x w x w squared = w cubed = 1.
recs.rel: The sum of the three cube roots of unity is 0.

recs.q: What is the currency of Turkey?
recs.facts: Turkey uses the Turkish lira.
recs.rel: Istanbul, the largest Turkish city, is not the capital; Ankara is.

recs.q: When did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah present his Fourteen Points?
recs.facts: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points at Delhi in March 1929, answering the Nehru Report.
recs.rel: The Fourteen Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, such as separate electorates and one third seats in the central legislature.

recs.q: Which is the hottest city of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Jacobabad in Sindh regularly records the highest temperatures in Pakistan, often over 50 degrees Celsius.
recs.rel: Jacobabad is among the hottest inhabited places on Earth.

recs.q: What is the integration of 1 with respect to x?
recs.facts: The derivative of x is 1, so the integral of 1 dx is x + C.
recs.rel: The constant C is the constant of integration.

recs.q: Which is the largest airport of Pakistan by area?
recs.facts: Islamabad International Airport opened in 2018 and is the largest in Pakistan by area (about 19 square km).
recs.rel: Karachi Jinnah International is the busiest airport, which is why candidates answered Karachi; sources can differ on what largest means.

recs.q: What is the largest city of Punjab by population?
recs.facts: Lahore is the capital of Punjab and its largest city.
recs.rel: Faisalabad is the second largest city of Punjab.

recs.q: What is the second pillar of Islam?
recs.facts: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Salah is the second.
recs.rel: Salah was made obligatory five times a day during the Night Journey (Miraj).

recs.q: The Treaty of Versailles, which ended World War I with Germany, was signed in which year?
recs.facts: The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919 at the Palace of Versailles in France.
recs.rel: It imposed heavy reparations on Germany and created the League of Nations.

recs.q: What was the relation of Abu Talib with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Abu Talib was the son of Abdul Muttalib and a brother of the Prophet's father Abdullah. He raised the Prophet after the death of Abdul Muttalib.
recs.rel: Abu Talib was the father of Hazrat Ali (RA) and protected the Prophet during the early years in Makkah.

recs.q: What was the old (previous) name of Makkah mentioned in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Holy Quran (Surah Al-Imran, verse 96) calls the place of the first house of worship Bakkah, which is an old name of Makkah. It was also known as Umm al-Qura.
recs.rel: Yathrib was the old name of Madina, not Makkah.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC T20 World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the final at Lord's in 2009 under captain Younis Khan. It is their only T20 World Cup title.
recs.rel: Pakistan were runners-up in 2007 and 2022; India won the 2024 and 2026 editions.

recs.q: In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to Madina take place, marking the start of the Hijri calendar?
recs.facts: The Prophet migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which is 1 AH. The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from this event.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar and its first month is Muharram.

recs.q: Between which two parties was the Lucknow Pact signed?
opts: Muslim League and the British Government
Muslim League and the Khaksar movement
recs.facts: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League. Both parties agreed to a joint demand for self-government.
recs.rel: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Quaid-e-Azam were the main leaders involved in making the pact.

recs.q: In which city was the OIC established at the first Islamic summit in 1969?
recs.facts: The first Islamic summit, which created the OIC, was held at Rabat in Morocco in 1969. Jeddah is the permanent headquarters of the OIC, not the place of its founding.
recs.rel: The Islamic Summit held in Lahore in 1974 was the second summit of the OIC.

recs.q: In which country is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj?
recs.facts: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia.
recs.rel: Pilgrims stone the Jamarat (pillars symbolising Satan) at Mina during Hajj.

recs.q: In which province is Ranikot (Rani Fort) located?
recs.facts: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills near Sann in Jamshoro district, Sindh.
recs.rel: It is often called the Great Wall of Sindh because of its long walls.

recs.q: Where is the Pakistan Navy headquarters?
recs.facts: Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.
recs.rel: The main naval base and Fleet Command are at Karachi.

recs.q: Where is the shrine of Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar?
recs.facts: Baba Farid Ganj Shakar is buried in Pakpattan, Punjab.
recs.rel: He was a major Chishti Sufi saint of the 12th and 13th centuries.

recs.q: Which country hosted the first Football World Cup in 1930?
recs.facts: The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay, which also won it.
recs.rel: Uruguay beat Argentina 4-2 in the final.

recs.q: Which is the biggest province of Pakistan by area?
recs.facts: Balochistan covers about 347,000 square km, roughly 44 percent of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Punjab is the largest province by population.

recs.q: Which SAARC country has the highest literacy rate?
recs.facts: The Maldives has a literacy rate of about 98 to 99 percent, the highest among SAARC countries, with Sri Lanka close behind.
recs.rel: Afghanistan and Pakistan are among the lowest in SAARC for literacy.

recs.q: Which Sahabi served the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for ten years?
recs.facts: Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet as a servant at Madina as a boy and served him for about ten years.
recs.rel: He narrated over 2,000 hadiths.

recs.q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The national flag was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kedwaii on the basis of the Muslim League flag. The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947.
recs.rel: The green part of the flag stands for the Muslim majority and the white strip for minorities.

recs.q: Who gave the name Pakistan?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
recs.rel: Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

recs.q: Who is the President of Iran?
recs.facts: Masoud Pezeshkian won the 2024 snap election and took office in July 2024.
recs.rel: His predecessor Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash in May 2024.

recs.q: Who is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
recs.facts: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas was only 20 when he died in 1971 stopping a traitor pilot, and got the award.
recs.rel: Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

recs.q: Who led the Quit India Movement of 1942?
recs.facts: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call Do or Die.
recs.rel: The Muslim League opposed the movement.

recs.q: Who rebuilt the Holy Kaaba with his son?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) rebuilt the Kaaba with his son Hazrat Ismail (AS).
recs.rel: The Quraysh also rebuilt it before the Prophet's prophethood, and the Prophet (PBUH) placed the Black Stone.

recs.q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: General Sir Frank Messervy was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army from August 1947 to February 1948.
recs.rel: Douglas Gracey succeeded him, and Ayub Khan was the first native Pakistani Commander-in-Chief in 1951.

recs.q: Who was the world's first woman Prime Minister?
recs.facts: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka became the world's first woman Prime Minister in 1960.
recs.rel: Indira Gandhi became India's Prime Minister in 1966.

recs.q: Who was the President of the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.
recs.rel: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan later served as its Speaker.

recs.q: Which team won the cricket World Cup in 1999?
recs.facts: Australia beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the 1999 final at Lord's.
recs.rel: Pakistan was the runner-up in 1999 and champion in 1992.

recs.q: A man going towards north turns left after some time, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing?
recs.facts: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.
recs.rel: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

recs.q: What is one third of 10% of 120?
recs.facts: 10% of 120 is 12, and one third of 12 is 4.
recs.rel: One third of one tenth equals 1/30, so the answer is 120/30.

recs.q: What is 90% of 70?
recs.rel: To find 90% of a number, subtract one tenth of it from the number.

recs.q: What is the derivative of a constant?
recs.facts: A constant does not change as x changes, so its rate of change is zero.
recs.rel: The derivative of x with respect to x is 1.

recs.q: Which one is different from the others: monkey, panda, baboon, chimpanzee?
recs.facts: Monkey, baboon and chimpanzee are primates, while the panda is a bear.
recs.rel: Giant pandas feed mainly on bamboo.

recs.q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution declared the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, ending its dominion status.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, now celebrated as Pakistan Day.

recs.q: Under the 1956 Constitution, the President of Pakistan was elected by:
opts: An electoral college of members of the National and Provincial Assemblies
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution provided for the President to be elected by the members of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza became the first President under this Constitution.

recs.q: In whose house in Madinah did the camel of the Prophet (PBUH) stop after the Hijrat?
recs.facts: The Prophet's camel Qaswa knelt near the house of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (Khalid bin Zayd), and he stayed there until his own quarters and mosque were built.
recs.rel: Abu Ayyub Ansari died during the Muslim siege of Constantinople and is buried near its walls.

recs.q: In which battle was the tooth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) broken?
recs.facts: The Prophet's lower front tooth was broken and he was wounded on the face during the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH, after the archers left their post.
recs.rel: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Madinah in March 625 CE.

recs.q: In which year did the United Nations come into being?
recs.facts: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the main founding members.
recs.rel: United Nations Day is observed every year on 24 October.

recs.q: With which wife of the Prophet (PBUH) was the compiled copy of the Quran kept after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had it collected?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Quran compiled in book form; it passed to Hazrat Umar (RA) and then was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA), the Prophet's wife. Hazrat Usman (RA) later borrowed it to prepare copies.
recs.rel: Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) led the compilation team under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

recs.q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record of the fastest century in ODIs (37 balls, 1996)?
recs.facts: New Zealand's Corey Anderson scored a century off 36 balls against the West Indies in January 2014 and broke Afridi's 17-year-old record.
recs.rel: AB de Villiers later broke Anderson's record with a 31-ball century against the West Indies in January 2015, and it still stands.

recs.q: A train is moving at 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
recs.facts: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 90 x 1/5 = 18 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.

recs.q: In which city is the Wazir Khan Mosque located?
recs.facts: The Wazir Khan Mosque stands in the walled city of Lahore. It was built in 1634-35 in the Mughal era.
recs.rel: It is famous for its Kashi tile work.

recs.q: On which river is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built?
recs.facts: The Diamer Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River in Gilgit-Baltistan, near Chilas.
recs.rel: Tarbela Dam is also on the Indus River.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) with Hazrat Abdul Muttalib?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, and Abu Talib was a son of Abdul Muttalib. So Hazrat Ali was his grandson.
recs.rel: Abdul Muttalib was also the grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), which made the two cousins.

recs.q: Which pass connects Pakistan with China?
recs.facts: The Khunjerab Pass in the Karakoram links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang in China.
recs.rel: At about 4,693 m it is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

recs.q: With the help of which country was Pakistan Steel Mills built?
recs.facts: Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical and financial assistance in the 1970s.
recs.rel: Its foundation stone was laid in 1973 and production began in 1981.

recs.q: In which district is Khanpur Dam located?
recs.facts: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River near Khanpur town in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and was completed in 1983.

recs.q: In which year was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, taken as 570 AD in Pakistani textbooks.
recs.rel: Some sources give 571 AD.

recs.q: After how many years of independence did Pakistan get its first constitution?
