recs.facts: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, nearly 9 years later.
recs.rel: 23 March was celebrated as Republic Day, and the 1956 constitution was abrogated in 1958 by Ayub Khan.

recs.q: At what age (approximately) did the last revelation descend upon Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Revelation began when the Prophet (PBUH) was 40 and continued for about 23 years, so the last revelation came at about age 63.
recs.rel: Most scholars say the last verses were revealed a few weeks before his death at 63.

recs.q: Boris Johnson served as Prime Minister (2019-2022) of which country?
recs.facts: Boris Johnson led the Conservative Party and was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from July 2019 to September 2022.
recs.rel: He is no longer in office, having resigned in 2022 and been followed by Liz Truss.

recs.q: For what purpose was the Khilafat Movement started?
recs.facts: Indian Muslims started it to save the Ottoman Caliph and the Ottoman Empire after World War I.
recs.rel: It began in 1919 and ended after Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.

recs.q: Harappa, a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization, was situated on the bank of which river?
recs.facts: Harappa lies in Sahiwal district of Punjab beside the (now partly dried) bed of the River Ravi.
recs.rel: Mohenjo-daro, the other great Indus city, stood on the bank of the Indus in Sindh.

recs.q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) were killed in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: About 70 Quraish fighters were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr.
recs.rel: Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr.

recs.q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu are there (Hanafi fiqh)?
recs.facts: The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to and including the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing the feet up to the ankles.
recs.rel: The faraiz of ghusl are three.

recs.q: How many rukus are there in the Holy Quran (Pakistani edition)?
recs.facts: Pakistani printed copies of the Quran are divided into 540 rukus, marked by the letter Ain in the margin.
recs.rel: Counts differ in other editions (for example 558 in Arabic prints).

recs.q: In which battle did Allah help the Muslims with angels?
recs.facts: The Quran (Surah Al-Imran and Al-Anfal) says Allah sent angels to help the Muslims at Badr.
recs.rel: Badr was fought in 2 AH with about 313 Muslims against about 1000 Quraish.

recs.q: Near which city in Punjab are the ruins of the Indus Valley site of Harappa?
recs.facts: The ruins of Harappa lie near the town of Harappa in Sahiwal district of Punjab, Pakistan. The site was first excavated in the 1920s.
recs.rel: Mohenjo-daro, the other great Indus Valley city, is in Larkana district of Sindh.

recs.q: Near which city is the Rohtas Fort located?
recs.facts: Rohtas Fort is near Dina in Jhelum district, Punjab. Sher Shah Suri built it in the 16th century.
recs.rel: Rohtas Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

recs.q: In which direction of Pakistan is India located?
recs.facts: India lies along the eastern border of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Pakistan-India border is about 2,900 km long.

recs.q: In which months does the monsoon season occur in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The monsoon rains reach Pakistan in July and last until about September.
recs.rel: Most of the monsoon rain falls in the northern and north-eastern parts of the country.

recs.q: In which mountain range is K2, the second highest peak in the world, located?
recs.facts: K2 (8,611 m) lies on the Pakistan-China border in the Karakoram range.
recs.rel: K2 is also called Mount Godwin-Austen and Chogori.

recs.q: Which is the last surah of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Surah An-Nas is number 114 and is the last surah in the order of the Quran.
recs.rel: The first surah in order is Al-Fatihah.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan co-host the ICC Cricket World Cup together with India and Sri Lanka?
recs.facts: The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka.
recs.rel: Pakistan also co-hosted the 1987 World Cup with India only.

recs.q: In which year was NATO founded?
recs.facts: NATO was founded by the North Atlantic Treaty signed in Washington in April 1949.
recs.rel: The Soviet-led rival Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955.

recs.q: In which year was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency?
recs.facts: Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.
recs.rel: Karachi was made its capital.

recs.q: Israel is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (A.S). The Children of Israel are his descendants.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqub (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (A.S) and the father of Hazrat Yusuf (A.S).

recs.q: Jihad is a word of which language?
recs.facts: Jihad is an Arabic word meaning striving or struggle.
recs.rel: The Quran was revealed in Arabic.

recs.q: Lira is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: The Turkish lira is the official currency of Turkey.
recs.rel: Italy used the lira before adopting the euro.

recs.q: On which side of Asia is Pakistan located?
recs.facts: Pakistan lies in South Asia (the Indian subcontinent).
recs.rel: Some sources place Pakistan in South-West Asia, but it is usually counted as a South Asian country.

recs.q: The first five ayats revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) were from which surah?
recs.facts: The first five ayats revealed in the cave of Hira belong to Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Muddaththir is commonly considered to follow after a pause in revelation.

recs.q: The Lowari Pass connects Chitral with which place?
recs.facts: The Lowari Pass links Chitral with Dir, and so with the rest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: The Lowari Tunnel, opened in 2017, now gives all-weather access to Chitral.

recs.q: The rate of change is called what?
recs.facts: In calculus the derivative measures the rate of change of a quantity with respect to another.
recs.rel: The derivative of distance with respect to time is velocity.

recs.q: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and whom?
recs.facts: After the 1971 war, Bhutto and the Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement at Shimla on 2 July 1972.
recs.rel: The agreement turned the cease-fire line in Kashmir into the Line of Control.

recs.q: What does Ahl-e-Bait mean?
recs.facts: Ahl means people or family and Bait means house, so Ahl-e-Bait is 'people of the house'.
recs.rel: The term refers to the family of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: What does LOC stand for in the context of Kashmir?
recs.facts: LOC stands for Line of Control, the military control line dividing Indian- and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
recs.rel: The LOC was established by the Simla Agreement of 1972.

recs.q: What does Saifullah mean?
recs.facts: Saif means sword and Allah is God, so Saifullah means Sword of Allah.
recs.rel: Saifullah was the title given to Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) by the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: What does WAPDA stand for?
recs.facts: WAPDA stands for Water and Power Development Authority.
recs.rel: WAPDA was created in 1958 to develop Pakistan's water and hydropower resources.

recs.q: What does yellow journalism mean?
recs.facts: Yellow journalism is journalism that exaggerates or sensationalises news to attract readers rather than reporting facts carefully.
recs.rel: The term arose from the 1890s newspaper rivalry between Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst.

recs.q: K2, the second highest mountain in the world, is also known as what?
recs.facts: K2 is also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, after the British surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen, and as Chogori.
recs.rel: K2 lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border and is 8,611 metres high.

recs.q: What is the capital of Armenia?
recs.facts: Yerevan is the capital and largest city of Armenia.
recs.rel: Armenia is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus.

recs.q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
recs.facts: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.
recs.rel: Bhutan is a landlocked Himalayan kingdom between India and China.

recs.q: What is the capital of Libya?
recs.facts: Tripoli is the capital and largest city of Libya.
recs.rel: Benghazi is the second largest city of Libya.

recs.q: What is the capital of Punjab (Pakistan)?
recs.facts: Lahore is the provincial capital of Punjab.
recs.rel: Maryam Nawaz is the current Chief Minister of Punjab, succeeding Usman Buzdar.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of selfless?
recs.facts: A selfless person thinks of others before himself, which is what altruistic means.
recs.rel: The opposite of selfless is selfish.

recs.q: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia?
recs.facts: Saudi Arabia uses the Saudi riyal.
recs.rel: The UAE uses the dirham and Kuwait the dinar.

recs.q: On what date is Youm-e-Takbeer observed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998, observed yearly as Youm-e-Takbeer.
recs.rel: Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister at the time.

recs.q: Which is the fastest bird in the world (in a dive)?
recs.facts: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive, making it the fastest animal on Earth.
recs.rel: The ostrich is the fastest running bird at about 70 km/h.

recs.q: Which surah contains the first verses of the Quran to be revealed?
recs.facts: The first five verses revealed to the Prophet (SAW) in the Cave of Hira were from Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Muddaththir is commonly mentioned as the next revelation after a pause.

recs.q: What is the full form of OPEC?
opts: Organization of Producing and Exporting Countries
Organization of Power and Energy Countries
recs.facts: OPEC stands for Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a group of oil producing nations.
recs.rel: OPEC was founded in 1960 in Baghdad and is headquartered in Vienna.

recs.q: What is the highest civil award of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil award given by the state of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Hilal-e-Imtiaz ranks below Nishan-e-Pakistan among civil awards.

recs.q: What is the highest military award of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest gallantry award of Pakistan, given for extraordinary bravery in battle.
recs.rel: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed was the first recipient in 1948.

recs.q: What is the highest military award of the Netherlands?
recs.facts: The Military William Order is the oldest and highest honour of the Netherlands.
recs.rel: It was established in 1815 by King William I.

recs.q: Where is the hottest recorded air temperature in the world, 56.7 degrees Celsius (1913)?
recs.facts: The official record of 56.7 degrees Celsius (134 F) was measured at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California, in July 1913.
recs.rel: Candidates answered Egypt, but Egypt does not hold the world record.

recs.q: What is the largest city of Balochistan by population?
recs.facts: Quetta is the provincial capital and the most populous city of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Quetta is known as the Fruit Garden of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the largest ocean in the world?
recs.facts: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square km, roughly a third of the Earth.
recs.rel: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest point on Earth.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the Amazon River according to common textbooks?
recs.facts: Most textbooks give the Amazon length as about 6,400 km.
recs.rel: Sources differ: some measurements give up to about 6,990 km, and the Nile is often listed as longest at about 6,650 km.

recs.q: Which is the longest river of Europe?
recs.facts: The Volga in Russia is about 3,530 km long and is the longest river in Europe.
recs.rel: The Danube is the second longest river in Europe and flows through ten countries.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Ijtihad?
opts: To exert effort to reach a legal ruling
recs.facts: Ijtihad means to strive or exert one's utmost effort, in Islamic law to derive a ruling from the Quran and Sunnah.
recs.rel: Allama Iqbal called ijtihad the principle of movement in Islam.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Jihad?
recs.facts: Jihad comes from an Arabic root meaning to strive or struggle in the way of Allah.
recs.rel: Scholars divide it into the struggle against one's own desires and the struggle in defence of the faith.

recs.q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
recs.rel: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates Hajra's search for water.

recs.q: What is the national game of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Field hockey is commonly given as the national game of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan has won the Hockey World Cup four times.

recs.q: What is the national language of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan under the Constitution.
recs.rel: English and Urdu are the official languages.

recs.q: In the usual order of the oceans by size, what is the number of the Indian Ocean?
recs.facts: By size the order is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic, so the Indian Ocean is third.
recs.rel: The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.

recs.q: What was the old name of Madina?
recs.facts: Madina was known as Yathrib before the Prophet (PBUH) migrated there in 622 CE.
recs.rel: Madina means the city of the Prophet.

recs.q: What is the land between two rivers called?
recs.facts: A doab is the strip of land between two converging rivers.
recs.rel: The Punjab has five doabs such as Rachna Doab and Bari Doab.

recs.q: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days, is located in which place?
recs.facts: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. The Quaid stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.
recs.rel: Ziarat is famous for its juniper forests, and the Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.

recs.q: What is the normal term of office of the Secretary General of the United Nations?
recs.facts: The Secretary General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council for a five-year term, which can be renewed.
recs.rel: The current Secretary General is Antonio Guterres of Portugal, in office since 2017, and his term ends on 31 December 2026.

recs.q: What is the total number of Ghazwat (battles in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part personally)?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks give 27 Ghazwat. Sources differ, as some list 26 or 29.
recs.rel: The expeditions he did not attend personally are called Sariyya.

recs.q: What is the total number of surahs in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran has 114 surahs.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Fatiha is the first and Surah An-Nas is the last.

recs.q: Which was the first battle fought by the Muslims?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
recs.rel: About 313 Muslims faced an army of nearly 1000 Quraish at Badr and won a decisive victory.

recs.q: Which city was the first capital of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Karachi served as the capital from 1947 when Pakistan was created. The capital was shifted to Rawalpindi in 1959 and then to Islamabad in the 1960s.
recs.rel: Islamabad was built as the new capital and replaced Rawalpindi, which was the interim capital.

recs.q: What was the profession of Mother Teresa?
recs.facts: Mother Teresa was a Roman Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950 to serve the poor and the sick.
recs.rel: She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and was declared a saint by the Catholic Church in 2016.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ismail (AS) with Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra. He was the elder of Ibrahim's two sons.
recs.rel: Father and son together raised the foundations of the Kaaba in Makkah.

recs.q: When did Namaz (salah) become farz (obligatory) for Muslims?
recs.facts: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Miraj, roughly five years before the Hijrat. Before this, the Muslims offered some prayers without a fixed five-time rule.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) received the command of five daily prayers directly from Allah during the Miraj.

recs.q: In which year was Basic Democracy introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan?
recs.facts: President Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies system through an order in October 1959. It had a five-tier structure with 80,000 Basic Democrats who elected the president.
recs.rel: The scheme was abolished after Ayub Khan resigned in 1969.

recs.q: In which year were the first general elections held under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973 and the first general elections under it were held in March 1977.
recs.rel: Those elections were followed by allegations of rigging and the imposition of martial law on 5 July 1977.

recs.q: Where and when was the All-India Muslim League founded?
recs.facts: The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference, at the house of Nawab Salimullah Khan.
recs.rel: Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk were among its early leaders, and Sir Aga Khan was its first president.

recs.q: Where does the Karakoram Highway (KKH) start in Pakistan?
recs.facts: In Pakistan the Karakoram Highway is commonly described as starting at Hassan Abdal and running north through Abbottabad, Gilgit and Sost to the Khunjerab Pass.
recs.rel: Some sources start it at Havelian, but Pakistani textbooks usually give Hassan Abdal.

recs.q: Where is Lake Victoria located?
recs.facts: Lake Victoria is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania in East Africa.
recs.rel: It is the largest lake in Africa and the source of the White Nile.

recs.q: In which city is Nishtar Hospital located?
recs.facts: Nishtar Hospital is a large teaching hospital in Multan, Punjab.
recs.rel: It is named after Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a Pakistan Movement leader.

recs.q: Where is the Bay of Biscay located?
opts: Atlantic Ocean, off the coasts of France and Spain
recs.facts: The Bay of Biscay is a gulf of the north-east Atlantic Ocean, bordered by the west coast of France and the north coast of Spain.
recs.rel: It is known for rough seas and strong storms.

recs.q: Which agreement was signed after the 1971 war between Pakistan and India?
recs.facts: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
recs.rel: The Tashkent Agreement was signed after the 1965 war.

recs.q: Which body regulates the distribution of Indus river system water among the provinces of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Indus River System Authority (IRSA) was set up in 1992 to apportion water among the provinces under the Water Apportionment Accord.
recs.rel: WAPDA is responsible for water and power development projects.

recs.q: Which city of Pakistan is called the Manchester of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Faisalabad is the centre of Pakistan's textile industry, like Manchester in England.
recs.rel: Faisalabad was formerly called Lyallpur.

recs.q: Which country is known as the land of a thousand lakes?
recs.facts: Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes, giving it this nickname.
recs.rel: Canada has the largest total number of lakes in the world.

recs.q: Which city is known as the city of mosques?
recs.facts: Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh, is known as the City of Mosques because of its thousands of mosques.
recs.rel: Dhaka is also known as the city of rickshaws.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
recs.facts: The correct word has a double c and a double m: accommodation.
recs.rel: Accommodate follows the same pattern with double c and double m.

recs.q: Which is the second most populous country of the world?
recs.facts: India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, so China is now second.
recs.rel: In 2021-22 China was the most populous and India second.

recs.q: Which is the world's third longest river?
recs.facts: By length the Nile and Amazon are first and second, and the Yangtze in China is third at about 6,300 km.
recs.rel: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

recs.q: Which mountain range is mainly associated with Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Hindu Kush range runs through central and northeastern Afghanistan into Pakistan.
recs.rel: Tirich Mir in Chitral is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

recs.q: Which is the highest mountain range of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Karakoram range contains K2 (8,611 m), the highest peak in Pakistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan's mountain ranges include Himalaya, Karakoram, Hindu Kush, Sulaiman and Kirthar.

recs.q: Which organization was formed by Turkey, Pakistan and Iran in 1964?
recs.facts: Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
recs.rel: RCD was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

recs.q: Which of the following is a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
recs.facts: The five permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
recs.rel: Each permanent member holds the power of veto.

recs.q: Who gave the idea of SAARC?
opts: J. R. Jayewardene of Sri Lanka
recs.facts: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh proposed regional cooperation in South Asia in 1980, leading to SAARC.
recs.rel: SAARC was formally founded in Dhaka in December 1985.

recs.q: Which company is responsible for inventing the iPhone, launched in 2007 under its co-founder Steve Jobs?
recs.facts: Apple Inc. launched the first iPhone in 2007, with Steve Jobs presenting it.
recs.rel: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak in 1976.

recs.q: Who is the Secretary General of the United Nations?
recs.facts: Antonio Guterres has held the post since 2017 and his term ends on 31 December 2026.
recs.rel: The selection of his successor is under way in 2026.

recs.q: Who suggested the name of the United Nations (UNO)?
recs.facts: US President Franklin D. Roosevelt suggested the name United Nations, first used in the Declaration of 1 January 1942.
recs.rel: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

recs.q: Who was the ruler of Pakistan after Yahya Khan?
recs.facts: Yahya Khan handed over power in December 1971 after the fall of Dhaka, and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became President and Chief Martial Law Administrator.
recs.rel: Bhutto later became Prime Minister under the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: Who was the first Mughal emperor of India?
recs.facts: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
recs.rel: Sher Shah Suri was not a Mughal; he briefly defeated Humayun.

recs.q: Who was the first woman martyred in Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA) was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to give up Islam.
recs.rel: Her husband Hazrat Yasir (RA) was also martyred.

recs.q: Who was the first person in space?
recs.facts: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.
recs.rel: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in 1963.

recs.q: Who was the second caliph (Khalifa) of Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA) became the second caliph in 13 AH after being nominated by Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). He ruled for about ten years.
recs.rel: He was martyred in 23 AH by Abu Lulu Firoz and was succeeded by Hazrat Usman (RA).

recs.q: Who accompanied the Prophet (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) travelled with the Prophet (PBUH) and they hid in the cave of Thawr.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) stayed behind in Makkah to return the trusts kept with the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Who wrote Shah Jo Risalo?
recs.facts: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai composed the Sindhi poetry collection Shah Jo Risalo.
recs.rel: His shrine is at Bhit Shah in Sindh.

recs.q: With which surah does the Holy Quran begin?
recs.facts: The Quran opens with Surah Al-Fatihah, which has seven verses.
recs.rel: Surah An-Nas is the last surah of the Quran.

recs.q: Ali walks towards north, then turns left, and after some time turns left again. In which direction does he face now?
recs.facts: North then left is west. A second left from west is south.
recs.rel: Candidates wrote North, but two left turns make a 180 degree turn.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 15th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days, and 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Monday gives Sunday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the vector (cross) product of two non-zero vectors is zero, how are the two vectors related?
recs.facts: The magnitude of the cross product is |A||B| sin(theta). It is zero only when sin(theta) = 0, so the vectors are parallel (or anti-parallel).
recs.rel: If the dot (scalar) product is zero instead, the vectors are perpendicular.

recs.q: In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are boys. How many girls are there?
recs.rel: Girls are 1/3 of the class, which is 10 students.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 360 / 500 x 100 = 72%.
recs.rel: The absent students are 140, which is 28%.

recs.q: What is 60% of 90?
recs.rel: The product is the same for 90% of 60, since percentages are multiplicative.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 120?
recs.facts: 120 divided by 4 is 30.
recs.rel: A quarter of a number is the same as 25% of it.

recs.q: Which letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ?
recs.facts: The gaps between letters are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. O is the 15th letter and the 21st is U.
recs.rel: The differences in this series increase by 1 each time.

recs.q: Your mother is my brother's sister. What is the relation between you and me?
recs.facts: My brother's sister is my own sister, so your mother is my sister. Therefore I am your maternal uncle.
recs.rel: A mother's brother is called the maternal uncle (mamu in Urdu).

recs.q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which three rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1960 Indus Waters Treaty gave the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab to Pakistan.
recs.rel: The treaty gave the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej to India and was brokered by the World Bank.

recs.q: Babusar Pass connects the Kaghan Valley with which town?
recs.facts: Babusar Pass links Kaghan Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: The pass is about 4,173 metres high and is usually open only in summer.

recs.q: The ELISA test is used to diagnose which disease?
recs.facts: ELISA detects antibodies or antigens in blood and is the standard screening test for HIV infection. Candidates who said tuberculosis were wrong.
recs.rel: ELISA stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay.

recs.q: Mahatma Gandhi was a famous leader of which country?
recs.facts: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi led the Indian independence movement and the Indian National Congress.
recs.rel: Gandhi was assassinated in January 1948 in New Delhi.

recs.q: How many Madani surahs does the Holy Quran contain, according to the common Pakistani textbook count?
recs.facts: Of the 114 surahs, 86 are Makki and 28 are Madani. Madani surahs were revealed after the Hijrat.
recs.rel: Scholars differ slightly on a few surahs, so some books give slightly different counts.

recs.q: In which year were the first Commonwealth Games (then called the British Empire Games) held?
recs.facts: The first British Empire Games were held in Hamilton, Canada, in 1930. They were later renamed the Commonwealth Games.
recs.rel: The Games are held every four years and were named the British Commonwealth Games in 1970 and the Commonwealth Games in 1978.

recs.q: Mohenjo-daro is located near which city of Sindh?
recs.facts: Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilisation, lies in Larkana District on the right bank of the Indus.
recs.rel: Mohenjo-daro means Mound of the Dead and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

recs.q: What are both houses of the Parliament of Pakistan (Senate and National Assembly) together called?
recs.facts: Under the 1973 Constitution the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora, consists of the President, the Senate and the National Assembly.
recs.rel: The Senate is the upper house and the National Assembly is the lower house.

recs.q: How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: The Muslim army at Badr numbered about 313 men, against roughly 1000 Quraish soldiers.
recs.rel: Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan are the Chagai Hills located?
recs.facts: The Chagai Hills lie in Chagai district in the northwest of Balochistan, near the Afghan and Iranian borders.
recs.rel: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests of May 1998 in the Chagai Hills.

recs.q: The 1996 Cricket World Cup was co-hosted by Pakistan along with which two countries?
recs.facts: The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka won the title by beating Australia in the final at Lahore.
recs.rel: The 1996 final was played at the Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore.

recs.q: Which country is the world's largest exporter of arms?
recs.facts: According to SIPRI, the United States is the largest arms exporter and supplies around 40 percent of global arms exports.
recs.rel: France has recently overtaken Russia as the second largest arms exporter.

recs.q: Which game is played on a court enclosed by four walls?
recs.facts: Squash is played in a closed court with four walls, and the ball may be hit off any wall except for out-of-play lines.
recs.rel: Squash was invented in England at Harrow School in the 19th century and Pakistan has been a champion nation in it.

recs.q: Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran?
recs.facts: Hazrat Musa (AS) is named about 136 times in the Quran, more than any other prophet.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is the next most frequently mentioned prophet.

recs.q: Which prophet was given a great kingdom, including rule over the jinn and the winds?
recs.facts: Allah gave Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) a unique kingdom, with jinn, birds and winds under his command.
recs.rel: Sulaiman (AS) was the son of Hazrat Dawud (AS), who was also a prophet and king.

recs.q: Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical form of the Quran?
recs.facts: When asked about the Prophet's character, Hazrat Ayesha replied that his character was the Quran.
recs.rel: This report is found in Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad.

recs.q: Who headed the committee that compiled the Holy Quran in one book during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), on the advice of Hazrat Umar (RA) after the Battle of Yamama, assigned Hazrat Zaid bin Sabit (RA), the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran. He had memorised the Quran and written much of it down in the Prophet's lifetime.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman (RA) later had standard copies prepared from this compilation.

recs.q: Which Sahabi is known by the title Zun-Noorain (Possessor of Two Lights)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA) married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW), one after the other, so he was called Zun-Noorain.
recs.rel: His wives from the Prophet's family were Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

recs.q: Zun-Noorain (Zunnurain), meaning 'possessor of two lights', is the title of which Companion of the Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (R.A) married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), one after the other. For this reason he is called Zun-Noorain.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the third Caliph of Islam and is also known as Ghani.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many houses does the Parliament of Pakistan have?
recs.facts: The Parliament consists of the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house), plus the President.
recs.rel: The Senate has 96 members after the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP.

recs.q: In which city is the Badshahi Mosque located?
recs.facts: The Badshahi Mosque stands in Lahore opposite the Lahore Fort.
recs.rel: It was built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673.

recs.q: Which is the world's largest uranium producing country?
recs.facts: Kazakhstan has been the top uranium producer since 2009 and supplied about 39 percent of world mine output in 2024.
recs.rel: Canada is second and Namibia third in recent World Nuclear Association data.

recs.q: 340 out of 500: what is the percentage?
recs.rel: Percent means per hundred.

recs.q: If today is Monday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: Tomorrow is Tuesday, so the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
recs.rel: The day after tomorrow is always two days ahead of today.

recs.q: On which date was the Battle of Uhud fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Uhud was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE) near Mount Uhud, close to Madina.
recs.rel: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred in this battle.

recs.q: If A and B are disjoint sets, what is A intersection B?
recs.facts: Disjoint sets have no common element, so their intersection is the empty set.
recs.rel: The empty set is written as phi or { }.

recs.q: What is a Ruku in the Holy Quran?
opts: A section of verses marked in the text
recs.facts: A ruku in the Quran is a group of verses forming a section, marked with the letter ain in the margin.
recs.rel: In prayer, ruku also means bowing, but in the Mushaf it means a section.

recs.q: Which is the world's largest silver producing country?
recs.facts: Mexico leads the world in mined silver, at about 173 million ounces in 2025, ahead of Peru and China.
recs.rel: Mexico has been the top silver producer for many years.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 120?
recs.rel: One third of 120 is ten times larger than one third of one tenth of 120, which is 4.

recs.q: What is a quarter of one tenth of 90?
recs.facts: One tenth of 90 is 9, and a quarter of 9 is 9 / 4 = 2.25.
recs.rel: A quarter of one tenth is 1/40 of the number.

recs.q: What is an angle less than 90 degrees called?
recs.facts: An angle smaller than 90 degrees is called an acute angle.
recs.rel: Two acute angles can add up to 90 degrees, in which case they are complementary.

recs.q: What is one third of 120?
recs.facts: One third of 120 is 120 / 3 = 40.
recs.rel: A number divisible by 3 has digits whose sum is divisible by 3; 1+2+0 = 3.

recs.q: A diagonal matrix is always what type of matrix?
recs.facts: A diagonal matrix has non-zero entries only on the main diagonal, and a main diagonal exists only for a square matrix. So every diagonal matrix is a square matrix.
recs.rel: An identity matrix is a special diagonal matrix in which every diagonal entry is 1.

recs.q: Abdul Sattar Edhi is associated with which city of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Edhi made Karachi the base of his welfare work, and the Edhi Foundation is headquartered there.
recs.rel: Edhi was born in Bantva, Gujarat (India) in 1928 and died in 2016.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, who resolves a dispute between the National Assembly and the Senate?
recs.facts: Under Article 70, a bill on which the two houses disagree is settled by a joint sitting of both houses, decided by a majority of the total members present.
recs.rel: The President summons the joint sitting.

recs.q: According to the Islamic calendar, in which month did Pakistan become independent?
recs.facts: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramazan 1366 AH, a Friday and the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) according to common belief.
recs.rel: Ramazan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

recs.q: Against whom did Shahid Afridi score his record 37-ball century in 1996?
recs.facts: Afridi hit the then fastest ODI century off 37 balls against Sri Lanka at Nairobi in October 1996.
recs.rel: The record stood for 18 years until broken by Corey Anderson in 2014 and then by AB de Villiers.

recs.q: Against whom was the Battle of Tabuk fought?
recs.facts: In 9 AH the Prophet (PBUH) led an army to Tabuk to face the Byzantine force, but no fighting took place.
recs.rel: It was the last military expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: By whom was the Objectives Resolution passed?
recs.facts: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 12 March 1949.
recs.rel: It later became the preamble of the 1956, 1962 and 1973 constitutions in some form.

recs.q: By whose hand was Hazrat Hamza martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: Wahshi bin Harb, a slave of Jubayr bin Mutim, killed Hazrat Hamza with a spear on the order of Hind.
recs.rel: Wahshi later accepted Islam.

recs.q: The Coastal Highway connects Gwadar with which city?
recs.facts: The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the Arabian Sea coast from Karachi to Gwadar.
recs.rel: It is about 653 km long and was completed in 2004.

recs.q: The Danube is the second longest river of which continent?
recs.facts: The Danube, about 2,850 km long, is the second longest river in Europe after the Volga.
recs.rel: It flows into the Black Sea.

recs.q: Desert Fox is the title of whom?
recs.facts: Field Marshal Erwin Rommel earned the name Desert Fox for his skilled command of the German Afrika Korps in North Africa.
recs.rel: He was defeated by Montgomery at El Alamein in 1942.

recs.q: Diphtheria is a disease of which part of the body?
recs.facts: Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the throat and upper airways.
recs.rel: It is prevented by the DPT vaccine.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He wasted his time ___ TV.
recs.facts: After the expression waste time, the gerund (-ing form) is used, so watching is correct.
recs.rel: The same pattern is used in spend time doing something.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: The Pacific is ___ than the Arctic Ocean.
recs.facts: The sentence compares two things and uses than, so the comparative deeper is needed.
recs.rel: The Pacific is the deepest and largest ocean on Earth.

recs.q: For the Khilafat Movement, Muslims of India migrated towards which country?
recs.facts: During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Muslims left India for Afghanistan as a protest against British rule.
recs.rel: The migration failed because the Afghan government could not support so many people.

recs.q: From which city did the Urdu-Hindi controversy start in 1867?
recs.facts: In 1867 Hindus of Banaras demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in government offices, starting the controversy.
recs.rel: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan took it as a sign that Hindus and Muslims could not remain together.

recs.q: The Gulf of Siam, now known as the Gulf of Thailand, mainly lies in which country?
recs.facts: The Gulf of Siam is the old name of the Gulf of Thailand, which borders Thailand mainly, as well as Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.
recs.rel: Sources differ on which country to name, but Thailand is the answer given in most textbooks.

recs.q: Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
recs.facts: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a Pakistani cricketer and the first captain of Pakistan in Test cricket.
recs.rel: He captained Pakistan in its first Test victory, at The Oval in 1954.

recs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which tribe?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Quraish tribe, to its clan Banu Hashim.
recs.rel: Banu Aws and Banu Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina who became the Ansar.

recs.q: How many ayats (verses) does Surah Al-Fatiha, the first surah of the Quran, have?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Fatiha has seven ayats, which is why it is also called Sab'a al-Mathani (the seven oft-repeated verses).
recs.rel: Some candidates remembered 5 but the correct number is 7.

recs.q: How many ayats were revealed in the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The first revelation in the Cave of Hira consisted of the first five ayats of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
recs.rel: The first revelation came in the month of Ramadan.

recs.q: How many continents are there in the world?
recs.facts: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia (Oceania).
recs.rel: Asia is the largest continent and Australia the smallest.

recs.q: How many Hajj did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) perform after his migration to Madina?
recs.facts: He performed only one Hajj, in 10 AH, known as Hajjat-ul-Wada (the Farewell Pilgrimage).
recs.rel: He delivered his Farewell Sermon on the plain of Arafat during this Hajj.

recs.q: How many Muslims were in the army at the Battle of Uhad (Uhud) in the end?
recs.facts: About 1000 set out, but Abdullah bin Ubayy withdrew with about 300 men, leaving about 700 Muslims.
recs.rel: The Quraish army at Uhad numbered about 3000.

recs.q: How many players are there in a football team on the field?
recs.facts: A football team fields eleven players including the goalkeeper.
recs.rel: A standard football match lasts 90 minutes.

recs.q: How many ayats are there in total in Surah Al-Baqarah?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, has 286 ayats.
recs.rel: It is the second surah of the Quran.

recs.q: For how many years did the Holy Prophet (SAW) live in Madina after the Hijrah?
recs.facts: He migrated to Madina in 622 AD (1 AH) and passed away there in 632 AD (11 AH), about ten years later.
recs.rel: He lived about 13 years in Makkah after receiving the first revelation.

recs.q: In how many fields is the Nobel Prize awarded today?
recs.facts: The Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics, which is six fields.
recs.rel: Originally there were five; the Economics prize was added in 1969.

recs.q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to India?
recs.facts: The 1960 treaty gave the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) to India and the western rivers to Pakistan.
recs.rel: India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, but the treaty allocation itself is unchanged.

recs.q: In which city is the historic Bala Hisar Fort located?
recs.facts: Bala Hisar Fort stands in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It overlooks the old city.
recs.rel: The fort was rebuilt by the Sikhs in the early 19th century.

recs.q: In which city is the Arfa Karim Tower located?
recs.facts: The Arfa Karim Tower is in Lahore, Punjab, near Gulberg. It is named after the young computer prodigy Arfa Karim.
recs.rel: Arfa Karim was the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional.

recs.q: In which city was the All India Muslim League founded in 1906?
recs.facts: The All India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 at the Muslim Educational Conference, hosted by Nawab Salimullah Khan.
recs.rel: Its first president was Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk, and Sir Aga Khan was the first permanent president.

recs.q: In which country does the Orange River mainly flow?
recs.facts: The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa and flows westward to the Atlantic Ocean. It rises in the mountains of Lesotho.
recs.rel: It forms part of the border between South Africa and Namibia.

recs.q: In which country is the volcano Mount Etna located?
recs.facts: Mount Etna is on the island of Sicily, Italy. It is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.
recs.rel: It is the highest active volcano in Europe.

recs.q: In which country were the 2016 Olympic Games held?
recs.facts: The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
recs.rel: They were the first Summer Olympics held in South America.

recs.q: In which direction of Pakistan is Iran located?
recs.facts: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan, bordering Balochistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan also shares borders with Afghanistan in the west and north-west and China in the north.

recs.q: In which Chinese city did the Covid-19 outbreak first appear in December 2019?
recs.facts: The first cases of Covid-19 were reported in Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, China, in December 2019.
recs.rel: The World Health Organization declared Covid-19 a pandemic in March 2020.

recs.q: In which game is the agricultural shot played?
recs.facts: The agricultural shot is a cricket stroke in which the batsman swings the bat across the line in a cow-corner heave, like a farmer swinging a scythe.
recs.rel: It is usually aimed towards the cow corner region of the field.

recs.q: In which Ghazwa did angels come to help the Muslims?
recs.facts: The Quran says that angels helped the Muslims in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.
recs.rel: About 313 Muslims faced an army of roughly 1,000 Quraysh at Badr.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
recs.rel: It was the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraysh.

recs.q: In which province is the Kharan Desert located?
recs.facts: The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan's first nuclear test site, Chagai, is also in Balochistan close to this desert region.

recs.q: In which quadrant does the point (-2, -3) lie?
recs.facts: Both the x-coordinate (-2) and the y-coordinate (-3) are negative, which is the third quadrant.
recs.rel: In the second quadrant x is negative and y is positive.

recs.q: In which surah is Ayat-ul-Kursi found?
recs.facts: Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
recs.rel: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran with 286 verses.

recs.q: In which war was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred?
recs.facts: Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 defending the BRB canal sector near Lahore.
recs.rel: He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.

recs.q: In which year did the Khilafat delegation led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar go to England?
recs.facts: The delegation went to England in 1920 to plead the case of the Ottoman Caliphate before Prime Minister Lloyd George.
recs.rel: The Khilafat Movement was launched in 1919.

recs.q: In which year did the Quit India Movement start?
recs.facts: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
recs.rel: The Muslim League opposed it and its slogan was Divide and Quit.

recs.q: The Olympic Games were cancelled in which year of World War 1?
recs.facts: The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled because of the war; the games are held every four years, so 1914 was not an Olympic year.
recs.rel: The Olympics were cancelled again in 1940 and 1944 during World War 2.

recs.q: In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted as the Government of India Act?
recs.facts: The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, which introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
recs.rel: The Government of India Act 1935 later introduced provincial autonomy.

recs.q: In which year was the first Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences awarded?
recs.facts: The economics prize was first awarded in 1969 to Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen.
recs.rel: It is funded by the Bank of Sweden and was not one of Alfred Nobel's original five prizes.

recs.q: In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
recs.facts: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901 in the original five categories.
recs.rel: Alfred Nobel died in 1896 and left his fortune to create the prizes.

recs.q: In which year was the Kargil war fought?
recs.facts: The Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan took place from May to July 1999.
recs.rel: It followed the 1998 nuclear tests of both countries.

recs.q: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
recs.facts: The partition of Bengal, made in 1905, was annulled in 1911 after Hindu agitation.
recs.rel: The 1911 decision disappointed Muslims of East Bengal.

recs.q: Into how many equal parts does a diameter divide a circle?
recs.facts: A diameter passes through the centre and splits the circle into two equal semicircles.
recs.rel: The diameter is twice the radius.

recs.q: Is the sun a star or a planet?
recs.facts: The sun is a star because it produces its own light and heat by nuclear fusion. Planets only reflect light.
recs.rel: The sun is a medium-sized yellow dwarf star at the centre of our solar system.

recs.q: Which of the following is a city of Libya?
recs.facts: Tripoli is the capital and largest city of Libya. Casablanca is in Morocco, Tunis in Tunisia and Cairo in Egypt.
recs.rel: Benghazi is another major city of Libya.

recs.q: On what date was CPEC formed?
recs.facts: Candidates and many Pakistani sources give 22 May 2013, when Pakistan and China signed the agreement on the economic corridor during Chinese Premier Li Keqiang's visit.
recs.rel: Sources differ: the 46 billion dollar CPEC package was announced in April 2015 during President Xi Jinping's visit.

recs.q: On what date was the OIC established?
recs.facts: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation was established at the Rabat summit on 25 September 1969.
recs.rel: It was set up after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque on 21 August 1969, and its headquarters are in Jeddah.

recs.q: On which date is Defence Day observed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Defence Day is observed on 6 September to commemorate the defence of Pakistan in the 1965 war.
recs.rel: The 1965 war with India was fought in September 1965.

recs.q: Ruble is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: The ruble is the currency of Russia.
recs.rel: The Russian capital is Moscow.

recs.q: Saifullah (Sword of Allah) was the title of whom?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) gave the title Saifullah to the great general Khalid bin Waleed (R.A).
recs.rel: He commanded the Muslim armies in the conquest of Syria and the battle of Yarmouk.

recs.q: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a famous poet of which province?
recs.facts: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was the great Sufi poet of Sindh. His collection is called Shah Jo Risalo.
recs.rel: His shrine is at Bhit Shah in Sindh.

recs.q: Sultan Bahu and Bulleh Shah are poets of which language?
recs.facts: Both Sufi poets wrote in Punjabi.
recs.rel: Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur and Sultan Bahu in Jhang.

recs.q: Swine flu is caused by what?
recs.facts: Swine flu is caused by influenza viruses, mainly the H1N1 strain.
recs.rel: The H1N1 swine flu pandemic occurred in 2009.

recs.q: The diameter of a circle is equal to how many radii of the circle?
recs.facts: The diameter is a line through the centre, which is made of two radii. So diameter = 2 x radius.
recs.rel: The circumference of a circle is pi times its diameter.

recs.q: The Hindu Kush mountain range connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: The Hindu Kush extends from central Afghanistan into northern Pakistan.
recs.rel: Tirich Mir (7708 m), the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, is in Chitral, Pakistan.

recs.q: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
recs.facts: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship of badminton, contested between national teams.
recs.rel: The women's equivalent of the Thomas Cup is the Uber Cup.

recs.q: The year 1995 was the golden jubilee (50th anniversary) of which international organisation?
recs.facts: The United Nations was founded in 1945, so 1995 marked its 50 years.
recs.rel: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, now celebrated as United Nations Day.

recs.q: Which Sahabi was married to two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), earning the title Dhun-Nurayn?
recs.facts: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).
recs.rel: Dhun-Nurayn means 'possessor of two lights'.

recs.q: Waris Shah is a famous poet of which language?
recs.facts: Waris Shah (1722-1798) wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer Ranjha.
recs.rel: Waris Shah is buried in Jandiala Sher Khan, Sheikhupura district.

recs.q: Warsak Dam, near Peshawar, was completed during the government of which ruler?
recs.facts: Warsak Dam was completed in 1960 under Field Marshal Ayub Khan's government.
recs.rel: It was built on the Kabul River with Canadian help under the Colombo Plan.

recs.q: How many faraiz does wuzu (ablution) have according to the Hanafi school?
recs.facts: The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head (masah) and washing the feet up to the ankles.
recs.rel: Schools of thought differ in details of wuzu, and the Hanafi count of four is common in Pakistani textbooks.

recs.q: What does the word ayat mean?
recs.facts: Ayat is the plural of ayah, meaning a sign, and it is used for the verses of the Quran.
recs.rel: A chapter of the Quran is called a surah.

recs.q: What does the word Jihad mean?
recs.facts: Jihad comes from the Arabic root j-h-d meaning to strive or exert effort.
recs.rel: Jihad bil nafs means striving against one's own base desires.

recs.q: What does OIC stand for?
recs.facts: OIC stands for Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the collective voice of the Muslim world.
recs.rel: It was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011 and is headquartered in Jeddah.

recs.q: What does Saif mean in Arabic?
recs.facts: Saif is the Arabic word for sword.
recs.rel: The Arabic word for shield is dir.

recs.q: What does zakat mean literally?
recs.facts: Zakat literally means purification and growth, as giving it purifies wealth and the soul.
recs.rel: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam and is usually 2.5 percent on savings above nisab.

recs.q: What is a scalar matrix?
opts: A diagonal matrix with all diagonal elements equal
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose rows and columns are interchanged
recs.facts: A scalar matrix is a square diagonal matrix in which all the main diagonal elements are the same and all other elements are zero.
recs.rel: A scalar matrix with diagonal elements equal to 1 is the identity matrix.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of cleverness?
recs.facts: Cleverness means mental sharpness, so intelligence is the closest in meaning.
recs.rel: Another synonym of cleverness is shrewdness.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of constant?
recs.facts: Constant means continuing without change, so steady is the closest in meaning.
recs.rel: In mathematics, a constant is a quantity whose value does not change.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of elation?
recs.facts: Elation means great joy or high spirits, so delight is a synonym.
recs.rel: Its opposite is dejection.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of idleness?
recs.facts: Idleness is the state of doing no work, which is laziness.
recs.rel: Its opposite is industriousness.

recs.q: What is Astola?
opts: An island off the Balochistan coast
recs.facts: Astola, also called Haft Talar, is an island in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Balochistan.
recs.rel: It is Pakistan's largest offshore island.

recs.q: What was the Lucknow Pact of 1916?
opts: An agreement between the Muslim League and Congress accepting separate electorates for Muslims
A treaty between Britain and Afghanistan
An agreement ending the War of Independence 1857
recs.facts: The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916 by the All India Muslim League and the Indian National Congress, and Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity for his role in it.

recs.q: What is the National Finance Commission (NFC) used for?
opts: Distributing federal divisible revenue between the federation and the provinces
recs.facts: The NFC Award decides how the divisible pool of federal taxes is shared between the centre and the four provinces.
recs.rel: The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.

recs.q: What is Sunnah?
opts: The way and practice of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
recs.facts: Sunnah literally means path or way, and in Islam it refers to the sayings, actions and approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Sunnah is the second source of Islamic law after the Quran.

recs.q: What is the value of tan 45 degrees?
recs.facts: At 45 degrees sin and cos are both 1 over root 2, so tan = sin/cos = 1.
recs.rel: The value of tan 60 degrees is root 3.

recs.q: What is the antonym of entire?
recs.facts: Entire means whole or complete, so its opposite is partial, meaning only a part.
recs.rel: Whole, complete and total are synonyms of entire.

recs.q: What is the antonym of persistent?
recs.facts: Persistent means continuing firmly without stopping. Occasional, meaning happening only now and then, is the opposite.
recs.rel: Persistent and persevering are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the arithmetic mean of x-3 and x+5?
recs.rel: The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.

recs.q: What is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
recs.facts: Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Quetta, which one candidate wrote, is the capital of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Peshawar is one of the oldest living cities in South Asia.

recs.q: What is the capital of Sindh?
recs.facts: Karachi is the capital of Sindh province.
recs.rel: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the currency of Albania?
recs.facts: Albania uses the lek.
recs.rel: Bulgaria's former lev and Romania's leu are similar-sounding currencies.

recs.q: What is the currency of Algeria?
recs.facts: Algeria uses the Algerian dinar.
recs.rel: Morocco uses the dirham, not the dinar.

recs.q: What is the currency of Brazil?
recs.facts: Brazil uses the real.
recs.rel: Brazil is the largest country in South America.

recs.q: What is the currency of Bulgaria?
recs.facts: Bulgaria replaced the lev with the euro on 1 January 2026, becoming the 21st eurozone member.
recs.rel: Before 2026 the Bulgarian lev (candidates' 2021-22 answer) was fixed at 1.95583 per euro.

recs.q: When did the Cripps Mission come to India?
recs.facts: Sir Stafford Cripps reached India in March 1942 with proposals for dominion status after World War II.
recs.rel: The Muslim League and Congress both rejected the proposals.

recs.q: Which is the deepest known part of the earth's oceans?
opts: Puerto Rico Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean
Java Trench in the Indian Ocean
Tonga Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
recs.facts: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific holds the deepest point, Challenger Deep. The candidate answer wrongly placed it in the Atlantic.
recs.rel: Challenger Deep is roughly 10,900 metres deep.

recs.q: What is the first pillar of Islam?
recs.facts: The first pillar is the declaration of faith (Shahada), which affirms Tauheed and the Prophethood of Muhammad (SAW).
recs.rel: The order of the pillars is Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj.

recs.q: What is the graph of a linear equation in two variables?
recs.facts: A linear equation such as y = mx + c has all its solutions on one straight line.
recs.rel: In y = mx + c, m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.

recs.q: What is the height of K2, the second highest mountain in the world?
recs.facts: K2 is about 8,611 m high (some sources give 8,609 m).
recs.rel: K2 lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border and is also called Mount Godwin-Austen.

recs.q: What is the height of Mount Everest?
recs.facts: The 2020 joint Nepal-China survey gave Everest a height of 8,848.86 m, commonly rounded to 8,849 m.
recs.rel: Before 2020 the accepted height was 8,848 m.

recs.q: Which is known as the highest battlefield of the world?
recs.facts: Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram, where Pakistani and Indian troops face each other at around 6,000 m, is the highest battlefield.
recs.rel: Siachen is about 76 km long, one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

recs.q: What is the highest point above sea level in Pakistan?
recs.facts: K2 (8,611 m) is the highest peak in Pakistan.
recs.rel: Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is the second highest mountain in Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the kunniyat (kunyah) of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
recs.facts: The Prophet (SAW) was called Abu al-Qasim after his first son Qasim.
recs.rel: His other sons Abdullah and Ibrahim also died in infancy.

recs.q: What is the largest bird in the world?
recs.facts: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird, up to about 2.7 m tall.
recs.rel: The ostrich cannot fly but is the fastest running bird.

recs.q: What is the largest city of Sindh by population?
recs.facts: Karachi is the capital of Sindh and the largest city in Pakistan.
recs.rel: Hyderabad is the second largest city of Sindh.

recs.q: What is the length of a marathon race?
recs.facts: The standard marathon distance is 26 miles 385 yards, which is 42.195 km.
recs.rel: The distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word Hadith?
recs.facts: In Arabic, Hadith means speech, statement, report or narration.
recs.rel: Technically, a Hadith is a report of the words, actions or approvals of the Prophet (SAW).

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word Quran?
opts: That which is recited or read
recs.facts: The word Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite.
recs.rel: Al-Furqan (the Criterion) and Al-Huda (the Guidance) are other names of the Quran.

recs.q: What is the lower house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
recs.facts: The National Assembly is the lower house and its members are directly elected by the people.
recs.rel: The upper house of Pakistan's Parliament is the Senate.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Al-Feel?
recs.facts: Al-Feel is Arabic for the elephant and is the name of Surah 105 of the Quran.
recs.rel: The surah describes the army of Abraha with elephants that attacked the Kaaba in the year of the Prophet's birth.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Ayat?
recs.facts: Ayat is the plural of ayah, which means a sign or a verse of the Quran.
recs.rel: The Quran has 114 surahs and 6,236 ayat according to the common count.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Badr?
recs.facts: Badr in Arabic means the full moon.
recs.rel: The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) near a well named Badr.

recs.q: What is a flea?
recs.facts: A flea is a small wingless jumping insect that feeds on the blood of animals.
recs.rel: Fleas can jump many times their own body length.

recs.q: What is Hudaibiya?
opts: A place near Makkah where a treaty was signed
recs.facts: Hudaibiya is a place near Makkah where the treaty between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraish was signed in 6 AH.
recs.rel: The Treaty of Hudaibiya set a ten-year truce and paved the way for the conquest of Makkah.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Islam?
opts: Submission to the will of Allah
recs.facts: Islam means submission and obedience to Allah, and the root also gives the sense of peace.
recs.rel: A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Maghfirat?
recs.facts: Maghfirat is Arabic for forgiveness or pardon.
recs.rel: Allah's name Al-Ghafoor means the Most Forgiving.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word obvious?
recs.facts: Something obvious is easy to see or understand and is clear to everyone.
recs.rel: Its opposite is obscure or hidden.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Quran?
recs.facts: Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite, so it means that which is recited.
recs.rel: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Riba in Islam?
recs.facts: Riba means increase and refers to interest or usury on loans, which Islam prohibits.
recs.rel: The prohibition of riba is stated in Surah Al-Baqarah.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Zakat?
recs.facts: Zakat means purification and growth, as paying it purifies a person's wealth.
recs.rel: Zakat is paid at 2.5 percent of savings held above the nisab for a year.

recs.q: What is the most populated city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: Peshawar is the provincial capital and the largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by population.
recs.rel: Mardan is among the next largest cities of the province.

recs.q: What is the multiplicative inverse of a non-zero number A?
recs.facts: The multiplicative inverse of A is the number which gives 1 when multiplied by A. Since A times 1/A = 1, it is 1/A.
recs.rel: Zero has no multiplicative inverse.

recs.q: Which pamphlet did Chaudhry Rehmat Ali write in 1933?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali wrote the pamphlet Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever in 1933.
recs.rel: In it he coined the name Pakistan.

recs.q: Who was the father of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

recs.q: What is the name of Pakistan's unmanned combat aerial vehicle?
recs.facts: Burraq is the armed drone developed by Pakistan and was first used in combat in 2015.
recs.rel: Shahpar is another Pakistani drone used mainly for surveillance.

recs.q: What is the border line between Pakistan's Punjab and India's Punjab called?
recs.facts: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 and divides Punjab between Pakistan and India.
recs.rel: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

recs.q: What is the name of the parliament of Finland?
recs.facts: The parliament of Finland is called the Eduskunta.
recs.rel: Storting is Norway's parliament and Riksdag is Sweden's.

recs.q: What is the name of the parliament of Japan?
recs.facts: The national parliament of Japan is called the Diet (Kokkai).
recs.rel: The Diet has two houses, the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.

recs.q: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Jasmine (Chambeli) is the national flower of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Its Latin name is Jasminum officinale.

recs.q: What is the national fruit of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The mango is the national fruit of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan is among the largest producers of mangoes in the world.

recs.q: What is the national game of Canada?
recs.facts: Canada officially declared lacrosse its national summer sport and ice hockey its national winter sport in 1994.
recs.rel: Ice hockey is also an official national sport, so questions may accept either depending on the options.

recs.q: What was the Nehru Report (1928)?
opts: Constitutional proposals for India drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru
recs.facts: The Nehru Report of 1928 was a set of constitutional proposals drafted by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru. It rejected separate electorates for Muslims.
recs.rel: Muhammad Ali Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

recs.q: What was the old name of Attock city?
recs.facts: Attock city was known as Campbellpur after Sir Colin Campbell.
recs.rel: Its old name was restored to Attock in 1978.

recs.q: What was the old name of Faisalabad?
recs.facts: Faisalabad was called Lyallpur after Sir James Lyall.
recs.rel: It was renamed in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: What was the old name of Sri Lanka?
recs.facts: Sri Lanka was known as Ceylon until it was renamed in 1972.
recs.rel: Burma is the old name of Myanmar and Siam of Thailand.

recs.q: Which is the oldest university of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The University of the Punjab, Lahore was founded in 1882 and is the oldest in Pakistan.
recs.rel: The University of Karachi was founded in 1951.

recs.q: What is the sign of the product of a positive number and a negative number?
recs.facts: A positive times a negative is always negative, for example 3 x (-2) = -6.
recs.rel: The product of two negative numbers is positive.

recs.q: What is the real name of Imam Bukhari?
recs.facts: Imam Bukhari's full name was Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari. He compiled the collection Sahih al-Bukhari.
recs.rel: Imam Bukhari was born in 810 CE in Bukhara and his Sahih is regarded as the most authentic hadith collection.

recs.q: What is the third pillar of Islam?
recs.facts: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Zakat is the third.
recs.rel: Zakat is generally 2.5 percent of qualifying savings held for a year.

recs.q: What is the shape of a basketball court?
recs.facts: A basketball court is a rectangle, 28 m long and 15 m wide in international play.
recs.rel: A basketball team has five players on court at a time.

recs.q: Which is the shortest surah of the Quran?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Kausar has only 3 verses and 10 words, making it the shortest surah.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 verses.

recs.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
recs.facts: The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone, about 3 mm long.
recs.rel: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone in the body.

recs.q: Which is the smallest planet of the solar system?
recs.facts: Mercury has a diameter of about 4,880 km, the smallest of the eight planets.
recs.rel: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

recs.q: What is the sound made by an eagle called?
recs.facts: An eagle's call is described as a screech or shrill cry.
recs.rel: Owls hoot while lions roar.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of curious?
recs.facts: Curious means eager to know or learn, which is the meaning of inquisitive.
recs.rel: Its opposite is incurious or indifferent.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of literal?
recs.facts: Literal means following the exact, word-for-word meaning, so exact is the closest synonym.
recs.rel: Its opposite is figurative.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of possession?
recs.facts: Possession means the state of having or owning something, so ownership is a synonym.
recs.rel: The word can also mean a thing that is owned, such as property.

recs.q: Which title of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) means Mercy for all the Worlds?
recs.facts: Rahmatul-lil-Alameen means Mercy for the Worlds and is a title of the Prophet (PBUH) taken from the Quran, Surah Al-Anbiya.
recs.rel: Khatam-un-Nabiyyin means Seal of the Prophets.

recs.q: What is the total number of rukus in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran is divided into 558 rukus (sections), a division mainly used in the Indian subcontinent.
recs.rel: The Quran is also divided into 30 paras.

recs.q: How many months are there in the Islamic calendar?
recs.facts: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is lunar and has 12 months, starting with Muharram.
recs.rel: It began with the Hijra of the Prophet (PBUH) in 622 CE.

recs.q: What are the Upper House (Senate) and Lower House (National Assembly) of Pakistan jointly called?
recs.facts: Together with the President, the Senate and the National Assembly form the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora.
recs.rel: The Senate of Pakistan has 96 members.

recs.q: What is the value of cos 0 degrees?
recs.facts: At 0 degrees the adjacent side equals the hypotenuse, so cos 0 = 1.
recs.rel: sin 0 = 0 and tan 0 = 0.

recs.q: Approximately what percentage of the adult human body is water?
recs.facts: Water makes up about 60 percent of an adult's body weight.
recs.rel: Infants have a higher share, around 75 percent.

recs.q: Which strip of land separates Pakistan from Central Asia (Tajikistan)?
recs.facts: The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan and Central Asia.
recs.rel: The corridor was created as a buffer between British India and Russian Empire in the 19th century.

recs.q: What type of state did Afghanistan act as for a long time between the British and Russian empires?
recs.facts: Afghanistan stood between British India and Tsarist Russia and served as a buffer state.
recs.rel: The Durand Line was drawn in 1893 as its border with British India.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Urwa bin Zubair with Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
recs.facts: Urwa was the son of Hazrat Zubair bin Awwam and Hazrat Asma, who was the sister of Hazrat Ayesha. This made Urwa her nephew.
recs.rel: Urwa bin Zubair is one of the seven famous jurists of Madina and a major narrator of hadith from his aunt Hazrat Ayesha.

recs.q: What was the caliphate number of Hazrat Umar (RA) among the Rashidun caliphs?
recs.facts: The order of the Rashidun caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them). Umar was therefore the second.
recs.rel: Hazrat Umar (RA) ruled from 634 to 644 AD and is called Al-Farooq.

recs.q: What was the most important event of 8 AH in Islamic history?
recs.facts: The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 AD). The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah and cleansed the Kaaba of idols.
recs.rel: The Battle of Hunain and the siege of Taif followed soon after the conquest of Makkah in the same year.

recs.q: Which battle of the American Civil War, fought in 1863, was the turning point of the war?
recs.facts: The Battle of Gettysburg was fought in July 1863 in Pennsylvania and ended in a Union victory over the Confederate army of Robert E. Lee. It is widely seen as the turning point of the war.
recs.rel: Abraham Lincoln delivered the famous Gettysburg Address at the battlefield in November 1863.

recs.q: What was the religion of Najashi, the king of Abyssinia (Habsha) who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
recs.facts: Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia was a Christian king. He protected the Muslim emigrants and refused to hand them over to the Quraish.
recs.rel: The Muslims made their first migration to Abyssinia in 5th year of the Prophethood.

recs.q: When was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency?
recs.facts: Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935. Sir Shah Nawaz Bhutto and others had campaigned for the separation.
recs.rel: The Quaid-e-Azam had included the separation of Sindh in his Fourteen Points of 1929.

recs.q: In which year did the Khilafat Movement start in India?
recs.facts: The movement started in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliph and the Muslim holy places after the First World War. Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.
recs.rel: The movement ended after Turkey abolished the caliphate in 1924.

recs.q: For what purpose is Namaz-e-Istisqa offered?
recs.facts: Istisqa means asking for water. Muslims offer this special prayer when there is drought and ask Allah for rain.
recs.rel: The prayer for a solar or lunar eclipse is called Namaz-e-Kusuf or Khusuf.

recs.q: In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India?
recs.facts: Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 during the Second World War. He offered dominion status after the war, which the Congress and the Muslim League rejected.
recs.rel: The Cabinet Mission was a different mission that came to India in 1946.

recs.q: In which year was the first census of Pakistan held?
recs.facts: The first census of Pakistan was held in 1951. Later censuses were held in 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998 and 2017.
recs.rel: The 2017 census was the first one after nearly 19 years since the 1998 census.

recs.q: When was the All India Muslim League established?
recs.facts: The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference. Nawab Salimullah Khan hosted the meeting.
recs.rel: Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk presided and Sir Agha Khan was the first honorary president.

recs.q: At what age did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) place the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) in the Kaaba?
recs.facts: When the Quraish rebuilt the Kaaba, they disputed who would put the Black Stone in place. The Prophet, aged 35, settled the matter by placing it on a cloth carried by all the tribal chiefs.
recs.rel: The Quraish called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and accepted his decision.

recs.q: In which year of the Hijra was the Qibla changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem) to the Kaaba?
recs.facts: The command to turn towards the Kaaba came in 2 AH, about sixteen to seventeen months after the Hijra, while the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer in Madina.
recs.rel: The mosque where this happened is known as Masjid Qiblatain.

recs.q: When and where was the Red Cross founded?
recs.facts: The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 on the initiative of Henry Dunant.
recs.rel: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

recs.q: Where are the Caucasus mountains located?
opts: Between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea
Between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf
Between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea
Between the Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea
recs.facts: The Caucasus range lies between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea and forms a boundary between Europe and Asia.
recs.rel: Its highest peak is Mount Elbrus in Russia.

recs.q: Where did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests on 28 May 1998?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan.
recs.rel: 28 May is observed every year as Youm-e-Takbeer.

recs.q: Which country is the place of origin of the game of squash?
recs.facts: Squash originated in England at Harrow School in the 19th century.
recs.rel: Pakistan dominated world squash through Hashim Khan, Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan.

recs.q: Lake Saif-ul-Malook is situated in which valley?
recs.facts: Lake Saif-ul-Malook lies near Naran in the Kaghan Valley, Mansehra district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It is at about 3,200 metres above sea level.

recs.q: In which city is the Mahabat Khan Mosque located?
recs.facts: The Mahabat Khan Mosque is a Mughal-era mosque in the old walled city of Peshawar, built in the 17th century.
recs.rel: It was built by Mahabat Khan, a governor of Peshawar under Shah Jahan.

recs.q: Where is the Gulf of Siam (Gulf of Thailand) located?
recs.facts: The Gulf of Siam, now usually called the Gulf of Thailand, is an arm of the South China Sea bordered by Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.
recs.rel: Bangkok lies at the head of the gulf.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International?
recs.facts: Amnesty International has its international secretariat in London.
recs.rel: It was founded in London in 1961 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

recs.q: Where is the famous Koh-i-Noor diamond kept today?
recs.facts: The Koh-i-Noor is set in a crown that is part of the British Crown Jewels displayed at the Tower of London.
recs.rel: Pakistan, India and others have claimed that it should be returned.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of NATO?
recs.facts: NATO has its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
recs.rel: NATO was founded in 1949, and its headquarters was in Paris before 1967.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
recs.facts: The OIC secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
recs.rel: Its intended permanent seat is East Jerusalem once it is liberated.

recs.q: Where is the shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam?
recs.facts: The shrine of Hazrat Shah Rukn-e-Alam is in Multan.
recs.rel: It is famed for its Tughlaq-era architecture.

recs.q: In which city is the Pakistan Steel Mills located?
recs.facts: Pakistan Steel Mills was built at Pipri near Karachi with Soviet help.
recs.rel: It began production in the early 1980s.

recs.q: Which angel brought revelation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jibrael (Gabriel, AS) conveyed the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.

recs.q: Which province of Pakistan is known as Bab-ul-Islam (Gateway of Islam)?
recs.facts: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam because Islam first entered the subcontinent there with Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 AD.
recs.rel: The question was asked about a city, but the standard answer is the province Sindh.

recs.q: Which continent is called the ice desert?
