recs.facts: Antarctica receives very little precipitation and is covered in ice, so it is called the ice desert.
recs.rel: It is the coldest, driest and windiest continent.

recs.q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of SAARC?
recs.facts: SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Myanmar is not a member.
recs.rel: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985 and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.

recs.q: Ban Ki-moon, former Secretary-General of the United Nations, belongs to which country?
recs.facts: Ban Ki-moon is a South Korean diplomat who served as UN Secretary-General from 2007 to 2016.
recs.rel: He was succeeded as Secretary-General by Antonio Guterres of Portugal.

recs.q: Which country is regarded as the birthplace of modern football (soccer)?
recs.facts: Modern football rules were codified in England in 1863 when the Football Association was formed.
recs.rel: Ancient ball games such as the Chinese cuju existed earlier, so sources differ on the earliest origin.

recs.q: Which international day is observed on 21 September?
opts: World Peace Day (International Day of Peace)
recs.facts: The UN International Day of Peace is observed on 21 September each year.
recs.rel: World Teachers Day is on 5 October and World Food Day on 16 October.

recs.q: The United Nations recognises 12 July as which day?
recs.facts: The UN declared 12 July Malala Day in 2013, Malala Yousafzai's birthday.
recs.rel: World Population Day falls on 11 July.

recs.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by volume?
recs.facts: Lake Baikal in Russia holds about 20 percent of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.
recs.rel: Baikal is also the deepest lake in the world.

recs.q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
recs.facts: Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of about 1,642 metres.
recs.rel: Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake.

recs.q: Which is the biggest river of South America?
recs.facts: The Amazon is South America's biggest river and the largest in the world by volume of water.
recs.rel: The Mississippi is a river of North America.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
recs.facts: The word follows the rule i before e except after c: chief.
recs.rel: Chef is a different word meaning a professional cook.

recs.q: Which is the largest bay in the world by area?
recs.facts: The Bay of Bengal, about 2.2 million square km, is generally considered the largest bay in the world.
recs.rel: Hudson Bay is often listed as the second largest.

recs.q: Which is the longest freshwater lake in the world?
recs.facts: Lake Tanganyika in Africa is about 676 km long, the longest freshwater lake in the world.
recs.rel: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world.

recs.q: Which is the second largest continent by area?
recs.facts: Asia is the largest and Africa is second largest with about 30.3 million square km.
recs.rel: Africa is also the second most populous continent.

recs.q: Which of the following countries is a member of SAARC?
recs.facts: Bhutan is one of the eight SAARC members.
recs.rel: SAARC members are Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.

recs.q: Which provincial assembly of Pakistan has the most seats?
recs.facts: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats (297 general, 66 women, 8 non-Muslim), the most of any province.
recs.rel: Sindh has 168, KP 145 and Balochistan 65 seats.

recs.q: Which surah of the Quran does not begin with Bismillah?
recs.facts: Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'at) is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.
recs.rel: Bismillah appears twice in Surah An-Naml, once at the start and once inside verse 30.

recs.q: Which surah is described in the Quran as Ahsan-ul-Qasas (the best of stories)?
recs.facts: Surah Yusuf tells the story of Hazrat Yusuf (A.S) and Allah calls it the best of stories.
recs.rel: Surah Yusuf is the 12th surah of the Quran.

recs.q: Which Surah is known as Ash-Shifa (the cure)?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Fatiha is known by many names including Ash-Shifa because it is recited for healing.
recs.rel: It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and Sab'a al-Mathani.

recs.q: In which Surah does Allah swear by time?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Asr begins with an oath by time (Wal-Asr).
recs.rel: Surah Al-Asr is the 103rd surah and has three verses.

recs.q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran?
recs.facts: Abu Lahab is named in Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) which condemns him.
recs.rel: He was the only enemy of the Prophet named in the Quran.

recs.q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar Farooq (R.A)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hafsa bint Umar (R.A) married the Prophet (PBUH) in 3 AH.
recs.rel: Hazrat Aisha was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A).

recs.q: Who proposed digging the trench in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Salman Farsi (R.A) suggested digging a trench, a Persian defence method, to protect Madina.
recs.rel: The battle took place in 5 AH.

recs.q: Who is credited with discovering the photovoltaic effect, the basis of solar energy?
recs.facts: Alexandre Edmond Becquerel observed the photovoltaic effect in 1839, which is the principle behind solar cells.
recs.rel: Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.

recs.q: Who established the Mughal rule in India?
recs.facts: Babar defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.
recs.rel: Babar was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan.

recs.q: Who founded the newspaper Dawn?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 to voice the Muslim League view.
recs.rel: Dawn moved to Karachi after the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

recs.q: Who has scored the most ODI runs for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Inzamam-ul-Haq leads Pakistan's ODI run list with 11,701 runs.
recs.rel: Mohammad Yousuf (9,554) and Saeed Anwar (8,824) follow him.

recs.q: Which country helped Pakistan build the Chashma nuclear power plant?
recs.facts: The Chashma Nuclear Power Plants in Punjab were built with Chinese assistance.
recs.rel: China also built later units such as C-3 and C-4 at Chashma.

recs.q: Which country helped the USA build relations with China in 1971?
recs.facts: Pakistan under Yahya Khan arranged the secret visit of Henry Kissinger to Beijing in July 1971.
recs.rel: President Nixon visited China in February 1972.

recs.q: Who introduced the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
recs.facts: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented it on 7 March 1949 and the Assembly passed it on 12 March 1949.
recs.rel: The Objectives Resolution later became the preamble and then Article 2A of the Constitution.

recs.q: Who introduced the presidential system in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan introduced the presidential system through the Constitution of 1962.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan became Pakistan's first military ruler in 1958.

recs.q: Who invented the electric bulb (practical incandescent lamp)?
recs.facts: Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent bulb in 1879.
recs.rel: Joseph Swan in Britain developed a similar lamp at about the same time.

recs.q: Who is Hazrat Jibrael (AS)?
recs.facts: Jibrael (AS) is the angel who brought the revelation of Allah to the prophets.
recs.rel: He first brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the cave of Hira.

recs.q: Who is known as Imam-e-Azam?
recs.facts: Imam Abu Hanifa, founder of the Hanafi school of fiqh, is called Imam-e-Azam, the greatest Imam.
recs.rel: Most Muslims of Pakistan follow the Hanafi school.

recs.q: Who is the Federal Minister for Education of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui holds the Federal Education and Professional Training portfolio in 2026.
recs.rel: Shafqat Mahmood held the post in 2021-22 when candidates sat the test.

recs.q: Who is the fastest man on earth (100 m world record holder)?
recs.facts: Usain Bolt of Jamaica holds the 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009.
recs.rel: He also holds the 200 m record of 19.19 seconds.

recs.q: Who is the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)?
recs.facts: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP in Lahore in 1967.
recs.rel: Benazir Bhutto later became the first woman prime minister of a Muslim country.

recs.q: Who is the Secretary General (head) of the Arab League?
recs.facts: Nabil Fahmy took office as Secretary General on 1 July 2026 for a five-year term.
recs.rel: His predecessor Ahmed Aboul Gheit served from 2016 to 2026.

recs.q: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.
recs.rel: The President appoints the service chiefs on the advice of the Prime Minister.

recs.q: Who signed the Tashkent Declaration on behalf of Pakistan?
recs.facts: President Ayub Khan signed it on 10 January 1966 with Indian PM Lal Bahadur Shastri.
recs.rel: Shastri died in Tashkent the next day.

recs.q: Who took over as martial law administrator after Ayub Khan resigned in 1969?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan handed power to the army chief General Yahya Khan in March 1969, who imposed martial law.
recs.rel: Yahya Khan ruled until December 1971.

recs.q: Who was the first captain of the Pakistan cricket team?
recs.facts: Abdul Hafeez Kardar captained Pakistan in its first Test series in India in 1952.
recs.rel: Under Kardar, Pakistan won its first Test on English soil at The Oval in 1954.

recs.q: Who was the first Governor General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Jinnah took the oath as the first Governor General of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
recs.rel: He held the office until his death on 11 September 1948.

recs.q: Who was the last Governor General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Iskander Mirza was the last Governor General and became the first President when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
recs.rel: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.

recs.q: Who was the first to translate the Holy Quran into Urdu?
recs.facts: Shah Abdul Qadir Dehlvi produced the first idiomatic Urdu translation, Mudih-ul-Quran, in the 1790s.
recs.rel: Sources differ: his brother Shah Rafiuddin made an earlier literal Urdu translation, but most Pakistani textbooks credit Shah Abdul Qadir.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim country?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1988, the first woman to head a Muslim country's government.
recs.rel: She was Prime Minister twice, in 1988-90 and 1993-96.

recs.q: Who was the founder of the Indian National Congress?
recs.facts: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885.
recs.rel: Its first session in Bombay was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

recs.q: Who was the last Mughal emperor of India?
recs.facts: Bahadur Shah Zafar was deposed by the British after the War of Independence of 1857.
recs.rel: He was exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.

recs.q: Who was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel?
recs.facts: Hazrat Isa (AS) was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel before Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
recs.rel: Hazrat Isa (AS) was given the Injeel.

recs.q: Who was the commander of the Quraish army in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: Abu Jahl (Amr bin Hisham) led the Quraish army at Badr in 2 AH and was killed in the battle.
recs.rel: Abu Sufyan led the trade caravan that the Quraish army came to protect.

recs.q: Who won the world amateur snooker championship in 1994 for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Muhammad Yousaf won the IBSF World Amateur Snooker Championship in 1994.
recs.rel: Muhammad Asif later won the same title in 2012.

recs.q: Which people lived at Khyber at the time of the Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Khyber was a fortified oasis inhabited mainly by Jewish tribes, and the Muslims conquered it in 7 AH.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for his role in the conquest of the fort of Khyber.

recs.q: Why did the Gandhi-Jinnah talks of 1944 fail?
opts: Gandhi refused to accept the Two-Nation Theory and the Muslim demand for Pakistan
recs.facts: The talks held in Bombay in September 1944 broke down because Gandhi did not accept that Muslims were a separate nation, while Jinnah insisted on it.
recs.rel: The talks were based on the C. R. Formula proposed by Chakravarti Rajagopalachari.

recs.q: Why is the colour of the sky blue?
opts: Scattering of sunlight by air molecules
Absorption of blue light by clouds
recs.facts: Air molecules scatter short wavelength light (blue) much more than long wavelengths (red). This is called Rayleigh scattering.
recs.rel: At sunrise and sunset the sky looks red because light travels through more air and blue is scattered away.

recs.q: With the help of which country was Warsak Dam built?
recs.facts: Warsak Dam on the Kabul River near Peshawar was built in the 1950s with Canadian aid under the Colombo Plan.
recs.rel: Candidates often said China, but the dam was Canadian-assisted.

recs.q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train moves at twice the speed of the car. How much time will the train take to cover 60 km?
recs.facts: Train speed is 120 km/h. Time = 60 / 120 = 0.5 hour = 30 minutes.
recs.rel: Time = distance divided by speed.

recs.q: A median divides a triangle into two triangles of what ratio of areas?
recs.facts: A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, so the two triangles have equal bases and the same height, hence equal areas.
recs.rel: The three medians meet at the centroid, which divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1.

recs.q: Ali walks 4 meters towards the north and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now?
recs.facts: A left turn from north points him to the west.
recs.rel: Anticlockwise order of directions is North, West, South, East.

recs.q: Arrange the letters YEBATU into a meaningful word.
recs.facts: The letters Y, E, B, A, T, U rearrange to BEAUTY.
recs.rel: BEAUTY has 6 letters, of which E, A and U are vowels.

recs.q: Convert 30 degrees into radians.
recs.facts: Radians = degrees x pi / 180 = 30 pi / 180 = pi / 6.
recs.rel: 180 degrees equals pi radians.

recs.q: Convert 450 degrees into radians.
recs.rel: 450 degrees is one full turn plus 90 degrees.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Angle, Triangle, Square, Rectangle.
recs.facts: Triangle, square and rectangle are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a closed figure.
recs.rel: A triangle has three sides and the sum of its angles is 180 degrees.

recs.q: How many dimensions does volume have?
recs.facts: Volume measures space in length, width and height, so it is three dimensional.
recs.rel: Volume is measured in cubic units such as cubic metres.

recs.q: How many months of the year have 30 days?
recs.facts: April, June, September and November have 30 days, which makes 4.
recs.rel: Candidates wrote 7, but that is the number of 31-day months.

recs.q: How many roots does a linear equation in one variable have?
recs.facts: A linear equation ax + b = 0 with a not zero has exactly one solution x = -b / a.
recs.rel: A quadratic equation has at most two roots.

recs.q: How many basic trigonometric functions are there?
recs.facts: They are sine, cosine, tangent, cosecant, secant and cotangent.
recs.rel: Cosecant, secant and cotangent are reciprocals of sine, cosine and tangent.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in: A W U E A P U?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, U, E, A and U, which is 5. W and P are consonants.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: If 5 boys write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how much time will one boy take to write one page?
recs.facts: Each boy writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 boys write 5 pages, one page each, in 5 minutes).
recs.rel: Rate per boy is 1 page per 5 minutes.

recs.q: If 9 : m :: 2 : 8, find the value of m.
recs.rel: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means.

recs.q: If the 14th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 4th day of that month?
recs.facts: The 14th is 10 days after the 4th. 10 mod 7 = 3, so go back 3 days from Monday: Sunday, Saturday, Friday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart always fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 13th?
recs.facts: The gap is 12 days. 12 mod 7 = 5, so Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
recs.rel: The 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th fall on the same weekday as the 1st.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Saturday, what day is the 26th?
recs.facts: The gap is 24 days. 24 mod 7 = 3, so Saturday plus 3 days is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Count only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7.

recs.q: If the 2nd of a month is Saturday, what day is the 28th of that month?
recs.facts: The gap is 26 days. 26 mod 7 = 5, so Saturday plus 5 days is Thursday.
recs.rel: The 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th would all be Saturdays in this month.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th?
recs.facts: The gap is 8 days. 8 mod 7 = 1, so Monday plus 1 day is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Dates exactly 8 days apart differ by one weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 18th?
recs.facts: The gap is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 18th is also a Sunday.
recs.rel: Dates that are multiples of 7 apart share the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 23rd?
recs.facts: The gap is 19 days. 19 mod 7 = 5, so Tuesday plus 5 days is Sunday.
recs.rel: Check: the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th are Tuesdays, so the 23rd is two days before the 25th, a Sunday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 16th?
recs.facts: The gap is 12 days. 12 mod 7 = 5, so Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
recs.rel: The 11th and 18th would be Mondays, so the 16th is two days before the 18th.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd?
recs.facts: The gap is 22 days. 22 mod 7 = 1, so Monday plus 1 day is Tuesday.
recs.rel: The 22nd is also a Monday here since it is 21 days (3 weeks) after the 1st.

recs.q: A circle whose radius is 1 is called what?
recs.facts: A circle with radius equal to 1 unit is called a unit circle.
recs.rel: The unit circle centred at the origin is used to define sine and cosine in trigonometry.

recs.q: If the second day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 28th?
recs.facts: The gap is 26 days. 26 mod 7 = 5, so Sunday plus 5 days is Friday.
recs.rel: The 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th are Sundays in this month.

recs.q: If the letters BEYTUA are rearranged to make a correct word, what is the last letter of that word?
recs.facts: The letters rearrange to BEAUTY, whose last letter is Y.
recs.rel: Beauty is a six-letter English word and the scrambled form BEYTUA uses exactly the same letters.

recs.q: If y = 2x + 1 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
recs.facts: Substitute x = 2: y = 2 x 2 + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5.
recs.rel: An equation of the form y = mx + c represents a straight line with slope m.

recs.q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day will tomorrow be?
recs.facts: If yesterday was Sunday, today is Monday, so tomorrow is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Tomorrow is always two days after yesterday.

recs.q: In a bus 30 passengers are travelling and 2/3 of them are male. How many males are in the bus?
recs.rel: The remaining 10 passengers (1/3) are female.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
recs.facts: Girls = 500 - 360 = 140. Percentage of girls = 140 / 500 x 100 = 28%.
recs.rel: The boys make up 72% of the students.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters PEOLARD to form a correct English word.
recs.facts: The letters P, E, O, L, A, R, D rearrange to make LEOPARD, a big cat.
recs.rel: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, and it is a strong climber.

recs.q: Solve for x: 2x - 5 = x + 7
recs.facts: Move x to the left and 5 to the right: 2x - x = 7 + 5, so x = 12.

recs.q: If y = 9x - 5 and x = 1, what is the value of y?
recs.facts: Substitute x = 1: y = 9 x 1 - 5 = 9 - 5 = 4.
recs.rel: Always substitute the value first and then do multiplication before subtraction.

recs.q: The age of Ali is 6 years and Sara is three times as old as Ali. What will Ali's age be after 6 years?
recs.facts: Ali is 6 now, so after 6 years he will be 6 + 6 = 12. Sara's age does not matter for this question.
recs.rel: Sara is currently 18 years old.

recs.q: Water is to ice as milk is to what?
recs.facts: Ice is the solid form obtained from water, and cheese is the solid product obtained from milk.
recs.rel: Cheese is made by curdling milk and separating the solid curds from the whey.

recs.q: What is 80% of 80?
recs.rel: 80% is the same as the fraction 4/5.

recs.q: What is a triangle with all sides equal called?
recs.facts: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles of 60 degrees each.
recs.rel: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and a scalene triangle has no equal sides.

recs.q: What is the derivative of x with respect to x?
recs.facts: By the power rule, d(x^1)/dx = 1 x x^0 = 1.
recs.rel: The derivative of x squared is 2x.

recs.q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
recs.facts: The area of a triangle is half the area of the parallelogram with the same base and height.
recs.rel: The area of a rectangle is length x width.

recs.q: What is the geometric mean of 3 and 12?
recs.facts: Geometric mean = square root of (3 x 12) = square root of 36 = 6.
recs.rel: The arithmetic mean of 3 and 12 is 7.5, which is always at least the geometric mean.

recs.q: What is the perimeter of a square of side 4 cm?
recs.facts: A square has four equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 x 4 = 16 cm.
recs.rel: The area of this square would be 16 square cm.

recs.q: What is the real part of -i(2i - 3)?
recs.facts: -i(2i - 3) = -2i squared + 3i = 2 + 3i, since i squared = -1. The real part is 2.
recs.rel: In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part.

recs.q: Which word is formed by the alphabet positions 18, 5, 19, 20?
recs.facts: Positions 18, 5, 19, 20 are R, E, S, T.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters, with Z at position 26.

recs.q: When Ali was 3, his sister's age was four times his age. How old is Ali's sister when Ali is 12?
recs.facts: When Ali was 3 his sister was 12, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 12 she is 12 + 9 = 21.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people stays constant over time.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ?
recs.facts: Each term is double the previous plus 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.
recs.rel: The terms are also 2^2 - 2, 2^3 - 2, ... so the next is 2^7 - 2 = 126.

recs.q: After how many years did East Pakistan (Bangladesh) separate from West Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan was created in 1947 and Bangladesh emerged in December 1971, which is 24 years later.
recs.rel: The separation followed the 1971 war and the fall of Dhaka on 16 December 1971.

recs.q: After which battle did the disbelievers become unable to attack Madinah (and Makkah-based enemies could no longer launch attacks)?
recs.facts: After the failed siege in the Battle of Khandaq the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said the Quraysh would no longer attack the Muslims, and the Muslims would march against them.
recs.rel: The Battle of Khandaq took place in 5 AH and a trench was dug on the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

recs.q: Against which country did Sachin Tendulkar score his 100th international century?
recs.facts: Tendulkar scored his 100th international century, 114 runs, against Bangladesh in the Asia Cup at Mirpur on 16 March 2012.
recs.rel: He is the only player to score 100 international centuries.

recs.q: Pakistan won the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final against which team?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval, London, on 18 June 2017.
recs.rel: Sarfraz Ahmed captained Pakistan and Fakhar Zaman scored 114 in the final.

recs.q: Along which parallel of latitude does the border between Canada and the United States largely run (west of the Great Lakes)?
recs.facts: The land border from the Pacific coast to Lake of the Woods follows the 49th parallel north, set by the Treaty of 1818 and later agreements.
recs.rel: The 38th parallel is the better-known line that originally divided North and South Korea.

recs.q: Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Under the 1973 Constitution the Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, then appointed by the President.
recs.rel: A candidate needs a majority of the total membership of the National Assembly.

recs.q: How many books are included in the Sihah Sittah (Sahih Sitta), the six authentic collections of hadith?
recs.facts: Sihah Sittah literally means the six correct books. The six collections are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai and Ibn Majah.
recs.rel: Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is regarded as the most authentic of them.

recs.q: How many manzils (stages) is the Holy Quran divided into?
recs.facts: The Quran is divided into seven manzils so that it can be recited in one week. Each manzil is read on one day of the week.
recs.rel: The Quran is also divided into 30 paras (juz).

recs.q: How many masarif (heads of expenditure) of zakat are mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
recs.facts: Surah At-Tawbah (9:60) names eight categories of zakat recipients: the poor, the needy, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, the cause of Allah and the wayfarer.
recs.rel: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.

recs.q: How many Nishan-e-Haider awards have been given so far, according to the commonly cited count?
recs.facts: The commonly cited current count is 11 recipients, all awarded posthumously. Older sources say 10, and the status of the eleventh name is sometimes disputed.
recs.rel: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award of Pakistan.

recs.q: In which surah is the longest verse of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The longest verse is Ayat ad-Dayn (verse 282) about written contracts of debt, in Surah Al-Baqarah.
recs.rel: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of the same surah.

recs.q: How old was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when his mother, Hazrat Amina, passed away?
recs.facts: Hazrat Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet (SAW) was about six years old.
recs.rel: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib then cared for him until he died when the Prophet (SAW) was eight.

recs.q: From which city did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate in 622 AD?
recs.facts: In 622 AD the Prophet (SAW) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib), which is called the Hijrat.
recs.rel: The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this migration.

recs.q: In which district of Balochistan is the Chamalang coal mine located?
recs.facts: The Chamalang coalfield lies in north-central Balochistan, mostly in Loralai district and extending towards Kohlu and Barkhan.
recs.rel: Some reports place the mine in the newly formed Duki district, which was carved out of Loralai; sources differ.

recs.q: In which district of Pakistan is the Chashma nuclear power plant located?
recs.facts: The Chashma Nuclear Power Complex stands near Chashma barrage on the Indus in Mianwali district, Punjab.
recs.rel: Chashma Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was built with Chinese help.

recs.q: For which achievement did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize in 2014?
recs.facts: She received the Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for the right of children and girls to education.
recs.rel: At 17 she is the youngest Nobel laureate in history and shared the prize with Kailash Satyarthi.

recs.q: In which Islamic month did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
recs.facts: Imam Hussain (RA) was martyred at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH, the day of Ashura.
recs.rel: The year of the event, 61 AH, fell during the rule of Yazid.

recs.q: In which Islamic month was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.
recs.rel: It is called Yaum ul Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is Ghotki located?
recs.facts: Ghotki is a city and district in northern Sindh, on the border with Punjab.
recs.rel: Ghotki lies on the Indus highway between Sukkur and Rahim Yar Khan.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan become a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
recs.facts: Pakistan (with India) was admitted as a full member at the SCO summit in Astana, Kazakhstan, in June 2017.
recs.rel: Pakistan had been an SCO observer since 2005.

recs.q: In which year was the M.A.O. School at Aligarh raised to the status of a College?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the school in 1875, and it became Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1877.
recs.rel: The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

recs.q: In which year was the war of independence (the Mutiny) fought in the subcontinent?
recs.facts: The War of Independence broke out at Meerut in May 1857 against East India Company rule.
recs.rel: It ended with the British Crown taking direct control of India in 1858.

recs.q: In which year were the modern Olympic Games first held?
recs.facts: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Baron Pierre de Coubertin revived the Games.
recs.rel: The International Olympic Committee was founded in 1894.

recs.q: On which prophet was the Torah (Taurat) revealed?
recs.facts: The Torah was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS) for the Bani Israil.
recs.rel: The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS), the Injeel on Hazrat Isa (AS) and the Quran on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

recs.q: Rooh Ullah (Ruhullah) is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah, the Spirit of Allah, because he was born by Allah's command without a father.
recs.rel: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) Khalilullah.

recs.q: The first 5 verses revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belong to which surah?
recs.facts: The first five ayats revealed in the Cave of Hira begin with Iqra bismi rabbika and are from Surah Al-Alaq.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Alaq is also called Surah Iqra.

recs.q: The OIC is an organization of which countries?
recs.facts: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is the collective voice of Muslim countries of the world.
recs.rel: The OIC was founded in 1969 in Rabat and its headquarters are in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: The Secretary-General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, belongs to which country?
recs.facts: Antonio Guterres, the ninth UN Secretary-General, is a former Prime Minister of Portugal.
recs.rel: His term ends on 31 December 2026 and the selection of his successor is under way; before him Ban Ki-moon of South Korea held the post.

recs.q: The Silk Road connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: The Karakoram Highway follows part of the ancient Silk Road and links Pakistan to China through the Khunjerab Pass.
recs.rel: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is a modern project built along this old route.

recs.q: Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
recs.facts: The treaty gave the three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan and the three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, to India.
recs.rel: The treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 and mediated by the World Bank.

recs.q: What does the Arabic word Badr (Badar) mean?
recs.facts: Badr means the full moon in Arabic. The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought at a place of that name near Madina.
recs.rel: The Battle of Badr was the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraysh.

recs.q: What is 28 May, the day Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998, known as?
recs.facts: On 28 May 1998 Pakistan carried out nuclear tests at Chagai, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer. Takbeer means proclaiming the greatness of God.
recs.rel: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear power and the first Muslim nuclear state.

recs.q: What does the word Pakistan mean?
recs.facts: Pakistan is a Persian and Urdu word made of pak (pure) and stan (land), so it means land of the pure. It is not related to truth.
recs.rel: The name was proposed by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.

recs.q: What does wuzu (wudu) mean?
recs.facts: Wuzu is the ritual ablution in which the face, arms, head and feet are washed or wiped before prayer. It is a condition for offering Salah.
recs.rel: Wuzu comes from an Arabic word connected with cleanliness and brightness.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word voyage?
recs.facts: A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space. Journey is the closest meaning.
recs.rel: The word voyage comes from Old French voiage.

recs.q: Another name for the Manila Pact of 1954 is:
recs.facts: The Manila Pact created the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO), signed in Manila in September 1954.
recs.rel: SEATO was dissolved in 1977.

recs.q: What does SAFTA stand for?
recs.facts: SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area. It is a trade arrangement among the member states of SAARC to reduce customs duties.
recs.rel: SAFTA was signed in 2004 and came into force on 1 January 2006.

recs.q: What is Sahih Muslim?
recs.facts: Sahih Muslim is a collection of authentic Hadith compiled by Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj.
recs.rel: Together with Sahih Bukhari it forms the Sahihain.

recs.q: Which name is given to the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) in the Quran?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khandaq (5 AH) is also called Ahzab (the Confederates), after the allied tribes who besieged Madinah.
recs.rel: The trench was dug on the advice of Salman al-Farsi.

recs.q: What is the capital of Balochistan?
recs.facts: Quetta is the provincial capital and largest city of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Quetta is known as the Fruit Garden of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word compassion?
recs.facts: Compassion is a feeling of concern and pity for the suffering of others. Sympathy is the closest meaning.
recs.rel: Its opposite is cruelty or ruthlessness.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word inhabitant?
recs.facts: An inhabitant is a person who lives permanently in a place. Resident has the same meaning.
recs.rel: The word comes from Latin inhabitare, meaning to dwell in.

recs.q: What is the special unstitched cloth worn by pilgrims during Hajj called?
recs.facts: Ihram is the two-piece unstitched white cloth worn by male pilgrims during Hajj and Umrah. Wearing it begins the state of ihram.
recs.rel: Women pilgrims wear ordinary modest clothing and do not wear a special unstitched sheet.

recs.q: In which month and Hijri year did the conquest of Makkah (Fatah Makkah) take place?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah with an army of about ten thousand in Ramadan 8 AH, traditionally dated 20 Ramadan.
recs.rel: The conquest took place almost without bloodshed and the Prophet (PBUH) granted a general amnesty.

recs.q: On which date was the Battle of Badr fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraish.
recs.rel: It is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

recs.q: What is the term of a Senator in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Senators are elected for a six-year term, and half retire every three years.
recs.rel: The Senate itself is a permanent house and is never dissolved.

recs.q: What is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
recs.facts: The Hijri calendar begins with Muharram, and 1 Muharram is the Islamic New Year.
recs.rel: The calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from the Hijrah to Madina.

recs.q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
recs.facts: Tirich Mir in Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, about 7,708 metres high.
recs.rel: Some Pakistani textbooks give 7,690 m, so sources differ slightly.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Wudu (Wuzu)?
opts: Ablution, the ritual washing before prayer
recs.facts: Wudu means ablution, the washing of the face, hands, head and feet before prayer, from a root meaning cleanliness.
recs.rel: In the Hanafi school wudu has four faraiz, as stated in Surah Al-Maidah.

recs.q: What is the period between a person's death and the Day of Judgment called in Islam?
recs.facts: Barzakh is the intermediate stage between death and resurrection, in which the soul stays until the Day of Judgment.
recs.rel: Barzakh is also the Quranic word for a barrier, for example between two seas in Surah Ar-Rahman.

recs.q: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
recs.facts: Vatican City covers about 0.44 square km, the smallest independent state in the world. Monaco is the second smallest.
recs.rel: Vatican City is an enclave inside the city of Rome, Italy.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hafsa (RA) with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA), married the Prophet (PBUH) and is a Mother of the Believers.
recs.rel: The first compiled copy of the Quran was kept with Hazrat Hafsa (RA).

recs.q: On which occasion did Hinda (wife of Abu Sufyan) accept Islam?
recs.facts: Hinda bint Utbah, who had opposed Islam at Uhud, accepted Islam when Makkah was conquered in 8 AH.
recs.rel: Her son Hazrat Muawiya (RA) later founded the Umayyad dynasty.

recs.q: On which date did the United Nations officially come into existence?
recs.facts: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, after ratification by China, France, the USSR, the UK, the USA and most other signatories. This date is celebrated as United Nations Day.
recs.rel: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk fought?
recs.facts: The Ghazwa of Tabuk took place in 9 AH (630 CE) against the Byzantine threat on the northern frontier. The Prophet (PBUH) led about 30,000 Muslims, but no fighting occurred.
recs.rel: Tabuk is also called Ghazwa-e-Usrah, the Expedition of Hardship, because of the heat and shortage of supplies.

recs.q: Where is Jabal-e-Noor (the mountain containing the Cave of Hira) located?
recs.facts: Jabal al-Noor is a mountain near Makkah in Saudi Arabia and holds the Cave of Hira where the first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, was received in this cave.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the World Bank located?
recs.facts: The World Bank has its headquarters in Washington, D.C., USA. It was set up in 1944 at the Bretton Woods conference.
recs.rel: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is also headquartered in Washington, D.C.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan does the River Soan flow?
recs.facts: The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar Plateau near Rawalpindi and Islamabad before joining the Indus.
recs.rel: The Soan valley is known for Stone Age sites.

recs.q: Which agreement was signed between Pakistan and India in January 1966 after the 1965 war?
recs.facts: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri. It ended the 1965 war and restored the earlier positions.
recs.rel: The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin mediated the talks.

recs.q: Which angels write down the good and bad deeds of every human being?
recs.facts: Kiraman Katibin are the two noble recording angels on a person's shoulders who write the deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.
recs.rel: Munkar and Nakir are the angels who question a person in the grave.

recs.q: Which batsman scored 400 not out in a Test innings?
recs.facts: Brian Lara of the West Indies scored 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004. It is the highest individual score in Test cricket.
recs.rel: Matthew Hayden's 380 was the previous record before Lara's 400.

recs.q: Which of the following Sahabah was NOT among the Ashra Mubashira (the ten companions given the glad tidings of Paradise)?
recs.facts: Talha, Zubair and Abdur Rahman bin Auf are all in the list of ten promised Paradise in one hadith. Abu Hurairah, a great narrator of hadith, is not in that list.
recs.rel: The ten are Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (RA).

recs.q: Which country is shaped like a long boot on the map?
recs.facts: Italy is a peninsula that looks like a long boot kicking the island of Sicily.
recs.rel: Rome, the capital of Italy, was the centre of the ancient Roman Empire.

recs.q: Which is the largest airport in the world by area?
opts: King Fahd International Airport (Dammam, Saudi Arabia)
recs.facts: King Fahd International Airport near Dammam covers about 776 to 780 square kilometres, far more than any other airport.
recs.rel: Denver International Airport is second largest at about 136 square kilometres.

recs.q: Which political party did Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto found?
recs.facts: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto founded the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) in Lahore.
recs.rel: The PPP was founded in November 1967 on the slogan of roti, kapra aur makan.

recs.q: Which Sahabi is known by the title Jame ul Quran (compiler of the Quran)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Uthman (RA) had the Quran copied into one standard text and sent copies to the major cities.
recs.rel: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) first gathered the Quran into one volume after the Battle of Yamama.

recs.q: Which province of Pakistan has the largest number of National Assembly seats?
recs.facts: Punjab has 141 of the 266 general seats of the National Assembly, far more than any other province.
recs.rel: The National Assembly has 336 seats in total, including 60 for women and 10 for non-Muslims.

recs.q: Who is the Federal Minister for Railways of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Muhammad Hanif Abbasi of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Railways in the current government.
recs.rel: Khawaja Saad Rafique held the same ministry in the 2022-23 coalition government.

recs.q: Who is the President of France?
recs.facts: Emmanuel Macron was first elected President of France in 2017 and re-elected in 2022; he is still in office.
recs.rel: The French President is elected for a five-year term.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom?
recs.facts: Andy Burnham became UK Prime Minister on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer stepped down as Labour leader.
recs.rel: Boris Johnson, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Prime Minister from 2019 to 2022.

recs.q: Who is the Pakistani who most recently won a Nobel Prize?
recs.facts: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, which makes her the latest Pakistani Nobel laureate.
recs.rel: Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate, winning the Physics prize in 1979.

recs.q: Who is the youngest Nobel Prize winner in history?
recs.facts: Malala Yousafzai was 17 years old when she received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, the youngest laureate ever.
recs.rel: Lawrence Bragg, aged 25, was the youngest laureate in a science field (Physics, 1915).

recs.q: Which Companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) is known as Sahib-e-Sirr (keeper of the secrets) of the Prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman (R.A) was entrusted with the Prophet's secrets, including the names of the hypocrites.
recs.rel: Hazrat Umar (R.A) used to ask him whether his own name was among the hypocrites.

recs.q: Which country opposed Pakistan's admission to the United Nations in 1947?
recs.facts: Afghanistan was the only country that voted against Pakistan's membership of the UN in September 1947. It later withdrew its objection.
recs.rel: Pakistan became the 56th member of the United Nations on 30 September 1947.

recs.q: Who recited Surah Maryam before the king Najashi of Abyssinia?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jaffar bin Abi Talib spoke for the Muslim migrants and recited verses of Surah Maryam, which moved Najashi and the bishops.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jaffar was later martyred at the Battle of Mutah and is known as Tayyar.

recs.q: Whom did Babur defeat in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526?
recs.facts: Babur defeated the Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat on 21 April 1526, which began Mughal rule in India.
recs.rel: Babur used artillery and field tactics learned from the Ottomans.

recs.q: Who was the opponent of Field Marshal Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Miss Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, contested as the joint candidate of the Combined Opposition Parties in January 1965. Ayub Khan won through the Basic Democrats electoral college.
recs.rel: She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

recs.q: Who was the first muezzin (caller to prayer) of Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA), an Abyssinian companion, gave the first adhan in Madina after the Prophet approved it. Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the adhan in a dream.
recs.rel: Hazrat Bilal (RA) also gave the adhan from the roof of the Kaaba on the day Makkah was conquered.

recs.q: Why was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in February 2017?
opts: To eliminate the remaining terrorist threat across the country
recs.facts: It was a nationwide operation of the armed forces to eliminate the remaining terrorist threat, consolidate earlier gains and strengthen border security.
recs.rel: It followed earlier operations such as Zarb-e-Azb and was launched on 22 February 2017.

recs.q: With the help of which country did Pakistan build the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
recs.facts: The JF-17 Thunder was developed jointly by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
recs.rel: JF-17 stands for Joint Fighter 17.

recs.q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When the boy is 11 years old, how old will his sister be?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 3 x 3 = 9 years, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11 she will be 11 + 6 = 17 years.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people never changes with time.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will be her age when Ali is 11 years old?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali gets 6 years older, so she will be 10 + 6 = 16 years.
recs.rel: The difference of 5 years between them never changes.

recs.q: Definitely is to absolutely as totally is to what?
recs.facts: Definitely and absolutely are synonyms, so the synonym of totally is entirely.
recs.rel: In analogy questions first find the relationship (here synonyms) and then apply it.

recs.q: How many sides does a quadrilateral (quadrangle) have?
recs.facts: Quad means four, and a quadrilateral is a closed figure with four sides.
recs.rel: The interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 12th is 11 days, and 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4. Moving 4 day(s) forward from Monday gives Friday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 12th is 10 days, and 10 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: What is the value of log 64 divided by log 4?
recs.facts: Write 64 as 4 cubed, so log 64 = 3 log 4. Therefore log 64 / log 4 = 3.
recs.rel: The change of base rule says log_b(a) = log a / log b, so this expression equals log base 4 of 64.

recs.q: Arrange the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order. Which is the 3rd letter?
recs.facts: The letters in order are A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The third letter is E.
recs.rel: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.

recs.q: Which is the odd one out: iron, brass, tin, copper?
recs.facts: Iron, tin and copper are pure metallic elements. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
recs.rel: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

recs.q: Against whom was the Battle of Uhud fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Uhud (3 AH) was fought between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh of Makkah led by Abu Sufyan.
recs.rel: The battle took place near Mount Uhud, just north of Madinah.

recs.q: The Cholistan Desert is located near which city?
recs.facts: Cholistan lies in southern Punjab and stretches from Bahawalpur towards the Indian border. It is also called Rohi.
recs.rel: Derawar Fort is a famous landmark in the Cholistan Desert.

recs.q: In which city was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto was killed after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
recs.rel: She was the first woman to head the government of a Muslim-majority country.

recs.q: Is a Pakistan Navy Lieutenant equal in rank to a Pakistan Army Captain?
opts: No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Major
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Lieutenant
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Colonel
recs.facts: A Navy Lieutenant ranks with an Army Captain and a Pakistan Air Force Flight Lieutenant.
recs.rel: A Navy Lieutenant Commander is equal to an Army Major.

recs.q: On what date was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
recs.facts: She was killed in a gun and bomb attack after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
recs.rel: She was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim-majority country.

recs.q: Which country is the world's largest producer of cotton?
recs.facts: China is the leading producer of cotton, with most of its crop grown in Xinjiang. India is second.
recs.rel: Pakistan is usually among the top five cotton producers.

recs.q: One mile is approximately equal to how many kilometres?
recs.facts: One mile is 1.609 km, which is about 1.6 km.
recs.rel: One kilometre is about 0.62 miles.

recs.q: After how many years does a leap year normally come?
recs.facts: A leap year occurs once every 4 years, when the year is divisible by 4, and adds 29 February.
recs.rel: Century years such as 1900 are leap years only if divisible by 400.

recs.q: A matrix is called a real matrix when:
opts: All its entries are real numbers
Its number of rows equals its number of columns
recs.facts: A real matrix is one whose every entry is a real number.
recs.rel: A matrix with some complex entries is called a complex matrix.

recs.q: In a rhombus, which of the following are all equal?
recs.facts: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal in length.
recs.rel: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles but are not equal unless it is a square.

recs.q: Abu al-Bashar (father of mankind) is the title of which Prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Adam (AS) is the first human being and the first Prophet, so he is called Abu al-Bashar.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Abu al-Anbiya, father of the Prophets.

recs.q: Abu Turab is the title of which companion of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) gave Hazrat Ali (RA) the title Abu Turab, meaning father of dust.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

recs.q: According to the 2023 census, which is the most populous district of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Lahore district had about 13 million people in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.
recs.rel: Karachi is larger as a city but is divided into several districts.

recs.q: What system of government did the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan establish?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister heads the government and the President is head of state.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

recs.q: Adolf Hitler was a politician of which country?
recs.facts: Hitler led Germany as head of the Nazi Party and became Chancellor in 1933.
recs.rel: Hitler was born in Austria in 1889 but gained political power in Germany.

recs.q: The Tashkent Declaration of January 1966 was signed after which war?
recs.facts: The Tashkent Declaration ended the September 1965 war between Pakistan and India.
recs.rel: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri under Soviet mediation.

recs.q: The USSR was formed after which revolution of 1917?
recs.facts: The Bolshevik (October) Revolution of 1917 led by Lenin brought the communists to power, and the USSR was formally formed in 1922.
recs.rel: The USSR broke up in December 1991.

recs.q: A number of the form a - ib, where a and b are real numbers and i is iota, is called:
recs.facts: Numbers written as a + ib or a - ib, with real a and b and i squared equal to -1, are complex numbers.
recs.rel: The numbers a + ib and a - ib are conjugates of each other.

recs.q: In which city was Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, born?
recs.facts: Arfa Karim Randhawa was born on 2 February 1995 in a village near Faisalabad, Punjab.
recs.rel: She died in January 2012 aged 16, and a software technology park in Lahore is named after her.

recs.q: Which city hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
recs.facts: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.
recs.rel: The 2022 Asian Games were held in Hangzhou, China, in 2023 after a postponement.

recs.q: At what age did Hazrat Ali (RA) accept Islam, according to the most commonly stated account?
recs.facts: Most sources say Hazrat Ali was a boy of about ten when he accepted Islam, making him among the first to do so.
recs.rel: Sources differ somewhat, with some giving 8 or 9 years, but 10 is the usual textbook figure.

recs.q: At what age did the first revelation (wahi) come to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came at the age of 40 in the Cave of Hira.
recs.rel: Gabriel (Jibreel) delivered the revelation in the month of Ramadan.

recs.q: At which place did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests in May 1998?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills of Balochistan on 28 and 30 May 1998.
recs.rel: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

recs.q: Ateeq is the title of which companion of the Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was given the title Ateeq, meaning one freed from the Fire.
recs.rel: He was also called Siddiq for confirming the Prophet's journey of Miraj.

recs.q: Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were tribes of which religion?
recs.facts: Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayzah were the Jewish tribes living around Madinah in the Prophet's time.
recs.rel: All three were later expelled or punished for breaking their agreements with the Muslims.

recs.q: Between which two leaders was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960?
recs.facts: The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Pakistan's President Ayub Khan and India's Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
recs.rel: The World Bank also signed it as a party to the treaty.

recs.q: In which river is the rare blind dolphin found?
recs.facts: The Indus river dolphin (bhulan) is blind and lives in the Indus river system.
recs.rel: Its main protected stretch in Pakistan is between Guddu and Sukkur barrages.

recs.q: Boxer Muhammad Ali belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali (born Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight boxer from Louisville, Kentucky.
recs.rel: He won the Olympic light heavyweight gold medal in Rome in 1960.

recs.q: By whom are the members of the Senate of Pakistan mainly elected?
recs.facts: Senators from each province are elected by the members of that province's assembly through single transferable vote.
recs.rel: Senators serve a six-year term and half of them retire every three years.

recs.q: By whom was Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal appointed governor of Yemen?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and judge around 10 AH.
recs.rel: The Prophet praised him as the most knowledgeable of the Ummah in halal and haram.

recs.q: Masjid Zarar (Dirar) was built by which group?
recs.facts: A group of hypocrites built it near Quba to divide the Muslims, and the Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) condemned it.
recs.rel: The Prophet ordered it to be demolished after returning from Tabuk.

recs.q: Campbellpur is the old name of which city of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The city of Attock in Punjab was called Campbellpur during British rule, after Sir Colin Campbell. It was renamed Attock in 1978.
recs.rel: Attock is named after the famous Attock Fort on the Indus River.

recs.q: Carbon dioxide gas in the atmosphere is mainly responsible for which problem?
recs.facts: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere. Increasing amounts cause the Earth to warm.
recs.rel: Other greenhouse gases include methane and nitrous oxide.

recs.q: Chess originated in which country?
recs.facts: Chess developed from an Indian game called chaturanga around the 6th century AD. It then spread to Persia and the Muslim world.
recs.rel: The Arabic and Persian word shatranj comes from the Sanskrit chaturanga.

recs.q: The COVID-19 outbreak first started in which province of China?
recs.facts: The first cases were reported in the city of Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, in December 2019.
recs.rel: The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020.

recs.q: Dadu is a district of which province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Dadu is a district in the northwest of Sindh, close to Lake Manchar.
recs.rel: The ancient site of Amri is located in Dadu district.

recs.q: Deficiency of vitamin D causes which disease?
recs.facts: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bones. Its lack causes soft, bent bones in children, called rickets.
recs.rel: Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D.

recs.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness?
recs.facts: Vitamin A is needed to make the light-sensitive pigment in the retina. Its lack makes it hard to see in dim light.
recs.rel: Carrots, liver and green leafy vegetables are good sources of vitamin A.

recs.q: Dr. Ruth Pfau is remembered for her work against which disease?
recs.facts: Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor, spent her life in Pakistan treating leprosy patients and helped control the disease.
recs.rel: She died in Karachi in August 2017 and was given a state funeral.

recs.q: During which years did the Khilafat Movement take place in India?
recs.facts: The movement began in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I. It ended in 1924 when Turkey abolished the caliphate.
recs.rel: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: ________ comes home first will cook the food.
recs.facts: Whoever is the subject of the clause 'comes home first' and means any person who. Whom, which and whatever do not fit.
recs.rel: Whoever is a compound relative pronoun.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: ____ sun rises in the east.
recs.facts: The sun is unique, so it takes the definite article the.
recs.rel: The article the is also used with unique things such as the moon and the earth.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Three pictures are hanging ____ the wall.
recs.facts: The preposition on is used for things attached to a surface such as a wall.
recs.rel: We say at the door but on the wall.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He is ____ I am.
recs.facts: Older takes than in comparisons, and the pronoun I am follows because it is a subject comparison.
recs.rel: Elder is used for family members, as in elder brother, and is not followed by than.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He is accused ____ murder.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is accused of.
recs.rel: Similarly, we say suspected of and convicted of.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He is adept ____ finding flaws in the system.
recs.facts: Adept is followed by at (or in), meaning very skilled.
recs.rel: Adept is a synonym of skilled and expert.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He is deprived ____ all his money.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is deprived of.
recs.rel: Similar phrases are robbed of and bereft of.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He is jealous ____ him.
recs.facts: The adjective jealous takes the preposition of.
recs.rel: Similarly, we say envious of and afraid of.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He lived here ____ six years.
recs.facts: For is used with a period of time such as six years, while since is used with a point in time.
recs.rel: We say since 2015 but for ten years.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He reminds me ____ his teacher.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is remind someone of someone.
recs.rel: Remind someone to do something is a different pattern.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He told me that Ali ____ ill.
recs.facts: In reported speech after the past tense told, the present is shifts to the past tense was.
recs.rel: This rule of changing tense is called backshift.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: I was tired, so I ____ to sleep.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the past tense (I was tired), so the past form went is needed.
recs.rel: Went is the past tense of go, and gone is its past participle.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: Ali said that he ____ TV.
recs.facts: In reported speech after said, the present continuous is watching becomes the past continuous was watching.
recs.rel: Direct speech: Ali said, I am watching TV.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: I am mad ____ games.
recs.facts: Mad about means very fond of or passionate about something.
recs.rel: Mad at is used when someone is angry with a person.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: I ____ three books since Monday.
recs.facts: The word since Monday shows an action continuing up to now, so the present perfect tense is needed: have read.
recs.rel: The present perfect is formed with have or has plus the past participle.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: I am good ____ games.
recs.facts: The correct preposition after good, when talking about skill, is at.
recs.rel: We also say bad at, clever at and quick at.

recs.q: Fill in the blank with a preposition: I agreed ____ her proposal.
recs.facts: We agree to a proposal or plan, but agree with a person.
recs.rel: We agree on a matter that is being settled by several people.

recs.q: Fill in the preposition: The computer is ___ the table.
recs.facts: An object resting on a flat surface is described with the preposition on.
recs.rel: In is used for enclosed spaces and at for exact points.

recs.q: Fill in the preposition: The fridge is ___ the kitchen.
recs.facts: A room is an enclosed space, so we use in.
recs.rel: We say in the kitchen but at home.

recs.q: Fill in the preposition: Tokyo is the most populated city ___ the world.
recs.facts: After a superlative we normally use in with a place: the most populated city in the world.
recs.rel: Of is used with a group, as in the best of all.

recs.q: For addition of matrices, what must both matrices have?
opts: The same order (same number of rows and columns)
The same number of columns only
recs.facts: Matrices are added element by element, so they must have the same number of rows and columns.
recs.rel: Matrix multiplication needs columns of the first to equal rows of the second.

recs.q: For what is Ziarat famous?
recs.facts: Ziarat in Balochistan is known for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days in 1948.
recs.rel: Ziarat is also known for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.

recs.q: For which religion is some area of Hassan Abdal sacred?
recs.facts: Hassan Abdal has Gurdwara Panja Sahib, which is sacred to Sikhs.
recs.rel: Panja Sahib is believed to hold a handprint of Guru Nanak on a boulder.

recs.q: From where do plants mainly obtain nitrogen for growth?
recs.facts: Plants absorb nitrogen through their roots from the soil as nitrates and ammonium. Atmospheric nitrogen is made usable by bacteria and lightning.
recs.rel: Legumes host Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules that fix nitrogen.

recs.q: Where does the Yangtze River originate?
recs.facts: The Yangtze rises on the Tibetan Plateau in Qinghai and flows east to the East China Sea.
recs.rel: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

recs.q: From which country did Allama Iqbal obtain his PhD?
recs.facts: Iqbal received his PhD from the University of Munich in Germany in 1908. He studied at Cambridge in England but his doctorate was from Munich.
recs.rel: His thesis was The Development of Metaphysics in Persia.

recs.q: From which country does the TAPI gas pipeline start?
recs.facts: TAPI stands for Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and the gas comes from Turkmenistan.
recs.rel: The gas source is the Galkynysh field in Turkmenistan.

recs.q: Hajj is which pillar of Islam?
recs.facts: The five pillars are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is the fifth.
recs.rel: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who can afford it.

recs.q: Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro belong to which civilization?
recs.facts: Both are major cities of the Bronze Age Indus Valley Civilization.
recs.rel: Mohenjo-Daro is in Sindh and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: She is always cleaning her home ___ cleanliness is called half faith.
recs.facts: The second clause gives the reason for her cleaning, so the conjunction because fits.
recs.rel: The saying Cleanliness is half of faith is attributed to the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Fill in the blank: The doctor ___ car makes noise is a good person.
recs.facts: Whose shows possession: the car belongs to the doctor.
recs.rel: Whose can be used for both people and things.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Why are you so ____ with him?
recs.facts: After the linking verb are, we need an adjective describing the subject, so angry.
recs.rel: Adverbs such as angrily describe verbs, not the subject after to be.

recs.q: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of which companion?
recs.facts: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA), the first Caliph.
recs.rel: Her mother was Umm Ruman and she is known as Siddiqa bint Siddiq.

recs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which clan (branch) of the Quraish tribe of Arabs?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish tribe. His grandfather was Abdul Muttalib, son of Hashim.
recs.rel: His father was Hazrat Abdullah and his mother was Hazrat Amina.

recs.q: According to a hadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), lying is a sign of which kind of person?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that the signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays.
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as Sadiq (truthful) and Ameen (trustworthy) even before prophethood.

recs.q: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of which Prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, and his son was Hazrat Yusuf (AS).

recs.q: Choose the correct word: He is afraid ___ dogs.
recs.facts: The adjective afraid is followed by the preposition of, so the correct sentence is He is afraid of dogs.
recs.rel: Similar adjective-preposition pairs are fond of, proud of and afraid of.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: He was born ___ 20 August 2001.
recs.facts: The preposition on is used with specific dates and days, so the sentence is He was born on 20 August 2001.
recs.rel: We use in for months and years (in August, in 2001) and at for clock times.

recs.q: Up to approximately what depth (in metres) does sunlight penetrate in the ocean (the sunlit or euphotic zone)?
recs.facts: Enough sunlight for photosynthesis reaches only to about 200 metres, which is called the sunlit (euphotic) zone.
recs.rel: Below it lies the twilight zone from about 200 m to 1000 m, and below 1000 m is the dark midnight zone.

recs.q: How is the empty set denoted in set theory?
recs.facts: The empty set has no elements, so it is written as { } or with the symbol phi. The set {0} is not empty because it contains the element 0.
recs.rel: The empty set is a subset of every set and has zero elements.

recs.q: What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line)?
recs.facts: The Durand Line, agreed in 1893, is most commonly given as about 2,640 km long.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly (figures from about 2,600 to 2,670 km are quoted), and Afghanistan does not formally recognise the line.

recs.q: How many amendments have been made to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan as of 2026?
recs.facts: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024 and the 27th Amendment was passed by Parliament in November 2025. A 28th amendment was still only under discussion in mid-2026.
recs.rel: The 27th Amendment created the post of Chief of Defence Forces and a Federal Constitutional Court.

recs.q: According to the Quran (Surah Al-Anfal), how many angels were promised by Allah to help the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Anfal (8:9) says Allah would reinforce the Muslims with a thousand angels in succession.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Imran mentions 3000 and 5000 angels in other verses, and Muslims at Badr numbered 313.

recs.q: According to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), how many countries are recognised as nuclear-weapon states?
recs.facts: The NPT recognises only the states that tested a nuclear device before 1 January 1967: USA, Russia, UK, France and China.
recs.rel: India, Pakistan and Israel never joined the NPT, and North Korea withdrew from it.

recs.q: How many ayats (verses) are there in Surah Al-Kausar?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Kausar (Surah 108) has 3 ayats, which makes it the shortest surah of the Quran.
recs.rel: It begins with the words Inna a'taina kal-Kausar.

recs.q: How many pieces of cloth are worn by a male pilgrim in the state of Ihram?
recs.facts: A male pilgrim wears two unstitched white sheets, one wrapped around the waist (izar) and one around the upper body (rida).
recs.rel: Women may wear their ordinary modest stitched clothes in Ihram.

recs.q: How many consecutive matches did the Pakistani squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his famous unbeaten run?
recs.facts: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches between 1981 and 1986, until Ross Norman beat him in the 1986 World Open.
recs.rel: Some authors have questioned the exact count because records were poorly kept, but 555 is the figure officially cited.

recs.q: How many countries have veto power in the United Nations Security Council?
recs.facts: Only the five permanent members have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
recs.rel: The Security Council also has 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms, who have no veto.

recs.q: How many Hafiz (memorisers) of the Quran are reported to have been martyred in the Battle of Yamama?
recs.facts: In the Battle of Yamama (12 AH) against the false prophet Musailima, about 70 Huffaz of the Quran were martyred, according to the commonly given account.
recs.rel: Some narrations give higher numbers, but this event led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran in one book.

recs.q: How many idols were placed in and around the Kaaba before the conquest of Makkah?
recs.facts: Traditional sources say 360 idols stood around the Kaaba when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah in 8 AH. He had them removed and the Kaaba cleansed.
recs.rel: The idol Hubal was the chief idol of the Quraysh inside the Kaaba.

recs.q: What is the total number of members of the Senate of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Senate has 96 members: 23 from each of the four provinces (92) plus 4 from the Islamabad Capital Territory. A November 2025 report still describes a 96-member Senate
recs.rel: The Senate had 104 members until the FATA seats were phased out after FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018.

recs.q: How many Senate seats are allocated to each province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Each province has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 for women, 4 for technocrats and 1 for non-Muslims.
recs.rel: The Senate is a permanent house; half of its members retire every three years.

recs.q: How many general (directly elected) seats does Punjab have in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Under the 2024 delimitation Punjab has 141 general seats in the 336-seat National Assembly. With its 32 reserved seats for women, Punjab's share rises to 173.
recs.rel: The National Assembly has 266 general seats, 60 for women and 10 for non-Muslims.

recs.q: Into how many paras (juz) is the Holy Quran divided?
recs.facts: The Quran is divided into 30 paras of roughly equal length so it can be read in a month. This is separate from its 114 surahs.
recs.rel: The first para is Alif Lam Meem.

recs.q: How many players are on the court for one team in a volleyball match?
recs.facts: A volleyball team has six players on the court at a time, three at the net and three at the back.
recs.rel: A basketball team has five players on court.

recs.q: How many players of one team are on the court at a time in basketball?
recs.facts: Each basketball team plays with five players on the court at a time.
recs.rel: A team may have up to 12 players in total on its roster in international games.

recs.q: How many consecutive matches did squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his unbeaten run between 1981 and 1986?
recs.facts: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches over about five and a half years, a record recognised in the Guinness Book of Records as the longest winning streak in a professional sport.
recs.rel: He won the British Open ten times in a row.

recs.q: How many states are there in the United States of America?
recs.facts: The USA has 50 states. Alaska and Hawaii were the last to join in 1959.
recs.rel: Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state.

recs.q: How many times does the full phrase Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem occur in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: It opens 113 surahs (all except Surah At-Tawbah) and also appears inside Surah An-Naml (27:30), giving 114 in total.
recs.rel: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.

recs.q: How many times is the name Muhammad mentioned in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The name Muhammad occurs in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:144), Al-Ahzab (33:40), Muhammad (47:2) and Al-Fath (48:29), so four times.
recs.rel: The name Ahmad, another name of the Holy Prophet (SAW), appears once, in Surah As-Saff (61:6).

recs.q: What is the Zakat nisab of silver in tolas?
recs.facts: The nisab of silver is 52.5 tolas, which is about 612.36 grams.
recs.rel: The nisab of gold is 7.5 tolas (about 87.48 grams), and the rate of Zakat is 2.5 percent.

recs.q: How many types of Hajj are there?
recs.facts: The three types are Ifrad, Qiran and Tamattu.
recs.rel: Hajj-e-Tamattu is the type in which Umrah is done first and the Ihram is then removed before Hajj.

recs.q: How often does the presidency of the UN Security Council change?
recs.facts: The presidency rotates every month among the 15 members in the English alphabetical order of their names.
recs.rel: The UN Security Council has 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: I was worried because I thought I might ___ my train.
recs.facts: Miss means to fail to catch a train. Loose means not tight, and found is the past of find.
recs.rel: Lose (to misplace) and loose (not tight) are often confused.

recs.q: ICAO is a specialized agency of which organization?
recs.facts: The International Civil Aviation Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations dealing with civil aviation standards.
recs.rel: ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.

recs.q: What is the noun form of the adjective safe?
recs.facts: Safety is the noun that corresponds to the adjective safe, while safely is an adverb.
recs.rel: Many adjectives form nouns with the suffix -ty, such as certain and certainty.

recs.q: If k is the unit vector along the z-axis, what is the scalar product k . k?
recs.facts: The dot product of a unit vector with itself is its magnitude squared, 1 x 1 = 1.
recs.rel: The dot product of two perpendicular unit vectors, such as i . j, is 0.

recs.q: In the Quaid-e-Azam's 14 Points (1929), Sindh was to be separated from which province?
recs.facts: The 14 Points demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency and made a separate province.
recs.rel: Sindh actually became a separate province in 1936.

recs.q: In the ratio a : b, what is a called?
recs.facts: The first term of a ratio is the antecedent and the second term is the consequent.
recs.rel: In the ratio 3 : 5, the antecedent is 3 and the consequent is 5.

recs.q: In the sentence 'The boy ran into serious difficulties this year', which word is the adjective?
recs.facts: Serious describes the noun difficulties, so it is the adjective.
recs.rel: An adjective describes or qualifies a noun or pronoun.

recs.q: In which battle were a large number of Hafiz-e-Quran Sahaba martyred?
recs.facts: Many Qurra (Hafiz) companions were martyred at Yamama against the false prophet Musaylima in 632 AD.
recs.rel: This loss led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to have the Quran compiled in one book.

recs.q: In which para (juz) of the Holy Quran is Ayat ul Kursi found?
recs.facts: Ayat ul Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, and this verse falls in Para 3 (Tilka ar-Rusul).
recs.rel: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, begins in Para 1 and ends in Para 3.

recs.q: In which city is Warsak Dam located?
recs.facts: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River about 30 km north-west of Peshawar, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: Warsak Dam was constructed in the 1960s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.

recs.q: In which city is the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) situated?
recs.facts: PIMS is a large public teaching hospital located in sector G-8 of Islamabad.
recs.rel: Federal Government Polyclinic and PIMS are the main federal hospitals of Islamabad.

recs.q: In which city of Pakistan does the Orange Line Metro Train run?
recs.facts: The Orange Line Metro Train is a rapid transit line in Lahore, built with Chinese financing under CPEC and opened in 2020.
recs.rel: It is Pakistan's first modern metro train system.

recs.q: In which city was the Indian National Congress founded in 1885?
recs.facts: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under W. C. Bonnerjee.
recs.rel: A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, was the main founder of the Congress.

recs.q: In which city did the tribes of Bani Aus and Bani Khazraj live?
recs.facts: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later named Madinah, and they accepted Islam after the Pledges of Aqaba.
recs.rel: They are known as the Ansar (helpers) of Madinah.

recs.q: In which country is the Gulf of Lion located?
recs.facts: The Gulf of Lion is a wide bay of the Mediterranean Sea off the southern coast of France.
recs.rel: Marseille and Montpellier are French cities near this coast.

recs.q: In which country is the city of Wuhan located?
recs.facts: Wuhan is the capital of Hubei province in central China, on the Yangtze River.
recs.rel: Wuhan is also the city where the COVID-19 outbreak was first reported in December 2019.

recs.q: In which country is the Suez Canal situated?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway running through Egypt.
recs.rel: It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and was opened in 1869.

recs.q: Where was the first Olympic Games of ancient times held?
