recs.facts: The ancient Olympic Games began at Olympia in Greece, traditionally dated to 776 BC.
recs.rel: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

recs.q: In which country was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) formed in 1969?
recs.facts: The OIC was founded at the Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969.
recs.rel: The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: To which land did the Muslims make their first migration (Hijrat) to escape persecution by the Quraish?
recs.facts: In the fifth year of the Prophethood a group of Muslims crossed the Red Sea to Abyssinia, whose Christian king Negus gave them protection.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman and his wife Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) were among the first migrants.

recs.q: In which district is the Kharan Desert located?
recs.facts: The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests of May 1998 at Chagai, a district near the Kharan Desert.

recs.q: In which district is the hill station Gorakh Hill located?
recs.facts: Gorakh Hill, about 2,300 metres high, lies in the Kirthar Mountains of Dadu district, Sindh.
recs.rel: It is called the Murree of Sindh and sometimes receives snow in winter.

recs.q: In which division is Narowal district?
recs.facts: Narowal district belongs to Gujranwala Division of Punjab.
recs.rel: Narowal became a separate district in 1991 after being split from Sialkot.

recs.q: In which mathematical equation does the expression b squared minus 4ac appear?
recs.facts: For ax squared + bx + c = 0, the quantity b squared minus 4ac is the discriminant under the square root of the quadratic formula.
recs.rel: If the discriminant is negative, the quadratic has no real roots.

recs.q: In which Ghazwa did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) adopt the war technique of digging a trench around Madina?
recs.facts: On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) a trench was dug to defend Madina against the Quraish and allied tribes.
recs.rel: This battle is also called Ghazwa Ahzab.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa Ahzab (Khandaq) fought?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks place the Battle of the Trench in Shawwal 5 AH (627 CE).
recs.rel: Some historians place it in 4 AH, so sources differ.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud, fought in Shawwal 3 AH.
recs.rel: He was killed by Wahshi and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Yarmouk fought?
recs.facts: The Muslims defeated the Byzantines at Yarmouk in 15 AH (636 CE), in the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).
recs.rel: The Muslim commander in this battle was Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA).

recs.q: In which Islamic month did Pakistan gain independence on 14 August 1947?
recs.facts: Pakistan came into being on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, which was 14 August 1947, a Friday.
recs.rel: 27 Ramadan is also known as Laylat al-Qadr in popular belief.

recs.q: In which Islamic month did the Battle (Ghazwa) of Uhad take place?
recs.facts: The Battle of Uhad was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH near Mount Uhad close to Madina.
recs.rel: The Battle of Badr was fought in the previous year, in Ramadan 2 AH.

recs.q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Fitr celebrated?
recs.facts: Eid ul Fitr is celebrated on 1 Shawwal after the month of fasting ends.
recs.rel: Eid ul Fitr was first celebrated in 2 AH.

recs.q: In which Islamic month is Laylat ul Qadr (the Night of Power)?
recs.facts: Laylat ul Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd nights.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Qadr is devoted to this night, which is described as better than a thousand months.

recs.q: In which mountain range of Pakistan is Tirich Mir located?
recs.facts: Tirich Mir lies in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, in the Hindu Kush range.
recs.rel: At about 7,708 metres it is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

recs.q: In which Nabawi year did the Year of Grief (Aam ul Huzn) occur?
recs.facts: In the 10th year of prophethood both Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadijah (RA) passed away within a short time.
recs.rel: The year corresponds to about 619 CE.

recs.q: In which province is Chagai district situated?
recs.facts: Chagai is a district in the west of Balochistan bordering Afghanistan and Iran.
recs.rel: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai in May 1998.

recs.q: In which province is the Gomal Zam Dam located?
recs.facts: Gomal Zam Dam is built on the Gomal River in South Waziristan, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It is a multipurpose dam completed in 2013.

recs.q: In which province is Kundol (Kundal) Lake situated?
recs.facts: Kundol Lake lies in the upper Swat valley near Kalam in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: Swat is famous for lakes such as Mahodand and Kundol.

recs.q: In which part of Pakistan is Mirpur located?
recs.facts: Mirpur is a city and district in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (the question is often worded as province, though AJK is not a province).
recs.rel: Mangla Dam is built near Mirpur on the Jhelum River.

recs.q: In which province is Narowal district located?
recs.facts: Narowal is a district in northeastern Punjab near the Indian border.
recs.rel: Narowal was made a separate district in 1991.

recs.q: In which province does the Soan River flow?
recs.facts: The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar plateau of Punjab (Rawalpindi area) to join the Indus.
recs.rel: The Soan valley is one of the oldest sites of early human tools in South Asia.

recs.q: On which river are the Victoria Falls situated?
recs.facts: Victoria Falls lies on the Zambezi River on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe.
recs.rel: Its local name is Mosi-oa-Tunya, the smoke that thunders.

recs.q: In which Surah does the phrase Bismillah occur twice (once at the start and once within a verse)?
recs.facts: In Surah Al-Naml the Bismillah appears at the start and again in verse 30 in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS) to the Queen of Sheba.
recs.rel: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah without Bismillah at its start.

recs.q: In which year did Britain annex Sindh?
recs.facts: Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at the Battle of Miani in 1843 and Sindh was annexed.
recs.rel: Punjab was annexed later, in 1849.

recs.q: In which year did Hazrat Hind (wife of Abu Sufyan) embrace Islam?
recs.facts: She accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE).
recs.rel: She was the mother of Hazrat Muawiyah (RA).

recs.q: In which year did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
recs.facts: Malala was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, jointly with Kailash Satyarthi.
recs.rel: At age 17 she became the youngest Nobel laureate ever.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Cricket World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand under Imran Khan, beating England in the final at Melbourne.
recs.rel: It remains Pakistan's only 50-over World Cup title.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan last win the Hockey World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994, the last of these in Sydney in 1994.
recs.rel: Pakistan is the most successful team in World Cup history along with the Netherlands, with four titles each.

recs.q: In which year was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Army launched Radd-ul-Fasaad in February 2017 as a nationwide intelligence-based operation against terrorism.
recs.rel: It followed Operation Zarb-e-Azb, which began in June 2014.

recs.q: In which year was the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia founded (unified) under Abdulaziz Ibn Saud?
recs.facts: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud proclaimed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932, which is marked as Saudi National Day.
recs.rel: Before that his realm was known as the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd.

recs.q: In which year did the first Muslim commander, Muhammad bin Qasim, invade India (Sindh)?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh in 712 AD.
recs.rel: Some sources give 711 AD for his arrival; most Pakistani textbooks give 712 AD.

recs.q: In which year did the Ottoman Empire come to an end?
recs.facts: The Ottoman Sultanate was abolished in November 1922, ending the empire, and Turkey became a republic in 1923.
recs.rel: The Caliphate was abolished separately on 3 March 1924 by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.

recs.q: In which year did the USA invade Afghanistan?
recs.facts: US-led forces began strikes on Afghanistan on 7 October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.
recs.rel: The US withdrawal from Afghanistan was completed in August 2021.

recs.q: In which year was Tarbela Dam completed?
recs.facts: Construction of Tarbela Dam on the Indus began in 1968 and the dam was completed in 1976.
recs.rel: Sources differ: civil works finished around 1974 and the full power project in 1984; 1976 is the usual textbook answer.

recs.q: In which year was the Pakistan Resolution passed?
recs.facts: The Resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League on 23 March 1940.
recs.rel: It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.

recs.q: In which year was the presidential system introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan under a new constitution?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan's constitution of 1962 introduced a presidential system with Basic Democracies.
recs.rel: The 1962 constitution was abrogated by Yahya Khan in 1969.

recs.q: In the straight line equation y = mx + c, what does m represent?
recs.facts: In y = mx + c, m is the slope (gradient) of the line, the change in y per unit change in x.
recs.rel: The constant c is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis.

recs.q: What is the shape of the graph of a quadratic equation?
recs.facts: The graph of y = ax^2 + bx + c with a not zero is a parabola.
recs.rel: The parabola opens upward if a is positive and downward if a is negative.

recs.q: What is the status of Iran in SAARC?
recs.facts: SAARC has eight full members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Iran is only an observer, so it is not a member.
recs.rel: Other SAARC observers include China, Japan, the USA, the European Union, Australia, South Korea, Mauritius and Myanmar.

recs.q: Is the number pi a rational or an irrational number?
recs.facts: Pi cannot be written as a fraction of two integers and its decimal expansion never ends or repeats. Hence it is irrational.
recs.rel: Fractions such as 22/7 are only approximations of pi (3.14159...).

recs.q: Joe Biden, who took office in January 2021, was which President of the USA?
recs.facts: Barack Obama was 44th and Donald Trump 45th, so Joe Biden who followed him was the 46th President.
recs.rel: Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025 as the 47th President.

recs.q: K2 lies on the border between Pakistan and which country?
recs.facts: K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan) and Xinjiang (China).
recs.rel: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world at about 8,611 m.

recs.q: Lapels are a part of which garment?
recs.facts: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a coat or jacket below the collar.
recs.rel: The lapel is the part where a flower or badge is often pinned.

recs.q: Matrix A is of order 2 x 1 and matrix B is of order 1 x 2. What is the order of the product AB?
recs.facts: For a product the columns of A (1) equal the rows of B (1), so AB exists. Its order is rows of A by columns of B, that is 2 x 2.
recs.rel: The product BA in this case would be of order 1 x 1.

recs.q: Narendra Modi is a famous politician of which country?
recs.facts: Narendra Modi is the Prime Minister of India, leading the BJP.
recs.rel: He has been Prime Minister since 2014 and is in his third term after the 2024 election.

recs.q: Musailma Kazzab was killed in which battle?
recs.facts: Musailma, the false claimant of prophethood, was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Yamama in 632-633 CE in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
recs.rel: Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.

recs.q: Nanga Parbat is which highest peak of the world?
recs.facts: Nanga Parbat, at 8,126 m, is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
recs.rel: It is the second highest peak in Pakistan after K2 and is nicknamed Killer Mountain.

recs.q: Nelson Mandela was the leader and later President of which country?
recs.facts: Mandela led the struggle against apartheid and became South Africa's first black President in 1994.
recs.rel: He was imprisoned for 27 years and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

recs.q: Nuku'alofa is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Nuku'alofa, on the island of Tongatapu, is the capital of the Kingdom of Tonga in the Pacific.
recs.rel: Tonga is a Polynesian monarchy and has never been fully colonised.

recs.q: On what date did Pakistan get its first constitution?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and the country became an Islamic Republic.
recs.rel: It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law on 7 October 1958 and 23 March is now Pakistan Day.

recs.q: The Simla Conference of 1945 was held on 25 June 1945 under which Viceroy?
recs.facts: Viceroy Lord Wavell called the conference at Simla to discuss his plan for an Executive Council with Indian members.
recs.rel: It failed because Congress and the Muslim League disagreed over the choice of Muslim members.

recs.q: On what date was the State Bank of Pakistan established?
recs.facts: The State Bank of Pakistan began working on 1 July 1948 and was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam.
recs.rel: Its first Governor was Zahid Hussain.

recs.q: On what date did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points, and in reply to which report?
opts: 28 March 1929, reply to the Nehru Report
23 March 1940, reply to the Cripps Mission
28 March 1929, reply to the Simon Report
12 December 1930, reply to the Lahore Resolution
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presented his 14 Points in Delhi on 28 March 1929 as an answer to the Nehru Report of 1928.
recs.rel: The 14 Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, including separate electorates and one-third seats in the central legislature.

recs.q: On which date of the Hijri month was the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (SAW) delivered?
recs.facts: The sermon was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH, in the Uranah valley of Mount Arafat during the Farewell Hajj.
recs.rel: Some people say 10th, but the standard account is the Day of Arafah, the 9th.

recs.q: On which date was SAARC formed?
recs.facts: SAARC was established at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985 by seven South Asian countries.
recs.rel: Its secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined in 2007.

recs.q: According to the Quran, on which mountain did the ark of Prophet Noah (AS) come to rest?
recs.facts: Surah Hud (verse 44) says the ark settled on Al-Judi, a mountain in the Kurdistan region.
recs.rel: The Bible names the mountains of Ararat, so sources differ.

recs.q: On which river is the Mirani Dam built?
recs.facts: Mirani Dam is built on the Dasht River in Kech district of Balochistan, near Turbat.
recs.rel: It was completed in 2006 mainly for irrigation and flood control in Makran.

recs.q: On which river is Sukkur Barrage built?
recs.facts: Sukkur Barrage was built across the Indus River at Sukkur in Sindh.
recs.rel: It was opened in 1932 and feeds seven major canals.

recs.q: On which river is Tarbela Dam built?
recs.facts: Tarbela Dam is an earth-filled dam on the Indus River in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world, completed in 1974.

recs.q: On whom was the Zaboor (Psalms) revealed?
recs.facts: The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Dawud (AS) was also a king, and his son Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) was a prophet too.

recs.q: Pakistan is a gateway to which region?
recs.facts: Pakistan lies between South Asia, Central Asia and the Arabian Sea, so its ports and routes give Central Asia access to the sea.
recs.rel: Gwadar Port is promoted as a trade outlet for landlocked Central Asian states.

recs.q: Pakistan is located in which continent?
recs.facts: Pakistan lies in South Asia, part of the continent of Asia.
recs.rel: Pakistan borders Afghanistan, China, India and Iran.

recs.q: Who started Pakistan's biggest ambulance service?
recs.facts: Abdul Sattar Edhi founded the Edhi Foundation, which runs Pakistan's largest ambulance network.
recs.rel: Edhi is known as the Angel of Mercy and died in 2016.

recs.q: Petrol is a mixture of what?
recs.facts: Petrol is a mixture of many liquid hydrocarbons obtained from crude oil.
recs.rel: Its octane number measures how well it resists knocking in an engine.

recs.q: Ping pong is another name for which game?
recs.facts: Ping pong is the popular name for table tennis.
recs.rel: Table tennis has been an Olympic sport since 1988.

recs.q: Pour le Merite is an award of which country?
recs.facts: Pour le Merite is a Prussian and German order of merit, first founded in 1740 by Frederick the Great.
recs.rel: In WWI the Blue Max was the nickname for its military class.

recs.q: In which constitution of Pakistan was the presidential form of government adopted?
recs.facts: The 1962 constitution given by Ayub Khan established a presidential system with a strong president.
recs.rel: The 1956 and 1973 constitutions set up a parliamentary system.

recs.q: Which countries does the 38th parallel divide?
recs.facts: The 38th parallel north was the dividing line between North and South Korea after 1945.
recs.rel: The present border, the Demilitarized Zone, was set by the 1953 armistice and runs near the 38th parallel.

recs.q: Rubber is obtained from which tree?
recs.facts: Natural rubber is made from latex tapped from the rubber tree, Hevea brasiliensis.
recs.rel: Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia are leading rubber producers.

recs.q: Ruh-ul-Qudus is the title of which angel?
recs.facts: Ruh-ul-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) is a title of the angel Hazrat Jibreel (AS), who brought revelation.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jibreel (AS) is also called Ameen.

recs.q: In which month is Shab-e-Qadr (Laylatul Qadr)?
recs.facts: Laylatul Qadr falls in Ramadan, most likely on an odd night of the last ten days.
recs.rel: The Quran was first revealed on this night, and Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: She said that she ___ to know.
recs.facts: In reported speech with the past tense verb said, the verb shifts to the past, so wanted is used.
recs.rel: This shifting of tense is called backshift.

recs.q: Sound travels in the form of what?
recs.facts: Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that needs a medium such as air to travel.
recs.rel: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

recs.q: Stainless steel is an example of what?
recs.facts: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium and often nickel.
recs.rel: Chromium of at least about 10.5 percent makes it resist rust.

recs.q: Which country mediated the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 between Pakistan and India?
recs.facts: The Soviet Union under Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent Declaration in January 1966.
recs.rel: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent soon after signing.

recs.q: The Thar desert of Sindh is rich in which mineral resource?
recs.facts: Thar has one of the world's largest lignite coal reserves, about 175 billion tonnes.
recs.rel: Thar coal is being used for power generation at Islamkot.

recs.q: The Battle of Furqan is the name of which ghazwa?
recs.facts: The Quran calls the day of Badr Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction between truth and falsehood. So the Battle of Furqan is the Battle of Badr.
recs.rel: Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) and about 313 Muslims faced roughly 1000 Makkan soldiers.

recs.q: The census of Pakistan is conducted by which organization?
recs.facts: Population and housing censuses in Pakistan are carried out by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. NADRA and the Election Commission only use the data or registers.
recs.rel: The 2017 and the digital 2023 censuses were both conducted by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.

recs.q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of which place?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal to Yemen as governor and teacher of the people.
recs.rel: Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal was known as the most knowledgeable of the Companions in halal and haram.

recs.q: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 was made with the mediation of which organization?
recs.facts: The treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi in September 1960.
recs.rel: India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, and Pakistan rejects this move.

recs.q: The nation of which prophet was destroyed by a rain of stones?
recs.facts: The Quran says the sinful people of Hazrat Loot (AS) were destroyed by a shower of baked clay stones.
recs.rel: The nation of Hazrat Nooh (AS) was destroyed by flood and the people of Aad by a violent wind.

recs.q: The Panama Canal connects the Pacific Ocean with which ocean?
recs.facts: The canal cuts across Panama and joins the Pacific Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean through the Caribbean Sea.
recs.rel: The Panama Canal was opened in 1914 while the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is bound to act on the advice of whom?
recs.facts: Article 48 of the Constitution requires the President to act on the advice of the Prime Minister (or the Cabinet).
recs.rel: Pakistan has a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister is the real executive head.

recs.q: The river Amazon is ___ largest river of South America.
recs.facts: A superlative such as largest takes the definite article the.
recs.rel: The Amazon is the largest river in the world by volume of water.

recs.q: Choose the correct reported speech: The teacher asked, Who is speaking English?
opts: The teacher wanted to know who is speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who was speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who has spoken English.
The teacher wanted to know who speaks English was.
recs.facts: In reported speech a present continuous question changes to past continuous, so is speaking becomes was speaking, and the question order becomes a statement.
recs.rel: The reporting verb asked is usually changed to wanted to know or enquired.

recs.q: The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from which country?
recs.facts: The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan lies between Pakistan on the south and Tajikistan on the north.
recs.rel: The corridor also touches China at its eastern end.

recs.q: The word Everyone is what part of speech?
recs.facts: Everyone stands in place of a noun (all people), so it is an indefinite pronoun.
recs.rel: Other indefinite pronouns are someone, anybody and nobody.

recs.q: Thimphu is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.
recs.rel: Bhutan is a Himalayan kingdom between China and India.

recs.q: Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Cancer not pass?
recs.facts: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees north) crosses India, Bangladesh and Egypt, but Pakistan lies north of it.
recs.rel: It also passes through Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Libya and southern China.

recs.q: Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Capricorn not pass?
recs.facts: The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5 degrees south) lies in the southern hemisphere, and India is entirely in the northern hemisphere.
recs.rel: It also crosses Chile, Argentina, Namibia, Botswana and Madagascar.

recs.q: To where did the Muslims first migrate?
recs.facts: In 615 CE (5th year of the Prophethood) a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia to escape persecution in Makkah.
recs.rel: The king of Abyssinia, Negus (Najashi), gave them protection.

recs.q: To which country does Olympic Airlines (now Olympic Air) belong?
recs.facts: Olympic Airlines was the national flag carrier of Greece, founded in 1957 by Aristotle Onassis. It was replaced by Olympic Air in 2009.
recs.rel: Olympic Airways was nationalised in 1975 and ceased operating as the flag carrier in 2009.

recs.q: To which place did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
recs.facts: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib). This migration is the Hijrat.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar begins from this migration.

recs.q: To which tribe did Hazrat Ali (RA) belong?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in Makkah into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe. He was the cousin of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Aws and Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina.

recs.q: Umm Kalsoom (Umm Kulthum) was what of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
recs.rel: She married Hazrat Usman (RA) after the death of her sister Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).

recs.q: Towards which place was the first Hijrat of the Muslims made?
recs.facts: In 615 AD a small group of Muslims migrated from Makkah to Habsha (Abyssinia) to escape persecution by the Quraysh. Its Christian king, the Negus, gave them protection.
recs.rel: The migration to Madina came about seven years later, in 622 AD.

recs.q: To whom was the Nishan-e-Haider last awarded?
recs.facts: Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed received the award for gallantry in the 1999 Kargil conflict; no later award is recorded.
recs.rel: Lalak Jan belonged to Yasin valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, and is the 11th recipient.

recs.q: According to the 2023 census, Urdu is the mother tongue of about what percentage of Pakistanis?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics 2023 census puts Urdu at about 9.25 percent of the population. Candidates in 2021-22 recalled about 7 percent, which was the 2017 census figure (7.08 percent).
recs.rel: Punjabi is the most common mother tongue, at about 37 percent.

recs.q: Which are the three largest oceans of the world, in order of size?
recs.facts: By area the Pacific is the largest, then the Atlantic, then the Indian Ocean. The Southern and Arctic Oceans are smaller.
recs.rel: The Pacific Ocean covers about one third of the Earth's surface.

recs.q: Which day is celebrated on 12 June?
recs.facts: The International Labour Organization observes the World Day Against Child Labour on 12 June each year.
recs.rel: World Environment Day is on 5 June and World Population Day on 11 July.

recs.q: What did Thomas Edison invent (practically)?
recs.facts: Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent electric light bulb in 1879. He also invented the phonograph.
recs.rel: The telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.

recs.q: What does the word Al-Fatiha mean?
recs.facts: Al-Fatiha means The Opening, because it opens the Quran and also opens the prayer.
recs.rel: It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and has seven verses.

recs.q: What does the Arabic word Ansar mean?
recs.facts: Ansar means helpers. It refers to the people of Madina who sheltered and helped the Muslims migrating from Makkah.
recs.rel: The migrants from Makkah are called Muhajirin.

recs.q: Uhad (Uhud) is the name of what?
recs.facts: Uhud is a mountain just north of Madina, near which the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.

recs.q: What was Hilf-ul-Fudul (Half-e-Fadool)?
opts: A pre-Islamic pact in Makkah to protect the oppressed and uphold justice
A treaty signed between the Muslims and the Quraish in 6 AH
A pact made by the Ansar of Madinah at Aqabah
A trade agreement between Makkah and Syria
recs.facts: Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pledge made by several Makkan clans to help victims of injustice and to see that wrongs were set right. The Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) said that even after Islam he would respond to a similar call.

recs.q: What does the term Ijtehad mean in Islamic law?
opts: Independent reasoning to derive rulings from the Quran and Sunnah
Migration for the sake of faith
recs.facts: Ijtehad means exerting one's utmost intellectual effort to find a legal ruling on a new matter from the Quran and Sunnah. A scholar who does this is called a Mujtahid.
recs.rel: Allama Iqbal strongly advocated Ijtehad as the principle of movement in Islam.

recs.q: What does the Arabic word Mantiq mean?
recs.facts: Mantiq is the Arabic word for logic, the science of correct reasoning. It is taught in Dars-e-Nizami madrassas.
recs.rel: Muslim philosophers such as Al-Farabi and Ibn Sina wrote extensively on Mantiq.

recs.q: What does NFC stand for in Pakistan's finance system?
recs.facts: NFC stands for National Finance Commission. It decides how federal tax revenue is shared between the federation and the provinces.
recs.rel: The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.

recs.q: What does the abbreviation PSL stand for in Pakistani cricket?
recs.facts: PSL stands for Pakistan Super League, the franchise Twenty20 cricket league of Pakistan. It began in 2016.
recs.rel: The PSL is run by the Pakistan Cricket Board.

recs.q: What does the word seething mean?
recs.facts: To seethe is to boil or churn, and it is used for a person who is extremely angry but does not show it. So seething means very angry.
recs.rel: Its literal meaning is bubbling as a liquid does when boiling.

recs.q: What does Tayammum mean?
opts: Dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
recs.facts: Tayammum is a substitute for wudu or ghusl performed with clean earth or dust when water is not available or cannot be used. It is taught in the Quran in Surah Al-Maidah.
recs.rel: Tayammum is made by striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face and hands.

recs.q: What does the Silk Route connect?
opts: China with the Mediterranean and Europe
recs.facts: The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade roads linking China through Central Asia to the Mediterranean world. Silk was a major good carried along it.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway in Pakistan follows part of the old Silk Route.

recs.q: What does the word Akhuwat mean?
recs.facts: Akhuwat is an Arabic and Urdu word meaning brotherhood. It is the name of a Pakistani organisation that gives interest-free loans.
recs.rel: The Akhuwat concept is based on the brotherhood between the Muhajirin and the Ansar of Madinah.

recs.q: What important event took place in 622 AD?
opts: The Hijrah (migration) of the Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madinah
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah in 622 AD. This year marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA).

recs.q: What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)?
recs.facts: By definition 0! = 1, because there is exactly one way to arrange no objects. This also keeps the formula n! = n x (n-1)! true for n = 1.
recs.rel: The number of ways to choose 0 items from n, nC0, equals 1 for this reason.

recs.q: What is a period of 100 years also called?
recs.facts: A century is a period of 100 years. A decade is 10 years and a millennium is 1000 years.
recs.rel: A score means 20 years or 20 items.

recs.q: What is 22 March observed as worldwide?
recs.facts: The United Nations observes 22 March each year as World Water Day. It raises awareness of fresh water and its sustainable use.
recs.rel: World Environment Day is on 5 June and World Health Day on 7 April.

recs.q: What does the United Nations observe on 24 January?
recs.facts: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 January as International Day of Education in December 2018. It was first observed in 2019.
recs.rel: International Literacy Day is on 8 September and World Teachers Day on 5 October.

recs.q: What is the value of (3 - 2i) - (3 + 2i)?
recs.facts: Subtract the real parts: 3 - 3 = 0. Subtract the imaginary parts: -2i - 2i = -4i, so the answer is -4i.
recs.rel: The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.

recs.q: What is an angle of 90 degrees called?
recs.facts: An angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle. Acute angles are smaller and obtuse angles are larger.
recs.rel: A straight angle measures 180 degrees.

recs.q: What was the relation of A. O. Hume with the Indian National Congress?
opts: He was one of its founders in 1885
He was its first Muslim president
He was the Viceroy who banned it
recs.facts: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped found the Indian National Congress in December 1885. He served as its first general secretary.
recs.rel: The first president of the Congress was W. C. Bonnerjee.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of complicated?
recs.facts: Complicated means made of many parts and hard to understand, which is the meaning of complex. Simple, easy and plain are its opposites.
recs.rel: The opposite of complicated is simple.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of conceal?
recs.facts: To conceal means to keep something out of sight, which is to hide it. Reveal, show and expose are antonyms.
recs.rel: The noun form is concealment.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'dormant'?
recs.facts: Dormant means temporarily inactive or sleeping, as in a dormant volcano.
recs.rel: The opposite of dormant is active.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'evacuate'?
recs.facts: To evacuate is to leave or empty a place, especially because of danger.
recs.rel: Evacuate comes from the Latin word vacuare, meaning to empty.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'exquisite'?
recs.facts: Exquisite describes something extremely beautiful and finely made.
recs.rel: Its opposite could be crude or coarse.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'persistent'?
recs.facts: Persistent means continuing firmly despite difficulty, which is what tenacious means.
recs.rel: Persistent is the antonym of giving up or wavering.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'savage'?
recs.facts: Savage means fierce, wild and untamed.
recs.rel: Savage comes from the Latin silvaticus, meaning of the woods.

recs.q: What is a zero vector also called?
recs.facts: A vector with zero magnitude and no definite direction is called a null vector.
recs.rel: Adding a null vector to any vector leaves it unchanged.

recs.q: What is the abscissa of a point in the Cartesian plane?
recs.facts: In a point (x, y), the abscissa is the x-coordinate, the horizontal distance from the y-axis.
recs.rel: The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

recs.q: What is Atomic Day (the day of Pakistan's 1998 nuclear tests) called in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan tested nuclear devices in the Chagai hills in 1998, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.
recs.rel: It is observed on 28 May each year.

recs.q: In statistics, what is the average of a set of numbers also called?
recs.facts: The average is the sum of the values divided by their count, which is the arithmetic mean.
recs.rel: The median is the middle value and the mode is the most frequent value.

recs.q: What is Bait ul Muqaddas?
recs.facts: Bait ul Muqaddas means the Holy House and refers to Jerusalem and its Masjid al-Aqsa.
recs.rel: It was the first Qibla of Muslims before the change to the Kaaba.

recs.q: What is Barzakh in Islamic belief?
opts: The period between death and the Day of Judgement
recs.facts: Barzakh is the barrier or intermediate state between a person's death and resurrection.
recs.rel: Barzakh is mentioned in Surah Al-Mu'minun of the Quran.

recs.q: Which event is commemorated on Kashmir Day (Youm-e-Yakjehti-e-Kashmir) in Pakistan?
opts: Solidarity with the people of Kashmir
recs.facts: Kashmir Day is observed to express support for the Kashmiri right to self-determination.
recs.rel: It is observed on 5 February each year.

recs.q: What is cot x . sec x equal to?
recs.facts: cot x = cos x / sin x and sec x = 1 / cos x, so the product = 1 / sin x = cosec x.
recs.rel: Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.

recs.q: What is the number of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) among the Khulafa-e-Rashideen?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was the first Rightly Guided Caliph after the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The order is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali (RA).

recs.q: What was Hilful Fudul?
opts: A peace pact of Makkan tribes to protect the oppressed
A treaty between Muslims and Jews of Madinah
recs.facts: Hilful Fudul was a pact formed in Makkah to defend the wronged and help the weak, and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) later said he would still respond to such a pact in Islam.

recs.q: In vector algebra, what is the value of j . j (dot product of the unit vector j with itself)?
recs.rel: Dot products of different unit vectors such as i . j are 0.

recs.q: What is Pakistan Standard Time relative to UTC?
recs.facts: Pakistan Standard Time (PST) is five hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.
recs.rel: India uses UTC+5:30.

recs.q: Among Muslim-majority countries, what is Pakistan's rank by population?
recs.facts: Indonesia has the largest population among Muslim-majority countries and Pakistan is second.
recs.rel: Bangladesh is usually ranked third.

recs.q: Which is the most populous district of Punjab, Pakistan?
recs.facts: Lahore has the largest population of any district in Punjab (about 13 million in the 2023 census).
recs.rel: Lahore is also the capital of Punjab.

recs.q: Stainless steel is mainly an alloy of iron with which metal?
recs.facts: Stainless steel is iron alloyed with at least about 10.5 percent chromium, which resists rust.
recs.rel: Nickel is often added as well.

recs.q: What is the 15th night of Shaban called?
recs.facts: The night of the 15th of Shaban is known as Shab-e-Barat (night of forgiveness or record).
recs.rel: Shaban is the eighth month of the Islamic calendar and comes just before Ramadan.

recs.q: Which is the 3rd surah of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Ali Imran, so the third is Ali Imran.
recs.rel: Surah Ali Imran has 200 verses and is a Madani surah.

recs.q: In the commonly taught Pakistani order of the five pillars of Islam (Kalima, Salah, Roza, Zakat, Hajj), which is the 4th pillar?
recs.facts: In this order the pillars run Shahada, Salah, Fasting, Zakat, Hajj, so the fourth is Zakat.
recs.rel: Sources differ: the hadith in Sahih Bukhari lists Hajj before fasting, which makes Hajj fourth.

recs.q: An acute angle is how large compared with a right angle?
recs.facts: A right angle is 90 degrees and an acute angle is any angle between 0 and 90 degrees, so it is smaller.
recs.rel: An angle larger than 90 and smaller than 180 degrees is called obtuse.

recs.q: On which date is American Independence Day celebrated?
recs.facts: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, and that day is celebrated as Independence Day.
recs.rel: The Declaration was mainly drafted by Thomas Jefferson.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'ally'?
recs.facts: An ally is a supporter or friend, and its opposite is an enemy or foe.
recs.rel: The word ally comes from the Latin alligare, meaning to bind to.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'cease'?
recs.facts: To cease means to stop, so its opposite is to continue.
recs.rel: Cease is also often used in the phrase ceasefire.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'chum'?
recs.facts: A chum is a close friend, and the opposite is an enemy.
recs.rel: Chum is an informal word and a synonym of buddy.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'climb'?
recs.facts: To climb is to go up, and the opposite is to descend (go down).
recs.rel: Descend comes from the Latin descendere.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'expansion'?
recs.facts: Expansion means growing larger, and its opposite is contraction (becoming smaller).
recs.rel: In economics the opposite phases are expansion and contraction (recession).

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'proceed'?
recs.facts: To proceed is to go forward, and the opposite is to halt or stop.
recs.rel: Proceed is a synonym of advance, continue and progress.

recs.q: What is the base of the natural logarithm?
recs.facts: The natural logarithm ln x is the logarithm to base e, where e is approximately 2.71828.
recs.rel: Common logarithms use base 10, and computer science often uses base 2.

recs.q: What is the value of tan(-x)?
recs.facts: Tangent is an odd function, because sin(-x) = -sin x and cos(-x) = cos x, so tan(-x) = -tan x.
recs.rel: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.

recs.q: Which is the biggest continent in the world by area?
recs.facts: Asia covers about 44.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest of all continents.
recs.rel: Asia is also the most populous continent.

recs.q: In Islam, which is the biggest sin?
recs.facts: The Quran and Hadith describe shirk as the greatest sin, and Allah does not forgive it unless a person repents.
recs.rel: The Quran (Surah An-Nisa 4:48) says that Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives lesser sins.

recs.q: What is the capital of Bangladesh?
recs.facts: Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.
recs.rel: Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan in 1971.

recs.q: What is the political capital of Burundi?
recs.facts: Burundi moved its political capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.
recs.rel: Bujumbura remains the economic capital and the largest city, and was the capital before 2019.

recs.q: What is the capital of Canada?
recs.facts: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, although Toronto is the largest city.
recs.rel: Ottawa lies on the Ottawa River in the province of Ontario.

recs.q: What is the capital of Germany?
recs.facts: Berlin is the capital of Germany.
recs.rel: Bonn was the capital of West Germany before reunification in 1990.

recs.q: What is the capital of Peru?
recs.facts: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru.
recs.rel: Bogota is the capital of Colombia, Quito of Ecuador and Santiago of Chile.

recs.q: What is the capital of Australia?
recs.facts: Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
recs.rel: Sydney is Australia's largest city.

recs.q: What is the capital of Azerbaijan?
recs.facts: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.
recs.rel: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia and Yerevan of Armenia.

recs.q: What is the capital of Uganda?
recs.facts: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
recs.rel: Entebbe, near Kampala, hosts Uganda's main international airport.

recs.q: Which city was the capital of the ancient Gandhara civilization in Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Taxila (Takshashila) is the capital of Gandhara most often given in Pakistani textbooks.
recs.rel: Sources differ: Pushkalavati and later Peshawar (Purushapura) also served as Gandhara capitals.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word abundant?
recs.facts: Abundant means existing in large quantities. Plentiful is the closest synonym.
recs.rel: The opposite of abundant is scarce.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word collaboration?
recs.facts: Collaboration means working together with others toward a common goal. Cooperation has the closest meaning.
recs.rel: The word collaborate comes from Latin meaning to labour together.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word extensive?
recs.facts: Extensive means covering a large area or having a wide range. Widespread is the closest meaning.
recs.rel: The opposite of extensive is limited.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word juvenile?
recs.facts: Juvenile refers to a young person or something belonging to young people. Youthful is the closest meaning.
recs.rel: A juvenile court deals with offenders below the adult age.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word slackness?
recs.facts: Slackness means lack of tightness, energy or care. Looseness or laziness fits best.
recs.rel: Slack is the opposite of taut.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word consent?
recs.facts: Consent means agreement or permission to do something.
recs.rel: The opposite of consent is dissent.

recs.q: What is the combination of the upper house and lower house of a legislature called?
recs.facts: The legislature made up of the upper and lower houses is called Parliament. In Pakistan it is the Majlis-e-Shoora.
recs.rel: Pakistan's Parliament consists of the National Assembly and the Senate together with the President.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
recs.facts: The final consonant n is doubled when adding ing to begin, giving beginning.
recs.rel: Similar doubling occurs in running and swimming.

recs.q: What is the currency of Belarus?
recs.facts: Belarus uses the Belarusian ruble (code BYN).
recs.rel: The hryvnia is the currency of Ukraine and the zloty that of Poland.

recs.q: What is the currency of Kenya?
recs.facts: Kenya uses the Kenyan shilling (code KES).
recs.rel: Ethiopia uses the birr and South Africa the rand.

recs.q: What is the currency of Libya?
recs.facts: Libya uses the Libyan dinar (code LYD).
recs.rel: The Libyan pound was replaced by the dinar in 1971.

recs.q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
recs.facts: Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan rupee (code LKR).
recs.rel: The taka is the currency of Bangladesh and the rufiyaa that of the Maldives.

recs.q: What is the date of America's Independence Day?
recs.facts: The Declaration of Independence of the United States was adopted on 4 July 1776, which is celebrated as Independence Day.
recs.rel: Americans celebrate it every year on 4 July.

recs.q: On what date did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah die?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam died in Karachi on 11 September 1948, a little over a year after Pakistan was created.
recs.rel: His death anniversary is observed on 11 September every year.

recs.q: On which date did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan die?
recs.facts: Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan, known as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021.
recs.rel: He was awarded Nishan-e-Imtiaz and Hilal-e-Imtiaz.

recs.q: What is the derivative of the exponential function e to the power x with respect to x?
opts: x times e to the power (x minus 1)
recs.facts: The function e^x is its own derivative, so d/dx of e^x equals e^x.
recs.rel: The derivative of a to the power x is a^x times ln a.

recs.q: What is the duty of Hazrat Mikail (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and the provision of sustenance.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Azrael takes souls.

recs.q: According to the Islamic teachings, which question is first asked from a person in the grave?
recs.facts: Munkar and Nakir first ask the deceased: Who is your Lord (Man Rabbuka)? Then they ask about his religion and his Prophet.
recs.rel: Salah is the first deed to be accounted for on the Day of Judgement.

recs.q: What is the full official name of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan was named an Islamic Republic for the first time in the Constitution of 1956.

recs.q: What is the standard time offset of Pakistan from GMT (UTC)?
recs.facts: Pakistan Standard Time is five hours ahead of GMT, that is UTC+5.
recs.rel: India uses UTC+5:30, so Pakistan is 30 minutes behind India.

recs.q: Which surah is called the heart (Qalb) of the Quran?
recs.facts: A hadith narrated in the books of Hadith describes Surah Yaseen as the heart of the Quran.
recs.rel: Surah Yaseen is the 36th surah and has 83 verses.

recs.q: What is the highest court of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Supreme Court of Pakistan, in Islamabad, is the apex court of the country.
recs.rel: The Federal Shariat Court examines whether laws conform to Islamic injunctions.

recs.q: What is the highest power of the variable in a polynomial called?
recs.facts: The degree of a polynomial is the largest exponent of its variable. For example, x^3 + 2x has degree 3.
recs.rel: A polynomial of degree 2 is called a quadratic.

recs.q: What is the integral part of a logarithm called?
recs.facts: A logarithm has two parts: the integer part is the characteristic and the decimal part is the mantissa.
recs.rel: The mantissa of a common logarithm is always kept positive.

recs.q: Which is the largest bone of the human body?
recs.facts: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
recs.rel: The smallest bone is the stapes in the middle ear.

recs.q: Which is the largest city of Pakistan by population?
recs.facts: Karachi is the most populous city of Pakistan, with over 14 million people at the 2017 census and about 20 million at the 2023 census.
recs.rel: Lahore is the second largest city.

recs.q: Which is the largest hot desert of the world?
recs.facts: The Sahara in North Africa covers about 9 million square kilometres and is the largest hot desert.
recs.rel: Counting cold deserts, Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.

recs.q: Which is the largest gulf in the world?
recs.facts: The Gulf of Mexico covers about 1.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest gulf.
recs.rel: The Persian Gulf is much smaller, at about 250,000 square kilometres.

recs.q: Which is the largest plateau of the world by area?
recs.facts: The Tibetan Plateau covers about 2.5 million square kilometres and is the largest as well as the highest plateau.
recs.rel: It is often called the Roof of the World.

recs.q: Which is the largest sea of Europe?
recs.facts: The Mediterranean Sea covers about 2.5 million square kilometres, more than any other sea touching Europe.
recs.rel: The Mediterranean connects to the Atlantic Ocean through the Strait of Gibraltar.

recs.q: What is the upgraded version of the Pakistani missile Hatf-IV (Shaheen-I) called?
recs.facts: Hatf-IV is the Shaheen-I ballistic missile, and its longer-range upgraded variant is called Shaheen-IA.
recs.rel: Shaheen-IA was first test fired in April 2012.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word Furqan?
opts: The criterion that separates right from wrong
recs.facts: Furqan comes from an Arabic root meaning to separate or distinguish. It therefore means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
recs.rel: Al-Furqan is a name of the Holy Quran and the title of the 25th surah.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word Islam?
opts: Submission and surrender to the will of Allah
recs.facts: Islam comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, meaning submission, surrender and also peace. It means submitting oneself to Allah.
recs.rel: A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of Tayammum?
opts: To intend or aim at something
recs.facts: Tayammum literally means to intend or to aim at something. In Islamic law it means purifying oneself with clean earth when water is unavailable.
recs.rel: Tayammum is allowed in place of wudu or ghusl when water is not available or its use would be harmful.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word Al-Noor?
recs.facts: Noor is an Arabic word meaning light, and Al-Noor means The Light.
recs.rel: Surah An-Nur is the 24th surah of the Holy Quran and Al-Nur is one of the names of Allah.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word conscious?
recs.facts: Conscious means being awake and aware of oneself or one's surroundings.
recs.rel: Its opposite is unconscious.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word gallant?
recs.facts: Gallant means brave and heroic, and also politely attentive to women.
recs.rel: Gallantry awards are given to soldiers for bravery in action.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Hilf-ul-Fudul?
recs.facts: Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah by chiefs who promised to defend the oppressed and give justice to all. Its name means the pact of the virtuous.
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man before prophethood and praised it later.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the name Israel?
recs.facts: Israel is a Hebrew name, the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), meaning servant of God (Abdullah).
recs.rel: The descendants of Hazrat Yaqub (AS) are called Bani Israel.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word oppression?
opts: Cruel or unjust treatment of people
recs.facts: Oppression means the prolonged cruel or unjust use of power over others.
recs.rel: Zulm is the Urdu and Arabic word for oppression.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Ruku in prayer?
recs.facts: Ruku means to bow, and in salah it is the posture of bowing with hands on the knees.
recs.rel: Sajdah, the prostration, is the posture that follows ruku.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word Tanzeel?
recs.facts: Tanzeel comes from an Arabic root meaning to send down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.
recs.rel: The Quran says it is a Tanzeel from the Lord of the worlds.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word voyage?
opts: A long journey, especially by sea
recs.facts: A voyage is a long journey, especially one made by sea or in space.
recs.rel: Bon voyage is a French phrase wishing someone a pleasant journey.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word defer?
recs.facts: To defer means to put off something until a later time.
recs.rel: Another meaning is to yield to someone's opinion, as in defer to the elders.

recs.q: What is the most abundant organic compound on Earth?
recs.facts: Cellulose forms the cell walls of plants and is the most abundant organic compound on Earth.
recs.rel: Cotton is almost pure cellulose.

recs.q: Which currency is most used in world trade?
recs.facts: The US dollar is the main currency for invoicing trade and for global reserves.
recs.rel: The euro is the second most used reserve currency.

recs.q: What is the multiplicative inverse of an identity matrix?
recs.facts: Since I times I equals I, the inverse of an identity matrix is the identity matrix itself.
recs.rel: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.

recs.q: Who was the father of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was his younger half-brother.

recs.q: What is the boundary line between Pakistan and India in Kashmir called?
recs.facts: The Line of Control (LoC) separates Pakistan-administered and Indian-administered Kashmir.
recs.rel: It was established by the 1972 Simla Agreement, based on the 1949 ceasefire line.

recs.q: Which continent is known as the Dark Continent?
recs.facts: Africa was called the Dark Continent because its interior was unknown to Europeans for a long time.
recs.rel: The nickname became popular through the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.

recs.q: What was the name of the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) who was married to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).

recs.q: What was the name of Pakistan's first satellite?
recs.facts: Badr-1, launched on 16 July 1990 from China, was the first satellite of Pakistan.
recs.rel: It was built by SUPARCO.

recs.q: Which strait separates Russia and the United States (Alaska)?
recs.facts: The Bering Strait lies between the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia and Alaska in the United States.
recs.rel: It connects the Pacific and Arctic oceans and is about 85 km wide.

recs.q: What is the national animal of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Markhor, a wild mountain goat with spiral horns, is the national animal of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Chukar partridge is the national bird, the Deodar the national tree and Jasmine the national flower of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which word is nearest in meaning to 'diversity'?
recs.facts: Diversity means a range of different things, which is what variety means. Uniformity and similarity are its opposites.
recs.rel: Its adjective form is 'diverse', meaning varied or different in kind.

recs.q: What is the new name of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD)?
recs.facts: RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
recs.rel: ECO has its secretariat in Tehran.

recs.q: What is the nisab (minimum threshold) of gold for zakat, in tola?
recs.facts: The nisab of gold is 7.5 tola (about 87.48 grams). The 52.5 tola figure is the nisab of silver.
recs.rel: Zakat on wealth at or above the nisab is 2.5 percent.

recs.q: What is the rate of ushr (zakat on agricultural produce) on land watered by rain?
recs.facts: Ushr means one tenth, so produce from rain-fed land is charged at 10 percent. Land irrigated at a cost is charged at half of that, 5 percent.
recs.rel: Ushr is due on the harvest itself rather than on yearly savings.

recs.q: What is the opposite of 'savage'?
recs.facts: Savage means wild and uncivilized, so its opposite is civilized. Fierce, wild and brutal are similar in meaning to savage.
recs.rel: Savage can also be used as a noun for a brutal person.

recs.q: What is the opposite of 'tame'?
recs.facts: Tame means domesticated and not dangerous, so its opposite is wild. Gentle, docile and domestic are close to tame in meaning.
recs.rel: Tame can also describe something dull, such as a tame film.

recs.q: What was the Pirpur Report (1938)?
opts: A report on the Bengal famine
A Muslim League report on the treatment of Muslims under Congress ministries
A report on the partition of Bengal
recs.facts: The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by the Raja of Pirpur. It listed the injustices done to Muslims in Congress-ruled provinces from 1937 to 1939.
recs.rel: The Muslim League also observed a Day of Deliverance in December 1939 when the Congress ministries resigned.

recs.q: What is the radian measure of a half circle (a straight angle)?
recs.facts: A full circle is 2 pi radians, so half of it is pi radians, which equals 180 degrees.
recs.rel: One radian is about 57.3 degrees.

recs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) was related to Hazrat Abu Talib as his:
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), who raised Ali's cousin the Prophet.
recs.rel: Ali's mother was Fatima bint Asad, and his brother Jafar was also a son of Abu Talib.

recs.q: What is the scalar (dot) product of two vectors A and B?
opts: A B sin(theta) as a vector
recs.facts: The scalar product is A.B = |A||B|cos(theta), where theta is the angle between them. The result is a number, not a vector.
recs.rel: The vector (cross) product uses sin(theta) and gives a vector.

recs.q: What is the other name of the Battle of Ahzab?
recs.facts: The Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates) is also called the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) because the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah. It was fought in 5 AH.
recs.rel: The trench was dug on the suggestion of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

recs.q: What is the shaving of the head during Hajj called?
recs.facts: Halq is shaving the whole head, and Qasr is trimming the hair. One of them is done to come out of the state of Ihram.
recs.rel: Women only trim a small portion of their hair (Taqsir).

recs.q: What is the source of the Yellow River (Huang He)?
opts: Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai, China
recs.facts: The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains of Qinghai Province, China. It then flows east into the Bohai Sea.
recs.rel: The river is about 5,464 km long, though sources differ on the exact figure.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to ADHERENT?
recs.facts: An adherent is a supporter or follower of a person, party or idea.
recs.rel: The verb adhere means to stick to or stay loyal to something.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to EXCITING?
recs.facts: Exciting means causing great enthusiasm or eagerness, which is thrilling.
recs.rel: The word excite comes from the Latin excitare, meaning to rouse.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to EXTREMELY?
recs.facts: Extremely means to a very high degree, which is exceedingly.
recs.rel: Words such as utterly and highly are also similar in sense.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to FLOURISH?
recs.facts: To flourish is to grow and develop in a healthy, successful way, which is to thrive.
recs.rel: Its opposite is to decay or wither.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to HERITAGE?
recs.facts: Heritage is what is passed down from earlier generations, such as traditions and property, which is a legacy.
recs.rel: UNESCO lists World Heritage Sites such as Moenjodaro and Taxila in Pakistan.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to HIERARCHY?
recs.facts: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged in order of rank or importance.
recs.rel: The army rank structure is a typical hierarchy.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to IMPAIR?
recs.facts: To impair is to damage or weaken something so that it works less well. The candidate answer Ridicule has a different meaning.
recs.rel: Its opposite is to enhance or improve.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to INDIFFERENCE?
recs.facts: Indifference is a lack of interest or concern, which is apathy.
recs.rel: Its opposite is concern or enthusiasm.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to LAXITY?
recs.facts: Laxity means lack of strictness or care, which is slackness.
recs.rel: Its opposite is rigour or strictness.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to LEISURE?
recs.facts: Leisure is time free from work or duties, which is free time.
recs.rel: The word comes from the Old French leisir, meaning to be permitted.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to MALICIOUS?
recs.facts: Malicious means intending to harm others, which is spiteful.
recs.rel: Its opposite is benevolent.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to MEDIATE?
recs.facts: To mediate is to step in between two sides in a dispute to settle it, which is to arbitrate.
recs.rel: A mediator is a neutral person who helps two parties reach agreement.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to OPPRESS?
recs.facts: To oppress is to keep people down by cruel or unjust use of power, which is to persecute.
recs.rel: Its opposite is to liberate.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to PRECEDING?
recs.facts: Preceding means coming before in time or order, which is previous.
recs.rel: Its opposite is succeeding or following.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to PREVENT?
recs.facts: To prevent is to stop something from happening, which is to avert.
recs.rel: Hinder and thwart are also close in meaning.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to PROMINENT?
recs.facts: Prominent means well known or important, which is eminent.
recs.rel: It can also mean easily seen or standing out.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to RESENTMENT?
recs.facts: Resentment is a feeling of bitter anger about unfair treatment, which is bitterness.
recs.rel: Its opposite is gratitude.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to SPLENDID?
recs.facts: Splendid means very impressive or excellent, which is magnificent.
recs.rel: Splendid comes from the Latin splendere, to shine.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to TIMID?
recs.facts: Timid means lacking courage or confidence, which is shy.
recs.rel: Its opposite is bold or daring.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to TOTALLY?
recs.facts: Totally means in every way or to the full extent, which is completely or entirely.
recs.rel: Utterly and wholly are other close words.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to TYRANT?
recs.facts: A tyrant is a ruler who uses power in a cruel and unjust way, which is a despot.
recs.rel: Its opposite in sense is a benevolent ruler.

recs.q: Which is the tallest animal living on land?
recs.facts: An adult giraffe can reach about 5 to 5.5 metres in height. No other land animal is taller.
recs.rel: Giraffes mostly eat leaves from acacia trees.

recs.q: What is the title (laqab) of Hazrat Adam (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Adam (AS) is called Abul Bashar, the father of mankind. He is also called Safiullah.
recs.rel: He was the first human and the first prophet in Islamic belief.

recs.q: What is the title of Hazrat Isa (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah (Spirit of Allah) and also Al-Masih. Khalilullah is for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Zabihullah for Ismail (AS).
recs.rel: He was born miraculously to Hazrat Maryam (AS) without a father.

recs.q: What is the title of Hazrat Jibrael (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jibrael (AS) is called Ruh ul Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit) in the Quran, and also Ruh ul Quds.
recs.rel: He brought revelation to all prophets, including the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: What is the length of the Line of Control (LoC) between Pakistan and India in Kashmir in kilometres, as most commonly given?
recs.facts: The Line of Control was set after the 1971 war and the Simla Agreement of 1972. It is most commonly given as about 740 km.
recs.rel: Sources differ, with some giving up to 776 km.

recs.q: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
recs.facts: An adult skeleton has 206 bones. A newborn has about 300 which fuse as the child grows.
recs.rel: The femur is the longest bone of the body.

recs.q: How many landlocked countries are there in the world?
recs.facts: Counting internationally recognised sovereign states with no sea coastline gives 44 landlocked countries.
recs.rel: Counts differ slightly between sources (up to 49) when partially recognised states such as Kosovo are included.

recs.q: What is the upper house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
recs.facts: Pakistan's Parliament has two houses, and the upper house is the Senate.
recs.rel: The lower house is the National Assembly.

recs.q: What is the rate of ushr on crops grown with artificial irrigation (tube wells, canals bought or built at cost)?
recs.facts: Ushr is 10 percent on rain-fed land and half of that, 5 percent, where artificial irrigation involves cost.
recs.rel: Zakat on gold, silver and cash is 2.5 percent.

recs.q: What is the rate of zakat on gold and silver (above nisab)?
recs.facts: Zakat on gold, silver and cash savings above nisab is one-fortieth, which is 2.5 percent.
recs.rel: Nisab for gold is about 7.5 tola (87.48 grams) and for silver 52.5 tola.

recs.q: Which is the world's most populous country today?
recs.facts: India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, according to the United Nations.
recs.rel: Before 2023 China was the most populous country.

recs.q: What is the Yellow River of China also called?
recs.facts: The Yellow River is known in Chinese as the Huang He.
recs.rel: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and Asia.

recs.q: What is Uhud?
recs.facts: Uhud is a mountain just north of Madinah where the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.

recs.q: Youm-ul-Furqan is the name given to the day of which battle?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
recs.rel: Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish.

recs.q: Which part of speech is the word 'ouch'?
recs.facts: 'Ouch' expresses sudden pain or emotion, which is the job of an interjection.
recs.rel: Other interjections include 'alas', 'hurrah' and 'wow'.

recs.q: What technique of defence was used in the Ghazwa Khandaq (Ahzab)?
recs.facts: Muslims dug a trench around the open northern side of Madinah to stop the Quraish cavalry.
recs.rel: The idea was suggested by Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) in 5 AH.

recs.q: What type of article is 'the'?
recs.facts: 'The' points to a specific noun, so it is the definite article.
recs.rel: 'A' and 'an' are the indefinite articles.

recs.q: What type of star is the Sun?
recs.facts: The Sun is a G2V main-sequence star, usually called a yellow dwarf.
recs.rel: In about five billion years it will become a red giant.

recs.q: For what is Hakeem Luqman best known?
recs.facts: Luqman was a sage whose wisdom and advice to his son are praised in the Quran.
recs.rel: Surah Luqman (Surah 31) is named after him.

recs.q: What was RCD, formed in 1964?
opts: Regional Cooperation for Development among Pakistan, Iran and Turkey
Regional Council for Defence of Asia
Regional Cooperation for Defence among Muslim states
recs.facts: RCD stood for Regional Cooperation for Development, an economic grouping of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
recs.rel: It was replaced by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

recs.q: For what is Sher Shah Suri best known?
opts: Grand Trade Road and administrative reforms
recs.facts: Sher Shah Suri (1540-45) rebuilt the Grand Trade Road, introduced the silver rupee and reformed revenue administration.
recs.rel: He defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa and Kannauj.

recs.q: What was the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961?
opts: A failed US-backed invasion of Cuba
A US naval battle with Japan
recs.facts: In April 1961 Cuban exiles trained by the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs and were defeated by Fidel Castro's forces.
recs.rel: It was followed in 1962 by the Cuban Missile Crisis.

recs.q: What was the Cripps Mission?
opts: A 1942 British mission offering India post-war dominion status
A 1946 plan for a united India
recs.facts: Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 with proposals to win Indian support in World War II; both Congress and the Muslim League rejected them.
recs.rel: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 is a different mission.

recs.q: Which is considered the first book of Hadith compiled?
recs.facts: Imam Malik compiled the Muwatta in Madinah in the 8th century, and it is generally taken as the first book of Hadith.
recs.rel: Some sources mention earlier small collections such as Sahifa Hammam ibn Munabbih.

recs.q: Which international organization was the predecessor of the United Nations (UNO)?
recs.facts: The League of Nations, founded in 1920 after World War I, failed to prevent World War II and was replaced by the UN in 1945.
recs.rel: The League of Nations was headquartered in Geneva.

recs.q: In which period did Hazrat Umar (RA) hold the caliphate?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umar (RA) became caliph after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) in 634 CE and was martyred in 644 CE, ruling about ten and a half years.
recs.rel: His caliphate corresponds to roughly 13 to 23 AH.

recs.q: What was the Simla Conference of 1945?
opts: A meeting of Wavell with Indian leaders on self-government that failed
The signing of the Pakistan-India peace agreement
The announcement of the Partition Plan
The first session of the Constituent Assembly
recs.facts: The Viceroy Lord Wavell called Indian leaders to Simla in June-July 1945 to discuss an Executive Council. It failed because Congress and the Muslim League could not agree on who nominates Muslim members.
recs.rel: The Wavell Plan was rejected as the Muslim League insisted on being the sole representative of Muslims.

recs.q: What was the so-called Pig War between the United States and Britain over?
recs.facts: The Pig War of 1859 was a border dispute over San Juan Island; it began after an American farmer shot a British-owned pig. The only casualty was the pig.
recs.rel: The dispute was settled by arbitration in 1872 in favour of the United States.

recs.q: According to the Hadith, what will a person be asked about first on the Day of Judgement regarding the rights of Allah?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) said that the first thing a servant will be called to account for on the Day of Judgement is prayer (Salah).
recs.rel: Regarding rights between people, the first matter judged will be bloodshed.

recs.q: When an ant stings, which acid is injected into the body?
recs.facts: Ant venom contains formic acid, which causes the burning pain of the sting.
recs.rel: Formic acid gets its name from the Latin word formica meaning ant.

recs.q: When did the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic begin?
recs.facts: The first cases were reported in Wuhan, China, in December 2019.
recs.rel: The WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March 2020.

recs.q: In which year did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh?
recs.facts: East Pakistan broke away after the 1971 war, and the Dhaka surrender took place on 16 December 1971.
recs.rel: The Hamoodur Rehman Commission investigated the causes of the 1971 debacle.

recs.q: In which year of the Hijri calendar did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Umrat-ul-Qaza?
recs.facts: After the Treaty of Hudaibiya the Muslims performed the Umrah they were stopped from in 6 AH. They did it the next year, in 7 AH.
recs.rel: It is called Umrat-ul-Qaza because it made up for the Umrah missed in 6 AH.

recs.q: In which year of prophethood did Hazrat Umar (RA) embrace Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umar (RA) accepted Islam in the 6th year of prophethood, after the Prophet's prayer that Allah strengthen Islam through one of the two Umars.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly, some placing it in the 5th year.

recs.q: When did India first present the Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
recs.facts: India took the Kashmir dispute to the UN Security Council on 1 January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.
recs.rel: The UNCIP resolutions of 1948-49 called for a plebiscite in Kashmir.

recs.q: What was the legislature setup under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution created a single-house (unicameral) National Assembly with equal representation (parity) for East and West Pakistan.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.

recs.q: In which year did India take the Kashmir issue to the UN Security Council?
recs.facts: India lodged its complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, after tribal and Pakistani forces entered Kashmir. The Security Council then set up the UN Commission for India and Pakistan (UNCIP).
recs.rel: The UN-brokered ceasefire in Kashmir came into effect on 1 January 1949.

recs.q: In which year did the First World War end?
recs.facts: The armistice with Germany took effect on 11 November 1918, ending the fighting. The Treaty of Versailles followed in 1919.
recs.rel: The First World War began in 1914.

recs.q: In which year did the Second World War end?
recs.facts: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan surrendered in August and September 1945. The war therefore ended in 1945.
recs.rel: The United Nations was founded in the same year, 1945.

recs.q: In which year did the Cabinet Mission visit India?
recs.facts: The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946 and announced its plan in May 1946. It proposed a loose federation, which the Congress and the Muslim League accepted only briefly.
recs.rel: The Cabinet Mission consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.

recs.q: In which year was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in India?
recs.facts: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat leaders, against British rule. Indians boycotted British courts, schools and goods.
recs.rel: Gandhi suspended the movement in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

recs.q: Around which year did the Ottoman Sultanate begin under Osman I?
recs.facts: Osman I founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1299. It lasted until the sultanate was abolished in 1922.
recs.rel: The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453 under Sultan Muhammad II (Mehmed the Conqueror).

recs.q: On which date is Kashmir Day (Kashmir Solidarity Day) observed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan observes Kashmir Solidarity Day on 5 February every year to express support for the people of Indian-held Kashmir.
recs.rel: Kashmiris also observe 27 October as Black Day, the day Indian troops landed in Srinagar in 1947.

recs.q: In which year did the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College, Aligarh, begin as a college?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded a school in 1875, which was raised to college level as the MAO College in 1877. Lord Lytton laid its foundation stone in 1877.
recs.rel: The MAO College became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Hajj made obligatory (according to the most commonly taught view)?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks teach that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH. The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj that year.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as some scholars give 6 AH or 10 AH; the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 AH.

recs.q: In which year was the state of Israel declared?
recs.facts: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate over Palestine ended. The first Arab-Israeli war followed immediately.
recs.rel: The UN General Assembly adopted the Palestine partition plan in November 1947.

recs.q: In which year was the National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) established?
recs.facts: The National Bank of Pakistan was established in November 1949 to help finance the agricultural sector, notably the jute and cotton crops. It later acted as an agent of the State Bank.
recs.rel: The State Bank of Pakistan began working earlier, on 1 July 1948.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver his Last (Farewell) Sermon?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) delivered the Last Sermon during the Farewell Hajj on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH (632 CE), at Arafat. He passed away in 11 AH.
recs.rel: The sermon was delivered at Mount Arafat in the valley of Uranah.

recs.q: In which year did Choudhary Rahmat Ali write the pamphlet 'Now or Never'?
recs.facts: Choudhary Rahmat Ali and his Cambridge colleagues issued the pamphlet 'Now or Never' in January 1933. It first proposed the name Pakistan for a Muslim homeland.
recs.rel: Rahmat Ali is known as the person who coined the name Pakistan.

recs.q: In which year was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) established by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
recs.facts: The RCD was formally established in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic cooperation. It replaced the earlier CENTO-linked arrangements in the economic field.
recs.rel: The RCD was succeeded by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

recs.q: In which year was the Second Battle of Panipat fought between Akbar's army and Hemu?
recs.facts: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556, when Akbar's general Bairam Khan defeated Hemu. It secured the Mughal throne for Akbar.
recs.rel: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was won by Babur against Ibrahim Lodhi.

recs.q: On what date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
recs.facts: The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973, and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. It was authenticated by President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.
recs.rel: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was the Prime Minister when the Constitution was enacted.

recs.q: In which year was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
recs.facts: The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT arrangement.
recs.rel: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

recs.q: At which place did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address of 1930 in which he presented the idea of a separate Muslim state?
recs.facts: Iqbal delivered the Presidential Address at the annual session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad in December 1930.
recs.rel: The Lahore Resolution was passed ten years later, in March 1940.

recs.q: In which region does the Yellow River (Huang He) of China originate?
