recs.facts: The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai province on the Tibetan Plateau and flows east to the Bohai Sea.
recs.rel: It is the second longest river in China after the Yangtze.

recs.q: In which country is Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, located?
recs.facts: Angel Falls (Salto Angel) is in Canaima National Park in Bolivar state, Venezuela.
recs.rel: It is about 979 metres high.

recs.q: Where is Lake Superior located?
recs.facts: Lake Superior is the northernmost of the Great Lakes and lies between the USA and Canada in North America.
recs.rel: It is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

recs.q: Where is the MAO College (founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) located?
recs.facts: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded in 1875 at Aligarh by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
recs.rel: It later became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

recs.q: In which city is the Margalla Hills National Park located?
recs.facts: The Margalla Hills form the northern backdrop of Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Faisal Mosque lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

recs.q: Which Indian Ocean water body is the Bay of Bengal part of?
recs.facts: The Bay of Bengal is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.
recs.rel: It is the largest bay in the world.

recs.q: Between which two countries does the Bay of Bothnia lie?
recs.facts: The Gulf or Bay of Bothnia is the northern arm of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland.
recs.rel: It is the northernmost part of the Baltic Sea.

recs.q: Between which countries does the Gulf (Bay) of Riga lie?
recs.facts: The Gulf of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea bordered by Latvia and Estonia.
recs.rel: Its main port is Riga, the capital of Latvia.

recs.q: In which country is Shark Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located?
recs.facts: Shark Bay is on the coast of Western Australia.
recs.rel: It was listed as a World Heritage Site in 1991.

recs.q: In which region was the ancient Gandhara civilization centred?
recs.facts: Gandhara flourished in the Peshawar valley and Potohar region of northwest Pakistan, with Taxila and Peshawar as major centres.
recs.rel: Gandhara art is famous for Greco-Buddhist sculpture.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of SAARC located?
recs.facts: The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987.
recs.rel: SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
recs.facts: The UN headquarters is on the east side of Manhattan in New York City, USA.
recs.rel: The UN also has major offices at Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC located?
recs.facts: OPEC moved from Geneva to Vienna, Austria in 1965 and has been headquartered there since.
recs.rel: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960.

recs.q: In which city or area is Simly Dam located?
recs.facts: Simly Dam is on the Soan River in the Islamabad Capital Territory, about 30 km from the city.
recs.rel: It is a major source of drinking water for Islamabad.

recs.q: Where is the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) located?
recs.facts: Data Ganj Bakhsh, the author of Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, is buried in Lahore near Bhati Gate. His shrine is one of the most visited in Pakistan.
recs.rel: His death anniversary (Urs) is held every year at the shrine in Lahore.

recs.q: Where is the tomb of the Punjabi poet Waris Shah located?
recs.facts: Waris Shah, author of the epic Heer Ranjha, is buried at Jandiala Sher Khan in Sheikhupura district, where he died in 1798.
recs.rel: Waris Shah was born in Jandiala Sher Khan and wrote Heer in 1766.

recs.q: Where is the Zhob River situated?
recs.facts: The Zhob River rises in Balochistan and flows through the Zhob district, joining the Gomal River.
recs.rel: The Gomal River later flows into the Indus River system through Dera Ismail Khan.

recs.q: Where is the world's largest active volcano, Mauna Loa, located?
recs.facts: Mauna Loa is on the Big Island of Hawaii and is regarded as the largest active volcano on Earth by volume. It erupted in November 2022 for the first time since 1984.
recs.rel: Mount Etna in Italy is Europe's most active volcano.

recs.q: The Yangtze and the Yellow River are the two longest rivers of which country?
recs.facts: Both the Yangtze and the Yellow River (Huang He) flow through China and empty into the sea on its east coast. The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
recs.rel: The Yellow River is called the cradle of Chinese civilization.

recs.q: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated in December 2007?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto was killed on 27 December 2007 after addressing an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. She was attacked as she left the venue.
recs.rel: She had been Prime Minister of Pakistan twice, in 1988-90 and 1993-96.

recs.q: In which city was Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan, assassinated in 1951?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 while addressing a public meeting at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
recs.rel: Company Bagh was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

recs.q: In which city was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
recs.facts: The Tashkent Declaration was signed in Tashkent, then in the Soviet Union and now the capital of Uzbekistan.
recs.rel: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent the day after the signing.

recs.q: Where was the atomic test of Pakistan conducted on 28 May 1998?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan on 28 May 1998.
recs.rel: Pakistan marks 28 May as Youm-e-Takbeer.

recs.q: Where was the Battle of Khaibar fought?
opts: Near Khaibar oasis north of Madinah, Arabia
recs.facts: The Battle of Khaibar was fought in 628-629 AD (7 AH) against the Jewish fortresses at the Khaibar oasis in Arabia. Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus.
recs.rel: The Khyber Pass in Pakistan is a different place with a similar name.

recs.q: Where did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
recs.facts: The first revelation (the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Noor near Makkah.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old at that time.

recs.q: Which acid is found in milk?
recs.facts: Sour milk contains lactic acid, formed when bacteria ferment lactose. Fresh milk is only slightly acidic.
recs.rel: Citric acid is found in lemons and oranges.

recs.q: Which military alliance was formed in 1955 by the Soviet bloc in response to NATO?
recs.facts: The Warsaw Pact was signed in 1955 by the USSR and its eastern European allies as a counter to NATO.
recs.rel: The Warsaw Pact was dissolved in 1991.

recs.q: Which angel will blow the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement?
recs.facts: Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel appointed to blow the Sur to end the world and again to raise the dead.
recs.rel: Hazrat Azrail (AS) is the angel of death.

recs.q: Which body regulates electronic media in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) regulates private television and radio channels.
recs.rel: PEMRA was established in 2002.

recs.q: Which city is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya)?
recs.facts: Multan is called the City of Saints because of its many shrines of Sufi saints, such as Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.
recs.rel: Multan is also known as the City of Mangoes.

recs.q: Which commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the boundary line between Pakistan and India in 1947?
recs.facts: The Boundary Commission chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe demarcated the Punjab and Bengal borders, and the line is called the Radcliffe Line. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.
recs.rel: The Radcliffe Award was announced after independence, on 17 August 1947.

recs.q: Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) addressed King Najashi of Abyssinia on behalf of the Muslim migrants?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib was the spokesman of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He recited verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi.
recs.rel: Najashi later accepted Islam, and the Prophet (PBUH) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.

recs.q: In which country is the Wakhan Corridor situated?
recs.facts: The Wakhan Corridor is a strip of land in the north-east of Afghanistan in Badakhshan province.
recs.rel: It was created as a buffer between the British and Russian empires in the 19th century.

recs.q: Which of the following are the Scandinavian countries?
recs.facts: The Scandinavian countries are Norway, Sweden and Denmark.
recs.rel: Finland and Iceland are usually counted with them as Nordic countries.

recs.q: Which two countries share the border that mostly follows the 49th parallel north?
recs.facts: Much of the border between the contiguous United States and Canada runs along the 49th parallel north.
recs.rel: The 49th parallel was fixed by the Treaty of 1818 and the Oregon Treaty of 1846.

recs.q: Which country was the first to recognise Pakistan after its creation in 1947, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks state that Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan. Iran also sent the first ambassador.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as some also credit Turkey, and Afghanistan opposed Pakistan's UN membership.

recs.q: Which country supplied S-400 air defence missile systems to India?
recs.facts: India signed a deal in 2018 with Russia for S-400 Triumf air defence systems. Deliveries began in 2021.
recs.rel: The S-400 is a Russian long range surface to air missile system.

recs.q: Which country hosted the third modern Olympic Games in 1904?
recs.facts: The third modern Olympics were held in St. Louis, Missouri, USA in 1904. The first was in Athens in 1896 and the second in Paris in 1900.
recs.rel: The 1904 Games were the first Olympics held outside Europe.

recs.q: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) formed in 1964?
recs.facts: The RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey. Afghanistan was never a member.
recs.rel: RCD was replaced by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

recs.q: Which country is known as the Land of the Long White Cloud?
recs.facts: The Maori name Aotearoa is translated as Land of the Long White Cloud and refers to New Zealand.
recs.rel: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand.

recs.q: Which country is the world's largest producer of chromite (chromium ore)?
recs.facts: According to USGS data, South Africa is by far the largest chromite producer, with about 22.9 million tonnes in 2024. Kazakhstan is second.
recs.rel: South Africa also holds the largest chromite reserves in the world.

recs.q: Which two countries jointly developed the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
recs.facts: The JF-17 Thunder was jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex (PAC) Kamra and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
recs.rel: Myanmar was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17.

recs.q: Which cricket league is played in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the professional Twenty20 league of Pakistan. It started in 2016.
recs.rel: Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and 2023.

recs.q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record for the fastest century in One Day Internationals?
recs.facts: Afridi scored a century off 37 balls in 1996. Corey Anderson of New Zealand reached a hundred in 36 balls against West Indies in January 2014 and broke it.
recs.rel: AB de Villiers later took the record with a 31-ball century against West Indies in 2015.

recs.q: Which international day does the United Nations observe on 24 June?
opts: International Day of Women in Diplomacy
recs.facts: The UN General Assembly declared 24 June as the International Day of Women in Diplomacy in 2022. It promotes the participation of women in diplomacy.
recs.rel: World Refugee Day is on 20 June and International Widows Day is on 23 June.

recs.q: Which famous musician was born in Salzburg, Austria?
recs.facts: Mozart was born in Salzburg on 27 January 1756. Beethoven was born in Bonn, Bach in Eisenach and Schubert in Vienna.
recs.rel: Mozart composed more than 600 works before his death in Vienna in 1791.

recs.q: Which was the last Ghazwa in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) personally took part?
recs.facts: The Ghazwa of Tabuk in 9 AH was the last military expedition led personally by the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Tabuk is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the expedition of hardship.

recs.q: Which authority regulates the oil and gas sector in Pakistan?
recs.facts: OGRA was established in 2002 to regulate the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector. NDMA handles disasters, WAPDA water and power, PEMRA electronic media.
recs.rel: OGRA also recommends the prices of petroleum products and natural gas.

recs.q: Which is the coldest desert in the world?
recs.facts: The Antarctic Desert is the coldest and largest desert on Earth, with extremely low rainfall and temperatures far below freezing.
recs.rel: The Gobi is the best known cold desert of Asia, but it is much warmer than Antarctica.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
recs.facts: The verb profit ends in a single t, and the stress is on the first syllable, so the consonant is not doubled: profited.
recs.rel: The same rule gives benefited and budgeted.

recs.q: Which is the deepest ocean in the world?
recs.facts: The Pacific Ocean has the greatest average depth and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point.
recs.rel: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 11,000 metres deep.

recs.q: Which was the first qiblah of the Muslims?
opts: Bait ul Muqaddas (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem
recs.facts: Muslims prayed towards Bait ul Muqaddas for about 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah. The qiblah was then changed to the Kaaba.
recs.rel: The change took place in 2 AH in the Masjid Qiblatain in Madinah.

recs.q: Which is the highest capital city of the world?
recs.facts: La Paz, the seat of government of Bolivia, stands at about 3,640 metres above sea level, higher than any other capital.
recs.rel: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, and Quito is the highest official capital.

recs.q: Which is the highest highway of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Karakoram Highway reaches about 4,693 metres at the Khunjerab Pass on the China border, the highest paved international road.
recs.rel: It links Hasan Abdal in Pakistan with Kashgar in China.

recs.q: Which is the highest peak of Pakistan?
recs.facts: K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen) is 8,611 metres high, the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world.
recs.rel: Nanga Parbat at 8,126 metres is the second highest peak in Pakistan.

recs.q: Which is the highest polo ground in Pakistan and the world?
recs.facts: The Shandur polo ground at Shandur Pass is about 3,700 metres high and is called the highest polo ground in the world.
recs.rel: A famous polo festival between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan is held at Shandur every year.

recs.q: Which mountain is known as the Killer Mountain?
recs.facts: Nanga Parbat is called the Killer Mountain because many climbers died on it in early attempts.
recs.rel: Nanga Parbat means Naked Mountain and is the ninth highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: Which is the largest country of Asia by population?
recs.facts: India overtook China in 2023 and is now the most populous country in both Asia and the world, with about 1.45 billion people.
recs.rel: Earlier, China was the most populous country, which was the answer in 2021-22.

recs.q: Which country is called the largest democracy in the world?
recs.facts: India has the largest electorate and the largest population of any democracy. It is called the world's largest democracy.
recs.rel: India overtook China as the world's most populous country in 2023.

recs.q: Which is the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan?
recs.facts: Pashtuns form the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan, roughly 40 percent of the population.
recs.rel: Tajiks are the second largest ethnic group of Afghanistan.

recs.q: Which is the largest lake of East Africa?
recs.facts: Lake Victoria covers about 68,800 square kilometres and is the largest lake in Africa by area.
recs.rel: Lake Victoria is the source of the White Nile.

recs.q: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
recs.facts: Kazakhstan has an area of about 2.72 million square kilometres and no coastline on an ocean. It is the largest landlocked country.
recs.rel: Mongolia is the second largest landlocked country.

recs.q: Which is the largest man-made lake (reservoir) of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Tarbela Reservoir on the Indus has the largest surface area of any reservoir in Pakistan, about 250 square kilometres.
recs.rel: Tarbela Dam is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

recs.q: Which is the largest salt mine of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Khewra Salt Mine in Jhelum district is the largest salt mine in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
recs.rel: Khewra salt is mostly rock salt, known as Himalayan pink salt.

recs.q: Which is the longest river in the world according to most textbooks?
recs.facts: Most textbooks give the Nile as the longest river, at about 6,650 kilometres.
recs.rel: Some sources measure the Amazon as longer, so sources differ.

recs.q: Which is the national news agency of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) is the state-run national news agency of Pakistan.
recs.rel: APP was nationalised in 1961 and has its headquarters in Islamabad.

recs.q: Which is the wettest place in the world (the one most commonly named in textbooks)?
recs.facts: Mawsynram in Meghalaya, India, receives the highest average annual rainfall of any inhabited place, over 11,000 mm.
recs.rel: Nearby Cherrapunji was once named the wettest place, so sources differ.

recs.q: In the Islamic calendar, which is the year called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)?
recs.facts: In the 10th year of Prophethood, both Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Abu Talib passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.
recs.rel: Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.

recs.q: Which lines are called parallel lines?
opts: Lines that intersect at a right angle
Lines in the same plane that never meet
Lines that meet at one point
recs.facts: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and stay the same distance apart, so they never meet however far they are extended.
recs.rel: A line that cuts two parallel lines is called a transversal.

recs.q: Which mountain (peak) lies on the border between China and Pakistan?
recs.facts: K2 in the Karakoram lies on the China-Pakistan border, between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.
recs.rel: At 8,611 m, K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: Which mountain range lies between France and Italy?
recs.facts: The Alps, including Mont Blanc, mark part of the border between France and Italy.
recs.rel: Mont Blanc, at about 4,800 m, is the highest peak in the Alps.

recs.q: Which mountain range separates Spain and France?
recs.facts: The Pyrenees run between France and Spain.
recs.rel: Andorra lies within the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

recs.q: Which obligatory act is mentioned in the Quran most often together with Zakat?
recs.facts: The Quran repeatedly pairs the command to establish Salah with the command to pay Zakat.
recs.rel: The phrase 'Aqeemus-Salah wa Atuz-Zakah' occurs many times in the Quran.

recs.q: Which ocean lies along the coast of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km is on the Arabian Sea, which is part of the Indian Ocean.
recs.rel: Karachi, Gwadar and Port Qasim are Pakistan's main ports.

recs.q: Which of the following does not mean big: huge, massive, scrap?
recs.facts: Huge and massive both mean very large, while scrap means a small piece or leftover.
recs.rel: Scrap can also mean to discard something as useless.

recs.q: Which ancient civilization flourished in Taxila?
recs.facts: Taxila was a major city of the Gandhara civilization and a famed centre of learning.
recs.rel: Taxila was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

recs.q: Which Pakistani army operation was launched nationwide in February 2017?
recs.facts: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was announced on 22 February 2017 after a wave of terror attacks across Pakistan.
recs.rel: Zarb-e-Azb began in June 2014 and Rah-e-Rast in 2009.

recs.q: Which principal organ of the United Nations is no longer active (suspended operations)?
recs.facts: The Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 after Palau, the last trust territory, became independent.
recs.rel: The other five principal organs are still functioning.

recs.q: Which organization oversees international civil aviation?
recs.facts: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), a UN agency, sets global standards for civil aviation.
recs.rel: ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.

recs.q: Which Pakistani batter holds the highest individual score in Test cricket for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958, still Pakistan's highest Test score.
recs.rel: Younis Khan's 313 against Sri Lanka in 2009 is the second highest by a Pakistani.

recs.q: Which Pakistani scientist won the Nobel Prize in 1979?
recs.facts: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the unified electroweak theory.
recs.rel: Abdus Salam is the only Pakistani Nobel laureate in Physics; Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

recs.q: Which planet is named after the Roman equivalent of the Greek god Zeus?
recs.facts: Jupiter is the Roman name of the king of the gods, whom the Greeks called Zeus.
recs.rel: Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system.

recs.q: Which planet comes closest to the Earth?
recs.facts: Venus approaches Earth to about 38 million km, closer than any other planet.
recs.rel: Some recent calculations show Mercury is nearest on average over time, but textbooks give Venus.

recs.q: Which prophet built the ark (boat) at the command of Allah before the great flood?
recs.facts: Allah commanded Hazrat Nuh (AS) to build the ark to save the believers from the flood.
recs.rel: Surah Nuh of the Quran is named after this prophet.

recs.q: Which Sahabi did the Prophet (PBUH) call the door of knowledge?
recs.facts: A hadith reports the Prophet (PBUH) saying: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its door.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

recs.q: Which preposition completes the sentence: 'He reminded me ___ my History teacher'?
recs.facts: The verb 'remind' takes 'of' when something resembles or recalls another person or thing.
recs.rel: 'Remind someone about' is used for a task or duty, for example remind me about the meeting.

recs.q: Which preposition is used with 'laugh' when making fun of someone: 'laughed ___ someone'?
recs.facts: To laugh at someone means to mock them; 'laugh at' is the correct phrasal form.
recs.rel: 'Laugh with someone' means to share the joke in a friendly way.

recs.q: Which province of Pakistan has the largest provincial assembly?
recs.facts: The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab has 371 seats, more than the other three assemblies.
recs.rel: Sindh has 168 seats, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 145 and Balochistan 65.

recs.q: Which surah of the Holy Quran is named after the ant?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Naml (the Ant), the 27th surah, takes its name from the story of the ant that warned its colony about Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) and his army.
recs.rel: Al-Nahl is the surah named after the bee and Al-Ankabut the one named after the spider.

recs.q: Which two oceans does the Panama Canal connect?
recs.facts: The Panama Canal cuts across the Isthmus of Panama and joins the Atlantic Ocean (via the Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean. This saves ships the long voyage around South America.
recs.rel: The Panama Canal was opened in 1914.

recs.q: Which two surahs of the Holy Quran are together called Muawwazatain?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah Al-Nas (114) both begin with a request to seek refuge (ta'awwuz) with Allah. That is why the pair is called Muawwazatain.
recs.rel: These are the last two surahs of the Quran and are commonly recited for protection.

recs.q: Which was the first Muslim country to become a nuclear power?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998 and became the first Muslim country with nuclear weapons.
recs.rel: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-armed country in the world, after India's tests earlier in May 1998.

recs.q: Which defensive technique was used by the Muslims in the Battle of Khandaq (Trench) in 5 AH?
opts: Building a wall of stones around Makkah
Fighting from the hills of Uhud
A night surprise attack on the enemy camp
recs.facts: On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA), the Muslims dug a long trench across the open side of Madinah. The Quraish and their allies could not cross it and had to retreat.
recs.rel: The battle is also called the Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates).

recs.q: Who are called Ahl ul Bait?
opts: All the companions of the Prophet (PBUH)
The family members of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
recs.facts: Ahl ul Bait means the people of the house, that is the family of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), including his wives, daughter Fatimah (RA), Hazrat Ali (RA) and their children.
recs.rel: The Quran addresses the Ahl ul Bait in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 33.

recs.q: Which of the following was a daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The four daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (RA). Aisha, Hafsa and Khadija (RA) were his wives.
recs.rel: All the daughters were born to Hazrat Khadija (RA).

recs.q: Who is called the Hawari (special helper) of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: On the day of Khandaq the Prophet (PBUH) said that every prophet has a Hawari and his Hawari is Zubair (RA), as recorded in Sahih Bukhari.
recs.rel: The word Hawari is also used in the Quran for the disciples of Prophet Isa (AS).

recs.q: Who broke Shahid Afridi's record for the most sixes in One Day Internationals?
recs.facts: Rohit Sharma hit his 352nd ODI six on 30 November 2025 against South Africa at Ranchi, passing Afridi's 351.
recs.rel: Chris Gayle, with 331 sixes, is third on the all-time ODI list.

recs.q: Who compiled the hadith collection Sahih Muslim?
recs.facts: Sahih Muslim was compiled by Imam Muslim bin al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi (died 261 AH).
recs.rel: Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim together are known as the Sahihain.

recs.q: Who conducts and governs the modern Olympic Games?
recs.facts: The International Olympic Committee, founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin, organises the modern Olympic Games.
recs.rel: The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

recs.q: Who elects the members of the Senate of Pakistan from the provinces?
opts: The members of the Provincial Assemblies
recs.facts: Senators from each province are elected indirectly by the members of that provincial Assembly through the single transferable vote system.
recs.rel: The Senate is a permanent house with half of its members retiring every three years.

recs.q: Who first raised the Kashmir issue in the United Nations Security Council, and when?
recs.facts: India lodged a complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, and the Security Council took up the matter.
recs.rel: Pakistan replied with its own complaint on 15 January 1948.

recs.q: Who founded the technology company Microsoft?
recs.facts: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft on 4 April 1975.
recs.rel: Microsoft began in Albuquerque, New Mexico, before moving to Washington State.

recs.q: Who gave the first Azan in Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA) was appointed by the Prophet (PBUH) as the first muezzin and called the first Azan in Madinah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the Azan in a dream, and the Prophet (PBUH) taught them to Bilal (RA).

recs.q: Who introduced the fictional spy character James Bond?
recs.facts: Ian Fleming created James Bond in the novel Casino Royale, published in 1953.
recs.rel: Fleming had worked in British naval intelligence during the Second World War.

recs.q: Who is known as the father of the hydrogen bomb?
recs.facts: Edward Teller, working with Stanislaw Ulam, is credited with the design of the hydrogen bomb, first tested in 1952.
recs.rel: Robert Oppenheimer is known as the father of the atomic bomb; sources sometimes also credit Ulam alongside Teller.

recs.q: Who was Abu Lahab?
opts: The uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who opposed him
The leader of the Banu Quraiza
recs.facts: Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza bin Abdul Muttalib) was an uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who strongly opposed Islam.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) of the Quran was revealed about him.

recs.q: Who was Baba Farid (Hazrat Fariduddin Ganj Shakar)?
opts: A Sufi saint of the Chishti order
A poet of the Sikh court
recs.facts: Baba Farid (1179-1266) was a famous Punjabi Sufi saint and poet of the Chishti order, and a disciple of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
recs.rel: His shrine is in Pakpattan, and his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

recs.q: Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in One Day Internationals?
recs.facts: Inzamam-ul-Haq scored 11,701 runs in ODIs, the most for Pakistan.
recs.rel: Mohammad Yousuf (9,554) and Saeed Anwar (8,824) follow him on the list.

recs.q: Which angel is responsible for rain and sustenance according to Islamic belief?
recs.facts: Hazrat Mikaeel (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.
recs.rel: Hazrat Israfeel (AS) will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgement.

recs.q: Who wrote Humayun Nama, an account of the reign of Emperor Humayun?
recs.facts: Gulbadan Begum, a daughter of Babur and aunt of Akbar, wrote Humayun Nama.
recs.rel: Akbar had asked her to record her memories for Abul Fazl's Akbarnama.

recs.q: Who was the half-brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was a son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) from Hazrat Sarah, while Hazrat Ismail (AS) was his son from Hazrat Hajra, so they were half-brothers.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

recs.q: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
recs.facts: Mir Sarfraz Bugti took office as Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and was still serving in mid-2026.
recs.rel: His predecessors included Abdul Quddus Bizenjo (2021-2023) and Jam Kamal Khan (2018-2021).

recs.q: Who is the Chief of the Naval Staff of the Pakistan Navy?
recs.facts: Admiral Naveed Ashraf took over as Chief of the Naval Staff in October 2023 and is the serving chief in 2026.
recs.rel: His predecessors were Admiral Muhammad Zakaullah and, before him, Admiral Muhammad Amjad Khan Niazi.

recs.q: Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq of the PML-N was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024 and is the current Speaker.
recs.rel: Asad Qaiser, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Speaker from 2018 to 2022.

recs.q: Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Khawaja Muhammad Asif of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Defence in the current government.
recs.rel: Pervez Khattak, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Defence Minister from 2018 to 2022.

recs.q: Who is the Federal Minister for Interior of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Mohsin Naqvi is the Federal Interior Minister in the current government.
recs.rel: He is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and president of the Asian Cricket Council.

recs.q: Who is the Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab?
recs.facts: Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan of the PML-N has been Speaker of the Punjab Assembly since February 2024.
recs.rel: He is a lawyer from Kasur and was earlier a Special Assistant to the Chief Minister.

recs.q: Who is the son of Hazrat Hajira (A.S)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hajira was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S).
recs.rel: The well of Zamzam sprang up near the infant Ismail (A.S) in Makkah.

recs.q: Who is known as the Traveler of Islam?
recs.facts: Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan scholar, traveled across much of the Muslim world and beyond for about 30 years and is called the Traveler of Islam.
recs.rel: His travel account is known as the Rihla.

recs.q: Who is the writer of the book The Spirit of Islam?
recs.facts: The Spirit of Islam (1891) was written by Syed Ameer Ali.
recs.rel: Ameer Ali also wrote A Short History of the Saracens.

recs.q: Who is the writer of the book Becoming?
recs.facts: Becoming (2018) is the memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.
recs.rel: It became one of the best-selling memoirs of all time.

recs.q: Who is the compiler of Tirmizi Sharif (Jami at-Tirmidhi)?
recs.facts: Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Isa at-Tirmidhi.
recs.rel: It is one of the six major Hadith collections known as the Sihah Sitta.

recs.q: Who served the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) for ten years in Madinah?
recs.facts: Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet (S.A.W) as a boy by his mother and served him for about ten years.
recs.rel: He narrated over 2000 Hadith.

recs.q: Who founded Facebook?
recs.facts: Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 from Harvard University with his college roommates.
recs.rel: The company was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021.

recs.q: Who is the father of Hazrat Usman (R.A)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the son of Affan bin Abi al-As of the Banu Umayya clan of Quraysh.
recs.rel: Abu Quhafa was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) and Khattab the father of Hazrat Umar (R.A).

recs.q: Who is called the father of modern chemistry?
recs.facts: Antoine Lavoisier is commonly called the father of modern chemistry for his work on oxygen and the law of conservation of mass.
recs.rel: Some sources give this title to Robert Boyle, so sources differ.

recs.q: Who is regarded as the founder of modern nursing?
recs.facts: Florence Nightingale established modern nursing practice and training after her work in the Crimean War.
recs.rel: She founded the Nightingale School of Nursing in London in 1860, and International Nurses Day is on her birthday, 12 May.

recs.q: Who mediated between Pakistan and India in the Tashkent Agreement of January 1966?
recs.facts: The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent. The agreement ended the 1965 war.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it, and Shastri died in Tashkent the next day.

recs.q: Who first proposed the name Pakistan?
recs.facts: Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
recs.rel: Allama Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address proposed a separate Muslim state but did not use the name Pakistan.

recs.q: Who refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature?
recs.facts: The French writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, saying he refused official honours.
recs.rel: Boris Pasternak was forced by Soviet authorities to decline his 1958 Nobel Prize.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, by whom are the senators of the provinces elected?
opts: The members of the provincial assembly
recs.facts: Senators for each province are elected by the members of that provincial assembly by the single transferable vote.
recs.rel: The Senate has a Chairman who acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.

recs.q: Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of Pakistan?
recs.facts: President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed the Simla Agreement with the Indian Prime Minister in July 1972.
recs.rel: The agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.

recs.q: Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement in India in 1920?
recs.facts: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat Movement.
recs.rel: It was called off in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

recs.q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to perform the functions of office?
opts: The Speaker of the National Assembly
recs.facts: Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President. If there is no Chairman, the Speaker of the National Assembly does so.
recs.rel: Muhammad Mian Soomro and Wasim Sajjad are among Senate Chairmen who have acted as President.

recs.q: Who were the Banu Nadir (Banu Nuzair) in the history of Madina?
opts: A branch of the Aws tribe
recs.facts: Banu Nadir was a Jewish tribe living near Madina. They were exiled in 4 AH after plotting against the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The other Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qainuqa and Banu Quraiza.

recs.q: Who became the Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan after Yahya Khan in December 1971?
recs.facts: After the fall of Dhaka, Yahya Khan handed power to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became President and the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator.
recs.rel: Martial law was lifted when the 1973 Constitution came into force.

recs.q: Who was the husband of Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayesha, daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr, was married to the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
recs.rel: She is known as Umm ul Momineen and narrated over two thousand hadith.

recs.q: Who was the second Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Liaqat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister. After his assassination in 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second.
recs.rel: Nazimuddin had been Governor-General before becoming Prime Minister.

recs.q: Who was the second President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Iskander Mirza was the first President under the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan removed him in 1958 and became the second.
recs.rel: Counts differ if the Governor-General office is included, but textbooks list Ayub Khan second.

recs.q: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1965 war with India?
recs.facts: General Muhammad Musa Khan was Commander-in-Chief from 1958 to 1966 and led the army in the 1965 war.
recs.rel: Yahya Khan succeeded him as Commander-in-Chief in 1966.

recs.q: Who was the closest friend of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) was the Prophet's closest friend and the first man outside his family circle to accept Islam. He is called Siddique and Yar-e-Ghar (companion of the cave).
recs.rel: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first caliph of Islam and ruled from 11 AH to 13 AH.

recs.q: Who was the commander of the Quraysh army in the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: Abu Sufyan bin Harb led the Makkan army of about 3,000 in 3 AH, because Abu Jahl had been killed at Badr. Khalid bin Walid commanded the cavalry wing.
recs.rel: Abu Sufyan later accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

recs.q: Who was the first Ameer-ul-Momineen (Commander of the Faithful) in Islamic history?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was called Khalifa-tu-Rasul Allah, while Hazrat Umar (RA) was the first to be addressed as Ameer-ul-Momineen. Most Islamic history books record this.
recs.rel: The title was adopted by later caliphs such as Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).

recs.q: Who was the first caliph of Islam?
recs.facts: After the Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, the Muslims chose Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) as their first caliph at Saqifa Bani Saida.
recs.rel: The four Rashidun caliphs ruled in the order Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman and Ali (RA).

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
recs.facts: Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg, for the electroweak theory. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim Nobel laureate in science.
recs.rel: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 and is the youngest Nobel laureate.

recs.q: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Under the 1956 Constitution, Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956. Before this, the head of state was the Governor General.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam and Ghulam Muhammad had served as Governor General, not as President.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani woman to climb K2?
recs.facts: Samina Baig reached the summit of K2 on 22 July 2022, a few hours before Naila Kiani. She was the first Pakistani woman to do so.
recs.rel: Samina Baig had earlier climbed Mount Everest in 2013 and completed the Seven Summits in 2014.

recs.q: Who was the first woman to travel to space?
recs.facts: Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963. She orbited the Earth 48 times.
recs.rel: Sally Ride became the first American woman in space in 1983.

recs.q: Who was the first woman officer of the Pakistan Army to be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General (three-star)?
recs.facts: Lt Gen Nigar Johar of the Army Medical Corps was promoted in June 2020 and became the first woman in the Pakistan Army to reach three-star rank. She was also appointed the first female Surgeon General of the Pakistan Army.
recs.rel: She is from Swabi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

recs.q: Who was the guarantor and third party that brokered the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan?
recs.facts: The World Bank mediated the long negotiations and signed the treaty as a party for certain provisions. The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.
recs.rel: Some sources describe the World Bank's role as a broker rather than a strict guarantor.

recs.q: Who was the head of state of Pakistan in 1960?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan took power in the October 1958 coup and was President of Pakistan in 1960. He remained in office until March 1969.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza, the first President, was removed by Ayub Khan in October 1958.

recs.q: Who was the false prophet and enemy leader fought by the Muslims in the Battle of Yamama?
recs.facts: The Battle of Yamama in 12 AH was fought against the false claimant to prophethood Musaylima Kazzab and his tribe Banu Hanifa. The Muslim commander was Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA), and Musaylima was killed.
recs.rel: Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.

recs.q: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906 that presented Muslim demands to the Viceroy Lord Minto?
recs.facts: The Simla Deputation of 1 October 1906 was led by Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, Agha Khan III. It asked for separate electorates for Muslims.
recs.rel: The All India Muslim League was founded a few months later in Dhaka in December 1906.

recs.q: Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty on behalf of Pakistan in 1960?
recs.facts: President Ayub Khan signed the treaty for Pakistan in Karachi on 19 September 1960. Jawaharlal Nehru signed it for India.
recs.rel: W. A. B. Iliff signed for the World Bank.

recs.q: Who was the second martial law administrator of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan imposed the first martial law in October 1958. General Yahya Khan imposed the second in March 1969 when Ayub resigned.
recs.rel: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed the third martial law in July 1977.

recs.q: Why is Hazrat Usman (RA) called Zun-Noorain?
opts: He married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW)
He had two lights on his sword
He was the leader of two armies
He migrated to two countries only
recs.facts: Zun-Noorain means Possessor of Two Lights. He married Ruqayyah (RA) and later Umm Kulthum (RA), both daughters of the Prophet (SAW).
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman (RA) was the third Rightly Guided Caliph and also migrated to Abyssinia with Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).

recs.q: Who were the Banu Nadir?
recs.facts: Banu Nadir was one of the main Jewish tribes living near Madinah. They were exiled after they broke their agreement with the Muslims.
recs.rel: The other Jewish tribes of Madinah were Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayza.

recs.q: Which of the following was an uncle of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was a paternal uncle of the Holy Prophet (SAW). Hazrat Ali (RA) was his cousin, while Abu Bakr and Umar were companions.
recs.rel: His other uncles included Abu Talib, Hazrat Abbas (RA) and Abu Lahab.

recs.q: Who wrote Hayat-e-Javed, the biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
recs.facts: Hayat-e-Javed, a biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, was written by Khawaja Altaf Hussain Hali in 1901.
recs.rel: Hali also wrote the Musaddas, and Dr Javed Iqbal wrote the Iqbal biography Zinda Rood.

recs.q: Who wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob?
recs.facts: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob is the oldest Persian book on Sufism and was written by Hazrat Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
recs.rel: His shrine is in Lahore.

recs.q: Who compiled the hadith book Sunan Nasai?
recs.facts: Sunan Nasai was compiled by Imam Nasai, whose full name was Ahmad ibn Shuayb al-Nasai.
recs.rel: It is one of the six major hadith collections known as Sihah Sittah.

recs.q: Who wrote the memoir Becoming?
recs.facts: Becoming is the 2018 memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.
recs.rel: It became one of the best selling memoirs in history.

recs.q: Who compiled the hadith book Sunan Abu Dawood?
recs.facts: Sunan Abu Dawood was compiled by Imam Abu Dawood Sulayman ibn al-Ashath al-Sijistani.
recs.rel: It is one of the six major hadith collections and focuses on legal rulings.

recs.q: Who wrote the pamphlet Now or Never (1933)?
recs.facts: Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish Forever? was written by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
recs.rel: In it he proposed the name Pakistan for a separate Muslim homeland.

recs.q: Who compiled Jami at-Tirmidhi (Sunan Tirmidhi)?
recs.facts: Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi.
recs.rel: It is one of the six major hadith collections and grades each hadith.

recs.q: Which of these countries has only a maritime border with Pakistan and no land border?
recs.facts: Pakistan has land borders with Afghanistan, China, India and Iran. Oman has no land border with Pakistan but shares a sea boundary in the Arabian Sea.
recs.rel: The Pakistan-Oman maritime boundary agreement came into force in 2000.

recs.q: With which Indian prime minister did Pakistan sign the Lahore Declaration in 1999?
recs.facts: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
recs.rel: Soon after, the Kargil conflict of 1999 damaged the peace process.

recs.q: With whom is the theory of relativity associated?
recs.facts: The theory of relativity was developed by Albert Einstein.
recs.rel: He published special relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1915.

recs.q: With the help of which country was the KANUPP-1 nuclear power plant at Karachi constructed?
recs.facts: KANUPP-1 is a CANDU heavy water reactor supplied by Canada and started operating in 1972.
recs.rel: Pakistan's later plants at Chashma were built with Chinese help.

recs.q: Yaum-ul-Furqan is the name of the day of which event?
recs.facts: The Quran calls the day of the Battle of Badr Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
recs.rel: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH.

recs.q: Y = mx + c is the formula of what?
recs.facts: It is the slope-intercept form of the equation of a straight line, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.
recs.rel: The line crosses the y-axis at the point (0, c).

recs.q: 1 degree is equal to how many seconds (of arc)?
recs.facts: 1 degree = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 1 degree = 60 x 60 = 3600 seconds.
recs.rel: A full circle is 360 degrees, which equals 1,296,000 seconds of arc.

recs.q: 15 is divisible by which prime numbers?
recs.facts: 15 = 3 x 5, and both 3 and 5 are prime numbers.
recs.rel: The number 1 is not a prime number because it has only one divisor.

recs.q: 8/7 is which type of fraction?
recs.facts: In 8/7 the numerator 8 is greater than the denominator 7, so it is an improper fraction.
recs.rel: 8/7 can be written as the mixed fraction 1 and 1/7.

recs.q: A boy bought a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. What is his profit percentage?
recs.facts: Profit = 700 - 500 = Rs 200. Profit percentage = 200 / 500 x 100 = 40%.
recs.rel: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

recs.q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. When Ali is 8 years old, what will his sister's age be?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 4 x 3 = 12 years, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 8 she will be 8 + 9 = 17 years.
recs.rel: Solve age questions by finding the fixed difference first.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 11?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 3 x 4 = 12 years, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 8 = 19 years.
recs.rel: The age difference stays constant, here always 8 years.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and Sara is 3 times Ali's age. What will Sara's age be when Ali is 12?
recs.facts: Sara is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 12 she will be 12 + 8 = 20 years.
recs.rel: Both ages increase by the same number of years.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ali is 11 years old, what is his sister's age?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15 years, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 10 = 21 years.
recs.rel: After 6 years both of them are 6 years older: 15 + 6 = 21.

recs.q: A train travels 60 km in 20 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
recs.facts: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Speed = 60 / (1/3) = 180 km/h.
recs.rel: To change km per minute into km per hour, multiply by 60.

recs.q: A train's speed is 100 km/h. How far does it cover in 1 minute (to two decimal places)?
recs.facts: 1 minute = 1/60 hour. Distance = 100 / 60 = 1.67 km (about 1667 metres).
recs.rel: 100 km/h is about 27.8 metres per second.

recs.q: A helicopter covers 320 km using 40 gallons of fuel. How many gallons are needed to cover 700 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km = 40/320 = 1/8 gallon. For 700 km: 700/8 = 87.5 gallons.
recs.rel: Fuel used is directly proportional to the distance covered.

recs.q: A helicopter covers 350 km using 80 gallons of fuel. How many gallons does it need for 700 km?
recs.facts: 700 km is twice 350 km, so the fuel needed is twice as much: 2 x 80 = 160 gallons.
recs.rel: In direct proportion, doubling the distance doubles the fuel.

recs.q: A jet covers 320 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons will it use to cover 700 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallon. For 700 km: 700 x 0.15625 = 109.375 gallons.
recs.rel: The same result comes from the proportion 50 x 700 / 320.

recs.q: A man walks towards north, after some time turns right and then turns left. In which direction is he moving now?
recs.facts: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. A left turn from east makes him face north again.
recs.rel: A right turn followed by a left turn cancels out.

recs.q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will come last?
recs.facts: Alphabetical order of the letters is A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.
recs.rel: Y is the 25th letter of the English alphabet.

recs.q: Ali and Hasan have 24 apples in total. Ali has 3 times as many apples as Hasan. How many apples does Hasan have?
recs.facts: Let Hasan have x apples, then Ali has 3x. So 4x = 24 and x = 6.
recs.rel: Ali then has 18 apples, and 18 + 6 = 24.

recs.q: Ali is older than Kashif and Kashif is older than Haris. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
recs.facts: Ali is older than Kashif, who is older than Haris, so Ali is the oldest and Haris the youngest.
recs.rel: Such ordering questions are solved fastest by writing the names in a single line from largest to smallest.

recs.q: Ali is taller than Osama and Osama is taller than Faheem. Who is the tallest of all?
recs.facts: Ali is taller than Osama, who is taller than Faheem, so Ali is the tallest.
recs.rel: Faheem is the shortest in this chain.

recs.q: Ali is younger than Hassan and Akbar is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
recs.facts: Hassan is older than Ali, who is older than Akbar, so Hassan is the oldest and Akbar the youngest.
recs.rel: Ali is in the middle, so he is neither the oldest nor the youngest.

recs.q: Ali's sister is three times Ali's age. If Ali is 3 years old, how old will his sister be when Ali is 7 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old when Ali is 3. The age gap is 6 years, so when Ali is 7 she is 7 + 6 = 13.
recs.rel: The difference between two people's ages always stays the same.

recs.q: Are the numbers 1, 3, 9, 11, 13 even or odd numbers?
recs.facts: Each of these numbers leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
recs.rel: Two is the only even prime number.

recs.q: Arrange these words alphabetically: beauty, leopard. Which comes first?
recs.facts: B comes before L in the alphabet, so beauty comes first and leopard second.
recs.rel: Dictionary order compares words letter by letter from the left.

recs.q: Complete the alphabet pairs series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
recs.facts: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) while the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W). The next pair is DW.
recs.rel: Pairs of letters taken from opposite ends of the alphabet always sum to position 27.

recs.q: Complete the series: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, ?
recs.facts: Terms at odd places: 115, 170, 235 (adding 55, then 65). Terms at even places: 55, 65, 75 (adding 10 each time).
recs.rel: Series with two interleaved patterns should be split into alternate terms.

recs.q: Complete the series: 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
recs.facts: Each term is double the previous one, so 16 x 2 = 32.
recs.rel: This is a geometric progression with common ratio 2.

recs.q: Cows are twice the number of horses and there are 9 goats. If there are 6 cows, how many animals are there in total?
recs.facts: Horses = 6 / 2 = 3. Total = 6 cows + 3 horses + 9 goats = 18.
recs.rel: Read carefully which quantity is the base of 'twice'.

recs.facts: The number 3 appears four times, more than any other value (2 and 5 appear twice).
recs.rel: The mode is the most frequent value in a data set.

recs.q: Find the next term in the coding series: 3Z, 4X, 5U, ?
recs.facts: Numbers rise by 1 (3, 4, 5, 6). Letter positions are Z=26, X=24, U=21, falling by 2, 3, then 4, so next is 17 = Q.
recs.rel: Convert letters to their alphabet positions to see the pattern.

recs.q: How do you find the midpoint of a line segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
opts: Average the x values and the y values
recs.facts: The midpoint is ((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2), the average of each coordinate.
recs.rel: The midpoint of a segment divides it into two equal parts.

recs.q: How many minutes are there in 20 degrees (angle measure)?
recs.facts: One degree = 60 minutes of arc, so 20 x 60 = 1200 minutes.
recs.rel: One minute of arc equals 60 seconds of arc.

recs.q: What is the maximum number of right angles a triangle can have?
recs.facts: Angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees, so two right angles (180) would leave nothing for the third angle. At most one right angle is possible.
recs.rel: A triangle with one right angle is called a right-angled triangle.

recs.q: How many vowels are in the letters: DACBIJUHOLEWPSI?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, I, U, O, E, I, which makes 6.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 28th be?
recs.facts: The 28th is 27 days after the 1st. 27 = 3 weeks + 6 days, so Monday + 6 days = Sunday.
recs.rel: The 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th share the same weekday.

recs.q: If 2 log 5 = x, find x.
recs.facts: By the power rule, n log a = log (a^n), so 2 log 5 = log 5^2 = log 25.
recs.rel: Numerically, log 25 to base 10 is about 1.398.

recs.q: If 20 pens cost Rs 2000, how much will 40 pens cost?
recs.facts: One pen costs 2000 / 20 = Rs 100, so 40 pens cost 40 x 100 = Rs 4000.
recs.rel: Doubling the number of items doubles the cost at a fixed price.

recs.q: If 3x - 5 = 4, find x.
recs.facts: Add 5 to both sides: 3x = 9, so x = 3.
recs.rel: Check: 3 x 3 - 5 = 4.

recs.q: If 6 : m :: 9 : 12, what is m?
recs.facts: Proportion gives 6/m = 9/12, so m = 6 x 12 / 9 = 8.
recs.rel: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (a x d = b x c).

recs.q: If the 12th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 12th to the 24th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Monday gives Saturday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 14th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Friday gives Wednesday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 25th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 25th is 23 days, and 23 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2. Moving 2 day(s) forward from Monday gives Wednesday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 24th is 22 days, and 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Monday gives Tuesday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 13th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 13th is 11 days, and 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4. Moving 4 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Thursday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 23rd day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Friday gives Friday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Monday gives Monday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 14th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Tuesday gives Sunday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 26th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 26th is 23 days, and 23 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2. Moving 2 day(s) forward from Friday gives Sunday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 13th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 13th is 10 days, and 10 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days, and 19 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Monday gives Saturday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 25th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Friday gives Friday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 21st day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 21st is 17 days, and 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Friday gives Monday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days, and 20 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Monday gives Sunday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 28th is 24 days, and 24 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 12th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 12th is 8 days, and 8 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Monday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 14th is 13 days, and 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Friday gives Thursday.
recs.rel: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: A car travels at 90 km per hour. How much distance does it cover in 40 minutes?
recs.facts: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, so distance = 90 x 2/3 = 60 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.

recs.q: If a helicopter needs 340 gallons of fuel to cover 500 km, how much fuel will it need to cover 700 km?
recs.facts: Fuel is proportional to distance: 340 x 700 / 500 = 476 gallons.
recs.rel: Consumption here is 0.68 gallons per km.

recs.q: If A is a subset of B, then A union B is equal to which set?
recs.facts: Every element of A is already in B, so combining A and B gives just B.
recs.rel: In the same case, A intersection B equals A.

recs.q: If log x = y (common logarithm, base 10), what is x?
recs.facts: By definition, log x = y with base 10 means x = 10^y.
recs.rel: Natural logarithm uses base e, so ln x = y gives x = e^y.

recs.q: If U is the universal set and A is a subset of U, what is the set U - A called?
recs.facts: U - A contains all elements of the universal set that are not in A. This set is called the complement of A.
recs.rel: The complement of A is written A' or A^c, and A union A' equals U.

recs.q: If (x - 1, y + 1) = (0, 0), what are the values of x and y?
recs.facts: Equal ordered pairs have equal components: x - 1 = 0 gives x = 1, and y + 1 = 0 gives y = -1.
recs.rel: Two ordered pairs are equal only when their first and second components are both equal.

recs.q: If y = 2x + 2 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
recs.rel: The graph of y = 2x + 2 is a straight line with slope 2 and y-intercept 2.

recs.q: In a class of 400 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of students present?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 340 / 400 x 100 = 85%.
recs.rel: Candidates remembered 80%, which would mean 320 present.

recs.q: In a class of 500 students, 240 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.facts: Absent students = 500 - 240 = 260. Percentage absent = 260 / 500 x 100 = 52%.
recs.rel: The present percentage here is 48%, and present plus absent always makes 100%.

recs.q: In a class of 500 boys, 340 are present. How many boys are absent?
recs.rel: The absent percentage is 160 / 500 x 100 = 32%.

recs.q: Out of 1200 students, 560 are boys. What is the percentage of girls (to two decimal places)?
recs.rel: The boys make up 560 / 1200 x 100 = 46.67% of the students.

recs.q: Into how many semicircles does a diameter divide a circle?
recs.facts: A diameter passes through the centre and cuts the circle into two equal halves, each called a semicircle.
recs.rel: A semicircle subtends an angle of 180 degrees at the centre.

recs.q: Multiply the biggest and the smallest of the numbers 7, 4, 3, 6, 5, 2, then subtract the product from the sum of all the numbers. What is the result?
recs.facts: Biggest is 7 and smallest is 2, so the product is 14. The sum is 7+4+3+6+5+2 = 27, and 27 - 14 = 13.
recs.rel: The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)/2.

recs.q: Odd one out: Islamabad, Lahore, Quetta, Rawalpindi.
recs.facts: Islamabad is the federal capital, Lahore is the capital of Punjab and Quetta is the capital of Balochistan. Rawalpindi is not a capital.
recs.rel: Rawalpindi is the headquarters of the Pakistan Army and neighbours Islamabad.

recs.q: P = mc + q is what type of equation?
recs.facts: The variable c appears only to the power one, so the equation is of the form y = mx + c, a linear equation.
recs.rel: The graph of a linear equation is a straight line.

recs.q: Point out the odd one out: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon.
recs.facts: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a shape but a measure formed by two rays.
recs.rel: A hexagon has six sides.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters IAPRS to form a word. What does the word name?
recs.facts: The letters I, A, P, R, S rearranged give PARIS, the capital of France.
recs.rel: Paris stands on the River Seine.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters RSPAI to get the name of a city.
recs.facts: The letters R, S, P, A, I rearrange to PARIS.
recs.rel: Paris is the capital of France, on the river Seine.

recs.q: Sheep is to wool as cat is to what?
recs.facts: Wool is the covering that grows on a sheep, and fur is the covering that grows on a cat.
recs.rel: Wool is obtained by shearing sheep.

recs.q: Speak is to hear as look is to what?
recs.facts: Speaking is matched by hearing, and looking is matched by seeing, the result received.
recs.rel: Hearing is the sense of the ear and seeing is the sense of the eye.

recs.q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 3?
recs.facts: 1.732 x 1.732 is about 3.0, so the square root of 3 is about 1.732.
recs.rel: The square root of 2 is about 1.414 and of 5 is about 2.236.

recs.q: The cube of unity (1 cubed) is equal to what?
recs.facts: 1 x 1 x 1 = 1, so the cube of unity is 1.
recs.rel: The three cube roots of unity are 1 and two complex numbers, each of which also cubes to 1.

recs.q: The population of a village was 2000 in the year 2000. If it doubled every five years, what was its population in 1980?
recs.facts: From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings. So the 1980 population is 2000 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 125.
recs.rel: Going back in time, a doubling quantity is halved each period.

recs.q: In division, the remainder is always less than which number?
recs.facts: If the remainder were equal to or larger than the divisor, the divisor could be taken once more, so the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
recs.rel: When the remainder is zero, the dividend is exactly divisible by the divisor.

recs.q: Today is Sunday. What will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: Tomorrow is Monday, so the day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
recs.rel: In Pakistan the working week traditionally runs Monday to Friday.

recs.q: There are 24 students and 1/4 of them are male. What is the percentage of females?
recs.facts: Males are 1/4 = 25%, so females are 100 - 25 = 75% (18 of 24).
recs.rel: 1/4 equals 25 percent.

recs.q: Total students in a class are 1500 and 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.rel: Present and absent percentages add up to 100%.

recs.q: What are the two square roots of 64?
recs.facts: 8 x 8 = 64 and (-8) x (-8) = 64, so the roots are +8 and -8.
recs.rel: Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative.

recs.q: What is 10% of 80?
recs.rel: To find 10% of a number, divide it by 10.

recs.q: What is the value of 1 - 2 + 2/2?
recs.facts: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 1 - 2 + 1 = 0.
recs.rel: BODMAS: brackets, orders, division and multiplication, then addition and subtraction.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 36?
recs.rel: 36 is divisible by 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12 and 18.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 + 2 x 2?
recs.facts: Multiplication comes first: 2 x 2 = 4, then 2 + 4 = 6.
recs.rel: BODMAS gives multiplication priority over addition.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 + 3/3?
recs.facts: Division first: 3/3 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.
recs.rel: Division is done before addition under BODMAS.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 x 3 + 3 x 6?
recs.rel: Both multiplications are done before the addition.

recs.q: What is 30% of 20?
recs.rel: 30% of 20 is 3 times 10% of 20, which is 2.

recs.q: What is the value of 3 + 3 x 3?
recs.facts: Multiplication first: 3 x 3 = 9, then 3 + 9 = 12.
recs.rel: Without BODMAS, one would wrongly compute (3 + 3) x 3 = 18.

recs.q: What is 60% of 80?
recs.rel: 60% is the same as 3/5, and 3/5 of 80 is 48.

recs.q: What is 90% of 9?
recs.rel: 90% of a number is the number minus 10% of it, so 9 - 0.9 = 8.1.

recs.q: What is a chord that passes through the centre of a circle called?
recs.facts: A chord through the centre is the longest chord of the circle and is called the diameter.
recs.rel: The diameter is twice the radius.

recs.q: What is an angle greater than 90 degrees (and less than 180 degrees) called?
recs.facts: An angle between 90 and 180 degrees is obtuse.
recs.rel: An angle of exactly 180 degrees is a straight angle.

recs.q: What is a matrix whose entries are all zero called?
recs.facts: A matrix with every element equal to zero is called a null (zero) matrix.
recs.rel: Adding a null matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.

recs.q: What is the value of cos 90 degrees?
recs.facts: On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1), and its x-coordinate, the cosine, is 0.
recs.rel: Sin 90 degrees equals 1.

recs.q: What is cos x multiplied by tan x equal to?
recs.facts: Since tan x = sin x / cos x, cos x times tan x = sin x.
recs.rel: Another identity: sin x divided by cos x equals tan x.

recs.q: What is one tenth of 30?
recs.facts: One tenth of 30 is 30 / 10 = 3.
recs.rel: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the left.

recs.q: What is the value of tan 0 degrees?
recs.facts: tan 0 = sin 0 / cos 0 = 0 / 1 = 0.
recs.rel: tan 90 degrees is undefined because cos 90 = 0.

recs.q: What is the 2nd letter of the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The alphabet runs A, B, C, so the second letter is B.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

recs.q: What is the conjugate of a real number?
recs.facts: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi. For a real number b = 0, so the conjugate is the same number.
recs.rel: A complex number equals its own conjugate only when it is real.

recs.q: What is the common difference in the series 4, 7, 10, 13?
recs.facts: 7 - 4 = 3, 10 - 7 = 3 and 13 - 10 = 3, so the difference is 3.
recs.rel: Such a series is called an arithmetic progression.

recs.q: What is the distance between the points (-2, 0) and (-2, -3)?
recs.facts: The x-coordinates are equal, so the distance is |0 - (-3)| = 3. By formula: sqrt(0 + 9) = 3.
recs.rel: Points with the same x-coordinate lie on a vertical line.

recs.q: Which is the distance formula between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
recs.facts: The distance comes from the Pythagorean theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences.
recs.rel: The formula (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) gives the slope, and the midpoint uses averages.

recs.q: What is the HCF of 18 and 24?
recs.facts: 18 = 2 x 3 x 3 and 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3. The common factors are 2 and 3, so HCF = 6.
recs.rel: Their LCM is 72, and HCF x LCM = 18 x 24 = 432.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 + 2/3?
recs.facts: Division comes first: 2/3. Then 2 + 2/3 = 6/3 + 2/3 = 8/3, which is 2 and 2/3.
recs.rel: In BODMAS, division is performed before addition.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of extension?
recs.facts: Extension means an act of making something longer or larger, which is expansion.
recs.rel: The antonym of extension is reduction or curtailment.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of severely?
recs.facts: Severely means in a very strict or intense manner, which is harshly.
recs.rel: The antonym of severely is mildly or leniently.

recs.q: Where does the line y = 3 + 5y lie?
opts: Parallel to the x-axis, so it is neither axis
recs.facts: Rearranging gives -4y = 3, so y = -3/4. This is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, not the axis itself.
recs.rel: The x-axis is the line y = 0 and the y-axis is the line x = 0.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: 1 X 2 Y Y 3 Z Z ?
recs.facts: The numbers 1, 2, 3 are followed by X once, Y twice and Z three times. So one more Z completes 3 ZZZ.
recs.rel: The letters follow the alphabetical order X, Y, Z.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: A2, D5, F9, ?
recs.facts: Letters move +3, +2, +1 (A, D, F, G) and numbers add 3, 4, 5 (2, 5, 9, 14). So the next term is G14.
recs.rel: In such series, check the letters and numbers separately.

recs.q: Which letter comes immediately before W in the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The alphabet runs ... U, V, W, X, so V comes just before W.
recs.rel: W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.

recs.q: Which letter comes next: A B C D E F G H ?
recs.facts: The letters are in alphabetical order, and the one after H is I.
recs.rel: I is the 9th letter of the alphabet.

recs.q: In the series A1, C3, D4, G?, what number follows G?
recs.facts: Each number is the alphabet position of its letter: A=1, C=3, D=4, so G=7.
recs.rel: G is the 7th letter of the alphabet.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: A5, B10, C15, ?
recs.facts: Letters move forward one step (A, B, C, D) and numbers increase by 5 (5, 10, 15, 20). So the next is D20.
recs.rel: The number part is the table of 5.

recs.q: Which of the letters A, H, I, W, M, O, T, U, Y look the same in a mirror (vertical mirror held beside the letter)?
opts: Only A, H, I and O
Only H, I, O and W
Only M, T, U and Y
recs.facts: Every one of these letters is symmetric about a vertical line, so each looks the same when reflected.
recs.rel: Letters like B, C, D, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 105, 55, 160, 65, 225, 75, ?
recs.facts: The numbers at odd places (105, 160, 225) rise by 55, then 65, so the next rise is 75: 225 + 75 = 300. The other numbers (55, 65, 75) rise by 10 each time.
recs.rel: Such interleaved series are solved by separating the odd and even places.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 170, 65, ?
recs.facts: Two series are mixed: 115, 170 rise by 55, then 65 more, so 170 + 65 = 235. The other series 55, 65 would continue with 75 afterwards.
recs.rel: Here the added amount is the same as the number that follows each term: 115+55=170, 170+65=235.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, 75, ?
recs.facts: Each big number is the previous big number plus the small number after it: 115+55=170, 170+65=235, 235+75=310.
recs.rel: The small numbers 55, 65, 75 increase by 10.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 225, 65, 335, ?
recs.facts: The odd places 115, 225, 335 rise by 110 each time. The even places 55, 65 rise by 10, so the next is 75.
recs.rel: The question asks for the next term, which falls in the even-place series.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 2, 4, 8, 14, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8. Hence 14 + 8 = 22.
recs.rel: When differences themselves form an arithmetic series, the series is quadratic.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 66, 63, 57, 45, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 3, 6, 12, doubling each time, so the next difference is 24. Hence 45 - 24 = 21.
recs.rel: Series with doubling differences are common in verbal reasoning tests.

recs.q: Which one is a prime number: 12, 25, 30, 37?
recs.facts: 12 and 30 are even, and 25 = 5 x 5. 37 has no divisor other than 1 and itself, so it is prime.
recs.rel: 2 is the only even prime number.

recs.q: Which one is different: A12, B13, D15, E19, C14?
recs.facts: Letter position plus 11 gives the number: A(1)=12, B(2)=13, C(3)=14, D(4)=15. For E(5) it should be 16, but it is 19.
recs.rel: The odd one out breaks the pattern shared by all the others.

recs.q: Which quantity has no unit?
recs.facts: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, so the units cancel and it is dimensionless. The others all have units.
recs.rel: Velocity is measured in m/s, density in kg/m3 and pressure in pascals.

recs.q: Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball?
recs.facts: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket, while football is played with the feet and no bat.
recs.rel: Football is the most widely played sport in the world.

recs.q: Who is the President of Russia?
recs.facts: Vladimir Putin is the President of Russia, in office since 2012 after earlier terms from 2000 to 2008.
recs.rel: He was re-elected in March 2024 for a term of six years.

recs.q: What is the capital of Nepal?
recs.facts: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal. It lies in the Kathmandu Valley in the Himalayan region.
recs.rel: Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, lies on the border of Nepal and China.

recs.q: Who is the President of the United States in October 2026?
recs.facts: Donald Trump won the 2024 election and was sworn in as the 47th President on 20 January 2025.
recs.rel: Joe Biden was President from January 2021 to January 2025, which is the answer candidates gave in 2022; the USA has a President and no Prime Minister.

recs.q: What is the capital of Lebanon?
recs.facts: Beirut is the capital and largest city of Lebanon.
recs.rel: Damascus is the capital of Syria.

recs.q: In which year did the Minto-Morley Reforms (Indian Councils Act) come into effect?
recs.facts: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Lord Minto was Viceroy and Lord Morley was Secretary of State for India.
recs.rel: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms followed in 1919.

recs.q: In which country did Pakistan open its first embassy?
recs.facts: Pakistan opened its first embassy in Iran, which was also among the first countries to recognise Pakistan in 1947.
recs.rel: Some sources differ on early diplomatic firsts, but Iran is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks and tests.

recs.q: Who is the current President of India?
recs.facts: Droupadi Murmu took oath as the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022.
recs.rel: Her predecessor Ram Nath Kovind, the answer given in 2022, served from 2017 to 2022.

recs.q: Which one is different: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta, Karachi, Rawalpindi?
recs.facts: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta and Karachi are all provincial capitals. Rawalpindi is not a provincial capital, so it is the odd one out.
recs.rel: Islamabad, not Rawalpindi, is the federal capital of Pakistan.

recs.q: Who wrote the book My Brother, about Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
