recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, wrote My Brother, which was published after her death.
recs.rel: Fatima Jinnah is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

recs.q: In which year did Fatima Jinnah die?
recs.facts: Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah died in Karachi on 9 July 1967 and was buried near the mausoleum of Quaid-e-Azam.
recs.rel: She is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

recs.q: Who is the author of the book India of My Dreams?
recs.facts: India of My Dreams is a collection of the writings of Mahatma Gandhi on his vision for India, compiled by R. K. Prabhu.
recs.rel: Gandhi's autobiography is titled The Story of My Experiments with Truth.

recs.q: What is the capital of the Philippines?
recs.facts: Manila is the capital of the Philippines.
recs.rel: Quezon City is the largest city of the country by population.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Harini Amarasuriya of the National People's Power became Prime Minister in September 2024 and was reappointed after the November 2024 election.
recs.rel: Earlier answers were Mahinda Rajapaksa (2019 to 2022) and Ranil Wickremesinghe (briefly in 2022).

recs.q: On which date was the Liaquat-Nehru Pact signed?
recs.facts: The Liaquat-Nehru (Delhi) Pact was signed on 8 April 1950 by Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru to protect minorities in both countries.
recs.rel: It is also called the Delhi Pact.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of France as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Sebastien Lecornu was appointed Prime Minister in September 2025 and reappointed in October 2025, and was still in office in October 2026.
recs.rel: Elisabeth Borne (2022-2024), whom candidates wrote in 2022, was later followed by Attal, Barnier and Bayrou; Emmanuel Macron is the President, not the PM.

recs.q: Who is the head of state of the United Kingdom?
recs.facts: The UK is a monarchy with no president, and King Charles III is the head of state.
recs.rel: Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026, and in 2022 candidates named Boris Johnson in this role.

recs.q: Zabihullah (the one sacrificed for Allah) is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah because he was offered for sacrifice by his father Ibrahim (AS) in obedience to Allah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah and Hazrat Ismail (AS) is the ancestor of the Arab tribes.

recs.q: Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
recs.facts: The Tashkent Declaration was signed by Pakistan and India to end the 1965 war.
recs.rel: The Soviet Union under Premier Kosygin mediated, and Indian PM Shastri died in Tashkent right after signing.

recs.q: Which region is called the Land of Prophets?
recs.facts: Palestine is called the Land of Prophets because many prophets, including Ibrahim, Dawud, Sulaiman, Isa and others, lived or preached there.
recs.rel: Jerusalem (Al-Quds) in Palestine holds Masjid al-Aqsa, the first qibla of Muslims.

recs.q: What percentage of the total area of Pakistan is covered by forest?
recs.facts: Pakistan's forest cover is about 4.8 percent of its land area according to commonly quoted figures.
recs.rel: This is low compared with the world average of about 30 percent; sources differ slightly.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Japan?
recs.facts: Sanae Takaichi became Japan's first woman Prime Minister in October 2025 and was re-designated after the February 2026 election.
recs.rel: Japan has no president; its head of state is Emperor Naruhito, and Fumio Kishida was PM in 2022.

recs.q: In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are men and the rest are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
recs.facts: Men = 2/3 x 30 = 20, so girls = 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage of girls = 10/30 x 100 = 33.33%.
recs.rel: Girls are 1/3 of the passengers.

recs.q: Which is the longest railway tunnel in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Khojak Tunnel, built in 1891 in the Khojak Pass of Balochistan on the Quetta-Chaman line, is about 3.9 km long and is Pakistan's longest railway tunnel.
recs.rel: The Lowari Tunnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is longer, but it is a road tunnel, not a railway tunnel.

recs.q: How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when his grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib passed away?
recs.facts: Abdul Muttalib took care of the Prophet (PBUH) after his mother died and passed away when the Prophet was 8 years old. Afterwards his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) lost his mother Hazrat Amina at the age of 6.

recs.q: Who is the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
recs.facts: Faisal Karim Kundi of the PPP has been Governor of KPK since May 2024. He took over from Haji Ghulam Ali.
recs.rel: Shah Farman, the answer given in 2022, was governor from 2019 to 2023.

recs.q: In which year was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) founded?
recs.facts: The SCO was formally founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai, China, by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
recs.rel: Its predecessor was the Shanghai Five of 1996, and Pakistan and India became full members in 2017.

recs.q: Where were the FIFA World Cup matches of 2022 played?
recs.facts: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar from November to December 2022. Argentina won it.
recs.rel: It was the first FIFA World Cup held in an Arab and Muslim-majority country.

recs.q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
recs.facts: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume.
recs.rel: The All-India Muslim League was formed later, in 1906 at Dhaka.

recs.q: Which city is commonly called the heart of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Lahore is popularly called the heart (Dil) of Pakistan because of its culture and history.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as Punjab province is also sometimes described as the heart of Pakistan.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book India Wins Freedom?
recs.facts: India Wins Freedom is the autobiographical account of the Indian independence struggle by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
recs.rel: Maulana Azad was the first Education Minister of independent India.

recs.q: Who is the Chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Mohsin Naqvi was elected PCB chairman unopposed on 6 February 2024 for a three-year term.
recs.rel: Ramiz Raja was PCB chairman from 2021 to December 2022, which was the answer in 2022.

recs.q: Which city in Pakistan is known as the City of Flowers?
recs.facts: Peshawar is called the City of Flowers because of its many gardens.
recs.rel: Lahore is known as the City of Gardens.

recs.q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Malaysia (October 2026)?
recs.facts: Anwar Ibrahim became the 10th Prime Minister of Malaysia in November 2022 and is still in office in 2026.
recs.rel: Ismail Sabri Yaakob was PM from 2021 to 2022, when candidates took the test.

recs.q: Which area is known as the Roof of the World?
recs.facts: The Pamir Plateau in Central Asia is called the Roof of the World because of its great height.
recs.rel: Tibet is also sometimes given this name.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani woman cricketer to take 100 ODI wickets?
recs.facts: Sana Mir became the first Pakistani woman to take 100 ODI wickets in February 2017 against Bangladesh in the World Cup Qualifier.
recs.rel: She finished her ODI career with about 150 ODI wickets, the most by a Pakistani woman, and was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame.

recs.q: How many articles does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan have?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution, Pakistan's third constitution, contains 280 articles.
recs.rel: It has 12 parts and 7 schedules and was enforced on 14 August 1973.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Reko Diq mine project located?
recs.facts: Reko Diq is a large copper and gold deposit in Chagai district in the west of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Reko Diq is one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits in the world.

recs.q: What is the official capital of Indonesia?
recs.facts: Jakarta is Indonesia's legal capital. A new capital, Nusantara in East Kalimantan, was planned by a 2022 law, but Jakarta stays the capital until a formal transfer decree is issued.
recs.rel: Nusantara is now planned only as a political capital (target 2028), so candidates who wrote Nusantara in 2022 were anticipating a move that has not formally happened.

recs.q: Which planet has the largest number of moons?
recs.facts: Saturn has the most confirmed moons of any planet, about 293 as of 2026. Jupiter is second with about 115.
recs.rel: Saturn's count was 83 in 2022 and rose sharply after new discoveries, so older answers differ.

recs.q: How many wajibat of Namaz are there according to the Hanafi school?
recs.facts: The Hanafi school counts 14 wajibat of Namaz, such as reciting Surah Fatiha and a further surah.
recs.rel: The fard acts of Namaz are 13 in number.

recs.q: What was the real (original) name of Titu Mir?
recs.facts: Titu Mir, the Bengali leader of the Barasat uprising, was born as Mir Nisar Ali.
recs.rel: He was killed in 1831 by British forces at his bamboo fort in Narkelbaria.

recs.q: Which companion (Sahabi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was his adopted son?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was freed and adopted by the Prophet (PBUH) before prophethood, and was known as Zaid bin Muhammad until adoption was abolished.
recs.rel: Zaid is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).

recs.q: When did the Al-Khalid main battle tank enter service with the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000), developed by Pakistan with Chinese help, entered service in 2001.
recs.rel: Some sources mention 2004 for its formal presentation, and the upgraded Al-Khalid-I was inducted in July 2020.

recs.q: Rough is to smooth as crude is to what?
recs.facts: Rough and smooth are opposites, so the opposite of crude (unrefined) is polished (refined).
recs.rel: Crude oil is oil that has not yet been refined.

recs.q: In which year was FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: The 25th Constitutional Amendment was passed in May 2018 and merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which was completed after the President signed it.
recs.rel: Candidates often confuse this with 2021, but the merger law was passed in 2018.

recs.q: In which year was the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: The 18th Amendment passed in April 2010 renamed NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Pakistan's parliament approved it that year.
recs.rel: The former FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018 through the 25th Amendment.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
recs.facts: The positions are 2, 5, 10, 17. The gaps are 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26, which is Z.
recs.rel: The positions are one more than the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 + 1 = 26.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of New Zealand (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Christopher Luxon of the National Party has been Prime Minister since November 2023 and is still in office in October 2026.
recs.rel: Jacinda Ardern (until January 2023) and Chris Hipkins (until November 2023) held the post earlier; the next election is on 7 November 2026.

recs.q: What is the antonym of abhor?
recs.facts: To abhor means to hate strongly, so its opposite is to love or admire.
recs.rel: Loathe and detest are synonyms of abhor.

recs.q: Aleem Dar is a famous umpire of which game?
recs.facts: Aleem Dar, from Lahore, is a famous Pakistani cricket umpire who stood in over 100 Test matches and won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times in a row (2009-2011).
recs.rel: He served on the ICC Elite Panel of Umpires for many years.

recs.q: Which bridge in Turkey connects Asia and Europe over the Bosphorus Strait?
recs.facts: The Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul spans the Bosphorus Strait and joins the European and Asian sides of the city.
recs.rel: It was renamed 15 July Martyrs Bridge in 2016, and Istanbul has other Bosphorus bridges too.

recs.q: Who is the President of China as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013 and also leads the Communist Party.
recs.rel: The head of government, the Premier, is Li Qiang, so the office of PM is not held by Xi.

recs.q: What is the height of the Diamer Bhasha Dam?
recs.facts: The Diamer Bhasha Dam on the Indus is 272 metres high, per WAPDA.
recs.rel: It is a roller-compacted concrete dam and one of the tallest of its kind in the world.

recs.q: On which date did Muhammad Ali Bogra present the Bogra Formula?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Bogra presented his constitutional formula on 7 October 1953.
recs.rel: The formula was never implemented because the Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1954.

recs.q: What is the relation between Hazrat Musa (AS) and Hazrat Haroon (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS) and was also a prophet.
recs.rel: Musa (AS) asked Allah to make Haroon (AS) his helper, as mentioned in the Quran.

recs.q: According to Islamic tradition, who first built the Kaaba?
recs.facts: Islamic tradition says the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS), and later rebuilt by Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) with his son Ismail (AS). Many candidates and sources give this answer for the first building.
recs.rel: Sources differ, and some Pakistani textbooks credit Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) with building it, but they rebuilt it on its old foundations.

recs.q: Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun?
recs.facts: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun; its name Nippon means origin of the sun.
recs.rel: Its capital is Tokyo.

recs.q: Vienna is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria on the Danube River.
recs.rel: Budapest, the capital of Hungary, is also on the Danube.

recs.q: In which surah of the Quran is the name Ahmad (for the Holy Prophet PBUH) mentioned?
recs.facts: The name Ahmad appears in Surah As-Saff (61:6), where Hazrat Isa (AS) gives the good news of a messenger named Ahmad coming after him.
recs.rel: The name Muhammad is mentioned four times in the Quran, in Al-Imran, Al-Ahzab, Muhammad and Al-Fath.

recs.q: How many articles did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan have?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first constitution, had 234 articles.
recs.rel: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan win the IBSF World Snooker Championship for the first time?
recs.facts: Muhammad Yousuf won the world amateur snooker title for Pakistan in 1994.
recs.rel: Muhammad Sajid won the world amateur title in 2006, Pakistan's second.

recs.q: Which is the last completely revealed surah of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Surah An-Nasr is regarded as the last complete surah to be revealed.
recs.rel: Sources differ about the last verse revealed, with Al-Baqarah verse 281 or Al-Maidah verse 3 often mentioned.

recs.q: Which of the following countries lies in both Europe and Asia?
recs.facts: Turkey is divided by the Bosphorus strait, with a small part in Europe and most of its land in Asia.
recs.rel: Istanbul is the major city that lies on both continents.

recs.q: Which one is different from the others: Circle, Square, Triangle, Angle?
recs.facts: Circle, square and triangle are closed geometric figures, while an angle is not a closed figure.
recs.rel: An angle is formed by two rays meeting at a common point.

recs.q: Whose mother was Hazrat Sara (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Sara (AS), wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).

recs.q: Which was the first ghazwa (expedition led personally by the Holy Prophet SAW) of Islam?
recs.facts: The first ghazwa, in Safar 2 AH, was Abwa, also called Waddan, in which the Prophet (SAW) himself went out but no fighting occurred.
recs.rel: The first major battle of Islam was Badr in Ramadan 2 AH.

recs.q: What is the capital of South Korea?
recs.facts: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea.
recs.rel: Pyongyang is the capital of North Korea.

recs.q: Malaysia has a king instead of a president. Who is the head of state (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) of Malaysia in 2026?
recs.facts: Malaysia is a constitutional monarchy with no president. Sultan Ibrahim of Johor has been the 17th Agong since 31 January 2024.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Sultan Abdullah of Pahang, who was Agong from 2019 to 2024.

recs.q: According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population is Muslim?
recs.facts: The 2023 census recorded Muslims at about 96.35 percent of the population of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The 2017 census figure was 96.47 percent, and candidates often quote 97 percent.

recs.q: About how many times is the command of Namaz (Salah) mentioned in the Holy Quran, according to common textbooks?
recs.facts: Salah and its related commands are repeated about 700 times in the Quran, showing its great importance.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact count, but 700 is the figure given in most Pakistani textbooks.

recs.q: What is the approximate total length of railway track in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan Railways reports about 11,881 track kilometres, counting all tracks including double-track sections.
recs.rel: The route length is shorter, about 7,791 km, which is why sources differ.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 90?
recs.facts: 90 divided by 3 = 30.
recs.rel: A third of 90 is ten times a third of 9.

recs.q: Who was the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan?
recs.facts: On 20 December 1971 Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto took over as President and became the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator after Yahya Khan stepped down.
recs.rel: Martial law was lifted in Pakistan in 1972 and the 1973 Constitution was adopted under Bhutto.

recs.q: In the word MANAGEMENT, arranged alphabetically, which letter is second last?
recs.facts: Alphabetical order is A A E E G M M N N T. The last letter is T and the second last is N.
recs.rel: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each appearing twice.

recs.q: What was the code name of Pakistan's first nuclear tests of 28 May 1998?
recs.facts: Pakistan's tests of 28 May 1998 at Chagai in Balochistan were code-named Chagai-I.
recs.rel: India's 1974 test was Smiling Buddha and its 1998 tests were Shakti; Pakistan's second test on 30 May 1998 was Chagai-II.

recs.q: Amsterdam is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government sits in The Hague.
recs.rel: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.

recs.q: Lima is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru. It lies on the Pacific coast.
recs.rel: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

recs.q: What is the name of the angel in charge of Hell (Jahannam)?
recs.facts: The Quran (Surah Az-Zukhruf) mentions Malik as the keeper of Hell.
recs.rel: Ridwan is the angel who is the keeper of Paradise.

recs.q: In which country are the headquarters of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
recs.facts: The ECO secretariat is in Tehran, the capital of Iran.
recs.rel: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of ECO.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Israel?
recs.facts: Benjamin Netanyahu has been Prime Minister of Israel since December 2022 and was still in office in October 2026.
recs.rel: Naftali Bennett (2021-2022) was PM when candidates wrote in 2022, and Israel's next general election is scheduled for 27 October 2026.

recs.q: What is the capital of the Netherlands?
recs.facts: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government and parliament sit in The Hague.
recs.rel: The International Court of Justice is located in The Hague.

recs.q: In which year was Bengal partitioned by the British?
recs.facts: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 into East Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: Who is the President of Ukraine?
recs.facts: Volodymyr Zelensky has been President of Ukraine since May 2019 and still holds the office in 2026.
recs.rel: Petro Poroshenko was his predecessor, from 2014 to 2019.

recs.q: Who announced the partition of Bengal in 1905?
recs.facts: Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal on 19 July 1905 and it took effect on 16 October 1905, creating a Muslim-majority eastern province.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911, and the All India Muslim League was formed in 1906 partly in reaction to these events.

recs.q: Who benefited from the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
recs.facts: The partition created a Muslim-majority province of East Bengal and Assam with Dhaka as its capital, which helped Muslims in education and jobs.
recs.rel: Hindus opposed it strongly and it was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: In which constitution was the bicameral (two-house) legislature introduced in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution created a bicameral Parliament of the National Assembly and the Senate.
recs.rel: The Senate was first formed in 1973 and the 1956 and 1962 constitutions had one house.

recs.q: On which date was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed?
recs.facts: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963 and settled the border of Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway linking the two countries was later built and opened to traffic in 1978.

recs.q: Which languages were declared official languages in the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution made Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Bengali language movement of 1952 forced this recognition.

recs.q: For how many years is the President of Pakistan elected?
recs.facts: Under the 1973 Constitution the President holds office for a term of five years.
recs.rel: The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies.

recs.q: Who was the father of Hazrat Yousuf (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Yousuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) is also known as Israel.

recs.q: What is the antonym of intimate (adjective)?
recs.facts: Intimate means close and familiar, so the opposite is distant.
recs.rel: Close, familiar and dear are synonyms of intimate.

recs.q: Who is the President of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Anura Kumara Dissanayake won the September 2024 presidential election and took office as President.
recs.rel: Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President until 2022 and Ranil Wickremesinghe until 2024.

recs.q: Between which two countries does the Line of Control (LOC) lie?
recs.facts: The Line of Control is the de facto military border dividing Indian-administered and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
recs.rel: It was established by the Simla Agreement of 1972.

recs.q: Who recited verses of the Quran in the court of King Najashi of Abyssinia?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jafar (RA) led the Muslim migrants to Abyssinia and recited the opening verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi. The king was moved and refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraish.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jafar (RA) is also known as Jafar Tayyar and was martyred at the Battle of Mutah.

recs.q: Which was the second major battle (ghazwa) fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah, after the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle of Islam and the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH was the second.
recs.rel: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Mount Uhud, close to Madinah, in Shawwal 3 AH.

recs.q: On what date did the Australian cricketer Shane Warne die?
recs.facts: Shane Warne died of a suspected heart attack in Koh Samui, Thailand, on 4 March 2022 at the age of 52.
recs.rel: Warne took 708 wickets in Test cricket, a record for a leg-spinner.

recs.q: The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed after which war?
recs.facts: After the 1971 war and the separation of East Pakistan, Pakistan and India met at Shimla in 1972 and signed the agreement.
recs.rel: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed after the 1965 war.

recs.q: One degree of an angle is equal to how many minutes?
recs.facts: A degree is divided into 60 minutes, and a minute into 60 seconds.
recs.rel: A full circle measures 360 degrees.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Shamshad Akhtar became the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2005.
recs.rel: She later served as Caretaker Finance Minister in 2023.

recs.q: In how many years was the revelation of the Holy Quran completed?
recs.facts: The Quran was revealed gradually to the Prophet (PBUH) over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Hira until shortly before his death.
recs.rel: About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.

recs.q: In which year was the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) established?
recs.facts: ECO was established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
recs.rel: RCD (Regional Cooperation for Development) was formed in 1964.

recs.q: On what date did Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad start?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Army launched Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad on 22 February 2017 against terrorism after a wave of attacks. It was a nationwide operation.
recs.rel: Operation Zarb-e-Azb in 2014 was an earlier operation in North Waziristan.

recs.q: In which year was the film Jinnah, on the life of Quaid-e-Azam, released?
recs.facts: The film Jinnah, starring Christopher Lee as Jinnah, was released in 1998.
recs.rel: It was directed by Jamil Dehlavi.

recs.q: Which city is known as the City of Gold?
recs.facts: Johannesburg in South Africa is called the City of Gold because it grew after gold was discovered in the Witwatersrand in 1886.
recs.rel: South Africa has long been one of the largest gold producers in the world, though sources differ on later rankings.

recs.q: Which plant is commonly named as the fastest growing plant (tree) in the world?
recs.facts: Some bamboo species can grow almost one metre in a single day, which is why bamboo is commonly named the fastest growing plant.
recs.rel: Bamboo is technically a grass, and the Paulownia is often called the fastest growing true tree, so sources differ.

recs.q: Habba Khatoon was a famous poet of which language?
recs.facts: Habba Khatoon (Zoon) was a 16th century Kashmiri poet known for her lyrical songs.
recs.rel: She is often called the Nightingale of Kashmir.

recs.q: About what percentage of Antarctica is covered by ice?
recs.facts: About 98 percent of Antarctica is covered by an ice sheet, and only about 2 percent is bare rock. Some sources give 97.6 or 99 percent.
recs.rel: The ice sheet is on average about 2 km thick.

recs.q: On which date is the International Day to Combat Islamophobia observed?
recs.facts: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 15 March as International Day to Combat Islamophobia in 2022, on a resolution moved by Pakistan on behalf of the OIC.
recs.rel: 15 March was chosen as the anniversary of the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks.

recs.q: Who is the Pakistani Nobel Prize winner in Physics, and how many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize in Physics?
recs.facts: Dr. Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the electroweak theory. He is the only Pakistani to win a Nobel in Physics.
recs.rel: Pakistan's other Nobel laureate is Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).

recs.q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which city of Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul through the Torkham border crossing and Jalalabad.
recs.rel: The pass lies in the Safed Koh range.

recs.q: What is the population of Pakistan according to the 2023 census?
recs.facts: The 2023 digital census recorded Pakistan's population as about 241.49 million.
recs.rel: The 2017 census had recorded about 207.7 million, and candidates in 2022 used estimates of about 220 million.

recs.q: Which was the first private television channel of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Shalimar Television Network, which began in 1990 as People's Television Network, was the first channel to break the monopoly of state-run PTV. It is the answer most textbooks give.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the word private: ARY Digital (2001) and Indus TV (2000) are often called the first fully independent channels.

recs.q: Who was the first poet of the Punjabi language?
recs.facts: Hazrat Baba Fariduddin Ganjshakar (1188-1266) is regarded as the first poet of Punjabi, and his verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.
recs.rel: His shrine is in Pakpattan.

recs.q: A quadratic equation is an equation of which degree?
recs.facts: The highest power of the variable in a quadratic equation is 2, so it is a second degree equation.
recs.rel: The general form is ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, where a is not 0.

recs.q: In which year was SUPARCO, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established?
recs.facts: SUPARCO was formally established on 16 September 1961 by an executive order, with Dr Abdus Salam as its first chairman.
recs.rel: Some sources trace a precursor committee to 1961 as well; candidate answers such as 1955 and 1959 are incorrect.

recs.q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper?
recs.facts: 5 papers take 5 minutes, so 1 paper takes 5 / 5 = 1 minute.
recs.rel: A rate of 1 paper per minute means that 60 papers would take an hour.

recs.q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of the students are absent (to two decimal places)?
recs.rel: The percentage present is 86.67%, which together with 13.33% makes 100%.

recs.q: According to the 1956 Constitution, what was the minimum age to become President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim of not less than 40 years of age.
recs.rel: Some candidates remembered 45, but 40 is the age given in the Constitution of 1956.

recs.q: Who dismissed (abrogated) the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution had lasted about seven years.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days. 15 days is 2 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Tuesday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: At what age did Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan, the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, die?
recs.facts: He was born on 1 April 1936 and died on 10 October 2021, which makes him 85 years old.
recs.rel: He died in Islamabad and was buried in the H-8 graveyard.

recs.q: What is the antonym of sublime?
recs.facts: Sublime means of very high excellence or beauty, so its opposite is ridiculous or lowly.
recs.rel: Magnificent, grand and noble are close in meaning to sublime.

recs.q: On which side of Pakistan does the Arabian Sea lie?
recs.facts: Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km runs along the Arabian Sea in the south, in Sindh and Balochistan.
recs.rel: Iran and Afghanistan lie to the west, China to the north-east and India to the east.

recs.q: In which province and city is the BRT (Zu Peshawar) transport system located?
recs.facts: The BRT Zu Peshawar is a bus rapid transit system of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It serves the city of Peshawar.
recs.rel: Lahore has the Orange Line Metro Train and Metro Bus, which are different projects.

recs.q: Which country is the current men's Hockey World Cup champion (2026 edition)?
recs.facts: Germany beat Spain 1-0 in the final on 30 August 2026 in Wavre, Belgium, to retain the title.
recs.rel: Belgium won the 2018 World Cup, and Germany won in 2023; Pakistan has four titles, the same as Germany.

recs.q: What is the derivative of sin x with respect to x?
recs.facts: The standard derivative of sin x is cos x.
recs.rel: The derivative of cos x is -sin x.

recs.q: In which year was the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) agreement signed and launched?
recs.facts: CPEC was launched in April 2015 when Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Pakistan and agreements worth about 46 billion dollars were signed.
recs.rel: A preliminary MoU on the corridor had been signed in 2013 during the visit of Premier Li Keqiang, which is why some sources give 2013.

recs.q: On which date was the Lahore Declaration signed by the prime ministers of Pakistan and India?
recs.facts: Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999 during Vajpayee's bus visit to Lahore.
recs.rel: Months later the Kargil conflict broke out in 1999.

recs.q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) came to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: The Makkan army at Badr was about 1000 strong, while the Muslims were about 313.
recs.rel: In the Battle of Uhad the Makkan army was about 3000 strong.

recs.q: Who developed the first successful polio vaccine?
recs.facts: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.
recs.rel: Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine.

recs.q: Which country hosted the extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers on the Afghan crisis in December 2021?
recs.facts: Pakistan hosted the 17th Extraordinary Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Islamabad on 19 December 2021 to discuss the Afghan humanitarian crisis.
recs.rel: The 47th regular CFM was held in Niamey, Niger, in November 2020.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Israel (as of October 2026, before the 27 October election)?
recs.facts: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel's government since December 2022, and he is campaigning for the election due on 27 October 2026.
recs.rel: Candidates in 2022 wrote Naftali Bennett, who was PM from June 2021 to June 2022, followed by Yair Lapid.

recs.q: Which country has the largest number of lakes in the world?
recs.facts: Canada has the most lakes in the world, with several hundred thousand, more than the rest of the world combined by most estimates.
recs.rel: Finland is known as the land of a thousand lakes but has far fewer lakes than Canada.

recs.q: Which is the longest river lying entirely within Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Helmand River, about 1,150 km long, is the longest river that flows wholly in Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border with Central Asia, so it is not counted as entirely Afghan; some sources differ.

recs.q: Whose motto is Faith, Unity, Discipline?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah gave the motto Faith, Unity, Discipline (Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem) to the nation.
recs.rel: It is the national motto of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: L, M, N, ?
recs.facts: The letters are in alphabetical order, so O follows N.
recs.rel: L, M, N, O are the 12th to 15th letters of the alphabet.

recs.q: Who is the chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)?
recs.facts: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has been PPP chairman since 2007 and was re-elected in April 2025.
recs.rel: Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the party.

recs.q: Who started the Reshmi Rumal (Silk Letters) Movement?
recs.facts: The Reshmi Rumal Tehreek was organised by Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi together with Shaikh-ul-Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan of Deoband. Secret messages were written on silk cloth to seek help against British rule.
recs.rel: The plot was discovered in 1916 and Maulana Mahmud Hasan was imprisoned in Malta.

recs.q: The Suez Canal separates Africa from which continent?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal in Egypt separates the African mainland from the Sinai Peninsula, which is part of Asia. It also joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
recs.rel: The canal was opened in 1869.

recs.q: Under which Prime Minister was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan framed and enforced?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the constitution in 1956, and it came into force on 23 March 1956.
recs.rel: 23 March is the day later celebrated as Republic Day, and Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.

recs.q: What is the antonym of applaud?
recs.facts: To applaud is to show approval or praise, so its opposite is to criticize or condemn.
recs.rel: Praise, cheer and admire are synonyms of applaud.

recs.q: Bashar al-Assad was the president of which country?
recs.facts: Bashar al-Assad ruled Syria from 2000 until his government fell in December 2024.
recs.rel: He succeeded his father Hafez al-Assad, who ruled Syria from 1971 to 2000.

recs.q: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Zahid Hussain was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan, appointed in 1948.
recs.rel: The bank was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam on 1 July 1948.

recs.q: Which is the hottest layer of the Earth?
recs.facts: Temperature increases with depth, so the inner core is the hottest layer at around 5,000 to 6,000 degrees Celsius.
recs.rel: The inner core is solid due to the immense pressure even though it is so hot.

recs.q: Which country developed the Sinopharm vaccine against Covid-19?
recs.facts: Sinopharm is a state-owned Chinese pharmaceutical company, and its BBIBP-CorV vaccine was developed in China.
recs.rel: Pakistan used the Chinese Sinopharm and CanSino vaccines in its Covid-19 vaccination drive.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'demise'?
recs.facts: Demise means death or end, so its opposite is birth or beginning.
recs.rel: Death, end and collapse are all synonyms of demise.

recs.q: Which desert is located in Sindh?
recs.facts: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is in the Tharparkar region of Sindh and is the largest desert of Sindh.
recs.rel: Thar is also home to the largest coal reserves of Pakistan.

recs.q: Completely is to what, as a synonym? Choose the word closest in meaning to 'entirely'.
recs.facts: Entirely means in every part or fully, the same as completely.
recs.rel: Wholly and totally are also synonyms.

recs.q: Who is the President of Israel?
recs.facts: Isaac Herzog was elected the 11th President of Israel in June 2021 and is still in office.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Reuven Rivlin, and the presidency is largely ceremonial.

recs.q: How many members does SAARC have?
recs.facts: SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
recs.rel: SAARC began in 1985 with seven founding members, and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.

recs.q: In which city is Mughalpura (famous for its railway workshops) located?
recs.facts: Mughalpura is an area of Lahore and is known for its large railway workshops and station.
recs.rel: Lahore Junction is the main railway station of the city.

recs.q: Which Sahabi narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Huraira (RA) narrated about 5,374 Ahadith, the highest number among the Companions.
recs.rel: He is known as Abu Huraira, meaning father of the kitten.

recs.q: NASA, the space agency, belongs to which country?
recs.facts: NASA stands for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, a United States government agency.
recs.rel: NASA was founded in 1958 and landed the first humans on the Moon in 1969.

recs.q: On which date did the partition of Bengal take effect?
recs.facts: The partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October 1905.
recs.rel: Muslims celebrated it, while Hindus observed the day as a day of mourning.

recs.q: Which planet is nearest to the Sun?
recs.facts: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, at about 58 million km.
recs.rel: Mercury is also the smallest planet of the solar system.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 120?
recs.facts: 1/3 of 120 is 40. A quarter of 40 is 40 divided by 4, which equals 10.
recs.rel: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 120 divided by 12.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Russia?
recs.facts: Mikhail Mishustin has been Prime Minister of Russia since January 2020, and he remains in office as of October 2026.
recs.rel: His predecessor as Prime Minister was Dmitry Medvedev.

recs.q: How many senses do human beings have according to the traditional classification?
recs.facts: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
recs.rel: Modern science recognises additional senses such as balance and body position awareness.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'tamed'?
recs.facts: Tamed means made gentle and under control, so its opposite is wild or untamed.
recs.rel: Domesticated is a synonym of tamed.

recs.q: After which event did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
recs.facts: Khalid bin Waleed (RA), who fought against Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam after the Treaty of Hudaibiya in 7 AH.
recs.rel: He is known as Saifullah, the Sword of Allah.

recs.q: The White House in Washington, D.C. is the official residence and workplace of whom?
opts: The President of the United States
The Chief Justice of the US
recs.facts: The White House is the official residence and main workplace of the President of the United States.
recs.rel: The official residence of the US Vice President is the Naval Observatory, not the White House.

recs.q: Which President introduced the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President and enforced the 1962 Constitution on 8 June 1962, framed by a commission headed by Justice Shahabuddin.
recs.rel: It introduced a presidential system with the President elected through Basic Democrats.

recs.q: Which is the third largest city of Pakistan by population?
recs.facts: By population Karachi is first, Lahore second and Faisalabad third, in both the 2017 and 2023 censuses.
recs.rel: Faisalabad was formerly called Lyallpur.

recs.q: Which prophet confronted the king Namrood (Nimrod)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) invited Namrood to worship one Allah, and Namrood had him thrown into a fire, which Allah made cool.
recs.rel: Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun).

recs.q: What is the antonym of autonomy?
recs.facts: Autonomy means self-rule, so its opposite is dependence, being controlled by others.
recs.rel: Synonyms of autonomy include independence and self-government.

recs.q: Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley.
recs.facts: Wheat, rice and barley are food grains (cereals) eaten by people, while hay is dried grass kept as fodder for animals.
recs.rel: Wheat and rice are the two major food crops of Pakistan.

recs.q: The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, Zu Peshawar, was built by which government?
recs.facts: The Peshawar BRT was started in 2017 by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government under Chief Minister Pervez Khattak. It runs in Peshawar, the provincial capital.
recs.rel: The Peshawar BRT was formally inaugurated on 13 August 2020 and has a corridor of about 27.5 km.

recs.q: What is the capital of China?
recs.facts: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.
recs.rel: Shanghai is China's largest city, but not its capital.

recs.q: Who wrote the book 'The Conquest of Happiness'?
recs.facts: The Conquest of Happiness (1930) was written by the British philosopher Bertrand Russell.
recs.rel: Russell won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.

recs.q: Where did the Holy Prophet (SAW) deliver the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat ul Wida)?
recs.facts: The Last Sermon was delivered in the valley of Uranah at the plain of Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
recs.rel: It was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah.

recs.q: In which year was the Sui gas field in Balochistan discovered?
recs.facts: Natural gas was discovered at Sui in Balochistan in 1952 and supply started in 1955.
recs.rel: Sui is the largest natural gas field of Pakistan by output historically.

recs.q: Which country occupies the Golan Heights?
recs.facts: Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the Six-Day War of 1967. It has held the area since then.
recs.rel: The Golan Heights overlook the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan valley.

recs.q: In which year did the Urdu-Hindi controversy begin?
recs.facts: The Urdu-Hindi controversy began in 1867 at Banaras (Varanasi), when Hindus demanded Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu.
recs.rel: The controversy led Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to conclude Hindus and Muslims could not progress together.

recs.q: How many sugar mills did Pakistan have at the time of independence in 1947?
recs.facts: Most colonial-era sugar mills lay on the Indian side of the border, and Pakistan inherited only two.
recs.rel: The first new sugar mill after independence was set up at Tando Muhammad Khan in Sindh in 1961.

recs.q: Lat, Manat and Uzza were what?
recs.facts: Lat, Manat and Uzza were the three chief idols worshipped by the pagan Arabs before Islam.
recs.rel: The Quran mentions them in Surah An-Najm.

recs.q: Which is the latest confirmed fighter jet inducted by the Pakistan Air Force?
recs.facts: The Chinese-made J-10C multirole fighter was inducted by the PAF in March 2022 and is the latest confirmed fighter type.
recs.rel: Reports about the Chinese J-35 stealth fighter for Pakistan remain unconfirmed.

recs.q: Which type of medicine is used to relieve pain?
recs.facts: Analgesics such as paracetamol and aspirin are painkillers. They reduce pain without making the person lose consciousness.
recs.rel: Anaesthetics are different because they cause loss of sensation before surgery.

recs.q: In which city of Pakistan was the first Metro Bus service inaugurated?
recs.facts: The Metro Bus Service was inaugurated in Lahore in February 2013. It runs between Gajju Matta and Shahdara.
recs.rel: Rawalpindi-Islamabad followed in 2015 and Multan in 2017.

recs.q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.01?
recs.rel: Zero has no multiplicative inverse.

recs.q: Which elements are found in the first period of the periodic table?
recs.facts: The first period has only one shell, which can hold two electrons, so it contains just hydrogen (H) and helium (He).
recs.rel: The second period begins with lithium and ends with neon.

recs.q: By what other name is the Pakistan Resolution known?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Resolution of 1940 was passed at Lahore, so it is also called the Lahore Resolution. It demanded independent states for the Muslims of India.
recs.rel: The Allahabad Address of 1930 by Allama Iqbal first outlined the idea of a Muslim state.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'stagnant'?
recs.facts: Stagnant means not flowing or moving, as in stagnant water. Its opposite is flowing.
recs.rel: Stagnant can also describe an economy that is not growing.

recs.q: In football, what did BPL originally stand for in the English league?
recs.facts: The English top division was sponsored by Barclays from 2001 to 2016 and was called the Barclays Premier League (BPL). Today it is simply the Premier League.
recs.rel: BPL also stands for the Bangladesh Premier League in cricket.

recs.q: What does the word venerate mean?
recs.facts: To venerate is to regard someone or something with deep respect and reverence. Its synonyms are revere and honour.
recs.rel: The adjective venerable describes a person worthy of great respect, often because of age or wisdom.

recs.q: Which of the following vitamins is NOT water soluble?
recs.facts: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and do not dissolve in water. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.
recs.rel: Fat soluble vitamins can be stored in the body, while water soluble ones are mostly excreted.

recs.q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Time for 1 km = 100 / 20 = 5 minutes.
recs.rel: His speed is 20 km in 100 minutes, which is 12 km per hour.

recs.q: Which party formed the government in the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) at the time of independence in 1947?
recs.facts: The ministry of Dr Khan Sahib, which belonged to the Indian National Congress (backed by the Khudai Khidmatgars), was in power in the province in August 1947.
recs.rel: The Governor dismissed the Khan Sahib ministry on 22 August 1947, and Abdul Qayyum Khan of the Muslim League then became Chief Minister.

recs.q: For how many days was the 1965 Pakistan-India war fought?
recs.facts: The war began in early September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days. It is remembered as the 17-day war.
recs.rel: Pakistan celebrates 6 September as Defence Day in memory of the 1965 war.

recs.q: In which year was the Mangla Dam completed?
recs.facts: Construction of Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River began in the early 1960s and it was completed in 1967. Sources differ slightly on the start year but agree on 1967.
recs.rel: Tarbela Dam on the Indus was completed later, in 1974.

recs.q: Which battle of the Muslims, fought in 3 AH, is counted as the second major battle after Badr?
recs.facts: The major battles in order are Badr (2 AH), Uhud (3 AH) and Khandaq (5 AH), so Uhud is the second.
recs.rel: Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.

recs.q: Which prophet was sent to the nation (Qaum) of Aad?
recs.facts: Allah sent Hazrat Hud (AS) to guide the people of Aad, who lived in Al-Ahqaf in southern Arabia.
recs.rel: Hazrat Salih (AS) was sent to the nation of Thamud.

recs.q: Who abrogated the 1956 constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan, the army chief, removed Iskander Mirza only 20 days later.

recs.q: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
recs.facts: His name was Abdullah bin Abi Quhafa, and he received the title Siddiq and Atiq.
recs.rel: Some narrations say his pre-Islamic name was Abd al-Kaba, which the Prophet (PBUH) changed to Abdullah.

recs.q: SUPARCO is the national organization of Pakistan for which field?
recs.facts: SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.
recs.rel: It was founded in 1961.

recs.q: How many votes in the 336-member National Assembly are needed to pass a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister?
recs.facts: A no-confidence resolution needs a majority of the total membership of the House. Half of 336 is 168, so 169 votes are needed.
recs.rel: Article 95 of the Constitution deals with the vote of no confidence against the Prime Minister. The National Assembly had 342 seats before 2018.

recs.q: What is cos(90 degrees - x) equal to?
recs.facts: By the complementary angle identity, cos(90 - x) = sin x.
recs.rel: Similarly sin(90 - x) = cos x.

recs.q: Which document paved the way for the constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Objective Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles for the constitutions of Pakistan and became their preamble.
recs.rel: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.

recs.q: In a village the population in 2000 was 4600 and it doubles every five years. What was the population in 1995?
recs.facts: Going back five years halves the population: 4600 / 2 = 2300.
recs.rel: Population in 2005 would be 9200 at the same rate.

recs.q: Which province of Pakistan was the first to issue driving licences to transgender persons (in 2018)?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa traffic police issued driving licences to transgender persons in March 2018, the first province to do so.
recs.rel: Punjab issued licences to 62 transgender drivers in June 2023.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960?
recs.facts: Jawaharlal Nehru signed the treaty with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi on 19 September 1960.
recs.rel: The World Bank mediated the treaty.

recs.q: How many doors (gates) does Jannah (Paradise) have according to hadith?
recs.facts: Authentic hadith state that Paradise has eight gates, one of them being Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
recs.rel: Hell has seven gates.

recs.q: What does FATF stand for?
recs.facts: FATF is the Financial Action Task Force, an international body that sets standards against money laundering and terror financing.
recs.rel: Pakistan was placed on the FATF grey list in June 2018 and removed in October 2022.

recs.q: Which woman is mentioned by name in the Quran?
recs.facts: Hazrat Maryam (AS), the mother of Prophet Isa (AS), is the only woman named in the Quran.
recs.rel: A complete Surah of the Quran, Surah Maryam, is named after her.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'forestall'?
recs.facts: To forestall means to prevent something from happening by taking action ahead of time.
recs.rel: Forestall is often confused with forest but has no connection with trees.

recs.q: Who sold the Kashmir valley to Gulab Singh in 1846?
recs.facts: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 7.5 million rupees.
recs.rel: Gulab Singh became the first Dogra Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

recs.q: Who was the first Hafiz of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it first, so he is called the first Hafiz.
recs.rel: Among the Companions, Hazrat Ali, Ubayy bin Kab and Zaid bin Thabit were also famous Huffaz.

recs.q: Who issues an ordinance at the federal level in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Under Article 89 of the 1973 Constitution, the President can promulgate an ordinance when the National Assembly is not in session.
recs.rel: Governors issue ordinances in the provinces when the provincial assembly is not in session.

recs.q: In which year was Pakistan's first postage stamp issued?
recs.facts: Pakistan issued its first set of four postage stamps on 9 July 1948.
recs.rel: Before that, stamps of British India overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.

recs.q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, including Hazrat Hamza (RA).
recs.rel: In the Battle of Badr only 14 Muslims were martyred.

recs.q: How many times did Jansher Khan win the World Open squash title?
recs.facts: Jansher Khan won the World Open squash championship eight times between 1987 and 1996.
recs.rel: He also won the British Open six times, while Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times.

recs.q: Who was the king (Najashi) of Habsha (Abyssinia) who gave shelter to the Muslim migrants?
recs.facts: The Christian king of Abyssinia, known by the title Najashi (Negus), was Ashama ibn Abjar. He protected the early Muslims who migrated there.
recs.rel: Abraha was the Abyssinian governor of Yemen who marched against the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.

recs.q: What does KRL stand for?
recs.facts: KRL stands for Khan Research Laboratories, named after Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan. It is located at Kahuta.
recs.rel: It was originally set up in 1976 as the Engineering Research Laboratories and renamed in 1981.

recs.q: What is the legislature of Pakistan called?
recs.facts: Pakistan's federal legislature is the Majlis-e-Shura (Parliament), made up of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
recs.rel: India's lower house is called the Lok Sabha.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan is the Neelum Valley and the Neelum River located?
recs.facts: The Neelum Valley and the Neelum River lie in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
recs.rel: The river flows through Muzaffarabad and joins the Jhelum, and its capital valley town is Athmuqam.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old?
recs.facts: The sister is 15 years old when Ali is 5, so she is 10 years older than him. When Ali is 10, she is 10 + 10 = 20 years old.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: In which city is Ayub National Park located?
recs.facts: Ayub National Park is a large public park on Murree Road in Rawalpindi, named after President Ayub Khan.
recs.rel: It has a lake, a zoo-like area and recreation facilities for families.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word prescribe?
opts: To recommend or order as a remedy or rule
recs.facts: To prescribe means to advise or order something, such as a medicine or a rule. Its synonyms include recommend, advise and ordain.
recs.rel: A doctor writes a prescription to prescribe medicine.

recs.q: Jabal-e-Rehmat (Mount of Mercy) is located near which city?
recs.facts: Jabal-e-Rehmat is a hill on the plain of Arafat, about 20 km southeast of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stand at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) delivered his Farewell Sermon near this area in 10 AH.

recs.q: In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed?
recs.facts: The Rowlatt Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919. It allowed arrest and detention without trial.
recs.rel: The Act was named after Justice Sidney Rowlatt, and it led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919.

recs.q: What was the Rowlatt Act?
opts: A law allowing arrest and detention without trial
recs.facts: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the British government power to imprison suspects without trial and to limit press freedom. Indians called it the Black Act.
recs.rel: Gandhi launched a nationwide protest against it.

recs.q: Which prophet is known for suffering patiently from a long skin disease?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayyub (AS) bore a long illness, said to be a skin disease, with great patience and is the model of sabr (patience).
recs.rel: The Quran mentions his prayer in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad.

recs.q: In which year was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh Dogra under the Treaty of Amritsar?
recs.facts: After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British signed the Treaty of Amritsar on 16 March 1846 and sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
recs.rel: The price was 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees.

recs.q: How many sons did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have?
recs.facts: He had three sons, Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyab and Tahir) and Ibrahim, and all of them died in infancy.
recs.rel: Ibrahim was the son of Hazrat Maria Qibtiyya and the others were sons of Hazrat Khadija.

recs.q: What is the capital of Turkey?
recs.facts: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, chosen by Ataturk in 1923 when the republic was founded.
recs.rel: Istanbul is the largest city of Turkey but not its capital.

recs.q: In which province does the Upper Indus Plain mainly lie?
recs.facts: The Upper Indus Plain, north of Mithankot, covers most of Punjab, where the five rivers join the Indus.
recs.rel: The Lower Indus Plain to the south lies mainly in Sindh.

recs.q: What is the original meaning of the word Urdu?
recs.facts: Urdu comes from the Turkish word ordu, meaning camp or army, as the language grew in the military camps and bazaars.
recs.rel: It is also called Lashkari zaban, the language of the army.

recs.q: What is 80% of 90?
recs.rel: 10% of 90 is 9, so 80% is 8 x 9.

recs.q: What is 1/10th of 90?
recs.facts: One tenth of 90 is 90 divided by 10, which is 9.
recs.rel: Dividing by 10 simply moves the decimal point one place to the left.

recs.q: What did the British call the War of 1857 that Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent called the War of Independence?
recs.facts: The British described the uprising of 1857 as a mutiny of their Indian soldiers (sepoys), calling it the Sepoy Mutiny or Indian Mutiny.
recs.rel: Indian and Pakistani historians call it the War of Independence; the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon afterwards.

recs.q: Who abrogated the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan in October 1958?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958, dissolved the assemblies and imposed martial law.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza himself was removed by General Ayub Khan only 20 days later.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: Who is generally listed as the first Governor-General of India (of Bengal, 1774)?
recs.facts: Warren Hastings became Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 and is commonly called the first Governor-General of India in textbooks.
recs.rel: Sources differ: Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of all India in 1833, and Lord Mountbatten was the first of independent India.

recs.q: Which is counted as the third major Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), after Badr and Uhud?
recs.facts: The major battles in order are Badr, Uhud and Khandaq (Ahzab), fought in 5 AH. The Muslims dug a trench on the advice of Salman Farsi.
recs.rel: Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.

recs.q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan in the absence of the President?
recs.facts: Under Article 49 of the constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
recs.rel: If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.

recs.q: Which prophet (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun)?
recs.facts: Allah sent Hazrat Musa (AS), together with his brother Hazrat Harun (AS), to invite Pharaoh to the truth and to free Bani Israel.
recs.rel: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kaleem-ullah (one who spoke to Allah).

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of ADVERSITY?
recs.facts: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, so its opposite is prosperity, meaning good fortune and success.
recs.rel: The plural form adversities is used for repeated difficulties.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to ADVERSITY?
recs.facts: Adversity means a state of serious difficulty or misfortune. Hardship is the nearest synonym.
recs.rel: The proverb says that adversity is the test of true friends.

recs.q: Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla is famous for composing what?
opts: The tune of the national anthem of Pakistan
The words of the national anthem of Pakistan
The design of the flag of Pakistan
recs.facts: Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla (1902-1953) was a Pakistani musician who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The words of the anthem were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.

recs.q: Which is the national airline of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) is the national flag carrier of Pakistan, established in 1955.
recs.rel: PIA operated its first flight in 1955 and is headquartered in Karachi.

recs.q: Syed-ul-Ansar was the title of which Sahabi?
recs.facts: Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA), chief of the Aws tribe of Madina, was given the title Syed-ul-Ansar.
recs.rel: Sources may differ on the title holder, but most Pakistani textbooks give Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).

recs.q: In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan officially approved and adopted?
recs.facts: The national anthem was officially approved by the government of Pakistan in August 1954.
recs.rel: Its tune was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla in 1949 and the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.

recs.q: What is the walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa during Hajj called?
recs.facts: Sa'i is the ritual walk between Safa and Marwa, commemorating Hazrat Hajra's search for water for Ismail (AS).
recs.rel: The Zamzam well appeared near the Kaaba after this search.

recs.q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (Companions of the Cave)?
recs.facts: The Quran in Surah Al-Kahf mentions that their dog lay at the entrance of the cave with outstretched paws.
recs.rel: The dog is traditionally named Qitmir.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies?
recs.facts: Unless dissolved earlier, the National and Provincial Assemblies serve a term of five years from their first meeting.
recs.rel: A Senator's term is six years, with half retiring every three years.

recs.q: Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
recs.rel: It was the first major battle of Islam.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word biased?
recs.facts: Biased means unfairly favouring one side, so its opposite is impartial.
recs.rel: Unbiased and neutral are other opposites.

recs.q: What is the border line between Pakistan and India (drawn in 1947) called?
recs.facts: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by the Boundary Commission headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe at the partition of India in 1947.
recs.rel: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and the McMahon Line is the India-China boundary.

recs.q: In a bus of 24 people, 2/3 are male. What percentage are female?
recs.facts: Males are 2/3 of 24 = 16, so females are 24 - 16 = 8. Percentage = 8/24 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
recs.rel: Females are 1/3 of the bus because the two fractions add up to 1.

recs.q: How many times did Jahangir Khan win the World Open squash championship?
recs.facts: Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times, the last in 1988.
recs.rel: He also won the British Open ten times in a row from 1982 to 1991.

recs.q: Which prophet was blessed with a son in his old age?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was granted Hazrat Ismail (AS) and later Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in his old age.
recs.rel: Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was also given a son, Hazrat Yahya (AS), in old age.

recs.q: The circumference of a circle of radius r is equal to
recs.facts: Circumference = 2 x pi x r, which is the same as pi x diameter.
recs.rel: The area of a circle is pi r squared.

recs.q: What are two circles called that have three points in common?
recs.facts: Three non-collinear points determine exactly one circle. If two circles share three points, they must be the same circle, so they coincide.
recs.rel: Two different circles can meet in at most two points.

recs.q: What are sets that have no common element called?
recs.facts: Sets with no element in common have an empty intersection, and such sets are called disjoint sets.
recs.rel: Sets that have the same number of elements are called equivalent sets.

recs.q: Who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The tune of the anthem was composed by Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla, while the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
recs.rel: The anthem was officially adopted in 1954.

recs.q: A. R. Cornelius, a Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
recs.facts: Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
recs.rel: He was known for his scholarship and integrity.

recs.q: Which crop is grown on the largest area in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Wheat is the staple food and covers the largest cropped area, about 9 million hectares.
recs.rel: Cotton is the major cash crop of Pakistan, but it is grown on a smaller area than wheat.

recs.q: Who is the current Prime Minister of India?
recs.facts: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 2014 and began his third consecutive term in June 2024.
recs.rel: He is the longest-serving Prime Minister of India after Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi in total years.

recs.q: What is a decimal called in which the digits repeat again and again?
recs.facts: A decimal in which a digit or block of digits repeats endlessly, like 0.333..., is called a recurring (repeating) decimal.
recs.rel: Every recurring decimal can be written as a fraction of two integers, so it is a rational number.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam declare in Dhaka that Urdu would be the state language of Pakistan?
recs.facts: On 21 March 1948 at Dhaka, Quaid-e-Azam declared that Urdu alone would be the state language of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Urdu was formally made the national language in the 1973 Constitution, so some sources give a different answer.

recs.q: A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called what?
recs.facts: A square matrix with determinant equal to zero has no inverse and is called a singular matrix.
recs.rel: A matrix with a non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.

recs.q: On whose advice does the President of Pakistan dissolve the National Assembly under the Constitution as it stands today?
recs.facts: Under Article 58 the President dissolves the National Assembly only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
recs.rel: Before the 18th Amendment of 2010 the President could also dissolve it on his own discretion under Article 58(2)(b).

recs.q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: What is the term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The National Assembly has a term of five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.
recs.rel: A Senator has a term of six years.

recs.q: What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan today?
recs.facts: Recent data for 2025 show hydel power as the largest single source, around 39 percent in some months. RLNG and nuclear follow.
recs.rel: In earlier decades thermal (oil and gas) plants produced most of Pakistan's electricity.

recs.q: How many articles are there in the English language?
recs.facts: The English articles are a, an and the. A and an are indefinite and the is definite.
recs.rel: Candidates often wrongly say 2, forgetting that a and an are separate forms.

recs.q: A train travels twice as fast as a car. If the car covers 30 km in 60 minutes, in what time will the train cover 30 km?
recs.facts: The car's speed is 30 km per hour, so the train's speed is 60 km per hour. The train covers 30 km in 30 / 60 hour = 30 minutes.
recs.rel: Time = distance / speed.

recs.q: Which is the fastest land (terrestrial) animal?
recs.facts: The cheetah is the fastest land animal and can run at about 100 to 110 km per hour in short bursts.
recs.rel: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in a dive.

recs.q: How many agencies were there in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)?
recs.facts: FATA had seven agencies: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan.
recs.rel: There were also frontier regions (FRs) attached to FATA.

recs.q: In which year was the Bogra Formula presented?
recs.facts: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the formula in 1953 to solve the constitutional deadlock.
recs.rel: It was announced in the Constituent Assembly in October 1953.

recs.q: What was the Bogra Formula?
opts: A constitutional proposal for a two-house legislature with parity between East and West Pakistan
A plan to make Urdu the only national language
recs.facts: It proposed a bicameral legislature, with equal representation of the provinces in the upper house and representation by population in the lower house.
recs.rel: It was named after Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra.

recs.q: In which galaxy does the Earth lie?
recs.facts: Our solar system and the Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy.
recs.rel: The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is Andromeda.

recs.q: The ancient region of Gandhara lay mainly between which two modern cities?
recs.facts: Gandhara covered the Peshawar valley and the Potohar plateau around Taxila, roughly from Peshawar to Rawalpindi in north-west Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sources differ on exact limits, but Taxila and Peshawar are its best-known centres.

recs.q: In which country do the Golan Heights lie?
recs.facts: The Golan Heights is a rocky plateau in south-western Syria. Most of it has been occupied by Israel since 1967.
recs.rel: Israel annexed the Golan Heights in 1981, but this is not recognised by most of the world.

recs.q: If Hamza is three times as old as Ali, what will be the age of Hamza when Ali is 7 years old?
recs.facts: Hamza's age is 3 times Ali's age, so 3 x 7 = 21 years.
recs.rel: Age problems are solved by first writing the ratio between the ages.

recs.q: For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah boycott Banu Hashim?
recs.facts: The Quraish imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim for about three years in the valley of Shib Abi Talib.
recs.rel: The boycott took place from the 7th to the 10th year of prophethood.

recs.q: What is the new name of the Kashmir Highway in Islamabad?
recs.facts: In August 2020 Pakistan renamed Islamabad's Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway in solidarity with Kashmiris.
recs.rel: The renaming was done on the first anniversary of India's revocation of Article 370 in 2019.

recs.q: Where was the ICC Men's T20 World Cup of 2021 played?
recs.facts: The 2021 T20 World Cup, officially hosted by the BCCI of India, was moved because of COVID-19 and played in the UAE and Oman in October and November 2021.
recs.rel: Australia won the 2021 final against New Zealand in Dubai.

recs.q: Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and was known for his patience?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayub (AS) was tested with loss of wealth, family and a long illness and kept patience, so his name is a proverb for sabr.
recs.rel: Allah cured him after he prayed, as mentioned in the Quran.

recs.q: What does the adjective intimate mean?
recs.facts: Intimate describes a very close, familiar relationship or a detailed, deep knowledge of something.
recs.rel: Intimate can also be a verb meaning to hint at something indirectly, pronounced differently.

recs.q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
recs.facts: According to authentic hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
recs.rel: Jahannam, by contrast, has seven gates.

recs.q: Which fighter jet has Pakistan produced jointly with China?
recs.facts: The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter built by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
recs.rel: Its Chinese designation is FC-1 Xiaolong.

recs.q: Who wrote the famous biography 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
recs.facts: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' in 1984.
recs.rel: Fatima Jinnah wrote 'My Brother' and Hector Bolitho wrote 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.

recs.q: Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Balochistan, Rawalpindi?
recs.facts: Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi are cities, while Balochistan is a province.
recs.rel: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.

recs.q: What kind of number is 5/7?
recs.facts: A number that can be written as a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator is rational. 5/7 is such a ratio.
recs.rel: Numbers such as pi and the square root of 2 cannot be written as a ratio of integers, so they are irrational.

recs.q: What is the capital of North Korea?
recs.facts: Pyongyang is the capital and largest city of North Korea.
recs.rel: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

recs.q: Which language is the lingua franca (common link language) of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Urdu is understood across all provinces and links people of different mother tongues. It is also the national language.
recs.rel: Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue in Pakistan.

recs.q: Which letter comes after G in the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The order is F, G, H, I, so H follows G.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

recs.q: Which letter comes after the letter that is followed by M?
recs.facts: The letter followed by M is L, and the letter after L is M.
recs.rel: M is the 13th letter, exactly in the middle of the alphabet.

recs.q: Who is Mark Zuckerberg?
recs.facts: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the CEO of its parent company Meta.
recs.rel: Facebook was renamed as Meta Platforms in 2021.

recs.q: On which date did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) arrive in Madina after the Hijrat?
recs.facts: After staying at Quba, the Prophet (PBUH) entered Madina on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 1 AH (September 622 AD). He had left Makkah a few days earlier.
recs.rel: Some sources give slightly different days for the departure and arrival, but 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal is the common Pakistani textbook date.

recs.q: What is the median of the data 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8?
recs.facts: The data is already in order and has 9 values, so the median is the 5th value. The 5th value is 5.
recs.rel: The median is the middle value of ordered data, and for an even count it is the mean of the two middle values.

recs.q: What is the midpoint of the points (3, 1) and (-3, 1)?
recs.rel: The midpoint formula is the average of the x values and the average of the y values.

recs.q: If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km is 50 divided by 320. For 400 km, 400 x 50 / 320 = 62.5 gallons.
recs.rel: This is a direct proportion question.

recs.q: In which Nabawi year was Namaz (the five daily prayers) made obligatory?
recs.facts: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Miraj, which most Pakistani textbooks place in the 10th year of prophethood.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact year of Miraj; some say the 11th or 12th Nabawi year.

recs.q: In which Nabawi year did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
recs.facts: The Hijrat took place in 622 CE, which was the 13th year of prophethood.
recs.rel: This Hijrat marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

recs.q: In which city is the head office (secretariat) of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
recs.facts: The ECO secretariat is located in Tehran, Iran.
recs.rel: ECO was founded in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.

recs.q: What does OGRA stand for?
recs.facts: OGRA stands for the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, which regulates the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector of Pakistan.
recs.rel: OGRA was established in 2002 and has its head office in Islamabad.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan purchase Gwadar from Oman?
recs.facts: Pakistan bought the Gwadar enclave from the Sultan of Oman in 1958, and it was formally handed over on 8 December 1958.
recs.rel: Gwadar became part of Balochistan province in 1977.

recs.q: Who originally built the Kaaba?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), with the help of his son Hazrat Ismail (AS), raised the walls of the Kaaba by Allah's command. This is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks.
recs.rel: Some traditions say the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS) or the angels, so sources differ.

recs.q: Geographically, into how many main regions is Pakistan divided according to most textbooks?
recs.facts: Pakistan is usually divided into six regions: Northern Highlands, Western Highlands, Balochistan Plateau, Potohar Plateau and Salt Range, Indus Plain, and Deserts.
recs.rel: Some books group them into three or five regions, so sources differ.

recs.q: Where was the Battle of Plassey fought?
