recs.facts: The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Plassey in Bengal, on the bank of the Bhagirathi river.
recs.rel: Plassey is in present-day West Bengal, India.

recs.q: According to Pakistani textbooks, how many prophets were sent by Allah in total?
recs.facts: A well-known hadith, as taught in Pakistani textbooks, gives the number of prophets as 124,000.
recs.rel: Only 25 prophets are named in the Quran, and some narrations give 224,000.

recs.q: Under which treaty did Gulab Singh purchase Kashmir from the British?
recs.facts: By the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846) the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu for 7.5 million rupees.
recs.rel: This created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir under Dogra rule.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word refute?
recs.facts: To refute a claim is to prove it wrong. Synonyms include disprove, rebut and counter.
recs.rel: Refute is sometimes wrongly used to mean simply deny.

recs.q: Which country does not have a regular army?
recs.facts: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 after a civil war. It relies on police forces for security.
recs.rel: Dominica, Iceland and Panama are other countries without a standing army.

recs.q: What does SUPARCO stand for and what is it related to?
opts: Pakistan's space and upper atmosphere research agency
recs.facts: SUPARCO is the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency. It was founded in 1961.
recs.rel: Pakistan launched its first satellite Badr-1 in 1990.

recs.q: Is the square root of 7 a rational or an irrational number?
recs.facts: 7 is not a perfect square, so its square root is a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal and cannot be written as a fraction of integers. Hence it is irrational.
recs.rel: The square root of any prime number is irrational.

recs.q: On what date was the Rowlatt Act passed in 1919?
recs.facts: The Imperial Legislative Council passed the Rowlatt Act on 18 March 1919.
recs.rel: Some sources give 21 March 1919, the date of the Viceroy's assent, so sources differ slightly.

recs.q: In which part of Punjab is the Salt Range located?
recs.facts: The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, between the Jhelum River and the Indus River south of Potohar Plateau. Khewra salt mine is in the range.
recs.rel: Mount Sakesar is the highest peak of the Salt Range.

recs.q: In which year was the Scientific Society founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the Scientific Society in 1864 at Ghazipur to translate Western scientific works into Urdu.
recs.rel: The society later moved to Aligarh in 1866, where it published the Aligarh Institute Gazette.

recs.q: In which year was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi on 17 October 1817.
recs.rel: He founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh, which later became Aligarh Muslim University.

recs.q: What is the value of tan 90 degrees?
recs.facts: tan 90 = sin 90 / cos 90 = 1 / 0, and division by zero is undefined.
recs.rel: tan 45 degrees equals 1 and tan 0 degrees equals 0.

recs.q: At what age of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the last revelation (wahi) revealed?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and the last verses shortly before his death at the age of 63.
recs.rel: He passed away in 11 AH (632 CE).

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and he is 4 years younger than his sister. When Ali is 8 years old, how old will his sister be?
recs.facts: Sister is 4 + 4 = 8 years old now, so she is 4 years older than Ali. When Ali is 8, she will be 8 + 4 = 12.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: What is the value of any non-zero number raised to the power zero?
recs.facts: By the law of exponents a^0 = a^n / a^n = 1 for any non-zero number a.
recs.rel: The expression 0 to the power 0 is treated as undefined or indeterminate in basic algebra.

recs.q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 1st of that month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 15th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both fall on the same weekday, Monday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: What is the value of sin 180 degrees?
recs.facts: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and sine is the y-coordinate, which is 0.
recs.rel: Also cos 180 degrees = -1 and sin 90 degrees = 1.

recs.q: What is the value of cos 180 degrees?
recs.facts: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and cosine is the x-coordinate, which is -1.
recs.rel: cos 0 degrees = 1, cos 90 degrees = 0 and cos 180 degrees = -1.

recs.q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution also used the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan, while the 1962 Constitution used Republic of Pakistan.

recs.q: How many seats are reserved for non-Muslim minorities in the National Assembly of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves ten seats in the National Assembly for non-Muslims.
recs.rel: Minority members are chosen on reserved seats in proportion to the seats won by each party.

recs.q: Which country hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics?
recs.facts: The 2022 Winter Olympics were held in Beijing, China, in February 2022. There was no Summer Olympics in 2022.
recs.rel: The 2020 Summer Olympics were held in Tokyo in 2021, and the 2024 Summer Games in Paris.

recs.q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is male?
recs.facts: 340 divided by 500 times 100 gives 68 percent.
recs.rel: The remaining 32 percent are female.

recs.q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Governors-General were Quaid-e-Azam, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55) and then Iskander Mirza.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.

recs.q: If a helicopter covers 320 miles using 80 gallons of fuel, how many gallons are needed for 700 miles?
recs.facts: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 miles: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
recs.rel: Such questions are solved with direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.

recs.q: For which field is Abdur Rehman Chughtai famous?
recs.facts: Abdur Rehman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a famous Pakistani painter and artist known for his Mughal-influenced style.
recs.rel: He is also known for designing Pakistan's early postage stamps.

recs.q: What is the meaning of abhor?
recs.facts: Abhor means to regard with disgust and hatred.
recs.rel: The noun form is abhorrence.

recs.q: What is a synonym of acute?
recs.facts: Acute can mean sharp or intense, as in acute pain, and severe is the closest synonym.
recs.rel: Acute angle means an angle less than 90 degrees.

recs.q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address at the Allahabad session of the Muslim League?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal gave his Allahabad Address in 1930, in which he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
recs.rel: He gave a series of lectures at Madras and other places in 1928-29, which became Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word ADHERE?
recs.facts: To adhere means to stick or hold fast to something, such as a surface, a rule or a belief. Its synonyms include stick, cling and follow.
recs.rel: The related noun adherent means a supporter or follower of a cause.

recs.q: What does the Arabic word Alfeel mean?
recs.facts: Alfeel means elephant. Surah Al-Fil of the Quran tells of Abraha's army with elephants that tried to destroy the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Year of the Elephant (about 570 CE).

recs.q: When was the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) founded?
recs.facts: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded at the Belgrade Summit in September 1961 by leaders such as Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno.
recs.rel: The movement grew out of the 1955 Bandung Conference.

recs.q: Which act of worship is mentioned in the Quran together with Zakat in many verses?
recs.facts: The Quran repeatedly commands to establish Salat and pay Zakat together, for example in Surah Al-Baqarah.
recs.rel: Salat is the second and Zakat the third pillar of Islam in the usual list (after Shahada).

recs.q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 24 balls. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
recs.facts: Let Ahmad keep x balls, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 24, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.
recs.rel: Amjad therefore kept 18 balls, and 18 is three times 6.

recs.q: What is the antonym of defile?
recs.facts: To defile means to make dirty or impure, so its opposite is to purify.
recs.rel: Pollute, stain and spoil are close to defile in meaning.

recs.q: What is the antonym of dilate?
recs.facts: To dilate is to become wider or larger, so its opposite is to constrict or contract.
recs.rel: The pupil of the eye dilates in dim light.

recs.q: Saudi riyal is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: The riyal is the official currency of Saudi Arabia, issued by the Saudi Central Bank.
recs.rel: Qatar and Oman also use a currency called riyal, but the Saudi riyal belongs to Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: What is the circling (going around) of the Kaaba during Hajj and Umrah called?
recs.facts: Tawaf is the act of walking seven times around the Kaaba in an anticlockwise direction.
recs.rel: Tawaf begins and ends at the Black Stone (Hajr-e-Aswad).

recs.q: How many articles did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan have?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution given by Ayub Khan had 250 articles.
recs.rel: It was suspended when martial law was imposed in 1969.

recs.q: Baltistan is also known as which of the following?
recs.facts: Baltistan, in Gilgit-Baltistan, is called Little Tibet (Tibet-e-Khurd) because of its culture and mountain landscape similar to Tibet.
recs.rel: Skardu is the main town of Baltistan.

recs.q: Where did the Quraish tribe belong?
recs.facts: The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and custodians of the Kaaba.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) was born into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.

recs.q: Which prophet (AS) was given the ability to understand the language of birds and animals?
recs.facts: The Quran says that Allah taught Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) the speech of birds, and he talked with the hoopoe and the ant.
recs.rel: Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) also ruled over the jinn and the wind, and he was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).

recs.q: On which date of the Islamic month was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born, according to the view most followed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant, which is about 570 AD in Makkah.
recs.rel: Some scholars and the Shia tradition give 17 Rabi-ul-Awwal, so sources differ on the exact day.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word brilliant?
recs.facts: Brilliant means very bright or very intelligent, and its opposite is dull.
recs.rel: Synonyms of brilliant include bright, radiant and gifted.

recs.q: On which river did India build the Baglihar dam?
recs.facts: The Baglihar hydroelectric dam is built by India on the Chenab river in Jammu and Kashmir. The Chenab flows on into Pakistan.
recs.rel: Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 the Chenab is one of the three western rivers allotted to Pakistan.

recs.q: What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
opts: A British mission sent to India to discuss the transfer of power
A Muslim League mission sent to London
A Congress mission sent to the Viceroy
A United Nations mission to Kashmir
recs.facts: The Cabinet Mission was a delegation of three British cabinet ministers sent to India in 1946. It proposed a plan for the transfer of power and a united India with a weak centre.
recs.rel: The Muslim League first accepted the plan and later withdrew its acceptance.

recs.q: Who was the third caliph of Islam?
recs.facts: The order of the Rightly Guided Caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. So the third was Hazrat Uthman (RA).
recs.rel: Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called Ghani and Zun-Noorain.

recs.q: If set A has 3 elements and set B has 4 elements, how many elements are in the Cartesian product A x B?
recs.facts: The number of elements in A x B is the product of the sizes: 3 x 4 = 12.
recs.rel: The number of elements of A x B equals that of B x A.

recs.q: How many players play in a game of chess?
recs.facts: Chess is played between two players, one with white pieces and one with black.
recs.rel: Each player starts with 16 pieces on a board of 64 squares.

recs.q: Which is the coldest inhabited place of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan records the lowest winter temperatures among Pakistan's inhabited places; it recorded about minus 21 degrees Celsius in December 2019.
recs.rel: Ziarat and Gilgit are also among the coldest places in winter.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 + 7i?
recs.facts: In a + bi the real part is a, so for 6 + 7i the real part is 6 and the imaginary part is 7.
recs.rel: The modulus of 6 + 7i is the square root of 85.

recs.q: In which year AD was Makkah conquered by the Muslims?
recs.facts: Makkah was conquered in Ramadan 8 AH, which corresponds to January 630 AD.
recs.rel: The conquest was almost bloodless and the Prophet (PBUH) announced a general amnesty.

recs.q: How many copies of the Quran were prepared by Hazrat Usman (RA) and sent to different regions?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA) had standard copies prepared from the Abu Bakr copy and sent them to major centres; most Pakistani textbooks say five copies.
recs.rel: Some sources say seven copies, including one kept in Madina, so sources differ.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word crude?
recs.facts: Crude means in a natural or raw state, not yet processed, or rough and lacking refinement.
recs.rel: Crude oil is petroleum before it is refined into petrol and diesel.

recs.q: Against whom did Nawab Siraj ud Daula fight the Battle of Plassey in 1757?
recs.facts: The British East India Company forces under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
recs.rel: The battle marked the beginning of British rule in India.

recs.q: Pakistan's friendship with which neighbouring country is described as higher than the mountains and deeper than the oceans?
recs.facts: Pakistani leaders describe the Pakistan-China friendship as higher than the Himalayas and deeper than the oceans.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway and CPEC link the two countries.

recs.q: Roughly what fraction of the Earth's land surface is covered by deserts (arid regions)?
recs.facts: Deserts and arid lands cover roughly one third of the Earth's land surface.
recs.rel: Sources differ depending on how a desert is defined.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word 'ecstasy'?
recs.facts: Ecstasy means overwhelming joy, so its opposite is deep unhappiness, which is misery. Rapture, elation and delight are its synonyms.
recs.rel: Agony and despair are also opposites of ecstasy.

recs.q: Who elects the President of Pakistan?
opts: An electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies
recs.facts: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies.
recs.rel: Asif Ali Zardari was elected President for a second time in March 2024.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word excuse (as a verb)?
recs.facts: To excuse someone means to forgive or pardon a fault. Blame, punish and accuse have the opposite sense.
recs.rel: As a noun, excuse means a reason offered to justify a fault, for example a pretext.

recs.q: According to Islam, fasting (Roza) protects a person from what?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that fasting is a shield. It teaches self-control and keeps a person away from sins and evil deeds.
recs.rel: The Quran says fasting was prescribed so that you may become pious (taqwa).

recs.q: What happened on 27 February 2019 when the Pakistan Air Force responded to an Indian incursion?
opts: Pakistan shot down two Indian aircraft and captured a pilot
recs.facts: On 27 February 2019 the PAF shot down Indian aircraft inside Pakistani airspace and the Indian pilot Wing Commander Abhinandan was captured.
recs.rel: Pakistan named its response Operation Swift Retort and returned the pilot to India on 1 March 2019.

recs.q: What was the name of the foster mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Halima Sadia of the Banu Saad tribe nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert.
recs.rel: Thuwaiba, a freed slave of Abu Lahab, nursed him briefly before Halima.

recs.q: Which is the fourth source of Islamic law (Shariah) in the usual order?
recs.facts: The four sources in order are the Holy Quran, the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus of scholars) and Qiyas (analogy).
recs.rel: Hanafi fiqh, followed by most Pakistanis, accepts all four sources.

recs.q: What is the capital of France?
recs.facts: Paris, on the River Seine, is the capital and largest city of France.
recs.rel: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.

recs.q: The Friendship Gate (Bab-e-Dosti) at Chaman is a border crossing between which two countries?
recs.facts: The Friendship Gate stands at Chaman in Balochistan on the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
recs.rel: It is on Pakistan's western border, the Durand Line, opposite Spin Boldak in Afghanistan.

recs.q: In which year of prophethood (Nabwi) was the Year of Grief (Aam-ul-Huzn)?
recs.facts: The Year of Grief was the 10th year of prophethood, when the Prophet (PBUH) lost his wife Hazrat Khadija (RA) and his uncle Abu Talib within a short time.
recs.rel: Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.

recs.q: What is Hajr-e-Aswad?
opts: The Black Stone fixed in the Kaaba
A gate of the Prophet's Mosque
recs.facts: Hajr-e-Aswad is the Black Stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.
recs.rel: Pilgrims try to kiss or point to it at the start of each Tawaf.

recs.q: What is the HCF of 6 and 12?
recs.facts: 6 divides 12 exactly, so the largest number dividing both is 6.
recs.rel: When one number divides the other, the smaller number is the HCF and the larger is the LCM.

recs.q: At what age is Hazrat Isa (AS) commonly said to have been raised to the heavens?
recs.facts: The commonly stated age at which Hazrat Isa (AS) was raised to the heavens is 33 years.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact age, but 33 is the figure most commonly given.

recs.q: Which is the highest mountain in the world?
recs.facts: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border, is the highest mountain above sea level.
recs.rel: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: Which is an important river of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
recs.facts: The Kabul River flows from Afghanistan through Peshawar and joins the Indus near Attock. Swat river is also a major river of the province.
recs.rel: The Hub River lies on the border of Sindh and Balochistan.

recs.q: What is the most important event of 10 Hijri?
opts: The Farewell Hajj and Last Sermon of the Prophet (PBUH)
recs.facts: In 10 AH the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Hajjatul Wida, and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.
recs.rel: The Conquest of Makkah took place in 8 AH.

recs.q: Which Chinese fighter jets did Pakistan Air Force formally induct in March 2022?
recs.facts: The PAF commissioned its first six J-10C multirole fighters from China in March 2022.
recs.rel: China's stealth fighter J-35 has been reported as a possible future PAF purchase, but no delivery has been officially confirmed.

recs.q: What is the integral of ln x with respect to x?
recs.facts: Integrating by parts with u = ln x and dv = dx gives x ln x - integral of (x times 1/x) dx = x ln x - x + C.
recs.rel: The derivative of ln x is 1/x.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word interim?
recs.facts: Interim describes something provided or done for the time between two events, that is, temporary.
recs.rel: An interim government rules only until a regular government is elected.

recs.q: Inzamam-ul-Haq, one of Pakistan's best batsmen, played which sport for the Pakistan national team?
recs.facts: Inzamam-ul-Haq played Test and One Day cricket for Pakistan from 1991 to 2007 and captained the team.
recs.rel: He scored 8830 Test runs and 11701 ODI runs.

recs.q: Who is regarded as the first martyr of Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Sumayyah (RA), mother of Hazrat Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is the first martyr of Islam.
recs.rel: Some sources name Harith bin Abi Hala as the first male martyr, so sources differ.

recs.q: How many Jewish tribes lived in Madina when the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrated there?
recs.facts: The three main Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir and Banu Quraizah.
recs.rel: The Charter of Madina (Misaq-e-Madina) was made with them after the Hijrah.

recs.q: Which was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan?
recs.facts: Bahawalpur was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan, in October 1947.
recs.rel: Its ruler, the Nawab Sadiq Muhammad Khan Abbasi V, acceded on 5 October 1947.

recs.q: Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa was a Pakistani girl from Faisalabad who became a Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9.
recs.rel: She died in January 2012 at the age of 16, and Lahore has a software technology park tower named after her.

recs.q: Kathmandu is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal.
recs.rel: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.

recs.q: On which river is the Khanpur Dam built?
recs.facts: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River in the Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

recs.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
recs.facts: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12 and multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The first common multiple is 12.
recs.rel: LCM times HCF of two numbers equals their product (12 x 2 = 24).

recs.q: What is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour (gas) called?
recs.facts: When a liquid gains heat and its molecules escape into the air as vapour, the change is called evaporation or vaporization.
recs.rel: The reverse process, vapour changing into liquid, is called condensation.

recs.q: What is the value of log 1 (to any valid base)?
recs.facts: Any base b raised to the power 0 equals 1, so the logarithm of 1 is 0.
recs.rel: The logarithm of 0 is undefined.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'loved'?
recs.facts: Loved means felt strong affection for, and its opposite is hated.
recs.rel: Loathed and detested are other close opposites.

recs.q: What was the approximate strength of the Muslim army sent against Musailma Kazzab in the Battle of Yamama?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) led about 13,000 Muslims against the army of Musailma Kazzab at Yamama in 633 CE (11 AH).
recs.rel: Musailma's army is usually given as about 40,000, though sources differ on exact numbers.

recs.q: In which city is Masjid-e-Nabawi located?
recs.facts: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built by the Holy Prophet (SAW) in Madina after the Hijrat.
recs.rel: It also contains the blessed grave of the Prophet (SAW).

recs.q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Navy?
opts: Vice Admiral H. M. S. Choudri
recs.facts: Vice Admiral James Wilfred Jefford of the Royal Navy became the first head of the Royal Pakistan Navy in 1947.
recs.rel: The first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Navy was Vice Admiral Muhammad Siddiq Choudri.

recs.q: A person walks 7 miles towards the north, then turns left, then turns left again. In which direction is he going now?
recs.facts: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. Turning left again from west makes him face south.
recs.rel: Two successive left turns make a total turn of 180 degrees.

recs.q: What is a matrix with only one row called?
recs.facts: A matrix having only one row is called a row matrix; its order is 1 x n.
recs.rel: A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.

recs.q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will one man write in 5 minutes?
recs.facts: 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes.
recs.rel: The rate is 1 page per man per 5 minutes, or 0.2 pages per minute.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: The prices of clothes are too ___.
recs.facts: Prices are described as high or low, so high is the correct word.
recs.rel: We use tall and long for height and length, not for prices.

recs.q: What is the antonym of provoke?
recs.facts: Provoke means to make someone angry or stir them up; the opposite is to pacify or calm them.
recs.rel: Appease and soothe are also antonyms of provoke.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 12?
recs.facts: A quarter means one fourth. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
recs.rel: A quarter of 120 is 30, ten times the answer here.

recs.q: Which political party launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942?
recs.facts: The Indian National Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay in August 1942 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. The Muslim League opposed the movement.
recs.rel: The Quit India Movement demanded an immediate end to British rule in India.

recs.q: Why do people read newspapers?
opts: To get information and knowledge about current events
recs.facts: Newspapers report news and information about local and world events. People read them mainly to gain knowledge and stay informed.
recs.rel: The first printed newspapers appeared in Europe in the early 1600s.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number -i(4i + 6)?
recs.facts: -i(4i + 6) = -4i squared - 6i = 4 - 6i since i squared = -1. The real part is 4.
recs.rel: The imaginary part of this number is -6.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Dead Reckoning: Memories of the 1971 Bangladesh War?
recs.facts: Dead Reckoning (2011) was written by Sarmila Bose and discusses the 1971 war and its casualty figures. It is often confused with works by authors with similar names.
recs.rel: Shrabani Basu wrote Victoria and Abdul, a different book.

recs.q: What does the word refund mean?
recs.facts: Refund means to give back money that was paid, for example for a returned item. Its synonym is reimburse.
recs.rel: Refund can be a noun (a refund) or a verb (to refund).

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word reluctant?
recs.facts: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something. A reluctant person does not want to act.
recs.rel: The noun form is reluctance.

recs.q: Which two hadith books are called the Sahihain?
recs.facts: Sahihain means the two Sahih books: Sahih al-Bukhari by Imam Bukhari and Sahih Muslim by Imam Muslim.
recs.rel: These two are considered the most authentic books of hadith.

recs.q: My brother's son's sister is my what?
recs.facts: My brother's son is my nephew, and his sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
recs.rel: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.

recs.q: The Sun is currently in which stage of a star's life?
recs.facts: The Sun fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, which is the main sequence stage. It has been in this stage for about 4.6 billion years.
recs.rel: In about 5 billion years the Sun will become a red giant.

recs.q: Which is the largest railway station of Pakistan, according to most sources?
recs.facts: Lahore Junction is most commonly named as the largest railway station of Pakistan by area.
recs.rel: Sources differ on this point, and Karachi Cantonment and Rohri are also described as very large.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of 'strenuous'?
recs.facts: Strenuous means needing great effort or energy. Arduous has the same meaning.
recs.rel: The opposite of strenuous is effortless or easy.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "normally"?
recs.facts: Normally means in the usual way, which is usually.
recs.rel: Its opposite is abnormally.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "retrieve"?
recs.facts: To retrieve is to get something back, which is to recover.
recs.rel: A retriever dog is named for fetching game.

recs.q: With what is Tayammum performed?
recs.facts: Tayammum is done by striking the hands on clean earth or dust and wiping the face and arms.
recs.rel: It is allowed instead of wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful to use.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word timid?
recs.facts: Timid means lacking courage, so its opposite is bold.
recs.rel: Shy, fearful and meek are synonyms of timid.

recs.q: Jami at-Tirmidhi (Tirmizi Sharif) is a book of what?
recs.facts: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of the sayings and actions (ahadith) of the Prophet (PBUH) compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.
recs.rel: It is one of the six major hadith collections known as Sihah Sitta.

recs.q: In which language was the Holy Quran first translated in the subcontinent (India)?
recs.facts: Shah Waliullah made the well-known first full translation into Persian in 1738, which is the usual textbook answer.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as an early Sindhi translation is also claimed; Shah Abdul Qadir later did the first Urdu translation.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: Soldiers are digging trenches.
opts: Trenches are being dug by soldiers.
Trenches have been dug by soldiers.
recs.facts: The present continuous active becomes am/is/are being plus the past participle in the passive.
recs.rel: The past continuous 'were digging' becomes 'were being dug'.

recs.q: In which year was Urdu declared the national language of Pakistan, as commonly taught?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam declared Urdu the state language at Dhaka in March 1948, and this is the usual textbook answer.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution also names Urdu as the national language of Pakistan.

recs.q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
recs.facts: Lord Canning became the first Viceroy in 1858 after the Government of India Act transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown.
recs.rel: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, and Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India.

recs.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
recs.facts: Influenza is caused by influenza viruses. Tuberculosis and cholera are caused by bacteria and malaria by a protozoan parasite.
recs.rel: Antibiotics do not work against viral diseases.

recs.q: Which is the highest waterfall in the world?
recs.facts: Angel Falls in Venezuela has a total height of about 979 metres, with an uninterrupted drop of about 807 metres, making it the highest waterfall in the world.
recs.rel: Angel Falls is located in Canaima National Park, Venezuela, and is named after the pilot Jimmie Angel.

recs.q: What does WWW stand for in internet addresses?
recs.facts: WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked pages accessed over the internet.
recs.rel: The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

recs.q: In which direction of Pakistan does the Chinese region of Xinjiang lie?
recs.facts: Xinjiang lies to the north (north-east) of Pakistan and meets Gilgit-Baltistan at the Khunjerab Pass.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with Xinjiang through the Khunjerab Pass.

recs.q: What is 90 divided by 90 (90/90)?
recs.facts: Any non-zero number divided by itself equals 1, so 90/90 = 1.
recs.rel: Division of zero by a non-zero number gives 0, but division by zero is undefined.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will be the 13th of that month?
recs.facts: The 13th is 9 days after the 4th, and 9 = 7 + 2. Sunday + 2 days = Tuesday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 14th of that month?
recs.facts: The 14th is 13 days after the 1st, and 13 = 7 + 6. Monday + 6 days = Sunday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: Which term comes next in the series: 3z, 6y, 9x, 15w, ?
recs.facts: The numbers 3, 6, 9, 15 follow the rule that each is the sum of the two before it (3+6=9, 6+9=15), so the next is 9+15=24. The letters go backwards from z, y, x, w to v.
recs.rel: A series where each term is the sum of the previous two is called a Fibonacci-type series.

recs.q: What is the square root of 1600?
recs.facts: 40 x 40 = 1600, so the square root of 1600 is 40.
recs.rel: The square root of 16 is 4, so the square root of 1600 is 4 x 10 = 40.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah receive the title of Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader), as most Pakistani textbooks state?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks say that Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed gave the title Quaid-e-Azam to Jinnah in 1938.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact year, and some mention 1936 or other dates.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 19th is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Sunday, which is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 24th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 3rd be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd back to the 24th is 21 days. 21 days is 3 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) before Tuesday, which is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: Which constitution was enforced in Pakistan in April 1972 after the separation of East Pakistan?
recs.facts: After 1971 a temporary Interim Constitution was adopted in April 1972, which ended martial law and ran until the permanent constitution of 1973.
recs.rel: The permanent Constitution of Pakistan was passed in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

recs.q: Under whose government was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan framed and passed?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution was drafted by a parliamentary committee and passed by the National Assembly during the premiership of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. It was adopted in April 1973.
recs.rel: Abdul Hafeez Pirzada, the law minister, played a leading role in drafting it.

recs.q: What is 2 x 2 divided by 2?
recs.facts: Work left to right: 2 x 2 is 4, and 4 divided by 2 is 2.
recs.rel: Multiplication and division have equal priority and are done left to right.

recs.q: In a school of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is female?
recs.facts: Females are 500 minus 340, which is 160. Then 160 divided by 500 times 100 gives 32 percent.
recs.rel: Males make up 68 percent.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What percentage of students is absent?
recs.facts: Absent students are 500 minus 360, which is 140. Then 140 divided by 500 times 100 gives 28 percent.
recs.rel: Present students here are 72 percent.

recs.q: What is 3x4 + 2x4 (also written 3x4 + 4x2)?
recs.facts: Multiply first: 3x4 = 12 and 2x4 = 8 (4x2 is also 8). Then add: 12 + 8 = 20.
recs.rel: In arithmetic, multiplication is done before addition (BODMAS).

recs.q: How many columns does a matrix of order 5x4 have?
recs.facts: A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns. For 5x4 there are 5 rows and 4 columns.
recs.rel: The total number of elements in a 5x4 matrix is 20.

recs.q: If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 8th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 8th to the 28th is 20 days, and 20 = 2 weeks + 6 days. Going back 6 days from Monday gives Tuesday.
recs.rel: Going back 6 days is the same as going forward 1 day in a week cycle.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Aam-ul-Wafood (Year of Delegations)?
recs.facts: Delegations from many Arab tribes came to Madina to accept Islam in 9 AH, after the conquest of Makkah. This year is called Aam-ul-Wafood.
recs.rel: The year 9 AH is also when the Battle of Tabuk took place.

recs.q: What is the meaning (synonym) of abolish?
recs.facts: To abolish a law or system means to formally put an end to it, which is to do away with it.
recs.rel: Annul, scrap and repeal are other synonyms of abolish.

recs.q: Who was the first among slaves to accept Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Textbooks list Abu Bakr among men, Khadija among women, Ali among children and Zaid bin Haritha among freed slaves as the first to accept Islam.
recs.rel: Some sources name Hazrat Bilal (RA) as the first slave to accept Islam, so sources differ.

recs.q: How many acute angles are there in an acute triangle?
recs.facts: In an acute triangle all three angles are less than 90 degrees, so all three are acute.
recs.rel: A right triangle has two acute angles and an obtuse triangle has two acute angles as well.

recs.q: When was the Indian Independence Act passed?
recs.facts: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947 and created the two dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.
recs.rel: It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

recs.q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of ADHERE?
recs.facts: Adhere means to stick to something, so its opposite is detach, meaning to separate or loosen.
recs.rel: Adhesive is a substance that makes things adhere to each other.

recs.q: What does an adjective describe or explain?
recs.facts: An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun by telling its quality, quantity or kind, as in a tall boy.
recs.rel: An adverb, in contrast, modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.

recs.q: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Durand Line was fixed in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and the Afghan ruler Amir Abdur Rahman Khan, and it forms the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Radcliffe Line separates Pakistan and India, and the McMahon Line is between India and China.

recs.q: Point out the odd one out: America, Africa, Asia, Euro.
recs.facts: America, Africa and Asia are continents, while Euro is the currency of many European countries.
recs.rel: The word Europe, not Euro, is the name of the continent.

recs.q: What is the (executive) capital of South Africa?
recs.facts: Pretoria is the administrative (executive) capital of South Africa. The country has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
recs.rel: Cape Town is the legislative capital and Bloemfontein is the judicial capital.

recs.q: Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ahmed is 9?
recs.facts: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ahmed becomes 9 after 6 years, so she will be 9 + 6 = 15 years.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 6 years).

recs.q: Who is the current President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026?
recs.facts: PML-N's Dr Najeeb Naqi was elected and sworn in as the 25th President of AJK on 24 September 2026 for a five-year term.
recs.rel: His predecessor Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry died on 31 January 2026, and acting presidents served until the new election.

recs.q: Which letter comes next after O in the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The alphabet runs ... M, N, O, P, Q, so P comes right after O.
recs.rel: N comes just before O.

recs.q: Which letter comes first in alphabetical order in the word MANAGEMENT?
recs.facts: The letters of MANAGEMENT are M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. Arranged alphabetically they begin with A, so A comes first.
recs.rel: Arranged fully, the word becomes A A E E G M M N N T.

recs.q: After arranging the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order, which letter is the third from the last?
recs.facts: MANAGEMENT has the letters M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. In alphabetical order: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. Counting from the end: T (1st), N (2nd), N (3rd), so the third letter from the last is N.
recs.rel: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters: A, E, M and N appear twice each.

recs.q: What is the national mammal of the United States of America?
recs.facts: The American bison was declared the national mammal of the USA in 2016.
recs.rel: The bald eagle is the national bird and emblem of the USA, which many people loosely call its national animal.

recs.q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 20 balloons. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balloons did Ahmad keep?
recs.facts: Let Ahmad keep x balloons, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20 and x = 5.
recs.rel: Amjad therefore kept 15 balloons, and 15 is three times 5.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of anarchy?
recs.facts: Anarchy means a state of disorder due to the absence of authority, which is the same as lawlessness.
recs.rel: The opposite of anarchy is order or good government.

recs.q: Which Sahabi was appointed by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as governor of Yemen?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor, judge and teacher of the people.
recs.rel: Before he left, the Prophet (PBUH) asked him how he would judge, and he replied that he would use the Quran, then the Sunnah, then his own reasoning.

recs.q: Which of the following is another name of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Furqan, meaning the criterion that separates right from wrong, is one of the names of the Holy Quran.
recs.rel: Other names of the Quran are Al-Kitab, Al-Dhikr and Al-Noor; Zabur, Injeel and Tauraat are other revealed books.

recs.q: What is the antonym of excrete?
recs.facts: To excrete is to get rid of waste matter from the body, so the opposite is to absorb or retain.
recs.rel: Kidneys excrete urea from the human body.

recs.q: What is the antonym of prohibited?
recs.facts: Prohibited means not permitted, so its opposite is allowed.
recs.rel: Forbidden, banned and barred are synonyms of prohibited.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of applaud?
recs.facts: To applaud is to show approval, which means the same as to praise.
recs.rel: The opposite of applaud is to criticize or condemn.

recs.q: What is the approximate total area of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan covers about 796,095 square kilometres, the 33rd largest country by area.
recs.rel: Balochistan is the largest province, covering about 44 percent of the country.

recs.q: Around which body does the Earth revolve?
recs.facts: The Earth orbits the Sun, completing one revolution in about 365.25 days.
recs.rel: The Moon revolves around the Earth, not the Sun directly.

recs.q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares Islam as the State religion?
recs.facts: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Article 1 names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

recs.q: In which part of Asia is India located?
recs.facts: India lies in South Asia, forming most of the Indian subcontinent.
recs.rel: SAARC was formed in 1985 by the countries of South Asia.

recs.q: Aslam was 28 years old in 1945. How old will he be in 1965?
recs.facts: From 1945 to 1965 is 20 years, so his age is 28 + 20 = 48.
recs.rel: Age problems come down to adding the difference in years.

recs.q: What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
recs.facts: Alphabetical order is A D E E G M N T U, so the third letter is E.
recs.rel: AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E appearing twice.

recs.q: Sahih Bukhari is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book?
recs.facts: Muslims regard the Holy Quran as the most authentic book, followed in authenticity by Sahih Bukhari among the hadith books.
recs.rel: Imam Bukhari compiled his collection over about 16 years.

recs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH (632 AD) at the age of 63 years.
recs.rel: He passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in Madina.

recs.q: In the coordinate plane, the y-axis is the
recs.facts: The y-axis is the vertical number line of the plane, and the y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
recs.rel: The x-axis and y-axis meet at the origin (0, 0).

recs.q: In the coordinate plane, the x-axis is the
recs.facts: The x-axis is the horizontal number line of the plane, and the x-coordinate is called the abscissa.
recs.rel: The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants.

recs.q: Against whom was the War of Independence of 1857 (Jang-e-Azadi) fought by the people of the subcontinent?
recs.facts: The 1857 revolt was an uprising of Indian soldiers and people against British East India Company rule.
recs.rel: The British called it the Mutiny, while Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent call it the War of Independence.

recs.q: Who is the author of the famous book Hujjatullah-il-Baligha?
recs.facts: Hujjatullah-il-Baligha is a famous work on Islamic wisdom by Shah Waliullah Muhaddith Dehlvi.
recs.rel: Shah Waliullah also translated the Quran into Persian.

recs.q: Ali and Ahmed have 25 balls in all. If Ali has 4 times as many as Ahmed, how many balls does Ahmed have?
recs.facts: Let Ahmed have x. Then x + 4x = 25, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.
recs.rel: Ali then has 20 balls.

recs.q: Who is the Governor of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
recs.facts: Jaffar Khan Mandokhail is serving as Governor of Balochistan in 2026.
recs.rel: Sarfraz Bugti is the Chief Minister, not the Governor.

recs.q: Which barrage is commonly described as the biggest and the first barrage of Pakistan on the Indus?
recs.facts: Sukkur Barrage, opened in 1932, is the one Pakistani textbooks name as the first and biggest barrage on the Indus.
recs.rel: Sources differ on size; Guddu and Taunsa are other large barrages on the Indus.

recs.q: What is the area of a triangle with base 3 cm and height 6 cm?
recs.facts: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 3 x 6 = 9 square cm.
recs.rel: Candidates often forget the half and give 18, which is the area of the rectangle.

recs.q: On which document is the Constitution of Pakistan based?
recs.facts: The Objectives Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles and was made a preamble and later a substantive part (Article 2A) of the Constitution.
recs.rel: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly.

recs.q: Pakistan's economy is predominantly based on which sector?
recs.facts: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy, supporting a large share of employment and exports like textiles from cotton.
recs.rel: Services now form the largest share of GDP, but agriculture remains the traditional base.

recs.q: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
recs.facts: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526, which started the Mughal Empire in India.
recs.rel: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556 and the Third in 1761.

recs.q: Where is the Bay of Riga located?
recs.facts: The Gulf (Bay) of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea lying between Latvia and Estonia.
recs.rel: The city of Riga, the capital of Latvia, stands on this bay.

recs.q: Where is the Bay of Siam located?
recs.facts: The Bay of Siam is an old name for the Gulf of Thailand, an arm of the South China Sea.
recs.rel: Siam was the former name of Thailand.

recs.q: Choose the correct statement about air at higher altitude.
opts: Air becomes lighter (thinner) as we go upward
Air becomes heavier as we go upward
Air density does not change with height
recs.facts: Atmospheric pressure and density decrease with height, so air becomes thinner and lighter as we go up.
recs.rel: This is why mountaineers use oxygen cylinders at great heights.

recs.q: To which religion did Rana Bhagwan Das belong?
recs.facts: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu who served as a judge of the Supreme Court and as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.
recs.rel: He was the first non-Muslim to serve as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which type of brick was used in the buildings of the Indus Valley Civilization?
recs.facts: Cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were built with uniform baked clay bricks, usually in a ratio of about 1:2:4.
recs.rel: Baked bricks made the drainage and the Great Bath waterproof and durable.

recs.q: What name did the British give to the War of Independence of 1857?
recs.facts: The British called the events of 1857 the Sepoy Mutiny (or Indian Mutiny) because it began with Indian soldiers in the Company army.
recs.rel: Muslims and Indian nationalists call it the War of Independence.

recs.q: Change the first word into a pronoun: Sana broke her pen.
recs.facts: Sana is a female name, so the pronoun that replaces it is She.
recs.rel: A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun.

recs.q: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the rule of which dynasty?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Walid bin Abdul Malik. The Mughals came centuries later.
recs.rel: Hajjaj bin Yusuf was the Umayyad governor of Iraq who sent him.

recs.q: The Panama Canal separates which two continents?
recs.facts: The Panama Canal cuts through the Isthmus of Panama, dividing North America from South America. It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
recs.rel: The canal opened in 1914.

recs.q: What is the capital of the country Georgia?
recs.facts: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus. Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia.
recs.rel: Yerevan is the capital of Armenia.

recs.q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
recs.facts: Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela.
recs.rel: Bogota is the capital of Colombia.

recs.q: On which date was the Indian pilot Abhinandan Varthaman captured in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Wing Commander Abhinandan's aircraft was shot down on 27 February 2019, a day after the Balakot air strike. He was returned to India on 1 March 2019.
recs.rel: The Pakistan Air Force shot down two Indian aircraft that day.

recs.q: In which year was CENTO (Central Treaty Organization, formerly the Baghdad Pact) established?
recs.facts: The Baghdad Pact was signed in 1955 and was renamed CENTO in 1959 after Iraq withdrew.
recs.rel: Pakistan was a member of both CENTO and SEATO.

recs.q: Through which point does the line x = 6y pass?
recs.facts: Putting x = 0 and y = 0 gives 0 = 0, so the line satisfies the equation at the origin. The same is true for y = 5x.
recs.rel: Any line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.

recs.q: Which device converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy?
recs.facts: A battery or electric cell uses chemical reactions to produce an electric current.
recs.rel: A generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy, and a solar panel converts light energy.

recs.q: Who was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army (1949)?
recs.facts: General Kodandera Madappa Cariappa took over as Commander-in-Chief from the British officer Sir Francis Butcher on 15 January 1949.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the phrase first army chief, since the British general Rob Lockhart briefly led the army after 1947; most textbooks give Cariappa.

recs.q: The Chauri Chaura incident of 1922 took place during which movement?
recs.facts: On 4 February 1922 a mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura and killed policemen, so Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.
recs.rel: Chauri Chaura is in Uttar Pradesh, India.

recs.q: What is 5 o'clock in the afternoon in 24-hour time?
recs.facts: For afternoon hours add 12: 5 + 12 = 17, so 5 PM is 1700 hours.
recs.rel: Military time uses the 24-hour clock from 0000 to 2359.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'immense'?
recs.facts: Immense means extremely large or great.
recs.rel: Its opposite is tiny or minute.

recs.q: What does the word 'cohesion' mean?
opts: Act of sticking together as a united whole
recs.facts: Cohesion is the state of sticking together or forming a united whole, as in a cohesive group.
recs.rel: The opposite of cohesion is disunity or disintegration.

recs.q: What is the transpose of a column matrix?
recs.facts: Transposing a matrix swaps its rows and columns. A column matrix of order n x 1 becomes a matrix of order 1 x n, which is a row matrix.
recs.rel: The transpose of a row matrix is a column matrix.

recs.q: What was the Simon Commission?
opts: A British commission sent to India in 1927 to review the Government of India Act 1919, with no Indian member
A commission for partition of Bengal
A Muslim League committee for Pakistan
A commission for dividing Punjab in 1947
recs.facts: The Simon Commission, led by Sir John Simon, arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform. It had only British members, so Indian parties boycotted it.
recs.rel: It was announced in November 1927 and its slogan of protest was Simon Go Back.

recs.q: In which city was the East India Company established?
recs.facts: The East India Company was formed in London and received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I.
recs.rel: Its first Indian trading post was set up at Surat in 1612.

recs.q: In which year was the East India Company first established?
recs.facts: The English East India Company received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
recs.rel: The Company won control of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: If he had called me, I ___ come.
recs.facts: This is the third conditional (if + past perfect), which needs would have + past participle in the main clause.
recs.rel: Past unreal conditions use 'if + had + past participle', then 'would have + past participle'.

recs.q: What kind of number is a - ib (where a and b are real and b is not zero)?
recs.facts: A number written in the form a + ib with real a and b is a complex number; a - ib is its conjugate, which is also complex.
recs.rel: A complex number has a real part and an imaginary part.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'composite'?
recs.facts: Composite means made up of several parts, and its opposite is simple, made of a single part.
recs.rel: In number theory the opposite of a composite number is a prime number.

recs.q: Which are the two largest continents of the world by area?
recs.facts: Asia is the largest continent and Africa is the second largest by area.
recs.rel: Asia is also the most populous continent.

recs.q: Which organization controls and develops Pakistan's water and electric power system?
recs.facts: WAPDA (Water and Power Development Authority) develops the country's water and hydropower resources.
recs.rel: IRSA, in contrast, distributes river water among the provinces.

recs.q: What is cos(-x) equal to?
recs.facts: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.
recs.rel: Sine is an odd function: sin(-x) = -sin x.

recs.q: What is sec x multiplied by cos x equal to?
recs.facts: Sec x = 1/cos x, so sec x . cos x = 1.
recs.rel: Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.

recs.q: What is cosec x multiplied by tan x equal to?
recs.facts: Cosec x . tan x = (1/sin x)(sin x/cos x) = 1/cos x = sec x.
recs.rel: Tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice located?
recs.facts: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.
recs.rel: It is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word crude?
recs.facts: Crude means raw or unrefined, so its opposite is refined, meaning processed or polished.
recs.rel: In manners, the opposite of crude is cultured or polite.

recs.q: On which date is Pakistan Day celebrated?
recs.facts: Pakistan Day is celebrated on 23 March to mark the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution of 1940.
recs.rel: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.

recs.q: Where is the deepest hole (borehole) drilled by humans in the world?
recs.facts: The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia reached about 12,262 metres in 1989.
recs.rel: It is deeper than the Mariana Trench is deep, which is about 10,935 metres.

recs.q: Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's surface?
recs.facts: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the western Pacific is the deepest known point, at about 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level.
recs.rel: Mount Everest, the highest point, would be covered by more than 2 km of water if placed in the Challenger Deep.

recs.q: What does the word 'delight' mean?
recs.facts: Delight means great pleasure or joy; as a verb it means to please greatly.
recs.rel: A synonym of delight is joy, and an antonym is sorrow.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Cholistan Desert located?
recs.facts: The Cholistan Desert lies in southern Punjab, near Bahawalpur.
recs.rel: It is locally called Rohi and is an extension of the Thar Desert.

recs.q: Which of the following is a desert of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Cholistan in Punjab is a desert of Pakistan, along with Thar, Thal and Kharan.
recs.rel: Gobi is in Asia (Mongolia and China), and Sahara and Kalahari are in Africa.

recs.q: In a diagonal matrix, if all the non-zero diagonal elements are equal, what is the matrix called?
recs.facts: A diagonal matrix with equal diagonal entries is called a scalar matrix.
recs.rel: A scalar matrix whose diagonal entries are all 1 is the identity matrix.

recs.q: In which year (CE) did the mother of the Holy Prophet (SAW) pass away?
recs.facts: The Prophet (SAW) was born in 570 CE and his mother died when he was about six, around 577 CE.
recs.rel: The exact year is given slightly differently in some sources.

recs.q: Which district of Pakistan has the largest population according to the census?
recs.facts: Lahore district had about 11.1 million people in 2017 and about 13.0 million in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.
recs.rel: Karachi is larger as a whole city, but it is divided into seven separate districts.

recs.q: Dog is to bitch as horse is to what?
recs.facts: A bitch is the female dog; the female horse is a mare.
recs.rel: A male horse is called a stallion and a young horse a foal.

recs.q: According to a hadith, how many good deeds (nekis) are earned by reciting one letter of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) said a good deed is rewarded tenfold, so one letter of the Quran earns ten good deeds.
recs.rel: This hadith is narrated in Sunan al-Tirmidhi.

recs.q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
recs.facts: ECO members are Pakistan, Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Saudi Arabia is not among them.
recs.rel: ECO has ten members and its secretariat is in Tehran.

recs.q: What is the meaning (synonym) of the word 'ecstasy'?
recs.facts: Ecstasy is a state of intense happiness or delight. Rapture is a close synonym.
recs.rel: The adjective form is ecstatic, meaning extremely happy.

recs.q: Where was Abdul Sattar Edhi born?
recs.facts: Edhi was born in 1928 in Bantva in Gujarat, British India, and migrated to Pakistan after Partition.
recs.rel: His family belonged to the Memon community.

recs.q: In whose government were the non-party based elections held in Pakistan in 1985?
recs.facts: General Zia-ul-Haq held non-party elections in February 1985. Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after them.
recs.rel: The 1985 assemblies passed the Eighth Amendment.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word 'embellish'?
recs.facts: To embellish is to make something more attractive by adding decoration. Its opposite is to disfigure or spoil.
recs.rel: Embellish can also mean to add exaggerated details to a story.

recs.q: What is the synonym of 'enigmatic'?
recs.facts: Enigmatic describes something puzzling and hard to understand, which is mysterious.
recs.rel: The noun enigma means a puzzle or riddle.

recs.q: In whose era was the Battle of Yamama fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Yamama was fought in 11-12 AH against the false prophet Musaylima during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
recs.rel: Many Huffaz died there, which led to the first compilation of the Quran.

recs.q: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belongs to the descendants of which prophet?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) descended from Hazrat Ismail (AS), son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), through the Quraysh.
recs.rel: Hazrat Essa (AS) had no father and no direct descendants.

recs.q: On what date did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Chagai hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998 (five tests, Chagai-I), followed by one more on 30 May 1998. This was a reply to India's tests earlier that month.
recs.rel: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

recs.q: How many Nobel Prizes in Physics has Pakistan received so far?
recs.facts: Dr Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. No other Pakistani has won in Physics.
recs.rel: Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate and Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

recs.q: Who started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal?
recs.facts: Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal in the early 19th century to make Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz) of Islam and give up un-Islamic customs.
recs.rel: After him, his son Dudu Miyan led the movement.

recs.q: How many farz (obligatory acts) does Namaz have according to the Hanafi school?
recs.facts: Namaz has 13 farz: 6 outside the prayer (conditions such as cleanliness, covering the body, facing the Qibla, time and intention) and 7 inside it (such as takbeer, qiyam, qira'at, ruku, sajdah, qa'da akhira).
recs.rel: Wajibat of Namaz are different from farz, and leaving a farz makes the prayer invalid.

recs.q: On which date of Ramadan was Makkah conquered (Fath-e-Makkah) in 8 AH?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 CE) for the conquest of Makkah, when the Muslims entered the city peacefully.
recs.rel: Some sources give other dates in Ramadan such as 10 or 17.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
recs.facts: The father of Quaid-e-Azam was Jinnahbhai Poonja, a merchant in Karachi. His mother was Mithibai.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.

recs.q: Who is the Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) of Pakistan, according to the latest available reports?
recs.facts: Rashid Mahmood Langrial was appointed FBR Chairman in August 2024 and the latest reports found show him still in office.
recs.rel: He succeeded Amjad Zubair Tiwana, who resigned in July 2024; the FBR chairmanship changes often, so check the latest news.

recs.q: A man walks a few steps towards the north, then turns right and walks, and then turns right again. In which direction is he now going?
recs.facts: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east; a second right turn makes him face south.
recs.rel: Two consecutive right turns always reverse the original direction.

recs.q: If 3x - 9 = 2x + 7, find x.
recs.facts: Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 9 = 7, so x = 16.

recs.q: Who was the founder of the USSR (Soviet Union)?
recs.facts: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and headed the new state when the USSR was formally created in 1922.
recs.rel: Joseph Stalin ruled the USSR after Lenin's death in 1924.

recs.q: What kind of fraction is 9/3?
recs.facts: In 9/3 the numerator 9 is larger than the denominator 3, so it is an improper fraction. It simplifies to the whole number 3.
recs.rel: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, such as 5/7.

recs.q: A plane uses 160 gallons of fuel to cover 330 nautical miles. About how many gallons will it use to cover 700 nautical miles?
recs.facts: Fuel per mile is 160 divided by 330, and 700 times 160 divided by 330 is 112000 divided by 330, which is about 339.4 gallons.
recs.rel: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance when the rate is constant.

recs.q: Robert E. Lee was a famous general of which war?
recs.facts: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army of Northern Virginia in the American Civil War (1861-1865). His main opponent on the Union side was Ulysses S. Grant.
recs.rel: Lee surrendered to Grant at Appomattox Court House in April 1865.

recs.q: What was the gift given to the Muslims on the night of Miraj?
recs.facts: On the night of Miraj, Allah made five daily prayers obligatory for the Muslims. The number was reduced from fifty to five.
recs.rel: Salah is often called the gift of Miraj.

recs.q: A brother is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when the brother is 12?
recs.facts: The sister is 3 x 5 = 15 years old now. The brother becomes 12 after 7 years, so the sister will be 15 + 7 = 22.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

recs.q: Who was the first Governor of the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) after the creation of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sir George Cunningham was appointed Governor of NWFP in August 1947 at the creation of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Cunningham also served as governor before independence, in 1937-1946.

recs.q: Who was the first Governor of Punjab after the creation of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sir Francis Mudie was the first Governor of West Punjab in 1947.
recs.rel: He served until 1949 and was succeeded by Sir Abdur Rab Nishtar.

recs.q: What was the name of the paternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Prophet's father was Abdullah, and Abdullah's father was Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal grandfather.
recs.rel: Abdul Muttalib was the son of Hashim and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.

recs.q: In which province does the Green Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system run?
recs.facts: The Green Line BRT runs in Karachi, which is the capital of Sindh province.
recs.rel: The Peshawar BRT (Zu Peshawar) is the equivalent system in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

recs.q: What is the HCF of 12 and 28?
recs.facts: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 28 = 2 x 2 x 7. The common part is 2 x 2 = 4.
recs.rel: The LCM of 12 and 28 is 84.

recs.q: Bait ul Mamoor is located in which heaven?
recs.facts: In the narration of the Miraj, the Prophet (PBUH) saw Bait ul Mamoor in the seventh heaven.
recs.rel: Seventy thousand angels enter it each day and never return to it again.

recs.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
recs.facts: The word hexagon comes from the Greek hex meaning six, so it has six sides.
recs.rel: The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is 720 degrees.

recs.q: For how many years did the Prophet (PBUH) preach Islam in Makkah before the Hijrat to Madina?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and migrated at 53, so he preached in Makkah for about 13 years.
recs.rel: He then lived about 10 years in Madina.

recs.q: In which month of the Hijri calendar was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed (6 AH)?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) set out for Umrah in Dhul Qadah 6 AH and the treaty was signed with Quraysh at Hudaibiya in that month.
recs.rel: The treaty set a ten-year truce and Muslims performed Umrah the following year.

recs.q: What is the multiplicative identity of a complex number, written as an ordered pair?
recs.facts: The complex number 1 + 0i is written (1, 0), and (a, b) times (1, 0) = (a, b) for every complex number.
recs.rel: The additive identity is (0, 0).

recs.q: Who wrote the book 'Culture and Imperialism'?
recs.facts: Culture and Imperialism (1993) was written by the Palestinian-American scholar Edward Said.
recs.rel: Said is also famous for his book Orientalism (1978).

recs.q: In which country did the first Industrial Revolution begin?
recs.facts: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in the second half of the 18th century, with steam power and mechanised textile production.
recs.rel: James Watt's improved steam engine (1769 patent) was a key invention of this revolution.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: Smoking is injurious ___ health.
recs.facts: The adjective injurious is followed by the preposition to, so the correct phrase is injurious to health.
recs.rel: The same pattern is used in harmful to, and detrimental to.

recs.q: According to the Holy Quran and hadith, killing one innocent person is equal to what?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul is as if he had killed all of mankind.
recs.rel: The same verse says that saving one life is as if one had saved all of mankind.

recs.q: Is the number 5/7 rational or irrational?
recs.facts: A rational number can be written as p/q with integers p and q and q not zero. 5/7 has this form, so it is rational.
recs.rel: The square root of 2 and pi are famous irrational numbers.

recs.q: Is 22/7 a rational or an irrational number?
opts: Irrational, because it is close to pi
Rational, because it is a ratio of two integers
recs.facts: 22/7 is a fraction of two integers, so it is rational. It is only an approximation of pi, which is irrational.
recs.rel: 22/7 is about 3.142857 while pi is about 3.141593.

recs.q: Where is Jabal Arafat (Jabal-e-Rahmat), the hill where pilgrims stand on 9 Dhul Hijjah?
opts: Near Makkah, in the plain of Arafat
recs.facts: Jabal Arafat, also called Jabal-e-Rahmat, stands in the plain of Arafat about 20 km southeast of Makkah.
recs.rel: Standing at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah is the most important rite (rukn) of Hajj.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: He said, "I have done my job."
opts: It was said by him that his job had been done by him.
It was said by him that he had done his job.
His job was done by him.
It is said by him that I have done my job.
recs.facts: In indirect passive form the statement becomes: It was said by him that his job had been done by him.
recs.rel: In reported speech, the present perfect changes to the past perfect after a past tense reporting verb.

recs.q: Change the narration: He says, "I did not care about my job."
opts: He says that he had not cared about his job.
He said that he did not care about his job.
He says that he did not care about his job.
He says that I did not care about my job.
recs.facts: The reporting verb says is in the present tense, so the tense of the reported speech does not change; only the pronouns change.
recs.rel: If the reporting verb were past (said), the verb inside would shift back to the past perfect.

recs.q: Which one is different from the others: chimpanzee, ape, baboon, kangaroo, monkey?
recs.facts: Chimpanzee, ape, baboon and monkey are all primates, while the kangaroo is a marsupial.
recs.rel: Kangaroos are native to Australia and carry their young in a pouch.

recs.q: The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: The Karakoram Highway runs from Hasan Abdal in Pakistan to Kashgar in China through the Khunjerab Pass.
recs.rel: The Khunjerab Pass, at about 4693 metres, is the highest paved border crossing in the world.

recs.q: Which of these is another name for the Karakoram Highway?
recs.facts: The Karakoram Highway is also called the Pakistan-China Friendship Highway and is numbered N-35.
recs.rel: It is sometimes called the Eighth Wonder of the World because of the difficulty of building it.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the karez system of irrigation mainly used?
recs.facts: A karez is an underground channel that carries water from a hillside, and it is widely used in dry Balochistan.
recs.rel: Karez is also known as qanat in Iran and is used across Central Asia.

recs.q: Who described Kashmir as the jugular vein of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The statement is credited to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, who stressed the strategic importance of Kashmir.
recs.rel: Pakistan marks Kashmir Solidarity Day on 5 February each year.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word justify?
recs.facts: To justify means to defend as right, and the opposite is to condemn or blame.
recs.rel: Another opposite of justify is to criticise.

recs.q: In which year AD was the Battle (Ghazwa) of Khyber fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khyber took place in 7 AH, which corresponds to 628 AD. It ended with the conquest of the Jewish fortresses of Khyber.
recs.rel: Some sources place the exact month between spring and mid 628 AD, but the year 628 AD (7 AH) is agreed.

recs.q: Foot is to knee as hand is to what?
recs.facts: The knee is the main joint of the leg above the foot, and the elbow is the main joint of the arm above the hand. So hand is to elbow.
recs.rel: The elbow joins the upper arm to the forearm.

recs.q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) fought against the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: The Makkan army at Uhud numbered about 3000 men, while the Muslims were about 1000 at the start and about 700 after 300 hypocrites withdrew.
recs.rel: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH.

recs.q: What is the capital of Sri Lanka as commonly given in textbooks?
recs.facts: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka and the usual textbook answer.
recs.rel: The official legislative capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, near Colombo.

recs.q: Which is the hottest layer of the Earth's atmosphere?
recs.facts: In the thermosphere, absorption of solar radiation can heat the thin air to over 1,000 degrees Celsius.
recs.rel: The mesosphere above the stratosphere is the coldest layer.

recs.q: What is the process by which water vapour is lost from the leaves of a plant?
recs.facts: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through the stomata of leaves.
recs.rel: It helps pull water up the plant and cools the leaves.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to LENIENT?
recs.facts: Lenient means merciful or not strict, so tolerant is the closest.
recs.rel: The opposite of lenient is strict or harsh.

recs.q: Which mountain range lies between Pakistan and China?
recs.facts: The Karakoram range along the north of Pakistan forms its border with China, crossed by the Karakoram Highway.
recs.rel: K2 lies in the Karakoram.

recs.q: Which pillar of Islam was made obligatory on the Prophet (PBUH) during the Mairaj?
recs.facts: Five daily prayers were gifted to the Muslims on the night of Mairaj, after being reduced from fifty.
recs.rel: The journey from Makkah to Bait-ul-Muqaddas is called Isra and the ascension to the heavens is called Mairaj.

recs.q: Which party won a majority of seats in East Pakistan in the 1970 general elections?
recs.facts: The Awami League led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 of the 162 East Pakistan seats.
recs.rel: The Pakistan People's Party won the most seats in West Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the capital of Malaysia?
recs.facts: Kuala Lumpur is the capital and largest city of Malaysia.
recs.rel: Putrajaya is the administrative capital where government offices are located.

recs.q: In a class of 30 students, 24 are male. What is the percentage of females?
recs.facts: Females = 30 - 24 = 6. Percentage = 6/30 x 100 = 20%.
recs.rel: Males are 80% of this class.

recs.q: What is the height of Mangla Dam (commonly quoted)?
recs.facts: Mangla Dam is about 147 metres (482 feet) high according to commonly cited figures.
recs.rel: Some sources give slightly different heights, as the dam was raised in the 2000s.

recs.q: What is the mean of -5 and -5?
recs.rel: The mean of identical numbers equals that number.

recs.q: What is the mean of 1, 4, 5, 6?
recs.rel: Mean is the sum of values divided by their count.

recs.q: What is the migration of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madina called?
recs.facts: The migration from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD is called Hijrat (Hijrah). The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar was introduced in the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).

recs.q: What is the total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the total fell to 336 seats. These are 266 general, 60 women and 10 minority seats.
recs.rel: Before this change the National Assembly had 342 seats.

recs.q: Who is the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional from Pakistan?
recs.facts: Arfa Karim Randhawa became a Microsoft Certified Professional at the age of nine in 2004. She was the youngest in the world at that time.
recs.rel: She died in 2012 and the Arfa Karim Software Technology Park in Lahore is named after her.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age to become a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 62 requires a candidate for the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old. A voter must be 18.
recs.rel: Candidates for the Senate must be at least 30 years old.

recs.q: Which planet has the largest moon in the Solar System?
recs.facts: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the Solar System. It is even bigger than the planet Mercury.
recs.rel: Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is second in size.

recs.q: Who was the first man to land on the Moon?
recs.facts: Neil Armstrong of the Apollo 11 mission stepped on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
recs.rel: Buzz Aldrin followed him, while Michael Collins stayed in orbit.

recs.q: Which pronoun is most suitable for the word mom?
recs.facts: Mom is a female parent, so the feminine subject pronoun she is used.
recs.rel: Her is the object form and herself is the reflexive form.

recs.q: What is the motto given by the Quaid-e-Azam to the nation?
recs.facts: The Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto Unity, Faith, Discipline (Ittehad, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam, Nazm). This is the order used in his speeches and in Pakistani textbooks.
recs.rel: In Urdu the motto is often written as Ittehad, Tanzeem, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam; some books change the order, but Unity, Faith, Discipline is the standard English form.

recs.q: How many companions are called the Ashra Mubashra?
recs.facts: Ashra Mubashra are ten Companions who were given the glad tidings of Paradise in their lifetime.
recs.rel: They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.

recs.q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.001?
recs.facts: The inverse of a number is 1 divided by it. 1 / 0.001 = 1000.
recs.rel: A number times its multiplicative inverse equals 1.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book Indian Musalmans (1871)?
recs.facts: Indian Musalmans: Are They Bound in Conscience to Rebel Against the Queen? was written by Sir William Wilson Hunter.
recs.rel: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and others wrote replies to Hunter's book.

recs.q: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Holy Quran mentions the names of 25 prophets.
recs.rel: The commonly quoted total number of prophets is 124,000, though the Quran does not state it.

recs.q: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am sorry."
opts: She said that she is sorry.
She said that she was sorry.
She said that I was sorry.
She said that she had been sorry.
recs.facts: In indirect speech after a past reporting verb the present tense changes to past, and the pronoun I changes to she, so am becomes was.
recs.rel: Quotation marks and the comma are dropped and that is added in indirect speech.

recs.q: How many nautical miles is the territorial sea of Pakistan under the UN Law of the Sea?
