recs.facts: Under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, a country's territorial sea extends 12 nautical miles from its coast, and Pakistan claims this limit.
recs.rel: Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone extends 200 nautical miles.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of the Netherlands as of 2026?
recs.facts: Rob Jetten of the D66 party became Prime Minister on 23 February 2026, succeeding Dick Schoof.
recs.rel: Mark Rutte, who was PM in 2022, later became the Secretary General of NATO in 2024.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: O, K, H, F, ?
recs.facts: The positions are 15, 11, 8, 6. The gaps are 4, 3, 2, so the next gap is 1 and 6 - 1 = 5, which is E.
recs.rel: The gaps decrease by 1 each time.

recs.q: How many nights did the Prophet (PBUH) spend in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three nights before going on to Madina.
recs.rel: The Cave of Thawr is near Makkah, on the way to Madina.

recs.q: Which type of noun is Islamabad?
recs.facts: A proper noun is the name of a particular person, place or thing. Islamabad is the name of one specific city, so it is a proper noun and it is written with a capital letter.
recs.rel: A common noun such as city names any one of a class.

recs.q: An obtuse angle measures more than 90 degrees and less than how many degrees?
recs.facts: An obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees (a right angle) but less than 180 degrees (a straight angle).
recs.rel: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees, and an angle of exactly 180 degrees is called a straight angle.

recs.q: What was the official name of the country under the 1962 constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1962 constitution named the country the Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The word Islamic was added back in 1963 by the First Amendment, and the 1973 constitution uses Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

recs.q: Ali is older than Waqas, and Usman is younger than Waqas. Who is the oldest of the three?
recs.facts: Ali is older than Waqas and Waqas is older than Usman, so the order from oldest is Ali, Waqas, Usman.
recs.rel: Such questions are solved by arranging the names in a single line of order.

recs.q: Which is generally considered the oldest civilization of the world?
recs.facts: The Mesopotamian (Sumerian) civilization, which arose between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers around 3500 BC, is usually regarded as the oldest.
recs.rel: The Indus Valley civilization of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa flourished around 2500 BC.

recs.q: What is the currency of Oman?
recs.facts: The official currency of Oman is the Omani rial.
recs.rel: The Omani rial is one of the highest-valued currencies in the world.

recs.q: What is meant by the order of a matrix?
opts: Number of rows by number of columns
recs.facts: The order of a matrix is stated as rows x columns, for example a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns is of order 2 x 3.
recs.rel: The order is also called the size or dimension of the matrix.

recs.q: Which of the following is a principal organ of the United Nations?
recs.facts: The six principal organs of the UN are the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council, International Court of Justice and the Secretariat. The others listed are agencies or funds.
recs.rel: The International Court of Justice sits at The Hague and is the only principal organ not based in New York.

recs.q: Out of 15000 students, 12000 are present. What is the percentage of students present?
recs.rel: The percentage absent is 100 - 80 = 20%, which is 3000 students.

recs.q: Mark Zuckerberg is the founder and head of which company?
recs.facts: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the chairman and CEO of its parent company, Meta Platforms.
recs.rel: Facebook Inc. renamed itself Meta Platforms in October 2021; the company also owns Instagram and WhatsApp.

recs.q: 6 is what percent of 20?
recs.facts: Percentage = 6/20 x 100 = 30%.
recs.rel: Similarly, 30% of 20 is 6.

recs.q: With what is Tayammum performed when water is not available?
recs.facts: Tayammum is performed by striking the hands on clean earth, dust or sand and wiping the face and the arms.
recs.rel: Tayammum is permitted when water is not available or its use would harm health.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word PERPETUAL?
recs.facts: Perpetual means never ending or continuing forever, which matches everlasting.
recs.rel: Its antonym is temporary or transient.

recs.q: What is the study of geometrical shapes in a plane called?
recs.facts: Plane geometry (Euclidean geometry) studies two-dimensional shapes such as lines, triangles and circles.
recs.rel: Solid geometry deals with three-dimensional figures.

recs.q: Between whom was the Battle of Plassey (1757) fought?
opts: The British East India Company and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal
recs.facts: At Plassey the East India Company force under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
recs.rel: The battle laid the foundation of British rule in India.

recs.q: Through which point does the line y = 5x pass?
recs.facts: Putting x = 0 gives y = 5 times 0 = 0, so the line passes through (0, 0). The other points do not satisfy y = 5x.
recs.rel: Any line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.

recs.q: Who is the co-chairperson of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)?
recs.facts: Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the PPP.
recs.rel: He is also the President of Pakistan, serving his second term since March 2024.

recs.q: Choose the correct preposition: My father died ___ the war.
recs.facts: We say died in a war, because the war is the event during which he died.
recs.rel: We say died of an illness but died in an accident or war.

recs.q: Who is the head of state of Jordan?
recs.facts: Jordan is a monarchy and King Abdullah II is its head of state, so it has no president.
recs.rel: King Abdullah II has ruled since 1999 after the death of his father King Hussein.

recs.q: What is the probability of a sure (certain) event?
recs.facts: A sure event is one that is certain to happen, so its probability is 1. Probability always lies between 0 and 1.
recs.rel: An impossible event has probability 0.

recs.q: Is 2x^2 + 3x + 2 a quadratic expression?
recs.facts: The highest power of x is 2, with a non-zero coefficient 2, so it has the form ax^2 + bx + c of a quadratic.
recs.rel: Its discriminant 9 - 16 = -7 is negative, so it has no real roots.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 90?
recs.facts: 1/3 of 90 is 30. A quarter of 30 is 30 divided by 4, which equals 7.5.
recs.rel: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 90 divided by 12.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word Rabb?
recs.facts: Rabb means Lord, Sustainer and Nourisher, the One who brings up and provides for all creation. It is used in the Quran for Allah, as in Rabbul Alameen.
recs.rel: Rabbul Alameen, meaning Lord of all the worlds, appears in Surah Al-Fatiha.

recs.q: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary between which two countries?
recs.facts: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to divide Punjab and Bengal between India and Pakistan. It is the border between Pakistan and India.
recs.rel: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

recs.q: Which angel is appointed by Allah to bring rain?
recs.facts: Hazrat Mikael (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and sustenance. This is the commonly taught view in Islamic books.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jibril (AS) brought revelation, and Hazrat Israfil (AS) will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgment.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 - 9i?
recs.facts: In a + bi form, the real part is the term without i. Here it is 6.
recs.rel: The conjugate of 6 - 9i is 6 + 9i.

recs.q: What was the real name of Iblis (Shaitan) before he was cursed?
recs.facts: Iblis is said in many Islamic traditions to have been called Azazil before he refused to bow to Adam (AS). He was a jinn and was cursed for his pride.
recs.rel: Some narrations give his earlier name as Harith, so sources differ.

recs.q: What is a decimal number that neither terminates nor repeats called?
recs.facts: A non-terminating, non-recurring decimal cannot be written as a fraction p over q. Such a number is called irrational.
recs.rel: Pi and the square root of 2 are common irrational numbers.

recs.q: A decimal in which one or more digits repeat endlessly in the same pattern is called:
recs.facts: In a recurring decimal, a digit or a block of digits repeats forever, such as 0.333... or 0.142857142857... Such numbers are rational.
recs.rel: 1 divided by 3 gives 0.333..., a recurring decimal.

recs.q: What did the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919) introduce in the provinces?
recs.facts: The 1919 reforms divided provincial subjects into transferred (under elected ministers) and reserved (under the Governor). This system was called dyarchy.
recs.rel: Dyarchy was ended by the Government of India Act 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy.

recs.q: Between which two regions does the Rann of Kutch lie?
recs.facts: The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh in the Thar desert area on the border between Sindh in Pakistan and Gujarat in India. A border dispute there was settled by tribunal in 1968.
recs.rel: The 1965 war began with clashes in the Rann of Kutch in April 1965.

recs.q: According to the Quran, which religion is accepted by Allah?
recs.facts: The Quran states that the religion with Allah is Islam (Surah Al-Imran 3:19). It also says no other religion will be accepted from anyone.
recs.rel: The Quran was completed with the verse declaring Islam as the chosen religion (Surah Al-Maidah 5:3).

recs.q: Nankana Sahib is a famous holy site of which religion?
recs.facts: Nankana Sahib is the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism. It is in Punjab, Pakistan.
recs.rel: Guru Nanak was born there in 1469.

recs.q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to whose challenge?
recs.facts: Lord Birkenhead, the Secretary of State for India, challenged Indian leaders to draft a constitution acceptable to all communities. The Nehru Report was the Congress-led answer to that challenge.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam rejected the Nehru Report and presented his Fourteen Points in 1929.

recs.q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution states that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Article 2 declares Islam to be the State religion of Pakistan.

recs.q: In which constitution of Pakistan was the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan first used?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution changed the name to the Republic of Pakistan, and the 1973 Constitution restored Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which country has the largest official gold reserves in the world?
recs.facts: The United States holds about 8,133 tonnes of official gold reserves, roughly double that of second-placed Germany.
recs.rel: Germany is second with about 3,350 tonnes, followed by Italy and France.

recs.q: In which city did the tribes of Aus and Khazraj reside?
recs.facts: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later called Madina. They became the Ansar after welcoming the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The two tribes had long been at war before Islam united them.

recs.q: On which date was the Pakistan Resolution (Lahore Resolution) presented?
recs.facts: The resolution was presented on 23 March 1940 at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League, having been moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and passed on 24 March.
recs.rel: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day.

recs.q: According to the commonly given order of revelation, which Surah was the third to be revealed?
recs.facts: The usual order is Al-Alaq first, Al-Qalam second and Al-Muzzammil third.
recs.rel: Sources differ; some lists place Al-Muddaththir ahead of Al-Muzzammil.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word reward?
recs.facts: A reward is something given in return for good work or conduct, that is, a recompense.
recs.rel: The opposite of reward is punishment.

recs.q: Which word is the synonym of rich?
recs.facts: Rich means having a great deal of money, and wealthy has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Affluent is also a synonym of rich.

recs.q: Which river is the largest in the world by volume of water discharged?
recs.facts: The Amazon carries the greatest volume of water of any river in the world.
recs.rel: The length of the Nile and the Amazon is disputed, so some sources name the Nile as longest.

recs.q: The name Punjab means the land of how many rivers?
recs.facts: Punjab is from the Persian words punj (five) and ab (water), meaning five rivers: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
recs.rel: Of these, the Beas and Sutlej are mainly in India after the Indus Waters Treaty.

recs.q: The Reshmi Romal (Silk Letter) Tehreek was started by Maulana Mahmud Hasan and which colleague?
recs.facts: The Silk Letter Movement of about 1913 to 1920 was organised by Shaikhul Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan with Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi.
recs.rel: Letters were written on silk cloth to communicate with allies abroad against British rule.

recs.q: What is the square root of 196?
recs.facts: 14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.
recs.rel: 196 is a perfect square, being 14 squared.

recs.q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 7?
recs.facts: 2.6 x 2.6 = 6.76 and 2.7 x 2.7 = 7.29, so the root lies between them; 2.65 x 2.65 = 7.02 so it is about 2.65.
recs.rel: The square root of 7 is an irrational number, about 2.6458.

recs.q: How many roots does a quadratic equation have?
recs.facts: A quadratic equation has degree 2, and an equation of degree n has n roots. So it has 2 roots, which may be real or complex.
recs.rel: A quadratic equation has the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0.

recs.q: In which battle were about 70 Sahaba martyred?
recs.facts: About 70 Sahaba were martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 Hijri.
recs.rel: Only 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr.

recs.q: In which year did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
recs.facts: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak theory.
recs.rel: He was the first Pakistani and first Muslim from Pakistan to win a Nobel Prize.

recs.q: Which of the following countries is a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) as of 2026?
recs.facts: Iran became a full member in 2023 and Belarus in 2024, bringing the SCO to ten full members. Turkey is only a dialogue partner, while Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.
recs.rel: The ten full members are China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran and Belarus.

recs.q: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside of its body (on the surface of the skin)?
recs.facts: The tiny seed-like dots on a strawberry are actually separate fruits (achenes) on the outer surface, each containing a seed. The other fruits keep their seeds inside.
recs.rel: The fleshy red part of a strawberry is the swollen receptacle of the flower rather than a true fruit.

recs.q: Who elects the President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
opts: An Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies
recs.facts: Under Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution the President is elected by an Electoral College made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.
recs.rel: The President serves a five-year term.

recs.q: What is the measure of an angle inscribed in a semicircle?
recs.facts: By Thales' theorem, an angle inscribed in a semicircle subtends the diameter and is always a right angle, 90 degrees.
recs.rel: The central angle on a diameter is 180 degrees, which is exactly double the inscribed angle.

recs.q: Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in the Muslim proposals of the 1920s?
recs.facts: Jinnah included the separation of Sindh from Bombay in the Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 and again in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
recs.rel: Sindh was actually separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936 and became a separate province.

recs.q: For what is the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) best known?
opts: A treaty with the Jews of Madinah
recs.facts: In the Last Sermon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared the equality of all people, the sanctity of life, property and honour, the rights of women and the abolition of interest and old blood feuds. It is therefore regarded as the first great charter of human rights.
recs.rel: The Last Sermon was delivered in the 10th year of Hijrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

recs.q: Where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver the Last Sermon?
opts: In the valley of Uranah on the plain of Arafat
recs.facts: During the Farewell Hajj the Holy Prophet (PBUH) addressed more than one hundred thousand Muslims on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah in the valley of Uranah at Arafat.
recs.rel: Part of the sermon was also given at Mina on the days after Arafat.

recs.q: Choose the correct preposition: She shouted ____ him.
recs.facts: The verb shout takes at when it means to speak angrily to someone, so the correct sentence is She shouted at him.
recs.rel: Shout to someone means to call out so that the person can hear you, with no anger.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'Siraat' (as in Siraat-e-Mustaqeem)?
recs.facts: 'Siraat' is an Arabic word meaning a path or way. In Surah Al-Fatiha, Siraat-e-Mustaqeem means the straight path.
recs.rel: The Siraat on the Day of Judgement is also described as a bridge over Hell that everyone must cross.

recs.q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will the age of his sister be when Adil is 15 years old?
recs.facts: The sister is now 3 x 5 = 15 years old. Adil needs 15 - 5 = 10 more years, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

recs.q: Where is Gwadar situated?
opts: On the Makran coast of Balochistan
On the coast of Sindh near Karachi
recs.facts: Gwadar is a port city on the Arabian Sea coast of the Makran region in Balochistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.

recs.q: In which country did the Black Lives Matter slogan and movement first start?
recs.facts: The hashtag and movement began in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
recs.rel: It spread worldwide in 2020 after the death of George Floyd.

recs.q: Who sold the Kashmir valley and to whom?
opts: The British East India Company to Gulab Singh Dogra
recs.facts: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh, the Dogra ruler of Jammu.
recs.rel: Gulab Singh became the first Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

recs.q: What is the trivial solution of a homogeneous system of linear equations in three unknowns x, y and z?
recs.facts: In a homogeneous system every right-hand side is 0, so putting every unknown equal to 0 always satisfies it. This is called the trivial solution (0, 0, 0).
recs.rel: A homogeneous system always has at least the trivial solution, so it is never inconsistent.

recs.q: Solve the proportion 8 : 4 :: X : 16. What is X?
recs.rel: The ratio 8 : 4 simplifies to 2 : 1.

recs.q: Solve for x: 4x - 1 = x + 2
recs.facts: Subtract x from both sides: 3x - 1 = 2. Add 1: 3x = 3, so x = 1.

recs.q: Ahsan Ramzan, who became the youngest world champion in 2022, is a player of which sport?
recs.facts: Ahsan Ramzan of Lahore won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in Doha in 2022 at the age of 16. He became the youngest ever winner.
recs.rel: He beat Iran's Amir Sarkosh in that final.

recs.q: Tiananmen Square is situated in which city?
recs.facts: Tiananmen Square lies in the centre of Beijing, the capital of China. It is named after the Gate of Heavenly Peace.
recs.rel: It is one of the largest public squares in the world.

recs.q: In which city was the first television station of Pakistan set up?
recs.facts: Pakistan Television started its first broadcast from Lahore on 26 November 1964. It was a pilot station.
recs.rel: Karachi and Dhaka stations followed in 1966.

recs.q: Marvi, the famous folk tale, belongs to which province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Umar Marvi is one of the seven famous folk heroines of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai's Sindhi poetry. The story belongs to Sindh.
recs.rel: Marvi was a village girl of Tharparkar who refused the offers of the ruler Umar Soomro.

recs.q: How many Muslim soldiers marched in the army for the Ghazwa of Tabuk?
recs.facts: The Prophet (SAW) led about 30,000 Muslim fighters to Tabuk in 9 AH. It was the largest Muslim army up to that time.
recs.rel: The campaign is also called the Army of Hardship (Jaish-ul-Usrah).

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'subversion'?
recs.facts: Subversion means weakening an authority, so its opposite is supporting or upholding it. Support is the best opposite among the options.
recs.rel: Subversion usually refers to secret acts against a government.

recs.q: After which event did Hazrat Abu Sufyan (RA) accept Islam?
recs.facts: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the time of the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH.
recs.rel: Before this he had led the Quraysh in several battles against the Muslims.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did Abu Sufyan accept Islam?
recs.facts: Abu Sufyan embraced Islam on the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, which took place in 8 AH.
recs.rel: Some candidates remember 6 AH, but the Conquest of Makkah was in 8 AH.

recs.q: Which surah is known as Arus-ul-Quran (the Bride of the Quran)?
recs.facts: Surah Ar-Rahman is called the Bride of the Quran because of its beauty and its repeated refrain.
recs.rel: Surah Yaseen is called the heart of the Quran.

recs.q: How many surahs of the Holy Quran are named after prophets, according to the commonly given list?
recs.facts: The commonly counted ones are Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Nuh and Muhammad, giving six.
recs.rel: Counts differ between sources depending on which names are included.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "evidence"?
recs.facts: Evidence is the facts or signs that show something is true, which is proof.
recs.rel: The adjective evident means obvious.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "negotiate"?
recs.facts: To negotiate is to discuss terms in order to reach agreement, which is to bargain.
recs.rel: A negotiator mediates between parties.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "replenish"?
recs.facts: To replenish is to fill up again, which is to refill.
recs.rel: Its antonym is deplete.

recs.q: Who is the President of Syria as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Ahmed al-Sharaa became president of the Syrian transitional government in January 2025 after Bashar al-Assad was overthrown in December 2024.
recs.rel: Bashar al-Assad was president from 2000 until December 2024, and the post of prime minister was abolished in March 2025.

recs.q: What is the other name of the Ghazwa of Tabuk?
recs.facts: Tabuk is also called Ghazwat al-Usrah, the Army of Hardship, because of the heat, distance and shortage of supplies.
recs.rel: It is the last expedition led by the Prophet (SAW) himself.

recs.q: A man travels towards the north and then turns to his left. In which direction is he now facing?
recs.facts: Facing north, a left turn points to the west.
recs.rel: A right turn from north would point to the east.

recs.q: Talha is moving towards the north and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now?
recs.facts: Facing north, a right turn points him towards the east.
recs.rel: A left turn from north would point him to the west.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'tame' (or 'tamed')?
recs.facts: To tame means to make an animal gentle and used to humans, so tame or tamed means domesticated.
recs.rel: Its antonym is wild.

recs.q: Ali is ten years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali is 20 years old, what will be his sister's age?
recs.facts: The sister is 20 when Ali is 10, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 20, she is 20 + 10 = 30.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: What is one third of one tenth of 120?
recs.facts: One tenth of 120 is 12 and one third of 12 is 4.
recs.rel: The order of taking fractions does not change the result: 120 x 1/3 x 1/10 is also 4.

recs.q: In set theory, what does the letter Z denote?
recs.facts: Z stands for the set of integers, that is, all positive and negative whole numbers and zero (from the German word Zahlen).
recs.rel: N is natural numbers, Q is rational numbers and R is real numbers.

recs.q: Which pronoun is used for a thing?
recs.facts: 'It' is the singular pronoun used for things and animals; he and she are for persons.
recs.rel: 'They' or 'them' are plural pronouns.

recs.q: What was the real (birth) name of Tipu Sultan?
recs.facts: Tipu Sultan was born as Sultan Fateh Ali Khan Tipu, son of Haider Ali of Mysore.
recs.rel: He was known as the Tiger of Mysore.

recs.q: Zun-Noon is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Zun-Noon means the one of the fish and is the title of Hazrat Yunus (AS).
recs.rel: He was swallowed by a fish and prayed Laa ilaha illa anta subhanaka.

recs.q: If today is Friday, what day will it be after 12 days?
recs.facts: 12 days is 1 week plus 5 days, and 5 days after Friday is Wednesday.
recs.rel: The week has 7 days, so only the remainder after dividing by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: The 2nd is Friday, so the 3rd is Saturday and the 4th is Sunday. The day after tomorrow means the 4th.
recs.rel: Day after tomorrow means two days after today.

recs.q: Xinjiang, a province of China, touches which side of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Xinjiang borders Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan across the Karakoram.
recs.rel: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with Xinjiang.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 15th of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the day is 4 days after Tuesday, which is Saturday.
recs.rel: Counting the difference in dates and taking the remainder after dividing by 7 solves every such day question.

recs.q: Umar's age is 4 years and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when Umar is 11 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 now, so she is 8 years older than Umar. When Umar is 11, she is 11 + 8 = 19.
recs.rel: After 7 years both ages increase by 7, so 12 + 7 = 19.

recs.q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Ukraine?
recs.facts: Serhii Koretskyi, formerly head of Naftogaz, was confirmed as Prime Minister by the Verkhovna Rada on 16 July 2026.
recs.rel: Yulia Svyrydenko served as Prime Minister from July 2025 before him, and Denys Shmyhal before her.

recs.q: Who was the first President of Ukraine?
recs.facts: Leonid Kravchuk became the first President of independent Ukraine in December 1991 after the Soviet Union broke up.
recs.rel: He served until 1994, when Leonid Kuchma succeeded him.

recs.q: Bakar is older than Ali and Umair is younger than Ali. Which statement is correct?
recs.facts: Bakar is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Umair, so the order is Bakar, Ali, Umair. Bakar is the oldest and Umair the youngest.
recs.rel: Such questions are solved by arranging the names in a line from oldest to youngest.

recs.q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hamza (RA), called Asadullah (Lion of Allah), was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
recs.rel: He is also known as Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, the chief of the martyrs.

recs.q: What is a matrix whose number of rows is not equal to its number of columns called?
recs.facts: A matrix with unequal numbers of rows and columns (m x n with m not equal to n) is a rectangular matrix.
recs.rel: If rows and columns are equal, it is a square matrix.

recs.q: In which city is the International Islamic University (IIUI) located?
recs.facts: The International Islamic University is in Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
recs.rel: It was established in 1980 and given its present status in 1985.

recs.q: Who lives and works in the White House in Washington, D.C.?
recs.facts: The White House is the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States.
recs.rel: The White House has been the residence of every US President since John Adams in 1800.

recs.q: Al-Lat and Al-Uzza were names of what in pre-Islamic Arabia?
recs.facts: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat were the three chief idols worshipped by the Arabs before Islam.
recs.rel: Al-Lat was worshipped at Taif and Al-Uzza near Makkah; Manat was worshipped near Madinah.

recs.q: If x = (1/3) y and y = 9, what is the value of x?
recs.facts: Substitute y = 9: x = (1/3) x 9 = 3.
recs.rel: Multiplying by 1/3 is the same as dividing by 3.

recs.q: How many vowels are in ASGJIOYTBUF?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, I, O and U, so there are 4. Y is counted as a consonant here.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
recs.facts: The WTO has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
recs.rel: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, replacing GATT.

recs.q: By what other name is Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) known?
recs.facts: Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, meaning servant of Allah, and his descendants are the Bani Israel.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS).

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'zenith' (also its synonym)?
recs.facts: Zenith means the highest point, peak or summit of something.
recs.rel: In astronomy the zenith is the point in the sky directly above the observer.

recs.q: If x = 9y + 1 and y = 1/3, what is x?
recs.rel: Always do multiplication before addition.

recs.q: What is 25% of 75?
recs.facts: 25% is one quarter: 75 / 4 = 18.75.

recs.q: What is 25% of 80?
recs.facts: 25% is one quarter: 80 / 4 = 20.
recs.rel: 25% equals 1/4.

recs.q: What is 70% of 80?
recs.rel: 70% of 80 equals 80% of 70.

recs.q: What is 120 multiplied by 7?
recs.rel: Multiplying by 7 is the same as multiplying by 10 and subtracting three times the number.

recs.q: What is 30% of 1/10 of 120?
recs.facts: One tenth of 120 is 12. Then 30% of 12 = 0.3 x 12 = 3.6.
recs.rel: Candidates sometimes remembered 3, but the exact answer is 3.6.

recs.q: If Monday is the 12th day of a month, what day will be the 1st of that month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 12th is 11 days, and 11 = 7 + 4. So the 1st is 4 days before Monday, which is Thursday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what days are the 12th and the 14th?
recs.facts: The 12th is 10 days after the 2nd, and 10 = 7 + 3, so it is Sunday + 3 = Wednesday. The 14th is 12 days after, 12 = 7 + 5, so Sunday + 5 = Friday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 12th of that month?
recs.facts: The 12th is 11 days after the 1st, and 11 = 7 + 4. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 13th of that month?
recs.facts: The 13th is 9 days after the 4th, and 9 = 7 + 2. Monday + 2 days = Wednesday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 13th of that month?
recs.facts: The 13th is 11 days after the 2nd, and 11 = 7 + 4. Monday + 4 days = Friday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 14th day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 25th of that month?
recs.facts: The 25th is 11 days after the 14th, and 11 = 7 + 4. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 15th day of a month is Friday, what day was the 4th of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days, and 11 = 7 + 4. So the 4th is 4 days before Friday, which is Monday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 15th of that month?
recs.facts: The 15th is 14 days after the 1st, which is exactly two weeks, so it is also a Friday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

recs.q: What is sin(180 - x) equal to?
recs.facts: Angles 180 - x and x lie on the same horizontal level of the unit circle, so they have the same sine: sin(180 - x) = sin x.
recs.rel: In the same way, cos(180 - x) = -cos x.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939?
recs.facts: Neville Chamberlain was Prime Minister from 1937 to May 1940 and declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.
recs.rel: The UK has no president; Winston Churchill replaced Chamberlain in May 1940, and Boris Johnson (named by a candidate) was PM only in 2019 to 2022.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 19th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Sunday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 20th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 20th is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Friday, which is Sunday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 21st be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 days is 2 full weeks plus 6 day(s), so the day is 6 day(s) after Sunday, which is Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 5th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 21st be?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 21st is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 23rd is 20 days. 20 days is 2 full weeks plus 6 day(s), so the day is 6 day(s) after Friday, which is Thursday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 days is 2 full weeks plus 5 day(s), so the day is 5 day(s) after Friday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 12th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 26th be?
recs.facts: From the 12th to the 26th is 14 days. 14 days is 2 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) after Friday, which is Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 27th is 23 days. 23 days is 3 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 27th be?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 27th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 28th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 28th is 25 days. 25 days is 3 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 28th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 28th is 24 days. 24 days is 3 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 29th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 4th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th back to the 29th is 25 days. 25 days is 3 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) before Tuesday, which is Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 29th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 29th is 26 days. 26 days is 3 full weeks plus 5 day(s), so the day is 5 day(s) after Friday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: If the 6th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 29th be?
recs.facts: From the 6th to the 29th is 23 days. 23 days is 3 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

recs.q: Which form of government was in force in Pakistan during the 1971 war?
opts: Martial law (military government under Yahya Khan)
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan had taken over in March 1969 and imposed martial law, so Pakistan was under military rule in 1971. Power passed to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in December 1971.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan, who ruled before Yahya Khan, had resigned in March 1969.

recs.q: A village had 1600 people in 2000, and its population doubles every five years. What was its population in 1980?
recs.facts: From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings, so the population in 2000 is 16 times that of 1980. Hence 1600 divided by 16 gives 100.
recs.rel: Going back in time with doubling growth means halving the number once for every period.

recs.q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct in total in May 1998?
recs.facts: Pakistan conducted five tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I) and one more on 30 May 1998 (Chagai-II), a total of six. Some sources mention only the five of 28 May.
recs.rel: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-weapon state and the first in the Muslim world.

recs.q: Which war took place between Pakistan and India in 1999?
recs.facts: The Kargil War was fought in the Kargil sector of Kashmir between May and July 1999.
recs.rel: The Lahore Declaration had been signed earlier in 1999 between Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 200 are absent. What percentage of students is present?
recs.facts: Present students are 1500 minus 200, which is 1300. Then 1300 divided by 1500 times 100 gives 86.67 percent.
recs.rel: Percentage equals part divided by whole times 100.

recs.q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2019?
recs.facts: According to UNHCR, Turkey hosted about 3.6 million refugees in 2019, mostly Syrians, which was the highest in the world.
recs.rel: In 2023 and 2024 Iran overtook Turkey as the largest refugee-hosting country.

recs.q: Which number comes next in the series 115, 55, 170, 65, 225, ?
recs.facts: There are two series mixed together. The odd places 115, 170, 225 rise by 55 each time, and the even places 55, 65, next rise by 10, so the next term is 75.
recs.rel: Alternating series are solved by separating the odd and even positions.

recs.q: Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution, Pakistan's second constitution, in 1969?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza abrogated the first constitution (1956) in October 1958.

recs.q: Which is the second longest river in the world according to common textbooks?
recs.facts: The Nile is usually named first at about 6650 km and the Amazon, flowing mainly through Brazil, second at about 6400 km.
recs.rel: Sources differ: some recent measurements make the Amazon longer than the Nile, though the Amazon is the largest river by volume.

recs.q: What is 4 x 3 + 2 x 3?
recs.facts: Multiply first: 4 x 3 is 12 and 2 x 3 is 6. Then 12 plus 6 gives 18.
recs.rel: In BODMAS, multiplication is done before addition.

recs.q: In a class of 1200 students, 300 are absent. What percentage of students is present?
recs.facts: Present students are 1200 minus 300, which is 900. Then 900 divided by 1200 times 100 gives 75 percent.
recs.rel: Absent percentage here is 25, and present plus absent always make 100 percent.

recs.q: In a class of 500 students, 320 are present. What percentage of students is absent?
recs.facts: Absent students are 500 minus 320, which is 180. Then 180 divided by 500 times 100 gives 36 percent.
recs.rel: Present students here are 64 percent.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 360 are boys. What percentage of the students is girls?
recs.facts: Girls are 1500 minus 360, which is 1140. Then 1140 divided by 1500 times 100 gives 76 percent.
recs.rel: Boys here are 24 percent.

recs.q: In a class of 400 students, 360 are boys. What percentage of the students is girls?
recs.facts: Girls are 400 minus 360, which is 40. Then 40 divided by 400 times 100 gives 10 percent.
recs.rel: Boys here are 90 percent.

recs.q: Who was the 3rd Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The order of Pakistan's early prime ministers was Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Muhammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Muhammad Ali and H. S. Suhrawardy. So the third was Muhammad Ali Bogra.
recs.rel: Muhammad Ali Bogra took office in April 1953 after Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed.

recs.q: Who was the 5th Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The first five prime ministers were Liaquat Ali Khan, Nazimuddin, Bogra, Chaudhry Muhammad Ali and then H. S. Suhrawardy. Fazal Elahi Chaudhry was a President, not a Prime Minister.
recs.rel: Suhrawardy served from September 1956 to October 1957 and was followed by I. I. Chundrigar.

recs.q: What is 4 + 4x4?
recs.facts: Multiplication comes first: 4x4 = 16. Then 4 + 16 = 20.
recs.rel: Following BODMAS, 4 + 4x4 is not (4 + 4)x4 which would be 32.

recs.q: What is one-fourth of 10% of 120?
recs.rel: One-fourth of 120 itself is 30.

recs.q: What is the transpose of a matrix of order 4x3?
recs.facts: The transpose swaps rows and columns, so a 4x3 matrix becomes a 3x4 matrix.
recs.rel: The transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives back the original matrix.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 8th day be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 8th is 6 days. Friday plus 6 days is Thursday.
recs.rel: Six days after any day equals one day before it.

recs.q: In a school of 3000 students, 2700 are present. What percentage of students are absent?
recs.rel: Present students are 90% of the total.

recs.q: By which title is Hazrat Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) well known?
recs.facts: Abdullah ibn Abbas was a great scholar of Quranic interpretation, so he is called Tarjuman-ul-Quran (interpreter of the Quran). He is also called Hibr-ul-Ummah.
recs.rel: Saifullah is the title of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA).

recs.q: Who was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abbas (RA) in relation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: He was the son of Hazrat Abbas (RA), the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), so he was the Prophet's cousin.
recs.rel: He was born about three years before the Hijrat.

recs.q: Who was Hazrat Halima Sadia (RA) in relation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Halima Sadia of Banu Saad nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert, so she was his foster mother.
recs.rel: The Prophet's real mother was Hazrat Amina.

recs.q: In which year was the 1962 constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan took over after Ayub Khan resigned and abrogated the 1962 constitution in March 1969 by imposing martial law.
recs.rel: The 1962 constitution had been introduced by Ayub Khan.

recs.q: Insert the correct form of the verb: Lightning ____ across the bridge last night.
recs.facts: The words last night show past time, so the simple past tense flashed is needed.
recs.rel: The past participle of flash is also flashed.

recs.q: Change to active voice: Why was the thief seen by Ali?
opts: Why did Ali see the thief?
Why had Ali seen the thief?
Why was Ali seeing the thief?
recs.facts: The past simple passive was seen becomes did ... see in the active, with Ali as the subject and the thief as the object.
recs.rel: In the active voice the doer of the action is the subject of the sentence.

recs.q: On what date did Allama Iqbal deliver his Allahabad Address?
recs.facts: The Allahabad session of the All India Muslim League was held in December 1930 and Iqbal delivered his address on 29 December 1930.
recs.rel: The idea of a separate Muslim state he gave there led to the Pakistan Resolution of 1940.

recs.q: What is the antonym of accept?
recs.facts: To accept means to receive or agree to something, and its opposite is to reject or refuse.
recs.rel: Decline and refuse are also antonyms of accept.

recs.q: Adnan is 12 years old and his sister is 2 times his age. What will be the age of the sister after 8 years?
recs.facts: The sister's age now is 2 x 12 = 24 years. After 8 years she will be 24 + 8 = 32 years.
recs.rel: Age problems are solved by first finding present ages and then adding the years that pass.

recs.q: FSB is the intelligence agency of which country?
recs.facts: The FSB (Federal Security Service) is the main security and counter-intelligence agency of the Russian Federation. It replaced the Soviet-era KGB's domestic functions.
recs.rel: The foreign intelligence agency of Russia is the SVR.

recs.q: MI5 is the security agency of which country?
recs.facts: MI5, the Security Service, is the domestic counter-intelligence and security agency of the United Kingdom.
recs.rel: MI6 (the Secret Intelligence Service) handles British foreign intelligence.

recs.q: MOIS is the intelligence agency of which country?
recs.facts: MOIS is the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran, also known as VAJA.
recs.rel: Pakistan's main intelligence agency is the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).

recs.q: Faiq and Ahmad were born in 1970 and 1977 respectively. What are their ages in 1999?
recs.facts: Faiq: 1999 - 1970 = 29 years. Ahmad: 1999 - 1977 = 22 years.
recs.rel: Age equals the given year minus the birth year.

recs.q: Which is the national airline of Russia?
recs.facts: Aeroflot is the flag carrier and largest airline of Russia, based in Moscow.
recs.rel: Lufthansa is from Germany and Emirates from the UAE.

recs.q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani of PML-N was elected the 17th Prime Minister of AJK on 28 August 2026 after the July-August 2026 elections.
recs.rel: Faisal Mumtaz Rathore was the previous prime minister before the 2026 elections.

recs.q: Who was the President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir before Dr Najeeb Naqi?
recs.facts: Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry was President of AJK from 2021 until his death on 31 January 2026. Acting presidents served until Dr Najeeb Naqi took oath in September 2026.
recs.rel: Chaudhry Latif Akbar acted as president for part of that interim period.

recs.q: Who was the first President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
recs.facts: Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan became the first President of Azad Kashmir in October 1947 after the Poonch uprising.
recs.rel: He served four non-consecutive terms and is called Ghazi-e-Millat.

recs.q: Akbar is older than Zarnab, and Ali is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
recs.facts: Ali is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Zarnab, so the order from oldest is Ali, Akbar, Zarnab. Zarnab is the youngest.
recs.rel: Ranking questions are solved by placing the names in a single line from oldest to youngest.

recs.q: Akram is 3 times as old as Zahra, whose age is 4 years. What will be Akram's age after 22 years?
recs.facts: Akram's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. After 22 years he will be 12 + 22 = 34 years.
recs.rel: Always find the present age first, then add the number of years.

recs.q: The expression 3y - 2x + 3 is an algebraic what?
recs.facts: It has variables, constants and operations but no equals sign, so it is an algebraic expression, not an equation.
recs.rel: This expression has three terms: 3y, -2x and 3.

recs.q: Who is Ali Sadpara?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Sadpara was a famous Pakistani high-altitude mountaineer from Skardu who climbed eight-thousanders such as Nanga Parbat in winter.
recs.rel: He went missing on K2 in February 2021 during a winter attempt.

recs.q: In the sentence 'Aliya is going to school', what part of speech is the word Aliya?
recs.facts: Aliya is the name of a person, so it is a proper noun.
recs.rel: A pronoun such as she would replace the name Aliya in the sentence.

recs.q: Khalil-ullah is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalil-ullah, meaning friend of Allah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Musa (AS) is Kaleem-ullah and Hazrat Isa (AS) is Ruh-ullah.

recs.q: On what date was Allama Muhammad Iqbal born?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal was born in Sialkot on 9 November 1877.
recs.rel: He died in Lahore on 21 April 1938.

recs.q: What is the position of the letter O in the English alphabet?
recs.facts: Counting A=1 to O gives A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, so O is the 15th letter.
recs.rel: The 26 letters have 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U.

recs.q: In which country does the world's largest volunteer ambulance service operate?
recs.facts: The Edhi Foundation of Pakistan runs the largest volunteer ambulance network in the world, recognised by Guinness World Records.
recs.rel: The Edhi Foundation was founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi, known as the Angel of Mercy.

recs.q: Boxer Amir Khan, a former world champion, belongs to which country?
recs.facts: Amir Khan was born in Bolton, England, and represented Great Britain; he is of Pakistani descent.
recs.rel: He won an Olympic silver medal in 2004 at Athens.

recs.q: Which word is the antonym of anarchy?
recs.facts: Anarchy means a state of disorder and absence of government, so its opposite is order.
recs.rel: Chaos, disorder and lawlessness are synonyms of anarchy.

recs.q: How many interior angles does a square have?
recs.facts: A square is a quadrilateral with four corners, so it has four angles, each of 90 degrees.
recs.rel: The four angles of a square add up to 360 degrees.

recs.q: Which is the largest animal in the world?
recs.facts: The blue whale grows up to about 30 metres in length and weighs up to nearly 200 tonnes, bigger than any other animal.
recs.rel: The African elephant is the largest living land animal.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah announce his 14 Points?
recs.facts: Jinnah presented his 14 Points in March 1929 in Delhi as a reply to the Nehru Report.
recs.rel: The 14 Points set out the minimum constitutional demands of the Muslims of India.

recs.q: On which date was the plan for the partition and independence of India announced?
recs.facts: Lord Mountbatten announced the Partition Plan, known as the 3 June Plan, on 3 June 1947.
recs.rel: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947.

recs.q: What is the solution of the equation 3x - 7 = -x + 9?
recs.facts: Move x terms to the left: 3x + x = 9 + 7, so 4x = 16 and x = 4.
recs.rel: Check: 3(4) - 7 = 5 and -4 + 9 = 5, so both sides are equal.

recs.q: What is the antonym of perfect?
recs.facts: Perfect means without any fault, so the opposite is faulty or imperfect.
recs.rel: Flawless, ideal and exact are synonyms of perfect.

recs.q: What is the antonym of abuse?
recs.facts: Abuse means to treat badly or insult, so its opposite is to respect or treat well.
recs.rel: Mistreat, insult and harm are close in meaning to abuse.

recs.q: What is the antonym of arbitrary?
recs.facts: Arbitrary means based on random choice rather than reason, so its opposite is reasoned.
recs.rel: Random and whimsical are synonyms of arbitrary.

recs.q: What is the antonym of blunt?
recs.facts: Blunt means not sharp or having no fine edge, so the opposite is sharp.
recs.rel: Blunt can also mean frank and outspoken in speech.

recs.q: What is the antonym of callousness?
recs.facts: Callousness is cruel lack of feeling for others, and its opposite is compassion.
recs.rel: Callous is an adjective and comes from the Latin word for hard skin.

recs.q: What is the antonym of elated?
recs.facts: Elated means very happy and proud, and its opposite is depressed or downcast.
recs.rel: Joyful, excited and cheerful are close in meaning to elated.

recs.q: What is the antonym of error?
recs.facts: An error is a mistake, so the opposite is accuracy or correctness.
recs.rel: Mistake, fault and blunder are synonyms of error.

recs.q: What is the antonym of evident?
recs.facts: Evident means clearly seen or understood, so its opposite is obscure or unclear.
recs.rel: Obvious, clear and plain are synonyms of evident.

recs.q: What is the antonym of frugal?
recs.facts: Frugal means careful in spending money, and its opposite is extravagant or wasteful.
recs.rel: Thrifty, careful and economical are synonyms of frugal.

recs.q: What is the antonym of imminent?
recs.facts: Imminent means about to happen soon, so its opposite is remote or distant.
recs.rel: Do not confuse imminent with eminent, which means famous.

recs.q: What is the antonym of liberal?
recs.facts: Liberal means open to new ideas and tolerant of others, so its opposite is conservative or narrow-minded.
recs.rel: Liberal can also mean generous in giving.

recs.q: What is the antonym of magnanimous?
recs.facts: Magnanimous means generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival, so its opposite is petty or mean-spirited.
recs.rel: Selfish is also given as an opposite in some word lists.

recs.q: What is the antonym of wail?
recs.facts: To wail is to cry loudly in grief, so the opposite is to rejoice.
recs.rel: Cry, lament and weep are close in meaning to wail.

recs.q: Where is Masjid Aqsa located?
recs.facts: Masjid Aqsa stands in the old city of Jerusalem in Palestine.
recs.rel: It was the first qibla of the Muslims and is the third holiest mosque in Islam.

recs.q: The Rann of Kutch is a marshy region lying between Sindh (Pakistan) and which Indian state?
recs.facts: The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh between the Sindh province of Pakistan and the Indian state of Gujarat.
recs.rel: A 1965 border dispute over the Rann was settled by an international tribunal in 1968.

recs.q: If 6 is the arithmetic mean between 4 and B, what is the value of B?
recs.facts: Mean = (4 + B) / 2 = 6, so 4 + B = 12 and B = 8.
recs.rel: The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.

recs.q: What is the arithmetic mean of 18 and 36?
recs.rel: The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by their number.

recs.q: What is the arithmetic mean of (y + 3) and (y - 2)?
recs.facts: Sum = (y + 3) + (y - 2) = 2y + 1; dividing by 2 gives y + 0.5.
recs.rel: Check with y = 1: the numbers are 4 and -1, whose mean is 1.5, which equals 1 + 0.5.

recs.q: Boxing is called the noble art of what?
recs.facts: Boxing has long been called the noble art of self-defence.
recs.rel: Modern boxing rules are based on the Marquess of Queensberry rules of 1867.

recs.q: In which year was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated on 27 December 2007 in Rawalpindi after an election rally.
recs.rel: She was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim country.

recs.q: Who promulgates ordinances in Pakistan when the National Assembly is not in session?
recs.facts: Under Article 89 of the Constitution, the President may promulgate an ordinance when Parliament is not in session.
recs.rel: An ordinance must be laid before Parliament and lapses after 120 days unless extended or approved.

recs.q: What is the currency of Australia?
recs.facts: Australia uses the Australian dollar (AUD).
recs.rel: Australia used the Australian pound until decimal currency was introduced in 1966.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Australia (as of 2026)?
recs.facts: Anthony Albanese of the Labor Party has been Prime Minister since May 2022.
recs.rel: His predecessor Scott Morrison served from 2018 to 2022.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book In the Line of Fire?
recs.facts: In the Line of Fire (2006) is the memoir of General Pervez Musharraf.
recs.rel: It was published when Musharraf was President of Pakistan.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book Mein Kampf?
recs.facts: Mein Kampf (My Struggle) was written by Adolf Hitler, partly while he was in prison in 1924.
recs.rel: It was published in two volumes in 1925 and 1926.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word autonomy?
recs.facts: Autonomy means the right or ability of a person, group or region to govern itself and make its own decisions.
recs.rel: An autonomous region is one that has its own local government within a larger country.

recs.q: A boy has an average of 50 marks in 5 tests. How many marks must he score in the 6th test to raise his average to 70?
recs.facts: Total of 5 tests = 50 x 5 = 250. Total needed for 6 tests = 70 x 6 = 420, so the next score is 420 - 250 = 170.
recs.rel: Average = sum of all values divided by the number of values.

recs.q: The line x = 5 is parallel to which axis?
opts: It is parallel to no axis
recs.facts: All points on x = 5 have the same x value, so it is a vertical line parallel to the y-axis.
recs.rel: The equation x = 0 is the y-axis itself.

recs.q: The line y = 6 is parallel to which axis?
recs.facts: All points on y = 6 have the same y value, so it is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, crossing the y-axis at (0, 6).
recs.rel: The equation y = 0 is the x-axis itself.

recs.q: What is the name of the autobiography of Field Marshal Ayub Khan?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan wrote Friends Not Masters, published in 1967.
recs.rel: In the Line of Fire is the autobiography of Pervez Musharraf.

recs.q: Who is Azazeel, according to Islamic tradition?
recs.facts: Azazeel is the name by which Iblis (Shaitan) was known before he refused to prostrate to Hazrat Adam (AS).
recs.rel: Iblis was a jinn who lived among the angels.

recs.q: Rehman Baba was a famous poet of which language?
recs.facts: Rehman Baba (17th century) is a celebrated Sufi poet of the Pashto language.
recs.rel: His shrine is in Peshawar.

recs.q: A boy walks 10 miles north, turns back and walks 10 miles, then turns right and again turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
recs.facts: After turning back he walks south and faces south. Turning right from south he faces west, and turning right again he faces north.
recs.rel: A right turn is a 90 degree clockwise turn.

recs.q: In which city of Pakistan is Liaquat Bagh located?
recs.facts: Liaquat Bagh is a park in Rawalpindi where Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated in 1951.
recs.rel: It is also known for the 2007 assassination of Benazir Bhutto nearby.

recs.q: On which date did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
recs.facts: British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd in Amritsar on 13 April 1919, the Baisakhi day.
recs.rel: The massacre led to a wave of anti-British feeling in India.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh (as of 2026)?
recs.facts: Tarique Rahman of the BNP became Prime Minister on 17 February 2026 after the general election.
recs.rel: Before him Muhammad Yunus led the interim government after Sheikh Hasina left in 2024.

recs.q: In which year was the World Bank established?
recs.facts: The World Bank was set up at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 and began operations in 1946.
recs.rel: Its headquarters is in Washington, D.C.

recs.q: Who were Banu Quraiza?
opts: A branch of the Quraish of Makkah
recs.facts: Banu Quraiza were a Jewish tribe living near Madinah. They broke their agreement with the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq).
recs.rel: After the Trench, the Muslims besieged their fortress and the matter was settled by the judgement of Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).

recs.q: What do the names of Surah Al-Fatiha and Surah Al-Baqarah mean in English?
recs.facts: Al-Fatiha means The Opening and Al-Baqarah means The Cow.
recs.rel: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran, and Al-Fatiha is its first.

recs.q: Where is the Sukkur Barrage located?
recs.facts: Sukkur Barrage is built on the River Indus at Sukkur in the province of Sindh.
recs.rel: It was completed in 1932 and feeds seven major canals.

recs.q: What is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 24 cm?
recs.facts: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 6 x 24 = 72 square cm.
recs.rel: The area of a triangle is always half of the rectangle with the same base and height.

recs.q: What is the height of a triangle whose base is 6 cm and area is 24 square cm?
recs.facts: Area = half x base x height, so 24 = 0.5 x 6 x h = 3h. Therefore h = 8 cm.
recs.rel: Height = 2 x area divided by base.

recs.q: Is the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan based on a parliamentary or a presidential system?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary form of government with the Prime Minister as chief executive and the President as head of state.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution, by contrast, was presidential.

recs.q: On which basis was Pakistan created, according to the resolution passed in 1940?
recs.facts: The Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940, based on the Two-Nation Theory, demanded separate Muslim states and led to Pakistan.
recs.rel: It was presented by A. K. Fazlul Haq and seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.

recs.q: Who is known as Afzalul Bashar Ba'd al-Anbiya (best of mankind after the prophets)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) is called Afzalul Bashar Ba'd al-Anbiya, the best of mankind after the prophets.
recs.rel: He was the first Caliph of Islam and the closest companion of the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali becomes 8 years old, how old will his sister be?
recs.facts: Sister is 2 x 4 = 8 years now. Ali needs 4 more years to be 8, so sister will be 8 + 4 = 12.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people never changes.

recs.q: Change into active voice: The rooms are being decorated by the students.
opts: The students were decorating the rooms.
The students are decorating the rooms.
The students have decorated the rooms.
recs.facts: The passive present continuous (are being decorated) becomes the active present continuous (are decorating).
recs.rel: In active voice the doer becomes the subject.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Did the students ----- a lot of work in class?
recs.facts: After the auxiliary did the verb takes its base form, so have is correct.
recs.rel: In questions with did, the main verb never takes the past form.

recs.q: To what name was Islamabad's Kashmir Highway changed in August 2020?
recs.facts: In August 2020 the government renamed Kashmir Highway in Islamabad as Srinagar Highway to show solidarity with Kashmiris.
recs.rel: It was done ahead of Youm-e-Istehsal on 5 August.

recs.q: Which constitution was in force in Pakistan before the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution, given by Ayub Khan, remained until it was abrogated in 1969 by Yahya Khan, apart from a brief interim period.
recs.rel: An Interim Constitution was in force in 1972 before the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, sovereignty belongs to whom?
recs.facts: The Preamble and Objectives Resolution state that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone, exercised by the people as a sacred trust.
recs.rel: The authority is exercised through chosen representatives within limits set by Allah.

recs.q: In which place was Benazir Bhutto buried?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto was buried in the family mausoleum at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana, Sindh, beside her father.
recs.rel: She was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.

recs.q: What was the name of Benazir Bhutto's mother?
recs.facts: Begum Nusrat Bhutto, of Iranian-Kurdish origin, was the wife of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and mother of Benazir.
recs.rel: She was also known as Mader-e-Jamhooriat (Mother of Democracy).

recs.q: Between whom was the brotherhood (Mukhawat) established after the migration to Madinah?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) created brotherhood between the Muhajirin who came from Makkah and the Ansar, the helpers of Madinah.
recs.rel: It helped settle the Muhajirin economically in Madinah.

recs.q: Near which town is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built?
recs.facts: Diamer Bhasha Dam is on the Indus River about 40 km downstream of Chilas on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It is planned as a very large dam for water storage and electricity.

recs.q: What is the meaning of biased?
opts: Prejudiced in favour of one side
recs.facts: A biased person unfairly favours or opposes someone or something.
recs.rel: Bias means prejudice.

recs.q: What is a bicameral legislature?
opts: A legislature chosen by the army
recs.facts: Bicameral means two chambers; the word camera means chamber.
recs.rel: Pakistan's Parliament has the National Assembly and the Senate.

recs.q: Which was the first bicameral legislature of Pakistan, consisting of a National Assembly and a Senate?
recs.facts: The 1956 and 1962 Constitutions provided a single House (unicameral legislature). The 1973 Constitution created Parliament with two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate.
recs.rel: The Bogra Formula of 1953 had proposed a two-house legislature, but it was never adopted; some sources differ on how the first bicameral body is described.

recs.q: Where is the Black Sea located?
opts: Between southeastern Europe and western Asia
recs.facts: The Black Sea lies between southeastern Europe and western Asia, bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia.
recs.rel: It connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles straits.

recs.q: In which year did Muhammad Ali Bogra become Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad dismissed Khawaja Nazimuddin in April 1953 and appointed Muhammad Ali Bogra, then ambassador to the USA, as Prime Minister.
recs.rel: Bogra remained Prime Minister until August 1955 and was succeeded by Chaudhry Muhammad Ali.

recs.q: Who bowled the fastest recorded delivery in cricket history at 161.3 km per hour?
recs.facts: Shoaib Akhtar bowled a delivery of 161.3 km per hour against England in the 2003 World Cup, which is still the official record.
recs.rel: He is known as the Rawalpindi Express.

recs.q: In a class the number of girls is 7 more than the number of boys and the total is 33. How many boys are there?
recs.facts: Let boys be x, so girls are x + 7 and 2x + 7 = 33, giving x = 13. Girls are therefore 20.

recs.q: Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan in March 1969?
recs.facts: When Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969, General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution in 1958.

recs.q: Which reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims in British India?
recs.facts: The Indian Councils Act 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted separate electorates to Muslims.
recs.rel: The Simla Deputation of 1906 had demanded separate electorates from Lord Minto.

recs.q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: In a bus of 24 people, 3/4 are male. What percentage are female?
recs.facts: Males are 3/4 of 24 = 18, so females are 24 - 18 = 6. Percentage = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.
recs.rel: The female share is 1 - 3/4 = 1/4, which is 25 percent.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: We have business classes ______ night.
recs.facts: The preposition 'at' is used with night in the phrase 'at night'.
recs.rel: We say in the morning, in the evening, but at night.

recs.q: From which country did Pakistan acquire the J-10C fighter aircraft?
recs.facts: The J-10C is a Chinese fighter built by Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. Pakistan Air Force inducted it from China.
recs.rel: Pakistan also operates the JF-17 Thunder, which it co-developed with China.

recs.q: How many days are there in a common (non-leap) calendar year?
recs.facts: A common year has 12 months totalling 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
recs.rel: A leap year comes every four years and adds 29 February.

recs.q: What is the complex number 4 - 2i called?
recs.facts: A number of the form a + bi with i the square root of minus 1 is a complex number. Here a = 4 and b = -2.
recs.rel: Its conjugate is 4 + 2i.

recs.q: Approximately how many prophets came to the world in total, according to popular Islamic tradition?
recs.facts: A popular narration says that about 124,000 prophets were sent. The number is not given in the Quran.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact number, and 313 is commonly given for the Rasuls (messengers).

recs.q: Who was the ruler of Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim invaded it in 711 AD?
recs.facts: Raja Dahir of the Brahman dynasty ruled Sindh from Aror. Muhammad bin Qasim defeated him in 712 AD.
recs.rel: The Sindh campaign took place under Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf.

recs.q: Zakat becomes obligatory on a minimum of how many camels?
recs.facts: The nisab for camels is five. One goat is due on 5 to 9 camels.
recs.rel: Zakat on gold has a nisab of 7.5 tola, and on silver 52.5 tola.

recs.q: Which canal separates Asia from Africa?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal in Egypt separates Africa from the Sinai Peninsula in Asia. It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
recs.rel: The canal opened in 1869.

recs.q: What is the capital of Argentina?
recs.facts: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.
recs.rel: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay.

recs.q: What is the capital of Bahrain?
recs.facts: Manama is the capital of Bahrain, an island country in the Persian Gulf.
recs.rel: Doha is the capital of Qatar.

recs.q: What is the capital of Cuba?
recs.facts: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.
recs.rel: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica.

recs.q: What is the capital of Denmark?
recs.facts: Copenhagen is the capital and largest city of Denmark.
recs.rel: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

recs.q: What is the capital of India?
recs.facts: New Delhi is the capital of India.
recs.rel: Capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

recs.q: What is the capital of Thailand?
recs.facts: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand.
recs.rel: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.

recs.q: On which date is International Women's Day celebrated?
recs.facts: International Women's Day is observed every year on 8 March.
recs.rel: International Labour Day falls on 1 May.

recs.q: How many centimetres are there in one metre?
recs.facts: The prefix centi means one hundredth, so 1 metre equals 100 centimetres.
recs.rel: 1 kilometre equals 1000 metres.

recs.q: Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani of the PPP was elected Chairman of the Senate and sworn in on 9 April 2024.
recs.rel: Sadiq Sanjrani was Senate chairman from 2018 to 2024.

recs.q: Who is the Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Mauritania's Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed was elected OIC Secretary General on 27 August 2026 in Jeddah, succeeding Hissein Brahim Taha of Chad.
recs.rel: Hissein Brahim Taha held the post from 2021, which was the answer in 2022.

recs.q: In mathematics, a quantity whose value can change is called a
recs.facts: A variable is a symbol that can take different values, unlike a constant whose value is fixed.
recs.rel: In the expression 3x + 5, x is the variable and 3 is the coefficient.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani C-in-C in January 1951, after British generals Messervy and Gracey.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan later became President of Pakistan after the 1958 coup.

recs.q: According to Islamic teaching, what is recited in the ear of a newborn baby?
recs.facts: It is Sunnah to recite the Azan in the baby's right ear soon after birth.
recs.rel: Iqamah is recited in the left ear according to many scholars.

recs.q: Which of the following is a Chinese COVID-19 vaccine?
recs.facts: Sinopharm is made in China; the other three were developed in the USA, Germany and the UK.
recs.rel: Sinovac and CanSino are other Chinese vaccines used in Pakistan.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: Who did you take this book ____?
recs.facts: The sentence means from whom the book was taken, so the preposition from is correct.
recs.rel: Formally the sentence would be: From whom did you take this book?

recs.q: In which US state is the Grand Canyon located?
recs.facts: The Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, is in northern Arizona.
recs.rel: It is about 446 km long and up to 1.8 km deep.

recs.q: In which period did the American Civil War take place?
recs.facts: The American Civil War between the Union and the Confederacy was fought from 1861 to 1865.
recs.rel: It ended slavery in the USA with the 13th Amendment in 1865.

recs.q: Who led the Union side in the American Civil War?
recs.facts: Abraham Lincoln was President of the Union (the Northern states) during the war.
recs.rel: Jefferson Davis led the Confederacy and Robert E. Lee was its top general.

recs.q: Mohenjo-daro, a famous site of the Indus Valley Civilization, is located in which province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Mohenjo-daro lies in Larkana district of Sindh on the bank of the Indus.
recs.rel: Harappa, the other major city, is in Punjab.

recs.q: Who were the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953?
recs.facts: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953.
recs.rel: Mallory and Irvine vanished near the summit in 1924 and their success is unproven.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'precious'?
recs.facts: Precious means of great value or highly prized.
recs.rel: Gold and diamonds are called precious metals and stones.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'breach'?
recs.facts: To breach something is to break or violate it, such as a rule or a contract.
recs.rel: A breach can also mean a gap made in a wall.

recs.q: Which line is the de facto boundary between India and China?
recs.facts: The India-China frontier is known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
recs.rel: The McMahon Line is the 1914 boundary in the east that China does not accept.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'coercive'?
recs.facts: Coercive means forcing someone to act by pressure or threat, so its opposite is voluntary, done by free choice.
recs.rel: The noun form is coercion, meaning the use of force or threats to make someone do something.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of 'coercive'?
recs.facts: Coercive means using force or pressure to make someone obey, which is close in meaning to compulsory.
recs.rel: Its antonym is voluntary.

recs.q: In a matrix of order 5 x 4, how many elements are there in each column?
recs.facts: The order 5 x 4 means 5 rows and 4 columns. Each column runs down through all the rows, so it has 5 elements.
recs.rel: The total number of elements in a 5 x 4 matrix is 20.

recs.q: Which letter and number come next in the series: Z1, X3, V5, T7, ?
recs.facts: The letters move back by 2 each time (Z, X, V, T, R) and the numbers increase by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is R9.
recs.rel: Letter series that skip every other letter are common in verbal tests.

recs.q: What is the synonym of 'command'?
recs.facts: To command means to give an authoritative instruction, which is the same as to order.
recs.rel: Command also means control over a unit, as in the command of an army.

recs.q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to which commission?
recs.facts: The Simon Commission of 1927 had no Indian member, and Lord Birkenhead challenged Indians to frame a constitution. The Nehru Report was the Indian reply.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam later put forward his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

recs.q: What is common in the series 4, 8, 12, 16?
recs.facts: 4 = 4 x 1, 8 = 4 x 2, 12 = 4 x 3 and 16 = 4 x 4, so every term is a multiple of 4 with a common difference of 4.
recs.rel: A series with a constant difference is called an arithmetic progression.

recs.q: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 gave benefits to which community?
recs.facts: It created the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving Muslims better chances in education, jobs and politics.
recs.rel: Hindu agitation led the British to annul the partition in 1911.

recs.q: 900 employees work in a company and 480 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
recs.rel: The percentage of men is 53.33%, and the two percentages add up to 100.

recs.q: In which year did the East India Company annex the Punjab?
recs.facts: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Punjab was annexed to the Company's territories in 1849.
recs.rel: Maharaja Ranjit Singh had ruled the Punjab until his death in 1839.

recs.q: Who compiled the hadith collection Musnad Ahmad?
recs.facts: Musnad Ahmad was compiled by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, founder of the Hanbali school of fiqh.
recs.rel: It contains tens of thousands of hadith arranged by narrator.

recs.q: What is the largest composite number from 1 to 99?
recs.facts: 97 is prime, 98 = 2 x 49 and 99 = 9 x 11 has factors other than 1 and itself. So 99 is the largest composite number.
recs.rel: A composite number has more than two factors.

recs.q: On what date was the Indian National Congress established?
