recs.facts: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay on 28 December 1885.
recs.rel: Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee.

recs.q: Which caliph received the surrender of Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) in 637 AD?
recs.facts: Jerusalem was besieged by Muslim armies under Abu Ubaidah and Amr bin al-As and its people surrendered to Caliph Umar (RA) in person.
recs.rel: Khalid bin Waleed (RA) conquered Damascus region, not Jerusalem.

recs.q: How many members did the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan originally have?
recs.facts: The first Constituent Assembly formed in 1947 had 69 members.
recs.rel: Its membership was later raised to 79 after the addition of more members.

recs.q: In which year did the construction of Tarbela Dam begin?
recs.facts: The contract was awarded in May 1968 and main construction ran from 1968 to 1976.
recs.rel: Tarbela Dam is built on the Indus River and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

recs.q: In which year was Rawal Dam built (completed)?
recs.facts: Rawal Dam on the Korang River in Islamabad is listed as completed in 1962.
recs.rel: Some sources give 1962 as the start of construction, so sources differ.

recs.q: Who performs the duties of the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to act?
recs.facts: Article 49 of the Constitution says the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
recs.rel: If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.

recs.q: Convert 60 degrees into radians.
recs.facts: Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.
recs.rel: 180 degrees equals pi radians.

recs.q: Convert to passive voice: He told me about the accident.
opts: I was told about the accident by him.
I am told about the accident by him.
The accident was told by him to me about.
I had told about the accident by him.
recs.facts: The past simple active becomes was/were plus past participle in passive, with the object I becoming the subject.
recs.rel: Passive voice puts the receiver of the action at the start of the sentence.

recs.q: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
recs.facts: A generator (dynamo) turns a coil in a magnetic field and produces electric current from mechanical motion.
recs.rel: An electric motor does the opposite and converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.

recs.q: What does SUPARCO stand for?
opts: Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
Satellite and Upper Atmosphere Research Corporation
Space Utilization and Planetary Research Commission
Science and Upper Atmosphere Research Council
recs.facts: SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency, called the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.
recs.rel: It was established in 1961.

recs.q: The Wakhan Corridor connects Pakistan to which province of Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip in Badakhshan province of north-eastern Afghanistan.
recs.rel: It separates Pakistan from Tajikistan.

recs.q: Between which two countries is the longest international border in the world?
recs.facts: The Canada-USA border is about 8,900 km long including the Alaska border, the longest in the world.
recs.rel: It is also the longest undefended border.

recs.q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.
recs.rel: At this speed the train runs at 72 km/h.

recs.q: A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
recs.facts: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour. So the distance is 120 / 5 = 24 km.
recs.rel: Speed in km per minute is distance in km/h divided by 60, here 2 km per minute.

recs.q: A train covers 90 km in 1 hour. How much time will it take to cover 120 km?
recs.facts: Time = distance / speed = 120 / 90 = 4/3 hours. 4/3 hours is 1 hour 20 minutes.
recs.rel: The same train covers 1.5 km every minute.

recs.q: If a car covers 20 km in an hour, what distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: 30 minutes is half an hour. So the distance is 20 / 2 = 10 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: If a car covers 90 km in one hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will it cover 1 km?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes for 90 km. So 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 10/9 minutes.
recs.rel: The car's speed is 54 km/h.

recs.q: Which of the following British reforms introduced separate electorates for the Muslims of the subcontinent?
recs.facts: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted Muslims separate electorates, which was a key demand of the Simla Deputation of 1906.
recs.rel: The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates, while the Cripps Mission came in 1942.

recs.q: Which is the major rabi (winter) crop of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Wheat is sown in October to December and harvested in April to May, which makes it the main rabi crop.
recs.rel: Cotton, rice and sugarcane are kharif (summer) crops.

recs.q: On which date is World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day celebrated?
recs.facts: It is observed on 8 May, the birthday of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.
recs.rel: Henry Dunant won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

recs.q: After the 2026 tournament, which country or countries will host the next FIFA World Cup in 2030?
recs.facts: FIFA awarded the 2030 World Cup to Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the centenary.
recs.rel: The 2026 World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, and Qatar hosted in 2022.

recs.q: What is the currency of Belgium (Brussels) and Finland?
recs.facts: Both Belgium and Finland are members of the Eurozone and use the euro.
recs.rel: Belgium used the Belgian franc before adopting the euro in 2002.

recs.q: What is the currency of Uganda?
recs.facts: Uganda's national currency is the Ugandan shilling.
recs.rel: The capital of Uganda is Kampala.

recs.q: What is the name of China's currency?
recs.facts: China's official currency is the renminbi, whose main unit is the yuan.
recs.rel: The word renminbi means the people's currency.

recs.q: Who is the current Director General of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Fuad Asadullah Khan has led the IB since 2022 and in May 2026 the Prime Minister approved a four-year extension for him.
recs.rel: He was the first officer from the intelligence cadre to head the IB.

recs.q: Who is the current Chancellor of Germany?
recs.facts: Friedrich Merz of the CDU became Chancellor in May 2025 and was still in office in October 2026.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Olaf Scholz (2021 to 2025), and before him Angela Merkel served from 2005 to 2021.

recs.q: If a circle is divided into 360 equal parts, what is each part called?
recs.facts: A full circle measures 360 degrees, so each of 360 equal parts is one degree.
recs.rel: A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, or 90 degrees.

recs.q: Which country announced the cutting of funding to the World Health Organization in 2020 and later withdrew from it?
recs.facts: In 2020 President Trump halted US funding to the WHO, and in 2025 the United States started its withdrawal.
recs.rel: The United States had been the largest single donor to the WHO.

recs.q: In which country is the Khanpur (Kahnpur) Dam located?
recs.facts: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Haripur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
recs.rel: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

recs.q: Hazrat Asma (R.A), known as Dhat un-Nitaqayn, was the daughter of which Sahabi?
recs.facts: Asma bint Abu Bakr was the elder sister of Hazrat Aisha (R.A) and helped the Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrah.
recs.rel: She was the mother of Abdullah ibn Zubair (R.A).

recs.q: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), who was married to Hazrat Uthman (R.A), was the daughter of whom?
recs.facts: Umm Kulthum was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and married Hazrat Uthman after the death of her sister Ruqayyah.
recs.rel: This is why Hazrat Uthman is called Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

recs.q: Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Ali (R.A) and Hazrat Fatima (R.A)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zainab bint Ali was a daughter of Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Fatima and sister of Hasan and Husain.
recs.rel: Their other daughter was Umm Kulthum bint Ali.

recs.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
recs.facts: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February, so it has 365 + 1 = 366 days.
recs.rel: A leap year comes every four years, for example 2024 and 2028.

recs.q: What is the definition of a noun?
opts: A word that describes an action
A word that names a person, place, thing or idea
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
recs.facts: A noun is a naming word: it names a person, place, animal, thing or idea.
recs.rel: A verb shows action, an adjective describes a noun, and a conjunction joins words or clauses.

recs.q: What is a square matrix?
opts: A matrix with equal number of rows and columns
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with only one column
recs.facts: A square matrix has the same number of rows as columns, for example 3 by 3.
recs.rel: Only square matrices have determinants and can have inverses.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of 'demise'?
recs.facts: Demise means death or the end of something.
recs.rel: Its antonym is birth.

recs.q: In which body were the Basic Democrats of Ayub Khan's system mainly represented?
opts: Electoral college for President and assemblies
recs.facts: Basic Democrats, elected from union councils, formed the electoral college that elected the President and members of the assemblies.
recs.rel: The system was announced in 1959 and used in the 1965 presidential election.

recs.q: How many Basic Democrats were there in Ayub Khan's system (40,000 in each wing)?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan's Basic Democracies had 80,000 members, 40,000 in East Pakistan and 40,000 in West Pakistan.
recs.rel: The number was later raised to 120,000, but 80,000 was the original figure.

recs.q: What is the derivative of tan x with respect to x?
recs.facts: d/dx (tan x) = d/dx (sin x / cos x) = (cos^2 x + sin^2 x) / cos^2 x = sec^2 x.
recs.rel: The derivative of cot x is minus cosec squared x.

recs.q: Which lake is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake?
recs.facts: Lake Turkana in northern Kenya lies in a desert region and is the largest permanent desert lake, nicknamed the Jade Sea.
recs.rel: It is a very alkaline lake in the Great Rift Valley.

recs.q: What is the determinant of a diagonal matrix?
recs.facts: For a diagonal matrix all off-diagonal entries are zero, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal elements.
recs.rel: The sum of diagonal elements is called the trace.

recs.q: What is a diagonal matrix?
opts: A square matrix whose off-diagonal elements are all zero
A matrix with all elements equal
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose determinant is always 1
recs.facts: A diagonal matrix is a square matrix in which every element outside the main diagonal is zero.
recs.rel: Scalar and identity matrices are special diagonal matrices.

recs.q: If the side of a square is a, what is the length of its diagonal?
recs.facts: By Pythagoras, diagonal = square root of (a^2 + a^2) = a times root 2.
recs.rel: The diagonals of a square are equal and bisect each other at right angles.

recs.q: What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 28?
recs.facts: Diameter = 2 x radius = 2 x 28 = 56.
recs.rel: Circumference equals pi times diameter.

recs.q: What is the radius of a circle with diameter 52 cm?
recs.facts: Radius = diameter / 2 = 52 / 2 = 26 cm.
recs.rel: Area of this circle is pi x 26 x 26.

recs.q: Which word comes first in the dictionary?
recs.facts: Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).
recs.rel: Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.

recs.q: On which date did the singer Lata Mangeshkar die?
recs.facts: Lata Mangeshkar, the Indian playback singer, died in Mumbai on 6 February 2022.
recs.rel: She was born on 28 September 1929.

recs.q: Where was democracy first practised in the world?
recs.facts: Democracy began in the ancient Greek city-state of Athens around the 5th century BC.
recs.rel: The word democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (rule).

recs.q: The voice of which animal is described in the Holy Quran as the worst of voices?
recs.facts: Surah Luqman says the harshest of voices is surely the voice of the donkey.
recs.rel: The advice is given by Hazrat Luqman to his son in Surah Luqman.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word diversity?
recs.facts: Diversity means variety; its opposite is uniformity, meaning sameness.
recs.rel: Diversity is a synonym of variety.

recs.q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
recs.facts: One pencil costs 60 / 12 = Rs 5, so 5 pencils cost 5 x 5 = Rs 25.
recs.rel: One dozen means 12 items.

recs.q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils?
recs.facts: Four pencils are one third of a dozen, so the cost is 27 / 3 = Rs 9.
recs.rel: One pencil costs Rs 2.25.

recs.q: What is the national dress of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Shalwar Kameez is worn across all provinces and is recognised as the national dress of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sherwani is the national dress for formal wear of men and is linked with Quaid-e-Azam.

recs.q: What is the cutting of hair by a pilgrim at the end of Hajj called?
recs.facts: Halq means shaving the head, and qasr means trimming the hair; one of them is done to leave the state of Ihram.
recs.rel: Women only trim a fingertip length of hair.

recs.q: What is the measure in degrees of each angle (corner) of a square?
recs.facts: A square has four equal angles and they sum to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 4 = 90 degrees.
recs.rel: A rectangle also has four right angles.

recs.q: What does ECO stand for?
recs.facts: ECO stands for Economic Cooperation Organization, a regional group of Asian countries.
recs.rel: It succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of 1964.

recs.q: Abdul Sattar Edhi, the famous humanitarian known as the Angel of Mercy, belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Edhi spent his life in Pakistan and founded the Edhi Foundation in Karachi. He is regarded as one of the greatest humanitarians of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Edhi died in Karachi on 8 July 2016.

recs.q: If one egg takes 2 minutes to boil, how many minutes will 5 eggs take when boiled together in the same pot?
recs.facts: Eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so the time does not depend on the number of eggs. All 5 eggs take 2 minutes.
recs.rel: This is a classic logic puzzle where the obvious multiplication is wrong.

recs.q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest?
recs.facts: Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.
recs.rel: Chain the comparisons to rank all persons.

recs.q: If Akbar is elder than Ahmad and Adnan is elder than Akbar, then who is the eldest?
recs.facts: Adnan is elder than Akbar, and Akbar is elder than Ahmad. So Adnan is the eldest.
recs.rel: The youngest in this chain is Ahmad.

recs.q: In which pact were separate electorates for Muslims granted?
recs.facts: Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress accepted the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates for Muslims.
recs.rel: Separate electorates were first given in the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

recs.q: What is a set that has no element called?
recs.facts: A set with no element is called the null set or empty set and is written as a circle with a slash or as curly brackets with nothing inside.
recs.rel: The empty set is a subset of every set.

recs.q: What is a set with exactly one element called?
recs.facts: A set containing only one element, such as the set containing 5 alone, is called a singleton set.
recs.rel: A singleton set has exactly two subsets.

recs.q: If every element of set A is also an element of set B, then A is called what of B?
recs.facts: When all elements of A belong to B, A is a subset of B, written A is contained in B.
recs.rel: B is then called a superset of A.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: cow, snake, elephant, monkey?
recs.facts: Cow, elephant and monkey are mammals, while a snake is a reptile.
recs.rel: Mammals are warm-blooded and feed milk to their young.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'embellish'?
opts: To make more attractive by adding decoration
recs.facts: Embellish means to decorate or beautify something, or to add extra details to a story.
recs.rel: Adorn and ornament are synonyms of embellish.

recs.q: When was the partition of Bengal enforced by Lord Curzon?
recs.facts: Lord Curzon divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal, and the partition took effect on 16 October 1905.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: Which of the following are the vowels of the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The five vowel letters of English are A, E, I, O and U.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters, so 21 are consonants.

recs.q: If RAT is coded as TAR (letters reversed), then what is FAT equal to?
recs.facts: RAT becomes TAR by reversing the order of letters. Reversing FAT gives TAF.
recs.rel: Reversal codes are the simplest letter codes.

recs.q: In trigonometry, what is tan x equal to?
opts: cos x divided by sin x
sin x divided by cos x
recs.facts: Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine, so tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.
recs.rel: Cot x is the reciprocal of tan x.

recs.q: What is cosecant x equal to?
opts: sin x divided by cos x
recs.facts: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec x = 1 / sin x.
recs.rel: Sec x = 1 / cos x and cot x = 1 / tan x.

recs.q: What type of equation is 6x - 5x - 7 = 0?
recs.facts: Simplifying gives x - 7 = 0, which has highest power 1 of x, so it is linear and gives x = 7.
recs.rel: A linear equation in one variable has exactly one root.

recs.q: Who headed the committee for the collection of the Holy Quran in the era of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) appointed Zaid bin Thabit, the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran into one volume.
recs.rel: Zaid also led the committee in the era of Hazrat Usman (RA).

recs.q: How many end points does a ray have?
recs.facts: A ray starts at one fixed point and extends endlessly in one direction, so it has one end point.
recs.rel: A line segment has two end points and a line has none.

recs.q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was among his bitter enemies?
recs.facts: Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza) strongly opposed the Prophet (PBUH) and a Surah of the Quran is named after him. Abu Jahal was not his uncle.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Masad condemns Abu Lahab.

recs.q: Which event did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) take part in after the Harb-e-Fijar?
recs.facts: After the Harb-e-Fijar, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in Hilf-ul-Fudul, a pact formed in Makkah to help the oppressed and protect travellers and the weak. He was a young man at the time.
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) later said that he would still accept such a pact even in Islam.

recs.q: What is the measure of each external angle of a regular hexagon?
recs.facts: The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. A hexagon has 6 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 6 = 60 degrees.
recs.rel: Each internal angle of a regular hexagon is 120 degrees.

recs.q: What is the measure of each external angle of a regular octagon?
recs.facts: The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. An octagon has 8 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 8 = 45 degrees.
recs.rel: Each internal angle of a regular octagon is 135 degrees.

recs.q: What is meant by Laissez-faire in economics?
opts: Minimum government interference in the economy
recs.facts: Laissez-faire is a French term meaning let do. It is the policy that the government should interfere as little as possible in economic affairs and leave markets free.
recs.rel: Adam Smith is the economist most associated with ideas of free markets.

recs.q: Which word comes first in the dictionary: False, Fallow, Faithful, Fallable, Falcon?
recs.facts: All words begin with Fa. The third letters are i (Faithful), l (the rest), so Faithful comes first. Then Falcon, Fallable, Fallow and False follow.
recs.rel: Dictionary order compares letters one by one from the left.

recs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) belonged to which family (clan) of Quraish?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, who was a son of Abdul Muttalib of Banu Hashim. He was thus a cousin of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) also belonged to Banu Hashim.

recs.q: For what industry is Gaddani in Balochistan famous?
recs.facts: Gaddani, on the coast of Balochistan near Karachi, has one of the largest ship breaking yards in the world, where old ships are dismantled.
recs.rel: Gaddani lies in Lasbela District.

recs.q: For which product is Sialkot famous?
recs.facts: Sialkot is world famous for sports goods, such as footballs, and also for surgical instruments and leather goods.
recs.rel: Footballs made in Sialkot have been used in FIFA World Cups.

recs.q: For what is Ziyarat in Balochistan famous?
recs.facts: Ziyarat is a hill town famous for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days in 1948, and for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.
recs.rel: The Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.

recs.q: A car travels at 120 km/h and another car travels twice as fast. How far will the second car travel in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: The second car's speed is 2 x 120 = 240 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it travels 240 x 1/2 = 120 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time.

recs.q: Son is to father as nephew is to what?
recs.facts: A son is the child of his father, and a nephew is the child of the brother or sister of an uncle or aunt, so the relation is nephew to uncle.
recs.rel: The female counterpart of a nephew is a niece.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.
recs.rel: His mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahab.

recs.q: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called by which name?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and Umm-ul-Quran because it sums up the message of the Quran.
recs.rel: It is also called Sab'a Mathani and is recited in every rakat of Namaz.

recs.q: For which crime was Fatimah bint Aswad (a woman of Banu Makhzum) punished in the time of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Fatimah bint Aswad of Banu Makhzum was found guilty of theft, and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) ordered the punishment for theft. He refused to let rank or family influence the decision.
recs.rel: He said that nations before them were destroyed because they punished the poor but spared the rich.

recs.q: Which day is observed in Pakistan on 5th February every year?
recs.facts: Pakistan observes 5 February as Kashmir Solidarity Day to express support for the people of Indian-administered Kashmir.
recs.rel: Pakistan Day is on 23 March and Defence Day on 6 September.

recs.q: Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ayub Khan promoted himself to the rank of Field Marshal in 1959.
recs.rel: Asim Munir was promoted to Field Marshal in May 2025, making him the second.

recs.q: Find x if 3x - 9 = x + 7.
recs.facts: Subtract x from both sides: 2x - 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.

recs.q: If 2x/28 = 2/7, find x.
recs.rel: Cross multiplying gives 14x = 56, which also gives x = 4.

recs.q: What is the mean of 1, 3, 5 and 6?
recs.facts: Sum = 1 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 15; divided by 4 numbers gives 3.75.
recs.rel: The mean is the sum of values divided by the number of values.

recs.q: Which letter comes after M in the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The alphabet runs L, M, N, so N follows M.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

recs.q: Arrange the letters 'IYTC' to form a meaningful word.
recs.facts: Rearranging I, Y, T, C gives the word CITY.
recs.rel: An anagram uses all the given letters exactly once.

recs.q: Which is the largest fort of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 26 km long and is often called the largest fort in the world.
recs.rel: It is also known as the Great Wall of Sindh.

recs.q: Between whom was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
opts: The Muslims of Madinah and the Quraish of Makkah
The Muslims and the Jews of Khyber
The Muslims and the Byzantine army
The Muslims and the tribe of Thaqif at Taif
recs.facts: Badr was fought in 2 AH between the small Muslim army led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the much larger army of the Quraish of Makkah.
recs.rel: Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day that separated right from wrong.

recs.q: Near which city is the mountain where the Battle of Uhud was fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Uhud was fought at the foot of Mount Uhud, a few kilometres north of Madinah.
recs.rel: The battle took place in 3 AH between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

recs.q: Which fraction comes next in the series: 3/5, 5/8, 8/12, 12/17, ?
recs.facts: Numerators are 3, 5, 8, 12, 17 with differences 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next is 17. Each denominator equals the next numerator, and the denominators 5, 8, 12, 17 continue with 17+6 = 23.
recs.rel: Each fraction's numerator equals the previous fraction's denominator.

recs.q: What is the currency of France?
recs.facts: France uses the euro, which replaced the French franc in 2002.
recs.rel: The euro is shared by most countries of the European Union eurozone.

recs.q: If the first day of a month is Friday, which day will the 17th be?
recs.facts: The 15th is 14 days (two full weeks) after the 1st, so it is also a Friday. The 17th is two days later, a Sunday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: Change the narration (direct speech) of: He bade farewell to his friends.
opts: He said to his friends that good-bye.
He told his friends, "Farewell to you."
recs.facts: To bid farewell means to say good-bye, so in direct speech it becomes: He said to his friends, "Good-bye."
recs.rel: Similar idioms: bade welcome becomes said, "Welcome", and wished becomes said, "Good luck."

recs.q: What is the full form of PIA?
recs.facts: PIA stands for Pakistan International Airlines, the national flag carrier of Pakistan.
recs.rel: PIA began as Orient Airways in 1946 and took its present name in 1955.

recs.q: In which city were the Olympic Games named Tokyo 2020 held?
recs.facts: The 2020 Summer Olympics were awarded to Tokyo, Japan. Because of COVID-19 they were postponed and held in Tokyo from July to August 2021.
recs.rel: Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics.

recs.q: How many doors (gates) does the Holy Kaaba have?
recs.facts: The Kaaba has a single door, on its north-east wall, about two metres above ground level.
recs.rel: The door is made of gold-plated material and is opened only on special occasions.

recs.q: Who served as both Governor General and Prime Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor General from 1948 to 1951 and then Prime Minister from 1951 to 1953.
recs.rel: He became Governor General after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.

recs.q: Who is the President of Germany?
recs.facts: Frank-Walter Steinmeier has been the Federal President of Germany since March 2017 and was re-elected in 2022. His second term ends in March 2027.
recs.rel: The President is the head of state, while the Chancellor (currently Friedrich Merz) is the head of government.

recs.q: In which Ghazwa was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) wounded?
recs.facts: In the Battle of Uhad (3 AH) the Prophet (PBUH) was wounded in the face and his blessed tooth was broken.
recs.rel: The Muslim archers left their post on the hill during Uhad, which let the Quraish attack from behind.

recs.q: What is jute commonly known as?
recs.facts: Jute is called the golden fibre because of its shiny golden-brown colour and its high value as a cash crop.
recs.rel: Bangladesh and India are the largest producers of jute.

recs.q: Who was the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb, so her father Wahb bin Abd Manaf was his maternal grandfather.
recs.rel: Wahb belonged to the Banu Zuhra clan of Quraish.

recs.q: The sign greater than or equal to is used in which type of mathematical statement?
recs.facts: The sign for greater than or equal to compares two quantities without saying that they are exactly equal, so it forms an inequality.
recs.rel: The sign for less than or equal to is also used in inequalities.

recs.q: To which language group does the Sindhi language belong, among the given options?
recs.facts: Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language that developed from Sanskrit and Prakrit. Of the given options, Sanskrit is the ancestral language group.
recs.rel: Sindhi is the official language of Sindh province and is written in a Perso-Arabic script.

recs.q: What is the first group of the periodic table called?
recs.facts: Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium, which are called alkali metals.
recs.rel: Hydrogen sits at the top of Group 1 but is not an alkali metal.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: They ___ seeds in flowers.
recs.facts: The subject They is plural, so the simple present plural verb grow is needed.
recs.rel: The verb grows is used with singular subjects such as he, she or it.

recs.q: The old fort of Gwadar/Chabahar region lies on the coast of the Gulf of which?
recs.facts: Gwadar and Chabahar lie on the coast near the Gulf of Oman, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
recs.rel: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958.

recs.q: Which hadith is called Muttafaq Alaih?
opts: A hadith narrated by both Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim
A hadith narrated by only one companion
A hadith narrated by Imam Tirmidhi
recs.facts: Muttafaq Alaih (agreed upon) is a hadith recorded in both Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
recs.rel: Such hadith are considered to be of the highest authenticity.

recs.q: Who received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the Kargil War of 1999?
recs.facts: Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for his bravery in Kargil.
recs.rel: Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed also received the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil.

recs.q: What is the straight line that divides a circle into two equal halves called?
recs.facts: A chord passing through the centre of a circle is the diameter and it cuts the circle into two equal semicircles.
recs.rel: The diameter equals twice the radius.

recs.q: Who is the author of the novel The Pursuit of Happiness (2001)?
recs.facts: The novel The Pursuit of Happiness was written by the author Douglas Kennedy.
recs.rel: Do not confuse it with The Conquest of Happiness by Bertrand Russell.

recs.q: What is the HCF of 12 and 16?
recs.facts: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. The common factors are 2 x 2, so the HCF is 4.
recs.rel: The LCM of 12 and 16 is 48.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO) located?
recs.facts: The ILO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
recs.rel: The ILO was founded in 1919 and became a UN agency in 1946.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the African Union located?
recs.facts: The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
recs.rel: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002.

recs.q: According to the Quran, who will be in the lowest depths of the Fire?
recs.facts: Surah An-Nisa says the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire.
recs.rel: Hypocrites outwardly claimed faith while hiding disbelief.

recs.q: With the help of which country did Pakistan carry out the Saindak project?
recs.facts: The Saindak copper-gold project in Balochistan was developed with Chinese help by the Metallurgical Corporation of China.
recs.rel: Saindak is in Chagai district, Balochistan.

recs.q: Which is the highest mountain range in the world?
recs.facts: The Himalayas contain Mount Everest and most of the world's highest peaks.
recs.rel: The Andes are the longest continental mountain range.

recs.q: On which hills is the city of Islamabad situated?
recs.facts: Islamabad lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills, part of the Himalayan foothills.
recs.rel: Faisal Mosque is at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old?
recs.facts: The sister is 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 10 she will be 20.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people stays the same over time.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old is his sister?
recs.facts: 3 x 5 = 15 years.
recs.rel: She is 10 years older than Ali.

recs.q: On which date of Rabi ul Awwal is the birthday of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) commonly observed?
recs.facts: Most Sunni Muslims observe the birth of the Prophet (PBUH) on 12 Rabi ul Awwal.
recs.rel: Shia scholars commonly observe it on 17 Rabi ul Awwal.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: The children ___ the honey on bread.
recs.facts: The plural subject children takes the plural verb eat.
recs.rel: Children is an irregular plural.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: Nadia's father ___ honey.
recs.facts: Father is singular and the sentence is active present, so the verb is buys.
recs.rel: A singular third person subject takes a verb ending in s in the simple present.

recs.q: Boy is to girl as horse is to what?
recs.facts: A girl is the female of a boy; the female of a horse is a mare.
recs.rel: A young horse is a foal.

recs.q: A man travels 90 km in 1 hour at a constant speed. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
recs.facts: 90 km takes 60 minutes, so 1 km takes 60 divided by 90 = 2/3 minute, which is 40 seconds.
recs.rel: Speed 90 km per hour equals 1.5 km per minute.

recs.q: Infections in the human body are caused by which of the following?
opts: Germs (pathogens such as bacteria and viruses)
recs.facts: Infections occur when disease-causing germs such as bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites enter the body and multiply.
recs.rel: Antigens are substances that trigger the immune system, while antibodies are made to fight them.

recs.q: What was the old name of Hyderabad (Sindh)?
recs.facts: Hyderabad in Sindh was built on the site of the old fort town called Neerunkot (Nerunkot), which was ruled by the Kalhora dynasty later.
recs.rel: Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhora founded the modern city of Hyderabad in 1768.

recs.q: If the eccentricity e of a conic is greater than 1, the conic is a:
recs.facts: A conic has e = 0 for a circle, e less than 1 for an ellipse, e = 1 for a parabola and e greater than 1 for a hyperbola.
recs.rel: A circle is the special case of an ellipse with zero eccentricity.

recs.q: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is known for his confrontation with which tyrant ruler?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) challenged the idol worship and the claim of divinity of King Namrood, who had him thrown into a fire that Allah made cool.
recs.rel: Pharaoh was the opponent of Hazrat Musa (AS).

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) to Hazrat Yaqub (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was father of Ishaq (AS), who was the father of Yaqub (AS), so Ibrahim was the grandfather of Yaqub.
recs.rel: Yaqub (AS) is also called Israel and his twelve sons were the tribes of Bani Israel.

recs.q: About what percentage of the world's ice is found in Antarctica?
recs.facts: Antarctica holds about 90 percent of all the ice on Earth, and about 70 percent of the world's fresh water.
recs.rel: Greenland holds most of the remaining ice.

recs.q: What is the first source of Islamic law (Shariah)?
recs.facts: The Quran is the primary source of Islamic law, followed by the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus) and Qiyas (analogy).
recs.rel: Ijtehad is the effort of scholars to derive rulings from these sources.

recs.q: What are the real part and the imaginary part of the complex number -3 + 4i?
recs.facts: In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part. Here a = -3 and b = 4.
recs.rel: i is defined by i squared = -1.

recs.q: What is the imaginary part of the complex number 7 - 2i?
recs.facts: Write 7 - 2i as 7 + (-2)i. The imaginary part is the coefficient of i, which is -2.
recs.rel: The conjugate of 7 - 2i is 7 + 2i.

recs.q: For which sport is Imam-ul-Haq famous?
recs.facts: Imam-ul-Haq is a left-handed Pakistani cricketer who plays as an opening batsman for the national team.
recs.rel: He is the nephew of former Pakistan captain Inzamam-ul-Haq.

recs.q: In which year was the International Monetary Fund (IMF) established?
recs.facts: The IMF was formally established in December 1945 after the Bretton Woods conference of July 1944, and began operations in 1947.
recs.rel: Some sources say 1944 because the agreement was drawn up at Bretton Woods that year.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
recs.facts: The IMF has its headquarters in Washington DC, United States, close to the World Bank.
recs.rel: The UN headquarters is in New York and the WTO is in Geneva.

recs.q: When was the third martial law imposed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977 by removing the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
recs.rel: The earlier martial laws were in 1958 (Ayub Khan) and 1969 (Yahya Khan); General Musharraf took power in 1999 without declaring martial law.

recs.q: What was the Kargil incident?
opts: A 1999 conflict between Pakistan and India in the Kargil sector of Kashmir
The 1965 war in the Rann of Kutch
recs.facts: In 1999 fighting took place in the Kargil district of Kashmir after infiltration across the Line of Control, ending in July 1999.
recs.rel: The Kargil conflict took place during the premiership of Nawaz Sharif.

recs.q: In a village the population was 16000 in the year 2000. If the population becomes 5 times every year, what was the population in 1998?
recs.facts: Each year the population is multiplied by 5. So 1999 was 16000 / 5 = 3200, and 1998 was 3200 / 5 = 640.
recs.rel: Going back in time means dividing by the growth factor.

recs.q: On what date did India get independence?
recs.facts: India became independent from British rule on 15 August 1947, one day after Pakistan.
recs.rel: India celebrates Republic Day on 26 January because its constitution came into force in 1950.

recs.q: In which years did Israel and Singapore get independence respectively?
recs.facts: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, and Singapore became independent from Malaysia on 9 August 1965.
recs.rel: Singapore first got self-government in 1959.

recs.q: Which law was adopted as the interim constitution of Pakistan after independence in 1947?
recs.facts: Pakistan adopted the Government of India Act 1935, with amendments, as its interim constitution until the 1956 constitution came into force.
recs.rel: The Objectives Resolution was passed in March 1949.

recs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
recs.facts: In Euclidean geometry the three interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.
recs.rel: The interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.

recs.q: What is the integral of sin x with respect to x?
recs.facts: The derivative of cos x is -sin x, so the derivative of -cos x is sin x. Hence the integral of sin x is -cos x + C.
recs.rel: The integral of cos x is sin x + C.

recs.q: What is the integral of tan x with respect to x?
recs.facts: Write tan x as sin x over cos x and put u = cos x; the integral becomes -ln |cos x| + C, which equals ln |sec x| + C.
recs.rel: The derivative of tan x is sec squared x.

recs.q: What is the antonym of interim?
recs.facts: Interim means temporary, so its opposite is permanent.
recs.rel: Provisional and temporary are synonyms of interim.

recs.q: How far does Pakistan's territorial sea extend from its baseline?
recs.facts: Pakistan's Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act of 1976 fixed the territorial sea at 12 nautical miles, in line with international law.
recs.rel: Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles.

recs.q: On which date in 1933 was the name Pakistan first put forward by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in the pamphlet Now or Never?
recs.facts: Choudhry Rahmat Ali issued the pamphlet Now or Never on 28 January 1933 and proposed the name Pakistan in it.
recs.rel: The Lahore Resolution came later, on 23 March 1940.

recs.q: Which of the following is the multiplicative inverse form of the 2 by 2 matrix with entries a, b in the first row and c, d in the second row?
opts: Matrix with d, -b in the first row and -c, a in the second row, multiplied by 1/(ad - bc)
Matrix with a, c and b, d, multiplied by 1/(ad - bc)
Matrix with d, b and c, a, multiplied by (ad - bc)
recs.facts: For a 2 by 2 matrix, swap a and d, change the signs of b and c, and divide by the determinant ad - bc.
recs.rel: The inverse exists only when the determinant is not zero.

recs.q: The inverse of a square matrix exists only if what condition holds?
recs.facts: The inverse equals the adjoint divided by the determinant, so the determinant must not be zero; such a matrix is called non-singular.
recs.rel: A matrix with zero determinant is called singular.

recs.q: What is the additive inverse of the ordered pair (-a, -b)?
recs.facts: The additive inverse is the pair that gives (0, 0) when added. (-a, -b) + (a, b) = (0, 0), so the answer is (a, b).
recs.rel: The additive identity of ordered pairs is (0, 0).

recs.q: What is the capital of Iran?
recs.facts: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.
recs.rel: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which type of number is 9/2?
recs.facts: 9/2 is a ratio of two integers, so it is rational, and every rational number is also a real number.
recs.rel: As a decimal, 9/2 equals 4.5, which terminates.

recs.q: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is known by which title?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah, the one offered for sacrifice, in the story of Hazrat Ibrahim's (AS) dream.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah.

recs.q: Which battle was fought by the Muslims after the Battle of Badr, as the second major battle of Islam?
recs.facts: Badr was fought in 2 AH and the Battle of Uhud followed in Shawwal 3 AH.
recs.rel: Uhud is a mountain near Madinah.

recs.q: Which is the 7th month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
recs.facts: The months are Muharram, Safar, Rabi-ul-Awwal, Rabi-ul-Sani, Jamadi-ul-Awwal, Jamadi-ul-Sani, then Rajab as the seventh.
recs.rel: Rajab is one of the four sacred months, and Shab-e-Meraj is observed in it.

recs.q: What is the capital of Israel as declared by Israel?
recs.facts: Israel declares Jerusalem as its capital, although most countries keep their embassies in Tel Aviv and the status of Jerusalem is disputed.
recs.rel: Pakistan does not recognise Israel.

recs.q: If the National Assembly and the Senate disagree on a bill, who resolves the issue under the Constitution of Pakistan?
opts: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament
recs.facts: Under Article 70 of the 1973 Constitution, a disputed bill is put before a joint sitting of both Houses and is passed by a majority of the total members present and voting.
recs.rel: The joint sitting is summoned by the President.

recs.q: What is the capital of Italy?
recs.facts: Rome is the capital and largest city of Italy.
recs.rel: Vatican City, the smallest country in the world, lies inside Rome.

recs.q: Who is the President of Italy?
recs.facts: Sergio Mattarella has been President of Italy since 2015 and was re-elected for a second term in 2022.
recs.rel: Giorgia Meloni is the Prime Minister of Italy, not the President.

recs.q: Where is Jannat-ul-Mualla (Jannatul Mula), the famous graveyard?
recs.facts: Jannat-ul-Mualla is the historic cemetery of Makkah, where Hazrat Khadijah (RA) is buried.
recs.rel: The famous graveyard of Madina is Jannat-ul-Baqi.

recs.q: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a famous book of what?
recs.facts: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of hadith compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.
recs.rel: It is counted among the Sihah Sittah, the six authentic books of hadith.

recs.q: Which of the following is a member of SAARC?
recs.facts: Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 as its eighth member, while Iran, Japan and China are only observers.
recs.rel: The other members are Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

recs.q: Banu Quraizah, a tribe of Madina, belonged to which religion?
recs.facts: Banu Quraizah was a Jewish tribe of Madina.
recs.rel: They broke their pact during the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab).

recs.q: Fill in the blank: ____ MA degree is requisite to get a job.
recs.facts: MA is pronounced em-ay, which begins with a vowel sound, so the article an is used.
recs.rel: The article depends on the sound, not the spelling, as in an hour and a university.

recs.q: Which defence organization did Pakistan join in 1954?
recs.facts: Pakistan joined the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) in September 1954.
recs.rel: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact, later CENTO, in 1955.

recs.q: According to hadith, about which act will a person be questioned first on the Day of Judgment in matters of worship?
recs.facts: The Prophet (SAW) said the first deed for which a servant will be called to account is his prayer (Salah).
recs.rel: Among matters between people, the first judgment will be about bloodshed.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Abu Jahl killed?
recs.facts: Abu Jahl was killed in the Battle of Badr, which took place in Ramadan 2 AH.
recs.rel: He was killed by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.

recs.q: Kabul is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Kabul is the capital and largest city of Afghanistan.
recs.rel: Kabul lies on the Kabul River and is close to the Khyber Pass route to Pakistan.

recs.q: On which river is the city of Kabul located?
recs.facts: The city of Kabul stands on the banks of the Kabul River.
recs.rel: The Kabul River flows into Pakistan and joins the Indus near Attock.

recs.q: Kaghan Valley is located in which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: Kaghan Valley lies in the Mansehra district of Hazara in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: Babusar Pass at the head of the valley connects it to Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.

recs.q: Hilal-e-Kashmir, the highest military gallantry award of Azad Kashmir, was awarded to whom?
recs.facts: Naik Saif Ali Janjua received it after dying in the 1947-48 war in Kashmir, and he is its only recipient.
recs.rel: It was declared equal to the Nishan-e-Haider in 1995.

recs.q: Which of these countries is not a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
recs.facts: Turkmenistan has never joined the SCO, while Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, China and Pakistan are members.
recs.rel: Pakistan and India became full SCO members in 2017.

recs.q: Between the Muslims and whom was the Ghazwa Khandaq (Battle of the Trench) fought?
recs.facts: The Quraish of Makkah joined with other Arab tribes and Jewish tribes to attack Madinah in 5 AH.
recs.rel: The battle is also called Ghazwa Ahzab, meaning the battle of the confederates.

recs.q: Against whom was the Khilafat Movement in India directed?
recs.facts: The movement, led by Muslims of India, opposed British treatment of the Ottoman Caliph after World War I.
recs.rel: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word justify?
recs.facts: To justify means to show something to be right or reasonable, and vindicate has a similar meaning.
recs.rel: Justification is the noun form of justify.

recs.q: Who led the Khilafat Movement in India?
recs.facts: The Khilafat Movement (1919 to 1924) was led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and his brother Maulana Shaukat Ali. It aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
recs.rel: Mahatma Gandhi of the Indian National Congress also supported the Khilafat Movement.

recs.q: What was the main theme of the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
opts: Human rights, equality and the abolition of all discrimination
recs.facts: In the Last Sermon the Prophet (SAW) declared that all humans are equal and that no Arab is superior to a non-Arab except by piety. He also stressed the sanctity of life, property and the rights of women.
recs.rel: It is regarded as one of the earliest charters of human rights.

recs.q: Where did the Holy Prophet (SAW) deliver his first Friday sermon (khutba) after migrating to Madina?
opts: Valley of Ranuna (Banu Salim bin Auf)
recs.facts: On the way to Madina the Prophet (SAW) led the first Jumuah prayer and delivered the first khutba in the valley of Ranuna, in the territory of Banu Salim bin Auf.
recs.rel: The first mosque built in Islam was the Quba mosque, where he stayed for some days before entering Madina.

recs.q: Where was the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat-ul-Wida) delivered?
recs.facts: The Last Sermon was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah 10 AH during the Farewell Pilgrimage, at the plain of Arafat in the valley of Uranah.
recs.rel: The Prophet (SAW) passed away about three months after the Farewell Pilgrimage.

recs.q: What type of fraction is 11/9?
recs.facts: In 11/9 the numerator 11 is greater than the denominator 9, so it is an improper fraction. It equals 1 and 2/9 as a mixed number.
recs.rel: Every fraction of two integers, including 11/9, is also a rational number.

recs.q: What was the old name of the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
recs.facts: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was formerly called the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP). It was renamed through the 18th Amendment in 2010.
recs.rel: The province was given its present name in April 2010.

recs.q: KRL (Khan Research Laboratories) is best known in Pakistan for work on which field?
opts: Uranium enrichment and nuclear and missile technology
recs.facts: KRL at Kahuta developed uranium enrichment using centrifuges and also worked on missiles such as the Ghauri.
recs.rel: Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan is regarded as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme.

recs.q: What is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range?
recs.facts: Tirich Mir, in Chitral, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush at about 7708 metres.
recs.rel: K2 and Nanga Parbat belong to the Karakoram and Himalaya ranges respectively.

recs.q: Which of the following is a land-locked country?
recs.facts: Nepal has no sea coast and is surrounded by India and China. The other three countries all have a coastline.
recs.rel: Afghanistan, Bhutan and Uzbekistan are other land-locked countries of Asia.

recs.q: How many official languages does the United Nations (UNO) have?
recs.facts: The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.
recs.rel: English and French are the two working languages of the UN Secretariat.

recs.q: About how many languages are spoken in the world today?
recs.facts: Language surveys such as Ethnologue count roughly 7,100 living languages in the world.
recs.rel: The exact number changes slightly every year as languages are documented or die out.

recs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) is known by which of these titles?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) is called Asadullah (Lion of Allah). Saifullah is Khalid bin Waleed, Siddiq is Abu Bakr and Farooq is Umar (RA).
recs.rel: He is also known as Haidar-e-Karrar and Abu Turab.

recs.q: Which is the largest island in the world?
recs.facts: Greenland covers about 2.16 million square kilometres, more than any other island. Australia is counted as a continent.
recs.rel: New Guinea is the second largest island.

recs.q: What is the LCM of 12 and 24?
recs.facts: 24 is a multiple of 12 and of itself, and no smaller number is a multiple of 24. So LCM is 24.
recs.rel: If one number divides the other, the larger number is the LCM.

recs.q: What is the LCM of 6 and 8?
recs.facts: 6 = 2 x 3 and 8 = 2 x 2 x 2, so LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 24.
recs.rel: HCF of 6 and 8 is 2, and 24 x 2 = 48 = 6 x 8.

recs.q: Which was the first short-range ballistic missile developed and tested by Pakistan?
recs.facts: Hatf-I was Pakistan's first indigenous short-range ballistic missile, tested in 1989.
recs.rel: Ghauri and Shaheen are medium-range missiles and Babur is a cruise missile.

recs.q: In which year was Instagram launched?
recs.facts: Instagram was launched in October 2010 by Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger.
recs.rel: Facebook bought Instagram in 2012.

recs.q: Which country launched the Tianhe core module of its space station into space?
recs.facts: China launched the Tianhe core module of the Tiangong space station in April 2021.
recs.rel: Tianhe means Heavenly Harmony.

recs.q: Who led the enemy forces against the Muslims in the Battle of Yamama?
recs.facts: Musailima the Liar claimed to be a prophet and was defeated and killed at the Battle of Yamama in 632 CE under Khalid bin Waleed.
recs.rel: The battle took place in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

recs.q: The maple leaf is shown on the flag of which country?
recs.facts: The red maple leaf in the centre of the white square is the national emblem of Canada.
recs.rel: The Canadian flag was adopted in 1965.

recs.q: The Parliament of Pakistan is of which type?
recs.facts: It has two houses: the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house).
recs.rel: Pakistan has a parliamentary form of government under the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: Which letter comes after H in the English alphabet?
recs.facts: The order is G, H, I, so I follows H.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U.

recs.q: Points that all lie on the same straight line are called what?
recs.facts: Collinear points lie on one straight line.
recs.rel: Coplanar points lie in the same plane.

recs.q: How many midpoints does a line segment have?
recs.facts: A line segment has exactly one midpoint, the point equidistant from both ends.
recs.rel: A full line extends infinitely and has no midpoint.

recs.q: The straight line given by the equation y = 6x passes through which point?
recs.facts: Putting x = 0 gives y = 6 times 0 = 0, so the line passes through (0, 0). Every line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.
recs.rel: In y = mx, the number m is the slope of the line, which is 6 here.

recs.q: Is the expression 2x + 3x + 1 = 0 a linear equation?
opts: No, because it has three terms
No, because it has two x terms
recs.facts: Adding the like terms gives 5x + 1 = 0. The highest power of x is 1, so it is a linear equation.
recs.rel: A linear equation in one variable has exactly one root.

recs.q: What is the degree of a linear equation?
recs.facts: In a linear equation the highest power of the variable is 1, so its degree is 1.
recs.rel: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line.

recs.q: Which region of Pakistan is commonly called Little Tibet?
recs.facts: Baltistan, with its capital Skardu, resembles Tibet in culture, language and landscape, so it is called Little Tibet.
recs.rel: Ladakh in India is also sometimes called Little Tibet.

recs.q: Which is the longest river entirely in England?
recs.facts: The Thames, about 346 km long, is the longest river wholly in England.
recs.rel: The Severn is longer overall (354 km) but part of it flows through Wales.

recs.q: Who was Lord Curzon at the time of the partition of Bengal in 1905?
recs.facts: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy and Governor-General of India from 1899 to 1905 and he carried out the partition of Bengal in 1905.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: Who designed the Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore?
recs.facts: The Minar-e-Pakistan was designed by the Russian-born architect Nasreddin Murat-Khan.
recs.rel: It was built in Iqbal Park, Lahore, where the Lahore Resolution was passed in 1940.

recs.q: What is the main religion of Pakistan?
recs.facts: About 96 percent of Pakistanis are Muslims, so Islam is the main religion and the state religion.
recs.rel: Article 2 of the Constitution declares Islam the state religion of Pakistan.

recs.q: On which date is the Mairaj (Shab-e-Mairaj) commemorated?
recs.facts: The night journey and ascension of the Prophet (PBUH) is observed on the night of 27 Rajab.
recs.rel: Shab-e-Barat is on 15 Shaban.

recs.q: Which Sahabi is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Ahzab (verse 37) mentions Zaid bin Harithah (RA) by name.
recs.rel: The Quran mentions Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by name four times.

recs.q: Which Air Force rank is equivalent to the Army rank of Major?
recs.facts: Squadron Leader equals Major in the Army and Lieutenant Commander in the Navy.
recs.rel: Wing Commander equals Lieutenant Colonel.

recs.q: Who was the first woman promoted to the rank of Major General in the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: Dr Shahida Malik, a medical doctor, became the first woman Major General in 2002.
recs.rel: Nigar Johar became the first woman Lieutenant General in 2020.

recs.q: A tangent to a circle makes what angle with the radius drawn to the point of contact?
recs.facts: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the angle is 90 degrees.
recs.rel: From an external point two tangents of equal length can be drawn to a circle.

recs.q: On which river is Dushanbe, the capital of Tajikistan, located?
recs.facts: Dushanbe lies in the Gissar valley on the Varzob River, which is called Dushanbinka within the city.
recs.rel: Dushanbe is the capital of Tajikistan, not a European city.

recs.q: In which mountain range is the Siachen Glacier located?
recs.facts: The Siachen Glacier lies in the eastern Karakoram range in the disputed Kashmir region.
recs.rel: It is about 76 km long and is among the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

recs.q: In a class of 24 people, 2/3 are male. How many females are there?
recs.facts: Males = 2/3 of 24 = 16. Females = 24 - 16 = 8.
recs.rel: Females here are 1/3 of the class.

recs.q: In a class of 24 students, 2/3 are male. What is the percentage of females?
recs.facts: Females are 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the class. 1/3 of 100 is 33.33%.
recs.rel: The percentage of females does not depend on the class size when the fraction is given.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Malta (2026)?
recs.facts: Robert Abela (Labour Party) has been Prime Minister since 2020 and was sworn in again in June 2026 after the general election.
recs.rel: Joseph Muscat was Prime Minister of Malta before Abela, from 2013 to 2020.

recs.q: Who is the President of Malta (2026)?
recs.facts: Myriam Spiteri Debono has been President of Malta since April 2024.
recs.rel: Her predecessor George Vella served from 2019 to 2024.

recs.q: Which is the famous man-made forest of Pakistan, located in Punjab?
recs.facts: Changa Manga near Lahore is one of the largest hand-planted forests, created in the 1860s by the British.
recs.rel: Changa Manga is in Kasur district, Punjab.

recs.q: Which letter is the third from the end (last) in the word MANAGEMENT?
recs.facts: The word ends with E, N, T. Counting from the end: T is 1st, N is 2nd, E is 3rd.
recs.rel: Counting from the end gives E while counting from the start gives N.

recs.q: In which country is Manchar Lake located?
recs.facts: Manchar Lake is in Sindh province, Pakistan, west of the Indus river.
recs.rel: It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.

recs.q: Manchar Lake in Sindh lies near which town?
recs.facts: Manchar Lake is located near Sehwan Sharif in the Dadu and Jamshoro area of Sindh.
recs.rel: Manchar Lake is Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.

recs.q: Mangla Dam is located near which city?
recs.facts: Mangla Dam is built near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
recs.rel: Mangla Dam is the second largest dam of Pakistan.

recs.q: Mangla Dam is built on which river?
recs.facts: Mangla Dam stands on the river Jhelum.
recs.rel: Tarbela Dam, in contrast, is on the Indus.

recs.q: How many kilometres long is a marathon race?
recs.facts: The official marathon distance is 42.195 km, which equals 26 miles and 385 yards.
recs.rel: The marathon is named after the legendary run from Marathon to Athens.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Maryam (AS)?
recs.facts: The Quran calls her 'Maryam daughter of Imran', and her father is named Imran.
recs.rel: Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was her guardian, not her father.

recs.q: Which is the highest individual ODI score by a Pakistani batsman?
recs.facts: Fakhar Zaman made 210 not out against Zimbabwe at Bulawayo in July 2018, beating Saeed Anwar's 194.
recs.rel: Saeed Anwar's 194 against India in 1997 had been the Pakistan record for 21 years.

recs.q: Which word fills the blank: He teaches us English ___ mathematics.
recs.facts: Besides means in addition to, which suits the sentence. Beside means next to.
recs.rel: Besides is also used as an adverb meaning moreover.

recs.q: Two matrices A and B are inverse of each other when:
recs.facts: Matrices A and B are inverses if their product in both orders equals the identity matrix I.
recs.rel: Only square matrices can have an inverse.

recs.q: A matrix having the same number of rows and columns (m = n) is called:
recs.facts: When the number of rows equals the number of columns, the matrix is a square matrix.
recs.rel: A matrix with one row only is called a row matrix.

recs.q: What are the vertical lines of entries in a matrix called?
recs.facts: Vertical lines of entries are columns, and horizontal lines are rows.
recs.rel: A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns.

recs.q: In which country was the phrase Black Lives Matter first used (as a hashtag in 2013)?
recs.facts: It began as the hashtag #BlackLivesMatter in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
recs.rel: The movement became global after the death of George Floyd in 2020.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'emancipation'?
recs.facts: Emancipation means being set free from legal, social or political restrictions, such as slavery.
recs.rel: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the Arabic word 'Hikmah'?
recs.facts: Hikmah means wisdom, sound judgement.
recs.rel: Al-Hakim, a name of Allah, comes from the same root.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'Sirat'?
recs.facts: Sirat means a path or road, as in Sirat-al-Mustaqeem, the straight path.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Fatihah asks Allah to guide us to the straight path.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'subsequently'?
recs.facts: Subsequently means at a later time, afterwards.
recs.rel: Its opposite is previously.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'amicability'?
recs.facts: Amicability means a friendly and peaceful attitude.
recs.rel: Its adjective is amicable.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'Ansari'?
opts: Helper (descendant of the Ansar of Madinah)
recs.facts: Ansar means helpers, the people of Madinah who helped the Muslim emigrants. Ansari relates to them.
recs.rel: The emigrants from Makkah are called Muhajirin.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'antique'?
recs.facts: An antique is an old object, usually valuable because of its age.
recs.rel: Antiques are generally at least 100 years old.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'cohesive'?
opts: Sticking together as a united whole
recs.facts: Cohesive means holding together firmly and united.
recs.rel: The noun is cohesion.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'doubt'?
recs.facts: Doubt means a feeling of uncertainty about something.
recs.rel: Its opposite is certainty or confidence.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'mitigate'?
opts: To make less severe or serious
recs.facts: To mitigate means to reduce the severity, seriousness or harm of something. For example, planting trees mitigates the effect of floods.
recs.rel: Mitigation is a common word in disaster management, as in flood mitigation.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'recalcitrant'?
recs.facts: A recalcitrant person obstinately refuses to obey rules or accept control. It is used for uncooperative people or animals.
recs.rel: Its synonyms include defiant, unruly and obstinate.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the verb 'rob'?
opts: To take property unlawfully, often by force
recs.facts: To rob means to steal from a person or place, usually using force or threat. A person who does this is called a robber.
recs.rel: Robbery differs from burglary because robbery involves force or threat against a person.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the Urdu/Arabic word 'Seerat'?
recs.facts: Seerat means a person's life, conduct and character, and is used mainly for the biography of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). It is also written as Seerah.
recs.rel: The earliest well-known Seerat of the Prophet (PBUH) was written by Ibn Ishaq and edited by Ibn Hisham.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'Zamzam'?
recs.facts: Zamzam is the name of the sacred well in Makkah, and the word is linked to plentiful, gushing water. The well sprang near the Kaaba for Hazrat Ismail (AS) and his mother Hazrat Hajra.
recs.rel: Pilgrims drink Zamzam water during Hajj and Umrah, and Sai is performed between Safa and Marwa near it.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'Iltijaa'?
recs.facts: Iltijaa is an Urdu word of Arabic origin meaning a humble request, plea or entreaty. It is used for earnestly asking someone for help.
recs.rel: Related words are darkhwast, arzi and dua, all meaning a request or prayer.

recs.q: What is the median of 2, 3, 5, 7?
recs.facts: There are 4 values, so the median is the mean of the two middle values 3 and 5. (3 + 5) / 2 = 4.
recs.rel: The mean of 2, 3, 5, 7 is 4.25, which differs from the median.

recs.q: What is the median of 3, 4, 7, 8, 6?
recs.facts: Arrange in order: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8. There are 5 values, so the median is the 3rd value, which is 6.
recs.rel: The mean of these numbers is 5.6, not the median.

recs.q: On what date did Pakistan become a member of SAARC?
recs.facts: Pakistan was one of the seven founding members of SAARC at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985. It did not join later.
recs.rel: Afghanistan became the eighth member in April 2007.

recs.q: How many member states does the United Nations have?
recs.facts: The UN has 193 member states. South Sudan was the latest to join, in 2011.
recs.rel: The Holy See and Palestine are non-member observer states.

recs.q: Which names of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) are mentioned in the Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran directly uses the names Muhammad (four times) and Ahmad (once, in Surah As-Saff). Other titles like Taha and Yasin are separate.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) is also addressed in the Quran with titles such as Nabi and Rasool.

recs.q: How many metres are there in 2 km?
recs.rel: One kilometre is about 0.62 miles.

recs.q: What is the midpoint of the points (4, 6) and (2, 6)?
recs.rel: Both points have the same y value, so the segment is horizontal.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'broke down' in the sentence: The car broke down one mile away from home?
recs.facts: To break down means a machine or vehicle stops working because of a fault. So the car stopped working one mile from home.
recs.rel: Break down can also mean to lose emotional control or to analyse something in parts.

recs.q: Which country has the largest number of active military personnel in the world?
recs.facts: China's People's Liberation Army has about two million active personnel, the most in the world. India and the United States follow.
recs.rel: Rankings change slowly, and India has the second-largest active force in most recent lists.

recs.q: Which of the following is a military alliance?
recs.facts: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is a collective defence military alliance founded in 1949. SAARC is regional cooperation, OPEC deals with oil and WTO with trade.
recs.rel: Its Article 5 says an attack on one member is an attack on all.

recs.q: What is the minimum age to become President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution says the President must be a Muslim, qualified to be a National Assembly member and at least 45 years old.
recs.rel: The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and the provincial assemblies.

recs.q: Who is the Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Muhammad Aurangzeb took charge as Finance Minister in March 2024 and presented the FY2026-27 budget. He is still in office in October 2026.
recs.rel: In 2022 the finance minister was Miftah Ismail, followed by Ishaq Dar.

recs.q: A train covers 20 km in one hour. About how much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
recs.facts: 1 hour is 60 minutes, so distance per minute is 20 divided by 60, which is 0.33 km. This is about 333 metres.
recs.rel: Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives km per minute.

recs.q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how many papers does he write in one minute?
recs.facts: Rate is 5 papers divided by 5 minutes, which is 1 paper per minute.
recs.rel: Rate equals work divided by time.

recs.q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 1 minute, how much time will 1 man take to write 1 page?
recs.facts: 5 men write 5 pages in 1 minute, so each man writes 1 page in 1 minute. One man therefore needs 1 minute for 1 page.
recs.rel: If each worker works at the same rate, work per worker is total work divided by number of workers.

recs.q: What was the real name of the Bengali freedom fighter Tito Mir?
recs.facts: Tito Mir's real name was Syed Mir Nisar Ali. He led a peasant uprising against landlords and the British in Bengal in 1831.
recs.rel: He built a bamboo fort at Narkelberia and died fighting in 1831.

recs.q: If a helicopter needs 80 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km is 80 divided by 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 400 km, 400 x 0.25 = 100 gallons.
recs.rel: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th be?
recs.facts: The 9th is 7 days after the 2nd. After a full week the day repeats, so it is Monday.
recs.rel: Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: In which year did Lord Mountbatten arrive in India as the last Viceroy?
recs.facts: Lord Mountbatten arrived in India in March 1947 to oversee the transfer of power. He announced the Partition plan on 3 June 1947.
recs.rel: He later became the first Governor General of independent India.

recs.q: A train moves at 120 km/h. What distance does it cover in 120 minutes?
recs.facts: 120 minutes is 2 hours. Distance = 120 x 2 = 240 km.
recs.rel: Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60.

recs.q: A train is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes?
recs.facts: 10 minutes is 1/6 hour. Distance = 60 x 1/6 = 10 km.
recs.rel: At 60 km/h a train covers 1 km each minute.

recs.q: In which year was Islamabad officially made the capital of Pakistan, replacing Rawalpindi as interim capital?
recs.facts: Karachi was first capital, then Rawalpindi served as interim capital while Islamabad was built. Islamabad officially became the capital in 1967.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact year, since the decision was taken in 1959-60 and the shift happened in stages.

recs.q: Who moved the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1949?
recs.facts: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objective Resolution, and it was passed on 12 March 1949.
recs.rel: It later became the preamble of the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: Which of the following is one of the Ashra Mubashra?
recs.facts: Hazrat Talha bin Ubaidullah (RA) is among the ten Companions given the glad tidings of Paradise. The others listed are not in the group.
recs.rel: The ten include Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah.

recs.q: What is the relation between multiplication and division?
recs.facts: Division undoes multiplication, so they are inverse operations. For example, 6 x 4 = 24 and 24 / 4 = 6.
recs.rel: Addition and subtraction are also inverse operations.

recs.q: What is the title of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him directly.
recs.rel: Khalilullah is Ibrahim, Safiullah is Adam and Ruhullah is Isa.

recs.q: Who was the mother of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb. Halima Sadia was his wet nurse.
recs.rel: Hazrat Amina passed away when he was about 6 years old.

recs.q: Which one is different from the following: actor, director, music, producer?
recs.facts: Actor, director and producer are all people who work on a film, while music is a thing, not a person.
recs.rel: Odd-one-out questions are solved by finding the item of a different category.

recs.q: Who was the Habshi (Abyssinian) king Najashi, who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
recs.facts: Najashi was the title of the Abyssinian king, whose real name was Ashama bin Abjar.
recs.rel: When he died in 9 AH, the Prophet (SAW) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.

recs.q: What is Namaz-e-Ishraq?
opts: An optional prayer offered after sunrise
A prayer offered during an eclipse
recs.facts: Ishraq is an optional (nafl) prayer offered about 15 to 20 minutes after sunrise, after the Fajr prayer.
recs.rel: Namaz-e-Istisqa is the prayer for rain.

recs.q: Where is the National Museum of Pakistan located?
recs.facts: The National Museum of Pakistan is in Karachi, in the Burnes Garden area.
recs.rel: The Lahore Museum is a separate and older museum.

recs.q: How many member countries does NATO have at present?
recs.facts: NATO has 32 members, after Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.
recs.rel: NATO was founded in 1949 with 12 members.

recs.q: Is sin x positive or negative in the first quadrant?
recs.facts: In the first quadrant the y-coordinate is positive and sin x equals y divided by r, so it is positive.
recs.rel: In the first quadrant all six trigonometric ratios are positive.

recs.q: The line x = 3 is ______ to the X axis.
recs.facts: The line x = 3 is a vertical line, and a vertical line meets the horizontal X axis at a right angle.
recs.rel: The line x = 3 is parallel to the Y axis.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Mrs. Rehan is not pleased ___ the new servant.
recs.facts: The adjective pleased is followed by the preposition with when it refers to a person. So the correct sentence is: not pleased with the new servant.
recs.rel: Other common adjective and preposition pairs are angry with, good at and afraid of.

recs.q: What is a bill called after it has been passed by Parliament and approved by the President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: A bill passed by both houses and assented to by the President becomes an Act of Parliament, which is law. An ordinance is a temporary law issued by the President when Parliament is not in session.
recs.rel: Under Article 75 of the Constitution the President has ten days to assent to a bill or return it.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: 3A, 5C, 7E, ?
recs.facts: The numbers increase by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9) and the letters skip one letter each time (A, C, E, G). So the next term is 9G.
recs.rel: The letters A, C, E, G are the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of the alphabet.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: 3x+4, 4x+2, ?
recs.facts: The coefficient of x increases by 1 each time (3, 4, 5) and the constant decreases by 2 (4, 2, 0). So the next term is 5x+0 = 5x.
recs.rel: Such a pattern is two arithmetic progressions running together.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: B2, C3, D4, E5, F?
recs.facts: Each letter moves one step forward and each number increases by 1. F pairs with 6, so the next term is F6.
recs.rel: B is the 2nd letter, C the 3rd, and so on, so each letter pairs with its own position number.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: 3W, 6X, 9Z, ?
recs.facts: The numbers increase by 3 (3, 6, 9, 12). The letters move forward by 1, then 2, then 3: W to X to Z to C (after Z the alphabet starts again). So the next term is 12C.
recs.rel: In such letter series, the alphabet is treated as a circle, so Z is followed by A.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, ?
recs.facts: These are the squares 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4. The next is 5x5 = 25.
recs.rel: The gaps between squares are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 155, 65, 165, 75, ?
recs.facts: The terms in odd positions go 155, 165 and the terms in even positions go 65, 75, each rising by 10. So the next term is 165 + 10 = 175.
recs.rel: This is an alternating series made of two separate series.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 2, 4, 6, 8, ?
recs.facts: Each number is 2 more than the one before it. So 8 + 2 = 10.
recs.rel: These are the first even natural numbers.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 9, 12, ?
recs.facts: Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 12 + 3 = 15.
recs.rel: This is the table of 3.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 9, ?
recs.facts: Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 9 + 3 = 12.
recs.rel: This is the table of 3.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 5, 10, 15, ?
recs.facts: Each number is 5 more than the one before. So 15 + 5 = 20.
recs.rel: This is the table of 5.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 66, 63, 57, 45, 21, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 3, 6, 12, 24, each double the last. The next difference is 48, so 21 - 48 = -27.
recs.rel: The same series appears as 66, 63, 57, 45, 21 where the next term after 45 is 21.

recs.q: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar served as the Governor of which province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a leader of the Pakistan Movement, was Governor of Punjab from 1949 to 1951.
recs.rel: Nishtar Medical University in Multan is named after him.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Zakat made obligatory?
recs.facts: According to the commonly taught view, Zakat became obligatory in the second year of Hijri, around the time Ramadan fasting was ordained. Some scholars give slightly different years.
recs.rel: Sources differ a little on the exact year of Zakat.

recs.q: School is a noun. Which pronoun can be used in its place?
recs.facts: A school is a singular, non-living thing, so the pronoun it is used for it.
recs.rel: The plural pronoun for schools is they.

recs.q: What is the word used in place of a noun called?
recs.facts: A pronoun is used in place of a noun to avoid repeating it, such as he, she, it and they.
recs.rel: Words like he, she and it are personal pronouns.

recs.q: What is the total number of nuclear-armed countries in the world today?
recs.facts: Nine countries have nuclear weapons: the USA, Russia, the UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, Israel (undeclared) and North Korea.
recs.rel: Pakistan is the only Muslim country with nuclear weapons.

recs.q: 13, 15, 17 and 19 are what type of numbers?
recs.facts: Each of these numbers leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
recs.rel: The only even prime number is 2.

recs.q: If a set has two elements, how many elements are in its power set?
recs.facts: The power set of a set with n elements has 2 to the power n elements. For n = 2 this is 4: the empty set, two single-element subsets, and the set itself.
