recs.rel: A set with 3 elements has a power set of 8 elements.

recs.q: Which languages were declared official languages of Pakistan by the 1962 constitution?
recs.facts: The 1962 constitution recognised Urdu and Bengali as the national languages of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The 1956 constitution had also named Urdu and Bengali as state languages.

recs.q: Which is generally regarded as the oldest city of Pakistan according to Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Peshawar is commonly described as the oldest living city of Pakistan, inhabited for over 2,500 years.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as Multan is also claimed to be among the oldest cities in South Asia.

recs.q: For whom are the Special Olympics held?
recs.facts: The Special Olympics are sports competitions for people with intellectual disabilities.
recs.rel: The Paralympic Games are held for athletes with physical disabilities.

recs.q: What is the capital of Oman?
recs.facts: Muscat is the capital and largest city of Oman.
recs.rel: Oman is ruled by a Sultan and is located on the south-eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: Open the door.
recs.facts: An imperative sentence is changed into the passive using Let + object + be + past participle, giving Let the door be opened.
recs.rel: Imperative sentences express commands, requests or advice.

recs.q: What does Allama Iqbal Open University mainly promote?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal Open University in Islamabad provides distance and open education to students who cannot attend regular institutions.
recs.rel: It was established in 1974 as the People's Open University and renamed in 1977.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: She opened the door ____.
recs.facts: A word describing how an action is done must be an adverb, so slowly is correct.
recs.rel: Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding ly to an adjective.

recs.q: What is the opposite of contiguous?
recs.facts: Contiguous means sharing a border or touching, so its opposite is separated or detached.
recs.rel: Contiguous comes from the Latin contingere, meaning to touch.

recs.q: What is 14 - 6 - 4?
recs.rel: Subtraction is carried out from left to right.

recs.q: What is the order of a square matrix having n rows?
recs.facts: A square matrix has equal rows and columns, so its order is n x n.
recs.rel: A 3 x 3 matrix is a square matrix of order 3.

recs.q: What are the coordinates of the origin on a Cartesian graph?
recs.facts: The origin is the point where the x-axis and y-axis cross, so both its x and y values are zero.
recs.rel: The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants that meet at the origin.

recs.q: Who built the Quba Mosque, the first mosque in Islam?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) laid the foundation of the Quba Mosque near Madinah on his Hijrah, and the Companions helped build it.
recs.rel: The Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) refers to a mosque founded on piety from the first day, which scholars identify as Quba.

recs.q: In which period was the first war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir fought?
recs.facts: The first Indo-Pak war over Kashmir began in October 1947 after tribal and Pakistani forces entered the state and India sent troops. It ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire on 1 January 1949.
recs.rel: The ceasefire line later became the Line of Control after the Simla Agreement of 1972.

recs.q: The Dawn newspaper is owned by which family-run group?
recs.facts: Dawn is published by Dawn Media Group, which is controlled by the Haroon family (with the Saigol family). The Haroon family bought majority shares in 1946.
recs.rel: Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in Delhi in 1941.

recs.q: What was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
opts: An agreement that ended the Civil Disobedience Movement and let Gandhi attend the Second Round Table Conference
A pact between Congress and the Muslim League
recs.facts: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy Lord Irwin. Congress suspended civil disobedience and the government released political prisoners.
recs.rel: Gandhi then attended the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931.

recs.q: Which area of Pakistan is called the Switzerland of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Swat valley is known as the Switzerland of Pakistan for its mountains, rivers and green scenery.
recs.rel: Faisalabad, by contrast, is known as the Manchester of Pakistan.

recs.q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, which institution is supreme?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Parliament is the supreme law-making body and the Prime Minister heads the government.
recs.rel: In practice the Constitution itself is supreme, and Parliament must act within it.

recs.q: What is the parliament of Israel called?
recs.facts: The Israeli parliament is called the Knesset and it has 120 members.
recs.rel: The Knesset sits in Jerusalem.

recs.q: On what date was the Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament?
recs.facts: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947 and created the two dominions of Pakistan and India.
recs.rel: The 3 June 1947 plan was announced by Lord Mountbatten before the Act.

recs.q: What is the Kunyat (kuniyyat) of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) was called Abu al-Qasim after his eldest son Qasim.
recs.rel: Abu Turab was the kunyat of Hazrat Ali (RA), and Abu Hafs of Hazrat Umar (RA).

recs.q: What is the perimeter of a circle called?
recs.facts: The distance around a circle is called its circumference, equal to 2 x pi x radius.
recs.rel: The diameter is twice the radius.

recs.q: What is the period of the function sin x?
recs.facts: The sine function repeats its values after every 2 pi radians (360 degrees), so sin(x + 2 pi) = sin x.
recs.rel: The period of tan x is pi.

recs.q: Aleem Dar is a famous personality in which field?
recs.facts: Aleem Dar is a Pakistani international cricket umpire, who won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times.
recs.rel: He officiated in more than 130 Test matches.

recs.q: If 5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days, how many papers will 1 person write in 5 days?
recs.facts: Each person writes 1 paper in 5 days (5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days). So 1 person writes 1 paper in 5 days.
recs.rel: In 25 days, 1 person would write 5 papers.

recs.q: Which pass connects Peshawar with Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pass, with the Torkham crossing, connects Peshawar with Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with Afghanistan and the Khunjerab Pass links Pakistan with China.

recs.q: Which pillar of Islam is related to the event of Meraj?
recs.facts: Five daily prayers were made obligatory during the Meraj (Night Journey).
recs.rel: Originally 50 prayers were prescribed and were reduced to five.

recs.q: Badr, where the first major battle of Islam was fought, is the name of what?
opts: A plain with wells near Madinah
recs.facts: Badr is a plain valley with wells about 150 km from Madinah where the Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.
recs.rel: Mount Uhud, in contrast, is a mountain near Madinah.

recs.q: Which is the brightest planet in the sky?
recs.facts: Venus is the brightest planet as seen from Earth because it is close and its thick clouds reflect much sunlight.
recs.rel: It is often called the morning or evening star.

recs.q: Inzamam-ul-Haq is a famous player of which game?
recs.facts: Inzamam-ul-Haq is a former Pakistan cricket captain and batter.
recs.rel: He was a member of the 1992 World Cup winning Pakistan team.

recs.q: What is the land of the pure people (Sarzamin-e-Pak) a name for?
recs.facts: The name Pakistan means land of the pure, from Urdu pak (pure) and stan (land).
recs.rel: The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

recs.q: Khushal Khan Khattak is a famous poet of which language?
recs.facts: Khushal Khan Khattak (1613-1689) was a warrior-poet who wrote in Pashto.
recs.rel: He is regarded as the national poet of the Pashtuns.

recs.q: Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar is regarded as the first major poet of which language?
recs.facts: Baba Farid (1173-1266) of Pakpattan is considered the first major poet of the Punjabi language.
recs.rel: Some of his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

recs.q: Which of the following points lies on the line y = 6x?
recs.facts: For (2, 12): 6 times 2 = 12, so it satisfies y = 6x. The others do not.
recs.rel: The line y = 6x has slope 6 and passes through the origin.

recs.q: What is the population of Punjab province according to the 2023 census?
recs.facts: The 2023 census counted about 127.7 million people in Punjab, the most populous province.
recs.rel: Punjab holds roughly half of Pakistan's population.

recs.q: Which of the following is a major port of Sri Lanka?
recs.facts: Colombo is the largest and busiest port of Sri Lanka.
recs.rel: Hambantota is another important port of Sri Lanka.

recs.q: When did Pakistan issue its first postage stamps?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first set of postage stamps was issued on 9 July 1948.
recs.rel: Before that, British Indian stamps overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.

recs.q: What is the value of x to the power 0 (for x not equal to 0)?
recs.facts: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1, because x to the power n divided by x to the power n equals x to the power 0, which equals 1.
recs.rel: The expression 0 to the power 0 is treated as undefined or indeterminate in many contexts.

recs.q: Which countries hold veto power in the UN Security Council?
recs.facts: The five permanent members of the Security Council (P5) have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
recs.rel: A single veto from any permanent member blocks a substantive resolution.

recs.q: Which regional organization was the predecessor of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
recs.facts: RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was revived and expanded as ECO in 1985.
recs.rel: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of both RCD and ECO.

recs.q: How many compiled copies of the Quran were prepared in the time of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
recs.facts: Under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the Quran was collected into one single compiled copy, kept with him and then with Hazrat Umar and Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
recs.rel: Copies were multiplied and sent to different regions later, during the time of Hazrat Uthman (RA).

recs.q: Which is the present constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan is currently governed by the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973.
recs.rel: It has been amended many times, including the 18th Amendment in 2010.

recs.q: If the price of 3 eggs is 4 rupees, what is the price of 18 eggs?
recs.facts: 18 eggs is 6 times 3 eggs, so the price is 6 times 4 = 24 rupees.
recs.rel: This is a direct proportion problem solved by the unitary method.

recs.q: Which country produces the most olives in the world?
recs.facts: Spain is the largest producer of olives and olive oil, mainly from the region of Andalusia.
recs.rel: Spain produces roughly half of the world's olive oil in a good year.

recs.q: What is the value of i x i, where i is the imaginary unit?
recs.facts: The imaginary unit is defined by i squared equals -1, so i x i = -1.
recs.rel: Higher powers repeat in a cycle: i cubed is -i and i to the fourth power is 1.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word prohibit?
recs.facts: To prohibit means to forbid something, so its opposite is to permit or allow it.
recs.rel: Prohibit comes from the Latin prohibere, meaning to hold back.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of prohibit?
recs.facts: Prohibit means to officially stop something from being done, which is the same as forbid.
recs.rel: Ban and bar are other synonyms of prohibit.

recs.q: Kharan is a district of which province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Kharan is a district and town in the west of Balochistan province.
recs.rel: The Kharan Desert, where Pakistan tested nuclear devices in 1998 near Chagai, lies in this region of Balochistan.

recs.q: How many seats does the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Assembly have?
recs.facts: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP in 2018, the assembly grew from 124 to 145 seats (115 general, 26 women, 4 non-Muslim).
recs.rel: Before the merger the assembly had 124 seats.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of provoke?
recs.facts: To provoke means to stir up a strong reaction, which is the same as to incite.
recs.rel: Instigate and arouse are other synonyms of provoke.

recs.q: What was the age of Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan at the time of Pakistan's first nuclear tests in May 1998?
recs.facts: Born on 1 April 1936, he was 62 years old on 28 May 1998.
recs.rel: The tests were carried out at Chagai in Balochistan.

recs.q: From whom did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Hindu ruler of Sindh, in 711-712 AD.
recs.rel: Raja Dahir was defeated near Raor.

recs.q: Where is Qila Derawar located?
recs.facts: Derawar Fort is a large fort in the Cholistan Desert near Ahmedpur East in Bahawalpur district, Punjab.
recs.rel: The fort was built by Rajput Bhatti rulers and is now on Pakistan's tentative UNESCO list.

recs.q: Where was Masjid Quba, the first mosque in Islam, built?
recs.facts: Masjid Quba was built in the village of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) laid its foundation when he arrived there during the Hijrat.
recs.rel: Masjid Quba is regarded as the first mosque built in Islam.

recs.q: The Khojak Pass connects Quetta with which Afghan city?
recs.facts: The Khojak Pass in Balochistan lies on the route from Quetta to Chaman and on to Kandahar in Afghanistan. The Khojak Tunnel runs beneath it.
recs.rel: The Bolan Pass links Quetta with Sibi and the plains of Sindh and Punjab.

recs.q: For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah socially and economically boycott the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Banu Hashim?
recs.facts: The Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib for about three years, and the family stayed in Shib Abi Talib. The boycott ended in the tenth year of prophethood.
recs.rel: Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadija (RA) both died soon after the boycott ended.

recs.q: Who is said to have been the first to memorise the whole Quran (hifz)?
recs.facts: The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it as it came and recited it to Hazrat Jibril (AS). He is therefore regarded as the first hafiz.
recs.rel: Among the companions, sources name several early huffaz, so this answer refers to the first hafiz overall.

recs.q: What is a circle with zero radius called?
recs.facts: If the radius is zero, all points of the circle coincide with the centre, so it is a single point called a point circle.
recs.rel: A circle with radius 1 is called a unit circle.

recs.q: If my age is 10 years and my brother's age is 2 times my age, what will be the ratio of my age to my brother's age after 10 years?
recs.facts: My brother is 2 x 10 = 20 years old now. After 10 years I will be 20 and he will be 30, so the ratio is 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.
recs.rel: The ratio of ages moves closer to 1 : 1 as both people grow older.

recs.q: Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was an organisation of which three countries?
recs.facts: RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic, technical and cultural cooperation.
recs.rel: RCD was later renamed ECO, which expanded in 1992 to include Central Asian states and Afghanistan.

recs.q: Change into active voice: The book is being read by her.
recs.facts: The passive form is being read becomes the active is reading, and the agent her becomes the subject she. The tense stays present continuous.
recs.rel: In active voice the doer of the action is the subject of the sentence.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: We are reading a book.
opts: A book was being read by us.
A book is read by us.
A book is being read by us.
A book has been read by us.
recs.facts: Present continuous passive uses is or are being plus the past participle. The object a book becomes the subject and we becomes by us.
recs.rel: Passive voice puts the focus on the action or receiver rather than the doer.

recs.q: What is the value of the real number -(4! + 6)?
recs.rel: The factorial of 5 is 120.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number 7 - 2i?
recs.facts: In a + bi form with a = 7 and b = -2, the real part is 7.
recs.rel: Real numbers are complex numbers whose imaginary part is zero.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters V I S R E L to make a word. What is the second last letter of that word?
recs.facts: The letters form the word SILVER. Its letters are S, I, L, V, E, R so the second last letter is E.
recs.rel: Silver has the chemical symbol Ag from the Latin argentum.

recs.q: How many Pakistani Nobel Prize winners have won in the field of physics?
recs.facts: Only Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics, in 1979 for the electroweak theory. Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
recs.rel: Abdus Salam shared the 1979 physics prize with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg.

recs.q: Which of the following is one of the eight categories of zakat recipients (masarif) mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
recs.facts: Surah At-Tawbah (verse 60) lists the fakir, miskin, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, fi sabilillah and travellers. Debtors (Al-Gharimin) are one of them.
recs.rel: Zakat cannot be given to the Prophet's family (Bani Hashim) according to the majority view.

recs.q: What is dead reckoning in navigation?
opts: Sailing only at night using the stars
Estimating current position from a known starting point, speed, time and direction
Measuring the depth of the sea
recs.facts: Dead reckoning calculates the present position by using a previously known position and adding the distance travelled on a known course. It does not need external signals.
recs.rel: Before GPS, ships and aircraft relied heavily on dead reckoning.

recs.q: In which year did China recognize Pakistan?
recs.facts: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed in 1949 and Pakistan recognized it in 1950, among the first countries to do so. Diplomatic relations began on 21 May 1951.
recs.rel: Pakistan was among the first Muslim countries to recognize the People's Republic of China.

recs.q: Where is the Red Sea located?
recs.facts: The Red Sea lies between northeast Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen). It connects to the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal.
recs.rel: The Red Sea joins the Indian Ocean through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, so he was a cousin. He married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

recs.q: What is the antonym of reluctant?
recs.facts: Reluctant means unwilling, so its opposite is willing or eager. The other options are synonyms.
recs.rel: Eager and keen are also antonyms of reluctant.

recs.q: For how many days did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stay in the Cave of Thawr (Ghar-e-Saur) during the Hijrat?
recs.facts: During the migration to Madinah the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three days. They then continued to Madinah.
recs.rel: The cave is near Makkah, south of the city.

recs.q: According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be a member of the National Assembly?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution required a member of the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly on some qualification details; the minimum age of the President under the 1962 Constitution is commonly given as 35 years.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age required to be elected President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution requires the President to be a Muslim, qualified to be a member of the National Assembly, and not less than 45 years old.
recs.rel: The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies for a five-year term.

recs.q: How many seats were reserved for women in the National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution provided a National Assembly of 300 general seats plus 10 seats reserved for women for ten years.
recs.rel: Under the 1973 Constitution today, 60 National Assembly seats are reserved for women.

recs.q: How many seats are reserved for women in the Punjab Assembly?
recs.facts: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general seats, 66 seats for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
recs.rel: Punjab has the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.

recs.q: At which place in Lahore was the Lahore Resolution presented in 1940?
recs.facts: The session of the All India Muslim League was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where Minar-e-Pakistan stands.
recs.rel: Minar-e-Pakistan was built to commemorate the resolution.

recs.q: Which gas is mainly responsible for global warming?
recs.facts: Carbon dioxide, released by burning fossil fuels, traps heat in the atmosphere as a greenhouse gas.
recs.rel: Methane is another important greenhouse gas.

recs.q: What is the meaning of retaliation?
recs.facts: Retaliation means paying back an injury or wrong with a similar action, that is, revenge.
recs.rel: Its verb form is retaliate.

recs.q: What is the antonym of retaliation?
recs.facts: Retaliation means revenge, so its opposite is forgiveness or pardon.
recs.rel: Revenge, vengeance and reprisal are synonyms of retaliation.

recs.q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are written in reverse order, which is the last letter?
recs.facts: BEAUTY reversed is YTUAEB, so the last letter is B.
recs.rel: The first letter of the reversed word is Y.

recs.q: According to the Hadith Qudsi on fasting, who will Himself give the reward of fasting?
recs.facts: In the Hadith Qudsi Allah says: Fasting is for Me and I shall reward it Myself.
recs.rel: Fasting is the third pillar of Islam in some counts and the fourth in the commonly taught Pakistani order.

recs.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
recs.facts: The Earth rotates from west to east, so the sun appears to rise in the east.
recs.rel: The sun sets in the west.

recs.q: Who has scored the most runs in Test cricket?
recs.facts: Sachin Tendulkar of India scored 15,921 runs in 200 Tests, and no one has passed this total as of October 2026.
recs.rel: Joe Root of England is second, having passed 14,000 Test runs in 2026.

recs.q: What is the capital of Russia?
recs.facts: Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia.
recs.rel: Saint Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire until 1918.

recs.q: Saleem is 3 years old and his sister is three times as old as him. How old will his sister be when Saleem is 12?
recs.facts: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now, so she is 6 years older than Saleem. When he is 12, she will be 12 + 6 = 18.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: What is the synonym of foe?
recs.facts: Foe means an enemy or opponent.
recs.rel: The antonym of foe is friend or ally.

recs.q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old?
recs.facts: When Ali is 3, Sara is 3 x 3 = 9, so Sara is 6 years older than Ali. The age gap stays the same, so when Ali is 8, Sara is 8 + 6 = 14.
recs.rel: The difference between two people's ages never changes with time.

recs.q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 15 years old?
recs.facts: When Ali is 3, Sara is 9, so she is 6 years older. When Ali is 15, Sara is 15 + 6 = 21.
recs.rel: The age gap of 6 years stays fixed for life.

recs.q: How many seats does the Provincial Assembly of Sindh have in total?
recs.facts: The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats: 130 general seats, 29 reserved for women and 9 reserved for non-Muslims.
recs.rel: The Punjab Assembly is the largest provincial assembly with 371 seats.

recs.q: How many general seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have in the National Assembly of Pakistan after the 2023 delimitation?
recs.facts: After the merger of FATA and the 2023 delimitation, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has 45 general seats in the National Assembly.
recs.rel: Before the merger of FATA the province had 35 general seats, while Punjab now has 141 general seats.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word selfless?
recs.facts: Selfless means putting others before oneself, so its opposite is selfish, meaning concerned only with oneself.
recs.rel: Unselfish and altruistic are synonyms of selfless.

recs.q: Under which Act was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936?
recs.facts: The Government of India Act 1935 created Sindh as a separate province, which came into effect on 1 April 1936.
recs.rel: The demand for separating Sindh from Bombay was part of the Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in this sequence: A Q W S T R H J C B D Y K L O?
recs.facts: The only vowels in the sequence are A and O, so the count is 2. Y is treated as a consonant here.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in the sequence: a d i u l k m e?
recs.facts: The vowels in the sequence are a, i, u and e, which makes 4.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has five vowels and twenty-one consonants.

recs.q: Complete the series: 1z, 2y, 3x, ?
recs.facts: The numbers go up by 1 each time and the letters go backwards through the alphabet (z, y, x, w). So the next term is 4w.
recs.rel: Z is the 26th letter and W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.

recs.q: Complete the series: a, c, f, ?
recs.facts: The gaps increase by 1: a to c is +2, c to f is +3, so the next is +4. F is the 6th letter and 6 + 4 = 10, which is j.
recs.rel: J is the 10th letter of the English alphabet.

recs.q: What is the next term in the series: A1, C3, D4, G7, ?
recs.facts: The number is the position of the letter in the alphabet, and the numbers 1, 3, 4, 7 each equal the sum of the two before (3 + 4 = 7). The next number is 4 + 7 = 11, which is K.
recs.rel: The numbers 1, 3, 4, 7, 11 are known as the Lucas numbers.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: ____ sun sets in the west.
recs.facts: There is only one sun, so the definite article the is used before it.
recs.rel: The definite article is also used with unique things such as the moon, the earth and the sky.

recs.q: In which year was the Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India signed?
recs.facts: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
recs.rel: It converted the ceasefire line of Kashmir into the Line of Control.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, what is the official name of the Parliament of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 50 of the Constitution says the Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate, and it is called Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).
recs.rel: The two houses of the Majlis-e-Shoora are the National Assembly and the Senate.

recs.q: In which direction of Pakistan does the port city of Gwadar lie?
recs.facts: Gwadar lies on the Arabian Sea coast in the south-west corner of Pakistan in the province of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan purchased Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.

recs.q: Which type of triangle has all three sides of different lengths?
recs.facts: A scalene triangle has no two sides equal, while an isosceles triangle has two equal sides and an equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
recs.rel: The angles of a scalene triangle are also all different.

recs.q: What is sin(-y) equal to?
recs.facts: Sine is an odd function, so reflecting the angle across the x-axis changes the sign of the sine. Therefore sin(-y) = -sin y.
recs.rel: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-y) = cos y.

recs.q: Which tense is normally used with the words 'since' and 'for' (for example, 'I have lived here since 2010')?
recs.facts: 'Since' and 'for' show how long an action or state has continued up to now, which is expressed by the present perfect (or present perfect continuous) tense. Example: She has worked here for five years.
recs.rel: 'Since' is used with a point in time and 'for' with a length of time.

recs.q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died at Aligarh on 27 March 1898.
recs.rel: He was born in 1817, so he lived about 80 years.

recs.q: Which type of brackets is used to write a solution set?
recs.facts: Sets, including solution sets, are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.
recs.rel: Round and square brackets are used for intervals.

recs.q: Solve the proportion 2 : x :: 14 : 28. What is x?
recs.facts: In a proportion the product of extremes equals the product of means: 2 x 28 = x x 14. So 56 = 14x and x = 4.
recs.rel: A proportion a : b :: c : d means a/b = c/d.

recs.q: Solve for x: 3x - 9 = 9 - x
recs.facts: Add x and 9 to both sides: 4x = 18, so x = 18/4 = 9/2 = 4.5.

recs.q: Who was the son of Hazrat Sarah (AS), the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Sarah was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), born when she was very old.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra.

recs.q: The sound of which animal is mentioned in the Quran as the most unpleasant of sounds?
recs.facts: Surah Luqman (31:19) says the harshest of sounds is surely the braying of the donkey.
recs.rel: This verse is part of Luqman's advice to his son to lower his voice.

recs.q: When was the Soviet Union (USSR) established?
recs.facts: The USSR was formally created on 30 December 1922 by the union of Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Transcaucasian republics.
recs.rel: It was dissolved in December 1991.

recs.q: Iqbal's famous 1930 speech at the annual session of the All India Muslim League is known as which address?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal delivered his Presidential Address at Allahabad in December 1930. In it he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
recs.rel: The Allahabad Address is considered the intellectual root of the Pakistan idea.

recs.q: What is the last sermon of the Holy Prophet (SAW) called?
recs.facts: The Prophet (SAW) delivered his final sermon during the Farewell Hajj at Arafat. It is called Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida.
recs.rel: The Farewell Hajj took place in 10 AH.

recs.q: A car runs at 60 km/hr and a train runs at twice the speed of the car. What is the speed of the train?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/hr. Speed does not change with the time taken, so it is still 120 km/hr after 30 minutes.
recs.rel: In 30 minutes this train would cover 60 km.

recs.q: What does OPAC stand for in library science?
recs.facts: OPAC means Online Public Access Catalogue. It is a computerised database that lets users search a library's holdings.
recs.rel: It replaced the traditional card catalogue.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: She arrived ___ the station.
recs.facts: We use the preposition at with a specific point or place such as a station. So the sentence is: She arrived at the station.
recs.rel: We use arrive in for large places such as cities and countries.

recs.q: After which battle did the Quraysh stop their attacks on Madina, as the Prophet (SAW) said they would no longer attack?
recs.facts: After the failed siege of Madina in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH, the Prophet (SAW) said that the Quraysh would not attack again and the Muslims would march against them.
recs.rel: The Battle of Khandaq was won mainly by the trench dug on the advice of Salman Farsi (RA).

recs.q: The graphical representation of which type of equation is a straight line?
recs.facts: A linear equation such as y = mx + c has degree one in its variables. Its graph is always a straight line.
recs.rel: A quadratic equation gives a parabola.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'strange'?
recs.facts: Strange means unusual or unexpected, and odd has the same meaning. The other options mean the opposite.
recs.rel: Other synonyms of strange are peculiar and queer.

recs.q: What is the central subject of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran is a book of guidance addressed to mankind. Its main subject is man and his success in this world and the Hereafter.
recs.rel: The Quran has 114 surahs and 30 paras.

recs.q: What is a synonym of 'subversion'?
recs.facts: Subversion means an attempt to weaken or overthrow an established authority from within. Undermining carries the same sense.
recs.rel: Sabotage is another close synonym.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani to reach the summit of K2?
recs.facts: Ashraf Aman reached the summit of K2 in 1977 as part of a Japanese-led expedition.
recs.rel: Nazir Sabir was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest, in 2000, and sources differ slightly on the exact K2 summit date in August 1977.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 16th of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 16th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 16th falls on the same day as the 2nd, Sunday.
recs.rel: Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the name of Surah Al-Ankabut?
recs.facts: Ankabut means spider, and the surah is named after the spider's web used as an example in it.
recs.rel: Al-Ankabut is the 29th surah of the Quran.

recs.q: Which two surahs are known as Muawwazatain?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are called Muawwidhatayn because they seek refuge in Allah.
recs.rel: They are the last two surahs of the Quran, 113 and 114.

recs.q: What is the capital of Sweden?
recs.facts: Stockholm is the capital and largest city of Sweden.
recs.rel: Sweden is a Scandinavian country in northern Europe.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "abate"?
recs.facts: To abate means to become less intense, which is to subside.
recs.rel: Abatement is the noun form.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquiesce"?
recs.facts: To acquiesce is to accept or go along with something without protest, so comply is closest.
recs.rel: Its noun form is acquiescence.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquisition"?
recs.facts: An acquisition is something gained or bought, close to purchase.
recs.rel: Companies use the word for takeovers.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "awful"?
recs.facts: Awful means very bad, same as terrible.
recs.rel: The word originally meant inspiring awe.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "brute"?
recs.facts: A brute is a savage or cruel creature, so beast is closest.
recs.rel: Brutal is the related adjective.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "exceptional"?
recs.facts: Exceptional means unusually good or rare, like extraordinary.
recs.rel: Its antonym is ordinary.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "irksome"?
recs.facts: Irksome means causing irritation, so annoying is closest.
recs.rel: To irk means to annoy.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "magistrate"?
recs.facts: A magistrate is a civil officer who acts as a judge in lower courts.
recs.rel: In Pakistan, judicial magistrates hear minor criminal cases.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "puzzled"?
recs.facts: Puzzled means confused, the same as perplexed.
recs.rel: Bewildered is another synonym.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "wield"?
recs.facts: To wield is to hold and use something such as a tool or power, so handle is closest.
recs.rel: One can wield a sword or wield influence.

recs.q: What is the capital of Tajikistan?
recs.facts: Dushanbe is the capital and largest city of Tajikistan.
recs.rel: Tajikistan borders Afghanistan, China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

recs.q: If 1 km takes 100 minutes, how many km can be covered in 12 minutes at the same rate?
recs.facts: Rate is 1/100 km per minute, so in 12 minutes the distance is 12 x 1/100 = 0.12 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: Which of the following was NOT among the Ashra Mubashra (the ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Talha is one of the ten given the glad tidings of Paradise, while Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is not on that list.
recs.rel: The ten include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.

recs.q: Which is the tallest building in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi is generally listed as Pakistan's tallest building, though its stated height varies by source (about 273 to 300 metres).
recs.rel: Habib Bank Plaza was long considered the tallest before the Icon Tower was built.

recs.q: Tarbela Dam is located in which district and province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus near Tarbela in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

recs.q: How many farz (obligatory acts) does Tayammum have according to the Hanafi school?
recs.facts: The three farz of Tayammum are making the intention, striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face, and wiping both arms up to the elbows.
recs.rel: Tayammum is performed when water is not available or cannot be used.

recs.q: On which date is International Tea Day observed?
recs.facts: The United Nations designated 21 May as International Tea Day, first observed in 2020.
recs.rel: Earlier, tea-producing countries had celebrated an International Tea Day on 15 December.

recs.q: A soldier's mother ____ her emotions as he left for the front. Choose the correct word.
recs.facts: The phrasal verb 'bottled up' means kept feelings hidden, and 'teared' is not the right form in this sense.
recs.rel: 'Bottle up' is the phrasal verb; the past tense is 'bottled up'.

recs.q: What is 20% of one tenth of 90?
recs.facts: One tenth of 90 is 9, and 20% of 9 is 1.8.
recs.rel: 20% is the same as one fifth.

recs.q: What is one tenth of 1/20?
recs.rel: Multiplying by one tenth moves the decimal point one place left.

recs.q: What is one third of one tenth of 9?
recs.facts: One tenth of 9 is 0.9 and one third of 0.9 is 0.3.
recs.rel: Equivalently 9 divided by 30 equals 0.3.

recs.q: What is cosec theta equal to?
recs.facts: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec theta = 1 / sin theta.
recs.rel: Sec theta is 1 / cos theta and cot theta is 1 / tan theta.

recs.q: In a right-angled triangle, sin theta is equal to which ratio?
recs.facts: Sine of an angle is the length of the opposite side (perpendicular) divided by the hypotenuse.
recs.rel: Cos theta is base / hypotenuse and tan theta is perpendicular / base.

recs.q: Which is the third surah of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, so the third surah is Al-Imran.
recs.rel: An-Nisa is the fourth surah.

recs.q: A number whose three times is 6 has 2 added to it. What is the result?
recs.facts: If 3 times the number is 6, the number is 2. Adding 2 gives 2 + 2 = 4.
recs.rel: The candidate answer 2 is only the number itself, not the final result.

recs.q: Through which point does the line y = 6x pass?
recs.facts: Putting x = 0 gives y = 0, so the line passes through the origin (0, 0).
recs.rel: A line of the form y = mx always passes through the origin.

recs.q: Watch is to time as barometer is to what?
recs.facts: A watch measures time and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
recs.rel: A thermometer measures temperature and an anemometer measures wind speed.

recs.q: What was the approximate age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Fujjar war?
recs.facts: The Fujjar war was fought in the sacred months and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part by handing arrows to his uncles at about the age of 15 years.
recs.rel: Some narrations give an age between 14 and 20 years, so sources differ slightly; 15 is the common textbook answer.

recs.q: When did Tipu Sultan die?
recs.facts: Tipu Sultan was killed defending Seringapatam against the British in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War on 4 May 1799.
recs.rel: The Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

recs.q: Which title is used for Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is known by the title Attiq, meaning freed from the fire of Hell, besides Siddiq.
recs.rel: Farooq is the title of Hazrat Umar (RA) and Murtaza of Hazrat Ali (RA).

recs.q: Habibullah (beloved of Allah) is the title of whom?
recs.facts: Habibullah is a famous title of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah.

recs.q: If today is Friday, what day will it be after 14 days?
recs.facts: 14 days is exactly 2 weeks, so the day is the same: Friday.
recs.rel: Any multiple of 7 days brings the same weekday.

recs.q: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 5 days?
recs.facts: Counting 5 days after Monday gives Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
recs.rel: Saturday and Sunday form the weekend.

recs.q: What is the line that touches a circle at exactly one point called?
recs.facts: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, while a secant cuts it at two points.
recs.rel: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

recs.q: How many tournaments make up the Grand Slam in tennis?
recs.facts: The four Grand Slam tennis tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
recs.rel: Wimbledon is the oldest of the four.

recs.q: What is the transpose of a row matrix called?
recs.facts: Transposing swaps rows and columns, so a 1 by n row matrix becomes an n by 1 column matrix.
recs.rel: The transpose of a square matrix is also a square matrix.

recs.q: What was the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) about?
opts: Sale of Kashmir by the British to Gulab Singh
End of the First Anglo-Sikh War handing Punjab to the Mughals
recs.facts: Under the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 7.5 million rupees.
recs.rel: It followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.

recs.q: Ali's present age is 3 years and his sister is twice his age. What will be the age of his sister when Ali is 8 years old?
recs.facts: Sister's age now is 2 x 3 = 6, so she is 3 years older than Ali. When Ali is 8, she is 8 + 3 = 11.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali is twice the age of Salman. When Salman is 12 years old, what will be the age of Ali?
recs.facts: Ali is 2 x 4 = 8 now, so he is 4 years older than Salman. When Salman is 12, Ali is 12 + 4 = 16.
recs.rel: Do not double the later age; only the present ages are in the ratio 2 to 1.

recs.q: What type of constitution was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, set up a federal parliamentary republic with a unicameral National Assembly.
recs.rel: It was abrogated in October 1958 when martial law was imposed.

recs.q: Beauty is to ugliness as adversity is to what?
recs.facts: Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of adversity (hardship) is prosperity.
recs.rel: Hardship, misfortune and difficulty are synonyms of adversity, not opposites.

recs.q: Beauty is to ugliness as diversity is to what?
recs.facts: Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of diversity (variety) is uniformity.
recs.rel: Variety, difference and range are close in meaning to diversity.

recs.q: Unscramble the word SAPIR. Is it the name of a bird, a country or a city?
recs.facts: The letters of SAPIR form PARIS, which is a city, the capital of France.
recs.rel: Paris stands on the River Seine.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was Hazrat Usman (RA) martyred?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA), the third caliph, was besieged in his house and martyred in Dhul Hijjah 35 AH (656 CE).
recs.rel: He was succeeded as caliph by Hazrat Ali (RA).

recs.q: If Y = 4x - 2 and x = 2, what is the value of Y?
recs.facts: Substitute x = 2: Y = 4 x 2 - 2 = 8 - 2 = 6.
recs.rel: Multiplication is done before subtraction in the order of operations.

recs.q: If y = 2x - 1 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
recs.facts: Substitute x = 2: y = 2 x 2 - 1 = 4 - 1 = 3.
recs.rel: Substitution means replacing a variable by its given value.

recs.q: What comes next in the series Z1, Y2, X3, ...?
recs.facts: The letters move backwards through the alphabet (Z, Y, X, W) while the numbers go up by 1 (1, 2, 3, 4). So the next term is W4.
recs.rel: Letter pairs like this often combine a reverse alphabet with an increasing number.

recs.q: On what date was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
recs.facts: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.
recs.rel: It came into force on 10 January 1920, the same day the League of Nations first met.

recs.q: What was the Treaty of Versailles?
opts: A peace treaty ending World War I with Germany
A treaty ending World War II
An alliance between Britain and France
A treaty founding the United Nations
recs.facts: The Treaty of Versailles was the peace settlement between Germany and the Allied Powers after World War I.
recs.rel: It forced Germany to accept war guilt, pay reparations and lose territory.

recs.q: According to the commonly accepted count, how many verses (ayat) does the Holy Quran have?
recs.facts: The Hafs count most widely followed gives 6236 verses across 114 surahs.
recs.rel: Counts differ slightly between recitation traditions; 6666 is a popular but not the standard figure.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He was very grateful that he ----- my computer promptly.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the past tense (was grateful), so the past tense repaired is correct.
recs.rel: Tense should stay consistent between the clauses of a sentence.

recs.q: Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
recs.facts: Lord Mountbatten served as the last Viceroy from March to August 1947 and then became the first Governor-General of independent India.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Lord Wavell.

recs.q: In which year did Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan make his official visit to the United States?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 at the invitation of President Truman.
recs.rel: This visit is seen as the start of close Pakistan-US relations.

recs.q: How many vowels are in the letter string AEDIPOUDLEC (Aedipoudlec)?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, E, I, O, U, E, which makes 6.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: How many vowels are in AZPQTVSJFIU?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, I and U, giving 3.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: How many vowels are in AdebccTEvIxyz?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, e, E and I, giving 4.
recs.rel: Capital and small letters count equally.

recs.q: Which country does India import the largest share of its weapons from, according to SIPRI data?
recs.facts: SIPRI data show Russia as India's largest arms supplier for 2020-24, with about 36 percent of India's imports. France is second.
recs.rel: Russia's share of Indian imports has fallen sharply from about 72 percent in 2010-14.

recs.q: Choose the correct form of the sentence: Amna will have repair her bike by next week.
opts: Amna will have repaired her bike by next week.
Amna will has repaired her bike by next week.
Amna will have repairing her bike by next week.
Amna will had repair her bike by next week.
recs.facts: The future perfect tense is formed with will have plus the past participle, so repair must become repaired.
recs.rel: The future perfect tense shows an action that will be completed before a stated time in the future.

recs.q: If 10 men can dig a well in 5 days, how many days will 5 men take to dig it?
recs.facts: Total work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days. With 5 men, days = 50 / 5 = 10 days.
recs.rel: Fewer workers need proportionally more time, which is called inverse proportion.

recs.q: In which country is the White House located?
recs.facts: The White House stands at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C., United States.
recs.rel: Construction of the White House began in 1792 and it was first occupied by President John Adams in 1800.

recs.q: Which country is traditionally called the Land of the White Elephant?
recs.facts: Thailand (formerly Siam) is known by this name because white elephants were sacred and symbols of royal power there.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly, as Myanmar and Laos have also been linked to white elephants, but Thailand is the textbook answer.

recs.q: Who won the seventh edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL 7) in 2022?
recs.facts: Lahore Qalandars beat Multan Sultans by 42 runs in the final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, on 27 February 2022.
recs.rel: It was the first PSL title for Lahore Qalandars, who also won PSL 8 in 2023.

recs.q: Which team won the 2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
recs.facts: Australia beat New Zealand by 8 wickets in the final in Dubai in November 2021 to win their first T20 World Cup.
recs.rel: Pakistan won the 2009 ICC T20 World Cup, and it reached the 2021 semi-final.

recs.q: When are the articles a and an used?
recs.facts: A and an are indefinite articles used before singular countable nouns; a is used before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
recs.rel: The article the is the definite article and can be used with singular, plural and uncountable nouns.

recs.q: What is the work of the angels Munkar and Nakir, according to Islamic belief?
opts: Blowing the trumpet on the Day of Judgement
Questioning a person in the grave
recs.facts: Munkar and Nakir are the two angels who question a person in the grave about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet.
recs.rel: The angels who record deeds are Kiraman Katibin, who sit on each person's shoulders.

recs.q: In which year did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) pass away?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 11 AH, which corresponds to June 632 CE, in Madina.
recs.rel: He was about 63 years old, and he was buried in the room of Hazrat Ayesha (RA).

recs.q: If one man writes one paper in 5 minutes, how long does one man take to write one paper?
recs.facts: The question already states that he takes 5 minutes for one paper, so the answer is 5 minutes.
recs.rel: At this rate, he would write 12 papers in one hour.

recs.q: Which famous book was written by Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri)?
recs.facts: Data Ganj Bakhsh wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, one of the oldest Persian works on Sufism.
recs.rel: His shrine is in Lahore.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Yamama fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Yamama was fought against the false prophet Musaylima in 11 AH (632 CE) in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
recs.rel: After heavy losses of Quran memorisers in this battle, the Quran was first compiled in book form.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) to Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
recs.facts: Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Ishaq (AS), who was the younger brother of Ismail (AS), so Yaqoob was Ismail's nephew.
recs.rel: Both Ishaq and Ismail were sons of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

recs.q: On which date (day) of Ramadan is Youm-e-Furqan observed?
recs.facts: Youm-e-Furqan marks the Battle of Badr, which was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.
recs.rel: Badr is called the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

recs.q: Which is the oldest of these heavenly books?
recs.facts: The Taurat was revealed to Hazrat Musa (AS), before the Zabur (Dawood AS), the Injeel (Isa AS) and the Quran (Muhammad PBUH).
recs.rel: The Quran is the last of the heavenly books.

recs.q: What is the well-known title of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zaid (RA) was so dear to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) that he was called Hibb Rasulullah.
recs.rel: He is the only Companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'zenith'?
recs.facts: Zenith means the highest point, so its opposite is nadir, the lowest point.
recs.rel: Apex, summit and peak are synonyms of zenith.

recs.q: Which Indian mathematician is credited with formalising the rules of arithmetic with zero in 628 CE?
recs.facts: Brahmagupta, in his Brahmasphutasiddhanta, gave the first clear rules for using zero in calculations.
recs.rel: Sources differ on who first invented the zero symbol; some credit Aryabhata and earlier Indian scholars.

recs.q: 3x - 5x + 2 is an example of what?
recs.facts: It has variables and constants joined by operations but no equals or inequality sign, so it is an algebraic expression (it simplifies to -2x + 2).
recs.rel: An equation needs an equals sign, such as 3x - 5x + 2 = 0.

recs.facts: A - B contains the elements of A that are not in B. Only 3 is in A but not in B.
recs.rel: B - A would be {5}.

recs.q: If Y = 4X and X = 2, what is Y?
recs.rel: Here 4 is the coefficient of X.

recs.q: In the expression 7X + 4, what is 7 called?
recs.facts: The number multiplying the variable X is its coefficient; 4 is the constant term.
recs.rel: X is the variable of the expression.

recs.q: What is (3 + 2i)(2i - 3)?
What is -10 - 10?
recs.facts: Subtracting 10 from -10 moves further down the number line to -20.
recs.rel: Two negative numbers added give a larger negative number.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 10% of 99?
recs.rel: 99 is divisible by 3, so 1/3 of 99 = 33.

recs.q: What is 2/2 + 1?
recs.rel: Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

recs.q: What is 20% of 50?
recs.rel: 20% equals one fifth.

recs.q: What is 2x + 3x + 1?
recs.facts: Add the like terms: 2x + 3x = 5x, so the result is 5x + 1.
recs.rel: Only like terms can be combined.

recs.q: What is 2 x 3 - 2 x 2?
recs.facts: Multiply first: 6 - 4 = 2.
recs.rel: This equals 2(3 - 2) = 2.

recs.q: What is 4x - 1 if x = 2?
recs.rel: Substitute first, then multiply, then subtract.

recs.q: What is 54% of 90?
What is 60% of 70?
recs.rel: 10% of 70 is 7, so 60% is 6 x 7.

recs.q: What is 80% of 40?
recs.rel: 80% equals 4/5.

recs.q: What is 80% of 75?
recs.rel: 80% equals 4/5 and 75 x 4 / 5 = 60.

recs.q: What is 9% of 9?
What is 90% of 91?
recs.facts: 90% of 91 = 0.9 x 91 = 81.9. Equivalently, 10% of 91 is 9.1, and 91 minus 9.1 = 81.9.
recs.rel: Taking 90% of a number is the same as subtracting 10% of it.

recs.q: What is 90% of 99?
recs.facts: 90% of 99 = 0.9 x 99 = 89.1. Equivalently, 10% of 99 is 9.9, and 99 minus 9.9 = 89.1.
recs.rel: 90% of 100 is 90, so 90% of 99 is 0.9 less than 90.

recs.q: In set theory, what is n(A-B) equal to?
recs.facts: A-B contains the elements of A that are not in B. These are all elements of A except those common to both, so n(A-B) = n(A) - n(A intersection B).
recs.rel: The union formula is n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B).

recs.q: What is the capital of Somalia?
recs.facts: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia on the Indian Ocean coast.
recs.rel: Hargeisa is the capital of the self-declared Somaliland.

recs.q: What is the capital of Malta?
recs.facts: Valletta is the capital of Malta and a UNESCO World Heritage city.
recs.rel: Mdina was the old capital of Malta before Valletta.

recs.q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
recs.facts: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan; it replaced Almaty as capital in 1997.
recs.rel: Astana was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and returned to the name Astana in 2022.

recs.q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which town of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pass runs from near Peshawar through Jamrud and Landi Kotal to the Torkham border with Afghanistan.
recs.rel: Landi Kotal is the highest point of the pass and lies close to the Afghan border.

recs.q: In which year was the first Cricket World Cup held?
recs.facts: The first Cricket World Cup (the Prudential Cup) was played in England and began on 7 June 1975.
recs.rel: West Indies won the first two tournaments, in 1975 and 1979.

recs.q: Who discovered X-rays in 1895?
recs.facts: Wilhelm Conrad Rontgen, a German physicist, discovered X-rays in 1895 while experimenting with cathode ray tubes.
recs.rel: Rontgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for this discovery.

recs.q: Which person led the launch of the iPhone, which Apple introduced in 2007?
recs.facts: Steve Jobs, co-founder and then CEO of Apple, unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007. Apple is the company that made it.
recs.rel: Steve Jobs died in 2011 and Tim Cook became Apple's CEO.

recs.q: Where and in which year were the first Asian Games held?
recs.facts: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951. Eleven countries took part.
recs.rel: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

recs.q: What does the green colour in the national flag of Pakistan represent?
recs.facts: The dark green field of the flag stands for the Muslim majority of Pakistan, while the white stripe stands for religious minorities.
recs.rel: The crescent symbolises progress and the star symbolises light and knowledge; the flag was adopted on 11 August 1947.

recs.q: Which of the following countries does NOT share a border with Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan borders India, China, Afghanistan and Iran. Tajikistan is separated from Pakistan by the narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Wakhan Corridor is only about 14 to 15 km wide at its narrowest point.

recs.q: Reykjavik is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland.
recs.rel: Reykjavik is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state in the world.

recs.q: What is the capital of Ghana?
recs.facts: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea coast.
recs.rel: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.

recs.q: What is the capital of Latvia?
recs.facts: Riga is the capital and largest city of Latvia.
recs.rel: Latvia is one of the three Baltic states.

recs.q: Which country won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
recs.facts: France beat Croatia 4-2 in the final in Moscow in July 2018.
recs.rel: Russia hosted the 2018 tournament, and Argentina won the next one in 2022.

recs.q: Who discovered bacteria?
recs.facts: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observed bacteria through his handmade microscope in the 1670s. He called them animalcules.
recs.rel: Louis Pasteur proved the germ theory of disease and Robert Koch identified the bacteria causing anthrax and tuberculosis.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the United States House of Representatives?
recs.facts: Nancy Pelosi of California became the first woman Speaker of the US House in January 2007. She held the post again from 2019 to 2023.
recs.rel: Pelosi was succeeded as Speaker by Kevin McCarthy in 2023, and later by Mike Johnson.

recs.q: Moroni is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Moroni is the capital of the Union of the Comoros, an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
recs.rel: Comoros lies between Mozambique and Madagascar.

recs.q: Which country has won the most Cricket World Cup titles?
recs.facts: Australia has won the men's Cricket World Cup six times (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015 and 2023).
recs.rel: India has won it twice and Pakistan once, in 1992.

recs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Salt Range?
recs.facts: Sakesar, in district Khushab, is the highest peak of the Salt Range at about 1522 m.
recs.rel: The Salt Range lies between the Jhelum and Indus rivers in Punjab.

recs.q: Who is credited with discovering the proton?
recs.facts: Ernest Rutherford identified the proton as a particle in 1917-1919.
recs.rel: Thomson discovered the electron and Chadwick discovered the neutron.

recs.q: Whose slave was Hazrat Bilal (RA) before he accepted freedom through Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was the slave of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who tortured him for accepting Islam. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed him.
recs.rel: Hazrat Bilal (RA) became the first muezzin of Islam.

recs.q: How many atmospheric layers does the Moon have?
opts: None, it has practically no atmosphere
recs.facts: The Moon is too small and its gravity too weak to hold an atmosphere. It has only an extremely thin exosphere that is almost a vacuum.
recs.rel: Because there is no air, sound cannot travel on the Moon and the sky looks black even in daytime.

recs.q: Who discovered the neutron?
recs.facts: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles.
recs.rel: Chadwick received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935 for this discovery.

recs.q: Which is the smallest ocean in the world?
recs.facts: The Arctic Ocean has an area of about 14 million square kilometres and is the smallest and shallowest ocean.
recs.rel: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.

recs.q: Which team won the Asia Cup cricket tournament in 2022?
recs.facts: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by 23 runs in the final in Dubai in September 2022 to win the T20 format Asia Cup.
recs.rel: The 2022 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates after being moved from Sri Lanka.

recs.q: In which year was the Suez Canal completed and opened?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal was opened to traffic on 17 November 1869 after about ten years of construction.
recs.rel: It was built under the French engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps and links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.

recs.q: In which surah of the Holy Quran are the faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu mentioned?
recs.facts: The faraiz of wudu are described in verse 6 of Surah Al-Maidah, which orders washing the face and arms, wiping the head and washing the feet.
recs.rel: The same verse also gives the command for tayammum when water is not available; Surah An-Nisa (4:43) also mentions tayammum.

recs.q: Ghani Khan, the famous poet and philosopher, wrote mainly in which language?
recs.facts: Ghani Khan (1914-1996) was a well known Pashto poet, painter and philosopher from Charsadda.
recs.rel: He was the son of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and wrote the book The Pathans.

recs.q: Which prophet (AS) was given the ability by Allah to soften and melt iron?
recs.facts: The Quran says Allah made iron soft for Hazrat Dawood (AS), so he could make armour from it. He is the prophet who received the Zabur.
recs.rel: Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).

recs.q: What is the currency of Japan?
recs.facts: Japan's currency is the yen. Its code is JPY.
recs.rel: The Bank of Japan issues the yen.

recs.q: During which months of 1999 was the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India fought?
recs.facts: The Kargil conflict began in early May 1999 and ended in late July 1999, after a ceasefire request following talks in Washington.
recs.rel: Kargil lies in the Ladakh region along the Line of Control.

recs.q: Who is known by the title Quaid-e-Millat?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, is known as Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
recs.rel: He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

recs.q: With which neighbouring country does Pakistan share a border of about 2,400 km?
recs.facts: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border, the Durand Line, is about 2,430 km long and is commonly quoted as about 2,400 km.
recs.rel: Pakistan's border with India is about 3,300 km, with Iran about 900 km and with China about 520 km.

recs.q: Napoleon Bonaparte belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Napoleon Bonaparte was a French general who became Emperor of the French. He was born on the island of Corsica, which was a French territory.
recs.rel: Napoleon was finally defeated at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.

recs.q: In the x,y coordinate system, what is the y-coordinate also called?
recs.facts: In a point (x, y), the x-value is called the abscissa and the y-value is called the ordinate.
recs.rel: The point where both coordinates are zero is called the origin.

recs.q: Where is the shrine of the famous Pashto poet Rehman Baba located?
recs.facts: The mausoleum of Abdur Rehman Mohmand, known as Rehman Baba, is at Hazar Khwani near Peshawar.
recs.rel: Rehman Baba is called the Nightingale of Pashto poetry and lived in the 17th century.

recs.q: What is the average height of the Potohar Plateau above sea level according to most Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: The Potohar Plateau lies between the Indus and Jhelum rivers and has an average height of about 300 to 600 metres.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly, with some giving the height in feet as about 1000 to 2000 feet.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan launch its first satellite, Badr-1?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1, was launched on 16 July 1990 from China by SUPARCO. It was a low-earth-orbit experimental satellite.
recs.rel: Pakistan later launched Badr-B in 2001 and PakSat-1R in 2011.

recs.q: What is the capital of Zambia?
recs.facts: Lusaka is the capital and largest city of Zambia.
recs.rel: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa that was formerly Northern Rhodesia.

recs.q: Which is the second highest mountain of Pakistan?
recs.facts: K2 is the highest peak in Pakistan and Nanga Parbat, at about 8,126 m, is the second highest.
recs.rel: Nanga Parbat is nicknamed the Killer Mountain and is in Gilgit-Baltistan.

recs.q: What does CPEC stand for?
recs.facts: CPEC stands for China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, a package of infrastructure and energy projects linking Gwadar port with western China.
recs.rel: CPEC was formally launched in 2015 and its flagship port is Gwadar in Balochistan.

recs.q: In which city is the Air Headquarters of the Pakistan Air Force located?
recs.facts: The Air Headquarters of the Pakistan Air Force is in Islamabad. The PAF Air Command and Staff College is at Karachi.
recs.rel: The Pakistan Air Force Academy is at Risalpur.

recs.q: In which year was the 18th Amendment to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan passed?
recs.facts: The 18th Amendment was passed by Parliament in April 2010 and signed by President Zardari. It transferred many powers from the centre to the provinces.
recs.rel: It renamed the North-West Frontier Province as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly under 58(2)(b).

recs.q: What is the antonym of superiority?
recs.facts: Superiority means being higher in quality or rank; the opposite is inferiority.
recs.rel: The terms inferiority complex and superiority complex were popularised by the psychologist Alfred Adler.

recs.q: Into which sea does the Indus River flow?
recs.facts: The Indus River flows through Pakistan and falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi in Sindh.
recs.rel: The Indus delta is near Thatta.

recs.q: What is the approximate maximum height of the Kirthar range (its highest point, Zardak Peak)?
recs.facts: The highest point of the Kirthar range is Zardak Peak at roughly 2,260 metres, or about 7,400 feet.
recs.rel: Sources give slightly different figures, from about 2,260 to 2,267 metres.

recs.q: What was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey renamed as in 1985?
recs.facts: The RCD was revived and renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985 by its three founding members.
recs.rel: ECO later expanded in 1992 to include Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

recs.q: Which is the busiest sea (ocean) trade route of the world according to standard textbooks?
recs.facts: The North Atlantic sea route links eastern North America with north-western Europe and carries the heaviest volume of ocean trade in most textbooks.
recs.rel: Modern shipping statistics sometimes rank Asian routes through the Strait of Malacca very high, so sources can differ.

recs.q: Who is traditionally credited in Pakistani textbooks with inventing the telescope?
recs.facts: Galileo Galilei built and used an improved telescope in 1609 to observe the Moon, Jupiter's moons and the planets. Textbooks therefore credit him with the telescope.
recs.rel: Sources differ: the Dutch spectacle maker Hans Lippershey filed the first known patent for a telescope in 1608.

recs.q: Which is the largest temple in the world?
recs.facts: Angkor Wat in Cambodia covers about 162 hectares and is the largest religious monument in the world.
recs.rel: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century by King Suryavarman II, first as a Hindu and later a Buddhist temple.

recs.q: Which is regarded as the first women's university in Pakistan, and in which city is it located?
opts: Kinnaird College for Women University, Lahore
Sardar Bahadur Khan Women's University, Quetta
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah Women University was founded in 1998 in Rawalpindi and is generally regarded as Pakistan's first women's university. It is named after Fatima Jinnah, the sister of the Quaid-e-Azam.
recs.rel: Some sources call it the first public sector women's university, because Kinnaird College in Lahore was a much older women's college.

recs.q: What was the code name of Pakistan's nuclear tests conducted in May 1998?
recs.facts: Pakistan's tests at Chagai in Balochistan were named Chagai-I (28 May 1998, five tests) and Chagai-II (30 May 1998, one test).
recs.rel: Pakistan observes 28 May as Youm-e-Takbeer; Smiling Buddha was the code name of India's 1974 test.

recs.q: In which city is the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations located?
recs.facts: The FAO has its headquarters in Rome, Italy. It leads international efforts against hunger and works on food and agriculture.
recs.rel: The FAO was founded in 1945 and its World Food Day is observed on 16 October.

recs.q: Who was the first ambassador of Pakistan to the United States?
recs.facts: Mirza Abol Hassan Ispahani, a close associate of Jinnah, was the first Pakistani ambassador to the USA. He served until 1952.
recs.rel: Sources differ on whether he took up the post in 1947 or 1948; he later served as High Commissioner to Britain.

recs.q: Tallinn is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Tallinn is the capital and largest city of Estonia, on the Gulf of Finland.
recs.rel: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are the three Baltic states.

recs.q: What do the five rings of the Olympic flag represent?
opts: Five inhabited continents of the world
recs.facts: The five interlocked rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined by Olympism: Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania.
recs.rel: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background, designed in 1913 and first flown in 1920.

recs.q: The Karakoram mountain range lies between Pakistan and which country?
recs.facts: The Karakoram range runs along the northern border of Pakistan and separates Gilgit-Baltistan from the Xinjiang region of China.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway crosses this range through the Khunjerab Pass and links Pakistan with China.

recs.q: According to the commonly given number in Pakistani textbooks, how many Companions served as Katib-e-Wahi (scribes of revelation) for the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Many Pakistani books state that about 40 Companions wrote down the revelation, including Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA).
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact number, and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) is the best known of the scribes.

recs.q: In which country did noodles originate?
recs.facts: The oldest known noodles, about 4000 years old, were found at the Lajia site in China, and China is generally credited with their origin.
recs.rel: Italy and China have long argued about the origin of pasta and noodles.

recs.q: The Olympic Games take their name from Olympia and Mount Olympus. In which country did the Olympic Games originate?
recs.facts: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece, and Mount Olympus is also in Greece. The modern Olympics are named after these ancient games.
recs.rel: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

recs.q: On which date was the Battle of Plassey fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company under Robert Clive and Nawab Siraj ud Daula of Bengal.
recs.rel: The Battle of Plassey is seen as the start of British political rule in India.

recs.q: The word 'terrorism' was first used in connection with which historical event?
recs.facts: The term came into use in the 1790s for the Reign of Terror of the Jacobins in revolutionary France.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact year, with 1794 and 1795 both quoted.

recs.q: Who wrote the poems Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa?
recs.facts: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa in 1909 and Jawab-e-Shikwa in 1913.
recs.rel: Both poems were later included in his Urdu collection Bang-e-Dra.

recs.q: What is the antonym of friendly?
recs.facts: Friendly means kind and welcoming; the opposite is hostile, meaning unfriendly or aggressive.
recs.rel: Hostile comes from the Latin hostis, meaning enemy.

recs.q: To which country did Winston Churchill, the famous leader of World War II, belong?
recs.facts: Winston Churchill was British and served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and again from 1951 to 1955.
recs.rel: Churchill won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.

recs.q: Who conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD?
recs.facts: The young Arab general Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the Umayyad caliphate. He defeated Raja Dahir.
recs.rel: Sindh is therefore called Bab-ul-Islam, the gateway of Islam, in the subcontinent.

recs.q: The determinant of the transpose of a square matrix A is equal to what?
opts: Negative of the determinant of A
The inverse of the determinant of A
recs.facts: Interchanging rows and columns does not change the determinant, so det(A transpose) = det(A).
recs.rel: Also det(AB) = det(A) x det(B) for square matrices of the same order.

recs.q: The speed of a train is double that of a car. If the car's speed is 60 km/h, what is the speed of the train?
recs.facts: Double of 60 km/h is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h.
recs.rel: Speed = distance divided by time.

recs.q: In which year did the Muslims of the subcontinent get the right of separate electorates?
recs.facts: Separate electorates were granted to the Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
recs.rel: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 later made the Congress accept separate electorates.

recs.q: What is the average gestation period of a cow?
recs.facts: A cow carries her calf for about 283 days, which is roughly nine months. This is close to the human pregnancy length.
recs.rel: The gestation period of a buffalo is longer, about 310 to 315 days.

recs.q: Kalimullah (the one who spoke with Allah) is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Musa (AS) spoke directly with Allah on Mount Tur, so he is called Kalimullah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah and Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah.

recs.q: Who has scored the most Test runs for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Younis Khan scored 10,099 runs in Tests and is Pakistan's leading Test run scorer. He was the first Pakistani to pass 10,000 Test runs.
recs.rel: Javed Miandad (8,832) and Inzamam-ul-Haq (8,829) come next.

recs.q: What does the name Moen jo Daro (Mohenjo-daro) mean?
recs.facts: Mohenjo-daro is a Sindhi name meaning Mound of the Dead. It was a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization.
recs.rel: It is located in Larkana district of Sindh and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

recs.q: Which Islamic Summit of the OIC was held in Pakistan (Lahore) in 1974?
recs.facts: The Second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC was hosted in Lahore in February 1974. The first summit was held in Rabat in 1969.
recs.rel: The Lahore summit was attended by many Muslim heads of state and led to Bangladesh being recognised by Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word plentiful?
recs.facts: Plentiful means more than enough, and its opposite is scarce, meaning in short supply.
recs.rel: Other antonyms of plentiful are rare, sparse and insufficient.

recs.q: On which date was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) established?
recs.facts: The SCO was formally established in Shanghai on 15 June 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan and India became full SCO members in 2017.

recs.q: What does SCO stand for?
recs.facts: SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a Eurasian political, economic and security grouping.
recs.rel: Its permanent bodies are the Secretariat in Beijing and the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure in Tashkent.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) have in the Senate of Pakistan?
recs.facts: After the 2018 merger of FATA and the 2024 changes, KPK has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat and 1 non-Muslim.
recs.rel: Before the merger of FATA, KPK had 22 seats and the Senate had 104 members.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'utility'?
recs.facts: Utility means the quality of being useful or serving a practical purpose. Usefulness is therefore its closest synonym.
recs.rel: The word 'utilize' means to make practical use of something.

recs.q: According to the 2017 census, what was the population of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 6th Population and Housing Census of 2017 counted 207,684,626 people in Pakistan.
recs.rel: The next census, held in 2023, counted about 241.5 million people.

recs.q: Who made the first solo non-stop flight across the Atlantic Ocean in 1927?
recs.facts: Charles Lindbergh flew the Spirit of St. Louis alone from New York to Paris in May 1927.
recs.rel: Alcock and Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight (not solo) in 1919, and Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly it solo in 1932.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word advance?
recs.facts: To advance means to move forward, and its opposite is to retreat or move backward.
recs.rel: Advance can also mean to lend money beforehand, in which case it is a noun meaning a loan paid early.

recs.q: Who described Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity?
recs.facts: Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title, praising his work for unity at the time of the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Her 1918 book on him is titled Mohomed Ali Jinnah: An Ambassador of Unity.
recs.rel: Gopal Krishna Gokhale had earlier made a similar remark about Jinnah, so some sources trace the phrase to him.

recs.q: What is the antonym of fertile?
recs.facts: Fertile land or a fertile mind produces plenty; the opposite is barren, which produces nothing.
recs.rel: Sterile is also accepted as an antonym of fertile, so sources may give either word.

recs.q: What is the antonym of protect?
recs.facts: To protect is to keep safe from harm; the opposite is to endanger, to put in harm's way.
recs.rel: Defend, guard and shield are synonyms of protect.

recs.q: What is the baby (young one) of a frog called?
recs.facts: A young frog hatches from an egg as a tadpole, which lives in water and breathes with gills. It later grows legs and lungs and becomes an adult frog.
recs.rel: The change from tadpole to frog is called metamorphosis.

recs.q: Bani Israel (Children of Israel) are the descendants of which prophet, whose title was Israel?
recs.facts: Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), and his twelve sons formed the twelve tribes of Bani Israel. Hence the people are called Bani Israel.
recs.rel: Hazrat Musa (AS) is the most prominent prophet sent to Bani Israel.

recs.q: Maputo is the capital of which country?
