recs.facts: Maputo, formerly Lourenco Marques, is the capital of Mozambique.
recs.rel: Mozambique gained independence from Portugal in 1975.

recs.q: There are 24 members in a committee and 5 are men. What is the percentage of women?
recs.facts: Women = 24 - 5 = 19. Percentage = 19 / 24 x 100 = 79.17 percent.
recs.rel: The men are 5/24 x 100 = 20.83 percent, and the two percentages add up to 100.

recs.q: How many nations and territories belong to the Commonwealth Games Federation, which takes part in the Commonwealth Games?
recs.facts: The Commonwealth Games Federation has 74 members (nations and territories), including dependent territories that compete under their own flags.
recs.rel: The Commonwealth of Nations has only 56 member states, and about 72 teams took part in the Glasgow 2026 Games according to some reports.

recs.q: Who introduced the system of Basic Democracies in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan introduced Basic Democracies through the Basic Democracies Order of 1959. Ordinary citizens elected Basic Democrats from local union councils, who then acted as the electoral college.
recs.rel: The system was ended by General Yahya Khan's government and replaced under the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: Diamond is an allotrope of which element?
recs.facts: Diamond is made of carbon atoms joined in a rigid tetrahedral crystal structure.
recs.rel: Graphite is another allotrope of carbon, and diamond is the hardest natural substance.

recs.q: What is the antonym of "embrace" in the sense of accepting an idea?
recs.facts: To embrace an idea is to accept it eagerly, so its opposite is to reject it.
recs.rel: Embrace also means to hold someone in the arms, and in that sense a synonym is hug.

recs.q: For what is Sadequain famous?
recs.facts: Sadequain (1930-1987) was a famous Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known for his Quranic calligraphy and murals.
recs.rel: He painted the ceiling mural at the Mangla Dam power house and the Frere Hall murals in Karachi.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Fatima (RA) to Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the youngest daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
recs.rel: She is known as Zahra and Sayyidat Nisa al-Alamin.

recs.q: The Flemish people are found mainly in which country?
recs.facts: The Flemish are the Dutch-speaking people of Flanders, the northern region of Belgium.
recs.rel: The French-speaking people of southern Belgium are called Walloons.

recs.q: What is the width (length between the posts) of a standard football goal?
recs.facts: The two posts of a standard football goal are 24 feet (7.32 m) apart.
recs.rel: The goal height is 8 feet (2.44 m).

recs.q: What is the capital of Iceland?
recs.facts: Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland. It is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
recs.rel: Iceland is a Nordic island country in the North Atlantic Ocean.

recs.q: In which city is the National Library of Pakistan located?
recs.facts: The National Library of Pakistan is located in Islamabad on Constitution Avenue in the same complex as other national institutions.
recs.rel: It was established in 1951 in Karachi and later moved to Islamabad.

recs.q: In which year was the construction of Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi started (established)?
recs.facts: The foundation of Pakistan Steel Mills was laid in 1973 by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto with Soviet help.
recs.rel: The mill began production in 1981.

recs.q: What is the length of the Panama Canal in nautical miles, approximately?
recs.facts: The Panama Canal is about 82 km (51 miles) long. Since 1 nautical mile is 1.852 km, this is about 44 nautical miles.
recs.rel: The canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans and opened in 1914.

recs.q: Which is generally regarded as the oldest sea port of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Karachi Port is the oldest and busiest port of Pakistan; modern port development there began in the 19th century.
recs.rel: Port Qasim is the second major port and Gwadar is the newest deep-sea port.

recs.q: How many provinces does Pakistan have?
recs.facts: Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.
recs.rel: Islamabad Capital Territory, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir are not provinces.

recs.q: Which angel is in charge of rain and provision according to Islamic belief?
recs.facts: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel entrusted with rain, vegetation and sustenance. Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Izrail takes souls.
recs.rel: Mikail is also spelled Mika'il and is mentioned by name in Surah Al-Baqarah.

recs.q: Who first suggested the name Pakistan?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
recs.rel: The name is made from the letters of Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan.

recs.q: How many main blood groups are there in the ABO system?
recs.facts: The main blood groups are A, B, AB and O, which makes four.
recs.rel: Each group can be Rh positive or Rh negative, giving eight common types.

recs.q: Who presented the famous Poor Man's (labourer's) Budget in the interim government of British India just before independence?
recs.facts: Liaqat Ali Khan, as Finance Member of the interim government, presented a budget that taxed big business and industrialists to relieve the poor. It was called the Poor Man's Budget.
recs.rel: The budget was presented on 28 February 1947; the interim government itself was formed in September 1946.

recs.q: To which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
recs.facts: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, which was then called Yathrib.
recs.rel: This migration, the Hijrah, marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

recs.q: Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. What will be the age of his sister after 12 years?
recs.facts: Sister's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. After 12 years she will be 12 + 12 = 24 years old.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same over time.

recs.q: What is the antonym of appropriate?
recs.facts: Appropriate means suitable for the situation; the opposite is inappropriate or unsuitable.
recs.rel: Suitable, fitting and proper are synonyms of appropriate.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan is Attabad Lake located?
recs.facts: Attabad Lake lies in the Hunza valley of Gilgit-Baltistan near Karimabad. It was formed by a landslide that blocked the Hunza River.
recs.rel: The landslide happened in January 2010 and the lake submerged part of the Karakoram Highway.

recs.q: The line y = 7 is parallel to which axis?
opts: It is parallel to neither axis
recs.facts: The line y = 7 is horizontal, because every point on it has y equal to 7. A horizontal line is parallel to the x-axis.
recs.rel: The line x = 7 would be vertical and parallel to the y-axis.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word breach?
recs.facts: To breach means to break a rule or agreement. Its opposite is compliance or observance, meaning keeping the rule.
recs.rel: Violation, rupture and gap are synonyms or near synonyms of breach, not opposites.

recs.q: What is the capital of Zimbabwe?
recs.facts: Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.
recs.rel: Harare was formerly called Salisbury.

recs.q: In a circle, what is the distance from the center to any point on the circle called?
recs.facts: The distance from the center to a point on the circle is the radius.
recs.rel: The diameter is twice the radius.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word 'comic'?
recs.facts: Comic means funny or amusing, while tragic means sad and causing sorrow, so tragic is the opposite.
recs.rel: Comedy and tragedy are the two classic types of drama.

recs.q: In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) institution founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Aligarh?
recs.facts: Sir Syed founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School at Aligarh on 24 May 1875, which later became MAO College.
recs.rel: The school was raised to MAO College in 1877 and became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920; some sources date the college itself to 1877.

recs.q: How many member countries does the Commonwealth of Nations have?
recs.facts: The Commonwealth of Nations has 56 member states, the latest being Gabon and Togo who joined in June 2022.
recs.rel: Before 2022 the Commonwealth had 54 members.

recs.q: In which year was the Communal Award announced by the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald?
recs.facts: The Communal Award was announced on 16 August 1932 and gave separate electorates to Muslims and other minorities.
recs.rel: Gandhi fasted against the grant of separate electorates to the Depressed Classes, which led to the Poona Pact.

recs.q: In which city and country is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank located?
recs.facts: The Asian Development Bank was founded in 1966 and has its headquarters in Mandaluyong City, Metro Manila, in the Philippines.
recs.rel: Japan and the United States are its largest shareholders, and Pakistan is a founding member.

recs.q: In which direction is China located with respect to Pakistan?
recs.facts: China lies to the north-east of Pakistan and borders Gilgit-Baltistan through the Khunjerab Pass.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan and China across the Khunjerab Pass.

recs.q: Change into indirect speech: Ali said, "I was doing work."
opts: Ali said that he was doing work.
Ali said that he had been doing work.
Ali said that I had been doing work.
Ali said that he has been doing work.
recs.facts: The reporting verb is in the past, so past continuous 'was doing' changes to past perfect continuous 'had been doing', and 'I' becomes 'he'.
recs.rel: Backshift moves each tense one step into the past in indirect speech.

recs.q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train is twice as fast. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in the string EAVNJEGFDUI?
recs.facts: The letters are E, A, V, N, J, E, G, F, D, U, I. The vowels are E, A, E, U and I, which makes 5.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: What does Radd-ul-Fasaad, the name of the Pakistan Army operation launched in 2017, mean?
recs.facts: Radd-ul-Fasaad is Arabic and means rejecting or eliminating discord and mischief. The operation was launched in February 2017 to remove the remaining terrorism and strengthen border security.
recs.rel: Operation Zarb-e-Azb (2014) was the earlier major operation in North Waziristan.

recs.q: Which of the following is a prime number: 7, 9, 18, 21?
recs.facts: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. 9 = 3 x 3, 18 = 2 x 9 and 21 = 3 x 7 are composite.
recs.rel: 2 is the only even prime number.

recs.q: Electric current is due to the flow of what?
recs.facts: In a metallic conductor, the free electrons drift under a potential difference, and this flow of charge is the electric current.
recs.rel: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of genuine?
recs.facts: Genuine means real and not imitation. Authentic has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Sincere is also used as a synonym of genuine when talking about feelings.

recs.q: The Kirthar Hills (Kirthar Range) lie along the border of which two provinces of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Kirthar Range runs north to south and forms the boundary between Sindh and Balochistan. It is the southern part of the Sulaiman-Kirthar system.
recs.rel: Zardak Peak (about 2,260 m) is generally named as its highest point, though sources differ slightly.

recs.q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and his wife Hazrat Sarah. He was born when Sarah was very old.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

recs.q: On which date is Labour Day (International Workers' Day) observed?
recs.facts: Labour Day is observed every year on 1 May, including in Pakistan, where it is a public holiday.
recs.rel: The day commemorates the Haymarket affair of Chicago in 1886.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word lethal?
recs.facts: Lethal means able to cause death, so its opposite is harmless. Deadly, fatal and poisonous are synonyms or close in meaning.
recs.rel: The word lethal comes from the Latin word letum, meaning death.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: Z, X, U, Q, ?
recs.facts: The positions are 26, 24, 21, 17 and the differences are 2, 3, 4, so the next difference is 5. 17 minus 5 is 12, which is L.
recs.rel: The differences in this series increase by 1 each time.

recs.q: The Kirthar Range is regarded as the southern extension of which mountain range?
recs.facts: The Kirthar Range runs north to south along the border of Sindh and Balochistan and is usually described as the southern extension of the Sulaiman Range.
recs.rel: Some sources treat the Kirthar Range as a separate range; its highest point is Kutte Ji Kabar.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the River Nile?
recs.facts: The Nile is about 6,650 km (4,130 miles) long. It is traditionally given as the longest river in the world.
recs.rel: Sources differ, and some textbooks give figures near 6,400 to 6,700 km; the Amazon is also claimed as longer by some measurements.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word obsolete?
recs.facts: Obsolete means no longer in use or out of date, so its opposite is current or modern.
recs.rel: Outdated and archaic are synonyms of obsolete.

recs.q: Porto-Novo is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin in West Africa.
recs.rel: Cotonou is the largest city and seat of government of Benin.

recs.q: By which process do green plants prepare their food?
recs.facts: Plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose in photosynthesis.
recs.rel: Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis.

recs.q: Who founded the political party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)?
recs.facts: PTI was founded by Imran Khan in April 1996 in Lahore. He has remained its founder and leader since.
recs.rel: Imran Khan became Prime Minister of Pakistan in August 2018 and was removed through a no-confidence vote in April 2022.

recs.q: Who said that the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran, that is, he was the embodiment of the Quran?
recs.facts: When asked about the character of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.
recs.rel: This narration is recorded in Sahih Muslim and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad.

recs.q: Which is the oldest seaport of Pakistan, as given in Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Karachi Port is generally given as the oldest and main seaport of Pakistan, with the modern port working from the 19th century. Gwadar and Port Qasim are much newer.
recs.rel: Karachi Port Trust was established in 1887; some sources name the ancient port of Banbhore as older.

recs.q: Which tennis Grand Slam tournament is still played on grass courts?
recs.facts: Wimbledon in London is the only Grand Slam still played on grass.
recs.rel: The French Open is played on clay, while the US Open and Australian Open use hard courts.

recs.q: What is the synonym of afraid?
recs.facts: Afraid means feeling fear, which is the same as frightened.
recs.rel: Fearless and courageous are antonyms of afraid.

recs.q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
recs.facts: The kelvin (K) is the base SI unit of temperature. Celsius and Fahrenheit are not SI units.
recs.rel: 0 K is called absolute zero, equal to minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'transparent'?
recs.facts: Transparent means see-through, so its opposite is opaque, which does not let light through.
recs.rel: Wood and metal are opaque materials.

recs.q: Which type of engine is used in jet aircraft?
recs.facts: Jet aircraft are powered by gas turbine engines such as the turbojet and turbofan. They produce thrust by expelling a fast stream of hot gas backwards.
recs.rel: Frank Whittle of Britain patented the turbojet engine in 1930.

recs.q: Which major event took place in the 10th year of Hijrah (10 AH)?
opts: Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
recs.facts: In 10 AH the Holy Prophet (PBUH) performed his only and last Hajj and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat. The other events took place in earlier years (Badr 2 AH, Hudaibiya 6 AH, Makkah conquest 8 AH).
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, a few months after the Farewell Pilgrimage.

recs.q: Which is the second highest mountain in the world?
recs.facts: K2, at about 8,611 m, is the second highest mountain in the world after Mount Everest.
recs.rel: K2 is the highest mountain of Pakistan and lies in the Karakoram range.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 380 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 380 / 500 x 100 = 76%.
recs.rel: The absent percentage is 24%.

recs.q: Find the next number in the series: 55, 579, 65, 580, ?
recs.facts: The series is two interleaved series. The 1st, 3rd and 5th terms go 55, 65, 75 (add 10) and the 2nd and 4th terms go 579, 580, 581 (add 1). The 5th term is 75.
recs.rel: Interleaved series are solved by reading odd and even positions separately.

recs.q: In which surah of the Holy Quran is Ruh-ul-Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit, Hazrat Jibreel AS) mentioned?
recs.facts: Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26:193) says that the Trustworthy Spirit brought down the Quran upon the heart of the Prophet (PBUH). The Trustworthy Spirit is Hazrat Jibreel (AS).
recs.rel: Jibreel is also called Ruh-ul-Qudus in other verses, for example in Surah Al-Baqarah.

recs.q: In what amount was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)?
recs.facts: By the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. This began Dogra rule in Kashmir.
recs.rel: The treaty was signed on 16 March 1846 after the First Anglo-Sikh War.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word amalgamate?
recs.facts: To amalgamate means to merge or combine into one. The opposite is to separate.
recs.rel: Amalgam is also the name of an alloy of mercury with another metal.

recs.q: What is the antonym of competent?
recs.facts: Competent means having the ability to do something well; the opposite is incompetent, meaning lacking ability.
recs.rel: Competent and capable are synonyms, so they cannot be the antonym.

recs.q: What is the antonym of foremost?
recs.facts: Foremost means first in position or importance; the opposite is last (hindmost).
recs.rel: Foremost, leading and chief are all synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of glory?
recs.facts: Glory means high honour and fame; the opposite is disgrace or shame.
recs.rel: Glory and honour are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of modern?
recs.facts: Modern means belonging to the present or recent time; the opposite is ancient, meaning belonging to the distant past.
recs.rel: Old-fashioned is another antonym of modern.

recs.q: In which year was the first Asia Cup cricket tournament held?
recs.facts: The first Asia Cup was played in Sharjah, UAE, in 1984. India won it.
recs.rel: The Asia Cup was started by the Asian Cricket Council founders including Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka.

recs.q: Who was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the son of Uthman, who was known as Abu Quhafa. He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.
recs.rel: Abu Bakr's mother was Salma bint Sakhr, known as Umm-ul-Khair.

recs.q: What is the base of the common logarithm?
recs.facts: The common logarithm uses base 10, so log 100 = 2 because 10 squared is 100.
recs.rel: The natural logarithm uses base e, which is about 2.718.

recs.q: In which part of the world do the Bushmen (San people) live?
recs.facts: The Bushmen or San are indigenous hunter-gatherers of southern Africa, living mainly in the Kalahari Desert in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa.
recs.rel: Their languages are known for click sounds.

recs.q: Accra is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea.
recs.rel: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.

recs.q: Saint John's is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Saint John's is the capital of Antigua and Barbuda, on the island of Antigua.
recs.rel: Antigua and Barbuda became independent from Britain in 1981.

recs.q: What is the capital of Greenland?
recs.facts: Nuuk is the capital and largest city of Greenland.
recs.rel: Greenland is an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark.

recs.q: What is the capital of Norway?
recs.facts: Oslo is the capital and largest city of Norway.
recs.rel: Norway is not a member of the European Union.

recs.q: In which years were the Olympic Games cancelled because of World War II?
recs.facts: The 1940 Games (Tokyo/Helsinki) and the 1944 Games (London) were cancelled due to the war.
recs.rel: The Olympics were also cancelled in 1916 because of World War I.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'clumsy'?
recs.facts: A clumsy person moves or handles things in an awkward way and often drops or breaks them.
recs.rel: The opposite of clumsy is graceful or deft.

recs.q: Change the voice: Were clothes dried by the mother?
opts: Did the mother dry the clothes?
Was the mother drying the clothes?
Had the mother dried the clothes?
Does the mother dry the clothes?
recs.facts: The sentence is passive in the past simple tense, so the active form is 'Did the mother dry the clothes?' with the agent as the subject and the verb in base form after did.
recs.rel: In the past simple, the passive uses was or were plus the past participle.

recs.q: Which of the following is the synonym of 'contain'?
recs.facts: To contain something means to have it inside or to hold it. 'Hold' is the closest in meaning.
recs.rel: 'Contain' can also mean to keep something under control, as in contain a fire.

recs.q: Which country owes the largest amount of unpaid dues (arrears) to the United Nations?
recs.facts: The United States is the biggest contributor to the UN budget and also has the largest unpaid arrears, over 2 billion US dollars on the regular budget in 2026 plus peacekeeping dues.
recs.rel: China is usually the second largest debtor, often paying its dues late in the year.

recs.q: In which year and at which city was the Lahore Declaration signed between Pakistan and India?
recs.facts: The Lahore Declaration was signed on 21 February 1999 in Lahore by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
recs.rel: It was signed a few months before the Kargil conflict of 1999.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word development?
recs.facts: Development means growth or advancement, while retrogression means moving backward or declining.
recs.rel: Other opposites of development include decline, regression and deterioration.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'difference'?
recs.facts: Difference means the quality of being unlike. Its opposite is similarity, meaning likeness.
recs.rel: Distinction, variety and contrast are synonyms or near synonyms of difference.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'divided'?
recs.facts: Divided means split apart. Its opposite is united.
recs.rel: Separated, split and broken are synonyms of divided.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of 'disgust'?
recs.facts: Disgust is a strong feeling of dislike and sickness at something. Revulsion has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Loathing and repugnance are also synonyms of disgust.

recs.q: What large sea wave is usually caused by an earthquake under the ocean floor?
recs.facts: A strong undersea earthquake suddenly moves the sea floor and displaces a huge volume of water, which travels as a tsunami.
recs.rel: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was caused by a magnitude 9 earthquake near Sumatra.

recs.q: Who was the first woman elected to the United States Congress?
recs.facts: Jeannette Rankin of Montana was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1916 and took her seat in 1917.
recs.rel: Nancy Pelosi became the first woman Speaker of the US House in 2007.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "essential"?
recs.facts: Essential means absolutely needed, which is the meaning of necessary.
recs.rel: Other synonyms are vital and indispensable.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'excuse' used as a verb meaning to forgive?
recs.facts: To excuse means to forgive or let go without blame. Its opposite is to accuse or blame someone.
recs.rel: 'Condemn' and 'blame' are also opposites of excuse in this sense.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'exhibit'?
recs.facts: To exhibit means to show openly. Its opposite is to conceal or hide.
recs.rel: An exhibition is a public show of things.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'exhibit'?
recs.facts: To exhibit means to show something publicly. 'Display' has the same meaning.
recs.rel: 'Exhibit' can also be a noun meaning an object shown in a museum or court.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'exponent'?
recs.facts: An exponent is a person who explains or promotes an idea or cause, so an advocate is the closest meaning. An opponent is the opposite.
recs.rel: In mathematics, an exponent is the small raised number that shows the power of a base.

recs.q: What is the antonym of futility?
recs.facts: Futility means uselessness or having no result. Fruitfulness, meaning being productive and useful, is the opposite.
recs.rel: Uselessness and vanity are synonyms of futility.

recs.q: Ali is going in the direction of west. He turns left and then turns right. In which direction is Ali going now?
recs.facts: Facing west, a left turn points him south. Then a right turn from south points him west again.
recs.rel: Facing west, his left is south and his right is north.

recs.q: One hectare is equal to how many square metres?
recs.facts: One hectare is a square of 100 m by 100 m, which is 10,000 square metres.
recs.rel: One hectare is about 2.47 acres.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the Himalaya mountain range?
recs.facts: The Himalayas stretch for roughly 2,400 km (about 1,500 miles) from the Indus gorge in the west to the Brahmaputra gorge in the east.
recs.rel: Some sources give 2,400 to 2,500 km; Pakistani textbooks use about 2,400 km.

recs.q: Which country was the world's largest arms importer in the latest SIPRI data (2021-25)?
recs.facts: SIPRI's March 2026 data for 2021-25 ranks Ukraine first, with about 9.7 percent of global arms imports, followed by India. The USA is a major exporter, not the top importer.
recs.rel: In the 2015-19 and earlier periods India or Saudi Arabia led, and India was second after Ukraine in 2020-24 data as well.

recs.q: At how many points can two distinct lines in a plane intersect each other?
recs.facts: Two distinct lines meet in at most one point. If they are parallel they do not meet at all.
recs.rel: Two coincident lines share all their points, so they are not distinct.

recs.q: The followers of Hazrat Isa (AS) are called what?
recs.facts: The followers of Hazrat Isa (Jesus) are called Christians. Christianity is the largest religion in the world by followers.
recs.rel: The Quran calls them Nasara (Nazarenes).

recs.q: Which animal did the people of Thamud kill, despite the warning of Prophet Salih (AS)?
recs.facts: The nation of Thamud killed the she-camel sent by Allah as a miracle for Prophet Salih (AS), and was then destroyed.
recs.rel: The people of Thamud lived at Al-Hijr in northern Arabia.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word 'kith' (as in 'kith and kin')?
recs.facts: Kith means one's friends, neighbours and acquaintances, while kin means blood relatives.
recs.rel: Candidates often answered relatives, but that is the meaning of kin.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'kith'?
recs.facts: Kith means friends and acquaintances, so its opposite is a stranger.
recs.rel: The phrase 'kith and kin' means friends and relatives.

recs.q: The word 'Pakistan' means the land of what?
recs.facts: Pakistan means 'Land of the Pure' (Pak means pure and stan means land).
recs.rel: The name was coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: The standard of living ____ since his son joined service.
recs.facts: The subject standard is singular and since needs the present perfect tense, so has risen is correct.
recs.rel: Since is followed by a point in time and goes with the present perfect tense.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: How did you manage it?
opts: How was it managed by you?
How it was managed by you?
How did it managed by you?
How is it managed by you?
recs.facts: A simple past question becomes was or were plus the past participle, so the passive is How was it managed by you?
recs.rel: In the passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

recs.q: On which date was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza imposed martial law on 7 October 1958 and General Ayub Khan became the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Ayub Khan then removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.
recs.rel: The second martial law came in 1969 under Yahya Khan and the third in 1977 under Zia-ul-Haq.

recs.q: Near which city is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj, located?
recs.facts: Mina is a valley about 5 km east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stay there and perform the stoning of the Jamarat.
recs.rel: Arafat and Muzdalifah are the other nearby sites of the Hajj rites.

recs.q: Mogadishu is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean coast.
recs.rel: Somalia is located in the Horn of Africa.

recs.q: Monrovia is the capital city of which country?
recs.facts: Monrovia is the capital and largest city of Liberia in West Africa.
recs.rel: Monrovia is named after the US President James Monroe.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: When morning ___, the murderer was caught.
recs.facts: The natural phrase is 'when morning came', meaning when daylight arrived.
recs.rel: 'Arrive' and 'reach' usually need a place or destination, while 'come' suits time and seasons.

recs.q: What is the height of Nanga Parbat, the ninth highest mountain in the world?
recs.facts: Nanga Parbat rises to 8,126 metres (26,660 feet) above sea level. It is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
recs.rel: Nanga Parbat is also called Diamer, meaning huge mountain, and is the second highest peak in Pakistan after K2.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word obscure?
recs.facts: Obscure means unclear or not well known, so its opposite is clear (or evident).
recs.rel: Synonyms of obscure include vague, unclear and dim.

recs.q: What was the old name of Thailand?
recs.facts: Thailand was officially known as Siam until 1939, and again briefly from 1945 to 1949. The name was changed to Thailand, meaning land of the free.
recs.rel: The Gulf of Siam is now called the Gulf of Thailand.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to optional?
recs.facts: Optional means left to choice and not required. Voluntary has the same sense, while the other options mean required.
recs.rel: Compulsory is the antonym of optional.

recs.q: From which region does the Indus River originate?
recs.facts: The Indus rises in the Tibetan plateau near Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar. It then flows through Ladakh and Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.
recs.rel: The Indus enters Pakistan through Gilgit-Baltistan.

recs.q: The girls are 33 and the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many boys are there?
recs.facts: Boys = girls + 7 = 33 + 7 = 40.
recs.rel: The total number of boys and girls here is 73.

recs.q: 6 is what percentage of 20?
recs.facts: Percentage = 6 / 20 x 100 = 30 percent.
recs.rel: Percentage = part divided by whole, multiplied by 100.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of office of the President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 44 gives the President a term of five years from the day he enters office.
recs.rel: A person cannot hold the office of President for more than two consecutive terms.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word plentiful?
recs.facts: Plentiful means existing in large quantities, which is the same as abundant.
recs.rel: Other synonyms of plentiful are ample, copious and bountiful.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is Gwadar Port located?
recs.facts: Gwadar is a coastal city on the Arabian Sea in southwestern Balochistan, and its deep-sea port is there.
recs.rel: Gwadar Port is a key part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

recs.q: Who invented the movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440?
recs.facts: Johannes Gutenberg of Germany developed the movable-type printing press in the mid-1400s.
recs.rel: Movable type had earlier been used in China and Korea, but Gutenberg's press is the textbook answer.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters RAPIS to form the name of a famous capital city. Which city is it, and of which country is it the capital?
recs.facts: The letters R, A, P, I, S rearrange to make PARIS. Paris is the capital of France.
recs.rel: Paris stands on the River Seine and is the capital of France.

recs.q: What does RCD stand for in the context of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
recs.facts: RCD stands for Regional Cooperation for Development, a 1964 economic cooperation body of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
recs.rel: It later became the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO).

recs.q: Which country joined the United Nations in 2002 after its people approved membership in a referendum?
recs.facts: Swiss voters approved UN membership in a referendum in March 2002, and Switzerland became the 190th member in September 2002.
recs.rel: Switzerland had earlier rejected UN membership in a 1986 referendum.

recs.q: Which Muslim League leader responded to the Nehru Report (1928) with his famous Fourteen Points in 1929?
recs.facts: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates and Muslim demands, so Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim reply.
recs.rel: Jinnah had earlier put forward his Delhi Muslim Proposals in 1927.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to seize?
recs.facts: To seize means to take hold of something suddenly and by force, which is to grab.
recs.rel: Capture and snatch are also synonyms of seize.

recs.q: Who founded the Scientific Society in the subcontinent in 1864?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur in 1864 to translate Western scientific works into Urdu. It later moved to Aligarh.
recs.rel: The society published the Aligarh Institute Gazette.

recs.q: For how many years did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) live in Madina after the Hijrat?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) migrated to Madina in 622 CE and stayed there until his death in 632 CE, about ten years. He migrated at age 53 and passed away at 63.
recs.rel: The first mosque he built in Madina was Masjid Quba, followed by Masjid-e-Nabawi.

recs.q: Approximately how many princely states existed in British India at the time of the partition in 1947?
recs.facts: At partition about 562 princely states were ruled by local rulers under British paramountcy, and each was to join India or Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly (562 to 565), and some candidates quote 530 or 565.

recs.q: The Holy Quran as revealed by Allah consists of which of the following?
recs.facts: The Quran itself is the Arabic text revealed by Allah. Translations and tafseer are human explanations and are not part of the Quran.
recs.rel: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.

recs.q: Choose the correct direct speech of: The teacher said that he could not meet all of his students.
opts: The teacher said, "I cannot meet all of my students."
The teacher said, "He could not meet all of his students."
The teacher said, "I could not meet all of your students."
The teacher said, "I did not meet all of my students."
recs.facts: In direct speech the past form could changes back to can and he and his change to I and my.
recs.rel: Reporting words said that is dropped and quotation marks are added in direct speech.

recs.q: The Dragon's Mouth (Bocas del Dragon) strait lies between Trinidad and which country?
recs.facts: The Dragon's Mouth is a strait between the north-west tip of Trinidad and the Paria Peninsula of Venezuela. It links the Gulf of Paria with the Atlantic Ocean.
recs.rel: Trinidad and Tobago is an island nation in the southern Caribbean.

recs.q: Which of the following are the three types of blood cells?
opts: Red cells, white cells and platelets
Red cells, white cells and haemoglobin
recs.facts: Blood contains red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. Plasma is the liquid part, not a cell.
recs.rel: Red blood cells carry oxygen using haemoglobin.

recs.q: Which of the following is a fard (obligatory) act of wudu according to the Hanafi school?
opts: Washing the hands up to the wrists
recs.facts: The four faraiz of wudu are washing the face, washing both arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing both feet up to the ankles. Gargling and rinsing the nose are sunnah.
recs.rel: The four faraiz of wudu are taken from verse 6 of Surah Al-Ma'idah.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
recs.facts: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' (1984).
recs.rel: Hector Bolitho wrote another well-known biography titled 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.

recs.q: What is 2 + 2?
recs.facts: Adding 2 and 2 gives 4.
recs.rel: Addition is commutative, so the order of the numbers does not matter.

recs.q: Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. How many students are absent?
recs.facts: Absent students = 1500 - 1200 = 300.
recs.rel: The percentage of absent students here is 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20%.

recs.q: Who was the first President under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, taking office in August 1973?
recs.facts: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister when the 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973. Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry became the President at that time.
recs.rel: Bhutto had been President before this, and he became Prime Minister under the new parliamentary system.

recs.q: Which country became independent in 1994, ending the last United Nations trusteeship?
recs.facts: Palau gained independence on 1 October 1994 and became the last UN Trust Territory to end its trusteeship.
recs.rel: Palau later joined the United Nations in December 1994.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 24th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 24th is 22 days. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra days, so count 1 days forward from Friday to reach Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2017?
recs.facts: UNHCR reported that Turkey hosted about 3.5 million refugees at the end of 2017, the largest number worldwide.
recs.rel: Turkey stayed at the top of the list for several years because of the Syrian refugee crisis.

recs.q: Who was the 7th President of the United States?
recs.facts: Andrew Jackson served as the 7th US President from 1829 to 1837, after John Quincy Adams.
recs.rel: Martin Van Buren followed Jackson as the 8th President.

recs.q: Which is the 6th most populous country in the world?
recs.facts: The ranking is India, China, USA, Indonesia, Pakistan and then Nigeria in sixth place.
recs.rel: Brazil is seventh, and Pakistan is fifth.

recs.q: If a helicopter uses 50 litres of fuel to travel 200 km, how many litres will it use to travel 350 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km = 50 / 200 = 0.25 litre. For 350 km: 350 x 0.25 = 87.5 litres.
recs.rel: This is a direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.

recs.q: Out of 400 students, 360 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 360 / 400 x 100 = 90%. The absent students are 40, which is 10%.
recs.rel: Present and absent percentages add up to 100%.

recs.q: A helicopter uses 80 gallons of fuel to fly 320 km. How many gallons will it need to fly 800 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km is 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 km the helicopter needs 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.
recs.rel: Problems like this are direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 1350 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.facts: Absent students = 1500 - 1350 = 150. Percentage absent = 150 / 1500 x 100 = 10 percent.
recs.rel: Percentage present in the same class is 90 percent, since the two parts add up to 100 percent.

recs.q: In a class of 500 students, 150 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.facts: Absent students = 500 - 150 = 350. Percentage absent = 350 / 500 x 100 = 70 percent.
recs.rel: The percentage present here is 150 / 500 x 100 = 30 percent.

recs.q: On which date is Pakistan Air Force Day celebrated?
recs.facts: PAF Day is celebrated on 7 September to honour the PAF's performance in the 1965 war. On that day in 1965 PAF pilots, including M. M. Alam, shot down several Indian aircraft.
recs.rel: Defence Day is observed on 6 September.

recs.q: In which year did the United States declare its independence?
recs.facts: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776. That is why 4 July is celebrated as American Independence Day.
recs.rel: In July 2026 the United States marked 250 years since its Declaration of Independence.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word annihilate?
recs.facts: To annihilate is to destroy something utterly so that nothing remains. Its closest meaning is to destroy completely.
recs.rel: The word comes from the Latin annihilare, meaning to reduce to nothing.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word sumptuous?
recs.facts: Sumptuous means grand and expensive-looking, so its opposite is meagre or poor. Lavish, splendid and rich are synonyms.
recs.rel: Sumptuous is often used for meals, such as a sumptuous feast.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word Almighty?
recs.facts: Almighty means having unlimited power. Its opposite is powerless or weak.
recs.rel: Almighty is used for God in Islam and in many other religions.

recs.q: What is the antonym of coma?
recs.facts: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness, so its opposite is consciousness (being awake and aware).
recs.rel: The word coma comes from the Greek koma, meaning deep sleep.

recs.q: What is the antonym of contiguous?
recs.facts: Contiguous means sharing a common border or touching; the opposite is separate or detached.
recs.rel: Pakistan and India are contiguous countries because they share a border.

recs.q: What is the antonym of divide?
recs.facts: Divide means to split into parts; the opposite is unite, to join together.
recs.rel: Unity is one of the three guiding principles of the Quaid-e-Azam: Unity, Faith and Discipline.

recs.q: What is the antonym of inaccuracy?
recs.facts: Inaccuracy means lack of correctness; the opposite is precision or accuracy.
recs.rel: Error, mistake and fault are synonyms of inaccuracy.

recs.q: What is the antonym of isolation?
recs.facts: Isolation means being alone and apart from others; the opposite is companionship or togetherness.
recs.rel: Isolation, seclusion and solitude are close synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of mild?
recs.facts: Mild means gentle or not severe; the opposite is harsh, meaning severe or rough.
recs.rel: Some candidates remembered tamed here, but tamed is not the standard antonym of mild.

recs.q: What is the antonym of normally?
recs.facts: Normally means in the usual way; the opposite is abnormally, meaning in an unusual way.
recs.rel: Usually, regularly and commonly are synonyms of normally.

recs.q: What is the antonym of prosperous?
recs.facts: Prosperous means rich and successful; the opposite is impoverished, meaning poor.
recs.rel: Prosperous, wealthy and thriving are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of retrieve?
recs.facts: To retrieve is to get something back; the opposite is to lose it.
recs.rel: Recover and regain are synonyms of retrieve.

recs.q: What is the antonym of timely?
recs.facts: Timely means happening at the right moment; the opposite is untimely, happening at the wrong moment.
recs.rel: Prompt, punctual and opportune are close synonyms of timely.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of apposite?
recs.facts: Apposite means very appropriate or relevant to the matter; the opposite is irrelevant or inapt.
recs.rel: Apposite, apt and pertinent are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the synonym (closest meaning) of appropriate?
recs.facts: Appropriate means right for a particular situation, which is the meaning of suitable.
recs.rel: Fitting and proper are also synonyms of appropriate.

recs.q: Which Surah of the Holy Quran was revealed immediately after Surah An-Naml (the Ant) in the commonly given order of revelation?
recs.facts: In the commonly used (Egyptian) order of revelation, Surah An-Naml is the 48th Surah revealed and Surah Al-Qasas follows it.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly on the exact order of revelation, but both An-Naml and Al-Qasas are Makki Surahs.

recs.q: Who is the custodian of the House in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Speaker presides over the sessions of the National Assembly and is regarded as the custodian of the House. He maintains order and decides points of procedure.
recs.rel: In the Speaker's absence the Deputy Speaker presides over the House.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
recs.facts: The IAEA has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. It promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy.
recs.rel: The IAEA is an independent organization that reports to the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah pass the matriculation examination of Bombay University?
recs.facts: Most sources state that Jinnah passed the Bombay University matriculation examination at the age of 16 in 1892. He then left for England in early 1893.
recs.rel: Some sources give 1891 for his matriculation because his birth year is itself disputed.

recs.q: On which date did the Pakistan Army launch Operation Zarb-e-Azb in North Waziristan?
recs.facts: Operation Zarb-e-Azb against militants in North Waziristan began on 15 June 2014. It followed the attack on Karachi airport and the failure of peace talks.
recs.rel: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017 as its follow-up.

recs.q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr, six from the Muhajirun and eight from the Ansar. About 70 of the Quraish were killed.
recs.rel: About 70 Sahaba were martyred later in the Battle of Uhud.

recs.q: Bait-ul-Maqdas (Bait-ul-Muqaddas), the first qibla of the Muslims, is also known by which name?
recs.facts: Bait-ul-Maqdas in Jerusalem is the site of Masjid-e-Aqsa (Al-Aqsa Mosque). The city itself is also called Al-Quds.
recs.rel: The qibla was changed from Bait-ul-Maqdas to the Kaaba in the second year of Hijra.

recs.q: A barometer is used to measure what?
recs.facts: A barometer measures the pressure of the atmosphere. A falling reading usually warns of bad weather.
recs.rel: Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.

recs.q: Basic Democracies of Ayub Khan were given constitutional status by which constitution?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution made the 80,000 Basic Democrats the electoral college that elected the President and the assemblies.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated by Yahya Khan in 1969.

recs.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
recs.facts: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961 to stop people leaving for West Berlin.
recs.rel: The Wall fell on 9 November 1989.

recs.q: How many surahs of the Quran begin with Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim?
recs.facts: There are 114 surahs and only Surah At-Tawbah does not begin with Bismillah, so 113 do.
recs.rel: Bismillah occurs twice in Surah An-Naml, once at the start and once inside verse 30.

recs.q: Why do we boil water before drinking it?
recs.facts: Boiling kills harmful bacteria and other germs that cause waterborne diseases.
recs.rel: Boiling for about one to three minutes is generally advised for unsafe water.

recs.q: In which of Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points was the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency demanded?
recs.facts: Point 9 of the Quaid's Fourteen Points (1929) demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency.
recs.rel: Sindh was finally separated from Bombay and made a separate province in 1936.

recs.q: Change the voice of the sentence: I bought a book.
opts: A book was bought by me.
A book is bought by me.
A book has been bought by me.
A book had been bought by me.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: A book was bought by me. The object becomes the subject.
recs.rel: In the passive voice the doer of the action is introduced with the word by.

recs.q: By whom, and for how much money, was Kashmir bought under the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846?
opts: Maharaja Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees
Maharaja Ranjit Singh for 50 lakh rupees
Maharaja Hari Singh for 75 lakh rupees
Maharaja Gulab Singh for 25 lakh rupees
recs.facts: After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British sold the valley of Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees under the Treaty of Amritsar.
recs.rel: Gulab Singh's dynasty ruled Jammu and Kashmir until Hari Singh, the last Maharaja, in 1947.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of Britain at the time of the partition of India in 1947?
recs.facts: Clement Attlee of the Labour Party was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951 and passed the Indian Independence Act 1947.
recs.rel: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India, not the Prime Minister.

recs.q: What does BRT stand for?
recs.facts: BRT stands for Bus Rapid Transit, a bus system running on dedicated lanes. Peshawar's BRT is called Zu Peshawar.
recs.rel: Peshawar's BRT was built by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government and opened in August 2020.

recs.q: Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini, which lies in present-day Nepal. He later attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya in India.
recs.rel: In his time his Shakya clan lived near the present Nepal-India border.

recs.q: What is the approximate gestation period of a buffalo?
recs.facts: A buffalo carries its calf for about 10 months, which is roughly 305 to 320 days.
recs.rel: A cow's gestation is shorter, about 280 days.

recs.q: In which city does the Green Line bus (BRT) service run?
recs.facts: The Green Line is a Bus Rapid Transit service in Karachi that runs from Surjani Town toward Numaish.
recs.rel: The Orange Line in Lahore is a metro train, and Peshawar's BRT is called Zu Peshawar.

recs.q: San Jose is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: San Jose is the capital and largest city of Costa Rica in Central America.
recs.rel: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948.

recs.q: What is the capital of Algeria?
recs.facts: Algiers is the capital and largest city of Algeria.
recs.rel: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area since the split of Sudan in 2011.

recs.q: What is the capital of Ethiopia?
recs.facts: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia.
recs.rel: Addis Ababa hosts the headquarters of the African Union.

recs.q: What is the capital of Fiji?
recs.facts: Suva is the capital and largest city of Fiji, on Viti Levu island.
recs.rel: Fiji is an island country in the South Pacific.

recs.q: What is the capital of Finland?
recs.facts: Helsinki is the capital and largest city of Finland.
recs.rel: Finland joined NATO in April 2023.

recs.q: What is the capital of Kenya?
recs.facts: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya.
recs.rel: Nairobi hosts a major United Nations office, UNEP headquarters.

recs.q: What are the members of a Cartesian plane called?
recs.facts: Every point of a Cartesian plane is written as an ordered pair (x, y) of coordinates.
recs.rel: The Cartesian plane is named after the French mathematician Rene Descartes.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: Dogs always chase the cats.
opts: The cats are always chased by dogs.
The cats were always chased by dogs.
The cats are always being chased by dogs.
The cats always chase the dogs.
recs.facts: The sentence is present simple, so the passive is 'am/is/are + past participle': the cats are always chased by dogs.
recs.rel: The 'being' form is used only for the present continuous passive.

recs.q: What causes earthquakes, including those under the ocean?
recs.facts: Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates slip or collide and release energy along faults, on land or the sea floor.
recs.rel: A big undersea earthquake can cause a tsunami.

recs.q: What is the center of a circle called?
opts: Point from which all boundary points are equidistant
recs.facts: The center is the fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from every point on the circle.
recs.rel: The fixed distance is called the radius.

recs.q: What is the centre of a circle?
opts: A fixed point equidistant from every point on the circle
The longest chord of the circle
recs.facts: The centre is the single fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from all points on the circumference. A circle has exactly one centre.
recs.rel: The fixed distance from the centre to the circle is called the radius.

recs.q: What was the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922?
opts: A mob burned a police station and killed policemen, after which Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement
A massacre of unarmed people at a garden in Amritsar
A mutiny of Indian soldiers in Meerut
A salt march to the sea
recs.facts: On 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh a crowd set fire to a police station, killing about 22 policemen. Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
recs.rel: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened earlier, in 1919.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'stagnancy'?
recs.facts: Stagnancy is the state of not moving, flowing or developing, so it means inactivity.
recs.rel: Stagnant water is water that does not flow and often becomes foul.

recs.q: What is a composite number?
opts: A number with exactly two factors
A positive integer greater than 1 with more than two factors
A number that is not divisible by 2
A number with only one factor
recs.facts: A composite number has at least one factor other than 1 and itself, so it has more than two factors. Examples are 4, 6, 8 and 9.
recs.rel: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'contentment'?
opts: Satisfaction and happiness with what one has
recs.facts: Contentment is a state of being happy and satisfied with what one has.
recs.rel: The related adjective is content, and its opposite is discontent.

recs.q: In which year AD was Khyber conquered by the Muslims?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khyber took place in Muharram 7 AH, which corresponds to about 628 AD.
recs.rel: The conquest of Makkah took place later, in 8 AH.

recs.q: Sahih Muslim is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book?
recs.facts: Scholars rank Sahih Bukhari first and Sahih Muslim second in authenticity among the hadith collections.
recs.rel: Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim together are called the Sahihain.

recs.q: What is the official currency of Iran?
recs.facts: The official currency of Iran is the Iranian rial. Ordinary people often quote prices in toman, which equals 10 rials.
recs.rel: Iran has passed a law to remove four zeros from the rial, and parliament kept the name rial rather than toman.

recs.q: Which river is the deepest river in the world?
recs.facts: The Congo River in Africa has been measured at depths of more than 220 metres, making it the deepest known river.
recs.rel: The Amazon carries the largest volume of water, while the Nile is often listed as the longest river.

recs.q: Who delivered the famous Allahabad Address of 1930 in which a separate Muslim state in the north-west of India was envisioned?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal delivered this address as President of the All India Muslim League session at Allahabad in December 1930.
recs.rel: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933.

recs.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word development?
recs.facts: Development means gradual growth or advancement, so improvement is the closest meaning.
recs.rel: Progress and advancement are also synonyms of development.

recs.q: What is a synonym of 'difficult'?
recs.facts: Difficult means needing much effort. Hard has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Easy and simple are antonyms of difficult.

recs.q: Which of the following is a division of Punjab?
recs.facts: Sahiwal is one of the divisions of Punjab. Hyderabad is in Sindh, Quetta in Balochistan and Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: Other Punjab divisions include Lahore, Multan, Faisalabad and Rawalpindi.

recs.q: How many minutes are there in 10 degrees in the DMS (degrees, minutes, seconds) system?
recs.facts: One degree is 60 minutes, so 10 degrees = 10 x 60 = 600 minutes.
recs.rel: One minute is 60 seconds, so one degree is 3600 seconds.

recs.q: Pakistan's economy has traditionally been described as predominantly what kind of economy?
recs.facts: Pakistani textbooks describe the country as agricultural because agriculture supports most of the rural population and provides raw material to industry.
recs.rel: Today the services sector gives the largest share of GDP, while agriculture still employs about a third or more of the workforce.

recs.q: By whom is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected under the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: The Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, usually the leader who has a majority there.
recs.rel: The President then appoints the elected member as Prime Minister.

recs.q: The algebraic expression 4a - 5b - 6 is what kind of expression?
recs.facts: Each variable has power 1, so the degree of the expression is 1 and it is a linear expression.
recs.rel: The expression 8y - 6x + 7 is also linear.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'eventually'?
recs.facts: 'Eventually' means at last, after a long time or a series of events. 'Ultimately' carries the same sense.
recs.rel: Another synonym of 'eventually' is 'finally'.

recs.q: What are all the factors of 10?
recs.facts: The factors of a number are the numbers that divide it exactly. 10 divided by 1, 2, 5 and 10 leaves no remainder.
recs.rel: 10 has the prime factors 2 and 5.

recs.q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in 60 minutes, how far does the train cover in the same time?
recs.facts: The car's speed is 60 km in 1 hour = 60 km/h. The train moves at twice this speed, 120 km/h, so it covers 120 km in 60 minutes.
recs.rel: 60 minutes equal 1 hour.

recs.q: A train's speed is twice that of a car, and the train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How far does the car travel in 15 minutes?
recs.facts: The train's speed is 120 km/h, so the car's speed is 120 / 2 = 60 km/h. In 15 minutes (a quarter of an hour) the car covers 60 / 4 = 15 km.
recs.rel: 15 minutes are one quarter of an hour.

recs.q: Which is the fastest animal on earth?
recs.facts: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive, which is faster than any other animal. The cheetah is the fastest land animal at about 110 km/h.
recs.rel: The cheetah can keep its top speed only for short distances.

recs.q: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the wife of whom?
recs.facts: Hazrat Fatima (RA) married Hazrat Ali (RA) in 2 AH.
recs.rel: Their children were Hazrat Hasan, Hazrat Husain, Hazrat Zainab and Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

recs.q: Who made the first successful powered aeroplane flight in 1903?
recs.facts: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew the first powered, controlled aeroplane at Kitty Hawk, USA, on 17 December 1903.
recs.rel: The Montgolfier brothers made the first hot air balloon flight in 1783.

recs.q: What is the formula of the discriminant of the quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0?
recs.facts: The discriminant is D = b^2 - 4ac, the expression under the square root in the quadratic formula. It decides the nature of the roots.
recs.rel: If D is positive the roots are real and distinct, if D is zero they are equal, and if D is negative they are complex.

recs.q: What is the meaning of futility?
recs.facts: Futility is the quality of having no useful result, so it means pointlessness or uselessness.
recs.rel: The adjective form is futile.

recs.q: Which general imposed the NRO (National Reconciliation Ordinance) in Pakistan in 2007?
recs.facts: The National Reconciliation Ordinance was issued by President General Pervez Musharraf in October 2007. It gave amnesty in many corruption cases.
recs.rel: The Supreme Court of Pakistan declared the NRO unconstitutional in December 2009.

recs.q: A class has 1500 students and 1200 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
recs.facts: Girls = 1500 - 1200 = 300. Percentage = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20 percent.
recs.rel: Boys make up the other 80 percent of this class.

recs.q: What is the height of a standard football goal (inside the posts, from ground to crossbar)?
recs.facts: The crossbar of a standard football goal is 8 feet (2.44 m) above the ground.
recs.rel: The candidate answer of 24 inches is wrong; 24 feet is the width of the goal.

recs.q: Who is the current Governor of Sindh (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Nehal Hashmi of the PML-N took oath as Governor of Sindh on 13 March 2026.
recs.rel: He replaced Kamran Khan Tessori of the MQM-P, who was governor in 2022.

recs.q: Who said that the life of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the best example?
recs.facts: Allah says in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:21) that the Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for those who hope in Allah.
recs.rel: The Quran also describes the Prophet's character as of the highest standard in Surah Al-Qalam (68:4).

recs.q: Which is the greatest number among 5, 4, 6, 9, 7 and 3?
recs.facts: Comparing all the numbers, 9 is larger than 5, 4, 6, 7 and 3.
recs.rel: The smallest number in this list is 3.

recs.q: After the death of which caliph was the compiled copy of the Quran passed to Hazrat Hafsa (RA) for safekeeping?
recs.facts: The copy compiled under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed to Hazrat Umar (RA), and after his death it was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
recs.rel: Hazrat Uthman (RA) later borrowed this copy from Hafsa (RA) to prepare standard copies of the Quran.

recs.q: What is the HCF of 16 and 40?
recs.facts: 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 and 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5, so the common part is 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.
recs.rel: HCF is also called the greatest common divisor (GCD).

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Ali ____ himself against a horde of ruffians.
recs.facts: The idiom is to pit oneself against someone, meaning to compete or struggle against them. The past tense is pitted.
recs.rel: Pit against means to set one person or force in a contest with another.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (Causes of the Indian Revolt)?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it in 1859 to explain the causes of the War of Independence of 1857 and defend Muslims against blame.
recs.rel: It was originally written in Urdu and later translated into English.

recs.q: Who was Hinda (Hind bint Utba) who accepted Islam?
recs.facts: Hinda was the wife of Abu Sufyan and the mother of Hazrat Muawiyah (RA). She accepted Islam after the Conquest of Makkah.
recs.rel: She was also the one who had mutilated the body of Hazrat Hamza (RA) at Uhud before she embraced Islam.

recs.q: Which is the higher mountain range, the Hindu Kush or the Himalaya?
recs.facts: The Himalaya is higher: Mount Everest is 8,849 m while the Hindu Kush peak Tirich Mir is 7,708 m.
recs.rel: The Himalaya has more than a hundred peaks above 7,200 m.

recs.q: Which country hosted the first Asian Games in 1951?
recs.facts: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
recs.rel: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

recs.q: Which city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2012?
recs.facts: The 2012 Summer Olympics were held in London, United Kingdom.
recs.rel: London became the first city to host the modern Olympics three times (1908, 1948 and 2012).

recs.q: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
recs.facts: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
recs.rel: The ancient Olympics were also held in Greece, at Olympia.

recs.q: What are the real and imaginary parts of the complex number 4 + 9i?
recs.facts: In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part. So the real part is 4 and the imaginary part is 9.
recs.rel: The imaginary part is the real coefficient b, not bi.

recs.q: Who is generally credited as a co-founder of Twitter (now X) and its first chief executive?
recs.facts: Twitter was founded in 2006 by Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone and Evan Williams. Jack Dorsey is the best known and was its first CEO.
recs.rel: Twitter was renamed X in 2023 after it was bought by Elon Musk in 2022.

recs.q: What is the capital of Ireland?
recs.facts: Dublin is the capital and largest city of the Republic of Ireland. It lies on the east coast.
recs.rel: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, which is part of the United Kingdom.

recs.q: In which year did the USSR veto a UN Security Council resolution on Kashmir, supporting India?
recs.facts: On 22 June 1962 the Soviet Union vetoed a Security Council resolution on Kashmir backed by Pakistan. This was one of several Soviet vetoes on the issue.
recs.rel: The USSR had also used its veto on Kashmir in 1957.

recs.q: Where is Jabal Tariq (Mount of Tariq) located?
recs.facts: Jabal Tariq is the Arabic name from which the word Gibraltar comes. It is named after Tariq bin Ziyad, who landed there in 711 AD.
recs.rel: Tariq bin Ziyad began the Muslim conquest of Spain.

recs.q: Which Muslim community of Kerala (Malabar coast), India, is well known?
recs.facts: The Moplah (Mappila) are the Muslim community of the Malabar coast of Kerala, descended from Arab traders and local converts.
recs.rel: The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 took place in the Malabar region.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Khewra salt mine located?
recs.facts: The Khewra salt mine lies in the Salt Range near Khewra in Jhelum district, in northern Punjab.
recs.rel: Khewra is one of the largest and oldest salt mines in the world.

recs.q: Amir Khusro is regarded as the first poet of which language (in its early form)?
recs.facts: Amir Khusro (1253-1325) composed verse in Hindavi, the early form of Urdu, and is called its first poet.
recs.rel: Amir Khusro also wrote in Persian and was a disciple of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya.

recs.q: In which valley is Ansoo Lake located?
recs.facts: Ansoo (Lake Ansoo) is a tear-shaped high-altitude lake in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: Lake Saif-ul-Malook is also in the Kaghan Valley.

recs.q: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite launched into space, was launched in which year?
recs.facts: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957, which started the space age.
recs.rel: The first crewed spaceflight was Vostok 1 carrying Yuri Gagarin on 12 April 1961.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to lethal?
recs.facts: Lethal means capable of causing death, which is the same as deadly.
recs.rel: Lethal injection is a method of execution in some countries.

recs.q: Which is the last heavenly (divine) book?
recs.facts: The Holy Quran was revealed to the last Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and is the final divine book. No book will come after it.
recs.rel: The other heavenly books are the Torah, Zaboor and Injeel.

recs.q: In which unit is latitude measured?
recs.facts: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the Equator, so it is measured in degrees.
recs.rel: The Equator is 0 degrees latitude and the poles are 90 degrees north and south.

recs.q: How does the word MTVWVTM look when reflected in a mirror placed beside it (lateral reflection)?
recs.facts: The letters M, T, V and W are each symmetrical about a vertical line, and the word reads the same from both ends. So its mirror image is identical.
recs.rel: Letters such as A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X and Y are symmetrical about a vertical axis.

recs.q: Who discovered X-rays and developed the X-ray machine?
recs.facts: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 in Germany.
recs.rel: He received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for this discovery.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He lives ___ United States.
recs.facts: The preposition in is used with the name of a country or large place where someone lives.
recs.rel: The preposition at is used for specific points such as at home or at school.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan is the Mangla Dam located?
recs.facts: Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum River near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
recs.rel: Mangla is one of the largest dams in Pakistan and was completed in 1967.

recs.q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of marginal in the sense of minor or slight?
recs.facts: Marginal means small or of little importance. The opposite is significant, meaning large or important.
recs.rel: Marginal can also mean at the edge, and then its opposite is central.

recs.q: What is a Field Marshal?
opts: The highest rank in an army
A rank in the navy only
A police officer in charge of a district
recs.facts: Field Marshal is the highest (five-star) rank in the army of many countries. It is often given as an honour and is rarely awarded.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan became the first and only Field Marshal of Pakistan Army in 1959.

recs.q: What is the median of 36 and 18?
recs.facts: For two values the median is their average: (18 + 36) / 2 = 54 / 2 = 27.
recs.rel: For an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle values.

recs.q: Which prophet (AS) was granted the ability by Allah to mould (soften) iron?
recs.facts: The Quran says that Allah made iron soft for Hazrat Dawud (AS) so he could make armour (Surah Saba).
recs.rel: Hazrat Dawud (AS) was given the holy book Zabur.

recs.q: According to Greek mythology, who flew too close to the sun with wings of wax and fell into the sea?
recs.facts: Icarus ignored his father's warning, flew too close to the sun, the wax melted and he fell.
recs.rel: His father Daedalus built the wings and the labyrinth of Crete.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 12, 55, 14, 65, 16, 75, ?
recs.facts: There are two interleaved series: 12, 14, 16 (add 2) and 55, 65, 75 (add 10). The term after 75 belongs to the first series, so it is 16 + 2 = 18.
recs.rel: The next term after 18 would be 85.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 55, 65, 75, ?
recs.facts: Each number increases by 10, so 75 + 10 = 85.
recs.rel: This is an arithmetic progression with common difference 10.

recs.q: On whom is Hajj obligatory (farz)?
opts: Every sane, adult Muslim who has the means to travel and afford it
recs.facts: Hajj is farz once in a lifetime on a sane, adult (baligh) Muslim who is physically and financially able (istita'at) to make the journey.
recs.rel: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam.

recs.q: Which of the following is a farz (obligatory act) of Hajj?
recs.facts: The faraiz of Hajj in the Hanafi school are Ihram, Wuquf-e-Arafah and Tawaf-e-Ziyarah. Stoning and shaving are wajib, not farz.
recs.rel: Missing Wuquf-e-Arafah invalidates the Hajj.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of pacify?
recs.facts: To pacify means to bring peace or to calm someone down. Calm has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Appease and soothe are other synonyms of pacify.

recs.q: In which year was the second constitution of Pakistan enforced?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first constitution came in 1956 and was abrogated in 1958. The second constitution, given by Ayub Khan, was enforced in 1962.
recs.rel: The third constitution of 1973 is still in force today with amendments.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 10 percent of 12?
recs.facts: 10 percent of 12 = 1.2. A quarter of 1.2 = 0.3.
recs.rel: A quarter means dividing by 4.

recs.q: Which of the following lists the five pillars of Islam correctly?
recs.facts: The five pillars are the declaration of faith (Kalima/Shahada), prayer (Salah), fasting (Sawm), charity (Zakat) and pilgrimage (Hajj).
recs.rel: In the order taught in Pakistan the pillars are Kalima, Salah, Roza, Zakat and Hajj.

recs.q: Convert to passive voice: The pilot landed the plane safely.
opts: The plane is landed safely by the pilot.
The plane was landed safely by the pilot.
The plane had landed safely by the pilot.
The plane was landing safely by the pilot.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was or were plus the past participle. The object plane becomes the subject: The plane was landed safely by the pilot.
recs.rel: Passive voice formula for simple past: object + was/were + third form of verb + by + subject.

recs.q: Where were the first Asian Games held in 1951?
recs.facts: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
recs.rel: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

recs.q: Sadequain, a famous name in Pakistani art, is known as a
recs.facts: Sadequain (1930-1987) was a renowned Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known especially for his calligraphy of Quranic verses and verses of Allama Iqbal and Ghalib.
recs.rel: He also painted murals, including the ceiling of the Frere Hall in Karachi.

recs.q: What is the approximate population of the Philippines in 2026?
recs.facts: Current estimates put the population of the Philippines at about 118 million in 2026, which ranks it around 14th in the world.
recs.rel: The 2020 census of the Philippines counted about 109 million people.

recs.q: How many Nobel Prizes has Pakistan won?
recs.facts: Pakistan has two Nobel laureates: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
recs.rel: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate in history.

recs.q: In which year was the One Unit scheme established in West Pakistan?
recs.facts: The provinces of West Pakistan were merged into one unit in 1955.
recs.rel: One Unit was dissolved by Yahya Khan in 1970.

recs.q: Past is to present as preceding is to:
recs.facts: Past and present are opposites, and the opposite of preceding is following.
recs.rel: Preceding means coming before.

recs.q: Who is the chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) as of 2026?
recs.facts: Barrister Gohar Ali Khan was elected PTI chairman unopposed in December 2023 as a temporary arrangement. He is still reported as chairman in 2026.
recs.rel: Imran Khan was chairman before 2023 and the party's founder; his camp still calls him the real chairman.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 1/20?
recs.rel: Multiplying two fractions means multiplying numerators together and denominators together.

recs.q: Overexposure to ultraviolet rays from the sun is most harmful to which part of the human body?
recs.facts: Ultraviolet rays damage skin cells and the eyes, causing sunburn, skin cancer and cataracts.
recs.rel: The ozone layer in the atmosphere absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

recs.q: Which city or territory of Pakistan has the highest literacy rate according to the 2023 census?
recs.facts: The 2023 census showed Islamabad Capital Territory with the highest literacy rate, about 84 percent, ahead of all provinces.
recs.rel: The national literacy rate was about 60.7 percent for people aged 10 and above.

recs.q: Which is the largest religion in the world by number of followers?
recs.facts: Christianity has about 2.4 billion followers, more than any other religion.
recs.rel: Islam is the second largest religion and is the fastest growing.

recs.q: What was the Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940?
opts: A demand for separate independent states for the Muslims of India
A demand for a united India
A plan to boycott the elections of 1946
recs.facts: At the Lahore session of the All-India Muslim League, the resolution demanded that Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped into independent states.
recs.rel: It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and later called the Pakistan Resolution.

recs.q: What is the cube root of 8?
recs.facts: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8, so the cube root of 8 is 2.
recs.rel: The cube root of 27 is 3 and the cube root of 64 is 4.

recs.q: What is the cube root of 92, approximately?
recs.facts: 4 cubed is 64 and 5 cubed is 125, so the cube root of 92 lies between 4 and 5. Since 4.5 cubed is 91.1, the value is about 4.5.
recs.rel: A perfect cube close to 92 is 91.125, which is 4.5 cubed.

recs.q: For how many years did Hazrat Usman (RA) rule as Caliph?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA) was Caliph from 23 AH to 35 AH, which is about 12 years.
recs.rel: He was the third Caliph and his rule was the longest among the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.

recs.q: What is the presiding officer who runs the sessions of the National Assembly of Pakistan called?
recs.facts: The National Assembly is presided over and run by its Speaker, who is elected by its members. In his absence the Deputy Speaker presides.
recs.rel: The Senate, by contrast, is presided over by the Chairman.

recs.q: Famous footballer Mohamed Salah belongs to which country?
recs.facts: Mohamed Salah was born in Nagrig, Egypt, and captains the Egyptian national team.
recs.rel: He is best known for his years at Liverpool in the English Premier League.

recs.q: Which is the busiest seaport in the world (by container traffic)?
recs.facts: Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port for 16 years in a row, handling about 55 million TEU in 2025. Singapore is second.
recs.rel: Ningbo-Zhoushan is the busiest port by total cargo tonnage.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word security?
recs.facts: Security means the state of being protected from danger, which is safety.
recs.rel: Another close word is protection.

recs.q: For how many terms can the Secretary-General of the United Nations normally serve?
opts: Two terms of five years each
Three terms of four years each
recs.facts: The UN Charter sets no limit, but by established practice the Secretary-General serves a five-year term that can be renewed once, so two terms.
recs.rel: The General Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on the recommendation of the Security Council.

recs.q: Who started the Pan-Islamism movement in the Muslim world?
recs.facts: Syed Jamaluddin Afghani called for the unity of all Muslims against European domination and is regarded as the founder of the Pan-Islamic movement.
recs.rel: In the subcontinent the Khilafat Movement was also influenced by Pan-Islamic ideas.

recs.q: In which year was the Simla Conference between the British, the Congress and the Muslim League held?
recs.facts: The Simla Conference was convened by Viceroy Lord Wavell in 1945 to discuss the Wavell Plan for an interim government.
recs.rel: The conference failed mainly because Congress refused to accept that the Muslim League alone represented the Muslims.

recs.q: On which date was the Simla Conference of 1945 held (it began on this date)?
recs.facts: Lord Wavell opened the Simla Conference on 25 June 1945 and it ended on 14 July 1945 without agreement.
