recs.rel: The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India of 1972 is a different event.

recs.q: On which date was the Simla (Shimla) Agreement between Pakistan and India signed?
recs.facts: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.
recs.rel: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 after the 1965 war.

recs.q: If one side of a square is 6 cm, what is its perimeter?
recs.facts: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side = 4 x 6 = 24 cm.
recs.rel: The area of this square would be 36 square cm.

recs.q: What is the value of sin 190 degrees?
recs.facts: 190 degrees lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, so sin 190 = -sin 10 = -0.174.
recs.rel: The candidate answer 0.997 is not correct for degrees.

recs.q: Who is the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan as of 2026?
recs.facts: Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has been Chief of Army Staff since November 2022 and was also named Chief of Defence Forces in December 2025.
recs.rel: General Qamar Javed Bajwa was the previous army chief from 2016 to 2022.

recs.q: What does WHO stand for?
recs.facts: WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency for international public health.
recs.rel: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word sublime?
recs.facts: Sublime means of very high excellence or grandeur, so majestic is closest.
recs.rel: Its antonym is a word like ordinary or lowly.

recs.q: Which vitamin do we get from sunlight?
recs.facts: Sunlight on the skin helps the body make vitamin D.
recs.rel: Lack of vitamin D causes rickets in children.

recs.q: What is the synonym of stagnant?
recs.facts: Stagnant describes water or conditions that are still and not moving or developing.
recs.rel: Stagnate is the verb form, meaning to become inactive or still.

recs.q: What is the synonym of might?
recs.facts: As a noun, might means great strength or power.
recs.rel: Might is also a modal verb expressing possibility, but the noun sense is meant here.

recs.q: What is the synonym of synopsis?
recs.facts: A synopsis is a brief summary of a book, film or plot.
recs.rel: An abstract is a synopsis of a research paper.

recs.q: In which Hijri month and year did the Ghazwa of Tabuk take place?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) marched towards Tabuk in Rajab of 9 AH, which is about October 630 CE.
recs.rel: It is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the Expedition of Hardship.

recs.q: Who is the current T20I captain of the Pakistan cricket team (October 2026)?
recs.facts: Pakistan named Sahibzada Farhan T20I captain in October 2026, ahead of the home series against Sri Lanka.
recs.rel: Salman Ali Agha led the side from March 2025 until this change, and Shaheen Shah Afridi remains ODI captain.

recs.q: Which bowler of the Pakistan women's team became the first Pakistani player to take 100 wickets in T20 internationals?
recs.facts: Nida Dar became the first Pakistan player, male or female, to reach 100 T20I wickets in July 2021.
recs.rel: Sana Mir took over 150 ODI wickets, and Dar has since passed 140 T20I wickets.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Thar desert mainly located?
recs.facts: The Pakistani part of the Thar desert lies in the south-east of Sindh, mainly in Tharparkar district.
recs.rel: The Thar desert extends into the Indian state of Rajasthan and is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

recs.q: What is the order of the transpose of a matrix of order m x n?
recs.facts: The transpose is obtained by interchanging rows and columns, so an m x n matrix becomes n x m.
recs.rel: The transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives back the original matrix.

recs.q: Who conquered Sindh during the Umayyad period?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD under the Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf and Caliph Walid I.
recs.rel: Raja Dahir was the ruler of Sindh at the time.

recs.q: In set theory, the universal set is what of every set under consideration?
recs.facts: The universal set contains all the elements of the sets under discussion, so every set is a subset of it and it is a superset of each.
recs.rel: The universal set is usually denoted by U.

recs.q: What is the complement of the universal set?
recs.facts: The complement of U contains the elements not in U, and there are none, so it is the empty set.
recs.rel: Likewise the complement of the empty set is the universal set.

recs.q: What is the approximate value of pi?
recs.facts: Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, approximately 3.14159. It is commonly written as 3.14 or 22/7.
recs.rel: Pi is an irrational number, so its decimal expansion never ends or repeats.

recs.q: Vehicle is to tyres as sound is to ___ ?
recs.facts: A vehicle has tyres as a part, and sound is made up of or travels as waves. The analogy links a thing with its essential component.
recs.rel: Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves that need a medium.

recs.q: Which animal uses sound waves (echolocation) to find its way, like eyes?
recs.facts: Bats emit high-frequency ultrasonic sounds and use the returning echoes to locate objects and prey in the dark. This is called echolocation.
recs.rel: Dolphins also use echolocation, and humans copy the idea in sonar.

recs.q: What does the white band in the flag of Pakistan represent?
recs.facts: The white stripe of the flag stands for the religious minorities of Pakistan, while the green stands for the Muslim majority.
recs.rel: The crescent in the flag represents progress and the star represents light and knowledge.

recs.q: How many wives did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have at the time of his death, according to the commonly taught account?
recs.facts: At the time of his death the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had 9 wives living. In total he married 11 wives; Hazrat Khadija (RA) and Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaima (RA) had died before him.
recs.rel: The wives of the Prophet (PBUH) are called Ummahat-ul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers).

recs.q: In the sentence 'Wow! This is my book', what part of speech is 'Wow'?
recs.facts: 'Wow' expresses a sudden feeling of surprise, and a word that does this is an interjection.
recs.rel: An interjection is usually followed by an exclamation mark.

recs.q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
recs.facts: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, although Auckland is its largest city.
recs.rel: New Zealand has no president; its head of state is the British monarch.

recs.q: What is (3 + i)(3 - i)?
recs.rel: The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 20?
recs.facts: One third of 20 is 20 divided by 3, which is 20/3 or about 6.67.
recs.rel: A mixed form of 20/3 is 6 and 2/3.

recs.q: What is 2 + 1/3?
recs.rel: 7/3 is an improper fraction.

recs.q: What is 1/10 of 1/5 of 120?
recs.rel: Taking 1/10 of a number just moves the decimal point one place to the left.

recs.q: What is one third of 25% of 120?
recs.facts: 25% of 120 = 30. One third of 30 = 10.
recs.rel: 25% is the same as one quarter.

recs.q: What is 125% of 25?
If the 13th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 27th day of that month be?
recs.facts: From the 13th to the 27th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the day is the same, Sunday.
recs.rel: A gap of 7, 14, 21 or 28 days always gives the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 23rd of a month falls on Friday, what day will the 14th of that month be?
recs.facts: From the 14th to the 23rd is 9 days. 9 = 7 + 2, so the 14th is 2 days before Friday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: When going backward, subtract the extra days after removing full weeks.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 14th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 14th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. The 14th is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Remove full weeks first, then count the remaining days.

recs.q: If the 29th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 15th be?
recs.facts: From the 15th to the 29th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both are Monday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 14 days apart fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 15th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Friday, which gives Thursday.
recs.rel: Thirteen days ahead is the same as one day behind.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 17th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Monday, which is Sunday.
recs.rel: Six days ahead equals one day behind, so Monday becomes Sunday.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 17th of the month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 17th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 17th is 2 days after Monday, which is Wednesday.
recs.rel: The 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th of a month always share the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 17th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Sunday, which is Saturday.
recs.rel: Six days ahead equals one day behind, so Sunday becomes Saturday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 18th of the month be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 18th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 18th is 2 days after Friday, which is Sunday.
recs.rel: Subtract full weeks (multiples of 7) and count only the remainder.

recs.q: What is one tenth of 10% of 140?
recs.facts: 10% of 140 = 14. One tenth of 14 = 1.4.
recs.rel: 10% and one tenth are the same value, so this is 140 x 0.1 x 0.1 = 1.4.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 1340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
recs.facts: Absent students = 1500 - 1340 = 160. Percentage = 160 / 1500 x 100 = 10.67%.
recs.rel: The percentage of present students here is 89.33%.

recs.q: Out of 2000 students, 1600 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.rel: The percentage of present students is 80%.

recs.q: The population of a city was 1600 in 1960 and it doubles every year. What will the population be in 1967?
recs.facts: From 1960 to 1967 is 7 years, so the population doubles 7 times: 1600 x 2^7 = 1600 x 128 = 204800.
recs.rel: 2^7 = 128 and 2^10 = 1024 are useful powers of two to remember.

recs.q: A car runs at a speed of 180 km/h. How much distance does it travel in 20 minutes?
recs.facts: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 180 x 1/3 = 60 km.
recs.rel: To convert km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18, so 180 km/h is 50 m/s.

recs.q: According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be elected President?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim and at least 35 years old.
recs.rel: Under the 1973 Constitution the minimum age for President is 45 years, and the 1956 Constitution required 40 years.

recs.q: Ali was born in 1974 and Azhar was born in 1970. Bilal is 2 years younger than Azhar. In which year was Bilal born?
recs.facts: Younger by 2 years means born 2 years later, so Bilal was born in 1970 + 2 = 1972.
recs.rel: Born later means younger; born earlier means older.

recs.q: What position did Pakistan achieve in the 1999 Cricket World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan reached the final of the 1999 World Cup in England but lost to Australia at Lord's.
recs.rel: Pakistan won the World Cup once, in 1992.

recs.q: Akbar was born in 1970 and Ammar in 1977. Bilal is older than Ammar. Who is the youngest of the three?
recs.facts: Bilal is older than Ammar, so Ammar is younger than Bilal. Ammar (1977) is also younger than Akbar (1970), so Ammar is the youngest.
recs.rel: A later birth year means a younger person.

recs.q: What is 2% of 200?
recs.rel: 1% of 200 is 2, so 2% is double that.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 21st be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 21st is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 8th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
recs.facts: From the 8th to the 21st is 13 days. 13 = 1 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Tuesday to reach Monday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 23rd be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 23rd is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Monday to reach Sunday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 24th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 24th be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Sunday to reach Tuesday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 25th be?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Sunday to reach Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 7th day of a month is Saturday, what day will the 26th be?
recs.facts: From the 7th to the 26th is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Saturday to reach Thursday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 27th is 26 days. 26 = 3 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 7th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
recs.facts: From the 7th to the 25th is 18 days. 18 = 2 weeks and 4 extra days, so count 4 days forward from Sunday to reach Thursday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: If the 7th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th be?
recs.facts: From the 7th to the 12th is 5 days. 5 = 0 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.
recs.rel: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

recs.q: The 24th of a month is Friday. What day is the 2nd of the same month?
recs.facts: The 2nd is 22 days before the 24th. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra day, so it is one day before Friday, which is Thursday.
recs.rel: Going back exactly 7 days always gives the same weekday.

recs.q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2016?
recs.facts: According to UNHCR figures for 2016, Turkey hosted about 2.9 million refugees, mostly Syrians, which was the largest number in the world.
recs.rel: Pakistan was the second largest host in 2016 with about 1.4 million refugees, mostly Afghans.

recs.q: Which country hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
recs.facts: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Indonesia, in the cities of Jakarta and Palembang.
recs.rel: The 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023, were hosted by Hangzhou in China.

recs.q: On which date did the 2018 Asian Games begin?
recs.facts: The 18th Asian Games opened in Jakarta on 18 August 2018 and ended on 2 September 2018.
recs.rel: Indonesia's Jakarta and Palembang shared hosting of that edition.

recs.q: Where were the 2018 Winter Olympic Games held?
recs.facts: The 2018 Winter Olympics took place in Pyeongchang, South Korea, in February 2018.
recs.rel: The 2018 Summer Olympics did not exist: the Summer Games were held in Rio in 2016 and Tokyo in 2021.

recs.q: Which country hosted the 2018 Asia Cup cricket tournament?
recs.facts: The 2018 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, in September 2018.
recs.rel: India won the 2018 Asia Cup by beating Bangladesh in the final.

recs.q: What is the value of the percentage of absent students if 300 out of 500 students are present?
recs.facts: Absent students = 500 - 300 = 200. Percentage absent = 200 / 500 x 100 = 40%.
recs.rel: Percentage present plus percentage absent always equals 100%.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 300 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.rel: The percentage present here is 20%.

recs.q: There are 1500 students in a class, 1200 are boys and 300 are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
recs.facts: Percentage of girls = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20%.
recs.rel: Boys make up the remaining 80%.

recs.q: Out of 1200 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students, to two decimal places?
recs.rel: The percentage present is 340 / 1200 x 100 = 28.33%.

recs.q: A helicopter flies at 340 km/h. About how much time does it take to cover 700 km?
recs.facts: Time = distance / speed = 700 / 340 = 2.06 hours, which is about 2 hours 4 minutes.
recs.rel: Speed = distance / time is the basic formula behind such questions.

recs.q: In a class of 500 students, 360 are present. How many students are absent?
recs.facts: Absent students = 500 - 360 = 140.
recs.rel: As a percentage, 140 out of 500 is 28%.

recs.q: A plane uses 80 gallons of fuel to cover 320 miles. How many gallons will 800 miles need?
recs.facts: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 miles: 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.
recs.rel: The same method works with kilometres and litres.

recs.q: A car travels at 78 km/h. How far will it travel in 12 minutes?
recs.facts: 12 minutes = 12 / 60 = 0.2 hour. Distance = 78 x 0.2 = 15.6 km.
recs.rel: To change minutes into hours, divide by 60.

recs.q: How many elements are there in each row of a matrix of order 4x3?
recs.facts: A matrix of order 4x3 has 4 rows and 3 columns, so each row has 3 elements.
recs.rel: The total number of elements in a 4x3 matrix is 12.

recs.q: A matrix is of order 4x3. How many rows does it have?
recs.facts: The order of a matrix is written as rows x columns, so a 4x3 matrix has 4 rows.
recs.rel: It has 3 columns.

recs.q: In which year was the first martial law in Pakistan lifted?
recs.facts: General Ayub Khan imposed martial law in October 1958 and it was lifted on 8 June 1962 when the new constitution came into force.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution gave Pakistan a presidential system with Ayub Khan as President.

recs.q: Which word is the antonym of abrogate?
recs.facts: To abrogate means to repeal or do away with a law. Its opposite is to enact or establish a law.
recs.rel: Repeal, annul and revoke are synonyms of abrogate.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of abrogate?
recs.facts: To abrogate means to formally cancel or repeal a law or agreement, so repeal has the same meaning.
recs.rel: The word comes from the Latin abrogare, meaning to repeal a law.

recs.q: On which date was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law on 25 March 1969 after Ayub Khan resigned, and the 1962 Constitution was abrogated.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan resigned on 25 March 1969 and handed power to the army chief Yahya Khan.

recs.q: On which date was the first Constitution of Pakistan (1956) adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
recs.facts: The Constituent Assembly adopted the 1956 Constitution on 29 February 1956.
recs.rel: It came into force on 23 March 1956, which is why that day was celebrated as Republic Day.

recs.q: What is the title of Imam Abu Hanifa's well-known book on beliefs?
recs.facts: Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is the creed work traditionally attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa.
recs.rel: Al-Muwatta is by Imam Malik and Kitab-ul-Umm is by Imam Shafi'i; some scholars debate how much of Fiqh-e-Akbar is by Abu Hanifa himself.

recs.q: What is the commutative property of addition?
opts: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
recs.facts: The commutative property says that changing the order of the numbers being added does not change the sum, so a + b = b + a.
recs.rel: Addition and multiplication are commutative, but subtraction and division are not.

recs.q: Who was the first black President of South Africa?
recs.facts: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first black President in May 1994 after the first fully democratic elections.
recs.rel: He spent 27 years in prison and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 jointly with F. W. de Klerk.

recs.q: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya (1870) in reply to which book?
opts: A Life of Mahomet by William Muir
recs.facts: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya was written to answer the objections raised against the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in William Muir's book A Life of Mahomet. Sir Syed wrote it after visiting England in 1869.
recs.rel: Sir Syed's own book on the 1857 war was Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya?
recs.facts: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya is a work in defence of Islam written by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. It was published in 1870.
recs.rel: Sir Syed founded the Aligarh Muslim (MAO) College in 1875.

recs.q: Ahmed is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ahmed is 14 years old, what will be his sister's age?
recs.facts: Sister's age now is 6 x 3 = 18 years, so she is 12 years older than Ahmed. When Ahmed is 14, she is 14 + 12 = 26.
recs.rel: In age problems the difference in ages stays fixed while both ages increase equally.

recs.q: On which date did Allama Muhammad Iqbal die?
recs.facts: Allama Iqbal died in Lahore on 21 April 1938. He is buried near the Badshahi Mosque.
recs.rel: Iqbal's birth date is 9 November 1877 in Sialkot, which is observed as Iqbal Day.

recs.q: Complete the analogy: Sailor is to Navy as Airman is to ____.
recs.facts: A sailor serves in the Navy, in the same way an airman serves in the Air Force.
recs.rel: Soldier, sailor and airman are the ranks-and-file terms for the Army, Navy and Air Force.

recs.q: How many sons did Hazrat Aisha (RA) have?
recs.facts: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), had no children. She is called Ummul Momineen.
recs.rel: She was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and is known for narrating many hadiths.

recs.q: On which date was the Jammu and Kashmir State Subject Rule issued?
recs.facts: The State Subject Rule defining who was a permanent resident of Jammu and Kashmir was issued by Maharaja Hari Singh on 20 April 1927. It limited land ownership and state jobs to state subjects.
recs.rel: Maharaja Hari Singh ruled Jammu and Kashmir from 1925 to 1947.

recs.q: If Ahmad is older than Akbar and Akbar is older than Ali, then Ali is ____.
recs.facts: The order of age is Ahmad, then Akbar, then Ali, so Ali is the youngest. Therefore Ali is younger than Ahmad (and Akbar).
recs.rel: Such statements can be solved by writing the names in order from oldest to youngest.

recs.q: Is 5x - 4y + 6 = 0 an algebraic expression or an equation?
recs.facts: It has an equals sign with an expression on each side (the right side is 0), so it is an equation. It is a linear equation in two variables.
recs.rel: An algebraic expression, such as 5x - 4y + 6, has no equals sign.

recs.q: The product of two algebraic expressions is ____ the product of their LCM and HCF.
recs.facts: For any two expressions (or numbers) f and g, f x g = LCM x HCF. So the product is equal to the product of LCM and HCF.
recs.rel: For numbers, 12 x 18 = 216 and LCM 36 x HCF 6 = 216.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: X3, Y2, Z?
recs.facts: The letters move forward X, Y, Z while the numbers go down 3, 2, 1. So the next term is Z1.
recs.rel: Letter-number series usually move the letters and numbers by fixed steps.

recs.q: If the letters of the word ARGUMENT are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter is third?
recs.facts: The letters of ARGUMENT in alphabetical order are A, E, G, M, N, R, T, U. The third letter is G.
recs.rel: ARGUMENT has 8 letters and 3 vowels: A, U and E.

recs.q: By what other name is Pakistan Day, observed on 23 March, also known?
recs.facts: Pakistan Day commemorates the Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) passed on 23 March 1940, so it is also called Resolution Day. It also marks the adoption of the first constitution in 1956.
recs.rel: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.

recs.q: Who is the angel of death (Malak-ul-Maut) in Islamic belief?
recs.facts: Hazrat Izrail (AS) is the angel entrusted with taking souls at death. The Quran refers to him as the angel of death in Surah As-Sajdah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel who will blow the trumpet on the Day of Judgement.

recs.q: Two adjacent angles which together form a right angle are called what?
recs.facts: Two angles whose sum is 90 degrees are complementary. Together they make one right angle.
recs.rel: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, which is a straight line.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word abolish?
recs.facts: To abolish is to put an end to something officially. Its opposite is to establish, meaning to set up.
recs.rel: Abolish, cancel, remove and end are all close in meaning to each other.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word accumulated?
recs.facts: Accumulated means gathered together over time. The opposite is dispersed, meaning scattered.
recs.rel: Accumulate is a synonym of amass and collect.

recs.q: Find the missing number in the analogy 2 : X :: 4 : 16.
recs.facts: Since 4 : 16 shows that 16 is the square of 4 (4 x 4 = 16), the same rule applies to 2, so X = 2 x 2 = 4.
recs.rel: Square numbers are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and so on.

recs.q: Anemia is mainly caused by the deficiency of which element?
recs.facts: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells. Without enough iron the blood cannot carry enough oxygen, which causes anemia.
recs.rel: Iodine deficiency causes goitre.

recs.q: Area of a parallelogram = base x ______.
recs.facts: The area of a parallelogram is its base multiplied by its perpendicular height, also called its altitude.
recs.rel: The area of a triangle is half of base times altitude.

recs.q: What is the antonym of despite?
recs.facts: Despite means in spite of something; the opposite idea is because of, which gives a cause.
recs.rel: Despite, in spite of and notwithstanding all mean the same thing.

recs.q: What is the antonym of eliminated?
recs.facts: Eliminated means removed or left out; the opposite is included or retained.
recs.rel: Eliminate comes from the Latin eliminare, meaning to drive out of doors.

recs.q: What is the antonym of evidently?
recs.facts: Evidently means in a clear and obvious way; the opposite is obscurely, meaning in an unclear way.
recs.rel: Evidently, obviously and clearly are synonyms of each other.

recs.q: What is the antonym of foe?
recs.facts: A foe is an enemy; the opposite is a friend.
recs.rel: Foe and enemy are synonyms, as are ally and friend.

recs.q: What is the antonym of improvement?
recs.facts: Improvement means becoming better; the opposite is deterioration, meaning becoming worse.
recs.rel: Progress and betterment are synonyms of improvement.

recs.q: What is the antonym of impudent?
recs.facts: Impudent means rude and disrespectful; the opposite is respectful or polite.
recs.rel: Impudent, insolent and cheeky are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of multitude?
recs.facts: A multitude is a very large number of people or things; the opposite is a handful, a very small number.
recs.rel: Multitude, crowd and throng are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of nourishment?
recs.facts: Nourishment is the food needed for life and growth; the opposite is starvation, the lack of food.
recs.rel: Nutrition and sustenance are synonyms of nourishment.

recs.q: What is the antonym of pragmatic?
recs.facts: Pragmatic means dealing with things in a practical way; the opposite is idealistic, based on ideals rather than reality.
recs.rel: Pragmatic, practical and realistic are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of purification?
recs.facts: Purification means making something clean; the opposite is contamination, making it impure.
recs.rel: Pollution is another antonym of purification.

recs.q: What is the antonym of recalcitrant?
recs.facts: Recalcitrant means stubbornly resisting authority; the opposite is obedient or compliant.
recs.rel: Candidates remembered willing or ready, which are also close in meaning to obedient.

recs.q: What is the antonym of refuse?
recs.facts: To refuse is to say no to something offered; the opposite is to accept.
recs.rel: Refuse as a noun means rubbish, but in this question it is the verb.

recs.q: What is the antonym of shameful?
recs.facts: Shameful means causing shame; the opposite is honourable, deserving respect.
recs.rel: Shameful, disgraceful and scandalous are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of strict?
recs.facts: Strict means demanding obedience to rules; the opposite is lenient, meaning easy-going or merciful.
recs.rel: Strict, stern and rigid are synonyms.

recs.q: What is the antonym of underhand?
recs.facts: Underhand means done in a secret or dishonest way; the opposite is honest or open.
recs.rel: Aboveboard is the usual one-word opposite of underhand.

recs.q: What is the antonym of virtue?
recs.facts: Virtue means moral goodness; the opposite is vice, meaning immoral behaviour.
recs.rel: The pair virtue and vice is a classic antonym pair.

recs.q: What is the supreme law (apex law) of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, adopted in 1973, is the supreme law of the country and all other laws must conform to it.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and has 280 Articles.

recs.q: What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 26?
recs.rel: The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly halfway between them.

recs.q: What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 36?
recs.rel: The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by how many there are.

recs.q: What is the arithmetic mean of 8 and 36?
recs.rel: The geometric mean of 8 and 36 is different: it is the square root of 288, about 16.97.

recs.q: Who were the Ashra-e-Mubashara?
opts: Ten Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) given the glad tidings of Paradise in one lifetime
The ten wives of the Prophet (PBUH)
Ten Muslim commanders of the Battle of Badr
recs.facts: The Ashra-e-Mubashara are ten Companions whom the Prophet (PBUH) named as people of Paradise while they were alive. They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.
recs.rel: Their names are listed in a famous hadith narrated by Abdur Rahman bin Awf and Sa'id bin Zaid.

recs.q: When did the USA drop atom bombs on Japan?
recs.facts: The USA dropped the atom bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
recs.rel: Japan announced its surrender soon afterwards, ending the Second World War.

recs.q: What is the national game of Australia, as commonly stated?
recs.facts: Cricket is commonly given as the national game of Australia. It is the most popular summer sport there.
recs.rel: Australia has no officially declared national game, so sources differ; Australian rules football is also very popular.

recs.q: After the Quran, what is the most authentic source of Islamic teachings?
recs.facts: The Hadith and Sunnah, the sayings and actions of the Prophet (PBUH), explain and complete the Quran. They are the second source of Islamic law.
recs.rel: Ijma and Qiyas are usually counted as the third and fourth sources.

recs.q: What is the average of 23 and 32?
recs.facts: Add the numbers: 23 + 32 = 55. Divide by 2: 55 / 2 = 27.5.
recs.rel: Average equals the sum of values divided by the number of values.

recs.q: What is the average of 28 and 36?
recs.facts: Add the numbers: 28 + 36 = 64. Divide by 2: 64 / 2 = 32.
recs.rel: The average of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.

recs.q: What is the average of 32 and 20?
recs.facts: Add the numbers: 32 + 20 = 52. Divide by 2: 52 / 2 = 26.
recs.rel: Average is also called the arithmetic mean.

recs.q: What is the y-axis also called in the coordinate plane?
recs.facts: The vertical y-axis is called the ordinate axis and the y-coordinate is the ordinate. The horizontal x-axis is the abscissa axis.
recs.rel: The point where both axes meet is called the origin.

recs.q: How many times is the name of Hazrat Ayesha (RA) mentioned in the Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran does not mention Hazrat Ayesha (RA) by name. She is referred to indirectly in some verses about the Prophet's household.
recs.rel: The Prophet's wives are addressed as the Mothers of the Believers in Surah Al-Ahzab.

recs.q: In which Surah was the incident of slander (Ifk) against Hazrat Ayesha (RA) addressed and her innocence declared?
recs.facts: Verses 11 to 20 of Surah An-Nur declare Hazrat Ayesha (RA) innocent of the false accusation. This is known as the incident of Ifk.
recs.rel: The incident took place after the expedition of Banu Mustaliq.

recs.q: According to the 14 Points of Quaid-e-Azam, what form of government should India have?
opts: A federation with residuary powers vested in the provinces
A unitary system with a strong centre
recs.facts: The 14 Points demanded that the future constitution of India be federal. The residuary powers were to remain with the provinces.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam presented the 14 Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

recs.q: Muslim Bagh in Balochistan is famous for which mineral?
recs.facts: Muslim Bagh in Zhob district of Balochistan is known for its chromite (chromium ore) deposits. Chromite is mined there on a large scale.
recs.rel: Chamalang in Balochistan is known for coal and Saindak for copper and gold.

recs.q: On which date was the Baghdad Pact first signed between Turkey and Iraq?
recs.facts: Turkey and Iraq signed the Baghdad Pact in Baghdad on 24 February 1955. Britain, Pakistan and Iran joined later in 1955.
recs.rel: After Iraq left in 1959 the pact was renamed CENTO.

recs.q: Who founded the city of Baghdad?
recs.facts: The Abbasid caliph Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 AD. He made it his capital and named it the City of Peace.
recs.rel: Baghdad reached its golden age under Haroon-ur-Rasheed and Mamun-ur-Rasheed.

recs.q: What is the approximate area of Balochistan province?
recs.facts: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square km, which is about 44 percent of Pakistan. It is the largest province by area.
recs.rel: Punjab covers about 205,344 square km and Sindh about 140,914 square km.

recs.q: Which was the first commercial bank of Pakistan, as commonly stated?
recs.facts: Habib Bank Limited (HBL), founded in 1941 and moved to Karachi after 1947, is generally called the first commercial bank of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sources differ somewhat, but most Pakistani textbooks name Habib Bank.

recs.q: In which city is the head office of the State Bank of Pakistan located?
recs.facts: The State Bank of Pakistan has its head office on I.I. Chundrigar Road in Karachi. It began operations on 1 July 1948.
recs.rel: The State Bank has a main branch in Islamabad too.

recs.q: Who were the Banu Quraysh?
opts: The ruling tribe of Makkah to which the Prophet (PBUH) belonged
recs.facts: Quraysh (Quraish) was the leading tribe of Makkah and the custodian of the Kaaba. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to its clan Banu Hashim.
recs.rel: Banu Quraiza, Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were Jewish tribes of Madina.

recs.q: By what other name is the Sukkur Barrage known?
recs.facts: The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus was opened in 1932 and named the Lloyd Barrage after the Governor of Bombay, Sir George Lloyd.
recs.rel: It irrigates millions of acres in Sindh through seven canals.

recs.q: The area of a triangle is 24 square cm and its base is 4 cm. What is its height?
recs.facts: Area = (1/2) x base x height, so 24 = (1/2) x 4 x h = 2h. Therefore h = 12 cm.
recs.rel: The height of a triangle is the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex.

recs.q: Akbar is 3 times as old as his sister. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 15 years old?
recs.facts: Akbar's age is 3 times his sister's age, so sister = 15 divided by 3 = 5 years.
recs.rel: In ratio questions, divide the larger age by the multiple to get the smaller age.

recs.q: Ali's sister is 3 times as old as Ali. How old will Ali's sister be when Ali becomes 14 years old?
recs.facts: Sister's age = 3 times Ali's age = 3 x 14 = 42 years.
recs.rel: Here the sister is the older one, so multiply Ali's age by 3.

recs.q: On which date did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic under the 1956 Constitution?
recs.facts: The first Constitution of Pakistan came into force on 23 March 1956 and the country became the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

recs.q: In which year did the revelation (wahi) first begin to descend on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old when Angel Jibreel brought the first revelation, in 610 AD during Ramadan.
recs.rel: The first revelation consisted of the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.

recs.q: Which countries jointly hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
recs.facts: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, from June to July 2026.
recs.rel: The previous World Cup in 2022 was held in Qatar.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Belgium as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Bart De Wever became Prime Minister of Belgium on 3 February 2025 and remains in office.
recs.rel: Charles Michel, the answer given by candidates in 2022, was PM from 2014 to 2019, and Alexander De Croo held office from 2020 to 2025.

recs.q: What is the Urdu meaning of the word Momin?
recs.facts: Momin means a believer, one who has faith (iman).
recs.rel: The plural Momineen is used in the title Ameer-ul-Momineen, meaning Commander of the Faithful.

recs.q: In which quadrant of the coordinate plane does the point (-5, 6) lie?
recs.facts: The x value is negative and the y value is positive, which is the second quadrant.
recs.rel: The signs by quadrant are (+,+), (-,+), (-,-) and (+,-) for the first to fourth quadrants.

recs.q: Microsoft, the technology company, belongs to which country?
recs.facts: Microsoft is headquartered in Redmond, Washington, in the United States.
recs.rel: Microsoft was founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen.

recs.q: The river Tigris mainly flows through which country?
recs.facts: The Tigris rises in Turkey and flows through Iraq, joining the Euphrates to form the Shatt al-Arab.
recs.rel: Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, stands on the Tigris.

recs.q: Which is the best month mentioned in the Quran by name?
recs.facts: Ramadan is the only month named in the Quran, and the Quran was revealed in it.
recs.rel: Laylatul Qadr, better than a thousand months, falls in Ramadan.

recs.q: Which is the longest tunnel of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Lowari Tunnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, linking Dir and Chitral, has a main bore of about 8.5 km and is the longest in Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Khojak Tunnel in Balochistan is a railway tunnel about 3.9 km long.

recs.q: Which is the longest river flowing within India?
recs.facts: The Ganga is the longest river flowing mainly within India, about 2,500 km.
recs.rel: The Indus and Brahmaputra are longer overall but rise outside India.

recs.q: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was a slave in the custody of which Quraish chief before he was freed?
recs.facts: Umayyah bin Khalaf tortured Hazrat Bilal (RA) for accepting Islam, until Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed him.
recs.rel: Hazrat Bilal (RA) became the first muazzin of Islam.

recs.q: What is the national bird of India?
recs.facts: The Indian peafowl (peacock) was declared the national bird of India in 1963.
recs.rel: The national bird of Pakistan is the chukar partridge.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: He has gone to ___ UK.
recs.facts: The name United Kingdom is a plural union of states, so UK takes the definite article: the UK.
recs.rel: Names like the USA, the UAE and the Netherlands also take the.

recs.q: Sky is to blue as blood is to what?
recs.facts: The sky is blue in colour and blood is red in colour, so the analogy is by colour.
recs.rel: Haemoglobin in red blood cells gives blood its red colour.

recs.q: On which date was the atomic bomb dropped on Nagasaki?
recs.facts: The United States dropped the atomic bomb on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, three days after the bomb on Hiroshima.
recs.rel: Japan announced its surrender on 15 August 1945 and signed the surrender document on 2 September 1945.

recs.q: On which date was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah born?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi. He died on 11 September 1948.
recs.rel: His birthplace is Wazir Mansion, Karachi.

recs.q: General Pervez Musharraf was born in which city?
recs.facts: Pervez Musharraf was born on 11 August 1943 in Delhi, British India. His family migrated to Pakistan in 1947.
recs.rel: He ruled Pakistan from the 1999 military takeover until he resigned in 2008.

recs.q: In which city was Prophet Muhammad (SAW) born?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (SAW) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, about 570 or 571 AD.
recs.rel: He migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which began the Hijri calendar.

recs.q: The Maginot Line was a line of fortifications built along the border between which two countries?
recs.facts: France built the Maginot Line in the 1930s along its eastern border with Germany (and Italy) to stop a German invasion.
recs.rel: Germany bypassed it in 1940 by invading France through Belgium.

recs.q: Which country has the longest bridge in the world?
recs.facts: The Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, about 164.8 km long, is the longest bridge in the world by total length. It carries the Beijing-Shanghai high-speed railway.
recs.rel: The second longest is the Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct in Taiwan.

recs.q: What is the son of my brother called in relation to me?
recs.facts: A brother's son is a nephew to his uncle or aunt.
recs.rel: A brother's daughter is called a niece.

recs.q: What is the approximate average lactation period of a buffalo?
recs.facts: A buffalo gives milk for about 270 to 305 days after calving, so about 300 days is the usual figure. It varies with breed and feeding.
recs.rel: Nili-Ravi is a famous Pakistani buffalo breed known for high milk yield.

recs.q: Which is the tallest building in the world?
recs.facts: Burj Khalifa in Dubai, 828 m high, is the tallest completed building in the world as of October 2026.
recs.rel: Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia is under construction and is expected to surpass it around 2028.

recs.q: Gun is to bullet as pitcher is to ___.
recs.facts: A gun fires a bullet, and in baseball a pitcher throws a ball. The relationship is a tool or person to the object it sends.
recs.rel: A bat is used by the batter to hit the ball.

recs.q: In a bus of 40 people, 30 are men. What percentage of the people are women?
recs.facts: Women = 40 - 30 = 10. Percentage = 10 / 40 x 100 = 25%.
recs.rel: The men make up the remaining 75%.

recs.q: In which month and Hijri year was the Treaty (Sulah) of Hudaibia signed?
recs.facts: The Prophet (SAW) set out for Umrah in Dhul Qadah 6 AH, was stopped at Hudaibia, and signed the treaty there with the Quraish.
recs.rel: The treaty is called a clear victory in Surah Al-Fath, and it was followed by the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

recs.q: The compilation of the Quran in book form was done under which caliph, who accepted Hazrat Umar's (RA) suggestion after the Battle of Yamama?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) ordered Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) to collect the Quran after many Huffaz were martyred at the Battle of Yamama.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman (RA) later had standard copies made and sent to the main cities.

recs.q: Lusaka is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Lusaka is the capital and largest city of Zambia.
recs.rel: Zambia was formerly called Northern Rhodesia and became independent in 1964.

recs.q: What is the official capital of Benin?
recs.facts: Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin, although the government sits in Cotonou.
recs.rel: Cotonou is the largest city and economic centre of Benin.

recs.q: What is the constitutional capital of Bolivia?
recs.facts: Bolivia's constitution names Sucre as its capital.
recs.rel: The government and legislature sit in La Paz, which is the seat of government.

recs.q: What is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina?
recs.facts: Sarajevo is the capital and largest city of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
recs.rel: The 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo triggered World War I.

recs.q: What is the capital of Egypt?
recs.facts: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt, on the River Nile.
recs.rel: Egypt is building a New Administrative Capital east of Cairo.

recs.q: What is the capital of Great Britain (the United Kingdom)?
recs.facts: London is the capital of the United Kingdom and England.
recs.rel: Edinburgh, Cardiff and Belfast are capitals of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

recs.q: What is the capital of Liberia?
recs.facts: Monrovia is the capital of Liberia and is named after US President James Monroe.
recs.rel: Liberia was founded by freed African American slaves.

recs.q: What is the capital of Madagascar?
recs.facts: Antananarivo is the capital and largest city of Madagascar.
recs.rel: Madagascar is the fourth largest island in the world.

recs.q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
recs.facts: Ulaanbaatar (Ulan Bator) is the capital of Mongolia.
recs.rel: Ulaanbaatar is one of the coldest capital cities in the world.

recs.q: What is the capital of Morocco?
recs.facts: Rabat is the capital of Morocco.
recs.rel: Casablanca is the largest city of Morocco.

recs.q: What is the capital of Turkmenistan?
recs.facts: Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan.
recs.rel: Turkmenistan is a Central Asian country bordering Iran and Afghanistan.

recs.q: What is the capital of Uzbekistan?
recs.facts: Tashkent is the capital and largest city of Uzbekistan.
recs.rel: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration between Pakistan and India was signed in this city.

recs.q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
recs.facts: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.
recs.rel: Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon) is the largest city of Vietnam.

recs.q: In which years was the FIFA World Cup not held because of World War II?
recs.facts: The World Cup was held in 1938 and then next in 1950, so the 1942 and 1946 tournaments were cancelled.
recs.rel: Brazil hosted the 1950 World Cup, the first after the war.

recs.q: What is the currency of Canada?
recs.facts: Canada uses the Canadian dollar (CAD).
recs.rel: The Canadian one dollar coin is nicknamed the loonie.

recs.q: Which dam in Pakistan was built with the help of Canada under the Colombo Plan?
recs.facts: Warsak Dam on the Kabul River near Peshawar was built in the 1950s with Canadian aid under the Colombo Plan.
recs.rel: Mangla Dam was built on the Jhelum River and Tarbela Dam on the Indus River.

recs.q: Who is the captain of the Pakistan women's cricket team in 2026?
recs.facts: Fatima Sana leads Pakistan women's team, including at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup.
recs.rel: Before Fatima Sana, Nida Dar and Bismah Maroof had captained the side.

recs.q: Change the narration: The captain said to his men, "Stand at ease."
opts: The captain told his men that they stood at ease.
The captain commanded his men to stand at ease.
The captain asked his men if they stood at ease.
The captain said to his men that stand at ease.
recs.facts: The quoted sentence is an order, so the reporting verb becomes commanded and the order is turned into an infinitive.
recs.rel: Imperative sentences in indirect speech use words such as ordered, commanded, requested or advised.

recs.q: Choose the part of speech of the word 'but' in: I ran fast to catch the train but I was late.
recs.facts: Here 'but' joins two clauses showing contrast, so it is a coordinating conjunction.
recs.rel: The coordinating conjunctions are for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.

recs.q: Change the voice: Dogs always chased cats.
opts: Cats are always chased by dogs.
Cats have always been chased by dogs.
Cats were always chased by dogs.
Cats were always being chased by dogs.
recs.facts: The sentence is past simple, so the passive uses 'was/were + past participle': cats were always chased by dogs.
recs.rel: In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

recs.q: In which city is the World Trade Center located?
recs.facts: The World Trade Center complex is in Lower Manhattan, New York City.
recs.rel: The original Twin Towers were destroyed in the attacks of 11 September 2001.

recs.q: What was the name of the camel of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Prophet's well-known camel was named Qaswa, which he rode during the Hijrat.
recs.rel: Sources also mention the name Adba for his camel, and Duldul was his mule.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan join CENTO (the Baghdad Pact)?
recs.facts: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact in 1955, which was renamed CENTO in 1959.
recs.rel: Pakistan left CENTO in 1979 after Iran withdrew.

recs.q: On a farm, the cows are 5, the camels are three times the cows and the goats are three times the camels. How many animals are there in total?
recs.facts: Cows = 5, camels = 3 x 5 = 15, goats = 3 x 15 = 45. Total = 5 + 15 + 45 = 65.
recs.rel: Always compute each group step by step before adding.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
recs.facts: The word is spelt circum-fer-ence, from Latin meaning carrying around.
recs.rel: Circumference comes from the Latin words circum (around) and ferre (to carry).

recs.q: Which are the three largest cities of Pakistan by population?
recs.facts: In the 2023 census the most populous cities were Karachi, then Lahore, then Faisalabad.
recs.rel: Karachi is the largest city and the capital of Sindh.

recs.q: Basel is a city of which country?
recs.facts: Basel lies on the River Rhine in north-west Switzerland, near the French and German borders.
recs.rel: Basel is home to the Bank for International Settlements.

recs.q: In which city is the Shahi Qila (Lahore Fort) located?
recs.facts: The Shahi Qila, also called the Lahore Fort, stands in the Walled City of Lahore. It was rebuilt in the Mughal era, notably under Akbar.
recs.rel: The Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens were listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1981.

recs.q: What is the characteristic of the logarithm (base 10) of 2458.4?
recs.facts: The characteristic is the number of digits before the decimal point minus one. 2458.4 has 4 digits before the point, so the characteristic is 3.
recs.rel: The decimal part of a logarithm is called the mantissa.

recs.q: What is the characteristic of log 99.96?
recs.facts: 99.96 has 2 digits before the decimal point, so its characteristic is 2 - 1 = 1.
recs.rel: Since log 100 = 2, log 99.96 is just under 2, that is 1 plus a mantissa close to 1.

recs.q: What is the characteristic of log 99.6?
recs.facts: 99.6 has 2 digits before the decimal point, so its characteristic is 2 - 1 = 1.
recs.rel: For numbers less than 1 the characteristic is negative.

recs.q: In the sentence 'The movie was amazing', what part of speech is the word 'amazing'?
recs.facts: The word 'amazing' describes the noun 'movie', so it is an adjective.
recs.rel: An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun.

recs.q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey Champions Trophy?
recs.facts: Pakistan won the Champions Trophy three times, in 1978, 1980 and 1994.
recs.rel: Australia is the most successful team in the tournament history, with 14 titles.

recs.q: Which country topped the medal table of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta?
recs.facts: China won the most gold medals (132) and the most medals overall at the 2018 Asian Games.
recs.rel: Japan finished second and South Korea third in 2018.

recs.q: Which country is the current FIFA World Cup champion (2026)?
recs.facts: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 final on 19 July 2026.
recs.rel: The previous champion was Argentina in 2022, and Germany won in 2014.

recs.q: Who is the Premier (Prime Minister) of China?
recs.facts: Li Qiang has been Premier of the State Council of China since March 2023.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Li Keqiang, who served from 2013 to 2023.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of 'up to date'?
recs.facts: Up to date means current or modern, including the latest information or style.
recs.rel: Its opposite is outdated or obsolete.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'cordial'?
recs.facts: Cordial means warm, friendly and polite.
recs.rel: Cordial can also be a noun meaning a sweet fruit drink.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'cute'?
recs.facts: Cute means pleasingly attractive or charming, especially in a small or sweet way.
recs.rel: Synonyms include adorable and lovely.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'distraction'?
recs.facts: A distraction is something that pulls attention away from what one is doing, so diversion (also deviation of attention) is closest.
recs.rel: The opposite of distraction is concentration.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'installed'?
recs.facts: To install something is to put or fix it in position ready for use, so installed means fitted in place.
recs.rel: The opposite of install is uninstall or remove.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'lubricant'?
recs.facts: A lubricant such as oil or grease is applied to moving parts to reduce friction between them.
recs.rel: Engine oil is a common lubricant used in vehicles.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'predicament'?
recs.facts: A predicament is an unpleasant or awkward situation that is hard to get out of, so difficult situation or dilemma fits best.
recs.rel: Synonyms of predicament include plight, dilemma and quandary.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'proceeding' as used in 'The work is proceeding well'?
recs.facts: To proceed means to go on or move forward, so proceeding means advancing or continuing.
recs.rel: As a noun, proceedings means the events of a meeting or a legal action.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'propel'?
recs.facts: To propel is to push or drive something forward with force.
recs.rel: A propeller is the device that propels a ship or aeroplane.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'purge'?
recs.facts: To purge means to rid something of unwanted things or people, in other words to cleanse or remove.
recs.rel: Purge is also used for a medicine that clears the bowels.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'safety'?
recs.facts: Safety means being protected from harm or danger, which is the same as security.
recs.rel: Danger, risk and threat are antonyms of safety.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'comic'?
recs.facts: Comic means causing laughter, so funny is the closest meaning.
recs.rel: Comical and humorous are also synonyms of comic.

recs.q: What is the international telephone country code of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan's international dialling code is +92.
recs.rel: +91 is India, +93 is Afghanistan and +98 is Iran.

recs.q: Which is the largest and coldest place on Earth?
recs.facts: Antarctica is the coldest, driest and windiest continent and is larger than Europe and Australia.
recs.rel: The lowest natural temperature recorded on Earth, about minus 89 degrees Celsius, was at Vostok Station in Antarctica.

recs.q: The common endpoint of two non-collinear rays forming an angle is called its what?
recs.facts: Two rays that start from the same point form an angle, and that shared endpoint is the vertex of the angle.
recs.rel: The two rays forming the angle are called its arms or sides.

recs.q: Which two colours are found on the national flag of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The flag has a dark green field with a vertical white stripe at the hoist, and a white crescent and star on the green.
recs.rel: The flag was designed by Syed Amir-uddin Kedwaii based on the Muslim League flag.

recs.q: Does a column matrix have an inverse?
opts: No, because it is not a square matrix
Yes, it is always a row matrix
Yes, it is the identity matrix
Only if all entries are zero
recs.facts: Only a square matrix with a non-zero determinant can have an inverse, and a column matrix has one column but several rows, so it is not square.
recs.rel: A column matrix can be turned into a row matrix by taking its transpose.

recs.q: How many rows and columns does the matrix [2 3] have?
recs.facts: The matrix is written in a single line, so it has 1 row, and it has two entries, so 2 columns. Its order is 1 x 2.
recs.rel: A matrix with only one row is called a row matrix.

recs.q: What is the common difference of the series 12, 16, 20, 24, 28?
recs.facts: 16 - 12 = 4, 20 - 16 = 4, and so on, so each term increases by 4.
recs.rel: A series with a constant common difference is an arithmetic progression.

recs.q: In which country were the first Commonwealth Games (then called the British Empire Games) held in 1930?
recs.facts: The first Games were held in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, in 1930.
recs.rel: The Games are held every four years.

recs.q: What is the conjugate of the complex number 6+3i?
recs.facts: The conjugate of a+bi is a-bi, so only the sign of the imaginary part changes. Hence the conjugate of 6+3i is 6-3i.
recs.rel: The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number, a squared plus b squared.

recs.q: What is the conjugate of the complex number 7+6i?
recs.facts: The conjugate of a+bi is a-bi, so the sign of the imaginary part is reversed. Hence the conjugate of 7+6i is 7-6i.
recs.rel: Complex roots of a real-coefficient polynomial always occur in conjugate pairs.

recs.q: What is the conjugate of a complex number a+bi?
recs.facts: The conjugate of a complex number is found by changing the sign of its imaginary part. So the conjugate of a+bi is a-bi.
recs.rel: Geometrically, the conjugate is the mirror image of the number in the real axis.

recs.q: Which of these numbers is a composite number: 1, 5, 8, 13?
recs.facts: 5 and 13 are prime and 1 is neither prime nor composite. 8 has factors 1, 2, 4 and 8, so it is composite.
recs.rel: The smallest composite number is 4.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'contentment'?
recs.facts: Contentment means satisfaction, so its opposite is discontent, meaning dissatisfaction or unhappiness.
recs.rel: Discontent can be used as both a noun and an adjective.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'controversy'?
recs.facts: Controversy means a prolonged public disagreement. Its opposite is agreement or harmony.
recs.rel: The word controversial describes something that causes disagreement.

recs.q: Choose the correct preposition: He should establish confidence ___ his clients.
recs.facts: The correct collocation is 'confidence in' someone. So the sentence reads: He should establish confidence in his clients.
recs.rel: We also say faith in, trust in and belief in.

recs.q: In which year AD is the conquest of Sindh by Muhammad bin Qasim completed, as commonly given in Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim landed in 711 AD and defeated Raja Dahir in 712 AD, completing the conquest of Sindh.
recs.rel: Some sources give 711 AD for the invasion and 712 AD for the conquest.

recs.q: Who conquered the fort of Khyber (Khaybar) in 7 AH?
recs.facts: The Muslims besieged the Jewish forts of Khyber, and Hazrat Ali (RA) led the final conquest of the main fort, Qamus. He was given the Prophet's flag.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) is known by the title Asadullah and Haidar-e-Karrar.

recs.q: What is the term of office of the UN Secretary-General?
recs.facts: The UN Secretary-General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council for a term of five years, which can be renewed.
recs.rel: Antonio Guterres has served since 2017 and his second term ends on 31 December 2026.

recs.q: In which Pakistani city have SAARC summits been held?
recs.facts: Pakistan hosted the 4th SAARC Summit in Islamabad in 1988 and the 12th in Islamabad in 2004.
recs.rel: The SAARC Secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal.

recs.q: With which Afghan province does the Khyber Pass connect Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Khyber Pass leads from Pakistan through Torkham into Nangarhar Province of Afghanistan. The provincial capital is Jalalabad.
recs.rel: The Khyber Pass lies in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa near Peshawar.

recs.q: Which body regulates the oil and gas industry in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) regulates the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector of Pakistan.
recs.rel: NEPRA regulates the electric power sector.

recs.q: In which year did the construction of Mangla Dam start, as given by WAPDA?
recs.facts: WAPDA gives 1962 as the start of construction of Mangla Dam on the Jhelum, and it was completed in 1967.
recs.rel: Some sources, including Wikipedia, give 1961 as the start year, so sources differ.

recs.q: What is cos x divided by sin x equal to?
recs.facts: By definition, cotangent is the ratio of cosine to sine, so cos x / sin x = cot x. It is the reciprocal of tan x.
recs.rel: The identity cot x = cos x / sin x is undefined where sin x equals 0, such as at 0 and 180 degrees.

recs.q: What are the values of sin 0 degrees and cos 90 degrees?
recs.facts: On the unit circle the point at 0 degrees is (1, 0), so sin 0 = 0. The point at 90 degrees is (0, 1), so cos 90 = 0.
recs.rel: In the same way, cos 0 = 1 and sin 90 = 1.

recs.q: What is sec x . cosec x equal to?
recs.facts: sec x . cosec x = 1 / (sin x cos x). Since sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x, sin x cos x = (sin 2x) / 2, so the product is 2 / sin 2x = 2 cosec 2x.
recs.rel: The same product also equals tan x + cot x.

recs.q: What is sin x . cos x equal to?
recs.facts: The double angle formula says sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x. Dividing both sides by 2 gives sin x cos x = (sin 2x) / 2.
recs.rel: The related formula cos 2x = cos squared x minus sin squared x is also widely used.

recs.q: Who is traditionally credited with the creation of the Urdu language?
recs.facts: Amir Khusro (1253-1325) is traditionally credited with using and promoting the early form of Urdu, then called Hindavi, in his poetry.
recs.rel: Sources differ: Urdu really developed over centuries from the mixing of Persian, Arabic and local languages in the army bazaars and courts.

recs.q: What is the value of i cubed, where i is the imaginary unit?
recs.facts: Since i squared = -1, i cubed = i squared x i = -1 x i = -i.
recs.rel: The powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1.

recs.q: What is the currency of Sweden?
recs.facts: Sweden uses the Swedish krona (SEK) and did not adopt the euro.
recs.rel: Denmark and Norway have their own kroner, but Sweden's currency is the krona.

recs.q: The yuan is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: The yuan, also called the renminbi, is the currency of China.
recs.rel: Japan uses the yen and South Korea uses the won.

recs.q: Who is the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia?
recs.facts: Mohammed bin Salman has been Crown Prince since June 2017, when he replaced Mohammed bin Nayef. He is also Prime Minister.
recs.rel: The reigning king is Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan is the Diamer-Bhasha Dam being built?
opts: Azad Kashmir, on the Neelum River
recs.facts: The Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River near Chilas, on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It is planned to be one of the highest roller-compacted concrete dams in the world.

recs.q: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite to the 90 degree angle is called what?
recs.facts: The longest side of a right-angled triangle lies opposite the right angle and is called the hypotenuse.
recs.rel: The Pythagoras theorem states that the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

recs.q: How many minutes are there in 10 degrees of an angle?
recs.facts: One degree equals 60 minutes, so 10 degrees equal 10 x 60 = 600 minutes.
recs.rel: One minute of angle equals 60 seconds, so 1 degree equals 3600 seconds.

recs.q: In a right-angled triangle, if one of the acute angles is 30 degrees, what is the other acute angle?
recs.facts: The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. So the third angle is 180 - 90 - 30 = 60 degrees.
recs.rel: A triangle with angles 30, 60 and 90 degrees has sides in the ratio 1 : root 3 : 2.

recs.q: Which symbol is used to denote the set of integers in mathematics?
recs.facts: The set of integers is written as Z, from the German word Zahlen meaning numbers.
recs.rel: N denotes natural numbers, Q rational numbers and R real numbers.

recs.q: In an arithmetic progression, the difference between consecutive terms is denoted by which symbol?
recs.facts: In an arithmetic progression the constant difference between consecutive terms is called the common difference and is written as d.
recs.rel: The nth term of an AP is a + (n - 1)d.

recs.q: Who is the current Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan (October 2026)?
recs.facts: Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah was elected Deputy Speaker on 1 March 2024 and still holds the office.
recs.rel: Qasim Khan Suri was the Deputy Speaker from 2018 to 2022, and Ayaz Sadiq is the current Speaker.

recs.q: In which surah of the Holy Quran are the commands for wuzu (ablution) and ghusl described together?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Maidah, verse 6, gives the detailed command for wuzu, ghusl and tayammum. Surah An-Nisa verse 43 also mentions them briefly.
recs.rel: Verse 6 of Surah Al-Maidah is known as the verse of wuzu.

recs.q: What is the determinant of a null (zero) matrix?
recs.facts: Every element of a null matrix is zero, so every row is zero and the determinant is 0.
recs.rel: A square matrix with determinant zero is called a singular matrix.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did Hazrat Fatima (RA), the daughter of the Holy Prophet (SAW), pass away?
recs.facts: Hazrat Fatima (RA) passed away in 11 AH, about six months after the death of the Holy Prophet (SAW).
recs.rel: She was the wife of Hazrat Ali (RA) and the mother of Hazrat Hasan and Hazrat Husain (RA).

recs.q: What is a decimal fraction in which one or more digits repeat endlessly (such as 0.333...) called?
recs.facts: A decimal whose digits repeat in a pattern forever is called a recurring (repeating) decimal. It always represents a rational number.

recs.q: Who took care of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the death of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib?
recs.facts: Abdul Muttalib entrusted the Prophet (PBUH) to his son Abu Talib before dying. Abu Talib looked after him until adulthood and long after.
recs.rel: Abu Talib protected the Prophet (PBUH) against the Quraish for many years, until his death in the year of sorrow.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'different'?
recs.facts: Different means not the same. Its opposite is same.
recs.rel: Distinct, various and unusual are close in meaning to different.

recs.q: In which district of Balochistan is the Reko Diq project located?
recs.facts: Reko Diq is a large copper and gold deposit near Nokkundi in Chagai district of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Chagai is also the district where Pakistan conducted its 1998 nuclear tests at Ras Koh hills.

recs.q: Odd one out among: Musician, Movie, Director, Writer.
recs.facts: Musician, director and writer are all people with professions. A movie is a work, not a person.
recs.rel: In odd-one-out questions, look for the item that belongs to a different category from the rest.

recs.q: What is the distance between the points (0, -2) and (0, 1)?
recs.facts: Both points lie on the y-axis, so distance = |1 - (-2)| = 3.
recs.rel: The general distance formula is the square root of (x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2.

recs.q: In which district of Punjab is Kalabagh located?
recs.facts: Kalabagh is a town on the Indus River in Mianwali district, Punjab.
recs.rel: The proposed Kalabagh Dam site is near this town.

recs.q: Change the voice: My brother must not be disturbed by you.
opts: You must not disturb my brother.
You did not disturb my brother.
My brother must not disturb you.
recs.facts: In the active voice the doer (you) becomes the subject, and the modal 'must not be disturbed' becomes 'must not disturb'.
recs.rel: Passive voice with a modal follows the pattern modal + be + past participle.

recs.q: What is the value of log 8 divided by log 2?
recs.facts: log 8 = log 2^3 = 3 log 2, so log 8 / log 2 = 3.
recs.rel: Also, log base 2 of 8 equals log 8 / log 2 by the change of base rule.

recs.q: How many divisions does Punjab (Pakistan) have at present?
recs.facts: Punjab had nine divisions for years. Gujrat was restored as the tenth division, notified in December 2024.
recs.rel: Before Gujrat was added, the nine divisions were Bahawalpur, DG Khan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Lahore, Multan, Rawalpindi, Sahiwal and Sargodha.

recs.q: If tangents are drawn to a circle from a point outside it, they are ___ in length.
recs.facts: The two tangents from an external point form congruent right triangles with the radii, so their lengths are equal.
recs.rel: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

recs.q: What did Christopher Columbus reach in 1492 on his voyage across the Atlantic?
recs.facts: Columbus, sailing for Spain, reached islands of the Caribbean in 1492, which opened the Americas to Europe.
recs.rel: He was actually searching for a sea route to India.

recs.q: What is the main duty of Hazrat Jibrael (AS)?
opts: To bring revelation (wahi) from Allah to the Prophets
To blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgement
To take the souls of the dying
recs.facts: Hazrat Jibrael (AS) is the angel who carried Allah's revelation to the Prophets, including the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
recs.rel: Hazrat Israfil (AS) will blow the Trumpet, Hazrat Mikael (AS) is in charge of rain and Hazrat Izrael (AS) takes souls.

recs.q: Which instrument is used to record and measure earthquakes?
recs.facts: A seismograph records the vibrations of seismic waves produced by an earthquake.
recs.rel: The Richter scale is the scale commonly used to express the magnitude of an earthquake.

recs.q: In the sentence "How many burgers had you eaten yesterday?", which part of speech is "how many"?
recs.facts: "How many" asks about quantity and describes the noun "burgers", so it works as an (interrogative) adjective.
recs.rel: Adjectives of quantity answer the questions how much or how many.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "efficient"?
recs.facts: Efficient means able to do something well with little waste of time or effort, which matches capable or competent.
recs.rel: The noun form is efficiency and its opposite is inefficiency.

recs.q: B is 6 years older than A. At what age of A will B be 3 times as old as A?
recs.facts: Let A be x. Then B is x + 6 and x + 6 = 3x, so 2x = 6 and x = 3.
recs.rel: At that time B is 9 years old, exactly 3 times A's age of 3.

recs.q: Usman is older than Khalid, and Khalid is older than Kadir. Who is the eldest?
recs.facts: Usman is older than Khalid and Khalid is older than Kadir, so the order is Usman, Khalid, Kadir.
recs.rel: Such ordering problems are solved by writing the persons in a line from oldest to youngest.

recs.q: In which year was the second general election held in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first general election on adult franchise was held in 1970 and the second in March 1977.
recs.rel: The 1977 election led to protests and the martial law of General Zia ul Haq in July 1977.

recs.q: In which year was the first general election held in Pakistan on the basis of adult franchise?
recs.facts: The first direct general election on adult franchise took place in December 1970 under General Yahya Khan.
recs.rel: The Awami League won a majority in the National Assembly in this election.

recs.q: What did the Fourteen Points of Quaid-e-Azam (1929) demand about electorates?
opts: Separate electorates to continue for Muslims
recs.facts: The Fourteen Points demanded that Muslims keep their separate electorates until they themselves agreed to give them up.
recs.rel: The Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 as an answer to the Nehru Report.

recs.q: If sets A and B have no common element, what is n(A union B)?
recs.facts: For any sets n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B). With no common element the intersection is empty, so n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B).
recs.rel: Sets with no common element are called disjoint sets.

recs.q: Where does the Indus River rise and where does it fall?
opts: Rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea
Rises in the Hindu Kush and falls into the Bay of Bengal
Rises in the Karakoram and falls into the Persian Gulf
Rises in Kashmir and falls into the Arabian Sea at Gwadar
recs.facts: The Indus rises from the Tibetan plateau near Lake Mansarovar, flows through Ladakh and Pakistan and ends in the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
recs.rel: It is Pakistan's longest river.

recs.q: What is the antonym of "entirely"?
recs.facts: Entirely means completely, and its opposite is partially, which means only in part.
recs.rel: Other opposites are partly and slightly.

recs.q: What is the equation y = 7x + 7 called?
recs.facts: The highest power of the variables x and y is 1, so it is a linear equation.
recs.rel: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line.

recs.q: On what date was the World Health Organization (WHO) established?
recs.facts: The WHO constitution came into force on 7 April 1948, which is why World Health Day is observed every year on 7 April. The WHO was set up as a specialised agency of the United Nations.
recs.rel: The WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.

recs.q: On what date was the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) of Pakistan established?
recs.facts: WAPDA was created by an Act in 1958 and began functioning on 12 February 1958. It was formed to develop Pakistan's water and power resources.
recs.rel: WAPDA was later split so that power distribution moved to separate companies, but it still builds dams such as Tarbela and Mangla.

recs.q: In which country does Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, mainly lie?
recs.facts: Mount Everest lies in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and the Tibet region of China. The main summit is usually described as being in Nepal.
recs.rel: Everest is about 8,849 metres high; Nepal calls it Sagarmatha and Tibet calls it Chomolungma.

recs.q: On what date did the War of Independence of 1857 begin at Meerut?
recs.facts: The sepoys of the Bengal Army at Meerut revolted on 10 May 1857, and this started the War of Independence. The rebels then marched to Delhi.
recs.rel: The last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, was declared the leader of the rebellion.

recs.q: Which product is Pakistan's largest export by value?
recs.facts: Textiles, including cotton cloth, yarn, bed linen and readymade garments, make up more than half of Pakistan's exports by value. Rice is the largest food export but is much smaller.
recs.rel: Pakistan is among the top cotton-producing countries in the world.

recs.q: In which year was Facebook founded?
recs.facts: Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook on 4 February 2004 from his Harvard University dormitory.
recs.rel: The company was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021.

recs.q: What is the value of 10! (factorial of 10)?
recs.rel: The factorial of 5 is 120.

recs.q: Factorise the expression x^2 + 5x - 6.
recs.facts: We need two numbers whose product is -6 and whose sum is +5. These numbers are +6 and -1, so x^2 + 5x - 6 = (x + 6)(x - 1).
recs.rel: The roots of this expression are x = 1 and x = -6.

recs.q: A farm has 3 goats, 5 cows and 14 hens. What is the total number of legs of these animals?
recs.facts: Goats and cows have 4 legs each: (3 + 5) x 4 = 32 legs. Hens have 2 legs each: 14 x 2 = 28 legs. The total is 32 + 28 = 60.
recs.rel: The count of the farmer's legs is not included.

recs.q: Who was the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound?
recs.facts: US Air Force pilot Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier on 14 October 1947 flying the Bell X-1 rocket plane.
recs.rel: The speed of sound at sea level is about 1,235 km/h, called Mach 1.

recs.q: The former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) became part of which province?
recs.facts: FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through the 25th Constitutional Amendment, passed in May 2018.
recs.rel: The merged areas were divided into districts such as North Waziristan and South Waziristan.

recs.q: What does FATA stand for?
recs.facts: FATA stands for Federally Administered Tribal Areas, the seven agencies on the Afghan border governed directly by the federal government.
recs.rel: FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) located?
recs.facts: The FATF secretariat is hosted at the OECD headquarters in Paris, France.
recs.rel: The FATF was set up by the G7 in 1989 to fight money laundering and terrorist financing.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Yunus (AS)?
recs.facts: According to Islamic tradition, Hazrat Yunus (AS) was the son of Matta (Matthew). He was sent to the people of Nineveh.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yunus (AS) is also called Dhun-Nun and Sahib al-Hut because of the incident of the fish.

recs.q: Who was the father of Hazrat Yaqub (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and the grandson of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the father of Hazrat Yusuf (AS).

recs.q: In which year was Fatima Jinnah born?
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah, the sister of Quaid-e-Azam, was born in Karachi in 1893.
recs.rel: Her birth date is given as 30 or 31 July 1893 in different sources, and she died in 1967.

recs.q: In which city was Fatima Jinnah born?
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah was born in Karachi in 1893 into the family of Jinnahbhai Poonja.
