recs.rel: She was given the title Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

recs.q: Surah Al-Fil of the Holy Quran is named after which animal?
recs.facts: Al-Fil means the elephant. The surah describes how Allah destroyed the army of Abraha that came with elephants to demolish the Kaaba.
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the same Year of the Elephant.

recs.q: In a class of 33 students, 2/3 are boys. How many are girls?
recs.rel: Girls are 1/3 of the class, which is the same as 33 divided by 3.

recs.q: To which country did the World War 2 leader Winston Churchill belong?
recs.facts: Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom during most of World War 2 (1940-1945).
recs.rel: He also served a second term as Prime Minister from 1951 to 1955.

recs.q: Find X: 3 : X :: 4 : 12
recs.facts: The ratio 4:12 equals 1:3, so 3:X must also be 1:3. Therefore X = 3 x 3 = 9.
recs.rel: In a proportion a:b :: c:d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (ad = bc).

recs.q: If the ordered pairs (x, y - 1) and (2, -1) are equal, what are the values of x and y?
recs.facts: Equal ordered pairs have equal coordinates. So x = 2 and y - 1 = -1, which gives y = 0.
recs.rel: Ordered pairs (a, b) and (c, d) are equal only when a = c and b = d.

recs.q: What is the height of K2 in feet?
recs.facts: K2 is 8,611 metres high. Multiplying by 3.28 gives about 28,251 feet.
recs.rel: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world after Mount Everest at 29,032 feet.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: It is time to eat food.
opts: It is time that food eats.
Food is time to be eaten.
It is time for food to be eaten.
It was time for food to be eaten.
recs.facts: The active infinitive 'to eat food' becomes 'for food to be eaten' in the passive, with the present tense 'is' kept.
recs.rel: In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

recs.q: Change into active voice: By whom is the boy being fed?
recs.facts: The passive 'is being fed' (present continuous) becomes 'is feeding' in the active, and 'by whom' becomes 'who'.
recs.rel: The agent after 'by' becomes the subject of the active sentence.

recs.q: Shoe is to foot as helmet is to what?
recs.facts: A shoe is worn to protect the foot, and a helmet is worn to protect the head.
recs.rel: This is a type of analogy based on an object and the body part it protects.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: square, yard, meter, foot?
recs.facts: Yard, meter and foot are units of length. Square is a geometric shape.
recs.rel: One yard equals three feet, and one meter is about 3.28 feet.

recs.q: What was the name of the foster sister of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) was nursed by Halima Sadia, whose daughter Shaima was his foster sister. She helped to care for him as a child.
recs.rel: Halima Sadia belonged to the tribe of Banu Saad.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word fostering?
recs.facts: To foster means to encourage the growth or development of something or someone. Nurturing has the closest meaning.
recs.rel: The word foster is also used for caring for a child who is not one's own, as in foster mother.

recs.q: What is the antonym of fostering?
recs.facts: Fostering means encouraging and caring for growth. Neglecting means failing to care, so it is the opposite.
recs.rel: Nurturing, supporting and promoting are synonyms of fostering.

recs.q: Where was the Battle (Ghazwa) of Khyber fought?
opts: An oasis north of Madinah inhabited by Jews
recs.facts: Khyber was a fortified oasis about 150 km north of Madinah, home to Jewish tribes. The Muslims fought there in 7 AH.
recs.rel: The famous fort of Khyber was conquered under the leadership of Hazrat Ali (RA).

recs.q: What is the SI unit of force?
recs.facts: Force is mass times acceleration, so its unit is kg m per second squared, which is called the newton (N).
recs.rel: One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 metre per second squared.

recs.q: Which country is the fourth most populous country in the world?
recs.facts: The ranking by population is India, China, the United States, then Indonesia. Pakistan is fifth.
recs.rel: Population rankings change over time; India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023.

recs.q: Who was the fourth Khalifa (Rightly Guided Caliph) of Islam?
recs.facts: The Rightly Guided Caliphs in order were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them).
recs.rel: Hazrat Ali (RA) ruled from 656 to 661 AD.

recs.q: What is the closest opposite of the word friend?
recs.facts: A foe is an enemy, which is the opposite of a friend. The other options are close in meaning to friend.
recs.rel: Another antonym of friend is enemy.

recs.q: What is the antonym of fugitive?
recs.facts: A fugitive is a person who has escaped or is running away. A captive is someone held and not free, which is the opposite.
recs.rel: Runaway and escapee are synonyms of fugitive.

recs.q: What is the synonym of fugitive?
recs.facts: A fugitive is a person who has escaped from custody or is hiding. Runaway has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Fugitive comes from the Latin word fugere, meaning to flee.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word full?
recs.facts: Full means containing as much as possible, so complete is a synonym. Empty, hollow and thin are not.
recs.rel: The antonym of full is empty.

recs.q: If a function is both onto and one-one, what is it called?
recs.facts: A function that is both one-one (injective) and onto (surjective) is called bijective. Such a function has an inverse.
recs.rel: A bijective function matches each element of the domain with exactly one element of the range and covers the whole range.

recs.q: Which book was written by Mahatma Gandhi as his autobiography?
opts: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
recs.facts: Gandhi wrote his autobiography titled The Story of My Experiments with Truth. It was first written in Gujarati.
recs.rel: The Discovery of India was written by Jawaharlal Nehru and India Wins Freedom by Maulana Azad.

recs.q: What is the antonym of genuine?
recs.facts: Genuine means real or authentic. Fake means not real, so it is the opposite.
recs.rel: Counterfeit and bogus are also antonyms of genuine.

recs.q: In a group, 2/3 of the people are men. What percentage of the group is women?
recs.facts: Women = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the group. 1/3 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
recs.rel: The fraction 1/3 equals 33.33 percent as a decimal-percent value.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: God gives us happiness.
opts: Happiness is given to us by God.
Happiness was given to us by God.
Happiness has been given us by God.
We are given by God happiness.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive uses is/are plus the past participle: Happiness is given to us by God.
recs.rel: In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

recs.q: The speed of a train is twice that of a car. What is the speed of the train when the car is going at 30 km/hr?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 30 = 60 km/hr.
recs.rel: Speed is distance divided by time, so a train at 60 km/hr covers 60 km in one hour.

recs.q: When a man asked the Prophet (PBUH) who most deserved his good treatment, whom did the Prophet name first?
recs.facts: In the well known hadith the Prophet (PBUH) said "your mother" three times, and only then "your father".
recs.rel: This hadith is reported in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

recs.q: If Ali is greater than Usama, then Usama is ___ than Ali.
recs.facts: Ali being greater means Usama is lesser, that is smaller, than Ali.
recs.rel: Greater and smaller (or less) are opposite comparisons.

recs.q: The Karen ethnic group lives mainly in which countries?
recs.facts: The Karen people live mostly in Myanmar (Burma), especially Kayin State, and in western Thailand along the border.
recs.rel: Karen rebels in Myanmar have fought the government since 1949.

recs.q: In which city is the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) based?
recs.facts: The NSG has no permanent headquarters, but its secretariat and point of contact work from Vienna, Austria, beside the IAEA.
recs.rel: The NSG was formed in 1974 after India's first nuclear test.

recs.q: To which clan of the Quraish did Hazrat Hafsa (RA), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), belong?
recs.facts: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA), who belonged to the Banu Adi clan of the Quraish.
recs.rel: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was married to the Prophet (PBUH) in 3 AH after the death of her first husband.

recs.q: What was the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) incident in the life of the Prophet (PBUH) before prophethood?
opts: He settled the Quraish dispute over who would place the Black Stone by lifting it on a cloak and placing it himself
He destroyed the idols around the Kaaba
He was given the first revelation near the Black Stone
He led the Quraish in a war over the Kaaba
recs.facts: While the Kaaba was being rebuilt, the tribes quarrelled over who would set the Black Stone. The Prophet (PBUH) placed it on a sheet, had the leaders lift it together, and set it in place himself.
recs.rel: The Quraish called him Al-Amin for this wise decision.

recs.q: What is half of 1/8?
recs.rel: Halving a fraction doubles its denominator.

recs.q: Finger is to hand as leaf is to what?
recs.facts: A finger is a part attached at the end of the hand, just as a leaf is a part attached to a branch.
recs.rel: Analogy questions are solved by finding the relationship between the first pair and applying it to the second.

recs.q: What is a square matrix called in which all the diagonal elements are one and all other elements are zero?
recs.facts: A square matrix with ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere is the identity matrix.
recs.rel: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.

recs.q: Who was Hazrat Sara (Saira) (AS)?
opts: Wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)
recs.facts: Hazrat Sara (AS) was the first wife of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).

recs.q: What is the HCF of 12 and 24?
recs.facts: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3, so the common factors give 2 x 2 x 3 = 12.
recs.rel: When one number divides the other, the smaller number is the HCF.

recs.q: Where was the headquarters of the Western European Union (WEU), now dissolved?
recs.facts: The WEU had its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
recs.rel: The WEU ended its operations in 2011 after its functions passed to the European Union.

recs.q: What is the commonly quoted height of Mount Sakesar, the highest peak of the Salt Range?
recs.facts: Mount Sakesar, in district Khushab, is about 4,992 feet (1,522 m) high and is the highest point of the Salt Range.
recs.rel: Some sources give about 1,525 m (5,003 ft), so sources differ slightly.

recs.q: In which direction was the Hijrat of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) made?
recs.facts: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib) to escape the persecution of the Quraish.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar begins from this migration.

recs.q: Which major expedition of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took place in 9 Hijri?
recs.facts: The Ghazwa of Tabuk against the Byzantines took place in Rajab 9 AH. This year is also known as the Year of Delegations.
recs.rel: Tabuk was the last Ghazwa in which the Prophet (PBUH) personally led the army.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa of Hunain fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Hunain was fought against the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif in Shawwal 8 AH, soon after the Conquest of Makkah.
recs.rel: The Muslims were first pushed back by an ambush but then won the battle.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 6 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 2 x 4 = 8 years now, so the age gap is 4 years. When Ali is 6, sister is 6 + 4 = 10 years.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people stays the same over time.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 8 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 years now, so the gap is 8 years. When Ali is 8, sister is 8 + 8 = 16 years.
recs.rel: Multiplying the new age by 3 (24) is a common mistake, as the gap stays fixed.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 6 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 4 x 4 = 16 years now, so the gap is 12 years. When Ali is 6, sister is 6 + 12 = 18 years.
recs.rel: The age gap never changes as both get older at the same rate.

recs.q: The Himalaya mountain range lies between the Indian subcontinent and which plateau?
recs.facts: The Himalayas separate the Indian plain (India, Nepal, Bhutan) in the south from the Tibetan Plateau of China in the north.
recs.rel: The range crosses five countries: Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and China.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the Hindu Kush mountain range?
recs.facts: The Hindu Kush extends about 800 km (500 miles) from central Afghanistan to northern Pakistan.
recs.rel: Tirich Mir (7,708 m) is its highest peak.

recs.q: Which is different from the rest: Kangaroo, Horse, Deer, Cow?
recs.facts: The horse, deer and cow are all hoofed land mammals, while the kangaroo is a marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.
recs.rel: Kangaroos are native to Australia.

recs.q: Which is different from the rest: Donkey, Zebra, Horse, Giraffe?
recs.facts: Donkey, zebra and horse all belong to the horse family (Equidae), while the giraffe belongs to a different family.
recs.rel: The giraffe is the tallest land animal.

recs.q: What was the relationship between Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah (AS). He was the younger brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

recs.q: Find the value of i(-2i + 3), where i is the imaginary unit.
recs.facts: Multiply out: i(-2i + 3) = -2i squared + 3i. Since i squared = -1, this is 2 + 3i.
recs.rel: The imaginary unit i is defined by i squared = -1.

recs.q: What is the imaginary part of the complex number 3 + 9i?
recs.facts: In the form a + bi the imaginary part is b. Here b = 9.
recs.rel: The real part of 3 + 9i is 3.

recs.q: What does IMF stand for?
recs.facts: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund. It is a UN-linked financial institution that supports global monetary cooperation.
recs.rel: The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and is headquartered in Washington DC.

recs.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
recs.facts: Jawaharlal Nehru became India's first Prime Minister on 15 August 1947 and served until 1964.
recs.rel: Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second Prime Minister of India.

recs.q: On which date did India's Constituent Assembly adopt the Constitution of India?
recs.facts: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Indian Constitution on 26 November 1949. It came into force on 26 January 1950.
recs.rel: India celebrates 26 January as Republic Day.

recs.q: On which river is the Bhakra Dam of India built?
recs.facts: The Bhakra Dam is built on the Sutlej River in Himachal Pradesh, India. It forms the Gobind Sagar reservoir.
recs.rel: The Sutlej was allotted to India under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.

recs.q: Which institution is responsible for distributing river water among the provinces of Pakistan?
recs.facts: IRSA was set up in 1992 under the Water Apportionment Accord of 1991 to distribute Indus system water among the provinces. WAPDA builds and runs dams and power projects.
recs.rel: The Water Apportionment Accord was signed in 1991 by the four provinces.

recs.q: What does integration (definite integral) of a function show geometrically?
recs.facts: A definite integral gives the area between the curve and the x-axis over an interval. Slope is given by differentiation.
recs.rel: Integration is the reverse process of differentiation.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN Human Rights)?
recs.facts: The OHCHR (UN Human Rights) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. The UN Human Rights Council also meets in Geneva.
recs.rel: The UN Headquarters itself is in New York.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) according to the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Surah Al-An'am names Ibrahim's father as Azar. Some scholars say Tarikh (Terah) was his given name, so sources differ.
recs.rel: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah, the friend of Allah.

recs.q: In which year was the first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, introduced?
recs.facts: The Penny Black was issued in Britain on 1 May 1840 and was the world's first adhesive postage stamp. It was introduced by the postal reformer Rowland Hill.
recs.rel: Sindh Dak, issued in 1852 in Sindh, was the first postage stamp of the subcontinent.

recs.q: In which year was the company Google founded?
recs.facts: Google was incorporated by Larry Page and Sergey Brin on 4 September 1998. The search project began earlier in 1996 at Stanford University.
recs.rel: Candidates often say 1996 because the BackRub research project started that year.

recs.q: In which year was WhatsApp founded?
recs.facts: WhatsApp was founded in 2009 by Jan Koum and Brian Acton. It started as a status-update app and soon became a messaging service.
recs.rel: Facebook (now Meta) bought WhatsApp in 2014.

recs.q: In which year was YouTube founded?
recs.facts: YouTube was founded in February 2005 by Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim. The first video was uploaded in April 2005.
recs.rel: Google bought YouTube in 2006.

recs.q: Who is credited with inventing the first compound microscope?
recs.facts: The Dutch spectacle maker Zacharias Janssen is generally credited with the first compound microscope around 1590. Other inventors are sometimes named.
recs.rel: Robert Hooke published Micrographia in 1665 and coined the word cell.

recs.q: Who invented the telephone?
recs.facts: Alexander Graham Bell was granted the first US patent for the telephone in 1876. He is credited as its inventor.
recs.rel: Bell's first successful call was made to his assistant Thomas Watson in 1876.

recs.q: What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Iran border?
recs.facts: The Pakistan-Iran border is commonly given as about 909 km. It separates Balochistan from Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province.
recs.rel: Some sources give about 959 km, so figures differ slightly by source.

recs.q: What is the currency of Ireland?
recs.facts: Ireland is a member of the Eurozone and uses the euro. It replaced the Irish pound in 2002.
recs.rel: The euro notes and coins entered circulation on 1 January 2002.

recs.q: The M-1 motorway connects Islamabad with which city?
recs.facts: The M-1 (Peshawar-Islamabad Motorway) links Peshawar with Islamabad. It is about 155 km long.
recs.rel: The M-2 motorway connects Islamabad with Lahore.

recs.q: In which Islamic month was Pakistan established in 1947?
recs.facts: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramadan 1366 AH. It was the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) by common belief.
recs.rel: It was also a Friday, the blessed day of the week.

recs.q: What is the currency of Israel?
recs.facts: Israel's currency is the New Israeli Shekel (ILS). It was introduced in 1985.
recs.rel: The Israeli currency symbol is the sign for the shekel.

recs.q: Which angel is the guardian of the gate of Jannah (Paradise)?
recs.facts: Ridwan is the angel in charge of Jannah according to Islamic belief. Malik is the keeper of Jahannam.
recs.rel: Jannah is said to have eight gates.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word Jannat?
recs.facts: Jannat comes from the Arabic root meaning to hide or cover. It literally means a garden with dense trees.
recs.rel: The Quran uses the word Jannah for Paradise.

recs.q: Jeddah is a famous port city of which country?
recs.facts: Jeddah is on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia. It is the main gateway for pilgrims travelling to Makkah.
recs.rel: Jeddah is the second largest city of Saudi Arabia after Riyadh.

recs.q: On which prophet did the angel Hazrat Jibrael (AS) bring the final revelation, the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jibrael (AS) brought the Holy Quran to the last Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), over about 23 years. The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.
recs.rel: Jibrael (AS) is also called Ruh-ul-Amin and brought revelation to earlier prophets as well.

recs.q: On which date of the Islamic calendar did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
recs.facts: Hazrat Imam Hussain (RA) and his companions were martyred at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH (October 680 CE), the day of Ashura.
recs.rel: The tragedy took place during the rule of the Umayyad ruler Yazid.

recs.q: Who is known as the conqueror of Khaibar (Khyber)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) led the final assault and conquered the fort of Qamus at Khaibar in 7 AH, so he is called Fateh-e-Khaibar.
recs.rel: He is also known as Haidar-e-Karrar and Asadullah.

recs.q: The Khilafat Movement in India arose mainly because of which event?
opts: The defeat of the Ottoman Empire in the First World War and the threat to the Caliphate
recs.facts: After the First World War the Allies defeated Turkey and threatened the Ottoman Caliph, so Indian Muslims launched the movement to save the Caliphate.
recs.rel: The Nehru Report (1928) came years after the Khilafat Movement (1919-1924).

recs.q: Who led the Muslim army in the Battle of Khyber?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought against the Jews of Khyber and the Muslim army was led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself.
recs.rel: The main fort Qamus was conquered at the hands of Hazrat Ali (RA).

recs.q: In mathematics, subtraction is which kind of operator?
recs.facts: Subtraction needs two operands (a - b), so it is a binary arithmetic operator.
recs.rel: The minus sign used with one number, as in -5, acts as a unary operator.

recs.q: Sikandar (Alexander the Great) was the king of which land?
recs.facts: Alexander the Great was king of Macedonia, a kingdom in northern Greece, and invaded India in 326 BC.
recs.rel: He fought King Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) in present-day Pakistan.

recs.q: Which country is known as the land of golden fibre?
recs.facts: Jute is called the golden fibre because of its golden colour and high value, and Bangladesh is the world's leading producer of it. So Bangladesh is called the land of golden fibre.
recs.rel: Bangladesh was East Pakistan until 1971.

recs.q: Who was appointed as the first commander of the Muslim army in the Battle of Mu'tah?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Zayd bin Haritha as commander, with Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib and Hazrat Abdullah bin Rawaha next in line. After all three were martyred, Hazrat Khalid bin Walid took command.
recs.rel: The Battle of Mu'tah was fought in 8 AH against the Byzantine forces.

recs.q: Who founded the All India Muslim League in 1906 at Dhaka, hosting the meeting where it was formed?
recs.facts: The All India Muslim League was formed on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka at a meeting hosted by Nawab Khwaja Salimullah of Dhaka. Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk were also prominent in its formation.
recs.rel: Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was its first president.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: a, c, d, f, ...?
recs.facts: The positions are 1, 3, 4, 6 and the steps alternate +2 and +1. After 6 the step is +1, giving position 7, which is g.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: A3, C5, E7, G9, ?
recs.facts: The letters skip one each time (A, C, E, G, I) and the numbers go up by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So the next term is I11.
recs.rel: Letters moving by two places each step are a common pattern in verbal reasoning.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: z1, x3, v5, ?
recs.facts: The letters go backwards skipping one (z, x, v, t) and the numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7). So the next term is t7.
recs.rel: z is the 26th letter, x the 24th, v the 22nd and t the 20th.

recs.q: Rearranging the letters AGREMYN gives the name of which country?
recs.facts: The letters A, G, R, E, M, Y, N can be arranged to spell GERMANY, using all seven letters exactly once.
recs.rel: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

recs.q: Which is the largest flower in the world?
recs.facts: Rafflesia arnoldii, found in the rainforests of Indonesia, has the largest single flower, which can be about one metre across.
recs.rel: It has no leaves, stems or roots and is a parasite on vines.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: All his friends laughed at him.
opts: He was laughed at by all his friends.
He is laughed at by all his friends.
He had laughed at all his friends.
All his friends were laughed at by him.
recs.facts: The sentence is in simple past tense, so the passive uses was or were with the past participle. The object him becomes the subject he, giving He was laughed at by all his friends.
recs.rel: Phrasal verbs such as laugh at keep their preposition in the passive voice.

recs.q: I want a book ___ is not in the library. Fill in the blank.
recs.facts: A relative pronoun for a thing is which, so it correctly links to the book. Who and whom are used for people.
recs.rel: That can also be used here in place of which.

recs.q: Is x = 3y + 1 a linear equation?
opts: Yes, it is linear in x and y
No, because it has a constant
No, because it has two variables
recs.facts: Each variable appears only with power 1 and there are no products of variables, so it is a linear equation in two variables. Its graph is a straight line.
recs.rel: A linear equation always has degree 1.

recs.q: In which month and year did the last US troops leave Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The final US military flights left Kabul airport on 30 August 2021 (31 August in Kabul), ending a war of about twenty years. The Taliban had taken Kabul on 15 August 2021.
recs.rel: The US-led invasion of Afghanistan began in October 2001.

recs.q: What is the value of log 2 + log 8 (same base)?
recs.facts: By the product rule, log a + log b = log (a x b). So log 2 + log 8 = log 16.
recs.rel: Also log 16 = 4 log 2, because 16 = 2 to the power 4.

recs.q: What is the value of log 8 divided by log 4?
recs.facts: log 8 = 3 log 2 and log 4 = 2 log 2. So the ratio is 3 log 2 / 2 log 2 = 3/2.
recs.rel: The ratio of two logs of the same base does not depend on the base chosen.

recs.q: Which country has the longest sea coastline in the world?
recs.facts: Canada has the longest coastline of any country, more than 200,000 km including its islands.
recs.rel: Indonesia, Russia and Australia are usually listed after Canada.

recs.q: In a class of 30 students, 20 are male. What percentage of the students are female?
recs.facts: Females = 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage = 10 / 30 x 100 = 33.33%.
recs.rel: Males make up 66.67% of this class.

recs.q: What is the capital of the Maldives?
recs.facts: Male is the capital and most populous city of the Maldives.
recs.rel: The Maldives is an island nation in the Indian Ocean.

recs.q: What is the currency of the Maldives?
recs.facts: The Maldivian currency is the rufiyaa.
recs.rel: Taka is the currency of Bangladesh and ngultrum is the currency of Bhutan.

recs.q: Who invented the printing press with movable type in Europe?
recs.facts: Johannes Gutenberg of Germany invented the movable-type printing press around 1440.
recs.rel: His first major printed work was the Gutenberg Bible.

recs.q: Which Caliph had copies of the Holy Quran prepared and sent to the major cities of the Islamic state?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA) had the Quran written in one standard dialect and sent copies to cities such as Kufa, Basra, Damascus and Makkah.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman (RA) is therefore called Jame-ul-Quran.

recs.q: What is the name of the native people who live in the highlands of Guatemala?
recs.facts: The Maya people form a large part of the population of the Guatemalan highlands and still speak Mayan languages.
recs.rel: The ancient Maya civilization also built great cities in Guatemala such as Tikal.

recs.q: What is the magnetic field outside an ideal long solenoid?
recs.facts: In an ideal long solenoid the field is uniform inside and almost zero outside, because the fields of the turns cancel there.
recs.rel: The field inside a solenoid is B = mu0 n I.

recs.q: What is the SI unit of magnetic induction (magnetic flux density)?
recs.facts: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla, which equals one weber per square metre.
recs.rel: Gauss is a smaller non-SI unit, with 1 tesla equal to 10,000 gauss.

recs.q: Which of the following is the meaning of the word marginal?
recs.facts: Marginal means small, slight or of minor importance, or relating to an edge or margin. A marginal gain is therefore a very small gain.
recs.rel: The word comes from the Latin word margo, meaning edge.

recs.q: Who was the President of Pakistan when the first martial law was imposed in 1958?
recs.facts: Iskander Mirza was President and he himself declared martial law on 7 October 1958 by abrogating the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan was Army chief and became the Chief Martial Law Administrator.
recs.rel: Mirza was forced out within three weeks and later went into exile in London.

recs.q: Who gave the atomic theory of matter in the early nineteenth century?
recs.facts: John Dalton proposed in 1803 that matter is made of tiny indivisible particles called atoms, with atoms of one element being alike. This is called Dalton's atomic theory.
recs.rel: Rutherford later discovered the nucleus and Bohr gave the planetary model of the atom.

recs.q: What is the median of 2, 3, 5, 4, 7?
recs.facts: Arrange in order: 2, 3, 4, 5, 7. With five values the middle (third) value is 4.
recs.rel: The mean of these numbers is 4.2, which is different from the median.

recs.q: What is the median of the series 2, 4, 6, 7, 9?
recs.facts: The numbers are already in order and there are five of them, so the middle (third) value is 6.
recs.rel: The mean is 28 / 5 = 5.6, which differs from the median.

recs.q: What is the meaning of deceit?
recs.facts: Deceit means the act of deceiving, that is, cheating or misleading someone by dishonest behaviour.
recs.rel: Its opposite is honesty.

recs.q: What is the meaning of disconnect?
opts: To break the connection or separate
recs.facts: Disconnect means to detach or break the link between two things, for example to cut off a phone line.
recs.rel: Its opposite is connect.

recs.q: What is the meaning of emancipate?
recs.facts: Emancipate means to free someone from legal, social or political restrictions, for example from slavery.
recs.rel: The Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 declared slaves in the Confederate states free in the USA.

recs.q: What is the meaning of mirth?
recs.facts: Mirth means joyful amusement, especially when shown by laughter.
recs.rel: Its synonyms are merriment and gaiety.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word geminate?
opts: To double or arrange in pairs
recs.facts: Geminate means to double something or to occur in pairs. It comes from the Latin gemini, meaning twins.
recs.rel: In linguistics a geminate is a doubled consonant sound.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the name Anas?
recs.facts: The Arabic name Anas means affection, friendliness or companionship. Hazrat Anas bin Malik (RA) was a famous servant and companion of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Anas bin Malik narrated over two thousand hadiths.

recs.q: In which country was the company Microsoft founded?
recs.facts: Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in 1975 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA. It later moved to Redmond, Washington.
recs.rel: Microsoft is best known for the Windows operating system and Microsoft Office.

recs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in 570 AD and migrated in 622 AD, which is commonly given as 53 years of age in Pakistani textbooks.
recs.rel: Some sources say 52 years because of differences in counting the years.

recs.q: For which purpose is the Nishan-e-Haider awarded in the Pakistan Armed Forces?
recs.facts: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award of Pakistan. It is given for extraordinary bravery in the face of the enemy.
recs.rel: Captain Raja Aziz Bhatti was among the recipients, for the 1965 war.

recs.q: Under which ministry do the Pakistan Army, Navy and Air Force work?
recs.facts: The three armed services work under the Ministry of Defence, which handles their administrative and policy matters.
recs.rel: The Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee works for coordination among the services.

recs.q: Under which federal ministry does the national food department fall in Pakistan?
opts: Ministry of National Food Security and Research
recs.facts: Food policy, wheat and crop matters are handled by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research.
recs.rel: The ministry was earlier called the Ministry of Food and Agriculture.

recs.q: What is the range of Pakistan's Ra'ad-II cruise missile?
recs.facts: Ra'ad-II is an air-launched cruise missile with a range of about 600 km. It is a nuclear capable weapon.
recs.rel: The original Ra'ad (Hatf-VIII) has a range of 350 km.

recs.q: What is the mode of the digits 7, 7, 7, 9, 9, 8, 8, 1, 0?
recs.facts: The mode is the value that occurs most often. The digit 7 appears three times, 9 and 8 twice each.
recs.rel: A data set can have more than one mode if values tie for the highest count.

recs.q: What is the mode of the digits 8, 5, 8, 7, 6, 5, 7, 8, 3, 8?
recs.facts: The digit 8 appears four times, 5 and 7 twice each, and 6 and 3 once. So the mode is 8.
recs.rel: Mean, median and mode are the three measures of central tendency.

recs.q: Which are the first and the last months of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
recs.facts: The Hijri year begins with Muharram and ends with Dhul Hijjah (Zil Hajj), the month of Hajj.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar starts from the migration of the Prophet (PBUH) to Madina in 622 AD.

recs.q: What was the main feature of the Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909?
opts: Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims
recs.facts: The Indian Councils Act 1909 (Minto-Morley Reforms) gave Muslims the right to elect their own representatives through separate electorates.
recs.rel: The reforms are named after Lord Minto (Viceroy) and John Morley (Secretary of State for India).

recs.q: The Faisal Mosque in Islamabad was designed by which architect?
recs.facts: The Faisal Mosque was designed by the Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay and its design is inspired by a Bedouin tent.
recs.rel: It was funded by the Saudi king Faisal bin Abdulaziz and is named after him.

recs.q: What is the motto of the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: The motto of the Pakistan Army is Iman, Taqwa, Jihad fi Sabilillah (Faith, Piety, Struggle in the way of Allah).
recs.rel: Faith, Unity, Discipline is the motto given by Quaid-e-Azam to the nation.

recs.q: In which country is Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in its range and home of the gods in myth, located?
recs.facts: Mount Olympus is located in northern Greece and is its highest mountain.
recs.rel: In Greek mythology it was the home of the twelve Olympian gods.

recs.q: Table Mountain, a famous flat-topped mountain, is located near which city?
recs.facts: Table Mountain overlooks the city of Cape Town in South Africa.
recs.rel: It is one of the New7Wonders of Nature.

recs.q: What was the Faraizi Movement?
opts: A religious reform movement among the Muslims of Bengal
A political party of the Hindus
recs.facts: The Faraizi Movement was started in Bengal by Haji Shariatullah to make Muslims follow the faraiz (obligations) of Islam and give up un-Islamic customs.
recs.rel: After Haji Shariatullah the movement was led by his son Dudu Miyan.

recs.q: Ali walks 10 km north, then turns left and then turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
recs.facts: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west; a right turn from west brings him back to face north.
recs.rel: A left turn followed by a right turn cancels out.

recs.q: Which was the first James Bond film?
recs.facts: Dr. No, released in 1962 with Sean Connery, was the first James Bond film.
recs.rel: James Bond was created by the writer Ian Fleming.

recs.q: What is 4x multiplied by 4x, plus 2x multiplied by 4x?
recs.facts: 4x times 4x = 16 x squared, and 2x times 4x = 8 x squared. Their sum is 24 x squared.
recs.rel: When multiplying terms, the coefficients are multiplied and the powers of x are added.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: The man was charged ___ murder.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is 'charged with' a crime.
recs.rel: 'Accused of' is also correct, but 'charged' takes the preposition 'with'.

recs.q: Why did Allah send Hazrat Musa (AS) to Pharaoh (Firaun)?
opts: To invite him to Allah and demand freedom for Bani Israel
To fight a war against him
recs.facts: Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent to call Pharaoh to worship one Allah and to free Bani Israel from slavery.
recs.rel: His brother Hazrat Harun (AS) was sent with him to help.

recs.q: To which place did the Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD (13 Nabawi)?
recs.facts: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib).
recs.rel: This migration (Hijrat) is the start of the Hijri calendar.

recs.q: What gift did Allah give to the Prophet (PBUH) during the Miraj?
recs.facts: During the Miraj the five daily prayers (Salah) were made obligatory for Muslims.
recs.rel: Salah is the only pillar of Islam that was given directly in the heavens.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan is Nanga Parbat located?
recs.facts: Nanga Parbat lies in the Diamer district of Gilgit-Baltistan, in the western part of the Himalayas.
recs.rel: It is known as the Killer Mountain because of the many climbers who died on it early on.

recs.q: Who was Napoleon Bonaparte?
opts: A French military leader and Emperor
recs.facts: Napoleon Bonaparte rose through the French army and made himself Emperor of France in 1804.
recs.rel: He was exiled to the island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

recs.q: Change the narration into indirect speech: He said, "He was playing football."
opts: He said that he is playing football.
He said that he had been playing football.
He said that he was play football.
He said that he will be playing football.
recs.facts: The reporting verb is in the past tense, so the past continuous in the direct speech becomes the past perfect continuous in indirect speech.
recs.rel: In indirect speech the past simple usually becomes the past perfect.

recs.q: What is the full form of NASA?
recs.facts: NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration, the space agency of the United States.
recs.rel: NASA was founded in 1958 and is headquartered in Washington, D.C.

recs.q: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is a specialized agency of which organization?
recs.facts: The FAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that deals with food and agriculture.
recs.rel: World Food Day is observed on 16 October, the day the FAO was founded.

recs.q: What is the nearest meaning of the word purify?
recs.facts: To purify means to remove impurities, which is the same as to cleanse.
recs.rel: The opposite of purify is contaminate or pollute.

recs.q: Which is the nearest star to the Sun?
recs.facts: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light years away, which makes it the nearest star to the Sun.
recs.rel: Proxima Centauri is part of the Alpha Centauri star system.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word never?
recs.facts: Never means at no time, so its opposite is always, meaning at all times.
recs.rel: Seldom, rarely and hardly are only partial negatives, not exact opposites.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Did you see the ____ news?
recs.facts: The adjective latest means most recent and correctly describes the noun news.
recs.rel: Lately is an adverb, so it cannot modify a noun.

recs.q: Which was the first Urdu newspaper of the subcontinent?
recs.facts: Jam-i-Jahan-Numa was started in Calcutta in 1822 and is generally regarded as the first Urdu newspaper.
recs.rel: Some sources name Delhi Urdu Akhbar of 1836 as an early paper, so sources differ.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: 6/12, 15/21, 25/31, 36/42, ?
recs.facts: The numerators 6, 15, 25, 36 increase by 9, 10, 11, so the next is 36 + 12 = 48. The denominators 12, 21, 31, 42 follow the same steps, so the next is 42 + 12 = 54.
recs.rel: Both parts of each fraction differ by 6.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: 1Z, 2X, 3V, ?
recs.facts: The numbers go up by 1 (1, 2, 3, 4). The letters go back by 2 (Z, X, V, T).
recs.rel: Letter positions here are 26, 24, 22, 20.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 12, 15, 18, ?
recs.facts: Each number increases by 3, so 18 + 3 = 21.
recs.rel: This is an arithmetic progression with common difference 3.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 17, 55, 27, 65, 37, 75, ?
recs.facts: There are two interleaved series: 17, 27, 37 (add 10) and 55, 65, 75 (add 10). The next term is from the first series, 37 + 10 = 47.
recs.rel: The term after 47 would be 85.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 3, 5, 7, 9, ?
recs.facts: The numbers are consecutive odd numbers, increasing by 2, so 9 + 2 = 11.
recs.rel: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 4, 8, 16, 32, ?
recs.facts: Each number is double the previous one, so 32 times 2 = 64.
recs.rel: This is a geometric progression with common ratio 2.

recs.q: Which term comes next in the series: A3, C5, F8, J13, ?
recs.facts: The letters move forward by 2, 3, 4, 5 (A, C, F, J, O). The numbers 3, 5, 8, 13 add 2, 3, 5, so the next is 13 + 8 = 21.
recs.rel: The number part follows a Fibonacci-like pattern.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: I bought a new shirt last night.
opts: A new shirt was bought by me last night.
A new shirt is bought by me last night.
A new shirt had bought by me last night.
A new shirt has been bought by me last night.
recs.facts: The past simple active becomes was or were plus the past participle, so the object becomes the subject: A new shirt was bought by me last night.
recs.rel: In passive voice the doer is introduced by the word by.

recs.q: 13, 15 and 17 are what type of numbers?
recs.facts: Each number differs from the next by 2 and none is divisible by 2, so they are consecutive odd numbers.
recs.rel: The only even prime number is 2.

recs.q: On whom is Namaz (the five daily prayers) obligatory?
recs.facts: Salah is farz on every Muslim who is sane and has reached puberty, man or woman, apart from times such as menstruation for women.
recs.rel: Children are advised to start praying at about age seven.

recs.q: What does OGDC stand for?
recs.facts: OGDC stands for Oil and Gas Development Company Limited, Pakistan's state-owned oil and gas exploration company.
recs.rel: OGDCL is listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange.

recs.q: Which name is commonly used as the old (popular) name of the Netherlands?
recs.facts: The Netherlands is popularly called Holland, after its two western provinces North Holland and South Holland. The official name is the Netherlands.
recs.rel: Strictly, Holland is only a region of the country, and the capital of the Netherlands is Amsterdam.

recs.q: Which is the only even prime number?
recs.facts: A prime number has exactly two factors. Every even number greater than 2 is divisible by 2, so it has more than two factors, which leaves 2 as the only even prime.
recs.rel: The number 1 is not a prime number.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word cruel?
recs.facts: Cruel means causing pain or suffering without pity. Its opposite is kind, meaning gentle and caring.
recs.rel: Merciful and compassionate are also antonyms of cruel.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word precede?
recs.facts: To precede means to come before something. Its opposite is to follow, which means to come after.
recs.rel: The noun form of precede is precedence, and the word proceed is a different word.

recs.q: What is the order of the matrix [1 2]?
recs.facts: The matrix has one row and two columns. Order is written as rows x columns, so it is 1 x 2.
recs.rel: A matrix with only one row is called a row matrix.

recs.q: The game of polo is believed to have originated in which country?
recs.facts: Polo began as a horseback game in ancient Persia and Central Asia. It later spread to India and then to Britain.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact origin, but Persia is the answer in most textbooks.

recs.q: Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, Abbottabad?
recs.facts: Karachi, Lahore and Peshawar are the capitals of Sindh, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Abbottabad is not a provincial capital.
recs.rel: Abbottabad is the home city of the Pakistan Military Academy at Kakul.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word pacify?
recs.facts: To pacify means to calm or quieten. Its opposite is to agitate, meaning to disturb or excite.
recs.rel: Provoke and anger are also opposites of pacify.

recs.q: If 5 men write 5 papers in 5 minutes, how many papers will 100 men write in 100 minutes?
recs.facts: One man writes 1 paper in 5 minutes. In 100 minutes one man writes 100 / 5 = 20 papers, so 100 men write 100 x 20 = 2000 papers.
recs.rel: In rate problems, first find the work done by one person in one unit of time.

recs.q: Who signed the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 on behalf of India?
recs.facts: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan. The Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated.
recs.rel: Shastri died in Tashkent a few hours after signing the declaration.

recs.q: Which charged particles carry the electric current in a metal wire?
recs.facts: In metals the outer electrons are loosely bound and move freely. Their flow under a potential difference is the electric current.
recs.rel: The conventional direction of current is opposite to the actual flow of electrons.

recs.q: A train has 30 people and 1/3 of them are men. How many are women?
recs.rel: Women form 2/3 of the people, which is about 66.67 percent.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: There is no ____ for more passengers in this compartment.
recs.facts: Here room means space, so there is no space for more passengers. The other words have different meanings.
recs.rel: Room is an uncountable noun when it means space.

recs.q: A train travels at 60 km per hour. How much time will it take to cover 3 km?
recs.facts: Speed is 60 km per hour, which is 1 km per minute. So 3 km takes 3 minutes.
recs.rel: 60 km per hour equals 1 km per minute, a handy conversion.

recs.q: In which Islamic month is Hajj performed?
recs.facts: Hajj rites are performed from the 8th to the 12th or 13th of Dhul Hijjah, the last month of the Islamic calendar.
recs.rel: Eid-ul-Adha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word perpetual?
recs.facts: Perpetual means lasting forever. Its opposite is temporary (transitory), which lasts only for a short time.
recs.rel: Eternal, endless and constant are synonyms of perpetual.

recs.q: According to the Ahadith, what is said about a person who eats his fill while his neighbour sleeps hungry?
opts: He is not a true believer
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that he is not a believer who eats his fill while his neighbour goes hungry by his side. This stresses the rights of neighbours.
recs.rel: Islam gives great importance to the rights of neighbours.

recs.q: Book is to cover as picture is to what?
recs.facts: A cover goes around and protects a book, in the same way a frame goes around and holds a picture.
recs.rel: Analogy questions depend on finding the relation between the first pair and applying it to the second.

recs.q: What type of image is formed on a photographic film by the lens of a camera?
recs.facts: A camera lens is a convex lens that forms a real, inverted image on the film or sensor. A real image can be captured on a screen or film.
recs.rel: A virtual image cannot be projected on a screen, for example the image in a plane mirror.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Pindi, Lahore, Karachi, Quetta, Peshawar.
recs.facts: Lahore, Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar are the capitals of the four provinces of Pakistan, while Pindi (Rawalpindi) is not a provincial capital.
recs.rel: Rawalpindi is the neighbour of Islamabad and hosts the General Headquarters of the Pakistan Army.

recs.q: What is the locus of a point in a plane that stays at a fixed distance from a fixed point called?
recs.facts: All points at the same distance from a fixed point (the centre) in a plane form a circle. The fixed distance is the radius.
recs.rel: The locus of a point equidistant from two fixed points is the perpendicular bisector of the line joining them.

recs.q: What is transpiration in plants?
opts: Loss of water vapour from the aerial parts, mainly leaves
recs.facts: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mostly through the stomata of leaves.
recs.rel: Transpiration helps pull water and minerals up from the roots and cools the plant.

recs.q: Which Indian province was first taken over by the British East India Company after the Battle of Plassey (1757)?
recs.facts: After defeating Siraj ud Daula at Plassey, the Company gained control of Bengal, and Mir Jafar was placed on the throne as a puppet.
recs.rel: The Company got the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa after the Battle of Buxar in 1764.

recs.q: What is the highest point on the surface of the Earth above sea level?
recs.facts: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal and China border, is about 8849 metres high and is the highest point above sea level.
recs.rel: K2 in Pakistan is the second highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: What is the distance between the points (4, 0) and (0, 3)?
recs.facts: Distance = square root of ((4 - 0)^2 + (0 - 3)^2) = square root of (16 + 9) = square root of 25 = 5.
recs.rel: The points (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3) form a 3-4-5 right-angled triangle.

recs.q: Ali is poor ___ he is honest.
recs.facts: The sentence joins two contrasting ideas, poverty and honesty, so the conjunction but is needed.
recs.rel: But, yet and however are used to show contrast.

recs.q: What is the approximate population of China in 2026?
recs.facts: China has about 1.41 billion people in 2026 according to current estimates, and its population is slowly falling.
recs.rel: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023.

recs.q: What is the approximate total population of the world in 2026?
recs.facts: World population passed 8 billion in November 2022 and is about 8.2 billion in 2026.
recs.rel: The world population was about 7.8 billion in 2020.

recs.q: Which is the sixth most populous country in the world in 2026?
recs.facts: The ranking is India, China, USA, Indonesia, Pakistan and then Nigeria, with about 240 million people.
recs.rel: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, with about 259 million people.

recs.q: Where is Bin Qasim Port located?
recs.facts: Port Qasim is a deep-sea port on the coast near Karachi in Sindh. It is the second busiest port of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Port Qasim was named after Muhammad bin Qasim and began operating in 1980.

recs.q: The inverse of which type of matrix does not exist?
recs.facts: A matrix has an inverse only if its determinant is not zero. A singular matrix has determinant zero, so it has no inverse.
recs.rel: A square matrix with a non-zero determinant is called non-singular or invertible.

recs.q: What is an equation of degree (highest power) one called?
recs.facts: An equation whose highest power of the variable is 1 is a linear equation, for example 2x + 3 = 7.
recs.rel: A quadratic equation has degree 2 and a cubic equation has degree 3.

recs.q: After the Battle of Uhud, whose funeral prayer did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) lead repeatedly along with the other martyrs?
recs.facts: Reports say the Prophet (PBUH) led the funeral prayer of his uncle Hazrat Hamza (RA) and the other martyrs of Uhud.
recs.rel: Hazrat Hamza (RA) is titled Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, and details of the prayers differ between narrations.

recs.q: Which of the following is a prime number: 25, 15, 30, 29?
recs.facts: 25 = 5 x 5, 15 = 3 x 5 and 30 is even, so they are composite. 29 has no divisor other than 1 and itself.
recs.rel: 2 is the only even prime number.

recs.q: What is the probability of getting an odd number when a fair die is rolled once?
recs.facts: The odd numbers are 1, 3 and 5, which is 3 outcomes out of 6, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
recs.rel: The probability of any event always lies between 0 and 1.

recs.q: What is the product of 0.02 x 0.1?
recs.facts: 2 x 1 = 2, and there are 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places in total, so the answer is 0.002.
recs.rel: Multiplying by 0.1 is the same as dividing by 10.

recs.q: Two matrices A and B can be added only if they have:
opts: The same number of rows and columns (same order)
Only the same number of rows
Only the same number of columns
recs.facts: Matrices are added entry by entry, so both must have the same order, meaning equal rows and equal columns.
recs.rel: Matrix multiplication needs columns of the first to equal rows of the second.

recs.q: Who was the first President of India?
recs.facts: Dr Rajendra Prasad became India's first President in January 1950.
recs.rel: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

recs.q: What does the word predominant mean?
recs.facts: Predominant means having the greatest influence or being the most noticeable.
recs.rel: Its noun form is predominance.

recs.q: To which tribe did Muhammad bin Qasim belong?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim was born in Taif and belonged to the Banu Thaqif tribe. He conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD.
recs.rel: He was a nephew of the Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf, who also belonged to Thaqif.

recs.q: What is a scalar quantity?
opts: A quantity with magnitude only and no direction
A quantity with both magnitude and direction
A quantity that is always constant
recs.facts: A scalar is fully described by its magnitude (size) alone. Examples are mass, time, speed and temperature.
recs.rel: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity or force, is called a vector.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 1/10 of 9?
recs.facts: 1/10 of 9 = 0.9. A quarter of 0.9 = 0.9 divided by 4 = 0.225.
recs.rel: A quarter of a number means dividing it by 4.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 90?
recs.facts: A quarter of 90 = 90 divided by 4 = 22.5.
recs.rel: A quarter equals 25%, so 25% of 90 is also 22.5.

recs.q: What is the quarter of 9?
recs.facts: A quarter of 9 = 9 divided by 4 = 2.25.
recs.rel: Half of 9 is 4.5, and half of that is 2.25.

recs.q: What was the old name of Quetta?
recs.facts: Quetta was historically known as Shal or Shalkot. The name Quetta comes from the word Kwatkot, meaning fort.
recs.rel: Quetta is the capital of Balochistan and is called the Fruit Garden of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the antonym of radiant?
recs.facts: Radiant means shining brightly, so its opposite is dull, which means lacking brightness.
recs.rel: Radiant also describes a person who looks very happy, as in a radiant smile.

recs.q: What is the meaning of radiant?
recs.facts: Radiant means sending out light or shining brightly. It can also mean glowing with joy.
recs.rel: The word comes from the Latin radiare, meaning to emit rays.

recs.q: What is the radius of the incircle of a triangle called?
recs.facts: The circle drawn inside a triangle touching all three sides is the incircle, and its radius is called the inradius. The circumradius belongs to the circle through all three vertices.
recs.rel: For a triangle, inradius = Area divided by semi-perimeter.

recs.q: In which year was Choudhry Rahmat Ali, who coined the name Pakistan, born?
recs.facts: Choudhry Rahmat Ali was born on 16 November 1897 in Balachaur, Punjab. He coined the name Pakistan in 1933.
recs.rel: He died in Cambridge, England, in February 1951.

recs.q: In the ratio X:Y, what is the first term X called?
recs.facts: In a ratio the first term is called the antecedent and the second term is called the consequent. So X is the antecedent.
recs.rel: A ratio with two equal ratios forming an equation is called a proportion.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number 1 - 2i?
recs.facts: In a + bi, the real part is a. For 1 - 2i the real part is 1 and the imaginary part is -2.
recs.rel: The symbol i represents the square root of minus one, so i squared equals -1.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 - 4i?
recs.facts: In a + bi, the real part is a. For 6 - 4i the real part is 6.
recs.rel: The imaginary part of 6 - 4i is -4.

recs.q: What is the real part of the complex number 2 + 9i?
recs.facts: In a + bi, the real part is a. For 2 + 9i the real part is 2.
recs.rel: The imaginary part of 2 + 9i is 9.

recs.q: Which of the following is a real number?
recs.facts: A real number has no imaginary part. 6 is real, while 4i, 6i and -4i are purely imaginary.
recs.rel: Every real number is also a complex number with imaginary part zero.

recs.q: What was the reason officially given for the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
opts: Administrative convenience because the province was too large
A demand of the Muslim League
recs.facts: Lord Curzon said Bengal was too large to administer well, so he divided it into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal.
recs.rel: Many saw the real aim as weakening Bengali nationalism, and the partition was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word refugee?
opts: A person forced to flee to another place to escape danger
A tourist visiting a foreign land
A soldier of a foreign army
recs.facts: A refugee is a person who has been forced to leave his home or country because of war, persecution or disaster.
recs.rel: The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) was established in 1950.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word refute?
recs.facts: To refute means to prove something wrong or to reject it. Its opposite is to accept or confirm it.
recs.rel: Refute is often confused with deny, but refute implies giving evidence against a claim.

recs.q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared during the term of which British Prime Minister?
recs.facts: Stanley Baldwin was British Prime Minister from 1924 to 1929, which covers 1928 when the Nehru Report appeared.
recs.rel: Ramsay MacDonald became Prime Minister in 1929, the year Jinnah gave his 14 Points.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Zainab (RA) with the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zainab (RA) was the eldest daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadijah (RA).
recs.rel: She was married to Abul As bin Rabi.

recs.q: What is the age required to be qualified as a member (and so to become Speaker) of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Under Article 62 and 51 of the 1973 Constitution, a person must be at least 25 years old to be a member of the National Assembly, and the Speaker is elected from its members.
recs.rel: A person must be at least 35 years old to be elected President.

recs.q: Against whom was the Reshmi Rumal (Silk Letters) Movement directed?
recs.facts: The movement, led by Maulana Mahmud Hasan, aimed to end British rule in India with help from Afghanistan, Turkey and Germany.
recs.rel: It was discovered in 1916 when the silk letters were intercepted.

recs.q: Complete the proverb: A rolling stone gathers no ________.
recs.facts: The proverb means that a person who keeps moving from place to place or job to job does not build up wealth or roots.
recs.rel: The word moss in the proverb stands for success and a settled life.

recs.q: Which metal is liquid at normal room temperature?
recs.facts: Mercury has a melting point of about minus 39 degrees Celsius, so it is liquid at room temperature. Lead, zinc and tin are solid.
recs.rel: Gallium also melts just above room temperature, at about 30 degrees Celsius, but mercury is the common textbook answer.

recs.q: What is the cube root of -2, correct to two decimal places?
recs.facts: The cube root of 2 is about 1.26 because 1.26 x 1.26 x 1.26 is about 2.0. A negative number has a negative real cube root, so the answer is -1.26.
recs.rel: The square root of 2 is about 1.41, which should not be confused with its cube root.

recs.q: For about how long did Hazrat Ali (RA) rule as the fourth Caliph?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) became Caliph in 35 AH (656 CE) and was martyred in 40 AH (661 CE). His rule lasted about four years and nine months.
recs.rel: He was martyred in Kufa by Abdur Rahman bin Muljim.

recs.q: Which river is considered sacred in India?
recs.facts: The Ganges (Ganga) is regarded as the holiest river by Hindus, who bathe in it at places such as Varanasi and Haridwar.
recs.rel: The Ganges flows into the Bay of Bengal through Bangladesh.

recs.q: Saleem is 12 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old is his sister?
recs.facts: Sister's age = 3 x 12 = 36 years.
recs.rel: Her age is 24 years more than Saleem's age.

recs.q: Sara is twice her brother's age and her brother is 5 years old. What will be Sara's age when her brother becomes 10?
recs.facts: Sara is now 2 x 5 = 10 years old. The brother needs 5 more years to reach 10, so Sara will be 10 + 5 = 15.
recs.rel: The difference between two people's ages always stays the same as time passes.

recs.q: Which country launched the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, into space in 1957?
recs.facts: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957. It began the space age.
recs.rel: The United States launched its first satellite, Explorer 1, in January 1958.

recs.q: Which country sent the second satellite, Sputnik 2, carrying the dog Laika, into space in November 1957?
recs.facts: Sputnik 2 was launched by the Soviet Union on 3 November 1957. It carried the dog Laika, the first animal to orbit the Earth.
recs.rel: Sputnik 1 was launched a month earlier, on 4 October 1957.

recs.q: Gossypium arboreum is the scientific name of which crop?
recs.facts: Gossypium arboreum is the species known as desi (Old World or tree) cotton. American upland cotton is Gossypium hirsutum, and sugarcane is a different plant.
recs.rel: Gossypium hirsutum (American upland cotton) gives most of Pakistan's cotton production.

recs.q: What did the Shanghai Five group change into in 2001?
recs.facts: The Shanghai Five (China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan) was formed in 1996. In 2001 Uzbekistan joined and it became the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
recs.rel: The SCO headquarters is in Beijing.

recs.q: Which Pakistani batter has scored the most runs in T20 internationals?
recs.facts: Babar Azam is Pakistan's leading run-scorer in T20 internationals, with over 4,500 runs as of 2026. Mohammad Rizwan is next among the top names.
recs.rel: Sahibzada Farhan, who was the top scorer at the 2026 T20 World Cup, was named Pakistan T20I captain in October 2026.

recs.q: Which is the largest seaport of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Karachi Port is Pakistan's largest and busiest seaport, handling most of the country's sea trade.
recs.rel: Port Qasim is the second major port near Karachi, and Gwadar is the deep sea port on the Balochistan coast.

recs.q: What is the value of secx . cosx?
recs.facts: secx = 1/cosx, so secx . cosx = (1/cosx) x cosx = 1.
recs.rel: Secant and cosine are reciprocals of each other, as are cosecant and sine.

recs.q: Who is the Leader of the Opposition in the Senate of Pakistan as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri of the Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen was appointed Leader of the Opposition in the Senate in January 2026 with the support of most opposition senators.
recs.rel: The post had been vacant since August 2025, when the earlier holder Shibli Faraz was disqualified.

recs.q: On which date did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh?
recs.facts: The Pakistan army in Dhaka surrendered on 16 December 1971, after which East Pakistan became Bangladesh.
recs.rel: The war between Pakistan and India began on 3 December 1971, and Bangladesh celebrates 26 March as its Independence Day.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: Z3, X5, V7, ?
recs.facts: The letters go back by two places (Z, X, V, T) and the numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9), so the next term is T9.
recs.rel: Letter series with a gap of two letters are common in verbal intelligence tests.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: A1, C3, F6, ?
recs.facts: The letters jump by 2, 3, 4 places (A, C, F, J) and the numbers are triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, so the next term is J10.
recs.rel: Triangular numbers are formed by adding 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on.

recs.q: In set theory, an empty set is also known as which of the following?
recs.facts: A set that contains no elements is called an empty set, also known as the null or void set.
recs.rel: The empty set is written as the symbol of an empty circle with a slash or as curly braces with nothing inside.

recs.q: Shandur Pass, famous for its polo festival, lies between Chitral and which region?
recs.facts: Shandur Pass connects the Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with the Ghizer district of Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: It is known as the roof of the world polo ground and hosts the Shandur Polo Festival each year.

recs.q: Who was the President of the All India Muslim League at the Simla Conference of 1945?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was President of the Muslim League and led its delegation at Simla.
recs.rel: Liaquat Ali Khan was the Secretary General of the Muslim League at that time.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: She bought her shoes yesterday but they were already ____ out.
recs.facts: The past participle worn is needed with the phrasal expression worn out, meaning damaged by use.
recs.rel: Worn is the past participle of the verb wear.

recs.q: Akbar is taller than Akmal, and Akmal is taller than Ali. Which statement is correct?
opts: Akmal is taller than Ali but shorter than Akbar
recs.facts: The order of height is Akbar, then Akmal, then Ali. So Akmal is in the middle.
recs.rel: Such questions are solved by arranging the persons in order.

recs.q: What is the symbol on the flag of the Olympic Games?
recs.facts: The Olympic flag has five interlocking rings of blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background.
recs.rel: The rings represent the five inhabited continents joined together.

recs.q: Sin (90 degrees - x) is equal to which of the following?
recs.facts: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement, so sin(90 - x) = cos x.
recs.rel: Similarly cos(90 - x) = sin x.

recs.q: Ali is 9 years old and his sister is 5 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 15 years old?
recs.facts: Sister now = 5 x 9 = 45 years, so she is 36 years older than Ali. When Ali is 15, she is 15 + 36 = 51 years.
recs.rel: In age problems the difference between two ages always stays the same.

recs.q: If Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 9, how old will the sister be when Ali is 11?
recs.facts: The age difference is 9 - 3 = 6 years and it never changes. When Ali is 11, his sister is 11 + 6 = 17 years.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people remains constant throughout life.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: You are so ____, come on!
recs.facts: After the verb 'are' we need an adjective that describes the subject 'you', so 'slow' is correct. 'Slowly' is an adverb and cannot follow 'are' here.
recs.rel: A linking verb such as is, am or are is followed by an adjective, not an adverb.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Aslam is slow ____ genius.
recs.facts: The sentence contrasts two opposite ideas (slow and genius), so the conjunction 'but' fits.
recs.rel: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction used to show contrast.

recs.q: Which Pakistani player won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012, 2019 and 2024?
recs.facts: Muhammad Asif of Faisalabad won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012, 2019 and 2024.
recs.rel: Muhammad Yousuf (1994) and Muhammad Sajjad (2006) were earlier Pakistani world amateur snooker champions.

recs.q: What is the biggest part of our solar system?
recs.facts: The Sun holds about 99.8 percent of the total mass of the solar system and is by far its biggest part.
recs.rel: Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system.

recs.q: What is the grammatical name (part of speech) of the word 'perfectly' in: He sang the solo perfectly?
recs.facts: 'Perfectly' tells how he sang, so it modifies the verb 'sang'. A word that modifies a verb is an adverb.
recs.rel: Many adverbs of manner are formed by adding -ly to an adjective.

recs.q: For which idea is the British astronomer Fred Hoyle best known?
opts: Steady State theory and coining the term Big Bang
recs.facts: Fred Hoyle supported the Steady State theory of the universe and coined the term 'Big Bang' in 1949 on BBC radio.
recs.rel: Hoyle also worked on stellar nucleosynthesis, the formation of heavy elements in stars.

recs.q: What is the name of the son of Hazrat Zakariya (AS)?
recs.facts: Allah granted Hazrat Zakariya (AS) a son in old age, named Yahya (AS) (John the Baptist).
recs.rel: Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was also the guardian of Hazrat Maryam (AS).

recs.q: Which large water body lies to the south of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan has a coastline of about 1,046 km along the Arabian Sea in the south.
recs.rel: Karachi and Gwadar are the main ports on this coast.

recs.q: How many dimensions does space have?
recs.facts: Ordinary space has three dimensions: length, width and height.
recs.rel: Physics adds time as a fourth dimension to form spacetime.

recs.q: What is the square of 7?
recs.facts: The square of 7 is 7 x 7 = 49.
recs.rel: 49 is the smallest square number that is the product of two equal primes greater than 5.

recs.q: What is true about the diagonals of a square?
opts: They are equal and bisect each other at right angles
They are equal but do not bisect each other
They are unequal and bisect at right angles
recs.facts: The diagonals of a square are equal in length and bisect each other at 90 degrees.
recs.rel: In a rhombus the diagonals are perpendicular but not equal.

recs.q: What does HTML stand for?
recs.facts: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard language for creating web pages.
recs.rel: It was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1991.

recs.q: What does LCD stand for?
recs.facts: LCD stands for Liquid Crystal Display, a flat panel display that uses liquid crystals.
recs.rel: LCDs are used in monitors, televisions and calculators.

recs.q: What does NADRA stand for?
recs.facts: NADRA is the National Database and Registration Authority of Pakistan, which issues CNICs.
recs.rel: NADRA was established in 2000.

recs.q: What does NCO stand for in the army?
recs.facts: NCO stands for Non-Commissioned Officer, a soldier such as a sergeant who rose from the ranks without a commission.
recs.rel: Commissioned officers hold a rank from Second Lieutenant upward.

recs.q: What does VIP stand for?
recs.facts: VIP stands for Very Important Person.
recs.rel: VIPs normally receive special security and protocol.

recs.q: What are the dimensions of a standard football goal?
recs.facts: A full-size football goal is 24 feet (7.32 m) wide and 8 feet (2.44 m) high.
recs.rel: These measures were fixed in the Laws of the Game in the 1860s.

recs.q: On which date did Pakistan Television (PTV) start its first broadcast from Lahore?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first television station started transmission in Lahore on 26 November 1964.
recs.rel: The second TV station started in Dhaka in 1965 and a third in Karachi in 1967.

recs.q: Who was the chief executive (head of the government and state) under the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution gave a presidential system in which the President was both head of state and chief executive.
recs.rel: Field Marshal Ayub Khan was the President who introduced this constitution.

recs.q: According to the 1962 Constitution, what was the status of the Bengali language?
opts: One of the two national languages with Urdu
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution named both Urdu and Bengali as national languages of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution had also made Urdu and Bengali the state languages.

recs.q: Akbar is taller than Ali and Usman is shorter than Ali. Who is the tallest of the three?
recs.facts: Akbar is taller than Ali, and Ali is taller than Usman, so the order is Akbar, Ali, Usman. Akbar is the tallest.
recs.rel: Chain comparisons like this are solved by writing the names in order from greatest to least.

recs.q: After which battle did the Quraish and the disbelievers stop attacking Madinah and lose the initiative against the Muslims?
recs.facts: After the siege of Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (5 AH) failed, the Quraish could never again launch a major attack, and the Prophet (PBUH) said the Muslims would now march against them.
recs.rel: Makkah was conquered peacefully three years later in 8 AH.

recs.q: Which area of the subcontinent did the East India Company first bring under its political control?
recs.facts: After the Battle of Plassey (1757) and the Battle of Buxar (1764) the Company ruled Bengal, its first big territory.
recs.rel: Siraj-ud-Daula, Nawab of Bengal, was defeated at Plassey.

recs.q: On what date was the Suez Canal officially opened?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal opened to ships on 17 November 1869.
recs.rel: Digging started on 25 April 1859.

recs.q: About how long is the Suez Canal in nautical miles?
recs.facts: The canal is about 193 km long, and 193 divided by 1.852 is about 104 nautical miles.
recs.rel: The figure 193 is the length in kilometres.

recs.q: In a triangle, the sum of any two sides is what compared with the third side?
recs.facts: By the triangle inequality, the sum of any two sides is always greater than the third side.
recs.rel: Sides 2, 3 and 6 cannot form a triangle because 2 + 3 is not greater than 6.

recs.q: What is the sum of the series 2, 4, 6, 8?
recs.rel: The sum of the first n even numbers is n times (n + 1), here 4 times 5 = 20.

recs.q: If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, which day is the 28th of that month?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 28th is 23 days. 23 divided by 7 leaves 2, so the day is Sunday + 2 = Tuesday.
recs.rel: The 12th, 19th and 26th are also Sundays, so the 28th is two days after the 26th.

recs.q: What is a synonym of fertilizer?
recs.facts: A fertilizer is a substance added to soil to make it more fertile, and manure is a similar substance.
recs.rel: Urea and DAP are common chemical fertilizers in Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the synonym of advanced?
recs.facts: Advanced means ahead in development, so progressive is closest in meaning.
recs.rel: The opposite of advanced is primitive or backward.

recs.q: What is the synonym of annihilation?
recs.facts: Annihilation means complete destruction.
recs.rel: The verb annihilate means to destroy utterly.

recs.q: What is the synonym of blame?
recs.facts: To blame is to hold someone responsible for a fault, which is close to censure.
recs.rel: Praise is an antonym of blame.

recs.q: What is the synonym of brutal?
recs.facts: Brutal means savagely harsh, which matches cruel.
recs.rel: Brutality is the noun form, meaning savage cruelty.

recs.q: What is the synonym of contentious?
recs.facts: Contentious means causing or likely to cause arguments, which is the sense of controversial.
recs.rel: The noun is contention, meaning heated disagreement.

recs.q: What is the synonym of diligent?
recs.facts: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort, so hardworking is closest.
recs.rel: Industrious is another synonym of diligent.

recs.q: What is the synonym of exhausted?
recs.facts: Exhausted means completely used up of energy, which is the sense of drained.
recs.rel: Fatigued is another synonym of exhausted.

recs.q: What is the synonym of extravagant?
recs.facts: Extravagant means spending or giving far more than is necessary, which matches lavish.
recs.rel: Frugal is an antonym of extravagant.

recs.q: What is the synonym of germinate?
recs.facts: To germinate is to begin to grow from a seed, which is to sprout.
recs.rel: Germination is the process by which a seed develops into a seedling.

recs.q: What is the synonym of identification?
recs.facts: Identification means the act of recognizing who or what something is.
recs.rel: An identification card is commonly called an ID card.

recs.q: What is the synonym of liberal?
recs.facts: Liberal can mean giving freely or in large amounts, which is generous.
recs.rel: Liberal also means open to new ideas, so sources may give broad-minded as another synonym.

recs.q: What is the synonym of pious?
recs.facts: Pious means deeply religious, which is the meaning of devout.
recs.rel: Piety is the noun form, meaning religious devotion.

recs.q: What is the synonym of strictly?
recs.facts: Strictly means in a way that follows rules exactly, which is rigidly.
recs.rel: Strict is the adjective and leniently is its opposite in manner.

recs.q: What is the synonym of tired?
recs.facts: Tired means in need of rest, which matches weary.
recs.rel: Exhausted is a stronger word than tired.

recs.q: What is the synonym of truth?
recs.facts: Truth means the quality of being true, and veracity is the formal word for it.
recs.rel: Veracity comes from the Latin word verus meaning true.

recs.q: Which team won the most recent T20-format Asia Cup, held in 2025?
recs.facts: India beat Pakistan by 5 wickets in the 2025 final in Dubai.
recs.rel: Sri Lanka won the 2022 T20 Asia Cup by beating Pakistan by 23 runs.

recs.q: With whose help was the Al-Khalid main battle tank developed in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Al-Khalid (MBT-2000) was co-developed by Heavy Industries Taxila and China's Norinco, based on the Chinese Type 90-II.
recs.rel: Its diesel engine initially came from Ukraine.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the main Tarbela Dam?
recs.facts: The main embankment dam of Tarbela is about 2,743 m long and 143 m high.
recs.rel: Tarbela on the River Indus is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world.

recs.q: In which district of Pakistan is the ancient city of Taxila located?
recs.facts: Taxila is a tehsil of Rawalpindi District in Punjab.
recs.rel: Taxila is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

recs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The teacher said, "I will meet you next day." (spoken to the students)
opts: The teacher said that he will meet you next day.
The teacher said that I would meet them the next day.
The teacher said that he would meet you the next day.
The teacher said that he would meet them the next day.
recs.facts: In reported speech will changes to would, I changes to he, you changes to them and next day changes to the next day.
recs.rel: Said that is used in indirect narration of statements.

recs.q: In which year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
recs.facts: NASA launched Hubble aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery in April 1990.
recs.rel: It is named after the astronomer Edwin Hubble.

recs.q: Which letter appears three times in the word 'temperature' but only once in the word 'cylinder'?
recs.facts: In 'temperature' the letter E appears 3 times (t-E-mp-E-ratur-E) while T and R appear twice. In 'cylinder' E appears once.
recs.rel: The word 'temperature' has 11 letters.

recs.q: If (x, 1) = (1, y), what is the ordered pair (x, y)?
