recs.facts: Two ordered pairs are equal when their corresponding elements are equal, so x = 1 and y = 1. Hence (x, y) = (1, 1).
recs.rel: The Cartesian product A x B is the set of all ordered pairs (a, b) with a in A and b in B.

recs.q: If today is Friday, what day of the week will it be after 30 days?
recs.facts: 30 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2. Two days after Friday is Sunday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so the weekday repeats every 7 days.

recs.q: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 15 days?
recs.facts: 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. One day after Monday is Tuesday.
recs.rel: After 14 days the same weekday comes back.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what will be the day after tomorrow (counting today as the 1st)?
recs.facts: Tomorrow is Tuesday (2nd), and the day after tomorrow is Wednesday (3rd).
recs.rel: The 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th of that month also fall on Monday.

recs.q: Which major battle in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) participated took place in 7 AH?
recs.facts: The Battle of Khyber against the Jews of Khyber was fought in 7 AH (628 AD).
recs.rel: The Conquest of Makkah came later, in 8 AH.

recs.q: Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in Test cricket?
recs.facts: Younis Khan scored 10,099 Test runs and is the leading Pakistani Test run scorer.
recs.rel: He passed Javed Miandad's 8,832 runs in 2015 and was the first Pakistani to reach 10,000 Test runs.

recs.q: What is the main subject (topic) of Sahih Bukhari?
opts: Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet)
recs.facts: Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is a collection of authentic hadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: It is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after the Quran.

recs.q: What are two circles that touch each other at exactly one point called?
recs.facts: Circles that meet at exactly one point are called tangent (touching) circles. They can touch externally or internally.
recs.rel: Concentric circles share the same centre and never meet.

recs.q: Which of these countries does not share a border with Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan borders India, China, Afghanistan and Iran. Bangladesh is separated from Pakistan by India.
recs.rel: Bangladesh was East Pakistan until 1971.

recs.q: What is a synonym of the word 'transparent'?
recs.facts: Transparent means allowing light to pass through so things can be seen clearly. Clear is the closest synonym.
recs.rel: Translucent means light passes through but objects cannot be seen clearly.

recs.q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 12 years old?
recs.facts: The sister is 2 x 3 = 6 when Ali is 3, so she is 3 years older. When Ali is 12, she is 12 + 3 = 15.
recs.rel: Age problems are solved by keeping the fixed age difference.

recs.q: Omar is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will his sister's age be when Omar is 11 years old?
recs.facts: The sister is 2 x 4 = 8 when Omar is 4, so she is 4 years older. When Omar is 11, she is 11 + 4 = 15.
recs.rel: The age difference stays the same for ever.

recs.q: A train travels 60 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes at the same speed?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 60/100 = 0.6 km per minute. In 12 minutes it covers 0.6 x 12 = 7.2 km.
recs.rel: Speed here is 36 km per hour.

recs.q: If a bus travels 20 miles in an hour, how many miles does it cover in 40 minutes?
recs.facts: 40 minutes = 2/3 of an hour, so distance = 20 x 2/3 = 13 1/3 miles (about 13.3).
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time, with time in the same unit as the speed.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks. So the 25th falls on the same day, Tuesday.
recs.rel: Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 25th is 23 days = 3 weeks + 2 days. Tuesday plus 2 days is Thursday.
recs.rel: Divide the gap in days by 7 and move forward by the remainder.

recs.q: How many equal sides does an isosceles triangle have?
recs.facts: An isosceles triangle has exactly two sides of equal length, and the angles opposite them are also equal.
recs.rel: A triangle with all three sides equal is called equilateral.

recs.q: To which tribe did Hazrat Khadija (RA) belong?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid belonged to the Banu Asad clan of the Quraish tribe of Makkah.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) himself belonged to Banu Hashim of the Quraish.

recs.q: Which was fought first, the Battle of Badr or the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: Badr was fought in 2 AH and Uhud in 3 AH, so Badr came first.
recs.rel: The Battle of Khandaq (Trench) followed in 5 AH.

recs.q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 72?
recs.facts: 72 = 36 x 2, so its square root is 6 x root 2 = 6 x 1.414 = about 8.49.
recs.rel: 8 squared is 64 and 9 squared is 81, so the root of 72 lies between 8 and 9.

recs.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
recs.facts: Electric current is measured in amperes (amps), the flow of charge per second.
recs.rel: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current.

recs.q: What is the capital of the USA?
recs.facts: Washington, D.C. is the federal capital of the United States and the seat of the White House and Congress. It lies on the Potomac River.
recs.rel: New York City hosts the United Nations headquarters but is not the capital.

recs.q: Who is the Vice President of the USA (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: J. D. Vance took office as Vice President on 20 January 2025 under President Donald Trump. He is still the Vice President in October 2026.
recs.rel: In 2022 the Vice President was Kamala Harris.

recs.q: Valletta is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Valletta is the capital city of Malta, an island country in the Mediterranean Sea. It is one of the smallest national capitals in Europe.
recs.rel: Malta is a member of the European Union and the Commonwealth.

recs.q: If 2x + 3x + y is simplified, what is the result?
recs.facts: Like terms 2x and 3x add up to 5x. The term y is unlike, so it stays separate, giving 5x + y.
recs.rel: Only like terms (same variable and power) can be added together.

recs.q: What is the main difference between a scalar and a vector quantity?
opts: A scalar has magnitude only, while a vector has magnitude and direction
A scalar has direction only, while a vector has magnitude only
A scalar is always negative, while a vector is always positive
recs.facts: A scalar is fully described by its magnitude, such as mass or speed. A vector needs both magnitude and direction, such as velocity or force.
recs.rel: Distance is a scalar while displacement is a vector.

recs.q: What is the magnitude of a unit vector?
recs.facts: A unit vector is defined as a vector of length one, so its magnitude is 1. It is used to indicate direction only.
recs.rel: The unit vectors along the x, y and z axes are i, j and k.

recs.q: Two non-zero vectors are parallel if their vector (cross) product is what?
recs.facts: The magnitude of A cross B is AB sin(theta). For parallel vectors theta is 0 or 180 degrees, so sin(theta) = 0 and the cross product is the zero vector.
recs.rel: For perpendicular vectors the dot product, not the cross product, is zero.

recs.q: What is the third form (past participle) of the verb 'flash'?
recs.facts: 'Flash' is a regular verb, so its three forms are flash, flashed, flashed. The third form is therefore flashed.
recs.rel: Flashing is the present participle form.

recs.q: Which Indian tribe was forced to walk the Trail of Tears?
recs.facts: The Trail of Tears was the forced removal of the Cherokee from the south-eastern USA to Indian Territory in 1838-39 after the Indian Removal Act of 1830. Thousands died on the way.
recs.rel: Other nations such as the Choctaw, Creek, Chickasaw and Seminole were also forcibly removed.

recs.q: A person walks 20 km north, then turns right, then left, then right again. In which direction is he now facing?
recs.facts: Facing north, a right turn gives east. A left turn then gives north, and a right turn again gives east.
recs.rel: A right turn moves clockwise by 90 degrees and a left turn moves anticlockwise by 90 degrees.

recs.q: What is the product of the frequency and the time period of a wave?
recs.facts: The time period T is the reciprocal of frequency f, that is T = 1/f. Therefore f times T = 1.
recs.rel: Frequency is measured in hertz, and time period in seconds.

recs.q: In Islamic history, what does Aam-ul-Wafood mean?
recs.facts: Aam-ul-Wafood is the Year of Delegations, 9 AH, when many Arab tribes sent delegations to Madinah to accept Islam.
recs.rel: The Year of Grief (Aam-ul-Huzn) was the year in which Hazrat Khadija and Abu Talib died.

recs.q: Which area of Pakistan is famous for its illegal (unlicensed) arms manufacturing market?
recs.facts: Darra Adam Khel, south of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is well known for its cottage-industry gunsmiths and arms bazaar.
recs.rel: Darra Adam Khel belongs to the Frontier Region area of the Kohat-Peshawar border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

recs.q: In the sentence 'He is clever as well as hardworking', what part of speech is the phrase 'as well as'?
recs.facts: 'As well as' joins two words or phrases of equal rank, so it works as a (compound) conjunction.
recs.rel: Other common compound conjunctions are 'as soon as', 'in order that' and 'as long as'.

recs.q: Which language has the largest number of speakers (native plus second-language) in the world?
recs.facts: English is spoken by about 1.5 billion people counting second-language speakers, which is more than any other language.
recs.rel: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers, so sources differ on the question depending on whether native or total speakers are counted.

recs.q: Length multiplied by width of a rectangle gives its what?
recs.facts: The area of a rectangle is length x width, measured in square units.
recs.rel: The perimeter of a rectangle is 2 x (length + width).

recs.q: What is the width of a standard football (soccer) goal?
recs.facts: A standard football goal is 8 yards (24 feet or 7.32 metres) wide and 8 feet (2.44 metres) high.
recs.rel: The width of a goal is measured between the inside edges of the two posts.

recs.q: Which famous writer refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1964?
recs.facts: The French philosopher and writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature.
recs.rel: Boris Pasternak was forced by the Soviet authorities to decline the 1958 Nobel Prize in Literature.

recs.q: If two thirds of a group are men, what percentage of the group are women?
recs.facts: Women are 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the group. 1/3 x 100 = 33.33%.
recs.rel: One third is equal to 33.33 percent.

recs.q: Change the narration: I said to him, 'Why are you working so hard?'
opts: I asked him why was he working so hard.
I told him why he was working so hard.
I asked him why he was working so hard.
I asked him that why he is working so hard.
recs.facts: A question in direct speech becomes 'asked' in indirect speech. The word order becomes statement order and the tense moves back to the past continuous: he was working.
recs.rel: The question mark is dropped in indirect speech.

recs.q: What is the name of the set of all positive numbers, negative numbers and zero (without fractions)?
recs.facts: Integers include the positive whole numbers, the negative whole numbers and zero.
recs.rel: Whole numbers contain zero and the positive integers only.

recs.q: What is -i(2i + 3)?
recs.facts: -i(2i + 3) = -2i squared - 3i = 2 - 3i, since i squared is -1.
recs.rel: The real part of this number is 2.

recs.q: What is -i(6 - 4i)?
recs.rel: The value of i squared is -1.

recs.q: What is 1/3 of 90% of 90?
recs.facts: 90% of 90 is 81, and one third of 81 is 27.
recs.rel: A percent means per hundred, so 90% is 90/100.

recs.facts: The denominators are equal, so add the numerators: 3/8.
recs.rel: 3/8 is equal to 0.375.

recs.q: What is 3 x 4?
recs.facts: Three groups of four make 12.
recs.rel: Multiplication is repeated addition: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

recs.q: What is 4 x 3 + 3 x 4?
recs.facts: Multiply first: 4 x 3 = 12 and 3 x 4 = 12. Then add: 12 + 12 = 24.
recs.rel: BODMAS says multiplication is done before addition.

recs.q: What is 60% of 9?
recs.rel: 60% is equal to 3/5.

recs.q: What is 7% of 80?
recs.rel: 10% of 80 is 8, so 7% must be a little less.

recs.q: What is 80% of 20?
recs.rel: 80% is equal to 4/5.

recs.q: What is 90% of 81?
What is a + ib, where a and b are real numbers and i is the square root of -1, called?
recs.facts: An expression of the form a + ib is called a complex number, with real part a and imaginary part b.
recs.rel: The number i is defined by i squared equal to -1.

recs.q: What is the value of Y = (1 - 2)(1 - 3)?
recs.rel: The product of two negative numbers is positive.

recs.q: Muhammad Ali Bogra held which office in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Bogra served as the third Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1953 to 1955, after Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed.
recs.rel: He is remembered for the Bogra Formula of 1953 on constitution making.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to fragment?
recs.facts: A fragment is a small broken part or piece of something larger.
recs.rel: The opposite of fragment is whole or complete.

recs.q: In which year was the first Round Table Conference held in London?
recs.facts: The first Round Table Conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931.
recs.rel: Three Round Table Conferences were held between 1930 and 1932.

recs.q: Freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed under which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 19 gives every citizen the right to freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable restrictions.
recs.rel: Article 19A of the 1973 Constitution, added in 2010, gives the right to information.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to zest?
recs.facts: Zest means great energy and enjoyment, which is enthusiasm.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is a synonym of 'disruption'?
recs.facts: Disruption means a break or interruption in the normal course of something. Disturbance has the same meaning.
recs.rel: The opposite of disruption is continuity.

recs.q: In which year did Queen Elizabeth II first visit Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Queen first visited Pakistan in February 1961 during a Commonwealth tour.
recs.rel: Her second visit was in 1997.

recs.q: Who discovered penicillin?
recs.facts: Alexander Fleming, a Scottish scientist, discovered penicillin in 1928 from the mould Penicillium.
recs.rel: Fleming shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Florey and Chain.

recs.q: Who is the current ODI captain of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Shaheen Shah Afridi was appointed Pakistan's ODI captain and was still leading the side in 2026.
recs.rel: Babar Azam was ODI captain in 2022 to 2023 and Mohammad Rizwan led briefly after him.

recs.q: Gwadar Port is linked through CPEC with which country?
recs.facts: Gwadar Port is the centrepiece of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, which links it with China's Xinjiang region.
recs.rel: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958.

recs.q: Which country lies to the west of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Iran borders Pakistan on the west, mainly along Balochistan.
recs.rel: Afghanistan lies to the north-west of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which is considered the largest desert of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks name the Thar Desert in Sindh as the largest desert of Pakistan. It is shared with India.
recs.rel: Sources differ: some measure only the Pakistani portion, where Cholistan is also large.

recs.q: In which city is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) located?
recs.facts: The WHO is a specialised agency of the United Nations and has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
recs.rel: The International Olympic Committee is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

recs.q: Why do parents give education to their children?
recs.facts: Parents educate children to groom them, that is, to prepare and train them for a successful life.
recs.rel: Groom means to prepare someone for a future role.

recs.q: In which year did Balochistan become a province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: When the One Unit scheme of West Pakistan was dissolved on 1 July 1970, Balochistan became a full province.
recs.rel: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: The aeroplane flew ___ my head.
recs.facts: The preposition over is used when something passes above a person or object. The other options do not suit the meaning.
recs.rel: Over means above, while across means from one side to the other.

recs.q: What is the approximate area of Sindh province?
recs.facts: Sindh covers about 140,914 square kilometres, which is about 17.7 percent of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sindh is the third largest province of Pakistan by area after Balochistan and Punjab.

recs.q: How many ayat (verses) does Surah Al-Ikhlas have?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) has 4 ayat. It describes the oneness of Allah.
recs.rel: Reciting it is said to equal one third of the Quran in reward.

recs.q: How many letters does the Pashto alphabet have according to the most commonly cited reference count?
recs.facts: The Pashto alphabet is written in an extended Arabic script and is most commonly cited as having 45 letters.
recs.rel: Some learner guides count 44 letters, so sources differ slightly; 45 is the figure candidates and many references use.

recs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He will not approve ___ your plan.
recs.facts: The verb approve takes the preposition of when it means to think well of something.
recs.rel: Disapprove is also followed by of.

recs.q: In which years was the First World War fought?
recs.facts: The First World War began in July 1914 and ended with the armistice of November 1918.
recs.rel: The Treaty of Versailles with Germany was signed in 1919.

recs.q: In which year did the Second World War start?
recs.facts: The Second World War began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland, and ended in 1945.
recs.rel: Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to obligation?
recs.facts: An obligation is something you must do, which means a duty.
recs.rel: In law, an obligation is a legal or moral duty that binds a person.

recs.q: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
recs.facts: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the final held in Qatar on 18 December 2022.
recs.rel: Lionel Messi captained Argentina to this win, their third World Cup title.

recs.q: In which years was the Second World War fought?
recs.facts: The Second World War began in 1939 when Germany invaded Poland and ended in 1945 with the defeat of Germany and Japan.
recs.rel: It was fought between the Allied Powers and the Axis Powers (Germany, Italy and Japan).

recs.q: How many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize so far?
recs.facts: Two Pakistanis have won it: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
recs.rel: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate in history.

recs.q: What does Makruh mean in Islamic law?
opts: A permitted act with no reward
A disliked act that is better avoided
An act that is strictly forbidden
recs.facts: A Makruh act is disliked and discouraged in Islam, but doing it is a lesser matter than a forbidden (Haram) act.
recs.rel: Makruh is one of the five categories of rulings: Fard, Mustahab, Mubah, Makruh and Haram.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to peril?
recs.facts: Peril means serious danger or risk.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: On which side of Punjab is the Cholistan Desert located?
recs.facts: The Cholistan Desert lies in the south of Punjab near Bahawalpur, along the border with India.
recs.rel: It is also called Rohi, and it is part of the greater Thar Desert.

recs.q: On which date was the Legal Framework Order (LFO) issued by President Yahya Khan?
recs.facts: President General Yahya Khan issued the Legal Framework Order on 30 March 1970 to arrange the first general elections on the basis of one man one vote. It also ended the One Unit.
recs.rel: Some sources give 28 March 1970, the date of its announcement; a different LFO was issued by General Pervez Musharraf in 2002.

recs.q: In which month and year was the Lucknow Pact signed between the Muslim League and the Indian National Congress?
recs.facts: The Lucknow Pact was agreed at the joint sessions of the Congress and the Muslim League in Lucknow in December 1916.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is known as the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity for this pact.

recs.q: Convert 90 degrees into radians.
recs.facts: 1 degree = pi/180 radian. So 90 degrees = 90 x pi/180 = pi/2 radians.
recs.rel: A full circle of 360 degrees equals 2 pi radians.

recs.q: A train's speed is double that of a car. If the car travels 60 km in 1 hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: The car speed is 60 km per hour, so the train speed is 120 km per hour. In 30 minutes (half an hour) the train covers 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
recs.rel: In the same 30 minutes the car covers 30 km.

recs.q: What is 0.01 x 100?
recs.facts: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right: 0.01 becomes 1.
recs.rel: 0.01 is the same as 1/100, so 0.01 x 100 = 1.

recs.q: Who is the current President of Bangladesh (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned in July 2026. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected by Parliament on 20 August 2026 and sworn in as the 23rd President.
recs.rel: Earlier answers such as Mohammed Shahabuddin (from 2023) are now outdated; Tarique Rahman is the Prime Minister.

recs.q: A rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns, written inside square brackets, is called what?
recs.facts: A rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns enclosed in brackets is called a matrix.
recs.rel: The size of a matrix is called its order, written as rows x columns.

recs.q: How many countries are there in Central Asia?
recs.facts: Central Asia has five countries: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
recs.rel: All five were part of the Soviet Union until 1991.

recs.q: Who was the father of Hazrat Yusuf (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS), who was also a prophet.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and the grandson of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

recs.q: Who was the leader of Germany in World War II?
recs.facts: Adolf Hitler led Germany as Chancellor and Fuhrer from 1933 until his death in 1945.
recs.rel: Churchill led Britain, Mussolini led Italy and Stalin led the Soviet Union.

recs.q: What was Hazrat Umme Kulsum (RA) to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Umme Kulsum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
recs.rel: She was married to Hazrat Uthman (RA) after the death of her sister Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).

recs.q: Ahmed got 15 marks out of 60. What is his percentage?
recs.facts: Percentage = 15/60 x 100 = 25%.
recs.rel: 15/60 simplifies to 1/4, which is 25%.

recs.q: Which is the oldest English newspaper of Pakistan still in publication?
recs.facts: Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in 1941 in Delhi and is the oldest widely cited English daily of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Dawn moved to Karachi after the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

recs.q: In which country is the headquarters of the Olympics (International Olympic Committee) located?
recs.facts: The International Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.
recs.rel: The modern Olympic Games first began in Athens in 1896.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word ominous?
opts: Threatening, suggesting that something bad will happen
recs.facts: Ominous describes something that gives a sign of coming trouble or danger. For example, ominous dark clouds suggest a storm.
recs.rel: Synonyms of ominous include threatening, sinister and foreboding.

recs.q: Which is the smallest of the five rivers of Punjab (Pakistan) in length?
recs.facts: The Ravi is about 720 km long, the shortest of the five rivers, and is commonly called the smallest river of Pakistan in textbooks.
recs.rel: The Jhelum is only slightly longer, at about 725 km, so some sources give slightly different rankings.

recs.q: Which country was the third largest host of refugees in 2016 according to the Amnesty International report?
recs.facts: Amnesty International's October 2016 report ranked Jordan first, Turkey second, Pakistan third (about 1.6 million) and Lebanon fourth.
recs.rel: The UNHCR figures of the same year ranked Turkey first, so rankings differ between organisations.

recs.q: Which country won the most medals at the Olympic Games held at Tokyo in 2020 (held in 2021)?
recs.facts: The USA topped the medal table with 113 medals, including 39 gold.
recs.rel: China had 38 gold medals, one fewer than the USA.

recs.q: On which date was the 1956 constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan took over as President on 27 October 1958.

recs.q: In which valley is Attabad Lake located?
recs.facts: Attabad Lake is in the Gojal area of the upper Hunza Valley in Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: The lake was formed in January 2010 when a landslide blocked the Hunza River.

recs.q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan provides the right to free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16?
recs.facts: Article 25A was added by the 18th Amendment in 2010. It obliges the State to give free and compulsory education to children from 5 to 16 years.
recs.rel: Article 37(b) also directs the State to remove illiteracy and provide free secondary education.

recs.q: Between which two countries does the Durand Line lie?
recs.facts: The Durand Line is the border drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan. Today it is the international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
recs.rel: It was agreed between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan.

recs.q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan gives the right to education?
recs.facts: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, makes education a right of children.
recs.rel: Article 37 also speaks about the promotion of education as a principle of policy.

recs.q: What is the value of sec 0 (secant of zero degrees)?
recs.facts: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, and cos 0 = 1, so sec 0 = 1/1 = 1.
recs.rel: Sec 90 degrees is undefined because cos 90 degrees is zero.

recs.q: On which date did Fatima Jinnah die?
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah, the sister of Quaid-e-Azam, died in Karachi on 9 July 1967.
recs.rel: She was born on 31 July 1893 in Karachi and is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

recs.q: What is the tense used to write about the future called?
recs.facts: Future tense describes actions that will happen later, usually with will or shall, as in: I will go.
recs.rel: English has four forms of future tense: simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.

recs.q: Geographically, Greenland belongs to which continent?
recs.facts: Greenland lies on the North American continental shelf, although politically it is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.
recs.rel: Greenland is the largest island in the world.

recs.q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
recs.facts: Methane traps heat in the atmosphere, while oxygen, nitrogen and argon do not.
recs.rel: Carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide are the main greenhouse gases.

recs.q: In which city is the headquarters of the European Union (EU) located?
recs.facts: The main institutions of the European Union, such as the European Commission and the Council, are based in Brussels, Belgium.
recs.rel: The European Parliament meets in Strasbourg, France, and has its secretariat in Luxembourg.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani cricketer to score a triple century in Test cricket?
recs.facts: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against the West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958. It was the first Test triple century by a Pakistani.
recs.rel: Hanif also scored 499 for Karachi in 1958-59, which was then the highest first-class score.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word lately?
recs.facts: Lately means in the recent past, which is the same as recently.
recs.rel: Do not confuse lately with late, which means after the expected time.

recs.q: In which year did the British occupy Punjab?
recs.facts: The British defeated the Sikhs in the Second Anglo-Sikh War and annexed Punjab in 1849.
recs.rel: Sindh had been annexed earlier, in 1843.

recs.q: Which Quetta-area peak, also called Loe Sar Nekan, is generally given as the highest peak of Balochistan?
recs.facts: Zarghun Ghar, near Quetta, at about 3,578 metres is generally given as the highest peak in Balochistan.
recs.rel: Sources differ a little on its exact height and name; Kuchnai Saar (about 3,404 m) is listed next.

recs.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'restricted'.
recs.facts: Restricted means kept within limits or not allowed freely, so the closest word is limited.
recs.rel: The antonym of restricted is unrestricted or free.

recs.q: In which mountain range are Pakistan's famous salt mines, such as Khewra, located?
recs.facts: The Salt Range in Punjab holds huge rock salt deposits, including the Khewra salt mine.
recs.rel: Khewra is one of the largest salt mines in the world.

recs.q: Between which two countries was the Shimla Agreement of 1972 signed?
recs.facts: The Shimla Agreement was signed by Pakistan and India in July 1972 after the 1971 war.
recs.rel: Under it both countries agreed to settle disputes peacefully and respect the Line of Control in Kashmir.

recs.q: How many straight lines can pass through a single given point?
recs.facts: Through one point we can draw a line in every possible direction, so there are infinitely many lines.
recs.rel: Exactly one straight line passes through two different points.

recs.q: What is the sum of two supplementary angles?
recs.facts: Two angles are supplementary when they add up to 180 degrees, for example 110 and 70.
recs.rel: Two angles that add up to 90 degrees are called complementary angles.

recs.q: Who has taken the most Test wickets for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Wasim Akram took 414 Test wickets, the highest by any Pakistani bowler, and the record still stands in 2026.
recs.rel: Waqar Younis is second for Pakistan with 373 Test wickets.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to thy?
recs.facts: Thy is an old English word meaning your (belonging to you).
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word undaunted?
recs.facts: Undaunted means not discouraged or frightened by difficulty or danger, so it means fearless.
recs.rel: Daunt means to make someone feel afraid or less confident.

recs.q: In which year did Zakat become compulsory (enforced by law) in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance was promulgated in 1980 under General Zia-ul-Haq, and Zakat deduction from bank accounts started that year.
recs.rel: Zakat is deducted from savings accounts on the first of Ramadan.

recs.q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be?
recs.facts: From the 14th to the 19th is 5 days. Sunday + 5 days = Friday.
recs.rel: The 7th, 21st and 28th of this month are also Sundays.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 30th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 30th is 26 days. 26 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5, and Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
recs.rel: The 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th are Mondays, so the 29th is Friday and the 30th is Saturday.

recs.q: How many degrees are there in the angle around a full circle?
recs.facts: A complete turn around the centre of a circle is 360 degrees.
recs.rel: A straight line makes 180 degrees and a right angle makes 90 degrees.

recs.q: How many daughters of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) passed away during his lifetime?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zainab, Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) passed away in his lifetime. Hazrat Fatima (RA) passed away about six months after him.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters in total.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of the word chaos?
recs.facts: Chaos means complete disorder and confusion. Its opposite is order.
recs.rel: The word chaos comes from the ancient Greek word for empty space.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word cherish?
recs.facts: To cherish means to hold dear and care for. Its opposite is to neglect or despise.
recs.rel: Cherish is often used with memories, such as to cherish a memory.

recs.q: In which year was the name Pakistan coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali?
recs.facts: Choudhry Rahmat Ali put forward the name Pakistan in 1933 in his pamphlet Now or Never.
recs.rel: The Lahore Resolution, which demanded separate Muslim states, was passed later in 1940.

recs.q: What do the five rings of the Olympic flag represent?
recs.facts: The five interlocked rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined together by the Olympic movement.
recs.rel: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background.

recs.q: What is the common difference in the series 4, 8, 12, 16?
recs.facts: 8 - 4 = 4, 12 - 8 = 4 and 16 - 12 = 4. So the difference is 4.
recs.rel: The next term in this series is 20.

recs.q: In which year was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution had been in force since 23 March 1956.

recs.q: Pakistani people are equal because of which common bond?
recs.facts: Pakistan was created in the name of Islam, and the Islamic teaching of equality unites its people despite different languages and cultures.
recs.rel: Pakistan has many languages and dresses but one common faith for the large majority.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word eradication?
recs.facts: Eradication means completely getting rid of or destroying something, which is elimination.
recs.rel: Smallpox is the best known disease to have been eradicated from the world, in 1980.

recs.q: Which of the following events took place in the 8th year of Hijri (Fateh Makkah, the conquest of Makkah)?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah peacefully with a large army in Ramadan 8 AH. Badr was in 2 AH, Uhud in 3 AH and Khandaq in 5 AH.
recs.rel: At the conquest the Prophet (PBUH) announced a general pardon for the people of Makkah.

recs.q: What is the full form of SCO?
recs.facts: SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a political, economic and security group of Eurasian countries.
recs.rel: Pakistan became a full member of the SCO in 2017.

recs.q: What is half of the diameter of a circle called?
recs.facts: The diameter is twice the radius, so half of the diameter is the radius.
recs.rel: The radius is the distance from the centre of a circle to its edge.

recs.q: Which is the largest (longest) surah of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran and has 286 ayat.
recs.rel: The shortest surah is Surah Al-Kausar with 3 ayat.

recs.q: Who led the Muslim army in the Battle (Ghazwa) of Badr?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH and the Muslim army was commanded by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself. The Muslims were about 313 men.
recs.rel: The Quraish army at Badr was commanded by Abu Jahl.

recs.q: Manchar Lake, the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan, is located in which district of Sindh?
recs.facts: Manchar Lake lies in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus River near Sehwan.
recs.rel: It is among the largest freshwater lakes in South Asia.

recs.q: What is a matrix in mathematics?
opts: A rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns
A single number with a sign
A curve drawn on a graph
recs.facts: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers (or symbols) arranged in horizontal rows and vertical columns.
recs.rel: The order of a matrix is written as number of rows by number of columns.

recs.q: What does the word Tanzil mean?
recs.facts: Tanzil is an Arabic word meaning sending down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.
recs.rel: The Quran says that it was sent down in stages over about 23 years.

recs.q: What is an obligatory act called in Islam?
recs.facts: An act that must be done and whose neglect is a sin is called Farz.
recs.rel: Wajib ranks just below Farz in the Hanafi school.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word panic?
recs.facts: Panic is wild fear. Calm (a peaceful, steady state) is its opposite.
recs.rel: Fear, alarm and terror are synonyms of panic.

recs.q: At which annual session of the All India Muslim League was the Pakistan Resolution passed in March 1940?
recs.facts: The Pakistan (Lahore) Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League in Lahore.
recs.rel: The session was held at Minto Park, Lahore, from 22 to 24 March 1940.

recs.q: How many princely states were there in British India at the time of partition in 1947?
recs.facts: About 562 princely states existed in British India in 1947. Each had to join India or Pakistan or stay independent.
recs.rel: Some sources give 565 because counting methods differ.

recs.q: What is the product of 3/2 and 2/3?
recs.facts: Multiply: (3 x 2) / (2 x 3) = 6/6 = 1. The two fractions are reciprocals of each other.
recs.rel: The product of a number and its reciprocal is always 1.

recs.q: According to the Hadith in Sahih Muslim, which prophet was a carpenter by profession?
recs.facts: Sahih Muslim reports that Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was a carpenter.
recs.rel: Hazrat Dawud (AS) made iron armour, and Hazrat Idris (AS) is commonly said to have been a tailor.

recs.q: Which game is played with a racket and a shuttlecock?
recs.facts: Badminton players hit a shuttlecock over a net using rackets.
recs.rel: Squash is played with a racket and a rubber ball inside a walled court.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word rash?
recs.facts: As an adjective, rash means acting without thinking about the results, so hasty and reckless.
recs.rel: As a noun, rash also means red spots on the skin.

recs.q: What type of number is 7/9?
recs.facts: 7/9 is a ratio of two integers, so it is a rational number.
recs.rel: Its decimal form 0.777... repeats forever.

recs.q: Which river is called the lifeline of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Indus is the longest river of Pakistan and its water supports most of the farming of the country, so it is called the lifeline of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Indus rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

recs.q: According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population lives in rural areas?
recs.facts: The 2023 census recorded about 61.2 percent rural and 38.8 percent urban population.
recs.rel: The earlier 2017 census showed about 63.6 percent rural population.

recs.q: Where is the Thal desert located in Pakistan?
opts: Between the Indus and Jhelum rivers in Punjab
In the Chagai district of Balochistan
In the Cholistan region near Bahawalpur
recs.facts: The Thal desert lies in the Punjab province in the area between the Indus and Jhelum rivers, covering districts such as Bhakkar, Layyah, Khushab and Mianwali.
recs.rel: The Thar desert is a different desert and lies in Sindh.

recs.q: What is the synonym of "troubled"?
recs.facts: "Troubled" means disturbed or anxious, which is close to worried or distressed.
recs.rel: The opposite of troubled is calm or peaceful.

recs.q: Under which Article of the Constitution of Pakistan is free and compulsory education a fundamental right?
recs.facts: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, makes free and compulsory education a right for children aged 5 to 16.
recs.rel: Article 19A gives the right to information.

recs.q: How many rivers were allotted to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960?
recs.facts: The treaty gave the three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan.
recs.rel: The three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, went to India.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 14th be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 14th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Sunday + 6 = Saturday.
recs.rel: The 14th is two weeks after the 1st minus one day, so it is the day before the 1st's weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 17th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 17th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Monday + 1 = Tuesday.
recs.rel: The 9th and 16th of this month are Mondays.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 26th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is Monday.
recs.rel: The 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th are all Sundays in this month.

recs.q: Which day is celebrated on 4th January every year?
recs.facts: World Braille Day is observed on 4 January, the birthday of Louis Braille, inventor of the Braille system.
recs.rel: The United Nations officially began observing it in 2019.

recs.q: On which side of Pakistan is Afghanistan situated?
recs.facts: Afghanistan lies along the western and north-western border of Pakistan. India is to the east and China to the north-east.
recs.rel: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border is called the Durand Line.

recs.q: Who is known as the founder of the technology company Apple?
recs.facts: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976 with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne and led it for many years.
recs.rel: Apple launched the iPhone in 2007 under Steve Jobs.

recs.q: What is the antonym of callous?
recs.facts: Callous means cold and unfeeling, so the opposite is compassionate.
recs.rel: Callous originally meant having hardened skin.

recs.q: According to the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan, who appointed the Prime Minister?
opts: The Speaker of the National Assembly
recs.facts: Under the 1956 Constitution the President appointed as Prime Minister the member of the National Assembly who had the confidence of the majority of its members.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution was the first constitution of Pakistan and was abrogated by Iskander Mirza in October 1958.

recs.q: Which word is made by arranging the letters POEARLD?
recs.facts: The letters P, O, E, A, R, L, D can be rearranged to spell LEOPARD, using all seven letters.
recs.rel: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, including northern Pakistan.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan become a nuclear (atomic) power?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai hills on 28 May 1998 and so became a declared nuclear power.
recs.rel: 28 May is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer in Pakistan.

recs.q: Who is known as Baba-e-Urdu (Father of Urdu)?
recs.facts: Maulvi Abdul Haq worked all his life for the promotion and development of the Urdu language and its dictionaries, so he is given the title Baba-e-Urdu.
recs.rel: He also founded the Anjuman Taraqqi-e-Urdu.

recs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: Put the pen ___ the basket.
recs.facts: Into shows movement from outside to the inside of something, which is what putting a pen in a basket means.
recs.rel: In shows position inside, while into shows movement towards the inside.

recs.q: In which type of brackets is a solution set written?
recs.facts: A solution set is a set, and sets are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.
recs.rel: Square brackets are used for matrices and for closed intervals.

recs.q: What is the fraction 11/7 called?
recs.facts: In 11/7 the numerator 11 is larger than the denominator 7, so it is an improper fraction. It equals 1 and 4/7.
recs.rel: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, such as 3/7.

recs.q: How many times were the modern Olympic Games cancelled because of world wars?
recs.facts: The Games were cancelled in 1916 (World War I), and in 1940 and 1944 (World War II). That makes three times.
recs.rel: The Olympics were postponed, not cancelled, in 2020 and held in Tokyo in 2021.

recs.q: Which country suffered the most deaths in World War II?
recs.facts: The Soviet Union lost an estimated 24 to 27 million people, mostly on the Eastern Front against Germany.
recs.rel: China also lost a very large number of people in the war.

recs.q: What is the total angle at the centre of a circle?
recs.facts: A full turn around the centre of a circle makes 360 degrees.
recs.rel: A semicircle makes an angle of 180 degrees at the centre.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to denounce?
recs.facts: To denounce means to publicly criticise or condemn something as wrong.
recs.rel: The noun form of denounce is denunciation.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to debate?
recs.facts: A debate is a formal discussion in which opposing views are put forward.
recs.rel: A debate usually ends with a vote or a decision by judges.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to rectify?
recs.facts: To rectify means to put something right or correct a mistake.
recs.rel: The word rectify comes from the Latin rectus, meaning right.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Children died ___ fever.
recs.facts: We use the preposition of with a cause of death, such as died of fever.
recs.rel: We say died of a disease but died in an accident.

recs.q: Which of these is the best conductor of electricity?
recs.facts: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals, higher than copper and gold.
recs.rel: Copper is the most widely used conductor because it is much cheaper than silver.

recs.q: What is the conjugate of the imaginary unit iota (i)?
recs.facts: The conjugate of 0 + 1i is 0 - 1i, which is -i.
recs.rel: The value of i squared is -1.

recs.q: What does the idiom 'a dark horse' mean?
opts: A little-known person who unexpectedly wins or succeeds
A person who is always late
recs.facts: A dark horse is a person or competitor about whom little is known but who may surprise everyone by winning. The idiom comes from horse racing.
recs.rel: The phrase became popular in politics after a surprise candidate won the US nomination in 1844.

recs.q: Which is the largest desert in the world by area?
recs.facts: A desert is an area with very little precipitation, and Antarctica, at about 14 million square km, is the largest. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
recs.rel: The Arctic Desert is the second largest and the Sahara is third.

recs.q: In which district of Punjab is Harappa located?
recs.facts: The ruins of Harappa lie near the Ravi River in Sahiwal district, Punjab.
recs.rel: Harappa was first excavated in the 1920s.

recs.q: In which year did Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, die?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
recs.rel: Company Bagh was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

recs.q: Who discovered micro-organisms (microscopic life)?
recs.facts: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observed bacteria and other tiny organisms with his own microscopes in the 1670s.
recs.rel: He is often called the father of microbiology.

recs.q: Where was the first All Pakistan Educational Conference held in 1947?
recs.facts: The first educational conference was held in Karachi in November and December 1947, soon after independence.
recs.rel: It was opened with a message from Quaid-e-Azam.

recs.q: In which year did Queen Elizabeth II visit Pakistan for the second time?
recs.facts: The Queen first visited Pakistan in 1961 and returned in October 1997, during the 50th anniversary of independence.
recs.rel: Her first visit was in 1961.

recs.q: What is the power set of the empty set?
opts: The set containing 0 and the empty set
The set containing the empty set
recs.facts: The empty set has one subset, itself, so its power set has 2 to the power 0 = 1 element, namely the set containing the empty set.
recs.rel: A set with n elements has 2 to the power n subsets.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: All people ___ the world are learning English.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is 'around the world', which means everywhere in the world.
recs.rel: 'All over the world' has the same meaning.

recs.q: Which game is known as the Gentleman's Game?
recs.facts: Cricket is called the gentleman's game because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship.
recs.rel: Cricket originated in England.

recs.q: Ali got 15 marks out of 60. What is his percentage?
recs.facts: Percentage = 15 divided by 60, times 100 = 0.25 times 100 = 25 percent.
recs.rel: 15 out of 60 is the same as one quarter of the marks.

recs.q: Who was the first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
recs.facts: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in Kashmir in 1948 and received the first Nishan-e-Haider.
recs.rel: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti received it for the 1965 war.

recs.q: What does the idiom snake in the grass mean?
opts: A treacherous person who pretends to be a friend
recs.facts: The idiom describes a person who appears friendly but secretly plans to harm you, like a snake hidden in grass.
recs.rel: The phrase comes from the Roman poet Virgil.

recs.q: What is the Indus River called in Hindi and Sanskrit?
recs.facts: The river is called Sindhu in Sanskrit and Hindi, and the name Sindhu gave rise to the words Sind, Hind and India.
recs.rel: The Persians pronounced Sindhu as Hindu, and the Greeks changed it to Indos, which became Indus.

recs.q: What is the antonym of "impoverished"?
recs.facts: Impoverished means made poor, so its opposite is wealthy or rich.
recs.rel: Affluent is another antonym of impoverished.

recs.q: How many member countries does the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) have?
recs.facts: The OIC has 57 member states spread over four continents.
recs.rel: It is the second largest intergovernmental organisation after the United Nations.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL located?
recs.facts: The General Secretariat of INTERPOL is in Lyon, France.
recs.rel: INTERPOL was earlier headquartered in Paris before moving to Lyon in 1989.

recs.q: Which is the current professional cricket league of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the franchise T20 league of Pakistan, played every year since 2016.
recs.rel: PSL matches are played in cities such as Karachi, Lahore, Multan and Rawalpindi.

recs.q: What is the value of the limit of sin x divided by x as x approaches 0?
recs.facts: This is a standard limit: as x approaches 0 (x in radians), sin x becomes almost equal to x, so the ratio tends to 1.
recs.rel: The same result gives that the limit of tan x divided by x is also 1 as x approaches 0.

recs.q: Who first introduced the photostat (photocopying) machine?
recs.facts: Chester Carlson, an American inventor, invented the dry photocopying process called xerography in 1938.
recs.rel: The first commercial xerographic copier was released by the Xerox company in 1959.

recs.q: Who has taken the most wickets in Test cricket?
recs.facts: Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka took 800 Test wickets, the highest ever.
recs.rel: Shane Warne is second with 708 and James Anderson third with 704; Wasim Akram took 414.

recs.q: To where did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah?
recs.facts: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Yathrib, which was later named Madinat-un-Nabi, or Madina.
recs.rel: The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this migration.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan win its first Olympic gold medal?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat India 1-0 in the hockey final at the Rome Olympics of 1960 to win its first gold.
recs.rel: The other golds came in 1968 at Mexico City and 1984 at Los Angeles.

recs.q: Who is called Shaheed-e-Millat in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi in 1951. He is therefore called Shaheed-e-Millat, the martyr of the nation.
recs.rel: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot at Company Bagh, which was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

recs.q: In which city is Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Al-Aqsa Mosque) located?
recs.facts: Bait-ul-Muqaddas is in Jerusalem, in Palestine. It was the first qibla of the Muslims.
recs.rel: The qibla was changed to the Kaaba in the second year of Hijra.

recs.q: What was the name of the brother of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS). He was also a prophet and helped Musa (AS) before Pharaoh.
recs.rel: Musa (AS) asked Allah to make Haroon (AS) his helper.

recs.q: Which term comes next in the series: A88, C76, F52, ?
recs.facts: Letters move forward by 2, 3, 4, so after F comes J. Numbers drop by 12, 24, 36: 88, 76, 52, 16. So the next term is J16.
recs.rel: When differences double or grow in steps, check the differences of the differences.

recs.q: Who discovered the nucleus of the atom?
recs.facts: Ernest Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus in 1911 through his gold foil experiment.
recs.rel: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 and J. J. Thomson discovered the electron.

recs.q: Yathrib is the old name of which city?
recs.facts: The city of Yathrib was renamed Madinah-tun-Nabi after the Hijrat of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Madinah is also called Madinah Munawwarah.

recs.q: What is photosynthesis?
opts: Making food by green plants using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
recs.facts: In photosynthesis, plants use chlorophyll in chloroplasts and sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
recs.rel: Photosynthesis releases the oxygen we breathe.

recs.q: Who won the Battle of Plassey (1757)?
recs.facts: The East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
recs.rel: The victory began British rule in India.

recs.q: With which surah does the Quran begin in its written order?
recs.facts: The first surah in the Mushaf (written order) is Surah Al-Fatiha, followed by Surah Al-Baqarah.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Fatiha has 7 verses and is recited in every rakat of prayer.

recs.q: If the diameter of a circle is 56, what is its radius?
recs.facts: Radius is half of the diameter. 56 / 2 = 28.
recs.rel: Diameter = 2 x radius.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word reasonable?
recs.facts: Reasonable means having good sense and being fair. Its synonym is sensible.
recs.rel: The opposite word is unreasonable.

recs.q: What was the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) according to Hazrat Aisha (RA)?
recs.facts: When asked about his character, Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.
recs.rel: This reply is reported in Sahih Muslim.

recs.q: In a room there are 18 girls and 6 boys. What percentage of the people in the room are boys?
recs.facts: Total people = 18 + 6 = 24. Percentage of boys = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.
recs.rel: The percentage of girls in the room is 75 percent.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: ____ you were sleeping, the telephone rang.
recs.facts: 'While' joins two actions that happen at the same time, and here it links a clause with a subject and verb.
recs.rel: 'During' is followed by a noun, not by a clause like 'you were sleeping'.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Throw the pen ___ the dustbin.
recs.facts: The preposition 'into' shows movement towards the inside of something, so the pen goes into the dustbin.
recs.rel: 'In' shows position while 'into' shows movement toward the inside.

recs.q: Change into indirect speech: She told, "It is a very cold day."
opts: She told that it is a very cold day.
She told that it was a very cold day.
She told that it had been a very cold day.
She told that it will be a very cold day.
recs.facts: The reporting verb is in the past tense, so the present tense "is" changes to the past tense "was". The quotation marks are removed and "that" is added.
recs.rel: In indirect speech, "today" changes to "that day" and "now" changes to "then".

recs.q: What is the antonym of "trivial"?
recs.facts: "Trivial" means of little importance, so its opposite is "important" or significant.
recs.rel: Synonyms of trivial include petty, minor and insignificant.

recs.q: On which date was the One Unit scheme enforced in West Pakistan?
recs.facts: The West Pakistan One Unit scheme was enforced on 14 October 1955, merging the western provinces and states into one unit.
recs.rel: One Unit was abolished by General Yahya Khan on 1 July 1970.

recs.q: Which Prime Minister of Pakistan was the first to visit China?
recs.facts: Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy visited China in October 1956 and was the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.
recs.rel: Pakistan recognised the People's Republic of China in January 1950.

recs.q: In a group of 24 people, 18 are women. What percentage of the group are men?
recs.rel: The women are 75% of the group.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: She said to me that she ___ TV.
recs.facts: The reporting verb said is in the past, so the present continuous is watching changes to was watching.
recs.rel: Were is used only with plural subjects or you.

recs.q: If the 19th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 26th be?
recs.facts: From the 19th to the 26th is 7 days, exactly one week, so the weekday is the same: Sunday.
recs.rel: Dates 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: Which session of the All India Muslim League passed the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution on 23 March 1940?
recs.facts: The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League held at Minto Park, Lahore, in March 1940.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam presided over this session, held from 22 to 24 March 1940.

recs.q: In which year was the present Constitution of Pakistan made?
recs.facts: The present Constitution was passed by the National Assembly in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.
recs.rel: It was drafted under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

recs.q: Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
recs.facts: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under the presidency of W. C. Bonnerjee.
recs.rel: A. O. Hume, the founder of the Congress, was its first general secretary.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word abhorrent?
recs.facts: Abhorrent means disgusting or hateful, so its opposite is admirable.
recs.rel: A synonym of abhorrent is detestable.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word abhorrent?
recs.facts: Abhorrent means causing strong disgust, which matches detestable.
recs.rel: The related noun is abhorrence, meaning strong hatred.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning of 'accomplished' when used for a person?
recs.facts: As an adjective, accomplished describes a person who is highly skilled or talented, such as an accomplished pianist.
recs.rel: As a verb form, accomplished also means achieved or completed.

recs.q: What is the meaning of 'admonished'?
recs.facts: To admonish someone is to warn or scold them firmly. Reprimand and rebuke are its synonyms.
recs.rel: The noun form is admonition, meaning a warning.

recs.q: Which part of speech describes or modifies a verb?
recs.facts: An adverb tells us how, when, where or how much an action happens. So it describes a verb.
recs.rel: An adverb can also modify an adjective or another adverb.

recs.q: An aeroplane flies in the air mainly because of which force?
recs.facts: The curved wings make air move faster over the top, creating lower pressure above and an upward force called lift. Lift must be greater than or equal to weight to fly.
recs.rel: The four forces on an aeroplane are lift, weight, thrust and drag.

recs.q: Which companion narrated the largest number of ahadith?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) is reported to have narrated about 5374 ahadith, the most of any companion.
recs.rel: Hazrat Aisha (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) are also among the major narrators.

recs.q: At which session of the All India Muslim League was the Lahore Resolution passed?
recs.facts: The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League, held at Lahore from 22 to 24 March 1940.
recs.rel: The resolution was moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq on 23 March 1940.

recs.q: Which word comes first alphabetically in a dictionary: Adidas or Addida?
recs.facts: Both words start with AD. The third letter of Addida is D and of Adidas is I, and D comes before I, so Addida comes first.
recs.rel: Dictionaries compare words letter by letter from the left until the first difference.

recs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: I always have a problem ____ my laptop.
recs.facts: The correct phrase in English is 'have a problem with' something.
recs.rel: Prepositions are fixed by usage, for example 'good at', 'suffer from' and 'problem with'.

recs.q: What is the antonym of obnoxious?
recs.facts: Obnoxious means very unpleasant or offensive, so its opposite is pleasant.
recs.rel: Synonyms of obnoxious are odious and objectionable.

recs.q: What is the antonym of disingenuous?
recs.facts: Disingenuous means not sincere or pretending to know less, so the opposite is candid, meaning frank and honest.
recs.rel: Ingenuous means innocent and frank.

recs.q: What is the antonym of spirited?
recs.facts: Spirited means full of energy and courage, so the opposite is lifeless or dull.
recs.rel: Wild is not an antonym of spirited, it is the antonym of tame.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word astonished?
recs.facts: Astonished means greatly surprised or amazed.
recs.rel: Synonyms of astonished include amazed, stunned and startled.

recs.q: In which year did the United States attack Afghanistan after the 9/11 events?
recs.facts: The US-led attack on Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001, after the attacks of 11 September 2001.
recs.rel: The US-led forces finally withdrew from Afghanistan in August 2021.

recs.q: What is the average of the first five natural numbers?
recs.facts: The first five natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Their sum is 15 and 15 / 5 = 3.
recs.rel: The average of the first n natural numbers is (n + 1) / 2.

recs.q: In aviation, in which unit is altitude commonly measured internationally?
recs.facts: International civil aviation standards use feet for altitude and flight levels.
recs.rel: A few countries, such as China and Russia, have used metres for altitude.

recs.q: In which year did Benazir Bhutto become Prime Minister of Pakistan for the second time?
recs.facts: Her first term was from 1988 to 1990 and her second term started in October 1993 after the 1993 elections.
recs.rel: Her second government was dismissed in 1996.

recs.q: Rana Bhagwandas, who served as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religious community?
recs.facts: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu from Sindh and became the first non-Muslim to serve as Chief Justice of Pakistan, in an acting capacity in 2007.
recs.rel: He was a judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan from 1994 until he retired in 2009.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the Pakistan-China border according to most Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks give the length of the border with China as about 523 km, running along the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: Sources differ, and some give about 596 km; the Khunjerab Pass is the only border crossing.

recs.q: Which angel brought the message (revelation) of Allah to the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Jibrail (A.S.) carried the revelation from Allah to the Prophet (S.A.W.). He is the angel of revelation.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jibrail (A.S.) is also called Ruh-ul-Amin.

recs.q: If there are 2 cows and the number of camels is twice the number of cows, how many camels are there?
recs.facts: Camels = 2 x 2 = 4.
recs.rel: Always read whether the question asks for camels only or for the total animals.

recs.q: For how many years did Hazrat Abdul Muttalib take care of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) after his mother passed away?
recs.facts: The Prophet (S.A.W.) was 6 when his mother died and 8 when his grandfather died, so Abdul Muttalib cared for him for about 2 years.
recs.rel: After that, his uncle Abu Talib took care of him.

recs.q: What does the idiom 'to bell the cat' mean?
opts: To take a dangerous task for the benefit of the group
recs.facts: The idiom comes from a fable in which mice wanted someone to tie a bell on the cat. It means to take on a risky task on behalf of others.
recs.rel: The fable is attributed to Aesop.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word charming?
recs.facts: Charming means pleasing and attractive. The opposite is unattractive or ugly.
recs.rel: Charming comes from the Latin word carmen, meaning song or spell.

recs.q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan before General Asim Munir?
recs.facts: General Qamar Javed Bajwa served as Chief of Army Staff from November 2016 to November 2022. General Asim Munir then took over from him.
recs.rel: General Raheel Sharif served before Bajwa, from 2013 to 2016.

recs.q: What is the common difference in the series 2, 6, 10, 14?
recs.facts: Each term is 4 more than the one before: 6 - 2 = 4, 10 - 6 = 4, 14 - 10 = 4.
recs.rel: A series with a constant difference is called an arithmetic progression.

recs.q: What is the conjugate of the complex number 8 - 3i?
recs.facts: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi, so the sign of the imaginary part changes: 8 + 3i.
recs.rel: The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.

recs.q: What is the idiom to throw cold water on something?
recs.facts: To throw cold water on a plan or idea means to discourage it or show doubt about it.
recs.rel: A similar idiom is to dampen someone's spirits.

recs.q: In a field there is 1 cow, the donkeys are twice the number of cows, and there are 7 horses. How many animals are in the field?
recs.facts: Donkeys are 2 times 1, which is 2. Total animals are 1 cow plus 2 donkeys plus 7 horses, which is 10.
recs.rel: If the question counted only donkeys and horses, the total would be 9.

recs.q: What is the derivative of 2x sin x with respect to x?
recs.facts: Use the product rule: d/dx (u v) = u'v + u v' with u = 2x and v = sin x. This gives 2 sin x + 2x cos x.
recs.rel: The product rule is also called Leibniz's rule.

recs.q: What is the derivative of ln x with respect to x?
recs.facts: The natural logarithm ln x has derivative 1/x for x greater than zero. This is a standard result of calculus.
recs.rel: The derivative of e to the power x is e to the power x itself.

recs.q: Where is the Kot Diji fort located, in terms of district?
recs.facts: Kot Diji is a town in Khairpur district of Sindh. Its fort was built by the Talpur rulers.
recs.rel: Kot Diji is also an important pre-Harappan archaeological site.

recs.q: Which of the following is a three-dimensional shape?
recs.facts: A cube has length, width and height, so it is three-dimensional. Square, triangle and circle are flat two-dimensional shapes.
recs.rel: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

recs.q: Which of these antonyms is opposite in meaning to 'disgusting'?
recs.facts: Disgusting means very unpleasant. Delightful is the opposite, meaning very pleasant.
recs.rel: Repulsive and foul are synonyms of disgusting.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'disgusting'?
recs.facts: Disgusting means causing strong dislike or sickness. Revolting has nearly the same meaning.
recs.rel: Other synonyms are repulsive, nasty and foul.

recs.q: Which group of vitamins does not dissolve in water?
recs.facts: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. They dissolve in fat and not in water.
recs.rel: Vitamins B-complex and C are water-soluble.

recs.q: In which division of Balochistan is Gwadar located?
recs.facts: Gwadar district is part of Makran Division in southwestern Balochistan.
recs.rel: Makran division also includes Kech (Turbat) and Panjgur districts.

recs.q: How many districts does Punjab (Pakistan) have at present?
recs.facts: Punjab has 41 districts grouped into 10 divisions. A claim of 45 districts was officially rejected.
recs.rel: Earlier counts were 36 and then 40 before the newer districts were added.

recs.q: Which document served as the basis for the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Objective Resolution of 1949 became the preamble and guiding basis of the constitutions of Pakistan, including 1973.
recs.rel: It was made a substantive part of the constitution by Article 2-A in 1985.

recs.q: Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan deals with which right?
recs.facts: Article 25-A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16.
recs.rel: The 18th Amendment was passed in April 2010.

recs.q: For about how long did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan remain in force?
recs.facts: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958. This is about two and a half years.
recs.rel: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic under this constitution.

recs.q: Which of the following lists the elementary row operations of a matrix?
recs.facts: A row can be swapped with another, multiplied by a non-zero constant, or have a multiple of another row added to it.
recs.rel: Elementary row operations do not change the solution set of a linear system.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to end in smoke'?
recs.facts: The idiom means that a plan or effort fails and produces no result.
recs.rel: A similar idiom is 'to go up in smoke'.

recs.q: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
recs.facts: Mount Everest lies in the Mahalangur sub-range of the Himalayas on the Nepal and China (Tibet) border.
recs.rel: K2, the second highest peak, is in the Karakoram range.

recs.q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still exists today?
recs.facts: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is the only one of the original seven wonders that still stands.
recs.rel: It was built about 2560 BC as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu.

recs.q: Ali is 2 years old and Faraz is twice Ali's age. How old is Faraz?
recs.facts: Faraz's age = 2 x 2 = 4 years.
recs.rel: After 2 more years Ali will be 4 and Faraz will be 6.

recs.q: Which prophet was thrown into fire by Namrood (Nimrod)?
recs.facts: Namrood threw Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) into a big fire, but Allah made it cool and safe for him.
recs.rel: This event is mentioned in Surah Al-Anbiya of the Quran.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word fondness?
recs.facts: Fondness means a feeling of liking or love, which is the same as affection.
recs.rel: Other close words for fondness are liking, love and attachment.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word fondness?
recs.facts: Fondness means liking, so its opposite is dislike.
recs.rel: Aversion and hatred are also opposites of fondness.

recs.q: From which ruler did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh in 712 AD?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Brahman ruler of Sindh, in 712 AD.
recs.rel: The conquest began after Arab ships were attacked near Debal, and Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam.

recs.q: Which city of Pakistan is known as the City of Gardens?
recs.facts: Lahore is called the City of Gardens because of its many Mughal and public gardens such as Shalimar and Jinnah Garden.
recs.rel: Lahore is also called the cultural capital of Pakistan.

recs.q: Greenland is an autonomous territory of which country?
recs.facts: Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
recs.rel: Its capital is Nuuk.

recs.q: Who was Hazrat Sarah (AS)?
opts: Wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)
recs.facts: Hazrat Sarah was the first wife of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS).
recs.rel: Hazrat Hajra (AS), the second wife of Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).

recs.q: What does the Arabic word Hijrat mean?
recs.facts: Hijrat means to leave one's homeland and migrate to another place, especially for the sake of faith.
recs.rel: The Islamic Hijri calendar begins from the Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD.

recs.q: What does the idiom "to pick holes" mean?
recs.facts: To pick holes in something means to look for its weak points and criticise it.
recs.rel: A similar phrase is "to find fault with".

recs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: We are pinning all our hopes ___ the new manager.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is "pin hopes on someone", meaning to depend on that person for success.
recs.rel: The same preposition is used in "pin the blame on someone".

recs.q: What is an identity matrix?
opts: A square matrix with all elements zero
A square matrix with 1 on the main diagonal and 0 elsewhere
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements equal to 1
recs.facts: An identity matrix is a square matrix whose main diagonal elements are all 1 and all other elements are 0.
recs.rel: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix of a suitable size leaves it unchanged.

recs.q: Which famous event took place in 8 Hijri?
recs.facts: The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH.
recs.rel: Battle of Hunain and the Battle of Muta also took place in 8 AH.

recs.q: What is the main use of insulin in medicine?
recs.facts: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is given to diabetic patients who cannot make enough of it.
recs.rel: Insulin is made by the beta cells of the pancreas.

recs.q: Who was Iskander Ali Mirza?
opts: The first Governor General of Pakistan
The first Prime Minister of Pakistan
The first Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan
recs.facts: Iskander Ali Mirza became Governor General in 1955 and then the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution.
recs.rel: He was removed by Ayub Khan after the 1958 martial law.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'indigenous'?
recs.facts: Indigenous means originating in or belonging naturally to a place, which is the meaning of native.
recs.rel: The word comes from the Latin indigena, meaning born in the country.

recs.q: On what date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
recs.facts: Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
recs.rel: Pakistan was the 56th member state of the UN.

recs.q: Pakistan is mainly what kind of country in terms of its economy and land use?
recs.facts: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy and a large part of its population depends on it.
recs.rel: The Indus plain of Punjab and Sindh is the main farming region.

recs.q: Who is the Federal Minister for Law and Justice of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Azam Nazeer Tarar is the Federal Minister for Law and Justice in the present government, as reported in 2026.
recs.rel: Farogh Naseem held the post earlier, in the 2021 government of Imran Khan.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: Z, Y, X, ?
recs.facts: The letters go backward in the alphabet one place at a time: Z, Y, X, then W.
recs.rel: W is the 23rd letter of the English alphabet.

recs.q: How many daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) died during his lifetime?
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters. Zainab, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum (RA) died in his lifetime, and only Fatimah (RA) died after him, about six months later.
recs.rel: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married two of the daughters, Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum, and is called Dhun-Nurayn.

recs.q: Who liberated Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) from the Crusaders in 1187 AD?
recs.facts: Salahuddin Ayyubi defeated the Crusaders in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 and then took back Jerusalem. He was the founder of the Ayyubid dynasty.
recs.rel: Jerusalem was first conquered by the Muslims in 637 AD under Hazrat Umar (RA).

recs.q: Which is the longest river of Pakistan, also called the Sindh river?
recs.facts: The Indus River is about 2,900 km long and is the longest river of Pakistan. It is also called Sindh or Abaseen.
recs.rel: It starts near Mount Kailash in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

recs.q: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as Umm-ul-Masakin (Mother of the Poor)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA) was famous for feeding and helping the poor, so she was called Umm-ul-Masakin.
recs.rel: She died soon after marriage, during the lifetime of the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: What does the word burgle mean?
opts: To enter a building illegally in order to steal
recs.facts: To burgle means to break into a house or building to steal things, and the person who does it is a burglar.
recs.rel: Burglary is different from robbery, which involves force against a person.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word compact?
opts: Closely packed and small in size
recs.facts: Compact means closely and neatly packed together, and taking little space.
recs.rel: A compact disc was named for its small, dense format.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the World Bank?
recs.facts: Pakistan joined the World Bank and the IMF on 11 July 1950.
recs.rel: The World Bank headquarters is in Washington DC.

recs.q: In which game has Pakistan won Olympic gold medals?
recs.facts: Pakistan won Olympic gold three times in hockey, in 1960, 1968 and 1984.
recs.rel: Pakistan also won a bronze in Tokyo 1964 in hockey.

recs.q: What is the commonly quoted range of Pakistan's Babur (Hatf-VII) cruise missile?
recs.facts: The Babur ground-launched cruise missile, first tested in 2005, is commonly given a range of about 700 km. Newer versions are reported with different ranges.
recs.rel: Sources differ because later versions such as Babur-1B and Babur-3 have other stated ranges.

recs.q: What is the antonym of modesty?
recs.facts: Modesty means not showing off or thinking too highly of oneself. The opposite is arrogance, which is excessive pride.
recs.rel: Vanity is another word opposite to modesty.

recs.q: Which mountain range lies along the Sindh side of Pakistan, on the border with Balochistan?
recs.facts: The Kirthar Range runs north to south along the Sindh and Balochistan border. Its highest point is Zardak Peak.
recs.rel: The Kirthar Range is the southern extension of the Sulaiman Range.

recs.q: Which holy book was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS)?
recs.facts: The Torah (Taurat) was revealed to Hazrat Musa (AS) on Mount Tur.
recs.rel: Zabur was revealed to Dawud (AS) and Injeel to Isa (AS).

recs.q: What comes next in the series: Z3, W5, T7, ?
recs.facts: The letters go back by 3 each time: Z, W, T, Q. The numbers go up by 2: 3, 5, 7, 9. So the next term is Q9.
recs.rel: Letter series are solved by counting positions in the alphabet.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of NASA located?
recs.facts: NASA, the United States space agency, has its headquarters in Washington, D.C.
recs.rel: NASA was founded in 1958.

recs.q: What does NATO stand for?
recs.facts: NATO stands for North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance formed in 1949.
recs.rel: NATO headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.

recs.q: Who was Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar?
opts: A leader of the Pakistan Movement and Governor of Punjab
The first Prime Minister of Pakistan
recs.facts: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar was a senior Muslim League leader and a close associate of Quaid-e-Azam. He later served as Governor of Punjab.
recs.rel: Nishtar Hospital in Multan is named after him.
