recs.rel: In the same battle many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred, which led to the first compilation of the Quran.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'at arm's length'?
opts: At a safe distance, not too close
recs.facts: To keep someone at arm's length means to avoid becoming too close or familiar with them.
recs.rel: The idiom comes from the idea of stretching out your arm to keep a person away.

recs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word Muhajireen?
recs.facts: Muhajireen is the plural of Muhajir, which means one who migrates. It is used for the Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madina.
recs.rel: The Muslims of Madina who helped them are called Ansar, meaning helpers.

recs.q: In which Surah is the command 'Stand up (to pray) at night, except a little'?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Muzzammil (73), verse 2, tells the Prophet (PBUH) to stand in prayer at night except for a small part.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Muzzammil is the 73rd Surah and was revealed in Makkah.

recs.q: In whose room did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) spend his last days and pass away?
recs.facts: During his last illness the Prophet (PBUH) took permission from his wives and stayed in the room of Hazrat Aisha (RA) in Madina, where he passed away in 11 AH.
recs.rel: He is buried in the same room, which is now inside Masjid-e-Nabawi.

recs.q: In which year did the Black Lives Matter movement begin?
recs.facts: The phrase Black Lives Matter started as a hashtag in 2013 in the USA after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
recs.rel: The movement became worldwide in 2020 after the death of George Floyd.

recs.q: What is the characteristic of the common logarithm of 2179?
recs.facts: The number 2179 has 4 digits in its whole part, so the characteristic is 4 - 1 = 3.
recs.rel: The decimal part of a logarithm is called the mantissa.

recs.q: What is the approximate value of log 0.9 (base 10)?
recs.facts: Since 0.9 is less than 1, its common logarithm is negative. Log 0.9 = log 9 - log 10 = 0.9542 - 1 = -0.0458.
recs.rel: Log of 1 is 0 for every valid base.

recs.q: Which country has the longest border with China?
recs.facts: China shares about 4,700 km of border with Mongolia, which is the longest, slightly more than its border with Russia.
recs.rel: China has land borders with 14 countries, the most in the world together with Russia.

recs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
opts: We look forward to win the match.
We look forward to winning the match.
We look forward to won the match.
We look forward for win the match.
recs.facts: The phrase look forward to is followed by a gerund (verb plus ing), because to is a preposition here. So winning is correct.
recs.rel: Similar phrases are: used to doing, object to doing and in favour of doing.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to lose heart'?
recs.facts: To lose heart means to lose hope or courage and become discouraged.
recs.rel: The opposite idiom is to take heart, meaning to become more hopeful.

recs.q: What was the last major ghazwa of the Muslims against the Quraish of Makkah?
recs.facts: The Muslims conquered Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE), which ended the war with the Quraish.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah after the conquest.

recs.q: In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are male. What is the percentage of males?
recs.facts: Percentage = 2/3 x 100 = 66.67%.
recs.rel: The remaining 1/3 are females, which is 33.33%.

recs.q: According to the Holy Quran, killing one innocent person is like killing whom?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul, it is as if he killed all of mankind.
recs.rel: The same verse says saving one life is like saving all of mankind.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the idiom "man of straw"?
opts: A person of no substance or strength
recs.facts: A man of straw is a weak person or an imaginary opponent with no real substance.
recs.rel: Straw is light and weak, which is why the idiom describes someone without real strength.

recs.q: Where is Masjid Qiblatain (Masjid-e-Zulqiblatain) located?
recs.facts: It is in Madinah, where the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer when the command came to turn towards the Kaaba.
recs.rel: The qibla was changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas to the Kaaba in 2 AH.

recs.q: What is the SI unit of mass?
recs.facts: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).
recs.rel: Weight is a force and is measured in newtons.

recs.q: What is the correct relation between the arithmetic mean (A.M), geometric mean (G.M) and harmonic mean (H.M) of positive numbers?
opts: A.M is greater than or equal to G.M, which is greater than or equal to H.M
H.M is greater than or equal to G.M, which is greater than or equal to A.M
G.M is greater than or equal to A.M, which is greater than or equal to H.M
All three are always different and unrelated
recs.facts: For positive numbers, A.M is at least G.M, which is at least H.M, with equality only when all numbers are equal.
recs.rel: For two numbers a and b, G.M squared equals A.M times H.M.

recs.q: What are the signs for greater than and less than called in mathematics?
recs.facts: Signs like greater than and less than show that two quantities are not equal, so they are inequality symbols.
recs.rel: The equals sign shows equality.

recs.q: Which word fills the blank: You have not seen me ___ we met last time?
recs.facts: The present perfect tense (have not seen) is used with since to show a starting point in the past, so since is correct.
recs.rel: For is used with a period of time, while since is used with a point in time.

recs.q: What does the word Hidayah mean?
recs.facts: Hidayah is an Arabic word meaning guidance, especially guidance to the right path.
recs.rel: Al-Hadi, the Guide, is one of the names of Allah.

recs.q: What does the word Hukm mean?
recs.facts: Hukm is an Arabic word meaning command, order or ruling (judgement).
recs.rel: Its plural Ahkam is used for the rules of Islamic law.

recs.q: What does Fiqh mean?
recs.facts: Fiqh literally means deep understanding and is the science of deriving Islamic rules from the Quran and Sunnah.
recs.rel: Imam Abu Hanifa is the founder of the Hanafi school of Fiqh.

recs.q: Who are the Muhajirs in Islamic history?
opts: Those Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madina
recs.facts: Muhajir means one who migrates, and the term is used for the Companions who left Makkah and migrated to Madina.
recs.rel: The Muslims of Madina who helped them are called the Ansar.

recs.q: What does the word Blind mean?
recs.facts: A blind person has no ability to see.
recs.rel: Louis Braille, who was blind, invented the Braille reading system.

recs.q: What does the word Climb mean?
recs.facts: To climb means to go up something such as a hill, tree or ladder.
recs.rel: Its antonym is descend.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word aqua?
recs.facts: Aqua comes from Latin and means water.
recs.rel: An aquarium is a tank of water for fish.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word coarsest?
recs.facts: Coarse means rough and not smooth, so coarsest means the most rough.
recs.rel: The antonym of coarse is fine.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word decompose?
opts: To rot or break down into simpler parts
recs.facts: To decompose means to break down into smaller parts, as dead plants and animals rot.
recs.rel: Bacteria and fungi are called decomposers in nature.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word expansive?
opts: Wide-ranging or covering a large area
recs.facts: Expansive means covering a wide area or range, or friendly and open in manner.
recs.rel: The noun form is expansion.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word opaque?
opts: Not allowing light to pass through
recs.facts: An opaque material blocks light, so one cannot see through it.
recs.rel: Glass is transparent, while wood is opaque.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word polite?
recs.facts: A polite person is courteous and shows good manners to others.
recs.rel: The antonym of polite is rude.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word spongy?
opts: Soft and full of small holes like a sponge
recs.facts: Spongy means soft, springy and porous like a sponge.
recs.rel: A sponge can absorb a lot of liquid.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word stupid?
recs.facts: Stupid describes someone who shows poor judgement or lacks intelligence.
recs.rel: The antonym of stupid is intelligent.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word suspicious?
opts: Feeling or causing doubt and distrust
recs.facts: A suspicious person doubts others, and a suspicious thing causes doubt.
recs.rel: The noun form is suspicion.

recs.q: How many delegates attended the first session of the Indian National Congress in Bombay in 1885?
recs.facts: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 with 72 delegates.
recs.rel: It was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

recs.q: In which game did Pakistan win its first Olympic medal?
recs.facts: Pakistan won its first Olympic medal, a silver in hockey, at Melbourne in 1956.
recs.rel: Pakistan has won three Olympic gold medals, all in hockey.

recs.q: In which continent is Moscow, the capital of Russia, located?
recs.facts: Moscow lies on the Moskva River in the western part of Russia, which is in the European part of the country. So it is counted as a European city.
recs.rel: Moscow is the largest city entirely in Europe by population.

recs.q: The Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909 were related to which country?
recs.facts: These reforms were the Indian Councils Act 1909, passed by the British government for British India. They gave Muslims separate electorates.
recs.rel: Lord Minto was the Viceroy and John Morley was the Secretary of State for India.

recs.q: What is the minimum number of ayat (verses) in a surah of the Quran?
recs.facts: The shortest surahs, Al-Asr, Al-Kawthar and An-Nasr, each have 3 ayat. No surah has fewer.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 ayat.

recs.q: Who is the current Foreign Minister of Pakistan (2026)?
recs.facts: Mohammad Ishaq Dar serves as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan. He was still in office in August 2026 according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
recs.rel: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari was Foreign Minister from 2022 to 2023 before Ishaq Dar took the post in 2024.

recs.q: Who was the first Finance Minister of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Malik Ghulam Muhammad was Finance Minister in the first cabinet of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1947. He later became the third Governor General.
recs.rel: He presented the first budget of Pakistan in 1948.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan launch its first rocket into space, the Rehbar-1?
recs.facts: Rehbar-1 was launched from Sonmiani in Balochistan on 7 June 1962 by SUPARCO. It made Pakistan the third country in Asia and the tenth in the world to launch a rocket into space.
recs.rel: SUPARCO was established in 1961.

recs.q: Find the missing number in the series: 66, 63, 56, 45, ?
recs.facts: The differences are minus 3, minus 7, minus 11, so the next difference is minus 15. Then 45 minus 15 equals 30.
recs.rel: The differences themselves fall by 4 each time.

recs.q: What is the synonym of modesty?
recs.facts: Modesty means a humble and unassuming attitude. Humility has the same meaning.
recs.rel: Modesty can also mean decent behaviour in dress.

recs.q: Who are called Ummul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers)?
opts: Female companions who fought in battles
recs.facts: The Quran calls the wives of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) the mothers of the believers. This is a title of respect.
recs.rel: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first of the Ummul-Momineen.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, which day will the 16th be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 16th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is one day after Monday, which is Tuesday.
recs.rel: The 8th and 15th of that month would also be Mondays.

recs.q: Which two cities does the M-2 motorway connect?
recs.facts: The M-2 is the Lahore-Islamabad Motorway, about 367 km long. It opened in 1997.
recs.rel: It is also known as the Salt Range Motorway because it passes through the Salt Range.

recs.q: A train is moving at 45 km per hour. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
recs.facts: 5 minutes is 5/60 = 1/12 hour. Distance = 45 x 1/12 = 3.75 km.
recs.rel: Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives the distance covered in one minute.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Delhi, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Sibbi.
recs.facts: Delhi, Ahmedabad and Mumbai are cities of India. Sibbi (Sibi) is a city of Balochistan, Pakistan.
recs.rel: Sibi is famous for its annual Sibi Mela and its very hot summers.

recs.q: Which term comes next in the series: B5, D7, F9, H11, ?
recs.facts: Letters skip one letter each time: B, D, F, H, J. Numbers go up by 2: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. So the next term is J13.
recs.rel: Skipping one letter means moving forward by 2 positions in the alphabet.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, ?
recs.facts: The series is made of odd numbers, each 2 more than the one before. 9 + 2 = 11.
recs.rel: Odd numbers always differ by 2.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 15, 11, 8, 6, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -4, -3, -2, so the next difference is -1. 6 - 1 = 5.
recs.rel: Here the amount subtracted gets smaller by 1 each step.

recs.q: Which number is missing: 19, 38, 57, ?, 95
recs.facts: The numbers are multiples of 19: 19 x 1, 19 x 2, 19 x 3, 19 x 4 = 76, 19 x 5 = 95.
recs.rel: Check the last term: 95 divided by 19 is 5, so the pattern fits.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 2, 5, 9, 14, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6. 14 + 6 = 20.
recs.rel: When the differences increase by 1 each time, the series is quadratic.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 22, 17, 13, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -5, -4, so the next difference is -3. 13 - 3 = 10.
recs.rel: The following term would then be 10 - 2 = 8.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 3, 9, 27, ?
recs.facts: Each term is multiplied by 3: 3 x 3 = 9, 9 x 3 = 27, 27 x 3 = 81.
recs.rel: This is a geometric series with common ratio 3.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 63, 57, 45, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -6, -12, so the next is -24 (doubling each time). 45 - 24 = 21.
recs.rel: The next difference after that would be -48.

recs.q: What is the mean of 6 and -9?
recs.rel: The mean of two numbers is their sum divided by 2.

recs.q: In the commonly taught order of the five pillars of Islam, at which number does Namaz (Salah) come?
recs.facts: The usual order taught in Pakistan is Kalima (Shahada), Salah, Roza (Sawm), Zakat and Hajj. So Salah is the second pillar.
recs.rel: Some hadith narrations list the pillars in a slightly different order.

recs.q: In which continent is the River Nile located?
recs.facts: The Nile flows through northeastern Africa, mainly Uganda, Sudan and Egypt, and ends in the Mediterranean Sea.
recs.rel: The Nile is generally counted among the longest rivers in the world.

recs.q: What is the sum of 2^2 + 4^2 + 6^2 + ... + (2n)^2?
recs.facts: The sum is 4(1^2+2^2+...+n^2) = 4 x n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = 2n(n+1)(2n+1)/3. Since 2n+2 = 2(n+1), option (a) gives 2n(2n+1) x 2(n+1)/6, which is the same.
recs.rel: The sum of squares of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word notorious?
recs.facts: Notorious means known for bad deeds, so its opposite is reputable, meaning having a good name.
recs.rel: Infamous and scandalous are synonyms of notorious, not antonyms.

recs.q: Asad is 3 times as old as Amna when Amna is 6 years old. Now Amna is 10 years old. What is Asad's age now?
recs.facts: When Amna was 6, Asad was 3 x 6 = 18, so Asad is 12 years older. Now Amna is 10, so Asad is 10 + 12 = 22 years.
recs.rel: The difference between two people's ages always stays the same.

recs.q: Ali is 3 years older than his brother. What will be Ali's age when his brother is 11 years old?
recs.facts: The age gap stays 3 years. When the brother is 11, Ali is 11 + 3 = 14 years.
recs.rel: In age problems, the difference in ages never changes with time.

recs.q: If you can see through an object but the view is blurry, what is the object called?
recs.facts: A translucent object lets some light pass but scatters it, so things look blurry. A transparent object shows a clear view.
recs.rel: Frosted glass is a common example of a translucent material.

recs.q: In which year was the Objective Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Objective Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949 during the time of Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan.
recs.rel: It later became a preamble to the constitutions of Pakistan and is now part of the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: In which month was Namaz made obligatory during the Mairaj?
recs.facts: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Mairaj, which is traditionally dated 27 Rajab.
recs.rel: Dates of Mairaj differ slightly in sources, but Rajab is the common view.

recs.q: In which year did the United States attack and occupy Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The US led an invasion of Afghanistan in October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.
recs.rel: US forces left Afghanistan in August 2021.

recs.q: Which is the odd one out: India, Pakistan, China, Spain?
recs.facts: India, Pakistan and China are Asian countries, while Spain is in Europe.
recs.rel: Spain's capital is Madrid.

recs.q: Which is the official language of Pakistan, used in government alongside the national language Urdu?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution makes Urdu the national language and keeps English as the official language for government use.
recs.rel: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the official name of the legislature of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Parliament of Pakistan is officially called Majlis-e-Shoora and has the National Assembly and the Senate.
recs.rel: The President is also a part of the Majlis-e-Shoora.

recs.q: What was the old name of Beijing?
recs.facts: Beijing was long known in English as Peking.
recs.rel: Beijing is the capital of China.

recs.q: Which word is the closest opposite of resentment?
recs.facts: Resentment is bitter anger over unfair treatment. Gratitude (thankfulness and goodwill) is its opposite feeling.
recs.rel: Other opposites of resentment are goodwill and forgiveness.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word clean?
recs.facts: Clean means free from dirt. The word with the opposite meaning is dirty.
recs.rel: Pure, neat and fresh are all close in meaning to clean.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word expensive?
recs.facts: Expensive means high in price. Cheap means low in price, so it is the opposite.
recs.rel: Costly, valuable and precious are synonyms of expensive.

recs.q: What is the opposite of the word retain?
recs.facts: Retain means to keep or continue to have something. Release (let go) is the opposite.
recs.rel: Another opposite of retain is discard.

recs.q: Which statement about the number 39 is correct?
opts: It is an odd composite number
recs.facts: 39 is not divisible by 2, so it is odd. 39 = 3 x 13, so it has factors other than 1 and itself and is composite, not prime.
recs.rel: The only even prime number is 2.

recs.q: Which number cancels out 15 when the two are added together (the additive inverse of 15)?
recs.facts: 15 + (-15) = 0, so -15 cancels out 15 in addition.
recs.rel: The multiplicative inverse of 15 is 1/15, because 15 x 1/15 = 1.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word overt?
recs.facts: Overt means open and visible, while covert means hidden or secret.
recs.rel: A synonym of overt is open or obvious.

recs.q: What is a synonym of the word pacifist?
recs.facts: A pacifist believes in peace and rejects war, so peace lover (peacemaker) is a synonym.
recs.rel: The dove is a common symbol of peace and pacifism.

recs.q: In which city was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement of 1963 signed?
recs.facts: The agreement was signed in Beijing (then written Peking) on 2 March 1963 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Chinese Foreign Minister Chen Yi.
recs.rel: The agreement settled the border between Pakistan and the Xinjiang region of China.

recs.q: On what basis is the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chosen?
opts: Elected by the members of the Provincial Assembly, as the leader of the majority
Elected directly by the people of the province
recs.facts: Under Article 130 of the Constitution, the Provincial Assembly elects the Chief Minister, who must command the confidence of the majority of members.
recs.rel: The Governor of the province appoints the person elected by the assembly.

recs.q: Who first suggested the name Pakistan?
recs.facts: Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
recs.rel: Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word panic?
recs.facts: Panic is a sudden strong fear that makes people act without thinking.
recs.rel: The word comes from Pan, the Greek god of the wild.

recs.q: Which book is generally regarded as the first book written in the Pashto language?
recs.facts: Khair-ul-Bayan, written by Bayazid Ansari (Pir Roshan) in the 16th century, is generally regarded as the first Pashto book.
recs.rel: Pata Khazana is a disputed anthology of early Pashto poets, so some sources name other early works.

recs.q: A bus has 30 passengers and two thirds of them are boys, the rest are girls. How many girls are there?
recs.rel: The girls are 1/3 of the passengers, which is 33.33 percent.

recs.q: Change the narration into indirect speech: She said to me, "Can you give me your pen?"
opts: She asked me if I could give her my pen.
She told me that can I give her my pen.
She said me whether I can give her pen.
She asked me that I can give me my pen.
recs.facts: A question in direct speech becomes a reporting verb asked plus if, and the tense and pronouns change: can becomes could, you becomes I, me becomes her.
recs.rel: In indirect speech a yes or no question is joined with if or whether and has no question mark.

recs.q: A car travels at 60 km per hour. How much distance will it cover in 20 minutes?
recs.facts: 20 minutes is 20/60 = 1/3 of an hour. Distance = 60 x 1/3 = 20 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed times time.

recs.q: Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's population is non-Muslim according to the 2023 census?
recs.facts: The 2023 census gave Muslims 96.35 percent, which leaves about 3.65 percent non-Muslim.
recs.rel: Hindus (about 1.61 percent) and Christians (about 1.37 percent) are the largest minorities, and Ahmadis are listed separately.

recs.q: What is 5/7 as a percentage (to two decimal places)?
recs.facts: 5 divided by 7 = 0.714285. Multiplying by 100 gives 71.43 percent.
recs.rel: 1/7 is about 14.29 percent.

recs.q: One side of a right-angled triangle is 8 and the perpendicular is 6. What is the length of the third side (hypotenuse)?
recs.facts: By Pythagoras, hypotenuse squared = 8 squared + 6 squared = 64 + 36 = 100, so the hypotenuse is 10.
recs.rel: 3, 4, 5 and its multiples such as 6, 8, 10 are Pythagorean triples.

recs.q: In a right-angled triangle, sine of an angle is the perpendicular divided by what?
recs.facts: Sin of an angle = perpendicular / hypotenuse.
recs.rel: Cos is base / hypotenuse and tan is perpendicular / base.

recs.q: What is the correct thing to do with the engine of your vehicle at a petrol pump?
recs.facts: Petrol vapour can catch fire from sparks, so the engine must be switched off while refuelling.
recs.rel: Smoking and using mobile phones at a petrol pump are also unsafe.

recs.q: In which year was the Pirpur Report on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces published?
recs.facts: The Pirpur Report, prepared by a committee of the Muslim League headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur, came out in 1938.
recs.rel: It listed complaints against Congress rule in the provinces from 1937.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: Let us play a game.
opts: A game was played by us.
recs.facts: For a sentence beginning with Let, the passive form is Let + object + be + past participle.
recs.rel: Another example is Let the work be done.

recs.q: What are the two parts of a common logarithm called?
recs.facts: A common logarithm has an integral part called the characteristic and a decimal part called the mantissa.
recs.rel: The mantissa is always kept positive.

recs.q: Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's oceans?
opts: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench
recs.facts: Challenger Deep lies in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean. It is about 10,900 metres deep.
recs.rel: The Mariana Trench is near Guam in the Pacific Ocean.

recs.q: According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population lives in Balochistan?
recs.facts: Balochistan has about 14.9 million people out of about 241.5 million in Pakistan. That is roughly 6 percent.
recs.rel: Balochistan is the largest province by area but the smallest by population.

recs.q: What is the population of Balochistan according to the 2023 census of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 2023 digital census recorded about 14.89 million people in Balochistan.
recs.rel: In the 2017 census Balochistan had about 12.3 million people.

recs.q: What is the population of Sindh according to the 2023 census of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 2023 digital census recorded about 55.7 million people in Sindh.
recs.rel: In the 2017 census Sindh had about 47.9 million people.

recs.q: Is Greece a nuclear-weapon state?
opts: Yes, it has tested a bomb
No, it is not a nuclear power
recs.facts: Greece has no nuclear weapons. It is a NATO member but does not own an atomic arsenal.
recs.rel: The nine nuclear-armed states are the USA, Russia, UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, North Korea and Israel (undeclared).

recs.q: Fill in the preposition: Do you agree ___ me?
recs.facts: We agree with a person and agree to a plan or proposal. Here the object is a person, so the correct word is with.
recs.rel: We say agree with someone, agree to a proposal, and agree on a matter.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: I always face difficulty ___ prepositions.
recs.facts: The common phrase is difficulty with something. So the correct preposition is with.
recs.rel: Difficulty in doing something is used with a verb-ing form, for example difficulty in understanding.

recs.q: In which year was Pakistan's first constitution enforced, and who became the first President under it?
recs.facts: The first constitution of Pakistan was enforced on 23 March 1956. Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza had earlier been the last Governor General of Pakistan.

recs.q: Is 19 a prime number?
opts: Yes, it is a prime number
recs.facts: 19 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7 or 11, and has no divisor other than 1 and itself. So it is prime.
recs.rel: The prime numbers below 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1973 when the new Constitution was adopted?
recs.facts: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister in August 1973 and the 1973 Constitution came into force under him.
recs.rel: Bhutto was earlier President of Pakistan from 1971 to 1973.

recs.q: What is the order of the product of a 3 x 2 matrix and a 2 x 3 matrix?
recs.facts: For a product AB, the inner orders (2 and 2) must match, and the result has the outer orders. So a 3 x 2 matrix times a 2 x 3 matrix gives a 3 x 3 matrix.
recs.rel: The product in the reverse order (2 x 3 times 3 x 2) would be a 2 x 2 matrix.

recs.q: Which property of multiplication is shown by 9 x 7 = 7 x 9?
recs.facts: Changing the order of the numbers does not change the product, which is the commutative property.
recs.rel: Addition is also commutative, but subtraction and division are not.

recs.q: Which type of tissue in the human body pumps blood regularly?
recs.facts: The walls of the heart are made of cardiac muscle, which contracts rhythmically without tiring.
recs.rel: Cardiac muscle is involuntary, meaning we cannot control it by will.

recs.q: Which companion headed the committee that prepared copies of the Quran during the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA) appointed Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) to lead the committee that wrote standard copies of the Quran and sent them to major cities.
recs.rel: Because of this work Hazrat Usman (RA) is called Jami ul Quran.

recs.q: To which caste (community) did Raja Dahir, the ruler of Sindh at the time of Muhammad bin Qasim's invasion, belong?
recs.facts: Raja Dahir belonged to the Brahmin dynasty that ruled Sindh after the Rai dynasty.
recs.rel: Chach, the father of Dahir, had founded the Brahmin dynasty of Sindh.

recs.q: Is mass a scalar quantity or a vector quantity?
recs.facts: Mass has only magnitude and no direction, so it is a scalar quantity.
recs.rel: Weight is a vector because it acts downward as a force.

recs.q: What is one quarter of one third of 36?
recs.facts: One third of 36 is 36/3 = 12. One quarter of 12 is 12/4 = 3.
recs.rel: One quarter of one third is the same as 1/12 of the number.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sindh, Peshawar, Quetta?
recs.facts: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Peshawar and Quetta are cities, while Sindh is a province.
recs.rel: Quetta is the capital of Balochistan and Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

recs.q: In which city did the Quraish tribe mainly reside?
recs.facts: The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and looked after the Kaaba.
recs.rel: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself belonged to the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.

recs.q: What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 56?
recs.facts: Diameter is twice the radius. 2 x 56 = 112.
recs.rel: The circumference of a circle is pi times the diameter.

recs.q: Ramiz Raja was a famous player of which game?
recs.facts: Ramiz Raja played for Pakistan in Tests and ODIs from 1984 to 1997.
recs.rel: He was later the PCB chairman (2021 to 2022) and is a well known commentator.

recs.q: In which province are the Ras Koh Hills located?
recs.facts: The Ras Koh Hills lie in Chagai district of Balochistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests of May 1998 in the Chagai area.

recs.q: What is a rational number?
opts: A number that cannot be written as a fraction
A number that can be written as p/q where p and q are integers and q is not zero
A number with a non-repeating infinite decimal
A number that is only positive
recs.facts: A rational number is any number that can be expressed as the ratio p/q of two integers with q not equal to 0.
recs.rel: Terminating and repeating decimals are rational numbers.

recs.q: How many rational numbers lie between 0 and 1?
recs.facts: Between any two rational numbers there is another one, for example their average, so the set between 0 and 1 is infinite.
recs.rel: Examples are 1/2, 1/3, 2/5 and 3/4.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters of CHIKARA to make the name of a city. Which city is it?
recs.facts: The letters C H I K A R A can be arranged to spell KARACHI.
recs.rel: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.

recs.q: Muammar Gaddafi was the long-time ruler of which country?
recs.facts: Muammar Gaddafi ruled Libya from 1969 until he was overthrown in 2011.
recs.rel: He was killed in October 2011 during the Libyan civil war.

recs.q: How many countries are strictly counted as Scandinavian countries?
recs.facts: Scandinavia strictly means Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
recs.rel: The wider Nordic region also includes Finland and Iceland, making five countries.

recs.q: Which symbol is commonly used to represent the common difference of an arithmetic sequence?
recs.facts: In an arithmetic sequence each term is found by adding a fixed number to the previous term. That fixed number is called the common difference and is written d.
recs.rel: The nth term of an arithmetic sequence is a + (n - 1)d, where a is the first term.

recs.q: Which number is different from the rest: 5, 7, 9, 12?
recs.facts: 5, 7 and 9 are odd numbers, while 12 is an even number.
recs.rel: A number is even if it is divisible by 2.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: A4, B5, C5, D7?
recs.facts: A, B, C, D are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th letters. The number is the letter position plus 3 in A4, B5 and D7 (1+3, 2+3, 4+3), but C5 breaks it because 3+3 is 6.
recs.rel: In letter-number odd-one-out questions, convert letters to their alphabet positions first.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: X5, Y6, Z9?
recs.facts: The numbers follow the letters in order: X is followed by 5 and Y by 6, so Z should be followed by 7. Z9 breaks the pattern.
recs.rel: X, Y and Z are the 24th, 25th and 26th letters of the alphabet.

recs.q: How many rings are there in the Olympic symbol?
recs.facts: The Olympic symbol has five interlocking rings coloured blue, yellow, black, green and red.
recs.rel: The rings represent the five inhabited continents joined together.

recs.q: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 divided how many rivers between India and Pakistan?
recs.facts: The treaty covered six rivers: the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went to India and the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) went to Pakistan.
recs.rel: The treaty was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.

recs.q: Gwadar Port is situated on the coast of which sea?
recs.facts: Gwadar is a deep sea port in Balochistan and lies on the Arabian Sea coast.
recs.rel: Gwadar is the main port of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

recs.q: Which event is commonly called the First War of Independence against British rule in the subcontinent?
recs.facts: The uprising of 1857 against the East India Company is called the War of Independence by Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent.
recs.rel: The British called the same event the Sepoy Mutiny.

recs.q: A train runs at a speed of 99 km/hr. What distance does it cover in 12 minutes?
recs.facts: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 99 x 1/5 = 19.8 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time, with time in hours when speed is in km/hr.

recs.q: What is the highest individual score by a Pakistani batter in Test cricket?
recs.facts: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against the West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958.
recs.rel: Inzamam-ul-Haq scored 329, Younis Khan 313 and Azhar Ali 302 not out.

recs.q: Which saint is buried in the city of Kasur?
recs.facts: The famous Punjabi Sufi poet Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur.
recs.rel: Baba Farid rests at Pakpattan and Data Ganj Bakhsh at Lahore.

recs.q: On which date was Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1, launched?
recs.facts: Badr-1 was launched on 16 July 1990 from China.
recs.rel: Pakistan's space agency SUPARCO built Badr-1.

recs.q: Where is the Yellow Sea located?
opts: Between China and the Korean Peninsula
recs.facts: The Yellow Sea is an arm of the Pacific Ocean lying between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula.
recs.rel: It gets its name from the yellow silt carried into it by rivers such as the Yellow River.

recs.q: What does SEATO stand for?
opts: Southern Europe and Asia Treaty Organization
recs.facts: SEATO stands for South East Asia Treaty Organization, a defence alliance led by the USA.
recs.rel: Pakistan was a member from 1954 until 1973.

recs.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: I ___ to school.
recs.facts: With the subject I, the simple present verb is go.
recs.rel: With he, she or it the verb takes s, as in goes.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: Z4, X8, V12, ?
recs.facts: The letters move back by two (Z, X, V, T) and the numbers go up by 4 (4, 8, 12, 16). So the next term is T16.
recs.rel: Skipping one letter each time gives the alphabet position falling by 2 each step.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, ?
recs.facts: Each term has a capital letter and its small letter, moving one letter forward each time. After Dd comes Ee.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: A2, D9, H16, M23, ?
recs.facts: The letters jump by 3, 4, 5 places (A, D, H, M) so the next jump is 6, giving S. The numbers increase by 7 each time (2, 9, 16, 23), giving 30. So the next term is S30.
recs.rel: M is the 13th letter, and 13 + 6 = 19, which is S.

recs.q: By which symbol is the universal set usually represented in set theory?
recs.facts: The universal set, which contains all elements under consideration, is written with the capital letter U.
recs.rel: The empty set is written with the symbol phi or with empty braces.

recs.q: What is a singleton set?
opts: A set with exactly one element
recs.facts: A singleton set has exactly one element, for example {5}.
recs.rel: A set with no element is called the empty or null set.

recs.q: What does the idiom "cold shoulder" mean?
opts: To treat someone in an unfriendly way and ignore them
To feel a pain in the shoulder
recs.facts: To give someone the cold shoulder means to deliberately ignore them or treat them coldly.
recs.rel: An idiom has a meaning different from the literal meaning of its words.

recs.q: Ali is 10 years old and he is twice as old as his sister. How old will his sister be after 20 years?
recs.facts: His sister is 10 divided by 2 = 5 years old now. After 20 years she will be 5 + 20 = 25.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people never changes with time.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 8 years old. When Ali is 10 years old, how old will his sister be?
recs.facts: The age difference is 8 - 5 = 3 years. When Ali is 10, his sister is 10 + 3 = 13.
recs.rel: The sister is always 3 years older than Ali.

recs.q: If my mother is your sister, what am I to you?
recs.facts: Your sister is my mother, so I am her child, which makes me your sister's child, that is your nephew or niece.
recs.rel: The child of your brother is also your nephew or niece.

recs.q: According to the Quran, whom should a person respect and obey most (after Allah)?
recs.facts: The Quran commands good treatment of parents right after the command to worship Allah alone, and tells us not even to say 'uff' to them.
recs.rel: Surah Bani Israil (verses 23 to 24) gives the command about kindness to parents.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: I go to sleep ____ I am tired.
recs.facts: 'When' shows the time at which something happens, so 'I go to sleep when I am tired' is correct.
recs.rel: 'Whenever' can also be used here to mean every time.

recs.q: Which is the smallest Muslim country of the world by area?
recs.facts: The Maldives covers only about 300 square kilometres, less than Bahrain (about 780) and Brunei (about 5,770).
recs.rel: The Maldives is also the smallest country in Asia.

recs.q: Father is to son as mother is to ____.
recs.facts: A father and his male child are father and son. In the same way a mother and her female child are mother and daughter.
recs.rel: Analogy questions test the same relationship in both pairs.

recs.q: Which of the following was a son of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Qasim (RA) was the first son of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA); he died as a small child.
recs.rel: Hasan and Husain were the grandsons of the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: On which side of Pakistan does China lie?
recs.facts: Pakistan's northern border, through Gilgit-Baltistan, meets China's Xinjiang region.
recs.rel: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with China.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: The Arabian Sea is ____ in the southern part of Pakistan.
recs.facts: The sentence needs the past participle 'situated' after 'is' to mean 'located'.
recs.rel: 'Is situated' is a passive form often used to describe locations.

recs.q: Select the correct spelling.
recs.facts: The word is spelled d-i-v-e-r-s-i-t-y, from the Latin word diversus.
recs.rel: Its opposite is uniformity.

recs.q: Who started the Khilafat Movement in the subcontinent?
opts: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk
Maulana Hasrat Mohani and Liaquat Ali Khan
recs.facts: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led by the Ali Brothers, Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali. It aimed to save the Ottoman Caliphate.
recs.rel: Mahatma Gandhi supported the movement for some time.

recs.q: Who started the Shuddhi movement in India?
recs.facts: The Shuddhi (purification) movement to bring converts back to Hinduism was begun by the Arya Samaj of Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
recs.rel: It became very active in the 1920s under Swami Shraddhanand and angered Muslims.

recs.q: As of 2026, has any woman been elected President of the United States?
opts: No, no woman has been elected so far
recs.facts: Hillary Clinton lost in 2016 and Kamala Harris lost in 2024. No woman has yet held the office of US President.
recs.rel: The next US presidential election after 2024 is due in 2028.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book The Story of the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: The Story of the Pakistan Army was written by Major General Fazal Muqeem Khan and first published in 1963.
recs.rel: Shuja Nawaz wrote the books Crossed Swords and The Battle for Pakistan.

recs.q: In set theory, a set that contains another set as its subset is called what?
recs.facts: If every element of A is also in B, then A is a subset of B and B is a superset of A.
recs.rel: The power set of a set is the set of all its subsets.

recs.q: What is the sum of the first seven multiples of 5?
recs.rel: The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)/2.

recs.q: What does CNG stand for?
recs.facts: CNG is natural gas, mostly methane, stored under high pressure and used as vehicle fuel.
recs.rel: CNG is cheaper and cleaner than petrol in most cases.

recs.q: What does RAW stand for in the name of the Indian intelligence agency?
recs.facts: RAW is the external intelligence agency of India, called the Research and Analysis Wing.
recs.rel: RAW was formed in 1968 after the 1962 and 1965 wars.

recs.q: What is Youm-e-Takbeer?
opts: Anniversary of Pakistan's nuclear tests of May 1998
Day of the passing of the Lahore Resolution
Anniversary of the independence of Pakistan
recs.facts: Youm-e-Takbeer is observed every year on 28 May to mark the five nuclear tests Pakistan carried out in the Chagai hills in 1998.
recs.rel: Takbeer means saying Allahu Akbar, and the tests made Pakistan the seventh nuclear power.

recs.q: The word Olympic is taken from which ancient Greek place?
recs.facts: The word Olympic comes from Olympia, the town in ancient Greece where the original games were held.
recs.rel: Some sources link the name to Mount Olympus, the home of the Greek gods, but Olympia is the usual textbook answer.

recs.q: What is the chemical symbol of gold in the periodic table?
recs.facts: The symbol Au comes from the Latin name aurum, meaning gold.
recs.rel: Ag is the symbol of silver, from the Latin argentum.

recs.q: What is the chemical symbol of potassium?
recs.facts: The symbol K comes from kalium, the Latin name for potassium.
recs.rel: Sodium has the symbol Na, from the Latin natrium.

recs.q: Against which team did Pakistan play its first Twenty20 International match?
recs.facts: Pakistan played its first T20I against England on 28 August 2006 at Bristol and won by five wickets.
recs.rel: The very first men's T20I in history was played between Australia and New Zealand on 17 February 2005.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to diatribe?
recs.facts: A diatribe is a bitter and angry verbal attack, the same as a tirade.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to turbulent?
recs.facts: Turbulent means stormy and wild, which is close to violent.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to acquisitive?
recs.facts: Acquisitive means eager to get more and more possessions, which is greedy.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to aggressive?
recs.facts: Aggressive means ready to attack or confront, which is close to hostile.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to anonymous?
recs.facts: Anonymous means having no name made known, that is unnamed.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to entice?
recs.facts: To entice is to attract someone by offering something pleasing, which is to lure.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to eradicate?
recs.facts: To eradicate is to remove completely, which is to eliminate.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to extraordinary?
recs.facts: Extraordinary means beyond the ordinary, which is remarkable.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to fertile?
recs.facts: Fertile land produces plenty of crops, so it is productive.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to nutritious?
recs.facts: Nutritious food gives the body what it needs to grow, so it is nourishing.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to reddish?
recs.facts: Reddish means slightly red, which is close to ruddy.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to restrain?
recs.facts: To restrain is to keep under control, which is to hold back.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to staunch?
recs.facts: Staunch means firmly faithful to a person or cause, which is loyal.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to sympathy?
recs.facts: Sympathy is feeling sorry for another person's trouble, which is compassion.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to tempted?
recs.facts: Tempted means attracted towards doing something, which is lured.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to tolerant?
recs.facts: A tolerant person accepts other views and behaviour, which is open-minded.
recs.rel: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

recs.q: What does the idiom 'out of temper' mean?
recs.facts: To be out of temper means to be in a bad mood and easily angered.
recs.rel: The opposite state is to be good-tempered, meaning calm and cheerful.

recs.q: What does the idiom 'to keep one's temper' mean?
opts: To remain calm and not lose control of anger
To keep a hot drink warm
recs.facts: To keep one's temper means to stay calm even when provoked.
recs.rel: The opposite idiom is 'to lose one's temper', meaning to become suddenly angry.

recs.q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 12?
recs.facts: One tenth of 12 is 1.2. One quarter of 1.2 is 1.2 / 4 = 0.3.
recs.rel: A quarter of a number is the same as dividing it by 4.

recs.q: What is one third of 1/80?
recs.rel: Multiplying fractions means multiplying the numerators and the denominators.

recs.q: What is one third of 10?
recs.facts: One third of 10 = 10 / 3 = 3.33, which is 3 and 1/3.
recs.rel: Ten is not exactly divisible by 3, so the answer is a fraction.

recs.q: Ali is 6 years older than his sister. When Ali's age was three times his sister's age, how old was the sister?
recs.facts: Let the sister be x. Then Ali is x + 6 = 3x, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. Ali was then 9.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: In which country is the Three Gorges Dam located?
recs.facts: The Three Gorges Dam is built on the Yangtze River in Hubei province, China.
recs.rel: It is the largest hydroelectric power station in the world by installed capacity.

recs.q: Khateeb ul Ambia (the orator among the prophets) is the title of which prophet?
recs.facts: Hazrat Shuaib (AS) was known for his powerful and eloquent speech, so he is called Khateeb ul Ambia.
recs.rel: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah, the one who spoke with Allah.

recs.q: Which number completes the pattern: 2x2 = 44, 2x3 = 49, 3x4 = 916, then 2x4 = ?
recs.facts: Each answer joins the squares of the two numbers: 2x2 gives 4 and 4, 2x3 gives 4 and 9, 3x4 gives 9 and 16. So 2x4 gives 4 and 16, which is 416.
recs.rel: The first digits come from the square of the first number and the rest from the square of the second.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan did the country carry out its nuclear tests in May 1998?
recs.facts: The tests were carried out in the Chagai Hills in Chagai district, Balochistan.
recs.rel: The Ras Koh Hills in the Chagai range was the site of the main tests of 28 May 1998.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the idiom "to take to one's heels"?
recs.facts: The idiom "take to one's heels" means to run away quickly, usually from danger.
recs.rel: A similar idiom is "to show a clean pair of heels", which means to outrun someone.

recs.q: What is a synonym of the word "total"?
recs.facts: "Total" means the whole amount after adding everything together, which is the same as "sum".
recs.rel: The opposite of total in this sense is "part" or "fraction".

recs.q: What is the length of a marathon race in miles?
recs.facts: A standard marathon is 42.195 km. Dividing by 1.609 gives about 26.2 miles.
recs.rel: The marathon distance of 42.195 km was fixed by World Athletics after the 1908 London Olympics.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: Our team ______ their track suits.
recs.facts: "Team" is treated here as one unit, so the singular verb "is wearing" is used.
recs.rel: In British English a collective noun like team can also take a plural verb, but the singular is the textbook answer.

recs.q: If A transpose is equal to A, then the matrix A is called what?
recs.facts: A square matrix with A^T = A is called a symmetric matrix. If A^T = -A, it is skew symmetric.
recs.rel: The diagonal entries of a skew symmetric matrix are always zero.

recs.q: A car travels 70 km in one hour. How much distance will it travel in 40 minutes at the same speed?
recs.facts: 40 minutes is 40/60 = 2/3 of an hour. Distance = 70 x 2/3 = 46.67 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: Insulin is used for the treatment of which disease?
recs.facts: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is used to treat diabetes.
recs.rel: Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the pancreas.

recs.q: Who was the scribe (writer) of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) wrote the text of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah as dictated by the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Suhail bin Amr represented the Quraish in the treaty.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word "trouble"?
recs.facts: "Trouble" means a problem or hardship, which is the same as difficulty.
recs.rel: Other synonyms include distress and worry.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 26th is 23 days. 23 divided by 7 leaves 2, so Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.
recs.rel: The 10th, 17th and 24th of this month are also Tuesdays.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Tuesday + 6 = Monday.
recs.rel: The 22nd is exactly 3 weeks after the 1st, so it is a Tuesday.

recs.q: Who was the leader of the Muslim army in the Battle of Uhud?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself commanded the Muslim army at Uhud.
recs.rel: He placed 50 archers on the Ainain hill under Abdullah bin Jubair.

recs.q: Umm-ul-Masakeen (Mother of the Poor) is the title of which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaymah (RA) was known as Umm-ul-Masakeen because of her great generosity to the poor.
recs.rel: She died within a few months of marrying the Prophet (PBUH) and is among the wives who passed away in his lifetime, along with Hazrat Khadija (RA).

recs.q: Which British queen was the first to visit Pakistan?
recs.facts: Queen Elizabeth II visited Pakistan in February 1961, the first reigning British monarch to do so.
recs.rel: She visited again in 1997 with Prince Philip.

recs.q: In which year did the Soviet Union complete its withdrawal from Afghanistan?
recs.facts: The last Soviet troops left Afghanistan on 15 February 1989, after the 1979 invasion.
recs.rel: The Soviet Union entered Afghanistan in December 1979.

recs.q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, what is the position of Pakistan relative to India on the rivers?
recs.facts: The rivers rise in or pass through Indian-held territory before entering Pakistan, so Pakistan is the lower riparian (downstream) state.
recs.rel: The treaty was signed in Karachi in 1960 with World Bank mediation.

recs.q: Who has taken the most wickets in One Day Internationals?
recs.facts: Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka took 534 ODI wickets, the highest ever.
recs.rel: Wasim Akram is second with 502 wickets, the most by a Pakistani.

recs.q: In which country is the White Sea located?
recs.facts: The White Sea is an inlet of the Barents Sea on the north-west coast of Russia.
recs.rel: The port city of Arkhangelsk lies on it.

recs.q: Complete the analogy: Man is to wallet as woman is to ____.
recs.facts: A man carries money in a wallet and a woman usually carries it in a purse.
recs.rel: Analogy questions test the relation between the first pair.

recs.q: Change into indirect speech: He told her, "I want to meet your father."
opts: He told her that he wanted to meet her father.
He told her that I want to meet your father.
He told her that he wants to meet your father.
He told her that he had wanted to meet his father.
recs.facts: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb, present tense becomes past, I becomes he, and your becomes her.
recs.rel: Say or tell with an object is changed to told in reported speech.

recs.q: Which country has the second largest population in the world (2026)?
recs.facts: India is first and China is second according to 2026 estimates.
recs.rel: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, and before that China was first.

recs.q: For which book is Gulbadan Begum, daughter of Babur, famous as a writer?
recs.facts: Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama, a history of the reign of her brother Humayun.
recs.rel: She was one of the first Mughal women to write history.

recs.q: Who wrote the work The Loyal Muhammadans of India?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it around 1860 to show that most Muslims were loyal to the British during the events of 1857.
recs.rel: Sir Syed also wrote Asar-us-Sanadid and founded the Aligarh movement.

recs.q: What was the name of the mother of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and Rifqa (Rebecca).
recs.rel: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is also known as Israel.

recs.q: What is the relation between Hazrat Zakariya (AS) and Hazrat Yahya (AS)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Yahya (AS) was the son of Hazrat Zakariya (AS), born in his old age by Allah's will.
recs.rel: Hazrat Yahya (AS) is mentioned in Surah Maryam.

recs.q: What was the relation of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) with the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was a freed slave whom the Prophet (SAW) adopted as his son before Islam.
recs.rel: He is the only Companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).

recs.q: Is zero a natural number, according to the definition taught in Pakistani textbooks?
opts: Yes, it is the first natural number
No, it is a whole number
No, it is a negative number
Yes, it is a prime number
recs.facts: Natural numbers are the counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. Zero is added to them to form the whole numbers.
recs.rel: Some modern books include zero among the natural numbers, so definitions differ.

recs.q: If A = 1, then what number matches M in the same pattern?
recs.facts: Letters are numbered by their place in the alphabet. A is 1st, and M is the 13th letter.
recs.rel: N, the letter after M, is 14.

recs.q: What is 1 + 1?
recs.facts: Adding one and one gives two.
recs.rel: In binary, 1 + 1 equals 10.

recs.q: What is 1.2 + 2/2?
recs.facts: Divide first: 2/2 = 1. Then 1.2 + 1 = 2.2.
recs.rel: By BODMAS, division is done before addition.

recs.q: What is 1/(1 + 2)?
recs.facts: First solve the bracket: 1 + 2 = 3. So the value is 1/3.
recs.rel: Brackets are solved first in BODMAS.

recs.q: What is 2 + 4 x 4?
recs.facts: Multiply first: 4 x 4 = 16. Then 2 + 16 = 18.
recs.rel: By BODMAS, multiplication is done before addition.

recs.q: What is 3 x 2?
recs.facts: 3 x 2 = 6, and 2 x 3 is also 6 because multiplication is commutative.
recs.rel: Changing the order of numbers does not change a product.

recs.q: What is 40% of 9?
recs.rel: 10% of 9 is 0.9, so 40% is four times that.

recs.q: What type of number is 7 - 3i?
recs.facts: A number written as a + bi, where i is the imaginary unit, is a complex number. Here a = 7 and b = -3.
recs.rel: The conjugate of 7 - 3i is 7 + 3i.

recs.q: What is 9 + 7?
recs.facts: Adding 9 and 7 gives 16.
recs.rel: Addition is commutative, so 7 + 9 is also 16.

recs.q: What is 90 / 9?
recs.facts: 9 times 10 is 90, so 90 divided by 9 is 10.
recs.rel: Candidates sometimes confuse this with 9 x 9 = 81.

recs.q: Krone is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: The Danish krone is the currency of Denmark. Norway also uses a krone.
recs.rel: Sweden uses the krona and Finland uses the euro.

recs.q: What is the boundary line between India and China called?
recs.facts: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and is the boundary India claims with China in the east.
recs.rel: China does not accept the McMahon Line.

recs.q: How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan has five peaks above 8000 m: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II and Broad Peak.
recs.rel: The whole world has 14 peaks above 8000 m, and K2 at 8611 m is the second highest.

recs.q: In which province is the Lower Indus plain mostly located?
recs.facts: The Lower Indus plain lies in Sindh, from near Sukkur down to the Arabian Sea.
recs.rel: The Upper Indus plain lies mainly in Punjab.

recs.q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2023 (New Delhi)?
recs.facts: The 2023 G20 summit was held in New Delhi, India, in September 2023. India held the G20 presidency that year.
recs.rel: Indonesia hosted in 2022 and Brazil in 2024.

recs.q: Kiwi, a flightless bird, is the national symbol of which country?
recs.facts: The kiwi is the national bird of New Zealand, and New Zealanders are often called Kiwis.
recs.rel: The kiwi fruit is also linked to New Zealand but it originally came from China.

recs.q: Who wrote the novel Ice Candy Man?
recs.facts: Ice Candy Man (1988) was written by the Pakistani novelist Bapsi Sidhwa. It tells the story of Partition through a Parsi girl in Lahore.
recs.rel: The novel was published in the USA as Cracking India and was filmed as 1947 Earth.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan play its first Test match?
recs.facts: Pakistan's first Test was played against India in Delhi in October 1952.
recs.rel: Pakistan's first Test win came against India at Lucknow in the same series.

recs.q: Car is to wheel as sound is to what?
recs.facts: A car moves by its wheels in the same way that sound travels as waves.
recs.rel: Sound is a mechanical wave and cannot travel through a vacuum.

recs.q: When did World War 2 start?
recs.facts: World War 2 began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.
recs.rel: It ended in 1945 with the surrender of Germany in May and Japan in September.

recs.q: Who is credited with inventing the electric motor?
recs.facts: Michael Faraday demonstrated the first electric motor in 1821, and most textbooks credit him.
recs.rel: Other inventors such as Jedlik, Jacobi and Davenport also built early motors, so sources differ.

recs.q: In which year was the Durand Line, the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, agreed?
recs.facts: The Durand Line agreement was signed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.
recs.rel: Afghanistan has not formally accepted the Durand Line as an international border.

recs.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Canada today (October 2026)?
recs.facts: Mark Carney became Prime Minister of Canada on 14 March 2025 and leads the Liberal Party. Canada has no president; the Prime Minister is head of government.
recs.rel: Justin Trudeau was Prime Minister before Carney (2015 to 2025), and King Charles III is Canada's head of state.

recs.q: Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bal-e-Jibreel (Gabriel's Wing)?
recs.facts: Bal-e-Jibreel was written by Allama Muhammad Iqbal and published in 1935.
recs.rel: Iqbal's other Urdu books include Bang-e-Dara and Zarb-e-Kaleem.

recs.q: Which element is the most abundant in the universe?
recs.facts: Hydrogen makes up about 75 percent of the ordinary matter in the universe by mass.
recs.rel: Helium is the second most abundant element, and oxygen is the most abundant in the Earth crust.

recs.q: In which year did Aligarh College (MAO College) become Aligarh Muslim University?
recs.facts: The MAO College was given university status in 1920 and became Aligarh Muslim University.
recs.rel: The MAO school began in 1875 and became a college in 1877, and sources differ slightly on these dates.

recs.q: For what is the city of Multan famous?
recs.facts: Multan is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya) because it has many famous shrines of Sufi saints.
recs.rel: Multan is also called the City of Pirs and is famous for its mangoes and blue pottery.

recs.q: Who conquered Sindh in 712 AD?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim, a young Arab general of the Umayyad caliphate, defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh.
recs.rel: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam, the Gateway of Islam, in the subcontinent.

recs.q: Which word is closest to the opposite of envious?
recs.facts: Envious means wanting what others have. A content person is satisfied with what they have, so content is the opposite.
recs.rel: The noun envy is opposed by contentment.

recs.q: Who was known as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity in the subcontinent?
recs.facts: Muhammad Ali Jinnah worked for Hindu-Muslim unity in the early part of his career, including the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Sarojini Naidu gave him this title.
recs.rel: Jinnah was a member of the Indian National Congress before he led the Muslim League.

recs.q: What was the first book of poetry of Allama Iqbal?
recs.facts: Asrar-e-Khudi, a Persian poetry book, was published in 1915 and is usually called his first poetry book.
recs.rel: His first prose book was Ilm-ul-Iqtisad (1903), so sources differ depending on the question.

recs.q: What is 1/4 of 1/10 of 120?
recs.rel: A quarter of a number is the same as dividing it by 4.

recs.q: Which is the hottest planet of the solar system?
recs.facts: Venus is the hottest planet, about 465 degrees Celsius, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
recs.rel: Mercury is closer to the Sun but has almost no atmosphere to hold heat.

recs.q: On which date did the full-scale 1965 war between Pakistan and India begin, according to Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: India attacked Lahore across the international border on 6 September 1965, which started the full-scale war. A ceasefire came on 23 September 1965.
recs.rel: Operation Gibraltar had begun earlier, in early August 1965, which is why some candidates remember 5 August.

recs.q: Which ruler is known as the Tiger of Mysore (Sher-e-Mysore)?
recs.facts: Tipu Sultan fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore wars and is called the Tiger of Mysore.
recs.rel: He was martyred in 1799 defending Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

recs.q: Into how many main physical regions is Pakistan commonly divided in Pakistan Studies textbooks?
recs.facts: Textbooks usually list six regions: Northern Mountains, Western Mountains, Potohar Plateau, Balochistan Plateau, Indus Plains and Deserts.
recs.rel: Sources differ, and some books group these into five regions.

recs.q: Who is regarded as the oldest (first) poet of the Pashto language?
recs.facts: Amir Kror Suri, a ruler of Ghor in the 8th century, is regarded as the earliest known Pashto poet.
recs.rel: Rahman Baba and Khushal Khan Khattak are famous later Pashto poets.

recs.q: Which is the oldest sport in the world according to most textbooks?
recs.facts: Wrestling is usually named as the oldest sport, as cave paintings and ancient records show it thousands of years ago.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as some also name running, archery or chess among the oldest.

recs.q: Where were all the Round Table Conferences (1930 to 1932) held?
recs.facts: The three Round Table Conferences were held in London to discuss constitutional reforms for India. They took place in 1930, 1931 and 1932.
recs.rel: The Muslim League was represented by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Allama Iqbal attended the second session.

recs.q: In which region of Pakistan is the Shina (Sheena) language mainly spoken?
recs.facts: Shina is the main language of the Gilgit area and nearby valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan. It belongs to the Dardic group of languages.
recs.rel: Shina is also spoken in parts of Indian-administered Kashmir and in Kohistan.

recs.q: Which vegetable is regarded as the national vegetable of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Okra, known locally as bhindi or lady finger, is commonly listed as Pakistan's national vegetable.
recs.rel: Lists of national symbols differ between sources because there is no well-known official notification.

recs.q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by a committee headed by whom?
recs.facts: The All Parties Committee that drafted the 1928 Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru.
recs.rel: Jawaharlal Nehru, his son, served as secretary of the committee.

recs.q: Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 100 rupee note?
recs.facts: The reverse of the Rs 100 note shows the Quaid-e-Azam Residency in Ziarat, Balochistan.
recs.rel: The Rs 5000 note shows the Faisal Mosque on its back.

recs.q: Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's area does Balochistan cover?
recs.facts: Balochistan has about 347,000 square km, which Pakistani textbooks give as roughly 44% of the country.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly, as some give about 40 percent depending on the total area used.

recs.q: Which person won two Nobel Prizes in his life, one of them the Nobel Peace Prize?
recs.facts: Linus Pauling won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 and the Nobel Peace Prize in 1962.
recs.rel: He is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes.

recs.q: Who built the Red Fort of Delhi?
recs.facts: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in Delhi, completed in 1648.
recs.rel: Shah Jahan also built the Taj Mahal and the Badshahi Mosque was built by Aurangzeb.

recs.q: In which Amendment to the 1973 Constitution were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim?
recs.facts: The Second Amendment, passed in 1974, declared Ahmadis non-Muslim for the purposes of the Constitution.
recs.rel: It was passed during the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

recs.q: Pablo Picasso, the famous painter, belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Pablo Picasso was born in Malaga, Spain, in 1881.
recs.rel: He spent most of his adult life in France and co-founded the Cubist art movement.

recs.q: Which is the largest dam of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is the largest earth filled dam in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
recs.rel: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum is the second largest.

recs.q: On which date did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh. He was born on 17 October 1817.
recs.rel: He is buried in the compound of the Jama Masjid at Aligarh Muslim University.

recs.q: Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Hindu Kush range lies in the north-west of Pakistan, along the border with Afghanistan.
recs.rel: Some sources also mention the Sulaiman Range, which lies to the west.

recs.q: In which city was the second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC held in 1974?
recs.facts: The second OIC Islamic Summit took place in Lahore in February 1974 and was hosted by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
recs.rel: The first Islamic Summit was held in Rabat, Morocco, in 1969.

recs.q: Who won the ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year (Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy) award for 2022?
recs.facts: Babar Azam of Pakistan won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy for 2022.
recs.rel: Shaheen Shah Afridi won it for 2021.

recs.q: What is the full form of ISPR?
recs.facts: ISPR stands for Inter Services Public Relations, the media wing of the Pakistan Armed Forces.
recs.rel: It is headed by a Director General, a serving army officer.

recs.q: Which dam of Pakistan is made of earth and rock fill and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world?
recs.facts: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is mostly built of earth and rock fill and is called the largest earth-filled dam.
recs.rel: Tarbela was completed in 1976.

recs.q: What is 3 + 3/3?
recs.facts: Division first: 3/3 = 1. Then 3 + 1 = 4.
recs.rel: BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

recs.q: Who was the Viceroy of India in 1911 when the partition of Bengal was annulled?
recs.facts: Lord Hardinge was Viceroy from 1910 to 1916. The annulment of the 1905 partition was announced at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911.
recs.rel: The capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

recs.q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage of the students are girls?
recs.rel: The percentage of boys here is 68%, and the two percentages add up to 100%.

recs.q: On which date did the USA drop the atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan?
recs.facts: The first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945.
recs.rel: A second bomb hit Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

recs.q: Humayun was defeated by which ruler, forcing him to leave India in 1540?
recs.facts: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and at Kannauj in 1540. Humayun then fled India.
recs.rel: Humayun regained his throne in 1555 after defeating the Suri ruler Sikandar Suri.

recs.q: On which date did Israel declare its independence?
recs.facts: David Ben-Gurion declared the State of Israel on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate ended.
recs.rel: Israel celebrates its Independence Day by the Hebrew calendar, so the Gregorian date changes each year.

recs.q: Which city is known as the City of Light?
recs.facts: Paris is called the City of Light because it was an early centre of education and ideas and one of the first cities with gas street lighting.
recs.rel: Paris is the capital of France and stands on the River Seine.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book Pakistaniat (What is Pakistaniat?)?
recs.facts: Pakistaniat is the idea of Pakistani national identity, and Javed Jabbar wrote a book on it titled What is Pakistaniat. He lists many elements that shape the identity of the Pakistani nation.
recs.rel: Javed Jabbar is a Pakistani politician, writer and former senator who also wrote Pakistan: Unique Origins, Unique Destiny.

recs.q: Germany invaded which country first in World War II in September 1939?
recs.facts: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France then declared war on Germany.
recs.rel: The Soviet Union also invaded Poland from the east on 17 September 1939.

recs.q: Butterfly is a technique (stroke) of which sport?
recs.facts: Butterfly stroke is one of the four main competitive swimming strokes.
recs.rel: The other strokes are freestyle, backstroke and breaststroke.

recs.q: What does OS stand for in computing?
recs.facts: In computers, OS stands for Operating System, the main software that runs the computer.
recs.rel: Windows, Linux, macOS and Android are well-known operating systems.

recs.q: The Wagah border connects Pakistan with which country?
recs.facts: Wagah, on the Grand Trunk Road between Lahore and Amritsar, is the main land crossing between Pakistan and India.
recs.rel: A daily flag-lowering ceremony is held there by both countries.

recs.q: What type of fraction is 9/2?
recs.facts: In 9/2 the numerator 9 is greater than the denominator 2, so it is an improper fraction. It equals the mixed number 4 and 1/2.
recs.rel: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, for example 2/9.

recs.q: Which country is Pakistan's biggest trading partner today?
recs.facts: China is Pakistan's largest trading partner, mainly because of large imports from China.
recs.rel: The United States is Pakistan's largest single export market, but China leads in total trade.

recs.q: Who is the head of state of Pakistan according to the 1973 Constitution (currently in office, 2026)?
recs.facts: The President is the head of state, and Asif Ali Zardari has held the office since 10 March 2024.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Arif Alvi (2018 to 2024); the Prime Minister is head of government.

recs.q: What is the tenure of a member of the Senate of Pakistan?
recs.facts: A Senator is elected for six years. Half of the members retire every three years.
recs.rel: The Senate is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.

recs.q: How many Prime Ministers did Pakistan have between 1947 and 1958?
recs.facts: They were Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Mohammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Mohammad Ali, H. S. Suhrawardy, I. I. Chundrigar and Feroz Khan Noon, which makes 7.
recs.rel: Martial law was imposed in October 1958 by Iskander Mirza and Ayub Khan.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Indian National Congress?
recs.facts: Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in 1906, when he attended its Calcutta session.
recs.rel: He joined the All India Muslim League later, in 1913.

recs.q: In which year was the C. R. (Rajagopalachari) Formula put forward?
recs.facts: C. Rajagopalachari proposed the formula in 1944 as a basis for talks between Gandhi and Jinnah.
recs.rel: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 failed, partly because Jinnah rejected the formula.

recs.q: Which sport is called the Game of Gentlemen?
recs.facts: Cricket is known as the Game of Gentlemen because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship. The phrase comes from its English origins.
recs.rel: Cricket began in England and its laws are kept by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).

recs.q: Who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement?
recs.facts: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Bacha Khan) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) movement around 1929 in the Pashtun areas.
recs.rel: Its members were known as Red Shirts and followed non-violence.

recs.q: In which city is Paradise Point located?
recs.facts: Paradise Point is a famous rocky beach spot on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.
recs.rel: It is close to Cape Monze (Ras Muari) and has a natural arch in the rocks.

recs.q: In which city of Pakistan is Iqbal Park located?
recs.facts: Iqbal Park in Lahore is the park where Minar-e-Pakistan stands and the Pakistan Resolution was passed in 1940.
recs.rel: It was earlier called Minto Park.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam return to India after his self-imposed exile in England?
recs.facts: Jinnah stayed in London for some years after the Round Table Conferences. He came back in 1934 at the request of Muslim leaders and was elected president of the Muslim League.
recs.rel: Some sources give 1935 for his final return, but 1934 is the common textbook year.

recs.q: A train moves at a speed of 60 km/hour. How much time will it take to cover 150 km?
recs.facts: Time = distance / speed = 150 / 60 = 2.5 hours.
recs.rel: 2.5 hours equals 2 hours 30 minutes.

recs.q: Who prepared the Pirpur Report of 1938 on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces?
opts: Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur
recs.facts: The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur.
recs.rel: Fazlul Haq issued a separate report in 1939 called the Sharif Report.

recs.q: Which constitution of Pakistan was enforced in 1962?
opts: The second constitution, with a presidential system
The first constitution, with a parliamentary system
The third constitution, with a parliamentary system
recs.facts: The 1962 constitution was the second constitution of Pakistan and gave a presidential system with strong powers to the President.
recs.rel: It was given by President Ayub Khan and ended in 1969 when Yahya Khan imposed martial law.

recs.q: Akbar is older than Khalid and Ahmed is younger than Khalid. Which statement is true?
recs.facts: The order from oldest is Akbar, Khalid, Ahmed. So Akbar is older than Ahmed.
recs.rel: Chaining two comparisons gives a third one.

recs.q: What does the crescent on the flag of Pakistan represent?
recs.facts: According to the usual explanation, the crescent stands for progress.
recs.rel: The five pointed star stands for light and knowledge, and the white strip for minorities.

recs.q: Who wrote the book 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'?
recs.facts: Pakistan: The Heart of Asia is a collection of speeches made by Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, during his 1950 visit to the USA.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan wrote the autobiography Friends Not Masters.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the International Labour Organization (ILO)?
recs.facts: Pakistan has been an ILO member since 1947, the year of its independence.
recs.rel: The ILO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.

recs.q: Between which latitudes does Pakistan lie?
recs.facts: Pakistan extends from about 24 degrees north in the south to about 37 degrees north in the north.
recs.rel: Pakistan's north-south extent is roughly 1,600 km.

recs.q: In which district of Sindh is Ranikot Fort (Rani Fort) situated?
recs.facts: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills of Jamshoro district in Sindh.
recs.rel: Ranikot is often called the largest fort in the world because its wall is about 26 km long.

recs.q: Which two countries are known for the greatest rivalry in Test cricket?
recs.facts: England and Australia play the Ashes series, the oldest and most famous rivalry in Test cricket.
recs.rel: The Ashes began in 1882 after Australia beat England at The Oval.

recs.q: In which war was Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed martyred?
recs.facts: Captain Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in the 1948 Kashmir war near Uri in October 1948.
recs.rel: He was the first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider.

recs.q: Who is called the Traveller of Islam?
recs.facts: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan explorer, travelled about 120,000 km across Africa, Asia and Europe in nearly 30 years.
recs.rel: He wrote the famous travel book called the Rihla.

recs.q: In which year was the Wavell Plan announced?
recs.facts: Lord Wavell, the Viceroy, announced his plan in June 1945, and it was discussed at the Simla Conference.
recs.rel: The Cripps Mission came earlier, in 1942.

recs.q: On a farm, goats are double the cows and camels are double the goats. If there are 10 goats, how many animals are on the farm?
