recs.facts: Nishtar Park is a large park and ground in the Saddar area of Karachi, named after Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar.
recs.rel: Nishtar Hospital, in contrast, is in Multan.

recs.q: On what date did India conduct its first nuclear test?
recs.facts: India carried out its first nuclear test, code named Smiling Buddha, at Pokhran on 18 May 1974.
recs.rel: India's second series of tests at Pokhran was in May 1998.

recs.q: What is the range of the numbers 69 and 9?
recs.facts: Range = largest value minus smallest value = 69 - 9 = 60.
recs.rel: Range is a measure of how spread out the data is.

recs.q: What is the antonym of obligation?
recs.facts: Obligation means something one must do, so its opposite is freedom or choice.
recs.rel: Duty and commitment are synonyms of obligation.

recs.q: What is the antonym of obvious?
recs.facts: Obvious means easily seen or understood, so its opposite is obscure, meaning unclear or hidden.
recs.rel: Evident, plain and clear are synonyms of obvious.

recs.q: Where was the G20 summit of 2023 held?
recs.facts: India held the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi on 9 and 10 September 2023.
recs.rel: The 2022 summit was in Bali, Indonesia, and the 2024 summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

recs.q: Which organization prepares the official map of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Survey of Pakistan, under the Ministry of Defence, is the national mapping organization that prepares official maps.
recs.rel: It was created in 1947 as successor to the Survey of India and is based in Rawalpindi.

recs.q: Which are the official languages of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
recs.facts: The OIC Charter names Arabic, English and French as its three official languages.
recs.rel: The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: Ali is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old is his sister?
recs.facts: Sister's age = 3 x 6 = 18 years.
recs.rel: Here times as old means multiply.

recs.q: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan opened Victoria School at Ghazipur in which year?
recs.facts: Sir Syed founded Victoria School at Ghazipur in 1863 while he was posted there.
recs.rel: In 1864 he also founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: He is a ___ worker (opposite of careful).
recs.facts: Careless means not taking care, which is the opposite of careful.
recs.rel: The suffix less means without, as in careless and helpless.

recs.q: What is the opposite of dominant?
recs.facts: Dominant means having power and control, so its opposite is submissive, meaning yielding to others.
recs.rel: Subordinate is another opposite of dominant.

recs.q: What is the antonym of oppression?
recs.facts: Oppression means harsh and unfair treatment, so freedom and justice are its opposite.
recs.rel: Liberty is another antonym of oppression.

recs.q: Through which province does the Orange Line Metro Train run?
recs.facts: The Orange Line Metro Train runs in Lahore, which is in Punjab.
recs.rel: It is Pakistan's first metro train service.

recs.q: In which year did the Ottoman Caliphate (Khilafat Usmania) come to an end?
recs.facts: The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished the caliphate in March 1924, ending the Khilafat Usmania.
recs.rel: The Ottoman Sultanate had been abolished earlier, in 1922.

recs.q: If the National Assembly and the Senate disagree on a bill, how is the matter resolved under the 1973 Constitution?
opts: By a joint sitting of Parliament
recs.facts: Under Article 70, the President calls a joint sitting of both Houses, and the bill passes by a majority of the members present.
recs.rel: The Senate has 96 members and the National Assembly 336 seats.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word pacific?
recs.facts: Pacific means peaceful and calm; the Pacific Ocean was named for its calm waters by Magellan.
recs.rel: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.

recs.q: On what date was the Third Battle of Panipat fought?
recs.facts: The Third Battle of Panipat took place on 14 January 1761.
recs.rel: The first two battles of Panipat were fought in 1526 and 1556.

recs.q: Which is the most widely spoken language in Pakistan among Pashto, Punjabi and Sindhi?
recs.facts: Punjabi is the mother tongue of the largest share of Pakistanis, followed by Pashto and Sindhi.
recs.rel: Urdu is the national language but is the mother tongue of a smaller share of people.

recs.q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 20 of them are women. What is the percentage of men?
recs.facts: Men = 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage = 10 divided by 30 times 100 = 33.33%.
recs.rel: Two thirds of 30 is 20, so women are 66.67% in this case.

recs.q: Plaster of Paris is made from which chemical compound?
recs.facts: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, made by heating gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate).
recs.rel: When mixed with water it sets into hard gypsum, which is why it is used for casts and moulds.

recs.q: Who framed the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution was drafted and passed by the elected National Assembly, which acted as the constituent assembly.
recs.rel: It was passed in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

recs.q: The Sinai Peninsula is part of which country?
recs.facts: The Sinai Peninsula lies between the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea and belongs to Egypt.
recs.rel: The Suez Canal separates Sinai from the rest of Egypt.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: He said, 'I got a new pen.' (reported as: He said he got a new pen.)
opts: It was said by him that he had got a new pen.
A new pen was got by him.
It is said by him that he got a new pen.
He was said to get a new pen.
recs.facts: The reported statement is changed with the passive form of the reporting verb, 'It was said by him that', followed by the clause. The clause stays in the past perfect form.
recs.rel: Passive voice puts the object of an action in the subject position.

recs.q: A train covers 120 km per hour. How much time will it take to cover 20 km?
recs.facts: Time = 20 / 120 hour = 1/6 hour. 1/6 of 60 minutes = 10 minutes.
recs.rel: Time = distance divided by speed.

recs.q: What percent of 6 is 2?
recs.rel: 2 out of 6 is the same as the fraction 1/3.

recs.q: What is the value of 5P3?
What is the value of 6P3?
How many permutations (arrangements) are there of 3 different things taken all together?
recs.rel: The six arrangements of A, B, C are ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA.

recs.q: An heir is a person who does what?
opts: Inherits the property or title of a deceased person
recs.facts: An heir is a person legally entitled to receive the property, rank or title of someone after that person dies.
recs.rel: A person who writes a will is called a testator.

recs.q: Pablo Picasso was famous in which field?
recs.facts: Picasso was a painter and sculptor and one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.
recs.rel: His famous painting Guernica shows the bombing of a Spanish town in 1937.

recs.q: Which is the coldest planet of the solar system?
recs.facts: Uranus has the lowest recorded atmospheric temperature, about minus 224 degrees Celsius.
recs.rel: Neptune is farther from the Sun, but sources differ because Uranus is colder at its cloud tops.

recs.q: Which is the largest nuclear power plant of Pakistan?
opts: Karachi Nuclear Power Plant (K-2 and K-3)
recs.facts: The Karachi twin units K-2 and K-3 are rated at 1100 MW each, 2200 MW in total, which is the largest in Pakistan.
recs.rel: The C-5 unit under construction at Chashma is planned to be about 1200 MW.

recs.q: Against which country did Pakistan play its first Test match?
recs.facts: Pakistan played its first Test against India at Delhi in October 1952.
recs.rel: Pakistan became a Test-playing nation in 1952.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan first take part in the Olympic Games?
recs.facts: Pakistan first took part in the Olympics at London in 1948, soon after independence.
recs.rel: Pakistan won its first Olympic medal, a bronze in hockey, at Melbourne in 1956.

recs.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: She told me not to play football.
She told me to not play football.
She told me did not to play cricket.
She told me not play football.
recs.facts: In reported commands, the negative is formed as 'told someone not to + verb'. 'Not to' stays together before the verb.
recs.rel: Reported commands use the infinitive form of the verb.

recs.q: Which country invaded Poland in September 1939, starting World War II in Europe?
recs.facts: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France then declared war on Germany.
recs.rel: The Soviet Union invaded Poland from the east on 17 September 1939.

recs.q: Which sport is the most popular and widely played sport in the world?
recs.facts: Football (soccer) is played and followed in almost every country, with billions of fans.
recs.rel: Cricket is the second most followed sport, mainly in South Asia, Australia, England and the West Indies.

recs.q: Who presented the famous Fourteen Points in 1929?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
recs.rel: The Fourteen Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, including separation of Sindh from Bombay.

recs.q: Is 39 a prime number or a composite number?
recs.facts: 39 = 3 x 13, so it has factors other than 1 and itself. Therefore it is composite.
recs.rel: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

recs.q: What is the product of all the fourth roots of unity?
recs.facts: The fourth roots of unity are 1, -1, i and -i. Product = (1)(-1)(i)(-i) = (-1)(1) = -1, because i x (-i) = 1.
recs.rel: The sum of all fourth roots of unity is 0.

recs.q: What was the profession of Dr. Ruth Pfau, who worked for leprosy patients in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Dr. Ruth Pfau was a German physician and nun who came to Pakistan in 1960. She devoted her life to fighting leprosy.
recs.rel: She died in Karachi in 2017 and was given a state funeral.

recs.q: What is a first person pronoun?
recs.facts: First person pronouns refer to the speaker. I, me, we and us are first person pronouns.
recs.rel: You is second person, while he, she, it and they are third person.

recs.q: Who was the first prophet of Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Adam (AS) was the first human being and the first prophet. The line of prophets ended with Hazrat Muhammad (SAW).
recs.rel: Hazrat Nuh (AS) is often called the first messenger sent to a disbelieving people.

recs.q: In which province is the Kachhi district located?
recs.facts: Kachhi district, with its headquarters at Dhadar, lies in Balochistan. The Bolan Pass area is part of it.
recs.rel: Kachhi plain is also known as the Kachhi-Bolan area.

recs.q: In which province is the city of Rahim Yar Khan located?
recs.facts: Rahim Yar Khan is a city and district in southern Punjab. It lies near the borders of Sindh and Balochistan.
recs.rel: It is part of the Bahawalpur division.

recs.q: How many states does India have?
recs.facts: India has 28 states and 8 union territories. Telangana became the 29th state in 2014, but Jammu and Kashmir became a union territory in 2019.
recs.rel: Ladakh became a separate union territory in 2019.

recs.q: In which year was PTCL (Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited) established?
recs.facts: PTCL was formed in 1996 by taking over the telecom operations of the Pakistan Telegraph and Telephone Department. It was partly privatised in 2006.
recs.rel: Etisalat of the UAE bought a controlling stake in 2006.

recs.q: What does PTCL stand for?
recs.facts: PTCL is the short form of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited. It is the country's largest telecom operator in fixed line services.
recs.rel: It owns the Ufone mobile brand.

recs.q: Who is the Education Minister of Punjab (Pakistan) at present?
recs.facts: Rana Sikandar Hayat is the School Education Minister in the Punjab government, as reported in 2026. Maryam Nawaz is the Chief Minister.
recs.rel: Ministers can change after a cabinet reshuffle.

recs.q: Which is the largest district of Punjab (Pakistan) by area?
recs.facts: Bahawalpur district covers about 24,800 square km, the largest in Punjab. Rahim Yar Khan and Dera Ghazi Khan are smaller.
recs.rel: Lahore is the largest district by population in Punjab.

recs.q: On which date were the Qadianis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The National Assembly passed the Second Amendment on 7 September 1974. It declared Qadianis non-Muslim.
recs.rel: 7 September is remembered in Pakistan as Khatm-e-Nubuwwat Day.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 1/10 of 1/120?
recs.rel: Taking a quarter of a number means dividing it by 4.

recs.q: What is a quarter of 1/10 of 1200?
recs.rel: A quarter of 1200 is 300, so one tenth of that is also 30.

recs.q: What is the range of the data 15, 11, 3, 2, 7, 9?
recs.facts: Range = largest value minus smallest value = 15 - 2 = 13.
recs.rel: Range is a simple measure of how spread out the data is.

recs.q: What is the range of the data 3, 7, 5, 12, 2, 4, 9?
recs.facts: Range = largest value minus smallest value = 12 - 2 = 10.
recs.rel: The range is affected strongly by extreme values.

recs.q: Why did Japan attack Pearl Harbor in December 1941?
opts: To destroy the US Pacific Fleet so it could not stop Japanese expansion in Asia
To take control of Hawaii permanently
recs.facts: Japan wanted to cripple the US Pacific Fleet so America could not interfere with its conquests in Southeast Asia and the Pacific. US oil and trade sanctions had also pushed Japan to act.
recs.rel: The attack on 7 December 1941 brought the United States into the Second World War.

recs.q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan receive the knighthood (KCSI)?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was given the title of Knight Commander of the Star of India (KCSI) in 1888.
recs.rel: He had earlier received the title of Jawad-ud-Daula in 1877.

recs.q: The Red Sea lies between Africa and which other continent?
recs.facts: The Red Sea separates northeastern Africa from the Arabian Peninsula of Asia.
recs.rel: The Red Sea joins the Mediterranean Sea through the Suez Canal.

recs.q: The Beas river mainly flows in which country?
recs.facts: The Beas river rises in Himachal Pradesh and flows through Punjab in India before joining the Sutlej.
recs.rel: The Beas is one of the five rivers of Punjab and was given to India under the Indus Waters Treaty.

recs.q: Who was the Viceroy of India when Bengal was divided in 1905?
recs.facts: Lord Curzon announced and carried out the Partition of Bengal in 1905.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: During whose reign was the East India Company formed (chartered) in 1600?
recs.facts: The English East India Company received its royal charter in 1600 from Queen Elizabeth I.
recs.rel: Queen Victoria took direct control of India in 1858 after the war of 1857.

recs.q: During whose reign did the East India Company first enter India (Surat, 1608)?
recs.facts: Captain William Hawkins reached the Mughal court in 1608 and Jahangir later allowed the company to trade at Surat.
recs.rel: Sir Thomas Roe came to Jahangir's court as English ambassador in 1615.

recs.q: A cardiogram (ECG) is related to which organ of the body?
recs.facts: An electrocardiogram records the electrical activity of the heart.
recs.rel: An EEG records brain activity.

recs.q: What does GT Road stand for?
recs.facts: GT Road means Grand Trunk Road, one of the oldest and longest major roads of South Asia.
recs.rel: It runs from Kabul in Afghanistan to Kolkata in India.

recs.q: Who rebuilt and developed the Grand Trunk Road in the sixteenth century?
recs.facts: Sher Shah Suri reconstructed the old road, added rest houses (sarais), wells and trees along it.
recs.rel: The road was originally an ancient route, and is also called Sarak-e-Azam.

recs.q: What is the result when a negative number is multiplied by a negative number?
recs.facts: The product of two numbers with the same sign is positive. For example, -3 x -4 = 12.
recs.rel: A positive number times a negative number gives a negative result.

recs.q: What is the square root of 4?
recs.facts: 2 x 2 = 4, so the square root of 4 is 2.
recs.rel: A perfect square has a whole number as its square root.

recs.q: What does the idiom 'a bed of roses' mean?
recs.facts: The idiom 'a bed of roses' means a pleasant, comfortable and easy situation.
recs.rel: It is often used in the negative, as in 'Life is not a bed of roses'.

recs.q: Which title is given to Hazrat Jibrael (AS), the angel who brought revelation?
recs.facts: Ruhul Quds (the Holy Spirit) is a title of the angel Hazrat Jibrael (AS).
recs.rel: He is also called Ruh-ul-Amin, the Trustworthy Spirit.

recs.q: For about how long did the Ottoman Empire rule?
recs.facts: The Ottoman Empire began around 1299 under Osman I and ended in 1922, so it lasted over 600 years.
recs.rel: It was one of the longest-lasting empires in history.

recs.q: In which year did Sindh come under British rule after the Battle of Miani?
recs.facts: Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at Miani in February 1843 and Sindh was annexed that year.
recs.rel: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936.

recs.q: In the DMAS rule of mathematics, which operation is carried out first?
recs.facts: DMAS stands for Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction, and the operations are done in this order.
recs.rel: BODMAS adds Brackets and Of before Division.

recs.q: Which country attacked the Soviet Union (Russia) in World War 2 in 1941?
recs.facts: Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941 under Operation Barbarossa.
recs.rel: The Soviet Union then joined the Allies against Germany.

recs.q: What is the full name of the hadith book Sahih Bukhari?
recs.facts: Imam Bukhari named his book Al-Jami al-Sahih (the Authentic Collection).
recs.rel: It is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after the Quran.

recs.q: What was the old name of the city of Sahiwal?
recs.facts: Sahiwal was called Montgomery during British rule and was renamed in 1967.
recs.rel: Lyallpur, now Faisalabad, was another city renamed after a British officer.

recs.q: Saleem has an average of 60 in 4 subjects. After the next test his average falls to 58. How many marks did he score in the next test?
recs.facts: Total of 4 subjects = 4 x 60 = 240. Total of 5 tests = 5 x 58 = 290. Next score = 290 - 240 = 50.
recs.rel: Average equals total marks divided by the number of tests.

recs.q: Change the narration into indirect speech: Sara said, "I am sorry."
opts: Sara said that she is sorry.
Sara said that she was sorry.
Sara said that I was sorry.
Sara said that she had been sorry.
recs.facts: In indirect speech the present tense changes to past after a past reporting verb, and I becomes she.
recs.rel: Pronouns in indirect speech change to match the reporter's point of view.

recs.q: Which two countries surround the Aral Sea?
recs.facts: The Aral Sea lies between Kazakhstan in the north and Uzbekistan in the south.
recs.rel: It has shrunk greatly since the 1960s.

recs.q: The Caucasus region lies between which two seas?
recs.facts: The Caucasus mountain region lies between the Black Sea in the west and the Caspian Sea in the east.
recs.rel: Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus is the highest peak in Europe.

recs.q: Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal in Egypt links the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
recs.rel: It opened in 1869.

recs.q: What is sec 2x equal to?
recs.facts: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, so sec of any angle is 1 divided by cos of that angle. For the angle 2x this gives sec 2x = 1 / cos 2x.
recs.rel: Sec 2x is not the same as 2 sec x.

recs.q: Fill in the preposition: A private secretary has no authority ___ his boss.
recs.facts: The correct phrase is authority over someone, meaning power to control them.
recs.rel: We say authority over a person but authority on a subject.

recs.q: What is the total number of women seats in the Senate of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Each of the four provinces has 4 seats for women, which is 16, and Islamabad has 1 women seat. The total is 17.
recs.rel: The Senate has 96 members in all.

recs.q: In a class of 33 students, 7 are boys. What is the percentage of girls (approximately)?
recs.rel: Boys are 7 / 33 x 100 = 21.21%, and the two add to 100%.

recs.q: What is the range of Pakistan's Shaheen-III missile?
recs.facts: Shaheen-III is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile with a range of about 2750 km.
recs.rel: Shaheen-I has a range of about 750 km.

recs.q: Which letter comes next in the series: b5, g8, l11, q14, ?
recs.facts: Letters move 5 steps each time (b, g, l, q, v) and the numbers go up by 3 (5, 8, 11, 14, 17). So the next term is v17.
recs.rel: Skipping 4 letters between terms gives a step of 5.

recs.q: Find the next letter in the series: A C G M ?
recs.facts: Positions are 1, 3, 7, 13. The gaps are 2, 4, 6, so the next gap is 8, giving position 21, which is U.
recs.rel: The gaps in this series are even numbers rising by 2.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: Z3, Y6, X9, ?
recs.facts: Letters go backward by one (Z, Y, X, W) and numbers go up by 3 (3, 6, 9, 12). So the next term is W12.
recs.rel: Z is the 26th letter and goes down one position each time.

recs.q: In which year was Colonel Sher Khan (Nishan-e-Haider) martyred?
recs.facts: Captain (later Colonel) Karnal Sher Khan was martyred in the Kargil conflict in July 1999. He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.
recs.rel: He is the only Pakistan Army officer of Kargil to receive the Nishan-e-Haider.

recs.q: What is the value of sin 45 degrees?
recs.facts: In a right isosceles triangle with equal sides 1, the hypotenuse is square root of 2, so sin 45 is 1 divided by square root of 2, about 0.707.
recs.rel: Cos 45 degrees has the same value as sin 45 degrees.

recs.q: Sidra is 6 years old and her brother is twice her age. How old will her brother be when Sidra becomes 11?
recs.facts: Brother is 6 x 2 = 12 now. Sidra becomes 11 after 5 years, so the brother will be 12 + 5 = 17.
recs.rel: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: Ali is 6 years old and his sister is 2 times his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 8 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 6 x 2 = 12 now. Ali becomes 8 after 2 years, so she will be 12 + 2 = 14.
recs.rel: Here the sister is 6 years older than Ali, and the gap never changes.

recs.q: What is Sihah Sitta?
recs.facts: Sihah Sitta means the six most reliable books of hadith: Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai and Ibn Majah.
recs.rel: Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are together called the Sahihain.

recs.q: Why did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan receive the title of Sir?
opts: He was knighted by the British Government in 1888 for his services
He was elected president of the Muslim League
He founded the city of Aligarh
recs.facts: The British Government honoured him with a knighthood (KCSI) in 1888 in recognition of his public and educational services.
recs.rel: He had earlier been given the title Javad-ud-Daula by the Mughal emperor.

recs.q: What was the slogan of the Pakistan National Alliance (PNA) movement of 1977?
recs.facts: The PNA, an alliance of nine parties against Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, campaigned for the enforcement of the system of the Prophet (PBUH), called Nizam-e-Mustafa.
recs.rel: The movement began after the March 1977 elections, and General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977.

recs.q: A pen is bought for Rs 50 and sold for Rs 70. What is the percentage of profit?
recs.facts: Profit = 70 - 50 = Rs 20. Profit percentage = 20/50 x 100 = 40%.
recs.rel: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price, not the selling price.

recs.q: A car has a speed of 120 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12.5 minutes?
recs.facts: 12.5 minutes = 12.5/60 hour. Distance = 120 x 12.5/60 = 25 km.
recs.rel: At 120 km/h a car covers 2 km every minute.

recs.q: Which ocean lies to the south of India?
recs.facts: The Indian Ocean surrounds the southern tip of the Indian peninsula, with the Bay of Bengal to the east and the Arabian Sea to the west.
recs.rel: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean in the world.

recs.q: In World War 2 (1939), which country did the Soviet Union attack first?
recs.facts: On 17 September 1939 the Soviet army invaded eastern Poland, soon after Germany invaded from the west.
recs.rel: The Soviet Union attacked Finland in the Winter War a few weeks later, in November 1939.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling of this military rank?
recs.facts: The correct spelling is Lieutenant.
recs.rel: In Pakistan Army the rank of Lieutenant is the first commissioned rank after passing out from PMA.

recs.q: What is the area of a square whose side is 5 units?
recs.facts: Area of a square = side x side = 5 x 5 = 25 square units.
recs.rel: The perimeter of this square would be 4 x 5 = 20 units.

recs.q: What is the square of 12?
recs.rel: 12 squared is also called one gross, which is 144 items.

recs.q: What is the square of 13?
recs.rel: 169 equals 144 + 25, which is 12 squared plus 5 squared.

recs.q: In which city is Tahrir Square located?
recs.facts: Tahrir Square is in the centre of Cairo, the capital of Egypt.
recs.rel: It was the main centre of the Egyptian revolution of 2011.

recs.q: Who is the legendary squash player of Pakistan who won the World Open six times?
recs.facts: Jahangir Khan is regarded as the greatest squash player ever and won the World Open six times.
recs.rel: He was unbeaten in 555 consecutive matches from 1981 to 1986.

recs.q: In which year were the Engineering Research Laboratories (later Khan Research Laboratories) of Dr A. Q. Khan established at Kahuta?
recs.facts: Dr A. Q. Khan founded the laboratory in 1976 to build uranium enrichment capability.
recs.rel: It was renamed Khan Research Laboratories in 1981 by President Zia-ul-Haq.

recs.q: Fill in the preposition: He waited ___ the station.
recs.facts: We use at with a place regarded as a point, such as a station.
recs.rel: Waited for is used with the thing or person awaited, such as waited for the train.

recs.q: Which is the highest railway station in Pakistan, at about 2,224 metres above sea level?
recs.facts: Kan Mehtarzai on the Zhob Valley Railway in Balochistan is cited as Pakistan's highest railway station.
recs.rel: The line is closed since 1986 and Kan Mehtarzai is no longer in use.

recs.q: Out of 540 students, 160 are present. What is the approximate percentage of students present?
recs.facts: Percentage = 160 / 540 x 100 = 29.63, which is about 29.6%.
recs.rel: The number of absent students is 540 - 160 = 380, which is about 70.4%.

recs.q: Syed Ahmad Shaheed (Barelvi), leader of the Mujahideen movement, was a student of whom?
recs.facts: Syed Ahmad Shaheed studied in Delhi under Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlawi, son of Shah Waliullah.
recs.rel: Syed Ahmad Shaheed was martyred at Balakot in 1831 fighting the Sikhs.

recs.q: Which battle is generally called the first major battle of the British in the subcontinent that gave them rule in Bengal?
recs.facts: In the Battle of Plassey (1757) the East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah.
recs.rel: Some sources count the earlier Carnatic wars as the first fights, but textbooks give Plassey.

recs.q: Which two water bodies does the Suez Canal connect?
recs.facts: The Suez Canal in Egypt joins the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
recs.rel: It was opened in 1869 and shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia.

recs.q: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) was the son of which prophet?
recs.facts: The Quran mentions Sulaiman (AS) as the son and heir of Prophet Dawud (AS).
recs.rel: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) was given control over the winds and the jinn.

recs.q: Takht-e-Sulaiman is the highest peak of which mountain range?
recs.facts: Takht-e-Sulaiman, about 3,487 metres high, is the highest peak of the Sulaiman Range in Balochistan.
recs.rel: The Sulaiman Range lies in the west of Pakistan along the Balochistan and KP border.

recs.q: What is a Madni (Madani) surah of the Quran?
opts: A surah revealed before the Hijrah
A surah revealed after the Hijrah
A surah revealed in Makkah only
A surah with the fewest verses
recs.facts: Surahs revealed after the Prophet's migration (Hijrah) to Madinah are called Madni surahs.
recs.rel: Madni surahs mostly deal with laws, society and the state.

recs.q: Which surah of the Quran contains the Bismillah twice?
recs.facts: Surah An-Naml has Bismillah at the start and again inside verse 30, in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS).
recs.rel: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that has no Bismillah at its start.

recs.q: According to the common textbook count, how many Makki and Madni surahs does the Quran have?
recs.facts: The common Pakistani textbook count is 86 Makki surahs and 28 Madni surahs, which total 114.
recs.rel: Scholars differ slightly in the count of some surahs.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'apology'?
recs.facts: An apology is an expression of regret for a wrong done.
recs.rel: To apologise means to say sorry.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'clever'?
recs.facts: Clever means quick to learn and understand, which is the same as intelligent.
recs.rel: The opposite (antonym) of clever is foolish or dull.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'ferocious'?
recs.facts: Ferocious means savage and violent, which is the same as fierce.
recs.rel: Ferocity is the noun form of ferocious.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'God'?
recs.facts: A deity is a god or divine being.
recs.rel: The word deity comes from the Latin deus, meaning god.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'retreat'?
recs.facts: To retreat means to move back or withdraw, especially from danger or an enemy.
recs.rel: The opposite (antonym) of retreat is advance.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'stereotypical'?
recs.facts: Stereotypical means following a fixed, common pattern, which is close to conventional.
recs.rel: A stereotype is an over-simplified fixed idea about a type of person or thing.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'talkative'?
recs.facts: Talkative means fond of talking a lot, which is the same as garrulous.
recs.rel: The opposite (antonym) of talkative is reserved or silent.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'garrulous'?
recs.facts: Garrulous means excessively talkative.
recs.rel: The noun form is garrulity.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'expunge'?
recs.facts: To expunge means to wipe out or erase completely.
recs.rel: Expunge is often used for removing names or remarks from a record.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'literally'?
recs.facts: Literally means in the exact, actual sense of the words.
recs.rel: The opposite idea is figuratively.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'lowly'?
recs.facts: Lowly means of low rank or status, which is close to humble.
recs.rel: The opposite (antonym) of lowly is exalted.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'boast'?
recs.facts: To boast means to talk proudly about oneself, which is the same as to brag.
recs.rel: A person who boasts too much is called boastful.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'disaster'?
recs.facts: A disaster is a sudden event causing great damage, which is a catastrophe.
recs.rel: Earthquakes and floods are examples of natural disasters.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'indescribable'?
recs.facts: Indescribable means too great or strange to be put into words, which is inexpressible.
recs.rel: The prefix in- here means not.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word insurgence?
recs.facts: Insurgence means an uprising or revolt against an authority. Rebellion has the same meaning.
recs.rel: An insurgent is a person who rises in revolt against a government.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word normal?
recs.facts: Normal means usual and as expected. Ordinary has the same meaning.
recs.rel: The opposite of normal is abnormal or unusual.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word pragmatic?
recs.facts: A pragmatic person deals with things in a sensible and realistic way. Practical has the same meaning.
recs.rel: The opposite of pragmatic is idealistic or impractical.

recs.q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word tamper?
recs.facts: To tamper means to interfere with something in order to damage or change it without permission. Interfere is the nearest meaning.
recs.rel: Tampering with evidence is a crime in most countries.

recs.q: Which tense is used in the sentence: They are watching TV?
recs.facts: The verb group are watching uses is/am/are plus verb-ing, which shows an action happening now. This is the present continuous tense.
recs.rel: The past continuous form would be: They were watching TV.

recs.q: If 1 = 7 and 3 = 9, then 13 = ?
recs.facts: Each number is 6 more than the given number: 1 + 6 = 7 and 3 + 6 = 9. So 13 + 6 = 19.
recs.rel: In such code questions first find the rule that fits all the given examples.

recs.q: What is one third of 20% of 60?
recs.facts: 20% of 60 = 12. One third of 12 = 4.
recs.rel: To find a percentage, multiply by the percent and divide by 100.

recs.q: What is one third of 30% of 120?
recs.facts: 30% of 120 = 36. One third of 36 = 12.
recs.rel: 30% of a number equals three tenths of it.

recs.q: What is one third of 95?
recs.facts: 95 divided by 3 = 31 with remainder 2, so the answer is 31 and 2/3 (31.67).
recs.rel: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3; 9 + 5 = 14 is not.

recs.q: Ali's age is 5 years and his sister is three times his age. What will be his sister's age when Ali is 20?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 20, she will be 20 + 10 = 30.
recs.rel: The age difference between two persons always stays the same.

recs.q: Hania is 4 years old and her sister is three times her age. What will her sister's age be when Hania is 10?
recs.facts: Sister's age now = 3 x 4 = 12, so she is 8 years older. When Hania is 10, the sister will be 10 + 8 = 18.
recs.rel: The age difference between two persons always stays the same.

recs.q: Who gave the first Azan inside the Kaaba after the conquest of Makkah?
recs.facts: On the day Makkah was conquered, the Prophet (PBUH) asked Hazrat Bilal (RA) to call the Azan from the roof of the Kaaba.
recs.rel: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was the first Muezzin of Islam.

recs.q: Who inaugurated the Mazar-e-Quaid (Quaid-e-Azam Mausoleum) in Karachi?
recs.facts: The mausoleum was opened to the public by President Yahya Khan in January 1971.
recs.rel: Its construction was completed in 1970 and the architect was Yahya Merchant.

recs.q: How many oceans are there in the world?
recs.facts: The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic Oceans.
recs.rel: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.

recs.q: In which year of prophethood did the Muslims first migrate to Habsha (Abyssinia)?
recs.facts: The first migration to Abyssinia took place in the 5th year of prophethood, around 615 CE.
recs.rel: The Muslims were given shelter by the just king Najashi.

recs.q: A train covers 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the train covers 20 / 100 = 0.2 km each minute. In 5 minutes it covers 5 x 0.2 = 1 km.
recs.rel: The speed of this train is 12 km per hour.

recs.q: The speed of a car is 60 km/h and a train goes at double that speed. How far does the train travel in 100 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 100 minutes (5/3 hour) it covers 120 x 5/3 = 200 km.
recs.rel: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

recs.q: A man travels 90 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
recs.facts: Total time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so time for 1 km = 100/90 = 1.11 minutes.
recs.rel: His speed is 54 km per hour.

recs.q: What type of number is 0?
recs.facts: Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3 and so on, so 0 is a whole number but not a natural number.
recs.rel: Natural numbers start from 1.

recs.q: After rearranging the letters of the word UEABYIFT, what is the last letter of the new word?
recs.facts: The letters make the word BEAUTIFY, which ends with Y.
recs.rel: BEAUTIFY means to make something beautiful.

recs.q: Who was the Man of the Tournament in the 1999 Cricket World Cup?
recs.facts: South African all-rounder Lance Klusener was named Man of the Tournament in 1999.
recs.rel: Australia won that World Cup, beating Pakistan in the final.

recs.q: Ali is shorter than Umar and Umar is shorter than Abdullah. What is the relation of Ali and Umar?
opts: Ali and Umar are of equal height
recs.facts: The first statement says directly that Ali is shorter than Umar.
recs.rel: From both statements, Abdullah is the tallest and Ali is the shortest of the three.

recs.q: Umer is 3 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old will his sister be when Umer is 9?
recs.facts: The sister is 6 now, so she is 3 years older than Umer. When Umer is 9, she will be 9 + 3 = 12.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people stays the same for life.

recs.q: What is the unit of lens power?
recs.facts: The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length in metres, and its unit is the dioptre (D).
recs.rel: A converging lens has positive power and a diverging lens has negative power.

recs.q: Who was the President of the USA for most of the Second World War?
recs.facts: Franklin D. Roosevelt was President from 1933 until his death in April 1945, covering most of the war.
recs.rel: Harry Truman succeeded him and ordered the atomic bombings of Japan in August 1945.

recs.q: An airplane uses 80 gallons of fuel to travel 320 km. How many gallons will it use to travel 700 km?
recs.facts: It uses 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon per km. For 700 km: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
recs.rel: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance when the rate is constant.

recs.q: At which place did India conduct its nuclear bomb tests in 1974 and 1998?
recs.facts: India tested its nuclear devices at Pokhran in the Rajasthan desert.
recs.rel: Pakistan conducted its tests in the Chagai hills in May 1998.

recs.q: What is a refrigerator (fridge) mainly used for?
recs.facts: A fridge keeps the inside cool so that food stays fresh and does not spoil quickly.
recs.rel: A refrigerator works by removing heat from its inside and releasing it outside.

recs.q: If Ali is older than Usman and Noman is older than Ali, who is the eldest?
recs.facts: Noman is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Usman, so the order is Noman, Ali, Usman.
recs.rel: Usman is the youngest of the three.

recs.q: What does USSR stand for?
recs.facts: USSR stands for the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, the communist state formed in 1922.
recs.rel: The USSR broke up in December 1991 into 15 independent countries.

recs.q: Where is the Kalash Valley located?
recs.facts: The Kalash valleys (Bumburet, Rumbur and Birir) lie in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: The Kalash people follow their own ancient religion and culture.

recs.q: What is the value of i^5, where i is the imaginary unit?
recs.facts: i^2 = -1 and i^4 = 1, so i^5 = i^4 x i = 1 x i = i.
recs.rel: The powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1.

recs.q: What is velocity?
opts: Rate of change of displacement with time
recs.facts: Velocity is a vector quantity: displacement divided by the time taken, so it has both speed and direction.
recs.rel: The SI unit of velocity is metre per second.

recs.q: What is the vertical arrangement of numbers in a matrix called?
recs.facts: Entries written from top to bottom form a column, while entries written left to right form a row.
recs.rel: A matrix with m rows and n columns is said to be of order m x n.

recs.q: Change the voice: You praised her very much.
opts: She is praised very much by you.
She was praised very much by you.
She had praised you very much.
She has been praised very much by you.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was or were with the past participle: She was praised very much by you.
recs.rel: In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

recs.q: Who was the Viceroy of India in 1913?
recs.facts: Lord Hardinge served as Viceroy from 1910 to 1916, which includes 1913.
recs.rel: The capital of British India was moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911 during his time.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the name Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pak means pure and stan means land, so Pakistan means Land of the Pure.
recs.rel: The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

recs.q: How many vowels are in the letter string AHGRUOVE?
recs.facts: The vowels in AHGRUOVE are A, U, O and E. That makes 4 vowels.
recs.rel: The five English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: How many vowels are in the letter string AHJKFSREKHVCIBKMNEI?
recs.facts: Going through the letters, the vowels are A, E, I, E and I. That makes 5 vowels.
recs.rel: Y is treated as a consonant in these verbal tests unless the question says otherwise.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in the word Tuesday?
recs.facts: The vowels in Tuesday are U, E and A. The letter Y is a consonant here, so the total is 3.
recs.rel: The word Tuesday has 7 letters, of which 4 are consonants.

recs.q: In which year did Shah Waliullah of Delhi die?
recs.facts: Shah Waliullah Dehlawi died in Delhi in 1762 (1176 AH).
recs.rel: He was born in 1703 and is famous for his book Hujjat Allah al-Baligha.

recs.q: A man walks 1 m north, turns right, walks 1 m and then turns back. In which direction is he facing now?
recs.facts: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. Turning back reverses the direction, so he faces west.
recs.rel: Turning back means turning through 180 degrees.

recs.q: Ali walked 20 km in 120 minutes. How much distance will Ali cover in 5 minutes at the same speed?
recs.facts: Speed is 20 km per 120 minutes, which is 1/6 km per minute. In 5 minutes he covers 5/6 km, about 0.83 km (833 m).
recs.rel: 20 km in 2 hours means a speed of 10 km/h.

recs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He walked ___ school.
recs.facts: The preposition towards shows the direction of movement, so 'He walked towards school' is correct.
recs.rel: The preposition to is also used with walk, as in 'walked to school'.

recs.q: In which years did the two World Wars take place?
recs.facts: World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918 and World War II from 1939 to 1945.
recs.rel: World War II began with the German invasion of Poland in September 1939.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: She said to me that she was watching TV.
opts: I was told by her that she was watching TV.
I told her that she was watching TV.
She was told by me that she was watching TV.
TV was being watched by her to me.
recs.facts: In the passive form the object (me) becomes the subject, and said to becomes was told by. The reported clause stays the same.
recs.rel: The verb tell is used in the passive instead of say for reported speech.

recs.q: What was the Wavell Plan?
opts: A plan to reconstitute the Viceroy's Executive Council with equal Hindu and Muslim representation
A plan to partition India into two states
A plan to give India dominion status immediately
A plan to hold elections for a Constituent Assembly
recs.facts: Wavell proposed an Executive Council in which all members except the Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief were Indians, with parity between caste Hindus and Muslims.
recs.rel: The plan failed because Congress and the Muslim League disagreed over who could nominate Muslim members.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: She is ___ weak in maths.
recs.facts: The adverb very is used before an adjective such as weak to give strength. Much, many and more do not fit here.
recs.rel: Very is an adverb of degree.

recs.q: Which symbol is used for the set of whole numbers?
recs.facts: The set of whole numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, ...) is written W.
recs.rel: N is for natural numbers, Z for integers and Q for rational numbers.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word widely?
recs.facts: Widely means over a large area or among many people, which is the same as extensively.
recs.rel: Narrowly is the opposite of widely.

recs.q: What is the area of a rectangle with length 5 and width 4?
recs.facts: Area of a rectangle is length times width, so 5 x 4 = 20 square units.
recs.rel: The perimeter of this rectangle would be 2 x (5 + 4) = 18 units.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word wildly?
recs.facts: Wildly means in an uncontrolled or fierce way, which is close to violently.
recs.rel: Calmly is its opposite.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word wildly?
recs.facts: Wildly means in an uncontrolled way, so the opposite is calmly.
recs.rel: Wild (adjective) has the opposite tame.

recs.q: If 1 man writes 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will 5 men write in 25 minutes?
recs.facts: One man writes 1 page per minute. So 5 men write 5 pages per minute, and in 25 minutes they write 5 x 25 = 125 pages.
recs.rel: Work problems are solved by first finding the rate of one worker.

recs.q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day is it today?
recs.facts: The day after Sunday is Monday.
recs.rel: Monday is the first working day after the weekend in many countries.

recs.q: What is the chemical symbol of zinc?
recs.facts: The symbol of zinc is Zn.
recs.rel: Zinc is used to galvanise iron to prevent rusting.

recs.q: What is 1 + 2/2 + 2?
recs.facts: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.
recs.rel: BODMAS says division comes before addition.

recs.q: What is 1 + 1/2?
recs.rel: 1.5 can also be written as 3/2.

recs.q: What is 10% of 33?
recs.rel: To find 10%, divide by 10.

recs.q: What is 20% of 41?
recs.rel: 20% equals one fifth.

recs.q: What is 22 + 2/2?
recs.facts: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 22 + 1 = 23.
recs.rel: BODMAS says division comes before addition.

recs.q: What is 3x + 3y written in factor form?
recs.facts: Both terms have the common factor 3, so 3x + 3y = 3(x + y).
recs.rel: Taking out a common factor is called factorisation.

recs.q: What is 60% of 60?
recs.rel: 60% equals 3/5.

recs.q: What is 65% of 70?
recs.rel: 10% of 70 is 7, so 60% is 42 and 5% is 3.5.

recs.q: What is 72% of 80?
recs.rel: 10% of 80 is 8, so 70% is 56 and 2% is 1.6.

recs.q: What is 80 x 80?
recs.facts: 8 x 8 = 64, and two zeros are added, giving 6400.
recs.rel: 80 squared is 6400.

recs.q: What is 81% of 81?
What is 90 x 90?
recs.facts: 9 x 9 = 81, and two zeros are added, giving 8100.
recs.rel: 90 squared is 8100.

recs.q: What is 90% of 89?
What does KG stand for?
recs.facts: KG is the short form of kilogram, the SI unit of mass.
recs.rel: One kilogram equals 1000 grams.

recs.q: What is the H.C.F of 4 and 16?
recs.facts: Factors of 4 are 1, 2, 4. All of these divide 16, so the highest common factor is 4.
recs.rel: If one number divides the other, it is the HCF.

recs.q: What was the Islamic date of the independence of Pakistan (14 August 1947)?
recs.facts: 14 August 1947 fell on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, the blessed night of Laylat ul Qadr as commonly believed.
recs.rel: Because of this date, Pakistan is often called a gift of the holy month of Ramadan.

recs.q: Arrange the letters of PLOEADR to make the name of an animal.
recs.facts: The letters P, L, O, E, A, D, R make the word LEOPARD, a big cat. It uses all seven letters once.
recs.rel: The leopard is a spotted big cat found in Asia and Africa.

recs.q: On what date did the Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) receive royal assent?
recs.facts: The Act got royal assent on 23 December 1919 and the reforms started in 1921. They introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
recs.rel: The 20 August 1917 date is Montagu's announcement in the House of Commons.

recs.q: What is the value of 3 factorial (3!)?
recs.rel: By definition, 0! = 1.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the ancient site of Kot Diji located?
recs.facts: Kot Diji is in Khairpur district of Sindh, near the Indus River. Its fort and Indus Valley site are well known.
recs.rel: The Kot Diji culture is an early phase of the Indus Valley civilization, before Mohenjo-daro.

recs.q: Qantas is the national airline of which country?
recs.facts: Qantas is the flag carrier of Australia. The name comes from Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services.
recs.rel: It was founded in 1920.

recs.q: According to grammar, what part of speech is the word 'between'?
recs.facts: 'Between' shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word, as in 'between the two trees'. A word that does this is a preposition.
recs.rel: 'Between' is normally used for two things, while 'among' is used for more than two.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book India, My Love?
recs.facts: India, My Love is a book by the French author Dominique Lapierre about his travels in India. The French title is India Mon Amour.
recs.rel: Lapierre also wrote City of Joy and, with Larry Collins, Freedom at Midnight; a different book called India My Love: A Spiritual Journey also exists.

recs.q: What is the commonly stated range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) short-range ballistic missile?
recs.facts: Nasr is a short-range, nuclear-capable missile with a reported range of 60 to 70 km, with the upgraded version given as 70 km. It is meant as a battlefield weapon.
recs.rel: Early reports gave 60 km, so sources differ depending on the variant.

recs.q: Which planet is called the sister planet of the Earth because of its similar size?
recs.facts: Venus is almost the same size and mass as Earth, so it is called Earth's sister.
recs.rel: Venus is the hottest planet of the solar system.

recs.q: A car is used for what purpose?
recs.facts: A car is a road vehicle used to travel from one place to another.
recs.rel: The first practical petrol car was built by Karl Benz in 1885.

recs.q: About how many litres of blood does an average adult human body contain?
recs.facts: An average adult has about 5 litres of blood, which is roughly 7 to 8 percent of body weight.
recs.rel: Blood is pumped around the body by the heart.

recs.q: Which ancient city is regarded as the centre of Buddhist learning in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Taxila, in the Gandhara region near Rawalpindi, was a famous centre of Buddhist learning and art.
recs.rel: Taxila was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

recs.q: Hawaii is a state of the USA. What is its capital?
recs.facts: The capital of Hawaii is Honolulu, on the island of Oahu.
recs.rel: Hawaii became the 50th US state in 1959.

recs.q: In which year did the first All Pakistan Educational Conference take place in Karachi?
recs.facts: The conference was held in Karachi from 27 November to 1 December 1947, just after independence. It was opened by Quaid-e-Azam's message on education policy.
recs.rel: Its date is the 27th of November 1947 as the start of the conference.

recs.q: Mahatma Gandhi was the leader of which political party?
recs.facts: Gandhi led the Indian National Congress in the freedom movement against British rule. He led campaigns such as Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah led the All India Muslim League.

recs.q: What is the average life span of a red blood cell in the human body?
recs.facts: Red blood cells live for about 120 days and are then broken down in the spleen and liver.
recs.rel: Red blood cells are made in the bone marrow.

recs.q: Approximately how many litres of blood does an average adult human body contain?
recs.facts: An average adult has roughly 4.5 to 5.5 litres of blood, usually given as about 5 litres. This is around 7 percent of body weight.
recs.rel: Women usually have slightly less blood volume than men.

recs.q: The famous Leaning Tower of Pisa is located in which country?
recs.facts: The Leaning Tower stands in the city of Pisa in Tuscany, Italy.
recs.rel: It is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral and its construction started in 1173.

recs.q: Which British commander defeated Tipu Sultan in the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92)?
recs.facts: Lord Cornwallis led the British forces and Tipu had to sign the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792.
recs.rel: Tipu Sultan was finally killed in 1799 in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, when Lord Wellesley was Governor-General.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, which day will the 17th be?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 17th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 17th is also a Monday.
recs.rel: A gap that is a multiple of 7 days gives the same weekday.

recs.q: The 24th of January is celebrated as the day of what?
recs.facts: The UN General Assembly declared 24 January the International Day of Education in 2018.
recs.rel: The day highlights the role of education in peace and development.

recs.q: A helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to cover 320 km. How many gallons does it need to cover 700 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallons. For 700 km: 0.15625 x 700 = 109.375, about 109.4 gallons.
recs.rel: Fuel used is directly proportional to the distance covered.

recs.q: What part of speech is the word 'against' in the sentence 'He leaned against the wall'?
recs.facts: 'Against' shows the relation between 'leaned' and 'the wall', so it is a preposition.
recs.rel: A preposition is normally followed by a noun or pronoun.

recs.q: What part of speech is the word 'eat' in the sentence 'Children eat fruit'?
recs.facts: 'Eat' names an action, so it is a verb.
recs.rel: A verb expresses an action, a state or an occurrence.

recs.q: Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi is a famous Pakistani player of which sport?
recs.facts: Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi is Pakistan's best-known tennis player, famous for doubles.
recs.rel: He reached the US Open men's doubles final in 2010 with Rohan Bopanna.

recs.q: How did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah respond to the Nehru Report of 1928?
opts: He rejected it and later presented his Fourteen Points
He asked the British to enforce it
He ignored it and left politics
recs.facts: The Nehru Report did not protect Muslim rights such as separate electorates, so Jinnah rejected it. In 1929 he gave his Fourteen Points as the Muslim demands.
recs.rel: Jinnah's earlier Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 had been turned down by the Congress.

recs.q: What is the logarithm of unity (1) to any base?
recs.facts: Any base raised to the power 0 gives 1, so log of 1 to any base is 0.
recs.rel: The logarithm of a negative number is not defined in real numbers.

recs.q: Peshawar is associated with which ancient civilisation?
recs.facts: Peshawar, once called Purushapura, was a capital of the Gandhara civilisation in Kushan times. Gandhara art blended Greek and Buddhist styles.
recs.rel: Taxila was another important Gandhara city.

recs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
opts: The Principal has accepted my application.
The Principal have accepted my application.
The Principal has accept my application.
recs.facts: Principal is singular, so it takes has, and the present perfect needs the past participle accepted.
recs.rel: Principal means head of a school, while principle means a rule.

recs.q: What is the date of birth of Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar?
recs.facts: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar was born on 10 December 1878 in Rampur, India.
recs.rel: He edited the newspapers Comrade and Hamdard and was a leader of the Khilafat Movement.

recs.q: Which disease is caused by the bite of an infected dog?
recs.facts: Rabies is a viral disease passed to humans through the saliva of an infected animal, usually a dog.
recs.rel: Rabies can be prevented by vaccination given soon after a bite.

recs.q: On which date is World Hepatitis Day observed every year?
recs.facts: World Hepatitis Day is observed on 28 July, the birthday of Dr Baruch Blumberg who discovered the hepatitis B virus.
recs.rel: World Health Day is on 7 April and World AIDS Day is on 1 December.

recs.q: Under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan, the office of Governor General was replaced by which office?
recs.facts: The Constitution of 1956 made Pakistan a republic, so the post of Governor General was replaced by the President.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza, the last Governor General, became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: She sits ___ the tree.
recs.facts: The preposition under shows she is below the tree, which gives a meaningful sentence.
recs.rel: Under is a preposition of place, like above, beside and near.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: 1Z, 3X, 5V, ?
recs.facts: Numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7) and letters go back by 2 (Z, X, V, T). So the next term is 7T.
recs.rel: Z is the 26th letter and T is the 20th.

recs.q: Complete the series: 3/2, 6/4, 10/8, 15/16, ?
recs.facts: Numerators increase by 3, 4, 5, 6 (3, 6, 10, 15, 21). Denominators double (2, 4, 8, 16, 32). So the next term is 21/32.
recs.rel: The numerators are triangular numbers.

recs.q: What is the total number of members of the UN Security Council?
recs.facts: There are 5 permanent members and 10 non-permanent members, so 5 + 10 = 15.
recs.rel: Non-permanent members are elected for two years.

recs.q: Choose the correct verb: My mother ___ at the hospital.
recs.facts: The subject my mother is third person singular, so the simple present verb takes -s: works.
recs.rel: In simple present tense, he, she and it take a verb ending in -s or -es.

recs.q: What is iota (i) in mathematics called, and what is its value?
opts: The imaginary unit, equal to the square root of -1
recs.facts: Iota i is the imaginary unit defined by i squared = -1, so i is the square root of -1.
recs.rel: Powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: The pilot landed the aeroplane safely.
opts: The aeroplane was landed safely by the pilot.
The aeroplane is landed safely by the pilot.
The aeroplane has been landed safely by the pilot.
The pilot was landed safely by the aeroplane.
recs.facts: The sentence is in simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: the object becomes the subject.
recs.rel: Passive voice is formed as: object + form of be + past participle + by + subject.

recs.q: How many centimetres are there in one inch?
recs.facts: By international definition, one inch is exactly 2.54 centimetres.
recs.rel: One foot is 12 inches, which is about 30.48 centimetres.

recs.q: PEMRA is the regulatory authority for which type of media in Pakistan?
recs.facts: PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority. It regulates and licenses television and radio channels.
recs.rel: PEMRA was established in 2002.

recs.q: If one person writes one page in one minute, how many pages will 5 persons write in 5 minutes?
recs.facts: One person writes 1 page per minute. 5 persons write 5 pages per minute, so in 5 minutes they write 25 pages.
recs.rel: Rate times people times time gives the total work.

recs.q: According to the 2023 digital census, what is the population of Pakistan (approximately)?
recs.facts: The 2023 census, approved by the CCI, recorded 241.49 million people.
recs.rel: The 2017 census had recorded 207.7 million.

recs.q: What is the value of 1 raised to any power n?
recs.facts: 1 multiplied by itself any number of times is always 1.
recs.rel: Any non-zero number raised to power zero is also 1.

recs.q: If the diameter of a circle is 35, what is its radius?
recs.facts: Radius is half of the diameter, so 35 divided by 2 = 17.5.
recs.rel: The diameter is twice the radius and the longest chord of a circle.

recs.q: When did the United Nations General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
recs.facts: The General Assembly adopted the Declaration in Paris on 10 December 1948.
recs.rel: 10 December is celebrated every year as Human Rights Day.

recs.q: What is the common short form (abbreviation) of Saudi Arabia?
recs.facts: Saudi Arabia is officially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, so its short form is KSA.
recs.rel: SAR is the code for the Saudi riyal, the currency of Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: What is the value of cosec x multiplied by sin x?
recs.facts: Cosec x is 1 divided by sin x, so cosec x times sin x equals 1 over sin x times sin x, which is 1.
recs.rel: Similarly sec x times cos x is 1 and cot x times tan x is 1.

recs.q: Which place in Pakistan is famous for making small arms (weapons) in home industry?
recs.facts: Darra Adam Khel, south of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is well known for its local small arms workshops.
recs.rel: Sialkot is instead famous for sports goods and surgical instruments.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'affection'?
recs.facts: 'Affection' means almost the same as 'fondness'.
recs.rel: Its opposite is 'dislike' or 'hatred'.

recs.q: The Victoria Cross is the highest military award of which country?
recs.facts: The Victoria Cross is the highest British award for bravery in the face of the enemy. It was created by Queen Victoria in 1856.
recs.rel: The highest American military award is the Medal of Honor.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word wild?
opts: Untamed or living in a natural state
recs.facts: Wild describes animals or plants living in their natural state, not tamed or cultivated.
recs.rel: The opposite of wild is tame or domestic.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Kitab ul Umm?
recs.facts: Kitab ul Umm is a major work of fiqh written by Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi'i.
recs.rel: Imam Malik wrote Al-Muwatta and Imam Ahmad compiled the Musnad.

recs.q: What is 60 percent of 100?
recs.rel: Percent means per hundred, so any percent of 100 equals the same number.

recs.q: The population of a town in the year 2000 is 1600 and it doubles every 5 years. What was the population in 1980?
recs.facts: From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings. So the 1980 population = 1600 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 100.
recs.rel: Going back in time with doubling means halving at each step.

recs.q: If the 14th day of a month is Monday, which day will the 24th be?
recs.facts: From the 14th to the 24th is 10 days. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days ahead of Monday: Thursday.
recs.rel: Divide the gap by 7 and move forward by the remainder.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, which day will the 24th be?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days. 20 = 14 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Sunday: Saturday.
recs.rel: Moving 6 days ahead is the same as moving 1 day back.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, which day will the 28th be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 28th is 26 days. 26 = 21 + 5, so move 5 days ahead of Monday: Saturday.
recs.rel: Weekdays repeat every 7 days.

recs.q: If the 16th day of a month is Sunday, which day is the 5th of the same month?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 16th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the 5th is 4 days before Sunday: Saturday, Friday, Thursday, Wednesday. So it is Wednesday.
recs.rel: For earlier dates, move backwards by the remainder of the gap divided by 7.

recs.q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, which day is the 23rd?
recs.facts: From the 5th to the 23rd is 18 days. 18 = 14 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. So it is Tuesday.
recs.rel: Two full weeks bring the same weekday back.

recs.q: Akbar and Khalid were born in 1970 and 1975 respectively, and Ikram is older than Khalid. Who is the youngest of the three?
recs.facts: Khalid (1975) is younger than Akbar (1970), and Ikram is older than Khalid. So Khalid is younger than both and is the youngest.
recs.rel: In age puzzles, a later birth year means a younger person.

recs.q: A bus carries 500 passengers, of which 350 are men and the rest are women. What percentage of the passengers are women?
recs.rel: Men are 70% and women 30%, so the two add up to 100%.

recs.q: Out of 1200 students, 800 boys are present. What percentage of the students are present?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 800/1200 x 100 = 2/3 x 100 = 66.67%.
recs.rel: 2/3 as a percentage is about 66.67%.

recs.q: In which year CE did Abu Jahal die?
recs.facts: Abu Jahal was killed in the Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, which is March 624 CE.
recs.rel: Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

recs.q: In which year was the national flag of Pakistan adopted?
recs.facts: The Constituent Assembly adopted the flag on 11 August 1947, a few days before independence.
recs.rel: The flag was designed on the basis of the Muslim League flag, with a white stripe for minorities.

recs.q: An adverb is a word that mainly modifies a what?
recs.facts: An adverb mainly modifies a verb. It can also modify an adjective or another adverb.
recs.rel: Adjectives, in contrast, modify nouns and pronouns.

recs.q: Which name of Allah means the Most Merciful?
recs.facts: Ar-Rahim means the Most Merciful (the Ever-Merciful).
recs.rel: Ar-Rahman is usually translated as the Most Gracious or the Beneficent.

recs.q: Ahmed is 5 years old and Sara is three times his age. How old will Sara be when Ahmed is 11?
recs.facts: Sara is 3 x 5 = 15 now. Ahmed becomes 11 after 6 years, so Sara will be 15 + 6 = 21.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: Akbar is 3 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 8?
recs.facts: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 now. Akbar becomes 8 after 5 years, so she will be 9 + 5 = 14.
recs.rel: Both people age by the same number of years.

recs.q: Why did the United States enter World War II in December 1941?
opts: Japan attacked its naval base at Pearl Harbor
recs.facts: Japan carried out a surprise air attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.
recs.rel: Germany and Italy then declared war on the United States a few days later.

recs.q: What is the spread of cultural traits from one society to another called?
recs.facts: Cultural diffusion is the transfer of ideas, customs and technology from one society to another. Cultural diversity only means many cultures exist together.
recs.rel: Cultural lag means material culture changes faster than beliefs and values.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'delight'?
recs.facts: Delight means great pleasure, so its opposite is sorrow or misery. The other options are synonyms.
recs.rel: Another opposite of delight is displeasure.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'fragile'?
recs.facts: Fragile means easily broken, so the opposite is sturdy or strong. Delicate, brittle and weak are close in meaning to fragile.
recs.rel: The word fragile comes from the Latin fragilis, meaning easily broken.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'secret'?
recs.facts: Secret means kept hidden from others, so the opposite is public or open. The other options are synonyms.
recs.rel: Overt is another opposite of secret in formal English.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'terrifying'?
recs.facts: Terrifying means causing great fear, so the opposite is comforting or soothing. The others are synonyms.
recs.rel: Reassuring is another good opposite of terrifying.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'condensed'?
recs.facts: Condensed means made shorter or more compact, so the opposite is expanded. The other options mean the same as condensed.
recs.rel: In science, condensation is the change of a gas into a liquid.

recs.q: What is the antonym of 'idleness'?
recs.facts: Idleness means doing no work, so the opposite is industry, meaning hard work. Laziness and sloth are synonyms.
recs.rel: The proverb says an idle mind is the devil's workshop.

recs.q: The Arabian Sea is a part of which ocean?
recs.facts: The Arabian Sea is the north-western part of the Indian Ocean. It lies between India, Pakistan, Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.
recs.rel: Pakistan's coastline along the Arabian Sea is about 1000 kilometres long.

recs.q: The separation of Bangladesh in 1971 benefited which neighbouring country the most?
recs.facts: India supported the separation and fought the 1971 war, which weakened its rival Pakistan. India therefore gained strategically.
recs.rel: The 1971 war ended with the surrender of about 90000 Pakistani personnel.

recs.q: What does ADB stand for?
recs.facts: ADB is the Asian Development Bank, which lends money to Asian countries for development. Pakistan is one of its members.
recs.rel: The ADB headquarters is in Manila, Philippines.

recs.q: What is the logarithm of a number to its own base?
recs.facts: By definition, log base a of a equals 1 because a raised to the power 1 is a. For example, log 10 to base 10 is 1.
recs.rel: The logarithm of 1 to any base is 0.

recs.q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, who is the head of government?
opts: The Speaker of the National Assembly
recs.facts: Pakistan has a parliamentary system. The Prime Minister heads the government and the President is the head of state.
recs.rel: The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.

recs.q: On which date of Ramadan was the Battle of Badr fought?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH, which is March 624 CE.
recs.rel: It is also called Youm-e-Furqan.

recs.q: How many population censuses had Pakistan held up to the 2023 census, including it?
recs.facts: Censuses were held in 1951, 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998, 2017 and 2023, which makes seven.
recs.rel: The 2023 census was the first fully digital census of Pakistan.

recs.q: Salman said that Ali ___ ill. Which option correctly completes this reported speech sentence?
recs.facts: In reported speech, a past reporting verb (said) changes the present tense of the original statement to the past tense, so is becomes was.
recs.rel: Direct speech: Salman said, "Ali is ill"; reported speech: Salman said that Ali was ill.

recs.q: Which event led the United States to enter World War 2 in December 1941?
opts: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
recs.facts: On 7 December 1941 Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, and the US declared war on Japan the next day.
recs.rel: The war in Europe had already begun in September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.

recs.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: I hate being laughed ___.
recs.facts: The phrasal verb is laugh at, so the passive form is being laughed at.
recs.rel: Similar verb and preposition pairs are look at, listen to and depend on.

recs.q: When was Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, who coined the name Pakistan, born?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali was born on 16 November 1897 in Balachaur, in East Punjab.
recs.rel: He published the pamphlet Now or Never in 1933 in which the name Pakistan was proposed.

recs.q: In linear programming, what is a point of the solution region where two of its boundary lines intersect called?
recs.facts: A vertex of the feasible region, where two boundary lines meet, is called a corner point.
recs.rel: The maximum or minimum of the objective function always occurs at a corner point of the feasible region.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: Go there ___ bus.
recs.facts: We use by with a means of transport when no article is used, as in by bus, by train, by car.
recs.rel: With an article we say on the bus or in the car.

recs.q: What is the capital of Gambia?
recs.facts: Banjul is the capital of Gambia, a small West African country.
recs.rel: Gambia is surrounded on land by Senegal.

recs.q: What is the capital of Switzerland?
recs.facts: Bern is the federal city and seat of the Swiss government, although many people wrongly think Geneva or Zurich is the capital.
recs.rel: Geneva hosts many international organisations such as the UN European office.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: That was ___ I was born.
recs.facts: The year is correct because the sentence refers to one specific year, so the definite article is needed.
recs.rel: The article an is used only before a vowel sound, so an year is always wrong.

recs.q: On which date did Makkah fall to the Muslims in the Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah)?
recs.facts: Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 AD) for the conquest. The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah peacefully.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly, some give 10 or 17 Ramadan 8 AH.

recs.q: On which date did Pakistan come into being according to the Islamic calendar?
recs.facts: Pakistan was created on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, a Friday. It was also the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) in many accounts.
recs.rel: The date 27 Rajab is Shab-e-Miraj, not Pakistan's birth.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
recs.facts: Each number is double the previous one: 3x2=6, 6x2=12, 12x2=24, so 24x2=48.
recs.rel: This is a geometric series with common ratio 2.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 80, 70, 62, 56, ?
recs.facts: The differences are -10, -8, -6, so the next difference is -4. Thus 56 - 4 = 52.
recs.rel: The differences themselves form an arithmetic series.

recs.q: A helicopter covers 240 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons are needed for the next 400 km?
recs.facts: Fuel per km is 50/240 gallons. For 400 km: 400 x 50 / 240 = 83 1/3 gallons.
recs.rel: This is a direct proportion question.

recs.q: Who is the Supreme Commander of all the armed forces of Pakistan?
opts: The Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
recs.facts: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. The Prime Minister runs the government.
recs.rel: The President appoints the service chiefs on the advice of the Prime Minister.

recs.q: In which continent is the Sahara Desert located?
recs.facts: The Sahara lies across North Africa. It is the largest hot desert in the world.
recs.rel: It covers an area of about 9 million square kilometres.

recs.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning a person who does something for pleasure and not as a job?
recs.facts: The correct spelling is amateur. It comes from the French word for lover.
recs.rel: The opposite word is professional.

recs.q: In which part of Pakistan is K2 located?
recs.facts: K2 is in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan, on the border with China. It is 8611 metres high.
recs.rel: K2 is the second highest peak in the world.

recs.q: What is the currency of North Korea?
recs.facts: North Korea uses the North Korean won. South Korea uses the South Korean won.
recs.rel: Its capital is Pyongyang.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: I take exercise daily.
opts: Exercise is taken by me daily.
Exercise was taken by me daily.
Exercise is being taken by me daily.
Exercise has been taken by me daily.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple present, so the passive uses is or are plus the past participle. So it becomes Exercise is taken by me daily.
recs.rel: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive.

recs.q: The Darling is a famous what, located in Australia?
recs.facts: The Darling is a river in Australia that joins the Murray River. It is about 1,500 km long.
recs.rel: The Murray-Darling basin is Australia's main river system.

recs.q: A is the father of B, but B is not a daughter. What is B to A?
recs.facts: B is a child of A and is not a daughter, so B is a son.
recs.rel: The relation of A to B is father.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Daughter of Destiny?
recs.facts: Daughter of Destiny is the autobiography of Benazir Bhutto, published in 1989. It was later reissued as Daughter of the East.
recs.rel: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan.

recs.q: Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration signed in 1966?
recs.facts: It ended the 1965 war between India and Pakistan. The Soviet Union mediated it.
recs.rel: It was signed in January 1966.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of a province of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Maryam Nawaz became Chief Minister of Punjab in February 2024, the first woman to hold the post in any province. She belongs to PML-N.
recs.rel: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman Prime Minister.

recs.q: Which is the largest river of China?
recs.facts: The Yangtze is about 6,300 km long and is the longest river in China and Asia. The Yellow River is second.
recs.rel: It flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai.

recs.q: Lyallpur is the old name of which Pakistani city?
recs.facts: Lyallpur was renamed Faisalabad in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia. It was named after Sir James Lyall.
recs.rel: Faisalabad is famous for textiles.

recs.q: The city of Savannah is located in which country?
recs.facts: Savannah is a historic port city in Georgia, United States. It lies on the Savannah River.
recs.rel: A savannah is also a type of grassland.

recs.q: What is the term for a line that meets another line at an angle of 90 degrees?
recs.facts: Two lines that meet at a right angle (90 degrees) are called perpendicular lines. Parallel lines never meet.
recs.rel: Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is minus 1.

recs.q: In a geometric progression, the constant ratio between consecutive terms is denoted by which letter?
recs.facts: In a geometric progression each term is the previous term multiplied by a fixed number called the common ratio, written r. The nth term is a times r to the power n minus 1.
recs.rel: In an arithmetic progression the common difference is denoted by d.

recs.q: What is the derivative of cos(2x) with respect to x?
recs.facts: By the chain rule, the derivative of cos(u) is -sin(u) times du/dx. With u = 2x, du/dx = 2, so the answer is -2 sin(2x).
recs.rel: The derivative of sin(2x) is 2 cos(2x).

recs.q: A decimal number that ends after a finite number of digits (for example 0.25) is called what?
recs.facts: A decimal with a finite number of digits after the point is a terminating decimal. It can always be written as a fraction.
recs.rel: A recurring decimal such as 0.333... has digits that repeat forever.

recs.q: Change into direct speech: He told me that he was playing a game.
opts: He said to me, "I was playing a game."
He said to me, "He is playing a game."
He said to me, "I am playing a game."
He said to me, "I will play a game."
recs.facts: In direct speech the reported past continuous tense changes back to the present continuous, and 'he' becomes 'I'. So the sentence is: He said to me, "I am playing a game."
recs.rel: When changing indirect to direct speech, 'told' usually becomes 'said to'.

recs.q: Change into direct speech: She said to me that she was watching TV.
opts: She said to me, "I am watching TV."
She said to me, "She was watching TV."
She said to me, "I will watch TV."
She said to me, "I have watched TV."
recs.facts: The past continuous 'was watching' goes back to the present continuous 'am watching', and 'she' becomes 'I'.
recs.rel: Direct speech is always written inside quotation marks.

recs.q: Rearrange the jumbled letters 'EBAUYT' to make a meaningful English word.
recs.facts: The six letters E, B, A, U, Y, T can be arranged to spell BEAUTY.
recs.rel: Beauty is a noun meaning the quality of being pleasing to the eye or mind.

recs.q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train moves twice as fast as the car. How much time will the train take to cover 30 km?
recs.facts: Speed of train = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. Time = 30 / 120 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.
recs.rel: Time equals distance divided by speed.

recs.q: Which gas is mostly named as the main greenhouse gas causing global warming in textbooks?
recs.facts: Carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels is the main greenhouse gas added by human activity. It traps heat in the atmosphere.
recs.rel: Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas, but its amount is controlled by temperature, so sources can differ on which is primary.
