recs.q: There are 24 students in a class and the number of boys is double the number of girls. How many girls are there?
recs.facts: Let girls = x, then boys = 2x, so 3x = 24 and x = 8. There are 8 girls and 16 boys.
recs.rel: Ratio boys to girls here is 2:1, so girls are one third of the class.

recs.q: The total number of students is 1500 and 340 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
recs.rel: Boys are 340/1500 x 100 = 22.67%, and the two percentages add up to 100.

recs.q: If the 7th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st day of that month be?
recs.facts: From the 7th to the 21st is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. After whole weeks the day stays the same, so it is Friday.
recs.rel: Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: Perpendicular divided by hypotenuse gives which trigonometric ratio?
recs.facts: In a right-angled triangle, sin of an angle = perpendicular / hypotenuse. Cos = base / hypotenuse and tan = perpendicular / base.
recs.rel: A memory aid is SOH CAH TOA: Sin = Opposite/Hypotenuse, Cos = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Tan = Opposite/Adjacent.

recs.q: Which is greater: -15 or -20?
recs.facts: On the number line, a number further to the right is greater. -15 lies to the right of -20, so -15 is greater.
recs.rel: Among negative numbers, the one closer to zero is the greater number.

recs.q: Arrange the letters AGRMYNE to form the name of a country.
recs.facts: The letters A, G, R, M, Y, N, E can be rearranged to spell GERMANY, a country in Europe.
recs.rel: The capital of Germany is Berlin.

recs.q: Who started the FIFA World Cup, as the FIFA president who proposed the tournament?
recs.facts: Jules Rimet, a Frenchman and FIFA president from 1921 to 1954, drove the idea of the World Cup. The first tournament was held in Uruguay in 1930.
recs.rel: The original World Cup trophy was named the Jules Rimet Trophy.

recs.q: According to grammar, what part of speech is the word 'hey'?
recs.facts: 'Hey' is a word used to express sudden feeling or to get attention, so it is an interjection.
recs.rel: Other interjections are 'oh', 'wow', 'alas' and 'hurrah'.

recs.q: A car runs at half the speed of a train that travels at 60 km/h. How far will the car go in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Car speed = 60 / 2 = 30 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 30 x 1/2 = 15 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time, so time must be in hours when speed is in km/h.

recs.q: What is half of 1/90?
recs.rel: Taking half of a fraction doubles its denominator.

recs.q: The Hazara people of Afghanistan and Pakistan are commonly said to be descended from whom?
recs.facts: The most common view is that the Hazara descend from Mongol (and Turkic) troops of Genghis Khan who settled in central Afghanistan in the 13th century.
recs.rel: Sources differ on exact origins, and the Hazara speak Hazaragi, a dialect of Persian.

recs.q: What is Hilal-e-Imtiaz?
opts: The second highest civil award of Pakistan
The highest military gallantry award of Pakistan
The highest civil award of Pakistan
recs.facts: Hilal-e-Imtiaz is the second highest civil award of Pakistan, given for excellence in fields such as arts, sports, science and public service.
recs.rel: The highest civil award of Pakistan is Nishan-e-Pakistan.

recs.q: Which city is considered the hottest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: Dera Ismail Khan in the southern plains of KPK regularly records the highest summer temperatures in the province, around 45 to 50 degrees Celsius.
recs.rel: The hottest city of Pakistan overall is usually given as Jacobabad in Sindh.

recs.q: What is 24 minutes past 10 pm in 24-hour format?
recs.facts: 10 pm = 22:00 in 24-hour time. Adding 24 minutes gives 22:24, written 2224.
recs.rel: To convert pm time to 24-hour format, add 12 to the hour (except 12 pm).

recs.q: Who was Habba Khatoon?
opts: A Kashmiri poetess known as the Nightingale of Kashmir
A queen of the Mughal Empire
recs.facts: Habba Khatoon was a 16th century Kashmiri poetess and the wife of Sultan Yusuf Shah Chak. She is known for her songs of love and longing.
recs.rel: She is called the Nightingale of Kashmir.

recs.q: What is the date of Independence Day of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947 as a result of the Indian Independence Act 1947.
recs.rel: India celebrates its Independence Day on 15 August.

recs.q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word justice?
recs.facts: Justice means fair treatment, so its opposite is injustice, which means unfair treatment.
recs.rel: The prefix in- is often added to a word to make its opposite.

recs.q: On which date did the 1999 Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India end?
recs.facts: The fighting in the Kargil sector began in early May 1999 and ended on 26 July 1999 when the last operations were over.
recs.rel: 26 July is observed in India as Kargil Vijay Diwas.

recs.q: Mount Godwin-Austen is another name of which mountain?
recs.facts: K2 was named Mount Godwin-Austen after the British surveyor Henry Haversham Godwin-Austen who explored the area.
recs.rel: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world at about 8611 metres.

recs.q: Which country is called the Land of the Midnight Sun?
recs.facts: In summer, parts of northern Norway have daylight all night, so it is called the Land of the Midnight Sun.
recs.rel: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun.

recs.q: Which country has the largest number of islands in the world?
recs.facts: Sweden has about 267,000 islands, the most of any country, though most are very small.
recs.rel: Indonesia has the most islands among large island nations, about 17,000.

recs.q: Which is the largest city of Japan?
recs.facts: Tokyo is the capital and the most populous city of Japan.
recs.rel: Osaka and Yokohama are other large Japanese cities.

recs.q: According to the Economic Survey of Pakistan 2025-26, what is Pakistan's literacy rate (population aged 10 and above)?
recs.facts: The Economic Survey 2025-26, released in June 2026, gave the literacy rate as 63 percent, up from about 61 percent the year before.
recs.rel: Older reports gave around 60 percent in 2023 and 53 percent in earlier years; Punjab has the highest provincial rate.

recs.q: The Margalla Hills of Islamabad are an extension of which mountain range?
recs.facts: The Margalla Hills are the foothills at the western end of the Himalayas.
recs.rel: Margalla Hills National Park lies in the north of Islamabad.

recs.q: What is a matrix called in which all the entries are zero?
recs.facts: A matrix whose every entry is zero is called a zero matrix or null matrix. It is the additive identity for matrices of the same order.
recs.rel: Adding a zero matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.

recs.q: In statistics, what is the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value of a data set called?
recs.facts: Range is the largest value minus the smallest value in the data. For example, in 3, 7, 12 the range is 12 - 3 = 9.
recs.rel: Range is the simplest measure of how spread out data is.

recs.q: What does the idiom 'call it a day' mean?
recs.facts: To call it a day means to stop what you are doing and finish for the time being. It is used when one has done enough work.
recs.rel: A similar idiom is 'call it a night'.

recs.q: What is an interjection in English grammar?
opts: A word that expresses sudden emotion, such as Wow or Alas
A word that names a person or place
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
recs.facts: An interjection is a word or short phrase that shows sudden feeling like surprise, joy or pain. Examples are Oh, Hurrah and Alas.
recs.rel: An interjection is usually followed by an exclamation mark.

recs.q: If the 12th day of a month is Monday, which day is the 25th of that month?
recs.facts: From the 12th to the 25th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, so Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.
recs.rel: Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, which day is the 15th of that month?
recs.facts: From the 3rd to the 15th is 12 days. 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5, so Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
recs.rel: The 10th and 17th of that month are also Mondays.

recs.q: Who built the Mohabbat Khan Mosque in Peshawar?
opts: Nawab Mohabbat Khan, Mughal governor of Peshawar
recs.facts: The mosque was built around 1630 by Nawab Mohabbat Khan, the Mughal governor of Peshawar under Emperor Shah Jahan.
recs.rel: It is one of the best known Mughal-era mosques of Peshawar.

recs.q: On which date was the Quit India resolution passed by the Indian National Congress in 1942?
recs.facts: The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942 and the movement began the next day. It demanded an end to British rule in India.
recs.rel: Gandhi gave the call Do or Die during this movement.

recs.q: What is 6 multiplied by 5?
recs.facts: 6 x 5 means five sixes: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30.
recs.rel: The multiplication table of 6 is 6, 12, 18, 24, 30.

recs.q: Which countries are the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council?
opts: USA, UK, France, Russia and China
USA, UK, France, Germany and Japan
USA, UK, Russia, India and China
USA, France, Germany, Russia and China
recs.facts: The five permanent members (P5) are the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia and China. Each has the power of veto.
recs.rel: Pakistan has been elected a non-permanent member of the Security Council several times, most recently for 2025-2026.

recs.q: Which country has won the most Olympic medals of all time?
recs.facts: The United States has the highest total of medals in the history of the Summer Olympic Games, well ahead of any other country.
recs.rel: Some tables count the former Soviet Union separately, but it still stays behind the United States.

recs.q: What was the capital of the Ottoman Empire after 1453?
recs.facts: Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 and made it the Ottoman capital. It remained the capital until the empire ended in 1922.
recs.rel: Ankara became the capital of the Republic of Turkey in 1923.

recs.q: Who coined the name Pakistan?
recs.facts: Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in his pamphlet Now or Never.
recs.rel: Allama Iqbal had given the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

recs.q: What is negative two divided by negative two?
recs.facts: A negative number divided by a negative number gives a positive result. So (-2) divided by (-2) = 1.
recs.rel: Any non-zero number divided by itself is equal to 1.

recs.q: What is the scattering (spread) of a set of numbers called in statistics?
recs.facts: Dispersion means how much the values are spread out. Range, variance and standard deviation are measures of dispersion.
recs.rel: Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency.

recs.q: A function in which different elements of the domain have different images in the range is called what?
recs.facts: In a one-one function, no two different inputs give the same output. Such a function is also called injective.
recs.rel: A function that is both one-one and onto is called bijective.

recs.q: Hens and cows together have 48 heads and 140 legs. How many hens are there?
recs.facts: Let hens be h and cows c. h + c = 48 and 2h + 4c = 140, so h + 2c = 70. Subtracting gives c = 22, so h = 48 - 22 = 26.
recs.rel: Check: 26 hens have 52 legs and 22 cows have 88 legs, which total 140.

recs.q: In which mountain range is Broad Peak located?
recs.facts: Broad Peak (8,051 m) lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border, near K2.
recs.rel: Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: If 40 percent of a number is 56, what is the number?
recs.facts: 40 percent of x = 56, so x = 56 times 100 divided by 40 = 140.
recs.rel: Check: 40 percent of 140 is 56.

recs.q: A period of ten years is also known as what?
recs.facts: A decade means ten years.
recs.rel: A century is 100 years and a millennium is 1000 years.

recs.q: How many Pakistanis have won the Nobel Prize in Physics?
recs.facts: Only Dr Abdus Salam won it, in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg.
recs.rel: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.

recs.q: From which substance do plants obtain hydrogen for making food?
recs.facts: In photosynthesis, water splits and gives hydrogen, which is used with carbon dioxide to make glucose.
recs.rel: Plants take in water through their roots.

recs.q: Between which two teams was the first Test cricket match played?
recs.facts: The first Test was played at Melbourne in 1877 between Australia and England.
recs.rel: Australia won that match by 45 runs.

recs.q: What is the lowest point of Pakistan?
opts: Sea level at the Arabian Sea coast
recs.facts: The lowest point is the coast of the Arabian Sea at 0 m.
recs.rel: The highest point of Pakistan is K2.

recs.q: What is the probability of getting a tail when a fair coin is tossed once?
recs.facts: There are 2 equally likely outcomes and one is a tail, so probability is 1/2.
recs.rel: The probability of a sure event is 1.

recs.q: Which Prophet (AS) was swallowed by a whale (big fish)?
recs.facts: The Quran tells that Hazrat Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a big fish and he prayed to Allah for forgiveness.
recs.rel: He is also called Dhun-Nun, the one of the fish.

recs.q: Which authority provides water supply and sewerage services in big cities such as Lahore?
recs.facts: WASA is the Water and Sanitation Agency of the city development authorities.
recs.rel: WAPDA looks after water and power development at national level.

recs.q: A book is bought for 40 rupees and sold for 40 rupees. What is the profit?
recs.facts: Profit = selling price minus cost price = 40 - 40 = 0.
recs.rel: When selling price equals cost price there is no profit and no loss.

recs.q: In which year did Queen Victoria die?
recs.facts: Queen Victoria died on 22 January 1901.
recs.rel: She became Empress of India in 1876.

recs.q: Which pass connects Quetta with Sibi?
recs.facts: The Bolan Pass lies in Balochistan between Quetta and Sibi.
recs.rel: Khojak Pass connects Quetta with Kandahar in Afghanistan.

recs.q: Who was the first woman pilot of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Shukriya Khanum earned a commercial pilot licence in 1959 and was the first Pakistani woman pilot.
recs.rel: Ayesha Farooq became the first woman fighter pilot of the PAF in 2013.

recs.q: The Hunza River is located in which region of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Hunza River flows through the Hunza valley in Gilgit-Baltistan and joins the Gilgit River.
recs.rel: The Karakoram Highway runs along the Hunza valley up to the Khunjerab Pass.

recs.q: Who presides over the sessions of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Speaker is the presiding officer who runs the business and sessions of the National Assembly.
recs.rel: In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: Mary said that she was sorry.
opts: It was said by Mary that she was sorry.
Mary was said that she was sorry.
That she was sorry has said Mary.
recs.facts: For reported speech, the passive form starts with It was said by, followed by the that clause unchanged.
recs.rel: The reporting verb said changes to was said in the passive.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the name Muhammad (SAW)?
recs.facts: Muhammad comes from the Arabic root h-m-d and means the one who is praised again and again.
recs.rel: Ahmad, another name of the Holy Prophet (SAW), also comes from the same root.

recs.q: On which date did Pakistan become a full member of the SCO?
recs.facts: Pakistan, along with India, became a full member at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.
recs.rel: Pakistan had been an observer since 2005.

recs.q: How many full member countries does the SCO have after Belarus joined in 2024?
recs.facts: The members are China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus, which makes ten.
recs.rel: Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in July 2024.

recs.q: Who scored the first Test double century for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Wicketkeeper Imtiaz Ahmed scored 209 against New Zealand at Lahore in October 1955.
recs.rel: Hanif Mohammad later made 337 against West Indies in 1958.

recs.q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats in the National Assembly are reserved in total (women and non-Muslims)?
recs.facts: 60 seats are reserved for women and 10 for non-Muslim minorities, so 60 plus 10 = 70.
recs.rel: Reserved seats are filled through proportional representation of the parties.

recs.q: Which legislative assembly in Pakistan has the highest number of seats?
recs.facts: The Punjab Provincial Assembly has 371 seats, more than the National Assembly (336) and all other assemblies.
recs.rel: The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats.

recs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five senses of a human being?
recs.facts: The five traditional senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. Balance is not counted in them.
recs.rel: Balance is sensed by the inner ear.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: X1, YY3, ZZZ5, ?
recs.facts: The letters go X, Y, Z, A in order and each letter is repeated one more time (1, 2, 3, 4 times). The numbers go up by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next term is AAAA7.
recs.rel: After Z the alphabet starts again from A in such series.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: Z1, X3, U6, Q10, L15, ?
recs.facts: Letters move back by 2, 3, 4, 5 and then 6 places: Z, X, U, Q, L, F. Numbers go up by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, so the next term is F21.
recs.rel: The numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 are called triangular numbers.

recs.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
recs.facts: The word pentagon comes from the Greek penta meaning five, so it has five sides.
recs.rel: The sum of the interior angles of a pentagon is 540 degrees.

recs.q: Ali is 6 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old is the sister?
recs.facts: Sister's age = 2 x 6 = 12 years.
recs.rel: The age difference between them is 6 years and it never changes.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'embellish'?
recs.facts: 'Embellish' means almost the same as 'adorn'.
recs.rel: Its opposite is a word such as 'disfigure'.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'specify'?
recs.facts: 'Specify' means almost the same as 'state clearly'.
recs.rel: The noun form is 'specification'.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'weird'?
recs.facts: 'Weird' means almost the same as 'strange'.
recs.rel: Its opposite is 'normal'.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'contemporary'?
recs.facts: 'Contemporary' means almost the same as 'modern'.
recs.rel: It can also mean living or existing at the same time.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'dearth'?
recs.facts: 'Dearth' means almost the same as 'scarcity'.
recs.rel: Its opposite is 'abundance'.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'absolute'?
recs.facts: 'Absolute' means almost the same as 'complete'.
recs.rel: An absolute monarch has complete power.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'spontaneous'?
recs.facts: 'Spontaneous' means almost the same as 'impulsive'.
recs.rel: Its opposite is 'planned' or 'deliberate'.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'supervision'?
recs.facts: 'Supervision' means almost the same as 'oversight'.
recs.rel: The person who supervises is called a supervisor.

recs.q: On which river is the Tanda Dam (Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) built?
recs.facts: Tanda Dam is in Kohat District and is filled with water of the Kohat Toi stream. It supplies irrigation water to nearby villages.
recs.rel: Tanda Dam was declared a Ramsar wetland site in 1976.

recs.q: Find the next term in the series: 3/6, 6/9, 10/15, 15/24, ?
recs.facts: Numerators 3, 6, 10, 15 increase by 3, 4, 5, so next is 15 + 6 = 21. Denominators 6, 9, 15, 24 increase by 3, 6, 9, so next is 24 + 12 = 36. The term is 21/36.
recs.rel: The numerators 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 are called triangular numbers.

recs.q: Ali is 5 years old and Ayesha is twice his age. What will be Ayesha's age when Ali is 15 years old?
recs.facts: Ayesha's present age = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali becomes 15 after 10 years, so Ayesha will be 10 + 10 = 20 years.
recs.rel: Ayesha is 5 years older than Ali, so she is always 5 years older.

recs.q: In which year did Turkey become a republic and gain its modern independent status under Mustafa Kemal Ataturk?
recs.facts: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed in July 1923, and the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923.
recs.rel: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk was the first President of Turkey and died in 1938.

recs.q: What type of equation is 2y = 1 + x?
recs.facts: Both x and y have power 1 only, so the highest degree is one. Such an equation is linear and its graph is a straight line.
recs.rel: A quadratic equation has a highest power of 2.

recs.q: Which is considered the oldest university in the world still in operation?
recs.facts: Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco was founded in 859 AD by Fatima al-Fihri. UNESCO and the Guinness World Records recognise it as the oldest.
recs.rel: Some sources name Al-Azhar (970 AD) or Bologna (1088) depending on the definition used.

recs.q: When did the Indus Valley Civilization flourish, according to commonly taught dates?
recs.facts: Pakistani textbooks give the period of the Indus Valley Civilization as about 2500 BC to 1500 BC. Its main cities were Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
recs.rel: Some modern sources give the mature phase as 2600 BC to 1900 BC, so dates differ between sources.

recs.q: Between which two values does probability always lie?
recs.facts: Probability of an impossible event is 0 and of a certain event is 1. Every other event lies between these two values.
recs.rel: Probability is often also written as a percentage between 0 percent and 100 percent.

recs.q: What is the range of the values 15, 7, 11, 10, 2, 3?
recs.facts: Range = largest value minus smallest value = 15 - 2 = 13.
recs.rel: Range is a measure of spread of data.

recs.q: What type of verb is 'could'?
recs.facts: Could is a modal auxiliary (helping) verb. It is the past form of can and shows ability or possibility.
recs.rel: Other modal verbs are can, may, might, must, shall, should, will and would.

recs.q: Choose the correct word: This jacket is very ___.
recs.facts: Very is followed by an adjective, and expensive is the correct adjective here. Much cheap and high do not fit the sentence.
recs.rel: Much is normally used with uncountable nouns, not directly before adjectives.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in the letters: A E Z Y U A W O L U E?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, E, U, A, O, U, E. That makes 7 vowels.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in: A G I F O M E J I U Y X E?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, I, O, E, I, U, E. That makes 7 vowels.
recs.rel: Y is counted as a consonant in such counting questions.

recs.q: Under whose government was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960?
recs.facts: The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by President Ayub Khan of Pakistan and Prime Minister Nehru of India.
recs.rel: The World Bank was a signatory as the broker of the treaty.

recs.q: Which bowler has taken the most wickets for Pakistan in international cricket (all formats combined)?
recs.facts: Wasim Akram took 414 Test and 502 ODI wickets, about 916 in international cricket, which is the most by any Pakistani bowler.
recs.rel: Wasim Akram is a left-arm fast bowler who captained Pakistan to the 1992 World Cup win as a key player.

recs.q: Which movement launched in 1920 asked Indians to refuse to cooperate with British rule?
recs.facts: The Non-Cooperation Movement, led by Gandhi with Khilafat support, asked people to boycott British schools, courts and goods.
recs.rel: The Quit India Movement came later, in 1942.

recs.q: Who wrote the famous travel book Rehla?
recs.facts: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, dictated his travels in the Rihla (Rehla) around 1355.
recs.rel: Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq.

recs.q: Ammar is older than Amjad, and Ali is younger than Ammar. Who is the oldest of the three?
recs.facts: Ammar is older than both Amjad and Ali, so Ammar is the oldest.
recs.rel: The order of Amjad and Ali cannot be known from this information.

recs.q: Saba is twice as old as her sister, and her sister is 8 years younger than Saba. How old will Saba be when her sister is 15?
recs.facts: Let sister be x, so Saba is 2x and 2x - x = 8, giving x = 8 and Saba = 16. Sister reaches 15 after 7 years, so Saba is 16 + 7 = 23.
recs.rel: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: What is the result when zero is multiplied by any number?
recs.facts: Any number multiplied by zero gives zero.
recs.rel: This is called the zero property of multiplication.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 + 1/2?
recs.rel: 2.5 can also be written as 5/2.

recs.q: What is 80/80?
recs.facts: Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
recs.rel: Division of a number by 1 gives the same number.

recs.q: What happened in the First Battle of Panipat?
opts: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi on 21 April 1526
Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas in 1761
recs.facts: On 21 April 1526 Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat, which began Mughal rule in India.
recs.rel: Babur used cannons and matchlocks, which gave him the victory.

recs.q: Articles (a, an, the) are used mainly before which part of speech?
recs.facts: An article is a word that comes before a noun (or its adjective) to show whether it is specific or general.
recs.rel: The word the is the definite article, while a and an are indefinite articles.

recs.q: In which ghazwa (battle campaign) did the Muslims return to Madinah without any fighting?
recs.facts: In Ghazwa Tabuk (9 AH) the Byzantine army withdrew, so the Muslim army returned to Madinah without a battle.
recs.rel: Tabuk was the last ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH) himself.

recs.q: Who became the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in Pakistan (Balochistan High Court, 2018)?
recs.facts: Justice Syeda Tahira Safdar took oath as Chief Justice of the Balochistan High Court on 1 September 2018, the first woman to hold such a post in Pakistan.
recs.rel: She was also the first woman civil judge in Balochistan.

recs.q: What was the currency of France before the Euro?
recs.facts: France used the French franc until it was replaced by the Euro (notes and coins from 2002).
recs.rel: The mark was the German currency and the lira was the Italian currency before the Euro.

recs.q: What is the capital of Sierra Leone?
recs.facts: Freetown is the capital and largest city of Sierra Leone.
recs.rel: Monrovia is the capital of neighbouring Liberia.

recs.q: Since which year has Pakistan celebrated Defence Day on 6 September?
recs.facts: The war with India took place in September 1965. The first Defence Day was observed on 6 September 1966, one year after the war.
recs.rel: Defence Day honours the armed forces for defending the country on 6 September 1965.

recs.q: Which keyboard key is used for spell check in Microsoft Word?
recs.facts: Pressing F7 starts the spelling and grammar check in Word.
recs.rel: F12 opens the Save As dialog in Word.

recs.q: Where do the Jhelum and Chenab rivers meet?
recs.facts: The Jhelum joins the Chenab at Trimmu near Jhang in Punjab.
recs.rel: The combined Chenab later meets the Ravi and Sutlej to form the Panjnad.

recs.q: What are the ambassadors of Commonwealth countries to each other called?
recs.facts: Commonwealth members exchange High Commissioners instead of ambassadors.
recs.rel: Pakistan has a High Commissioner in London.

recs.q: In which country was the 1955 Bandung (Asian-African) conference, the forerunner of the Non-Aligned Movement, held?
recs.facts: The Asian-African Conference of April 1955 was held in Bandung, Indonesia.
recs.rel: The Non-Aligned Movement itself was formally founded in Belgrade in 1961.

recs.q: In a room, males are 3/2 of the females and the room has 30 people. How many females are in the room?
recs.facts: Let females be F. Males are 1.5F, so F + 1.5F = 2.5F = 30. Then F = 12 and males = 18.
recs.rel: The male to female ratio here is 3 to 2.

recs.q: What is the integral of cot x with respect to x?
recs.facts: cot x = cos x / sin x. Put u = sin x, then du = cos x dx, so the integral is ln|u| + C = ln|sin x| + C.
recs.rel: The integral of tan x is -ln|cos x| + C.

recs.q: Which three countries are known as the Baltic states?
recs.facts: The Baltic states are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea.
recs.rel: All three joined NATO and the European Union in 2004.

recs.q: What is the process of cutting away the unwanted area of an image called?
recs.facts: Cropping removes the outer unwanted parts of a picture.
recs.rel: Resizing changes the whole size of a picture without removing parts.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Mirani Dam located?
recs.facts: Mirani Dam is on the Dasht River in Kech district near Turbat, Balochistan.
recs.rel: It supplies water to Turbat and Gwadar areas.

recs.q: Who founded the Urdu Defence Association in 1900?
recs.facts: Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk formed the Urdu Defence Association in 1900 to protect Urdu during the Hindi-Urdu controversy.
recs.rel: The controversy began when UP governor Anthony MacDonnell favoured Hindi in 1900.

recs.q: What is the circumference of the Earth at the equator?
recs.facts: The Earth's equatorial circumference is about 40,075 km.
recs.rel: Its circumference through the poles is slightly smaller, about 40,008 km.

recs.q: Which nutrient is the best source of quick energy for an athlete?
recs.facts: Carbohydrates are broken into glucose, which the body can use fastest for energy.
recs.rel: Fats give more energy per gram but release it slowly.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did fasting in Ramadan (Roza) become farz?
recs.facts: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in 2 AH, in Madinah.
recs.rel: The first Ramadan fasts were kept in the same year as the Battle of Badr.

recs.q: Which of the following is a main function of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
opts: Promoting exchange rate stability and giving short-term loans to countries with balance of payments problems
Printing the currency of member countries
Fixing the price of oil for member countries
Giving military aid to member countries
recs.facts: The IMF works for international monetary cooperation and stable exchange rates, and lends to countries facing balance of payments difficulties.
recs.rel: The IMF has its headquarters in Washington D.C. and was established in 1944 at Bretton Woods.

recs.q: Which vitamin helps in the healing of wounds?
recs.facts: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed to make collagen, which repairs skin and wounds.
recs.rel: Deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy.

recs.q: Kalam Valley is located in which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: Kalam is a popular valley at the top of the Swat valley in Swat district.
recs.rel: The Swat river starts near Kalam from the Ushu and Utror streams.

recs.q: The Khojak Pass in Balochistan lies in Qila Abdullah district and leads towards which border town?
recs.facts: The Khojak Pass in the Khwaja Amran range leads from Qila Abdullah to Chaman on the Afghan border.
recs.rel: The Khojak Rail Tunnel is one of the longest railway tunnels in Pakistan.

recs.q: Which country has the lengthiest written constitution in the world?
recs.facts: The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.
recs.rel: It was adopted in 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

recs.q: In which year was the Badshahi Mosque of Lahore built?
recs.facts: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir and completed in 1673.
recs.rel: For centuries it was the largest mosque in the world by capacity, and it stands opposite Lahore Fort.

recs.q: In which area of Pakistan is the largest coal reserve found?
recs.facts: The Thar coalfield in Sindh holds about 175 billion tonnes of lignite coal, the largest reserve in Pakistan.
recs.rel: Thar coal is now used to generate electricity near Islamkot.

recs.q: What were the old names of India?
recs.facts: India has been called Hindustan, Bharat and Bharatvarsha since ancient times.
recs.rel: The name India comes from the River Indus (Sindhu).

recs.q: On which date was the Objectives Resolution presented in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented the Objectives Resolution on 7 March 1949.
recs.rel: It was passed on 12 March 1949.

recs.q: Pakistan opposed the entry of India into which group?
recs.facts: India applied for NSG membership in 2016 and Pakistan opposed it, saying it should be treated equally with India.
recs.rel: The NSG is a group of countries that controls exports of nuclear material.

recs.q: Pakistan became a full member of which organization in 2017?
recs.facts: Pakistan and India became full members of the SCO at the Astana summit in June 2017.
recs.rel: Pakistan had been an observer in the SCO since 2005.

recs.q: What is the Pentagon?
opts: Headquarters of the US Department of Defense
The residence of the US President
recs.facts: The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia is the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense.
recs.rel: It is named after its five-sided shape.

recs.q: Which word is closest in meaning to Prescribe?
recs.facts: To prescribe means to order or lay down a rule, which is close to dictate.
recs.rel: A doctor prescribes medicine by ordering it for a patient.

recs.q: What does the Saindak Project produce?
recs.facts: The Saindak Project in Chagai, Balochistan produces copper, gold and some silver.
recs.rel: It is run with Chinese help.

recs.q: The Ziarat Residency in Balochistan is associated with which leader?
recs.facts: Quaid-e-Azam spent the last days of his life at the Ziarat Residency in 1948 for rest and treatment.
recs.rel: Ziarat is also famous for its juniper forests, among the oldest in the world.

recs.q: Between which two rivers does the Bari Doab lie?
recs.facts: A doab is the land between two rivers. The Bari Doab lies between the Ravi and the Beas, with the Sutlej forming its lower boundary.
recs.rel: The name Bari Doab comes from the first letters of Beas and Ravi.

recs.q: Which is the longest national highway of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The N-5 runs from Karachi to Torkham, about 1,819 km, and is the longest highway in Pakistan.
recs.rel: It follows much of the old Grand Trunk Road route.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly?
recs.facts: Rahila Hameed Khan Durrani was elected Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly in 2008, the first woman in this post.
recs.rel: Fehmida Mirza was the first woman Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the space between the margin and the start of the first line of a paragraph called?
recs.facts: Indentation is the blank space left at the start of a line to mark a new paragraph.
recs.rel: In justified text, both left and right edges are aligned.

recs.q: How many times is the name of Hazrat Jibrael (AS) mentioned in the Quran?
recs.facts: The name Jibreel appears three times, in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:97 and 2:98) and Surah At-Tahrim (66:4).
recs.rel: Some counts differ because he is also mentioned as Ruh-ul-Ameen without the name.

recs.q: Atique is the title of which Companion of the Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is known as Atique, meaning freed from the fire, and also as Siddique.
recs.rel: He was the first Caliph of Islam.

recs.q: What is the main purpose of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
recs.facts: The WTO sets and enforces rules for trade between nations and settles trade disputes.
recs.rel: The WTO was set up in 1995 and replaced GATT.

recs.q: If a train covers 120 km per hour, how far will it cover in 18 minutes?
recs.facts: 18 minutes is 18/60 = 0.3 hour. Distance = 120 x 0.3 = 36 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time, and the time must be in hours when the speed is in km per hour.

recs.q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan in 1999?
recs.facts: General Pervez Musharraf became Chief of Army Staff in October 1998 and held the post in 1999, including the Kargil conflict and the October 1999 takeover.
recs.rel: He remained army chief until November 2007, and his predecessor was General Jahangir Karamat.

recs.q: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1971 war?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan was army chief from 1966 and also President in 1971, when the war with India took place.
recs.rel: General Gul Hassan Khan took over as army chief on 20 December 1971.

recs.q: Which two soldiers received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the 1999 Kargil conflict?
opts: Havaldar Lalak Jan and Captain Karnal Sher Khan
Major Raja Aziz Bhatti and Major Tufail
Sawar Muhammad Hussain and Major Shabbir Sharif
Lance Naik Muhammad Mahfuz and Major Akram
recs.facts: Havaldar Lalak Jan (Northern Light Infantry) and Captain Karnal Sher Khan (27 Sindh) were awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil 1999.
recs.rel: Karnal Sher Khan was a Captain at the time of his martyrdom and was promoted to Colonel after death.

recs.q: Who persuaded Hazrat Usman (RA) to accept Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) presented Islam to Hazrat Usman (RA), who then accepted it at an early stage of the Prophet's mission.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman (RA) is known as Zun-Noorain because he married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Which instrument is used to measure the altitude (angle above the horizon) of the sun?
recs.facts: A sextant measures the angle between the horizon and a celestial body such as the sun, which gives its altitude.
recs.rel: Sailors use the sextant for navigation by finding their latitude.

recs.q: Near which city did the plane crash that killed General Zia ul Haq in 1988 take place?
recs.facts: General Zia ul Haq died on 17 August 1988 when his aircraft crashed shortly after take-off near Bahawalpur.
recs.rel: US Ambassador Arnold Raphel and several Pakistani generals also died in the crash.

recs.q: What is the touching or kissing of the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) during Tawaf called?
recs.facts: Istilam means touching or kissing the Black Stone, or pointing towards it when the crowd is too large.
recs.rel: Tawaf is the circling of the Kaaba seven times.

recs.q: Who is the author of the play Hamlet?
recs.facts: Hamlet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare around 1600.
recs.rel: Other famous tragedies by Shakespeare are Macbeth, Othello and King Lear.

recs.q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah present the Delhi Proposals?
recs.facts: The Delhi Muslim Proposals were put forward by Jinnah in March 1927 as a way to settle Hindu-Muslim differences on the constitution.
recs.rel: The year 1916 is that of the Lucknow Pact, and the 14 Points came in 1929.

recs.q: In which city is the cemetery Jannat ul Baqi located?
recs.facts: Jannat ul Baqi is the main cemetery of Madinah, close to the Prophet's Mosque.
recs.rel: Many family members and Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) are buried there.

recs.q: How many players are there in a baseball team on the field?
recs.facts: A baseball team puts nine players on the field at a time.
recs.rel: Cricket and football teams have 11 players each.

recs.q: What is the date of birth of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the Gregorian calendar, as commonly given in Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Pakistani textbooks commonly give 22 April 571 AD, in the Year of the Elephant, as the birth date.
recs.rel: Sources differ slightly, with some giving 20 April 571 AD, and the Islamic date is 12 Rabi ul Awwal in the commonly followed view.

recs.q: Sofia is the capital of which country?
recs.facts: Sofia is the largest city and capital of Bulgaria.
recs.rel: Bulgaria is a Balkan country on the Black Sea.

recs.q: What is the capital of Haiti?
recs.facts: Port-au-Prince is the capital and largest city of Haiti.
recs.rel: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, whose capital is Santo Domingo.

recs.q: What is the capital of Honduras?
recs.facts: Tegucigalpa is the capital of Honduras.
recs.rel: Managua is the capital of Nicaragua.

recs.q: What is the capital of Qatar?
recs.facts: Doha is the capital and largest city of Qatar.
recs.rel: Qatar hosted the FIFA World Cup in 2022.

recs.q: On which date was the Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline agreement signed in 2010?
recs.facts: Iran and Pakistan signed the gas pipeline agreement on 16 March 2010.
recs.rel: A formal gas export contract followed in June 2010, and Pakistan's section was inaugurated in March 2013.

recs.q: Which country is well known for having no official capital city?
recs.facts: Nauru has no official capital. Its government offices are in the Yaren district, which is treated as the de facto capital.
recs.rel: Nauru is the smallest island nation and the smallest republic in the world.

recs.q: Rickets in children is caused by the lack of which vitamin?
recs.facts: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium. Without it the bones of children stay soft and bend, which is called rickets.
recs.rel: The adult form of this bone softening is called osteomalacia.

recs.q: Which type of cell has no true nucleus?
recs.facts: Prokaryotic cells such as bacteria have no membrane-bound nucleus. Their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm.
recs.rel: Mature red blood cells of humans also lose their nucleus.

recs.q: What is the land area between the Chenab and Jhelum rivers called?
recs.facts: The doab between the Jhelum and Chenab is called Chaj Doab, a name made from the first letters of Chenab and Jhelum.
recs.rel: The doab between the Ravi and Chenab is called Rachna Doab.

recs.q: In which Chinese city was the first China International Import Expo (CIIE) held in November 2018, which Prime Minister Imran Khan attended?
recs.facts: The first CIIE was held in Shanghai from 5 to 10 November 2018. Pakistan took part and Imran Khan visited China at that time.
recs.rel: The CIIE is held in Shanghai every November.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters (Secretariat) of the Commonwealth of Nations?
recs.facts: The Commonwealth Secretariat is at Marlborough House in London, United Kingdom.
recs.rel: The Commonwealth has its own Secretary-General.

recs.q: The Simla Conference, held by Viceroy Lord Wavell to discuss self-government, took place in which year?
recs.facts: Lord Wavell called the Simla Conference in June 1945. It failed because Congress and the Muslim League did not agree on Muslim representation.
recs.rel: The Wavell Plan was the proposal discussed at the conference.

recs.q: The Tochi Pass links North Waziristan in Pakistan with which Afghan province?
recs.facts: The Tochi Pass runs from Bannu and North Waziristan towards Ghazni in Afghanistan.
recs.rel: The Tochi River flows through this pass.

recs.q: The Malakand Pass links the Peshawar valley with which regions?
recs.facts: The Malakand Pass lies in Malakand district and is the gateway from the Peshawar plain to Swat, Dir and Chitral.
recs.rel: The Malakand Pass was the scene of the British campaign of 1897.

recs.q: Which continent consists of only one country?
recs.facts: The continent of Australia is one single country, the Commonwealth of Australia.
recs.rel: Antarctica has no countries and Europe has more than 40.

recs.q: Which team won the 2003 Cricket World Cup?
recs.facts: Australia beat India in the final in Johannesburg, South Africa, in March 2003.
recs.rel: Australia was captained by Ricky Ponting.

recs.q: Which of these is a Kharif crop of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Kharif crops are sown in summer (April to June) and harvested in autumn. Rice, cotton, maize and sugarcane are Kharif crops.
recs.rel: Wheat, gram and mustard are Rabi (winter) crops.

recs.q: Under whose captaincy did Pakistan win the 1992 Cricket World Cup?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne in 1992 under the captaincy of Imran Khan.
recs.rel: This is Pakistan's only Cricket World Cup title so far.

recs.q: Which country won the 2020 Kabaddi World Cup (circle style) held in Lahore?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat India 43-41 in the final at Punjab Stadium, Lahore, on 16 February 2020.
recs.rel: It was Pakistan's first Kabaddi World Cup title.

recs.q: Kip is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: The kip is the national currency of Laos.
recs.rel: Cambodia uses the riel and Myanmar uses the kyat.

recs.q: Pound sterling is the currency of which country?
recs.facts: Pound sterling is the official currency of the United Kingdom.
recs.rel: It is one of the oldest currencies still in use.

recs.q: What is the currency of Vatican City?
recs.facts: Vatican City uses the euro, although it issues its own euro coins.
recs.rel: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.

recs.q: What is the currency of Vietnam?
recs.facts: The Vietnamese dong is the official currency of Vietnam.
recs.rel: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.

recs.q: On which river is the Ghazi Brotha Dam (barrage) located?
recs.facts: Ghazi Barotha is on the Indus River, below Tarbela Dam, in Attock district.
recs.rel: It is a run-of-the-river hydropower project of about 1450 MW.

recs.q: On what date did the USSR formally break up?
recs.facts: The Supreme Soviet declared the USSR dissolved on 26 December 1991, a day after Gorbachev resigned on 25 December.
recs.rel: Russia became the main successor state.

recs.q: In which country is the Great Victoria Desert?
recs.facts: The Great Victoria Desert is the largest desert in Australia.
recs.rel: It lies in Western and South Australia.

recs.q: Who wrote the book A Discipline Divided: Schools and Sects in Political Science?
recs.facts: Gabriel Almond wrote A Discipline Divided in 1988 about the divisions inside political science.
recs.rel: Almond is also known for his work on political culture.

recs.q: Who wrote the book The Dividing Discipline: Hierarchy and Diversity in International Theory?
recs.facts: K. J. Holsti wrote The Dividing Discipline in 1985 on the state of international relations theory.
recs.rel: Holsti is a Finnish-Canadian scholar of international relations.

recs.q: Modern badminton developed from the game Poona played by British army officers in which country?
recs.facts: British officers in India (at Pune, called Poona) played it in the 1870s and took it to England, where it was named after Badminton House.
recs.rel: Sources differ on small details of the early history of the game.

recs.q: Fort Munro is a hill station in which district?
recs.facts: Fort Munro lies in the Sulaiman Mountains in Dera Ghazi Khan district, Punjab.
recs.rel: It is one of the few hill stations of Punjab.

recs.q: Which party won the most seats in the 2008 general election in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Peoples Party won the most seats in February 2008, and Yousuf Raza Gilani became Prime Minister.
recs.rel: The election was held after the death of Benazir Bhutto in December 2007.

recs.q: In which year was the Israeli intelligence agency Mossad established?
recs.facts: Mossad was founded on 13 December 1949 and took its present name in 1951.
recs.rel: Its full name is the Institute for Intelligence and Special Operations.

recs.q: On what date was the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) established?
recs.facts: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP at a meeting in Lahore on 30 November 1967.
recs.rel: The PPP first came to power after the 1970 election.

recs.q: What is the full name of the conqueror of Sindh, Muhammad bin Qasim?
recs.facts: Muhammad bin Qasim belonged to the Banu Thaqif tribe of Taif, so he is known as al-Thaqafi.
recs.rel: He invaded Sindh in 711-712 AD during the Umayyad rule under governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf.

recs.q: Kahuta Research Laboratories (the Engineering Research Laboratories) were established during the government of which leader?
recs.facts: The nuclear programme was started by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, and the Engineering Research Laboratories at Kahuta were set up in 1976 during his government.
recs.rel: The laboratories were later renamed Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) in 1981 after Dr A. Q. Khan.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the CIA (Central Intelligence Agency) located?
recs.facts: The CIA headquarters is in Langley (McLean area), Virginia, near Washington D.C.
recs.rel: The CIA was established in 1947 under the National Security Act.

recs.q: In which country is the city of Heidelberg located?
recs.facts: Heidelberg is a city in south-western Germany in the state of Baden-Wuerttemberg on the Neckar river.
recs.rel: Heidelberg University, founded in 1386, is the oldest university in Germany.

recs.q: Which country has the highest number of satellites in orbit?
recs.facts: The United States owns by far the largest number of active satellites, mainly because of large constellations such as Starlink.
recs.rel: Sputnik 1 of the Soviet Union in 1957 was the first artificial satellite.

recs.q: In which year (Nabwi) did the first Hijrat (migration) of Muslims to Habsha (Abyssinia) take place?
recs.facts: The first migration to Abyssinia took place in the 5th year of prophethood (about 615 AD) to escape the persecution of Quraish.
recs.rel: The king Najashi (Negus) gave shelter to the Muslims; some sources differ on the date of the second migration.

recs.q: What is the capital of the Holy See?
recs.facts: The Holy See is the government of the Catholic Church and is based in Vatican City.
recs.rel: Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world and lies inside Rome.

recs.q: Which of the following was a paternal aunt (Phuphi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Safiyya was a daughter of Abdul Muttalib and so a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Other paternal aunts include Atika, Arwa, Umm Hakim al-Bayda, Barra and Umaima.

recs.q: Which idol was worshipped by the people of Taif?
recs.facts: Al-Lat was the main idol of the Thaqif tribe of Taif.
recs.rel: Al-Uzza was worshipped near Nakhla and Manat near Qudayd, and Hubal was the chief idol inside the Kaaba.

recs.q: On which date did India conduct its Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998?
recs.facts: India carried out the first of its Pokhran-II tests on 11 May 1998, followed by more tests on 13 May.
recs.rel: Pakistan answered with its tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998; India's first test was in 1974.

recs.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as what?
recs.facts: The Indian Councils Act 1909 was introduced by Lord Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy), so it is called the Morley-Minto Reforms.
recs.rel: It gave Muslims separate electorates.

recs.q: How many barrages are built on the River Indus in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The six barrages on the Indus are Jinnah, Chashma, Taunsa, Guddu, Sukkur and Kotri.
recs.rel: Sukkur Barrage, completed in 1932, is the oldest of them.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the Indus Highway (N-55) in Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Indus Highway runs from Karachi to Peshawar along the Indus river and is about 1264 km long.
recs.rel: It is numbered N-55 in the national highway network.

recs.q: How many Muslims and how many disbelievers (Kuffar) took part in the Ghazwa of Khandaq?
recs.facts: About 3000 Muslims defended Madina against a combined army of about 10000 from the Quraish and their allies.
recs.rel: The trench was dug on the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

recs.q: Who was the leader of the Quraish (disbelievers) army in the Ghazwa of Khandaq?
recs.facts: Abu Sufyan, who had not yet accepted Islam, led the Quraish in the Battle of Khandaq. Abu Jahl had been killed earlier at Badr.
recs.rel: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

recs.q: In which district of Punjab is Namal (Numal) Lake located?
recs.facts: Namal Lake is an artificial lake in Mianwali district near the Namal Valley.
recs.rel: It lies in the Salt Range area.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word Urdu in the Turkish language?
recs.facts: The word Urdu comes from Turkish ordu which means army or military camp.
recs.rel: Urdu developed in the army camps and bazaars of the Mughal period.

recs.q: What is the approximate length of the Line of Control (LOC) between Pakistan and India in Kashmir?
recs.facts: The Line of Control is about 740 km long, as commonly stated.
recs.rel: It was established after the 1971 war by the Simla Agreement of 1972; sources give slightly different lengths.

recs.q: Which strait lies between Greenland and Iceland?
recs.facts: The Denmark Strait separates Greenland from Iceland and links the Arctic and Atlantic oceans.
recs.rel: Davis Strait lies between Greenland and Canada.

recs.q: Kachura Lake is located near which city?
recs.facts: Upper and Lower Kachura Lakes are near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: Lower Kachura is also called Shangrila Lake.

recs.q: Rawal Lake is located in which city?
recs.facts: Rawal Lake is an artificial reservoir in Islamabad that supplies water to Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
recs.rel: It is fed by the Korang River.

recs.q: On which date was Hazrat Ali (RA) martyred?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali (RA) was attacked by Abdur Rahman bin Muljam while praying in Kufa and was martyred on 21 Ramzan 40 Hijri.
recs.rel: This date matches about 30 January 661 AD.

recs.q: Where is Masjid Khaif located?
recs.facts: Masjid Khaif is a historic mosque in the valley of Mina near Makkah. Many prophets are said to have prayed there.
recs.rel: Mina is where pilgrims stay and perform the stoning of the Jamarat during Hajj.

recs.q: What is the full form of IRDA?
recs.facts: IRDA stands for Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, the body that regulates the insurance sector in India.
recs.rel: It was set up under an Act of the Indian Parliament in 1999.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word Islam?
recs.facts: The word Islam comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, meaning submission to Allah and peace.
recs.rel: A person who follows Islam is called a Muslim, meaning one who submits.

recs.q: What does the word Miraath mean?
recs.facts: Miraath is an Arabic word meaning inheritance, the property left by a dead person.
recs.rel: The rules of inheritance are given in Surah An-Nisa of the Quran.

recs.q: Which two Surahs of the Quran are called Muawwidhatain (Moaztain)?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah An-Nas (114) teach us to seek refuge with Allah, so they are called Muawwidhatain.
recs.rel: They are the last two surahs of the Quran.

recs.q: What is the highest mountain of the Balochistan plateau?
recs.facts: Zarghun Ghar near Quetta is the highest peak in Balochistan at about 3,578 metres.
recs.rel: Takatu mountain overlooks Quetta city and is a well known nearby peak.

recs.q: Where is Mount Whitney located?
recs.facts: Mount Whitney, about 4,421 metres, is in the Sierra Nevada range in California.
recs.rel: It is the highest peak in the contiguous United States.

recs.q: Who appointed Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of Yemen?
recs.facts: The Holy Prophet (SAW) sent Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and teacher in 10 Hijri.
recs.rel: He is known as the most knowledgeable Companion about halal and haram.

recs.q: Which of the following was NOT a daughter of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
recs.facts: The four daughters of the Prophet (SAW) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA). Aisha (RA) was his wife.
recs.rel: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the youngest and married Hazrat Ali (RA).

recs.q: Hub Dam and Hub Lake are near which city?
recs.facts: Hub Dam is on the Hub River on the border of Sindh and Balochistan, and it supplies water to Karachi.
recs.rel: The Hub River forms part of the border between Sindh and Balochistan.

recs.q: If nP2 = 20, what is the value of n?
recs.rel: nPr = n! divided by (n-r)!.

recs.q: On which date was the League of Nations founded?
recs.facts: The League of Nations came into being on 10 January 1920 after the Treaty of Versailles, with its headquarters in Geneva.
recs.rel: It was replaced by the United Nations in 1945.

recs.q: Who defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556)?
recs.facts: The army of the young Akbar, led by Bairam Khan, defeated Hemu (Hemachandra Vikramaditya) at Panipat in 1556.
recs.rel: Akbar was only 13 years old at the time.

recs.q: Whom did Ahmad Shah Abdali defeat in the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761)?
recs.facts: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) defeated the Marathas led by Sadashiv Rao Bhau at Panipat in 1761.
recs.rel: The defeat greatly weakened Maratha power in north India.

recs.q: Where is the permanent secretariat of SAARC?
recs.facts: The SAARC Secretariat was set up in Kathmandu in 1987.
recs.rel: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985.

recs.q: In which year was interest (riba) finally prohibited in Islam, as commonly taught?
recs.facts: The final prohibition of riba came near the end of the Prophet's life and was announced in the Farewell Hajj sermon in 10 Hijri.
recs.rel: Sources differ on the exact stage dates of the prohibition of riba.

recs.q: How many sajdas (places of prostration) are there in the Quran according to the Hanafi school?
recs.facts: The Quran has 14 verses of sajda according to the commonly taught view.
recs.rel: The Shafi school counts 15 by including one in Surah Al-Hajj.

recs.q: Which Companion of the Prophet (SAW) has the title Jami ul Quran?
recs.facts: Hazrat Usman (RA) is called Jami ul Quran because he had copies of the Quran made in one standard text.
recs.rel: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) first collected the Quran in a book form.

recs.q: Between which two places was the first railway line in present Pakistan opened?
recs.facts: The first railway line in the area now Pakistan ran from Karachi to Kotri and opened in 1861.
recs.rel: It was part of the Scinde Railway.

recs.q: What is the length of the Mariana Trench?
recs.facts: The Mariana Trench is about 2,550 km long and about 69 km wide.
recs.rel: It is in the western Pacific Ocean near the Mariana Islands.

recs.q: What is the Mariana Trench?
opts: The deepest part of the Earth's oceans, in the Pacific
The highest plateau in the world
recs.facts: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known place in the oceans, and its deepest point is called Challenger Deep.
recs.rel: Challenger Deep is about 10,900 metres deep.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Committee of the Red Cross located?
recs.facts: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva by Henry Dunant, and its headquarters is still in Geneva, Switzerland.
recs.rel: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

recs.q: What was the approximate duration of the revelation of the Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran was revealed gradually over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Makkah to the last in Madinah.
recs.rel: About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.

recs.q: On which river is Balakot located?
recs.facts: Balakot is a town in Mansehra district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the bank of the Kunhar River.
recs.rel: Balakot was badly hit by the October 2005 earthquake.

recs.q: On which river is Wular Lake located?
recs.facts: Wular Lake in Kashmir is fed by the Jhelum River, which flows through it.
recs.rel: Wular Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.

recs.q: Sadiq Sanjrani held which office in Pakistan from 2018 to 2024?
recs.facts: Sadiq Sanjrani, from Balochistan, was elected Chairman of the Senate in March 2018 and served until 2024.
recs.rel: Since April 2024 the Chairman of the Senate is Yousaf Raza Gilani.

recs.q: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
recs.facts: Sher Shah Suri is buried in a large tomb in the middle of a lake at Sasaram in Bihar, India.
recs.rel: Sher Shah built the Grand Trunk Road and introduced the rupee.

recs.q: Titu Meer, the leader of the Bengal peasants' movement, was the son of whom?
recs.facts: Titu Meer (Mir Nisar Ali) was born in 1782 to Syed Mir Hassan Ali and Abida Ruqayya Khatoon in West Bengal.
recs.rel: He built a bamboo fort at Narkelberia and fought the British and landlords in 1831.

recs.q: Who was the eldest son of Zaheeruddin Babur?
recs.facts: Humayun was the eldest son of Babur and succeeded him as the second Mughal emperor in 1530.
recs.rel: Babur's other sons were Kamran, Askari and Hindal.

recs.q: What does HIT stand for?
recs.facts: HIT stands for Heavy Industries Taxila, a defence production complex in Taxila near Rawalpindi.
recs.rel: HIT makes Al-Khalid tanks and other armoured vehicles.

recs.q: For which period did the Congress ministries remain in power in the provinces of British India?
recs.facts: After the 1937 elections the Congress formed ministries in 7 provinces, and they resigned in 1939 when India was dragged into World War II.
recs.rel: Muslims celebrated a Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 after the resignations.

recs.q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in the subcontinent?
recs.facts: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.
recs.rel: The empire lasted formally until 1857.

recs.q: Amjad and Ahmed kept 24 balloons in total, and Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmed. How many balloons did Amjad keep?
recs.facts: Let Ahmed have x, then Amjad has 3x. So 4x = 24, x = 6, and Amjad has 18.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: They are three brothers, Ali is ______ of the three.
recs.facts: The superlative degree is used when one person is compared with more than two, so cleverest is correct.
recs.rel: The comparative degree is used for two persons only.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Construction of Religious Boundaries?
recs.facts: Harjot Oberoi wrote The Construction of Religious Boundaries (1994) about Sikh identity.
recs.rel: The book is a well-known study of Sikh tradition and culture.

recs.q: Who wrote the Persian poetry book Zabur-e-Ajam?
recs.facts: Zabur-e-Ajam (1927) is a Persian book of poetry by Allama Iqbal.
recs.rel: It contains the famous Gulshan-e-Raz-e-Jadid and Bandagi Nama.

recs.q: What is the relation of Hazrat Asma (RA) with Hazrat Zubair (RA)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Asma bint Abu Bakr (RA) was the wife of Hazrat Zubair bin Awwam (RA).
recs.rel: Their son was Abdullah bin Zubair (RA).

recs.q: Which sea has the saltiest water among the well-known seas of the world?
recs.facts: The Dead Sea has about 34 percent salt, nearly ten times that of ocean water, so people float easily in it.
recs.rel: Strictly it is a salt lake, and its shore is the lowest land on Earth.

recs.q: Which pact was signed in 1916 between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League?
recs.facts: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an agreement between the Congress and the Muslim League on joint political demands. Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity for his role in this pact.

recs.q: Who imposed martial law in Pakistan in July 1977 and served as Chief Martial Law Administrator?
recs.facts: General Zia ul Haq, the Chief of Army Staff, removed Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto on 5 July 1977 (Operation Fair Play) and imposed martial law.
recs.rel: Zia ul Haq ruled until his death in an air crash on 17 August 1988.

recs.q: Who dismissed the first government of Benazir Bhutto in August 1990?
recs.facts: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan used the power of Article 58(2)(b) to dismiss her government in August 1990 on charges of corruption and misrule.
recs.rel: Nawaz Sharif became Prime Minister after the October 1990 elections.

recs.q: If 300 out of 500 students are present, what is the percentage of present students?
recs.facts: Percentage present = 300 divided by 500 times 100 = 60 percent.
recs.rel: The percentage of absent students in this case would be 40 percent.

recs.q: Who wrote the novel The Alchemist?
recs.facts: The Alchemist was written by the Brazilian author Paulo Coelho and published in 1988.
recs.rel: It is one of the best-selling books in the world and has been translated into over 80 languages.

recs.q: Which continent has the largest number of countries?
recs.facts: Africa has 54 countries recognised by the United Nations, the most of any continent.
recs.rel: Asia has about 48 to 49 countries and Europe about 44 to 50, depending on the source.

recs.q: A car travels at 30 km/h and a train travels twice as fast. What is the speed of the train?
recs.facts: Twice the car's speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h, so the train covers 60 km in one hour.
recs.rel: In 30 minutes the same train would cover 30 km.

recs.q: On what date did Field Marshal Ayub Khan resign as President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Ayub Khan resigned on 25 March 1969 after mass protests and handed power to General Yahya Khan.
recs.rel: Yahya Khan then imposed martial law.

recs.q: Which famous leaning tower is located in Italy?
opts: Tower of Pisa (Leaning Tower of Pisa)
recs.facts: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the bell tower of the cathedral in Pisa, Italy, and leans because of soft ground.
recs.rel: Its construction began in 1173.

recs.q: Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore commemorates which historical event?
recs.facts: Minar-e-Pakistan was built at Iqbal Park (Minto Park) to mark the passing of the Lahore Resolution on 23 March 1940.
recs.rel: Its construction was completed in 1968.

recs.q: In which year did Pervez Musharraf resign as President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Musharraf resigned on 18 August 2008 to avoid impeachment.
recs.rel: He had come to power by a coup on 12 October 1999.

recs.q: Who dismissed the first Nawaz Sharif government in 1993?
recs.facts: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan dismissed the government in April 1993 using Article 58(2)(b).
recs.rel: The Supreme Court restored it in May 1993, but both Nawaz Sharif and the President resigned in July 1993.

recs.q: On what date did Khawaja Nazimuddin, the second Prime Minister of Pakistan, take office?
recs.facts: After Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated on 16 October 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Prime Minister on 17 October 1951.
recs.rel: He was dismissed by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad on 17 April 1953.

recs.q: What is the product of sec and cos (of the same angle)?
recs.facts: sec theta = 1 / cos theta, so sec theta x cos theta = 1.
recs.rel: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, and cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent.

recs.q: Who gave the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech, and in which country was it delivered?
recs.facts: Martin Luther King Jr delivered the speech in Washington DC at the Lincoln Memorial on 28 August 1963.
recs.rel: The speech was given during the March on Washington for civil rights.

recs.q: A train travels at twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 20 km in one hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 20 = 40 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 40 x 1/2 = 20 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time.

recs.q: Who became Prime Minister of Pakistan after the non-party general elections of 1985?
recs.facts: After the 1985 non-party elections, General Zia ul Haq nominated Muhammad Khan Junejo, who became Prime Minister in March 1985.
recs.rel: Zia dismissed the Junejo government in May 1988.

recs.q: Who ended the second government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in October 1999?
recs.facts: General Pervez Musharraf, the army chief, took over power in a bloodless coup on 12 October 1999 and ended Nawaz Sharif's government.
recs.rel: Musharraf first took the title of Chief Executive and became President in June 2001.

recs.q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan in 2002 after the general elections?
recs.facts: Mir Zafarullah Khan Jamali was elected Prime Minister on 23 November 2002 after the October 2002 general elections.
recs.rel: He resigned in June 2004 and Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain served briefly before Shaukat Aziz.

recs.q: Under which article of the 1973 Constitution does the President appoint the Chief of Army Staff?
recs.facts: Article 243 deals with command of the armed forces, and under it the President appoints the Chief of Army Staff on the advice of the Prime Minister.
recs.rel: This article was amended by the 27th Amendment of November 2025, which also created the post of Chief of Defence Forces.

recs.q: In which country did Mahatma Gandhi start his non-violent (satyagraha) struggle?
recs.facts: Gandhi developed satyagraha in South Africa from 1906 while protesting against discriminatory laws against Indians.
recs.rel: He returned to India in 1915.

recs.q: Which book was written by Adolf Hitler?
recs.facts: Mein Kampf (My Struggle) was written by Hitler while in prison in 1924-25 and sets out his political ideas.
recs.rel: Hitler led Nazi Germany from 1933 until 1945.

recs.q: On what date did Amnesty International receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
recs.facts: Amnesty International was awarded the 1977 Nobel Peace Prize, and the prize was presented on 10 December 1977 in Oslo.
recs.rel: The award was announced on 10 October 1977.

recs.q: Which city is called the gold capital of the world in many Pakistani textbooks?
recs.facts: Johannesburg in South Africa grew from a gold rush in 1886 and is known as the City of Gold.
recs.rel: Sources differ, as Dubai is also nicknamed the City of Gold for its gold trade.

recs.q: All planets rotate on which of the following?
recs.facts: Every planet spins (rotates) on its own axis, while it revolves around the Sun along its orbit.
recs.rel: Earth's rotation on its axis causes day and night.

recs.q: Who dismissed the first government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto in 1990?
recs.facts: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan dismissed her government on 6 August 1990 under Article 58(2)(b) on charges of corruption.
recs.rel: Her second government was dismissed in 1996 by President Farooq Leghari.

recs.q: What is the factorial of 2?
recs.facts: 2 factorial is 2 x 1 = 2.
recs.rel: 0 factorial and 1 factorial are both equal to 1.

recs.q: Who designed the national flag of Pakistan according to most Pakistani sources?
recs.facts: The flag was designed by Syed Amiruddin Kidwai, based on the flag of the All India Muslim League, and adopted on 11 August 1947.
recs.rel: Some sources also mention Master Altaf Hussain as the one who prepared the first flag, so sources differ.

recs.q: A helicopter uses 120 gallons of fuel to travel 60 km. How far will it travel on 700 gallons at the same rate?
recs.facts: Distance per gallon is 60 / 120 = 0.5 km. So 700 gallons cover 700 x 0.5 = 350 km.
recs.rel: This is a direct proportion question: more fuel gives more distance.

recs.q: After which pact was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity?
recs.facts: Jinnah worked to bring the Muslim League and Congress together in the Lucknow Pact of 1916, and was then called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity.
recs.rel: The title is commonly credited to Sarojini Naidu.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did Pakistan come into being (14 August 1947)?
recs.facts: 14 August 1947 fell in Ramadan 1366 AH.
recs.rel: It was the 27th of Ramadan, though some candidates remember it as 17 Ramadan.

recs.q: What is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 5 cm?
recs.facts: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 6 x 5 = 15 sq cm.
recs.rel: A triangle has half the area of a rectangle with the same base and height.

recs.q: What does GHQ stand for, and in which city is it located?
recs.facts: GHQ means General Headquarters, the headquarters of the Pakistan Army, located in Rawalpindi.
recs.rel: The Chief of Army Staff works from GHQ.

recs.q: Who is the Director General of ISI (Inter-Services Intelligence) of Pakistan as of 2026?
recs.facts: Lt Gen Muhammad Asim Malik has been DG ISI since September 2024 and was still in the post in 2026.
recs.rel: His predecessor was Lt Gen Nadeem Anjum.

recs.q: Who is credited with the famous saying "Knowledge is power"?
recs.facts: The phrase "knowledge itself is power" is credited to the English philosopher Francis Bacon (1597).
recs.rel: Thomas Hobbes also used a similar phrase later, but Bacon is the usual answer in textbooks.

recs.q: In mathematics, what is a row matrix?
opts: A matrix with only one column
A matrix with only one row (1 x n)
A matrix with equal rows and columns
A matrix with all zero entries
recs.facts: A row matrix has exactly one row and n columns, so its order is 1 x n.
recs.rel: A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.

recs.q: In which year was the Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore completed?
recs.facts: Construction of Minar-e-Pakistan started in 1960 and it was completed in 1968.
recs.rel: It stands in Iqbal Park, Lahore, where the Lahore Resolution was passed in 1940.

recs.q: Which name did Pakistan give to its military response to India in May 2025?
recs.facts: Pakistan named its response Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos, meaning a solid wall (from Surah As-Saff, verse 4).
recs.rel: The operation was launched on 10 May 2025.

recs.q: Kamal is older than Jamal, Jamal is older than Hussain, and Hussain is older than Waqar. Who is the oldest?
recs.facts: The order from oldest is Kamal, Jamal, Hussain, Waqar. So Kamal is the oldest.
recs.rel: Waqar is the youngest in this chain.

recs.q: Which one is the odd man out: Socrates, Handel, Beethoven, Mozart?
recs.facts: Handel, Beethoven and Mozart were famous composers of music. Socrates was a Greek philosopher.
recs.rel: Socrates was the teacher of Plato, who was the teacher of Aristotle.

recs.q: On what date did the second government of Benazir Bhutto take office as Prime Minister?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto won the 1993 election and took oath as Prime Minister for the second time on 19 October 1993.
recs.rel: Her first term started on 2 December 1988, and she was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim-majority country.

recs.q: Which parallel divides South Korea and North Korea?
recs.facts: After the Second World War, Korea was divided along the 38th parallel north into North and South.
recs.rel: The 17th parallel divided North and South Vietnam.

recs.q: What is the derivative of x to the power 5 with respect to x?
recs.facts: By the power rule d/dx of x^n = n x^(n-1), so the derivative of x^5 is 5x^4.
recs.rel: The derivative of a constant is zero.

recs.q: What did the Pakistan Resolution of 23 March 1940 demand, and who moved it?
opts: Separate electorates for Muslims, moved by Allama Iqbal
Full provincial autonomy within India, moved by Liaquat Ali Khan
Independent Muslim states in the north-western and eastern zones of India, moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq
A united India with a Muslim president, moved by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
recs.facts: The resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League and demanded independent states in the Muslim-majority zones. It was moved by Bengal Chief Minister A. K. Fazlul Huq.
recs.rel: It was seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman and is also called the Lahore Resolution.

recs.q: Which is the largest river of South Africa?
recs.facts: The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa, about 2,200 km long.
recs.rel: It flows west into the Atlantic Ocean and forms part of the border with Namibia.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'defer'?
recs.facts: To defer means to put off until a later time, which is to postpone.
recs.rel: Defer can also mean to yield to someone's opinion.

recs.q: Who dismissed the second government of Benazir Bhutto in November 1996?
recs.facts: President Farooq Leghari, a former member of her own party, dismissed her government on 5 November 1996 on charges of corruption and the killing of Murtaza Bhutto.
recs.rel: Her first government had been dismissed in 1990 by Ghulam Ishaq Khan.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day is the 18th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 18th is 17 days. 17 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 3, so the day is 3 days after Friday, which is Monday.
recs.rel: Days repeat every 7 days, so dates 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29 fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 20th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 1st to the 20th is 19 days. 19 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 5, so the day is 5 days after Monday, which is Saturday.
recs.rel: If the 1st is Monday, then the 15th is also Monday, so the 20th is five days later.

recs.q: In which country was the G20 Leaders' Summit of 2025 held?
recs.facts: The 2025 G20 summit was held in Johannesburg, South Africa, in November 2025. It was the first G20 summit hosted in Africa.
recs.rel: The United States holds the G20 presidency for 2026, with the summit planned at Doral, Miami, in December 2026.

recs.q: What is the full form of the abbreviation LLB?
recs.facts: LLB comes from the Latin Legum Baccalaureus and means Bachelor of Laws, the basic law degree.
recs.rel: The master's degree in law is abbreviated LLM.

recs.q: What is the full form of OIC?
recs.facts: OIC stands for Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, a group of 57 member states. It was formerly named the Organisation of the Islamic Conference.
recs.rel: The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

recs.q: What is the full form of PMA?
recs.facts: PMA stands for Pakistan Military Academy, the institution that trains officers for the Pakistan Army.
recs.rel: The Pakistan Military Academy is located in Kakul, Abbottabad.

recs.q: What is the full form of PTA in Pakistan's telecom sector?
recs.facts: PTA is the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, the regulator of telecom services in Pakistan, set up in 1996.
recs.rel: PEMRA regulates electronic media, while PTA regulates telecommunications.

recs.q: Through which amendment to the 1973 Constitution was NWFP renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: The 18th Amendment, passed in April 2010, renamed the North-West Frontier Province as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: The same amendment removed the President's power to dismiss the assembly under Article 58(2)(b) and gave more powers to the provinces.

recs.q: Who started the Aligarh Movement in the subcontinent?
recs.facts: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan started the Aligarh Movement to promote modern education among Muslims after 1857.
recs.rel: He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.

recs.q: In which year was Amnesty International established?
recs.facts: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 by the British lawyer Peter Benenson.
recs.rel: It won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977 for its work for human rights.

recs.q: What is the antonym of the word medieval?
recs.facts: Medieval refers to the Middle Ages and old times, so its opposite is modern.
recs.rel: The Middle Ages in Europe lasted roughly from the 5th to the 15th century.

recs.q: Aslam walks towards the east, after some time he turns left, and some steps later he turns right. In which direction is he now moving?
recs.facts: Facing east, a left turn makes him face north. Turning right from north makes him face east again.
recs.rel: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

recs.q: Who dissolved the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in October 1954?
recs.facts: Governor General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly on 24 October 1954. The Federal Court upheld this in the Maulvi Tamizuddin case.
recs.rel: The dissolution is seen as a key blow to democracy in early Pakistan.

recs.q: Who is Data Ganj Bakhsh?
opts: A Sufi saint of Lahore, Hazrat Ali Hujwiri
