recs.facts: Data Ganj Bakhsh is the title of Hazrat Ali bin Usman Al-Hujwiri, an 11th-century Sufi saint who settled in Lahore. His shrine in Lahore is one of the most visited in Pakistan.
recs.rel: He wrote the famous Persian book on Sufism, Kashf-ul-Mahjoob.

recs.q: Who was the first Governor of Balochistan after it became a province in 1970?
recs.facts: Balochistan became a province on 1 July 1970 when One Unit was dissolved, and Lt Gen Riaz Hussain was its first Governor.
recs.rel: Ghous Bakhsh Raisani, who followed him, is described as the first civilian Governor of Balochistan.

recs.q: Who served as Chief Adviser of Bangladesh's interim government from August 2024 until February 2026?
recs.facts: After Sheikh Hasina left in August 2024, Nobel laureate Dr Muhammad Yunus led the interim government as Chief Adviser. His term ended when Tarique Rahman became Prime Minister on 17 February 2026.
recs.rel: Today Bangladesh has an elected Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman, so there is no Chief Adviser now.

recs.q: On which date did Benazir Bhutto first become Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1988?
recs.facts: After the November 1988 elections her PPP was the largest party, and she took oath as Prime Minister on 2 December 1988.
recs.rel: She was the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.

recs.q: Who became Prime Minister of Pakistan after the death of General Zia ul Haq in 1988?
recs.facts: Zia died in a plane crash on 17 August 1988. Elections were held in November 1988 and Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in December 1988.
recs.rel: Ghulam Ishaq Khan, the Senate Chairman, became acting President after Zia's death.

recs.q: Who became Prime Minister of Pakistan in April 2022 after Imran Khan lost a no-confidence vote?
recs.facts: Imran Khan was removed by a no-confidence vote in the National Assembly on 10 April 2022, and Shehbaz Sharif was elected Prime Minister the next day.
recs.rel: Imran Khan was the first Pakistani Prime Minister removed through a no-confidence vote.

recs.q: In which month and year did the United States declare its independence?
recs.facts: The Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Continental Congress on 4 July 1776.
recs.rel: Britain formally recognised American independence in the Treaty of Paris in 1783.

recs.q: Which law governed the constitutional setup of British India just before independence in 1947?
recs.facts: The Government of India Act 1935 was the last major constitutional law of British India and was used with changes as Pakistan's interim constitution.
recs.rel: Pakistan worked under the amended 1935 Act until its first Constitution came in 1956.

recs.q: Between which two values do the sine and cosine functions always lie?
recs.facts: On the unit circle, sine and cosine are the y and x coordinates of a point, so they can never go below -1 or above 1.
recs.rel: Tangent, unlike sine and cosine, has no upper or lower limit.

recs.q: Complete the proverb: The early bird catches the ____.
recs.facts: The proverb says that a person who starts early gets the best chance of success, like a bird that finds the worm first.
recs.rel: A similar saying is Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.

recs.q: Why is milk boiled before drinking?
recs.facts: Heating milk to boiling point kills harmful bacteria and makes it safe to drink.
recs.rel: The process of heating milk to kill germs and then cooling it is named pasteurisation after Louis Pasteur.

recs.q: What is the name of the house in Karachi where Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born?
recs.facts: Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 at Wazir Mansion, Kharadar, Karachi.
recs.rel: Wazir Mansion is now a protected national monument and a museum.

recs.q: In a class of 30 students, 2/4 are boys. What percentage of the class are girls?
recs.facts: 2/4 of 30 is 15 boys, so girls are 30 minus 15 which is 15. Girls percentage is 15 divided by 30 times 100, which is 50 percent.
recs.rel: 2/4 is the same as 1/2, so half the class is girls.

recs.q: On which date did the Cabinet Mission arrive in India in 1946?
recs.facts: The British Cabinet Mission reached India on 24 March 1946 to discuss transfer of power.
recs.rel: It announced its plan on 16 May 1946, proposing a loose federation with three groups of provinces.

recs.q: What is the alimentary canal?
opts: The long tube of the digestive system from mouth to anus
The tube that carries air to the lungs
The vessel that carries blood to the heart
The tube that carries urine from the kidneys
recs.facts: The alimentary canal, also called the gut, runs from the mouth through the oesophagus, stomach and intestines to the anus, and digests and absorbs food.
recs.rel: The small intestine is where most absorption of food takes place.

recs.q: In which country is the Suez Canal located and which two seas does it join?
opts: Egypt; Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea
Egypt; Red Sea and Arabian Sea
Saudi Arabia; Red Sea and Persian Gulf
recs.facts: The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway in Egypt joining the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
recs.rel: It was opened in 1869 and shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia.

recs.q: What is the capital of Iraq?
recs.facts: Baghdad, on the River Tigris, is the capital and largest city of Iraq.
recs.rel: Baghdad was the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate from 762 CE.

recs.q: Which team has won the ICC Champions Trophy the most times?
recs.facts: India has won three titles: 2002 (shared with Sri Lanka), 2013 and 2025.
recs.rel: Pakistan won the Champions Trophy once, in 2017, beating India in the final.

recs.q: Which team won the ICC Champions Trophy in 2025?
recs.facts: India beat New Zealand in the final played in Dubai on 9 March 2025.
recs.rel: The 2025 tournament was hosted by Pakistan, but India played its matches in Dubai.

recs.q: What is the diameter of a unit circle?
recs.facts: A unit circle has radius 1, so its diameter is 2 times the radius, which is 2.
recs.rel: The circumference of a unit circle is 2 times pi.

recs.q: What is the circulatory system?
opts: The system that moves blood around the body
The system that controls breathing only
recs.facts: The circulatory system carries blood, oxygen and nutrients to all body parts and takes waste away.
recs.rel: William Harvey described blood circulation in 1628.

recs.q: What are the main parts of the human circulatory system?
recs.facts: The heart pumps blood, blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries) carry it, and blood is the fluid that moves in them.
recs.rel: Arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins bring it back.

recs.q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan in 1977?
recs.facts: General Zia ul Haq was Army Chief from 1976 and took over power through martial law on 5 July 1977.
recs.rel: He remained Army Chief until his death in August 1988.

recs.q: Complete the sentence: Practice makes us ____.
recs.facts: The saying is Practice makes perfect, meaning regular practice improves skill.
recs.rel: Another similar saying is Slow and steady wins the race.

recs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
opts: She did returned back from London.
recs.facts: Returned already means came back, so the word back is repeated and wrong (redundant).
recs.rel: Similar repeated phrases are reply back and revert back.

recs.q: Under which article of Pakistan's 1973 Constitution is a Qadiani (Ahmadi) defined as a non-Muslim?
recs.facts: Article 260(3) defines who is a Muslim and who is a non-Muslim. It was added by the Second Amendment of 1974.
recs.rel: The Second Constitutional Amendment was passed in September 1974 under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

recs.q: Which company first launched the PlayStation game console?
recs.facts: Sony Computer Entertainment launched the original PlayStation in Japan in December 1994.
recs.rel: Microsoft later entered the console market with the Xbox in 2001.

recs.q: On what date was the first session of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan held in Karachi?
recs.facts: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan met on 10 August 1947 in Karachi. On 11 August 1947 it elected Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as its President.
recs.rel: The Objectives Resolution was passed by this Assembly on 12 March 1949.

recs.q: What is the integral of cos inverse (1/x) with respect to x, for x greater in size than 1?
opts: x sec inverse(x) minus ln|x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)| + C
x sec inverse(x) plus ln|x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)| + C
x cos inverse(x) minus sqrt(1 - x^2) + C
sec inverse(x) divided by x + C
recs.facts: cos inverse(1/x) equals sec inverse(x). Integrating by parts, the integral of sec inverse(x) dx is x sec inverse(x) minus the integral of 1 / sqrt(x^2 - 1) dx, which gives x sec inverse(x) minus ln|x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)| + C.
recs.rel: The derivative of sec inverse(x) is 1 / (|x| sqrt(x^2 - 1)).

recs.q: In which country is the Amazon rainforest and most of the Amazon River basin located?
recs.facts: Brazil holds about 60 percent of the Amazon rainforest and most of the river basin.
recs.rel: The Amazon River flows into the Atlantic Ocean and carries the largest volume of water of any river.

recs.q: What does INTERPOL stand for in full?
recs.facts: INTERPOL is the International Criminal Police Organization, which helps police forces of its member countries to cooperate.
recs.rel: Its headquarters are in Lyon, France.

recs.q: If a man covers 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes, how much distance does he cover in 20 minutes at the same speed?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so speed is 20 / 100 = 0.2 km per minute. In 20 minutes he covers 0.2 x 20 = 4 km.
recs.rel: Speed in km per hour here is 12 km/h.

recs.q: If a train covers 100 km in 1 hour 40 minutes, how much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes. Distance per minute is 100 km / 100 minutes = 1 km.
recs.rel: The train's speed is 60 km per hour.

recs.q: Which two provinces were created when Lord Curzon divided Bengal in 1905?
opts: Eastern Bengal and Assam, and Western Bengal
recs.facts: The 1905 partition created the new Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam with Dhaka as capital, leaving Western Bengal with Calcutta.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911 after Hindu protests.

recs.q: What is the superlative degree of the adjective good?
recs.facts: Good is an irregular adjective: good, better, best. Best is the superlative form.
recs.rel: Better is the comparative degree.

recs.q: Which of these is a vector quantity, unlike speed?
recs.facts: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Speed has only magnitude, so it is a scalar.
recs.rel: Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

recs.q: On what date was SUPARCO established?
recs.facts: SUPARCO, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, was set up on 16 September 1961 with Dr Abdus Salam as its first head.
recs.rel: Pakistan launched its first rocket, Rehbar-I, in 1962.

recs.q: Which country is called the Cockpit of Europe?
recs.facts: Belgium has been the battlefield of many European wars, so it is called the Cockpit of Europe.
recs.rel: Its capital Brussels is also the headquarters of the European Union and NATO.

recs.q: After how many years did Pakistan host an ICC event again with the Champions Trophy in 2025?
recs.facts: Pakistan last hosted an ICC event in 1996 (the World Cup, shared with India and Sri Lanka). The 2025 Champions Trophy came 29 years later.
recs.rel: India played its matches in Dubai under a hybrid model.

recs.q: Finland is famous as a country of many what?
recs.facts: Finland is called the Land of a Thousand Lakes and has about 188,000 lakes.
recs.rel: Its capital is Helsinki.

recs.q: How many inches are in one foot?
recs.facts: One foot is defined as 12 inches.
recs.rel: One yard is 3 feet, which equals 36 inches.

recs.q: What is the full form of GDP?
recs.facts: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year.
recs.rel: GNP (Gross National Product) also counts income earned by citizens abroad.

recs.q: What is the full form of NEPRA in Pakistan?
opts: National Energy Production and Research Agency
National Electricity Pricing and Revenue Authority
recs.facts: NEPRA stands for National Electric Power Regulatory Authority, which regulates the power sector of Pakistan.
recs.rel: NEPRA was established in 1997 and its head office is in Islamabad.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the National Radio and Telecommunication Corporation (NRTC) of Pakistan?
recs.facts: NRTC is a defence production organisation based in Haripur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: In 2021 the government handed Telephone Industries of Pakistan over to NRTC.

recs.q: Who gave the Six Points formula of 1966 demanding autonomy for East Pakistan?
recs.facts: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman presented the Six Points at a conference of opposition parties in Lahore in February 1966.
recs.rel: The Six Points became the base of the Awami League movement that led to Bangladesh in 1971.

recs.q: In which year was UNESCO founded?
recs.facts: UNESCO was founded in 1945 when its constitution was adopted in London, as the United Nations agency for education, science and culture.
recs.rel: Its constitution came into force in November 1946 and its headquarters is in Paris.

recs.q: On which date is Human Rights Day observed every year?
recs.facts: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the day the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.
recs.rel: 24 October is United Nations Day.

recs.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the 3rd June Plan of 1947?
recs.facts: Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, announced the 3rd June Plan which proposed the partition of India.
recs.rel: He became the first Governor General of independent India after independence.

recs.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 took place in protest against which act?
recs.facts: People gathered in Amritsar to protest the Rowlatt Act, which allowed arrest without trial, and General Dyer fired on them.
recs.rel: The massacre took place on 13 April 1919.

recs.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919?
recs.facts: Lord Chelmsford was Viceroy and Governor General of India from 1916 to 1921.
recs.rel: Lord Reading succeeded him in 1921.

recs.q: What was the original name of the Mughal emperor Jahangir?
recs.facts: Jahangir was born as Prince Salim (Nur-ud-Din Muhammad Salim) and took the title Jahangir when he became emperor.
recs.rel: His son Prince Khurram later became Emperor Shah Jahan.

recs.q: What is the negative form of a past indefinite (simple past) sentence?
opts: Subject + did not + base form of verb
Subject + does not + base form of verb
Subject + was not + verb with ing
recs.facts: In the simple past, the negative is made with did not plus the first form of the verb, for example: He did not go.
recs.rel: Past indefinite verbs in the positive use the second form, such as went.

recs.q: If 4 June is Sunday, what day of the week will 15 June be?
recs.facts: From 4 June to 15 June is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the day is 4 days after Sunday, which is Thursday.
recs.rel: The days repeat every 7 days.

recs.q: Nanga Parbat is also known by which name?
recs.facts: Nanga Parbat is called Killer Mountain because of the many climbers who died on it in early attempts.
recs.rel: K2 is the one known as the Savage Mountain.

recs.q: In which year did Liaquat Ali Khan join the All India Muslim League?
recs.facts: Liaquat Ali Khan joined the Muslim League in 1923.
recs.rel: He became its General Secretary in 1936 and was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan.

recs.q: The McMahon Line is the border line between which two countries?
recs.facts: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 as the boundary between British India and Tibet and is now the disputed border of India and China in the east.
recs.rel: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

recs.q: The Himalayas mountain range is located in which continent?
recs.facts: The Himalayas stretch across Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and China, all in Asia.
recs.rel: The Himalayas contain Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world.

recs.q: What is the main source of the economy of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy because it employs a large share of the workforce and supports exports like cotton and rice.
recs.rel: Cotton, wheat, rice and sugarcane are Pakistan's major crops.

recs.q: Which resolution passed in March 1949 is regarded as the basis (foundation) of the constitutions of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Objectives Resolution laid down the guiding principles for Pakistan's constitution and later became its preamble.
recs.rel: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word "abhorrence"?
recs.facts: Abhorrence means a feeling of strong hatred or disgust towards something.
recs.rel: The verb form is "abhor", which means to hate strongly.

recs.q: What is the meaning of the word "sensible"?
recs.facts: Sensible describes a person or choice that shows good judgement and is practical.
recs.rel: Do not confuse it with "sensitive", which means easily hurt or affected.

recs.q: Who is the Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
recs.facts: Attaullah Tarar holds the information and broadcasting portfolio and was still in office in October 2026.
recs.rel: He was earlier Minister of State for Law and Justice.

recs.q: In which year did Martin Luther King Jr. receive the Nobel Prize?
recs.facts: Martin Luther King Jr. was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.
recs.rel: He was the youngest person to receive the Nobel Peace Prize at that time (aged 35).

recs.q: On which date did Martin Luther King Jr. receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo?
recs.facts: He received the prize in Oslo on 10 December 1964, which is Nobel Prize ceremony day.
recs.rel: His famous speech "I Have a Dream" was on 28 August 1963.

recs.q: Who started the Home Rule Movement in India in 1916?
opts: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
Sir Syed and Altaf Hussain Hali
recs.facts: Tilak launched his Home Rule League in April 1916 and Annie Besant launched hers in September 1916.
recs.rel: Its aim was self-government for India within the British Empire.

recs.q: In which year was the Muhammadan Educational Conference formed by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
recs.facts: Sir Syed formed the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886 to spread modern education among Muslims.
recs.rel: It held its first meeting at Aligarh.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: A1, C3, E5, G7, ?
recs.facts: Letters skip one each time (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is I9.
recs.rel: Alternating letter-number series are solved by finding the rule for letters and numbers separately.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, ?
recs.facts: Each term is double the previous one: 32 x 2 = 64.
recs.rel: This is a geometric series with common ratio 2.

recs.q: Which comes next in the series: A9, C12, E15, G18, ?
recs.facts: Letters skip one each time (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers go up by 3 (9, 12, 15, 18, 21). So the next term is I21.
recs.rel: In such series the letter rule and number rule are independent.

recs.q: Which number comes next: 112, 55, 225, 65, ?
recs.facts: This is two alternating series. Terms 1, 3, 5: 112, 225 (112 x 2 + 1), then 225 x 2 + 1 = 451. The other series is 55, 65 (plus 10).
recs.rel: When terms jump up and down, split the series into odd and even positions.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and Ahmad is twice his age. What will Ahmad's age be when Ali is 15?
recs.facts: Ahmad is 8 when Ali is 4, so he is 4 years older. When Ali is 15, Ahmad is 15 + 4 = 19.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people never changes.

recs.q: Which pair is the odd one out: CE, IJ, AC, GI, EG?
recs.facts: In CE, AC, GI and EG the second letter is 2 places after the first. In IJ, J is only 1 place after I, so IJ is odd.
recs.rel: Check the gap between letters in each pair to find the odd one.

recs.q: What is the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
opts: A military alliance of Western states
A group of states not formally aligned with any major power bloc
A trade union of oil producers
recs.facts: NAM is a group of states that chose not to join either the US-led or the Soviet-led bloc during the Cold War.
recs.rel: NAM was founded in Belgrade in 1961, after the 1955 Bandung conference.

recs.q: In the 1956 constitution of Pakistan, Urdu and which other language were given the status of national language?
recs.facts: The 1956 constitution made both Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The language issue was strong in East Pakistan, and the 1952 Language Movement was about Bengali.

recs.q: Alaska is part of which country?
recs.facts: Alaska is a state of the USA. The USA bought it from Russia in 1867.
recs.rel: Alaska became the 49th US state in 1959.

recs.q: Under the partition plan, what share of the cash balance of undivided India was agreed for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan's share of the cash balances was set at Rs 75 crore. India paid Rs 20 crore and withheld the remaining Rs 55 crore.
recs.rel: Gandhi fasted in January 1948 partly to press India to release the balance.

recs.q: What was the Partition of Bengal of 1905?
opts: Bengal was divided into East Bengal and Assam, and West Bengal, by Lord Curzon
Bengal was given to the French
Bengal was made a separate country
recs.facts: Viceroy Lord Curzon divided the Bengal Presidency into Eastern Bengal and Assam (capital Dhaka) and the rest of Bengal.
recs.rel: It was annulled in 1911 after strong Hindu protests.

recs.q: Which British Indian province was partitioned in 1905?
recs.facts: In 1905 the Bengal Presidency was split into two parts.
recs.rel: The partition was announced by Lord Curzon.

recs.q: What is a preposition?
opts: A word that shows the relation of a noun or pronoun with another word
A word that names a person
A word that describes a verb
A word that joins two sentences
recs.facts: A preposition shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word, for example in, on, at.
recs.rel: A preposition is normally followed by a noun or pronoun.

recs.q: Which is the busiest port of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Karachi Port handles the largest share of Pakistan's sea trade.
recs.rel: Port Qasim is the second major port and Gwadar is a deep sea port on the Makran coast.

recs.q: What is a polynomial?
opts: An expression with variables having whole number powers, joined by plus or minus signs
An expression with a variable in the denominator only
recs.facts: A polynomial is a sum of terms like a x to the power n, where n is a whole number, for example x^2 + 3x + 2.
recs.rel: The highest power of the variable is called the degree of the polynomial.

recs.q: Who was the first President of the United States?
recs.facts: George Washington was the first President of the USA, serving from 1789 to 1797.
recs.rel: John Adams was the second President.

recs.q: Which Iranian nuclear sites did the United States strike in June 2025?
recs.facts: On 21-22 June 2025 the US attacked the Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan nuclear sites in Operation Midnight Hammer.
recs.rel: It was the first combat use of the GBU-57 bunker-buster bomb, and Iran disputed the extent of damage.

recs.q: Which player has won the most men's singles titles at the Australian Open in the Open era?
recs.facts: Novak Djokovic has won the Australian Open 10 times, more than any other man in the Open era.
recs.rel: Carlos Alcaraz beat Djokovic in the 2026 final, so Djokovic's total stayed at 10.

recs.q: On what date did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
recs.facts: Malala was announced as a Nobel Peace Prize winner on 10 October 2014 and received the prize at the ceremony in Oslo on 10 December 2014.
recs.rel: She shared the 2014 prize with Kailash Satyarthi of India and is the youngest Nobel laureate ever.

recs.q: In which movement was Chaudhry Rehmat Ali mainly involved?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali was a student leader at Cambridge who worked for a separate Muslim homeland, which became the Pakistan Movement.
recs.rel: He coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.

recs.q: Where is the Sadpara Dam located?
recs.facts: Sadpara Dam is built on the Sadpara stream near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan.
recs.rel: It supplies drinking water to Skardu city and is near Sadpara Lake.

recs.q: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Senate of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 59 of the 1973 Constitution requires a Senate candidate to be at least 30 years old.
recs.rel: The minimum age for the National Assembly is 25 years.

recs.q: What are the values of sin 0 degrees and cos 0 degrees?
recs.facts: From the standard trigonometric table, sin 0 = 0 and cos 0 = 1.
recs.rel: Sin 90 = 1 and cos 90 = 0, which is the reverse.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 10 times his age. What will be Ali's age after 12 years?
recs.facts: Ali is 4 now, so after 12 years he will be 4 + 12 = 16 years old.
recs.rel: His sister's age after 12 years would be 40 + 12 = 52 years.

recs.q: A person bought a pen for Rs 20 and sold it for Rs 30. What is the percentage of profit?
recs.facts: Profit = 30 - 20 = Rs 10. Profit percent = 10 / 20 x 100 = 50 percent.
recs.rel: Profit percent is always calculated on the cost price.

recs.q: In Washington DC, what does DC stand for?
recs.facts: Washington DC is the capital of the USA and DC stands for District of Columbia.
recs.rel: The city is not part of any US state.

recs.q: What does ASRC stand for in the Pakistan Army?
recs.facts: ASRC is the centre where candidates for the Pakistan Army appear for the initial tests. Its full form is Army Selection and Recruitment Centre.
recs.rel: ISSB is the later selection board that tests officer candidates.

recs.q: What does CPU stand for in computing?
recs.facts: The CPU is the main chip that carries out instructions in a computer, so it is the Central Processing Unit.
recs.rel: It is often called the brain of the computer.

recs.q: What does U.A.E stand for?
recs.facts: U.A.E is the short form of United Arab Emirates, a country made of seven emirates.
recs.rel: Its capital is Abu Dhabi and its largest city is Dubai.

recs.q: How many types of swimming strokes are there in competitive swimming?
recs.facts: The four competitive strokes are freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.
recs.rel: The individual medley combines all four strokes in one race.

recs.q: Who introduced the Doctrine of Lapse in the subcontinent?
recs.facts: Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.
recs.rel: Under it, a princely state without a natural male heir was annexed by the British.

recs.q: In which continent is Sudan located?
recs.facts: Sudan lies in north-eastern Africa and borders Egypt and the Red Sea.
recs.rel: Its capital is Khartoum.

recs.q: What is the sum of the roots of the equation x^2 - 5x + 1 = 0?
recs.facts: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is -b/a. Here a = 1 and b = -5, so the sum is 5.
recs.rel: The product of the roots is c/a = 1.

recs.q: What is a synonym?
opts: A word with the opposite meaning
A word with a similar meaning to another word
A word that sounds the same but is spelled differently
recs.facts: A synonym is a word that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another word.
recs.rel: A word with the opposite meaning is called an antonym.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'vital'?
recs.facts: Vital means absolutely necessary, which is the meaning of essential.
recs.rel: Vital comes from the Latin word vita, meaning life.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'optimistic'?
recs.facts: An optimistic person expects good outcomes, so hopeful is the closest word.
recs.rel: The antonym of optimistic is pessimistic.

recs.q: What is the synonym of the word 'venerate'?
recs.facts: To venerate means to respect deeply, which is to revere.
recs.rel: Veneration is often used for saints, elders and religious figures.

recs.q: What type of government system does Pakistan follow?
recs.facts: Under the 1973 Constitution Pakistan is a federal parliamentary republic in which the Prime Minister heads the government.
recs.rel: The President is the ceremonial head of state.

recs.q: What do plants take in and release at night?
opts: They take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide
They take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen
They take in nitrogen and release oxygen
They take in hydrogen and release carbon dioxide
recs.facts: At night there is no light for photosynthesis, so plants only respire. They take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide.
recs.rel: During the day photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so plants release net oxygen.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: EH, AD, MP, QS?
recs.facts: Letter gaps: E to H is 3 (5 to 8), A to D is 3 (1 to 4), M to P is 3 (13 to 16), but Q to S is only 2 (17 to 19).
recs.rel: In odd-one-out letter pairs, always compare the gaps in alphabet positions.

recs.q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 11?
recs.facts: Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ali needs 8 more years to reach 11, so she will be 9 + 8 = 17.
recs.rel: The age gap between two people always stays the same over time.

recs.q: Umair is 5 years older than Amir, and Amir is 15 years old. How old will Umair be after 7 years?
recs.facts: Umair is 15 + 5 = 20 now. After 7 years he will be 20 + 7 = 27.
recs.rel: Add the years to the present age to find the future age.

recs.q: Who served as Prime Minister of Pakistan three times?
recs.facts: Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister in 1990, 1997 and 2013, so three terms.
recs.rel: Benazir Bhutto and Shehbaz Sharif each served twice as Prime Minister.

recs.q: Which male tennis player has won the most singles titles in the Open Era?
recs.facts: Jimmy Connors holds the record with 109 ATP singles titles. Federer has 103.
recs.rel: Djokovic has passed 100 titles and is third, so rankings by titles can change; sources differ on his exact count.

recs.q: What is the total area of Islamabad?
recs.facts: Islamabad Capital Territory covers about 906 square kilometres.
recs.rel: Islamabad became the capital of Pakistan in the 1960s, replacing Karachi.

recs.q: Is the flu (influenza) caused by a virus or by bacteria?
recs.facts: Influenza is caused by influenza viruses, not by bacteria.
recs.rel: Antibiotics do not work against viruses such as flu.

recs.q: How many vowels are in these letters: A, c, I, t, v, a, e, o, u?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, I, a, e, o, u, which makes 6. The letters c, t and v are consonants.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: How many vowels are there in AIUDAUOEZXBGH?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, I, U, A, U, O, E, which makes 7. D, Z, X, B, G and H are consonants.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has 5 vowels and 21 consonants.

recs.q: Which athlete has won the most Olympic gold medals in history?
recs.facts: American swimmer Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals, the most ever.
recs.rel: Phelps won 28 Olympic medals in total, also a record.

recs.q: Who wrote the book My Experiments with Truth?
recs.facts: My Experiments with Truth is the autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi.
recs.rel: It was first written in Gujarati and later translated into English.

recs.q: What is 2 + 2/1?
recs.facts: Division first: 2/1 = 2. Then 2 + 2 = 4.
recs.rel: By BODMAS, division is done before addition.

recs.q: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
recs.facts: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare in the 1590s.
recs.rel: Shakespeare also wrote Hamlet, Macbeth and Othello.

recs.q: Which currency is used in Denmark?
recs.facts: Denmark uses the Danish krone (DKK) and has not adopted the euro.
recs.rel: Sweden uses the Swedish krona and Norway the Norwegian krone.

recs.q: About how many people lived in the Gaza Strip before the war that began in October 2023?
recs.facts: Before October 2023 the Gaza Strip had around 2.1 to 2.2 million people, according to Palestinian and UN estimates.
recs.rel: Gaza is only about 365 square km, so it is one of the most densely populated places on earth; sources differ slightly on the exact number.

recs.q: Emperor Hirohito was the emperor of which country during World War II?
recs.facts: Hirohito was the emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989 and ruled during World War II.
recs.rel: Japan surrendered in August 1945 after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

recs.q: Who wrote the book The Story of the Malakand Field Force (1898)?
recs.facts: Winston Churchill wrote it as a young army officer and war correspondent after the 1897 Malakand campaign.
recs.rel: The book was Churchill's first published work on war.

recs.q: How many foci does an ellipse have?
recs.facts: An ellipse is defined by two fixed points called foci; the sum of distances from any point on it to the two foci is constant.
recs.rel: A circle is a special ellipse in which both foci coincide at the centre.

recs.q: Which cricketer scored 13,000 runs in One Day Internationals in 2023, doing it faster than anyone before?
recs.facts: Virat Kohli reached 13,000 ODI runs in September 2023 against Pakistan in the Asia Cup. He took only 267 innings, the fastest ever.
recs.rel: Sachin Tendulkar reached 13,000 ODI runs in 321 innings, which was the earlier record.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the Chief Justice of Pakistan appointed?
recs.facts: Article 175A deals with the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court, and it covers the appointment of the Chief Justice of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Article 175A was inserted by the 18th Amendment (2010) and changed by the 26th Amendment (October 2024), which lets a parliamentary committee pick the Chief Justice from the three senior-most judges.

recs.q: Which city was the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate?
recs.facts: The Abbasids moved the capital from Damascus to the new city of Baghdad, founded by Caliph al-Mansur in 762 AD.
recs.rel: The Umayyad Caliphate before them had its capital at Damascus.

recs.q: Which is the largest country of Africa by area?
recs.facts: Algeria has an area of about 2.38 million square km, the largest in Africa since South Sudan separated from Sudan in 2011.
recs.rel: Before 2011 Sudan was the largest country in Africa.

recs.q: The Rafah crossing connects the Gaza Strip with which country?
recs.facts: Rafah is the border crossing between the southern Gaza Strip and Egypt's Sinai region.
recs.rel: It is the only crossing of Gaza that does not open directly into Israel.

recs.q: Karl (Carl) Benz is known as the inventor of which machine?
recs.facts: Karl Benz built the Benz Patent-Motorwagen in 1885 to 1886, regarded as the first practical petrol-powered automobile.
recs.rel: The company he founded later joined Daimler to form Mercedes-Benz.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: She left her keys ___ the table.
recs.facts: Keys resting on a flat surface such as a table take the preposition on.
recs.rel: In is used for enclosed spaces, for example in the drawer.

recs.q: What is the name of the Pakistani military operation launched against India in May 2025?
recs.facts: Pakistan named its military response to India in May 2025 Bunyan-um-Marsoos.
recs.rel: The name means a solid structure, taken from a verse of the Quran (Surah As-Saff).

recs.q: Which country launched the Chandrayaan-3 mission in 2023?
recs.facts: India launched Chandrayaan-3 on 14 July 2023 and landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.
recs.rel: India became the first country to land near the south pole of the Moon.

recs.q: Who is known as the father of chemistry?
recs.facts: Jabir bin Hayyan (Geber) is called the father of chemistry in most Pakistani textbooks because of his early experimental work.
recs.rel: Some sources call Antoine Lavoisier the father of modern chemistry, so sources differ.

recs.q: What is the currency of Mongolia?
recs.facts: The currency of Mongolia is the tugrik (togrog), code MNT.
recs.rel: Its capital is Ulaanbaatar.

recs.q: Who is known as the Daughter of the East?
recs.facts: Daughter of the East is the title of the autobiography of Benazir Bhutto, and it is also used for her.
recs.rel: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman prime minister of a Muslim-majority country.

recs.q: In which city was the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) formed by signing the treaty in 1949?
recs.facts: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington DC on 4 April 1949.
recs.rel: NATO headquarters are today in Brussels, Belgium.

recs.q: Who were the founders of YouTube?
opts: Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim
recs.facts: YouTube was started in 2005 by three former PayPal employees: Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim.
recs.rel: Google bought YouTube in 2006.

recs.q: Which Pakistani athlete won an Olympic gold medal at Paris 2024 with a throw of 92.97 metres?
recs.facts: Arshad Nadeem won the javelin throw gold at Paris 2024 with an Olympic record of 92.97 metres.
recs.rel: It was Pakistan's first individual Olympic gold medal and its first Olympic gold since 1984.

recs.q: What is the length of the Gaza Strip?
recs.facts: The Gaza Strip is a narrow coastal strip about 41 km long and 6 to 12 km wide.
recs.rel: Its total area is roughly 365 square kilometres.

recs.q: Who won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work on mRNA vaccines?
recs.facts: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman for nucleoside base modifications that enabled effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19.
recs.rel: Their work made the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines possible.

recs.q: What are people who deny Allah and do not believe in Him called in Islamic terminology?
recs.facts: A Kafir is a person who rejects belief in Allah. A Munafiq is a hypocrite and a Fasiq is a sinner.
recs.rel: A Muttaqi is a God-fearing person.

recs.q: Who is the owner of X (formerly Twitter)?
recs.facts: Elon Musk bought Twitter in October 2022 and renamed it X in July 2023.
recs.rel: Jack Dorsey was a co-founder of Twitter.

recs.q: Which Pakistani scientist received the Khwarizmi International Award from Iran in 2024?
recs.facts: Prof Dr M. Raza Shah of the University of Karachi won the 37th Khwarizmi International Award, an Iranian science prize, in January 2024.
recs.rel: Dr Atta-ur-Rahman is another well-known Pakistani chemist and received the UNESCO Science Prize.

recs.q: Which country hosted the 2023 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Heads of State summit?
recs.facts: India chaired the SCO in 2023 and hosted the summit virtually in July 2023.
recs.rel: Pakistan hosted the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Islamabad in October 2024.

recs.q: A train covers 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
recs.facts: Speed = distance divided by time = 120 / 2 = 60 km/h.
recs.rel: To convert km/h into m/s, multiply by 5/18, so 60 km/h is about 16.7 m/s.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 12th of that month be?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 12th is 10 days. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days forward from Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday.
recs.rel: The same weekday repeats every 7 days, so the 2nd, 9th, 16th and 23rd are all Fridays here.

recs.q: What is 1369 x 1369?
recs.rel: 1369 is a perfect square, because 37 x 37 = 1369.

recs.q: What is 45% of 300?
How many parts does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan have?
recs.facts: The 1973 Constitution is divided into 12 parts, containing 280 articles and several schedules.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and came into force on 14 August 1973.

recs.q: What are the capitals of Australia, Canada and Japan, in that order?
recs.facts: The capital of Australia is Canberra, of Canada is Ottawa and of Japan is Tokyo.
recs.rel: Sydney, Toronto and Osaka are bigger or famous cities but they are not capitals.

recs.q: According to Pakistan's official stand, which city should be the capital of Palestine?
recs.facts: Pakistan supports a two-state solution with an independent Palestine on the pre-1967 borders and East Jerusalem (Al-Quds Al-Sharif) as its capital.
recs.rel: Ramallah is the administrative seat of the Palestinian Authority, but it is not the claimed capital.

recs.q: What is the chemical formula of the ammonium ion?
recs.facts: The ammonium ion is formed when ammonia (NH3) gains a hydrogen ion, giving NH4 with a positive charge.
recs.rel: Ammonium salts such as ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulphate are widely used as fertilizers.

recs.q: Which instrument is used to measure the area of an irregular figure on a map or drawing?
recs.facts: A planimeter is a mechanical instrument that measures area by tracing the outline of a shape.
recs.rel: An odometer measures distance travelled, and a hygrometer measures humidity.

recs.q: Army is to soldier as navy is to what?
recs.facts: A soldier is a member of the army, in the same way a sailor is a member of the navy.
recs.rel: A member of the air force is called an airman.

recs.q: Who is the author of the book On the Origin of Species?
recs.facts: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, explaining evolution by natural selection.
recs.rel: Alfred Russel Wallace developed a similar idea of natural selection independently.

recs.q: Who is the author of the political book The Prince?
recs.facts: The Prince was written by the Italian thinker Niccolo Machiavelli, around 1513.
recs.rel: The book advises rulers to be practical in politics, which gave rise to the word Machiavellian.

recs.q: What was the educational qualification of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
recs.facts: Jinnah studied law at Lincoln's Inn in London and qualified as a barrister at a very young age.
recs.rel: He was called to the Bar in 1896 and was among the youngest Indians to be a barrister.

recs.q: Who was Baba Bulleh Shah?
recs.facts: Baba Bulleh Shah (1680 to 1757) was a famous Sufi poet who wrote in Punjabi, known for his kafis.
recs.rel: His shrine is in Kasur, Punjab.

recs.q: Emperor Hirohito belonged to which country?
recs.facts: Hirohito was the Emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989, including the whole period of World War II.
recs.rel: His reign was the longest of any historical Japanese emperor.

recs.q: Which country was the top source of workers' remittances to Pakistan in 2024 and also in FY2026?
recs.facts: State Bank of Pakistan data show Saudi Arabia as the largest source, with about 9.78 billion US dollars in FY2026, ahead of the UAE at about 8.81 billion.
recs.rel: Total remittances reached a record of about 41.6 billion US dollars in FY2026.

recs.q: Who won the men's Ballon d'Or in 2023?
recs.facts: Lionel Messi won the 2023 Ballon d'Or, his eighth, after Argentina won the 2022 World Cup.
recs.rel: Ousmane Dembele is the reigning winner (2025), and the 2026 award is due on 26 October 2026.

recs.q: Is the area of a figure always positive or negative?
recs.facts: Area measures the size of a surface, so it is always a positive quantity.
recs.rel: Area is measured in square units such as square metres.

recs.q: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee all belong to which group of animals?
recs.facts: Monkeys, apes and chimpanzees are all members of the order Primates.
recs.rel: Humans also belong to the primates.

recs.q: Which is the biggest country in the world by population?
recs.facts: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, with more than 1.4 billion people.
recs.rel: China was the most populous country until 2022, and Pakistan ranks among the top six.

recs.q: Fill in the blank with a preposition: He is kind ___ slaves.
recs.facts: The adjective kind takes the preposition to, so the correct phrase is kind to.
recs.rel: Similar adjective-preposition pairs are cruel to, good at and fond of.

recs.q: Fill in the blank: They said that Adil ___ ill.
recs.facts: The reporting verb said is in the past tense, so the reported clause also moves to the past: was.
recs.rel: In reported speech, present tense usually shifts one step back into the past tense.

recs.q: In which year did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests at Chagai?
recs.facts: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills on 28 May 1998, after India tested in May 1998.
recs.rel: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

recs.q: Who wrote the book The Republic?
recs.facts: The Republic is a famous philosophical work written by the Greek philosopher Plato.
recs.rel: Plato was a student of Socrates and the teacher of Aristotle.

recs.q: What are the capital and currency of Mexico?
recs.facts: The capital of Mexico is Mexico City and its currency is the Mexican peso (MXN).
recs.rel: Mexico City is one of the largest cities in North America.

recs.q: Who was the captain of the Pakistan ODI cricket team at the 2023 World Cup?
recs.facts: Babar Azam captained Pakistan in ODIs at the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and resigned as captain after it.
recs.rel: The current ODI captain is different from Babar Azam, so the 2023 answer is not the answer for today.

recs.q: The speed of a train is twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 60 km in 30 minutes. How many km does the train cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Car speed = 60 km in half an hour = 120 km/h. Train speed = 2 x 120 = 240 km/h, so in 30 minutes it covers 120 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time.

recs.q: A car runs at 90 km/h and the train runs at double the car speed. How much distance does the train cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 180 / 2 = 90 km.
recs.rel: To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: Parents send their children to school.
opts: Children were sent to school by their parents.
Children are sent to school by their parents.
Children is sent to school by parents.
Children have been sent to school by their parents.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive uses are plus the past participle: are sent.
recs.rel: Passive form for the simple present is: is/am/are plus past participle.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: They constructed a wall.
opts: A wall is constructed by them.
A wall has been constructed by them.
A wall was constructed by them.
A wall were constructed by them.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: was constructed.
recs.rel: Passive form for the simple past is: was/were plus past participle.

recs.q: Change into passive voice: We boil the milk.
opts: The milk was boiled by us.
The milk is boiled by us.
The milk is being boiled by us.
recs.facts: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive is: The milk is boiled by us.
recs.rel: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.

recs.q: Which ray is negatively charged?
recs.facts: Beta rays are streams of electrons, so they carry a negative charge.
recs.rel: Alpha rays are positively charged helium nuclei, and gamma rays have no charge.

recs.q: Hen is to chicken as cow is to what?
recs.facts: A chicken is the young one of a hen, and a calf is the young one of a cow.
recs.rel: A lamb is the young of a sheep, a foal of a horse and a kid of a goat.

recs.q: What is the name of the border between India and China?
recs.facts: The effective border between India and China is called the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
recs.rel: The McMahon Line is the traditional boundary in the eastern sector.

recs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
opts: Ali runs more faster than Akram.
Ali runs most faster than Akram.
recs.facts: Faster is already a comparative, so more must not be added before it.
recs.rel: Double comparatives such as more better or more faster are always wrong.

recs.q: What is the correct indirect speech of: He said, "We won the match."?
opts: He said that they won the match.
He said that they had won the match.
He said that we had won the match.
He said that they have won the match.
recs.facts: We changes to they, and the simple past won changes to the past perfect had won.
recs.rel: In indirect speech after a past reporting verb, the simple past becomes the past perfect.

recs.q: What is the least count of a standard screw gauge?
recs.facts: A standard screw gauge has a pitch of 1 mm and 100 circular divisions, so least count = 1 / 100 = 0.01 mm.
recs.rel: A vernier caliper usually has a least count of 0.1 mm.

recs.q: Which country won the Cricket World Cup in 1992?
recs.facts: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.
recs.rel: It remains Pakistan's only ODI World Cup title.

recs.q: How many days are there in a week?
recs.facts: A week has seven days, Monday to Sunday.
recs.rel: A normal year has 52 weeks and one extra day.

recs.q: What is a poem written on the death of a beloved person or friend called?
recs.facts: A poem of mourning written for someone who has died is called an elegy.
recs.rel: An ode praises a person or thing, and a sonnet has fourteen lines.

recs.q: What is the definition of a radian?
opts: The angle at the centre of a circle made by an arc equal in length to the radius
The angle made by an arc equal to the diameter
The angle of a full circle
recs.facts: One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length equals the radius.
recs.rel: A full circle is 2 pi radians, which equals 360 degrees.

recs.q: Torque depends on which two quantities?
opts: Force and distance from the axis
recs.facts: Torque is force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.
recs.rel: The SI unit of torque is the newton metre.

recs.q: Which one is different from the rest: Mango, Carrot, Apple, Banana?
recs.facts: Mango, apple and banana are fruits, while carrot is a vegetable.
recs.rel: Carrot is a root vegetable rich in vitamin A.

recs.q: Who discovered hydrogen?
recs.facts: Henry Cavendish identified hydrogen as a distinct substance in 1766.
recs.rel: Lavoisier later gave hydrogen its name.

recs.q: What is the unit of acceleration due to gravity?
recs.facts: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time, so its unit is metre per second squared.
recs.rel: Near Earth's surface g is about 9.8 m/s squared.

recs.q: What is the biggest source of fresh water on Earth?
recs.facts: About two thirds of the world's fresh water is locked in glaciers and ice caps.
recs.rel: Only about 3 percent of all water on Earth is fresh water.

recs.q: On which sector does the economy of Pakistan mainly depend?
recs.facts: Agriculture is the largest employer and the backbone of Pakistan's economy, with cotton, wheat and rice as major crops.
recs.rel: Textiles, based on cotton, are the largest export sector.

recs.q: What is the degree (highest power) of a quadratic equation?
recs.facts: A quadratic equation has the form ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, so its highest power is 2.
recs.rel: A quadratic equation has at most two roots.

recs.q: Which country issued the world's first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, in 1840?
recs.facts: The Penny Black was issued in Great Britain in May 1840.
recs.rel: Pakistan issued its first postage stamps in 1947.

recs.q: In which year was the Palestinian group Hamas founded?
recs.facts: Hamas was founded in 1987 during the first Palestinian intifada.
recs.rel: The Palestine Liberation Organization was founded earlier, in 1964.

recs.q: In which year was the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) founded?
recs.facts: The PLO was founded in 1964 at a meeting of the Arab League in Jerusalem.
recs.rel: Hamas was founded much later, in 1987.

recs.q: Where was the G20 summit of 2023 held, and where was the one of 2025 held?
opts: Rio de Janeiro, then New Delhi
recs.facts: The 2023 summit was in New Delhi, India, and the 2025 summit was in Johannesburg, South Africa.
recs.rel: It was the first G20 summit held on African soil.

recs.q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2024?
recs.facts: The 2024 G20 summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
recs.rel: Brazil held the G20 presidency from December 2023 to November 2024.

recs.q: In which sport is the word love used for a zero score?
recs.facts: In tennis, a score of zero is called love.
recs.rel: Other tennis scores run 15, 30, 40 and then game.

recs.q: How many general seats are there in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: After the merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the National Assembly has 266 general seats, plus 60 women and 10 minority seats.
recs.rel: The total strength is 336 seats; before the merger it was 342 with 272 general seats.

recs.q: Who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023?
recs.facts: The 2023 Nobel Peace Prize went to Narges Mohammadi of Iran for her fight against the oppression of women.
recs.rel: She was jailed in Iran at the time of the award.

recs.q: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2023?
recs.facts: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the Norwegian writer Jon Fosse.
recs.rel: Annie Ernaux of France won in 2022.

recs.q: Which country hosted the Hajj in 2024?
recs.facts: Hajj is performed in Makkah and nearby places in Saudi Arabia, which hosts it every year.
recs.rel: Hajj 2024 took place in June 2024.

recs.q: What is the highest temperature officially recorded in Pakistan, at Turbat in 2017?
recs.facts: Turbat in Balochistan recorded 53.7 C on 28 May 2017, accepted as Pakistan's highest reliable temperature.
recs.rel: Jacobabad is commonly known as the hottest city of Pakistan.

recs.q: Which country hosted the COP28 climate summit in 2023?
recs.facts: COP28 was held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, from November to December 2023.
recs.rel: COP27 was in Egypt in 2022 and COP29 in Azerbaijan in 2024.

recs.q: Which country brought a genocide case against Israel before the International Court of Justice in December 2023?
recs.facts: South Africa filed the case at the ICJ in December 2023, under the Genocide Convention.
recs.rel: The ICJ sits in The Hague, Netherlands.

recs.q: Which international organization's 1947 partition plan (Resolution 181) paved the way for the creation of Israel?
recs.facts: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181 in November 1947, proposing separate Arab and Jewish states.
recs.rel: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948.

recs.q: Who is the Supreme Leader of Iran as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Ali Khamenei was killed on 28 February 2026, and the Assembly of Experts chose his son Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader in March 2026.
recs.rel: Ali Khamenei had held the post since 1989; Masoud Pezeshkian is the President, not the Supreme Leader.

recs.q: Which of these countries became a full member of BRICS in January 2024?
recs.facts: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined BRICS as full members on 1 January 2024.
recs.rel: Indonesia joined later, in January 2025.

recs.q: What does KPK stand for?
recs.facts: KPK is the short form of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a province of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The province was renamed from North-West Frontier Province in 2010.

recs.q: What is the approximate area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
recs.facts: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa covers about 101,741 square kilometres.
recs.rel: Balochistan is the largest province, with about 347,190 sq km.

recs.q: Which is the largest city of Israel by population?
recs.facts: Jerusalem has the largest population of any Israeli city, about one million people.
recs.rel: Tel Aviv is the largest commercial centre, and most countries keep their embassies there.

recs.q: What does Newton's second law of motion state?
opts: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
A body stays at rest unless a force acts on it
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
recs.facts: Newton's second law says F = ma: the force on a body equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration.
recs.rel: The unit of force, the newton, is named after him.

recs.q: Which letter is missing in the sequence A, E, I, __, U?
recs.facts: The sequence lists the English vowels in order: A, E, I, O, U.
recs.rel: The English alphabet has five vowels.

recs.q: Which is the lightest metal?
recs.facts: Lithium has the lowest density of all metals, about 0.53 g per cubic centimetre.
recs.rel: Lithium is used in rechargeable batteries.

recs.q: What is the value of log 100 to base 10?
recs.facts: Since 10 raised to the power 2 equals 100, log 100 = 2.
recs.rel: The common logarithm of 10 is 1.

recs.q: What is the value of log of 60 to the base 4, to two decimal places?
recs.facts: log4(60) = ln 60 divided by ln 4 = 4.0943 divided by 1.3863, which is about 2.95. It lies between 2 (log4 16) and 3 (log4 64).
recs.rel: log4(64) is exactly 3, so log4(60) must be a little less than 3.

recs.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach the Earth?
recs.facts: The Sun is about 150 million km away and light travels at about 300,000 km per second. This gives about 500 seconds, or 8 minutes 20 seconds.
recs.rel: Moonlight takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth.

recs.q: What is the property of a skew-symmetric matrix A?
opts: A transpose equals the inverse of A
recs.facts: A matrix is skew-symmetric when its transpose is the negative of itself, A^T = -A. Because of this all its diagonal elements are zero.
recs.rel: A transpose equal to A is the property of a symmetric matrix.

recs.q: What does the word 'optimistic' mean?
recs.facts: An optimistic person has a positive outlook and expects good outcomes.
recs.rel: The opposite of optimistic is pessimistic.

recs.q: If Ali's sister is your mother, then what is Ali to you?
recs.facts: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mama). Ali is the brother of your mother, so he is your maternal uncle.
recs.rel: A father's brother is called a paternal uncle (chacha).

recs.q: In which country does the Kanchenjunga mountain lie?
opts: On the border of India and Nepal
recs.facts: Kanchenjunga lies on the border between Nepal and Sikkim (India) in the Himalayas.
recs.rel: At 8,586 m it is the third highest mountain in the world after Everest and K2.

recs.q: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
recs.facts: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889.
recs.rel: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa.

recs.q: Which is the largest country in North America by area?
recs.facts: Canada is about 9.98 million square km, slightly larger than the United States, and the largest country in North America.
recs.rel: Canada is the second-largest country in the world after Russia.

recs.q: Why has Pakistan not recognised Israel?
opts: It supports Palestinian rights and wants a Palestinian state first
Because Israel is too far away
Because of a border war with Israel
recs.facts: Pakistan says it will not recognise Israel until a fair solution gives Palestinians an independent state based on the 1967 borders with Al-Quds as capital.
recs.rel: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah also opposed the creation of Israel.

recs.q: Is zero included in the natural numbers? Choose the textbook answer.
recs.facts: Natural numbers are counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. Adding zero gives the whole numbers.
recs.rel: Some modern books include zero in natural numbers, so definitions differ.

recs.q: What is the difference between rational and irrational numbers?
opts: A rational number can be written as p over q, an irrational number cannot
A rational number has no decimals
An irrational number is always negative
Rational numbers are always whole numbers
recs.facts: Rational numbers can be written as a fraction p over q with q not zero. Irrational numbers like root 2 and pi cannot, and their decimals never end or repeat.
recs.rel: The square root of 2 was among the first numbers proven irrational.

recs.q: Ali is six years older than his sister. When Ali's sister is 12 years old, how old is Ali?
recs.facts: Ali's age is the sister's age plus 6, so 12 + 6 = 18 years.
recs.rel: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: How many medals did Pakistan win at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
recs.facts: Pakistan won one medal, the gold medal of Arshad Nadeem in javelin throw.
recs.rel: Arshad Nadeem threw an Olympic record 92.97 m.

recs.q: Out of 1500 students, 1340 are male. What is the percentage of females?
recs.rel: Male students are 89.33% of the total.

recs.q: What was the name of Pakistan's military operation against India in May 2025, in reply to India's Operation Sindoor?
recs.facts: Pakistan named its response Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos, meaning a wall of lead.
recs.rel: Swift Retort was the name used for the February 2019 response.

recs.q: The Simla Agreement of 1972 between Pakistan and India took place after which war?
recs.facts: The Simla Agreement was signed after the 1971 war that led to the creation of Bangladesh.
recs.rel: It was signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.

recs.q: Who is generally called the pioneer of Artificial Intelligence, having coined the term in 1956?
recs.facts: John McCarthy coined the term Artificial Intelligence at the 1956 Dartmouth conference.
recs.rel: Alan Turing is also called a founder of AI for his earlier work.

recs.q: Where is the deepest point of the Pacific Ocean?
recs.facts: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,900 m deep, the deepest known point of the oceans.
recs.rel: The Mariana Trench lies in the western Pacific near Guam.

recs.q: What is the present status of Palestine at the United Nations?
recs.facts: Since 2012 Palestine has been a non-member observer state at the UN. Full membership is blocked in the Security Council by a US veto.
recs.rel: In May 2024 the General Assembly gave Palestine extra rights, but not a vote.

recs.q: Which Palestinian organisation is resisting Israel and controls the Gaza Strip?
recs.facts: Hamas is a Palestinian group that has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007.
recs.rel: Hezbollah is based in Lebanon.

recs.q: Which country gives the most military aid to Israel?
recs.facts: The United States is the largest provider of military aid to Israel, about 3.8 billion dollars each year under a 2016 agreement.
recs.rel: Germany is usually named as the second-largest arms supplier.

recs.q: Which border did Pakistan support for a Palestinian state at the UN?
opts: The 1967 borders with Al-Quds as capital
recs.facts: Pakistan supports a two-state solution with an independent Palestine on pre-1967 borders and Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
recs.rel: The Six-Day War of 1967 led to Israel occupying the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem.

recs.q: What did Pakistan demand at the UN for Palestine and Gaza?
recs.facts: Pakistan has repeatedly demanded an immediate and lasting ceasefire in Gaza and humanitarian aid.
recs.rel: Pakistan has been a vocal supporter of Palestine at the OIC and UN.

recs.q: Which letter and number come next in the series: B3, D5, F7, ?
recs.facts: Letters move by two (B, D, F, H, J) and numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So the next term is H9, followed by J11.
recs.rel: Such series follow two patterns at once, one for letters and one for numbers.

recs.q: Z=3, X=5, V=7, T=9. What comes next?
recs.facts: Letters go back by two (Z, X, V, T, R) and numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So next is R=11.
recs.rel: The letters skipped are Y, W, U and S.

recs.q: Who is the President of the State of Palestine (Palestinian Authority) as of October 2026?
recs.facts: Mahmoud Abbas has been President of the Palestinian Authority since 2005 and was re-elected Fatah leader in May 2026. Presidential elections have been announced for 2027 but may be delayed.
recs.rel: Abbas is also known as Abu Mazen and leads the Fatah movement.

recs.q: What is the system called in which one person holds absolute power over a country?
recs.facts: In an autocracy, one person has unlimited power and is not bound by elections or a legislature. A monarchy can be an autocracy only if the monarch rules absolutely.
recs.rel: Rule by a small group is called oligarchy, while rule by the people is democracy.

recs.q: If 15 pencils cost Rs 175, what is the price of 12 pencils?
recs.facts: Price of 12 pencils = 175 x 12 / 15 = 2100 / 15 = Rs 140.
recs.rel: This is a direct proportion question: fewer items cost proportionally less.

recs.q: A man buys a pen for Rs 30 and sells it at a 40 percent profit. What is the selling price?
recs.facts: Profit = 40 percent of 30 = 12 rupees. Selling price = 30 + 12 = Rs 42.
recs.rel: Selling price = cost price x (100 + profit percent) / 100.

recs.q: Which two regions does the Khunjerab Pass connect?
recs.facts: The Khunjerab Pass lies on the Karakoram Highway and links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.
recs.rel: At about 4,693 metres it is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

recs.q: In which province of Pakistan is the Warsak Dam situated?
recs.facts: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar, which is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
recs.rel: It was built in the 1960s with Canadian help under the Colombo Plan.

recs.q: How many vowel letters are in the series: A b d A U C M A u E?
recs.facts: The vowels are A, A, U, A, u and E, which makes 6.
recs.rel: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

recs.q: Who was the first woman Governor of Sindh?
recs.facts: Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan became Governor of Sindh in 1973, the first woman to hold the post in Pakistan.
recs.rel: She was the wife of Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan.

recs.q: Solve for x: 4x + 5 = 6.
recs.rel: Always move the constant to the other side first, then divide by the coefficient of x.

recs.q: On which date did the current Gaza war begin?
recs.facts: The war began on 7 October 2023 after Hamas attacked southern Israel and Israel launched a military campaign in Gaza.
recs.rel: A ceasefire framework was agreed in October 2025, but fighting and disputes continued afterwards.

recs.q: What are the capital and currency of the United States?
recs.facts: The capital of the United States is Washington D.C. and its currency is the US Dollar (USD).
recs.rel: Washington D.C. is named after the first President, George Washington.

recs.q: What are the capital and currency of the United Kingdom?
recs.facts: The capital of the United Kingdom is London and its currency is the Pound Sterling (GBP).
recs.rel: The pound is one of the oldest currencies still in use in the world.

recs.q: What is the Sun?
recs.facts: The Sun is a star, a huge glowing ball of hot gas that produces energy by nuclear fusion.
recs.rel: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres from the Earth.

recs.q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 12 years old?
recs.facts: The sister is 12 when Ali is 4, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 12 she will be 12 + 8 = 20.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

recs.q: Which billionaire bought Twitter, which was later renamed X?
recs.facts: Elon Musk bought Twitter in October 2022 for about 44 billion US dollars and renamed it X in 2023.
recs.rel: Musk is also the head of Tesla and SpaceX.

recs.q: What is the SI unit of the modulus of elasticity (Young's modulus)?
recs.facts: Young's modulus is stress divided by strain. Strain has no unit, so the unit is that of stress, N/m squared, called the pascal.
recs.rel: Strain itself is a pure ratio and has no unit.

recs.q: Which isotope is used to treat goiter and thyroid disorders?
recs.facts: The thyroid gland absorbs iodine, so radioactive iodine-131 is used to shrink an overactive thyroid or goiter.
recs.rel: Cobalt-60 is used mainly in cancer radiotherapy.

recs.q: A man walks 20 km in 40 minutes. How long does he take to walk 1 km?
recs.facts: Time per km = 40 / 20 = 2 minutes.
recs.rel: Speed here is 30 km per hour.

recs.q: Whom did the British blame most for the War of 1857?
recs.facts: After 1857 the British held the Muslims mainly responsible, as the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar had led the revolt.
recs.rel: Muslims paid a heavy price, and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind to explain the causes.

recs.q: If 5 men complete a piece of work in 11 days, how many days will 1 man take to do it?
recs.facts: Total work = 5 x 11 = 55 man-days. One man needs 55 days.
recs.rel: Fewer workers need proportionally more days, which is inverse proportion.

recs.q: Who wrote the science fiction novel Dune?
recs.facts: Dune was written by the American author Frank Herbert and published in 1965.
recs.rel: Frank Patrick Herbert Jr. wrote several sequels to Dune.

recs.q: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Claudia Goldin for her work on what?
recs.facts: Claudia Goldin was honoured for improving our understanding of women's earnings and labour market participation over the centuries.
recs.rel: She was the third woman to win the economics Nobel prize.

recs.q: Which country won the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2023?
recs.facts: Spain beat England 1-0 in the 2023 final held in Sydney, Australia.
recs.rel: It was Spain's first women's World Cup title, and the 2023 event was co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand.

recs.q: Rearrange the letters BUYAET to form a word. What is the last letter of the word?
recs.facts: The letters BUYAET form the word BEAUTY, which ends with the letter Y.
recs.rel: Unscrambling words is a common verbal intelligence question.

recs.q: For what work was the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded?
opts: Nucleoside base modifications that enabled mRNA vaccines against COVID-19
recs.facts: Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman won it for discoveries about nucleoside base modifications that made effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 possible.
recs.rel: Their work helped develop the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna vaccines.

recs.q: A rectangle has a width of 8 and a length of 4. What is its area?
recs.facts: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 4 x 8 = 32.
recs.rel: Perimeter of this rectangle would be 2 x (4 + 8) = 24.

recs.q: Into which river does the Ravi River fall?
recs.facts: The Ravi joins the Chenab near Ahmad Pur Sial in Punjab, Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Chenab later joins the Sutlej and then the Indus.

recs.q: Boat is to water as aeroplane is to what?
recs.facts: A boat moves through water, and an aeroplane moves through air, the medium it travels in.
recs.rel: Analogy questions test the same relation in both pairs.

recs.q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place in India?
recs.facts: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district. A mob burned a police station, after which Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
recs.rel: The Non-Cooperation Movement was suspended soon after the incident.

recs.q: If AX = B, where A is an invertible matrix, what is X?
recs.facts: Multiply both sides on the left by the inverse of A. This gives (A inverse)(A)X = (A inverse)B, so X = A inverse times B.
recs.rel: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so the order of A inverse and B matters.

recs.q: What is the value of (x^2 times x^2) divided by x^2?
recs.facts: x^2 times x^2 = x^4 by adding powers. Then x^4 divided by x^2 = x^2 by subtracting powers.
recs.rel: When multiplying powers of the same base you add exponents, and when dividing you subtract them.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 square root 8 plus 3 square root 8?
recs.facts: Both terms have the same radical, so add the coefficients: 2 + 3 = 5. The result is 5 square root 8, which equals 10 square root 2.
recs.rel: Only like radicals (same number under the root) can be added directly.

recs.q: What is 70% of 70?
What is 90% of 90?
recs.rel: 10% of 90 is 9, so 90% is 90 minus 9 = 81.

recs.q: What is one-third of 10% of 120?
recs.facts: 10% of 120 = 12, and one-third of 12 = 4.
recs.rel: 10% of a number is the number divided by 10.

recs.q: What is one-third of 10% of 90?
recs.facts: 10% of 90 = 9, and one-third of 9 = 3.
recs.rel: One-third of a number is the number divided by 3.

recs.q: What is one-fourth of 120?
recs.facts: 120 divided by 4 = 30.
recs.rel: One-fourth is the same as 25%.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what will be the 24th day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days; 20 mod 7 = 6, and Monday plus 6 days = Sunday.
recs.rel: A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart fall on the same weekday.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what will be the 23rd day of that month?
recs.facts: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days = exactly 3 weeks, so the day is again Sunday.
recs.rel: Dates 7, 14 or 21 days apart share the same weekday.

recs.q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of the sister when the boy is 11 years old?
recs.facts: Sister is 9 when the boy is 3, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11, she is 11 + 6 = 17.
recs.rel: The age difference between two people never changes.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present and absent students?
recs.facts: 1200/1500 x 100 = 80% present, so absent = 300 students = 20%.
recs.rel: If 1300 were present, the percentage would be 86.67% present.

recs.q: Amjad and Ahmad kept 25 balls. Amjad kept 4 times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
recs.facts: Let Ahmad have x; then x + 4x = 25, so x = 5 (Amjad has 20).
recs.rel: Total shares = 1 + 4 = 5, and 25 divided by 5 = 5.

recs.q: Ali bought a pen for Rs. 30 and sold it for Rs. 40. What is his profit percentage?
recs.rel: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

recs.q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, how much time will he take to cover 1 km?
recs.facts: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100/90 = 10/9 minutes, about 1.11 minutes.
recs.rel: His speed is 90 km per 100 minutes, i.e. 54 km per hour.

recs.q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, in how many minutes will 1 man write 1 page?
recs.facts: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 men x 5 minutes gives 5 pages, one page per man).
recs.rel: Rate per man is 1 page per 5 minutes.

recs.q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed = 120 km/h; in half an hour it covers 60 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time.

recs.q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the number of women?
recs.rel: Women are 1/3 of the passengers.

recs.q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the oldest?
recs.facts: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Umair is the oldest.
recs.rel: Chain comparisons can be written as a single ordered line.

recs.q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
recs.facts: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Ahmad is the youngest.
recs.rel: The person who is older than nobody in the chain is the youngest.

recs.q: Ali moves towards the north, after some time he turns left, then again turns left. What is his present direction?
recs.facts: Facing north, a left turn gives west, and another left turn gives south.
recs.rel: Two left turns (or two right turns) reverse the direction.

recs.q: A man walked towards the north, then he turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
recs.facts: North, left turn gives west, right turn from west gives north again.
recs.rel: A left turn followed by a right turn cancel each other.

recs.q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word MANAGEMENT when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
recs.facts: Sorted letters: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The 3rd letter is E.
recs.rel: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.

recs.q: What will be the 3rd letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
recs.facts: Sorted letters: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U. The 3rd letter is E.
recs.rel: AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E repeated twice.

recs.q: The jumbled word UTYEAB is rearranged to form a word. What will be the last letter of that word when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
recs.facts: UTYEAB forms BEAUTY. Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.
recs.rel: Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet, the highest letter in this word.

recs.q: Arrange the jumbled word OPERALD to form a word and identify its category.
recs.facts: OPERALD rearranges to LEOPARD, a big wild cat.
recs.rel: The leopard is a member of the big cat family.

recs.q: According to the dictionary order, which word comes first: MOUNTAIN, MARGALLA, MACHINE?
recs.facts: All start with M; the second letters A, A, O put Mountain last. Between MACHINE and MARGALLA, C comes before R, so Machine is first.
recs.rel: Dictionary order compares letter by letter from the left.

recs.q: What comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
recs.facts: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9: 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.
recs.rel: The gaps are consecutive odd numbers.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Maize.
recs.facts: Wheat, rice and maize are food grains for humans, while hay is dried grass used as animal fodder.
recs.rel: Wheat is the main staple crop of Pakistan.

recs.q: Find the odd one out: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda.
recs.facts: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.
recs.rel: Chimpanzees are apes, not monkeys.

recs.q: If my brother's sister is your mother, who am I to you (taking me as a male)?
recs.facts: My brother's sister is also my sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, your maternal uncle.
recs.rel: Mother's brother is Mamu; father's brother is Chacha.

recs.q: The sister of my brother's son is my what?
recs.facts: My brother's son is my nephew; his sister is my brother's daughter, i.e. my niece.
recs.rel: A nephew is a brother's or sister's son; a niece is a daughter.

recs.q: Vehicle is to wheels as Sound is to ?
recs.facts: A vehicle moves by means of wheels, and sound travels by means of waves.
recs.rel: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because it needs a medium for its waves.

recs.q: Water is to flow as Air is to ?
recs.facts: Water flows and air blows.
recs.rel: Moving air is called wind.

recs.q: A bat cannot see well and a snake cannot ?
recs.facts: The analogy is a sense that the animal lacks; snakes have no outer ears and are largely deaf to airborne sound.
recs.rel: Snakes sense ground vibrations and smell with their forked tongue.

recs.q: How many months of the year have 31 days?
recs.facts: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days.
recs.rel: February has 28 or 29 days; April, June, September and November have 30.

recs.q: What is the value of 3P2 (3 permutation 2)?
recs.rel: nPr = n!/(n-r)!

recs.q: What is the area of a rectangle whose width is 3 and height is 8?
recs.facts: Area = width x height = 3 x 8 = 24.
recs.rel: Perimeter of this rectangle would be 2(3 + 8) = 22.

recs.q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
recs.facts: A triangular prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces, 5 in total.
recs.rel: It has 9 edges and 6 vertices.

recs.q: What is the eccentricity of a parabola?
recs.facts: A parabola is the conic section with eccentricity exactly 1.
recs.rel: Circle e = 0, ellipse e less than 1, hyperbola e greater than 1.

recs.q: The probability of an event always lies between which values?
