recs.facts: Probability is 0 for an impossible event and 1 for a certain event; all others lie in between.
recs.rel: Probabilities are sometimes expressed as percentages from 0% to 100%.

recs.q: Which city is known as the heart of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Lahore is commonly called the heart of Pakistan (and the cultural capital).
recs.rel: Lahore is the capital of Punjab and is also called the City of Gardens.

recs.q: What was the earlier capital of Pakistan before Islamabad?
recs.facts: Karachi was the first capital from 1947; Rawalpindi was temporary capital and Islamabad became capital in the 1960s.
recs.rel: Islamabad was built in the 1960s at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

recs.q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
recs.facts: Astana is the capital; it was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022 and then renamed Astana again.
recs.rel: Almaty was the earlier capital and is the largest city.

recs.q: What is the capital of Ghana?
recs.facts: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana.
recs.rel: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.

recs.q: What is the capital of Austria?
recs.facts: Vienna is the capital of Austria.
recs.rel: Vienna lies on the River Danube.

recs.q: What is the capital of Somalia?
recs.facts: Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia.
recs.rel: Somalia is in the Horn of Africa.

recs.q: Who is the Foreign Minister of Iran?
recs.facts: Abbas Araghchi has been Iran's Foreign Minister since August 2024 and still held the post in late 2026 reports.
recs.rel: Javad Zarif was the earlier Foreign Minister who negotiated the 2015 nuclear deal.

recs.q: Who is the President of China?
recs.facts: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013.
recs.rel: Li Qiang is the Premier of China, not the President.

recs.q: Who was the leader of Germany in World War 2?
recs.facts: Adolf Hitler led Nazi Germany as Fuhrer from 1934 to 1945.
recs.rel: World War 2 began in 1939 with Germany's invasion of Poland.

recs.q: What is the most important resource of the Arabian countries?
recs.facts: Oil (petroleum) is the main economic resource of the Arab Gulf countries.
recs.rel: Saudi Arabia has one of the world's largest proven oil reserves.

recs.q: What is the currency of Japan?
recs.facts: The Japanese currency is the yen.
recs.rel: The Chinese currency is the yuan and the South Korean currency is the won.

recs.q: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
recs.facts: Australia (Oceania) is the smallest continent by land area.
recs.rel: Europe is the second smallest continent.

recs.q: Which is the 2nd largest continent in the world?
recs.facts: Asia is the largest, and Africa is second with about 30.3 million sq km.
recs.rel: Africa has 54 recognised countries.

recs.q: What is the main source of freshwater in the world?
recs.facts: About 68-69% of the world's freshwater is locked in glaciers and ice caps.
recs.rel: Only about 3% of all water on Earth is fresh.

recs.q: Which country is the biggest coffee producer in the world?
recs.facts: Brazil is the largest coffee producer, supplying roughly a third of the world's coffee.
recs.rel: Vietnam is usually the second largest producer.

recs.q: Which country is known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes?
recs.facts: Finland has about 188,000 lakes and is called the Land of a Thousand Lakes.
recs.rel: Minnesota in the USA is also nicknamed Land of 10,000 Lakes.

recs.q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
recs.facts: Lake Baikal in Russia is about 1,642 m deep, the deepest lake on Earth.
recs.rel: Baikal holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.

recs.q: Which is the longest river in the world (by the traditional measurement)?
recs.facts: The Nile is traditionally ranked longest at about 6,650 km; the Amazon is the largest by water volume.
recs.rel: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.

recs.q: Which is the fastest bird in the world?
recs.facts: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive.
recs.rel: The ostrich is the fastest running bird.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations (UNO)?
recs.facts: The UN headquarters is in New York City, USA.
recs.rel: The UN was founded in 1945.

recs.q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank?
recs.facts: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines.
recs.rel: The ADB was established in 1966.

recs.q: At the end of 2016, which country was the third-largest refugee-hosting country in the world according to UNHCR?
recs.facts: UNHCR Global Trends 2016: Turkey (2.9 million) was first, Pakistan (1.4 million) second and Lebanon (1.0 million) third.
recs.rel: Most refugees in Pakistan are from Afghanistan.

recs.q: Why did America take part in World War 2?
opts: Because of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
Because of the sinking of the Titanic
Because of the Cuban Missile Crisis
recs.facts: The USA entered the war after Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941.
recs.rel: Pearl Harbor is in Hawaii.

recs.q: The 2015 nuclear agreement between Iran and world powers (including the USA) is known as?
recs.facts: The JCPOA was agreed in July 2015 with Iran by the P5+1; the USA withdrew from it in 2018.
recs.rel: The JCPOA limited Iran's uranium enrichment in return for lifting sanctions.

recs.q: In which year did India conduct its first nuclear test?
recs.facts: India's first test (Smiling Buddha) was on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran.
recs.rel: India's second series of tests, Pokhran-II, was in May 1998.

recs.q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
recs.facts: Kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.
recs.rel: 0 K is absolute zero, about minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

recs.q: What is the antonym of Wild?
recs.facts: Tamed (domesticated) is the opposite of wild.
recs.rel: Fierce and savage are synonyms of wild.

recs.q: What is a synonym of Gorgeous?
recs.facts: Gorgeous means very beautiful or stunning.
recs.rel: Its antonyms include ugly and plain.

recs.q: Who is the author of Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa?
recs.facts: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa (1909) and Jawab-e-Shikwa (1913).
recs.rel: Both poems are included in his Urdu collection Bang-e-Dra.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Friends Not Masters?
recs.facts: Field Marshal Ayub Khan wrote his autobiography Friends Not Masters in 1967.
recs.rel: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto wrote The Myth of Independence.

recs.q: Who wrote the book Jinnah of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote Jinnah of Pakistan (1984).
recs.rel: Hector Bolitho wrote Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan.

recs.q: What is the national bird of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Markhor is the national animal.

recs.q: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The national flower of Pakistan is jasmine (Chambeli).
recs.rel: Jasmine is a symbol of grace and beauty in Pakistan.

recs.q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The national flag of Pakistan was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kidwai, based on the Muslim League flag.
recs.rel: The flag was adopted on 11 August 1947.

recs.q: In which region of Asia is Pakistan located?
recs.facts: Pakistan is a country of South Asia.
recs.rel: It borders Iran, Afghanistan, China and India.

recs.q: Which is the largest river of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan, about 3,180 km long.
recs.rel: It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

recs.q: Which is the largest district of Pakistan by area?
recs.facts: Chagai in Balochistan is the largest district of Pakistan, with about 44,748 square km.
recs.rel: Pakistan's nuclear tests of 1998 were held in the Chagai hills.

recs.q: How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan has five peaks above 8000 m: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II and Broad Peak.
recs.rel: K2 (8611 m) is the second highest mountain in the world.

recs.q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Tirich Mir in Chitral is 7708 m high.
recs.rel: It is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range.

recs.q: Which line is the boundary between China and India in the eastern sector?
recs.facts: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and marks the China-India border in the eastern sector; China does not accept it.
recs.rel: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

recs.q: The Wakhan border of Pakistan is shared with which country?
recs.facts: The Wakhan strip is part of Afghanistan and touches northern Chitral in Pakistan.
recs.rel: The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from Tajikistan.

recs.q: How was Attabad Lake in Gilgit-Baltistan formed?
recs.facts: A massive landslide in January 2010 blocked the Hunza River and formed the lake.
recs.rel: Attabad Lake is in the Hunza valley near Karakoram Highway.

recs.q: In which province is Mohenjo-Daro located?
recs.facts: Mohenjo-Daro is in Larkana district, Sindh.
recs.rel: Harappa, the other Indus Valley city, is in Punjab.

recs.q: Why do people visit Ziarat in Balochistan?
opts: The tomb of Allama Iqbal is there
recs.facts: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days, is in Ziarat.
recs.rel: Ziarat is also famous for its juniper forests.

recs.q: Why do we boil milk?
recs.facts: Boiling kills harmful germs and bacteria in milk.
recs.rel: Pasteurisation also kills germs using controlled heating.

recs.q: Why do parents send children to school?
opts: To groom them and give them education
To keep them away from home
recs.facts: Parents send children to school for education and character building.
recs.rel: Education is a fundamental right under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.

recs.q: PEMRA is the regulatory body for which media?
recs.facts: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority regulates TV and radio.
recs.rel: PEMRA was established in 2002.

recs.q: Which city started television broadcasting first in Pakistan?
recs.facts: Pakistan Television started in Lahore on 26 November 1964.
recs.rel: PTV later opened stations in Dhaka, Karachi, Rawalpindi and Peshawar.

recs.q: When did Pakistan join the United Nations?
recs.facts: Pakistan became the 56th member of the UN on 30 September 1947.
recs.rel: Afghanistan, Yemen and Pakistan were admitted in that period.

recs.q: When did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points?
recs.facts: Jinnah presented the 14 Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
recs.rel: The Nehru Report was of 1928.

recs.q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver the Allahabad Address?
recs.facts: Iqbal gave his presidential address at the Muslim League session in Allahabad in December 1930.
recs.rel: He proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.

recs.q: When did Muslims get the right of separate electorates?
recs.facts: Separate electorates for Muslims were granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
recs.rel: The Congress accepted them in the Lucknow Pact of 1916.

recs.q: When did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
recs.facts: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913.
recs.rel: The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in 1906.

recs.q: What was the date of the Lahore Resolution?
recs.facts: The Lahore Resolution was passed on 23 March 1940, moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq.
recs.rel: It was seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.

recs.q: What was the official reason given for the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
recs.facts: Lord Curzon said Bengal was too big to govern, so it was divided for administrative reasons.
recs.rel: The partition was annulled in 1911.

recs.q: Who became the Prime Minister of Pakistan after Liaquat Ali Khan?
recs.facts: Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor-General and then became Prime Minister in 1951 after Liaquat Ali Khan was killed.
recs.rel: Liaquat Ali Khan was Pakistan's first Prime Minister.

recs.q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The order was Jinnah, Nazimuddin, then Malik Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55).
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza was the fourth Governor-General and later first President.

recs.q: Which Act was used as the basis of Pakistan's first (interim) constitution?
recs.facts: Pakistan adopted the Government of India Act 1935 with changes as its interim constitution.
recs.rel: The first full constitution came in 1956.

recs.q: The 1956 Constitution was framed under the Prime Ministership of which leader?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the first constitution was adopted on 23 March 1956.
recs.rel: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic on that day.

recs.q: The 1962 Constitution of Pakistan was abrogated by whom?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated it in March 1969.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan had given the 1962 Constitution.

recs.q: When were the first general elections held after the 1962 Constitution was abrogated?
recs.facts: General elections were held in December 1970 under Yahya Khan.
recs.rel: They were the first elections on the basis of one man one vote.

recs.q: How many general seats did the Awami League win in the 1970 elections?
recs.facts: The Awami League of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 general seats, all in East Pakistan.
recs.rel: The PPP won 81 seats in West Pakistan.

recs.q: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between which two leaders?
opts: Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
recs.facts: Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed it in Shimla on 2 July 1972.
recs.rel: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 was signed by Ayub Khan and Shastri.

recs.q: In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed?
recs.facts: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement in 1963.
recs.rel: Diplomatic relations began in 1951.

recs.q: How many days did the 1965 Pakistan-India war last?
recs.facts: The war ran from 6 September to 23 September 1965, which is 17 days.
recs.rel: The Tashkent Declaration ended it in January 1966.

recs.q: In which year did Fatima Jinnah die?
recs.facts: Fatima Jinnah, Madar-e-Millat, died on 9 July 1967.
recs.rel: She contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.

recs.q: What is the date of Pakistan's first nuclear test?
recs.facts: Pakistan conducted its first nuclear tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I).
recs.rel: 28 May is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.

recs.q: How many nuclear blasts did Pakistan conduct in 1998?
recs.facts: Five blasts on 28 May and one on 30 May 1998, a total of six.
recs.rel: India had tested earlier in May 1998.

recs.q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of Pakistan (and of the Muslim world)?
recs.facts: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in December 1988, the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.
recs.rel: She was elected again in 1993.

recs.q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Punjab (Pakistan)?
recs.facts: Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024, the first woman in this post.
recs.rel: Shehbaz Sharif is the Prime Minister.

recs.q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Balochistan?
recs.facts: Mir Sarfraz Bugti was elected Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and still holds the office.
recs.rel: He belongs to the PPP.

recs.q: Pakistan created the post of Chief of Defence Forces through which constitutional amendment?
recs.facts: The 27th Amendment (November 2025) changed Article 243 and created the Chief of Defence Forces.
recs.rel: The post of Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee was abolished by the same amendment.

recs.q: Which Chinese-made fighter jet was inducted by the Pakistan Air Force in 2022 and used in the May 2025 conflict?
recs.facts: The PAF inducted the Chinese J-10CE in 2022 and used it in May 2025.
recs.rel: JF-17 Thunder is jointly produced by Pakistan and China.

recs.q: What is the Uraan Pakistan plan?
opts: A plan to build a new airport
A military exercise of the Air Force
A national economic transformation plan launched in December 2024
recs.facts: Uraan Pakistan is the government's economic transformation plan led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, with five pillars including exports and digital economy.
recs.rel: Its stated aim is a 3 trillion dollar economy by 2047.

recs.q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
recs.facts: Dr. Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979.
recs.rel: Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

recs.q: Ahsan Ramzan is a famous player of which sport?
recs.facts: Ahsan Ramzan is a Pakistani snooker player who won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012.
recs.rel: Muhammad Asif and Muhammad Sajjad are other Pakistani snooker world champions.

recs.q: Jahangir Khan is famous for which sport?
recs.facts: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times and was unbeaten for about five years.
recs.rel: Jansher Khan was another great Pakistani squash player.

recs.q: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
recs.facts: Kardar was the first captain of Pakistan's Test cricket team.
recs.rel: Pakistan's first Test win came against India in 1952 in Lucknow.

recs.q: Who has scored the most Test runs for Pakistan?
recs.facts: Younis Khan scored 10,099 Test runs and is Pakistan's top Test run scorer.
recs.rel: He was the first Pakistani to pass 10,000 Test runs.

recs.q: Which game is played with a racket and a shuttle?
recs.facts: Badminton uses rackets and a shuttlecock.
recs.rel: Squash uses a ball and a closed court.

recs.q: Which ICC tournament did Pakistan host in 2025?
recs.facts: Pakistan hosted the ICC Champions Trophy in February-March 2025, its first ICC event in about 29 years.
recs.rel: India played its matches in Dubai.

recs.q: Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical interpretation of the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: When asked about his character, Hazrat Ayesha R.A said his character was the Quran.
recs.rel: She is among the main narrators of Ahadith.

recs.q: Over what period was the Holy Quran revealed?
recs.facts: Revelation began in 610 CE and ended about 23 years later, around 632 CE.
recs.rel: About 13 years were in Makkah and about 10 in Madinah.

recs.q: How many Ayats are in Surah Al-Baqarah?
recs.facts: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 Ayats.
recs.rel: It is the longest Surah of the Quran.

recs.q: How many Prophets are mentioned by name in the Holy Quran?
recs.facts: The Quran names 25 Prophets.
recs.rel: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) is the last of them.

recs.q: What is the meaning of Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin?
recs.facts: Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:40) means the Seal or Last of the Prophets.
recs.rel: No Prophet will come after Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH).

recs.q: Who was the first martyr of Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Sumayyah R.A was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is known as the first martyr of Islam.
recs.rel: Her husband Hazrat Yasir R.A was also martyred.

recs.q: Who was the first woman to accept Islam?
recs.facts: Hazrat Khadija R.A was the first person to accept Islam after the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: She was the first wife of the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Who narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A narrated about 5,374 Ahadith.
recs.rel: He was a companion of the Ahl-e-Suffa.

recs.q: Which of the following lists names all four daughters of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The four daughters were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima R.A.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman R.A married Ruqayyah and later Umm Kulthum.

recs.q: Hazrat Ayesha R.A was the daughter of which Sahabi?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayesha R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A and wife of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: Hazrat Hafsa R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Umar R.A.

recs.q: Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ayesha R.A (and also Hazrat Asma R.A) were daughters of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A.
recs.rel: Hazrat Hafsa R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Umar R.A.

recs.q: Hazrat Ali R.A belonged to which clan?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali R.A was from Banu Hashim, the clan of the Prophet (PBUH).
recs.rel: He was the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Which was the first major battle of Islam, fought between Muslims and the Quraysh?
recs.facts: Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle; earlier expeditions such as Widdan had no fighting.
recs.rel: Widdan (Abwa) was the first ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH).

recs.q: Youm-e-Furqan is the title of which battle?
recs.facts: The Quran calls the day of Badr Youm-ul-Furqan, the day that separated truth from falsehood.
recs.rel: It was fought on 17 Ramadan.

recs.q: In which year of Hijrah did the Battle of Badr take place?
recs.facts: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
recs.rel: Uhud was in 3 AH.

recs.q: How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr?
recs.facts: About 313 Muslims fought against about 1000 Quraysh.
recs.rel: The Muslims had only 2 horses and about 70 camels.

recs.q: How did Abu Jahl die?
opts: Killed in the Battle of Uhud
Killed in the Battle of Badr, struck by two young boys Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh
recs.facts: Two young Ansari brothers, Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, struck him down at Badr and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud finished him.
recs.rel: Abu Jahl was the chief enemy of Islam among the Quraysh leaders.

recs.q: What does the word Ahzab mean?
recs.facts: Ahzab means groups or confederates; the tribes allied against Madinah in 5 AH.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Ahzab is the 33rd Surah of the Quran.

recs.q: Which companion suggested digging a trench in the Battle of Ahzab (Khandaq)?
recs.facts: Hazrat Salman Farsi R.A suggested the Persian idea of a trench to defend Madinah.
recs.rel: The trench was about 5 km long.

recs.q: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
recs.facts: The treaty was signed in Dhul Qa'dah 6 AH (628 CE).
recs.rel: The Quran called it a clear victory in Surah Al-Fath.

recs.q: Which special prayer is performed in the middle of the night?
recs.facts: Tahajjud is the voluntary night prayer offered after sleeping, in the last part of the night.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Muzzammil urges night prayer.

recs.q: Where is Mina located?
recs.facts: Mina is a valley about 5 km from Makkah where pilgrims stay during Hajj and stone the Jamarat.
recs.rel: Arafat and Muzdalifah are the other Hajj sites near Makkah.

recs.q: Where is Mina located?
opts: Near Makkah (about 5 km east of it)
recs.facts: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah where pilgrims stay and stone the Jamarat during Hajj.
recs.rel: Pilgrims spend the 8th to 13th Dhul Hijjah nights in the tents of Mina.

recs.q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
recs.facts: Authentic Ahadith state that Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
recs.rel: Jahannam, in contrast, has seven gates.

recs.q: Who will blow the Trumpet (Soor) on the Day of Judgment?
recs.facts: Angel Israfil A.S has been entrusted to blow the Soor to announce Qiyamat and again for resurrection.
recs.rel: Jibrail brings revelation, Mikail looks after rain and provision, Izrail takes souls.

recs.q: According to Pakistani textbooks, in which year A.D. was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born (in Rabi-ul-Awwal, commonly given as 22nd April)?
recs.facts: The year of the Elephant is taken as 571 A.D in Pakistani textbooks, with the date given as 22nd April (12 Rabi-ul-Awwal). Some historians give 570 A.D.
recs.rel: He was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant.

recs.q: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The father of the Prophet (PBUH) was Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.
recs.rel: Abdullah died in Madina on a trade journey, while Amina was pregnant.

recs.q: What was the name of the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The mother of the Prophet (PBUH) was Amina bint Wahb of Banu Zuhra.
recs.rel: She died at Abwa when the Prophet was about six years old.

recs.q: What was the name of the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Amina was the daughter of Wahb bin Abd Manaf, chief of Banu Zuhra, so he was the maternal grandfather.
recs.rel: Abdul Muttalib chose Amina for his son Abdullah.

recs.q: What was the name of the maternal grandmother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), as given in the list?
recs.facts: Amina's mother was Barrah bint Abd al-Uzza, which the list spells as Batarah.
recs.rel: Fatima bint Amr was the paternal grandmother, the mother of Abdullah.

recs.q: What was the real name of Abdul Muttalib, grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Abdul Muttalib's real name was Shaybah; he was called Abdul Muttalib because he was brought up by his uncle Muttalib.
recs.rel: He was the chief of Quraish and the custodian of Zamzam.

recs.q: What was the name of the paternal grandmother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the mother of Abdullah?
recs.facts: Abdullah's mother was Fatima bint Amr of Banu Makhzum, so she was the Prophet's paternal grandmother.
recs.rel: Amina was his mother, not his grandmother.

recs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) travel to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib?
recs.facts: At age 12 he went with Abu Talib on a trade caravan, where the monk Bahira recognised signs of prophethood.
recs.rel: His second trade trip to Syria, at 25, was for Khadija R.A.

recs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry Hazrat Khadija R.A?
recs.facts: He married Khadija R.A at age 25, while she was about 40.
recs.rel: Khadija R.A was his first wife and all his children except Ibrahim were from her.

recs.q: Among adult free men, who was the first to accept Islam?
recs.facts: Abu Bakr Siddiq R.A was the first adult free man to accept Islam.
recs.rel: He is titled Siddiq and was the first Caliph.

recs.q: Who was the first among children to accept Islam?
recs.facts: Ali R.A, then about ten years old and living in the Prophet's house, was the first child to accept Islam.
recs.rel: Zaid bin Haritha R.A is counted as the first freed slave among the early Muslims.

recs.q: After the first revelation, which relative of Hazrat Khadija R.A confirmed that the Prophet (PBUH) was the awaited Prophet?
recs.facts: Khadija R.A took the Prophet (PBUH) to her cousin Waraqa bin Naufal, a Christian scholar, who confirmed his prophethood.
recs.rel: Waraqa died soon afterwards and the revelation paused for a time (Fatrat-ul-Wahy).

recs.q: How many children did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have, according to the common Seerah account?
recs.facts: The common account gives 3 sons (Qasim, Abdullah, Ibrahim) and 4 daughters (Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatima).
recs.rel: Ibrahim was the only child not born to Khadija R.A; his mother was Maria Qibtiyya.

recs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation (Wahy)?
recs.facts: The first revelation came in the cave of Hira when he was 40 years old.
recs.rel: The first verses were from Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.

recs.q: Who was the second wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: After Khadija R.A passed away, the Prophet (PBUH) married Sawda R.A, so she is his second wife. The name Zubaida in the list is not correct.
recs.rel: Ayesha R.A, daughter of Abu Bakr, married him soon after, in Makkah.

recs.q: In which year A.D. did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate to Madina?
recs.facts: The Hijrah took place in 622 A.D, which is the start of the Islamic calendar.
recs.rel: The Hijri calendar was started in the time of Hazrat Umar R.A.

recs.q: Which pair were among the foster mothers (wet nurses) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Thuwaybah (the freed slave of Abu Lahab) and Halima Sa'diyah both nursed the Prophet (PBUH). The list's Sobia is Thuwaybah.
recs.rel: Halima belonged to the tribe of Banu Sa'd.

recs.q: Besides Hazrat Halima, whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) call his mother?
opts: Hazrat Asma bint Abu Bakr R.A
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) called Umm Ayman, who raised him after Amina's death, 'my mother after my mother'.
recs.rel: Her son was Usama bin Zaid R.A.

recs.q: How many years after the birth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) did his mother Hazrat Amina die?
recs.facts: Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet was about six years old.
recs.rel: After her, his grandfather Abdul Muttalib took care of him until he died when the Prophet was 8.

recs.q: What was the name of the foster sister of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: Shaima (Hudhafa bint Harith), daughter of Halima, used to carry and care for the Prophet (PBUH) as a child.
recs.rel: She was captured in the battle of Hunain and treated with great respect by the Prophet.

recs.q: Which of these was a foster brother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), a son of Hazrat Halima?
recs.facts: Abdullah bin Harith, son of Halima and Harith, was nursed with the Prophet (PBUH) and is known as his foster brother.
recs.rel: The list gives the name as Abdullah bin Abu Sheema.

recs.q: For how long, according to the common account, did Hazrat Halima look after the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The common Seerah account says the Prophet stayed with Halima in the desert for around four years (some say five).
recs.rel: Desert upbringing gave him pure Arabic and strong health.

recs.q: How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) incident?
recs.facts: When the Kaaba was rebuilt, the Prophet (PBUH), then 35, settled the dispute by placing the stone on a sheet carried by all tribal leaders.
recs.rel: He was called Al-Amin (the Trustworthy) before prophethood.

recs.q: Who used to spread thorns in the way of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
opts: Umm Jamil, wife of Abu Lahab
recs.facts: Umm Jamil bint Harb, wife of Abu Lahab, used to put thorns on the Prophet's path; Surah Al-Lahab mentions her as the carrier of firewood.
recs.rel: She was the sister of Abu Sufyan.

recs.q: Whose house was used as the centre of secret preaching by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
opts: Hazrat Arqam bin Abi Arqam R.A
recs.facts: The house of Arqam on Mount Safa was Dar-e-Arqam, the first centre of Islamic teaching in Makkah.
recs.rel: Umar R.A accepted Islam and the Muslims then began to preach openly.

recs.q: In which year of Prophethood did the boycott of Banu Hashim begin?
recs.facts: Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib from the 7th year of prophethood and they stayed in Shib Abi Talib for about three years.
recs.rel: The boycott ended in the 10th Nabvi, the year of grief.

recs.q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the first heaven during Miraj?
recs.facts: Authentic Ahadith of Bukhari and Muslim say he met Adam A.S in the first heaven.
recs.rel: Ibrahim A.S was met in the seventh heaven.

recs.q: Which Prophets did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the second heaven during Miraj?
opts: Hazrat Musa A.S and Hazrat Haroon A.S
Hazrat Isa A.S and Hazrat Yahya A.S
recs.facts: In the second heaven he met the cousins Isa A.S and Yahya A.S.
recs.rel: Isa and Yahya were maternal cousins.

recs.q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the third heaven during Miraj?
recs.facts: Authentic Hadith says he met Yusuf A.S in the third heaven. The list's answer Yaqub is not correct.
recs.rel: Yusuf A.S was given half of all beauty.

recs.q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the fourth heaven during Miraj?
recs.facts: He met Idris A.S in the fourth heaven.
recs.rel: Idris A.S is mentioned in the Quran as a truthful Prophet raised to a high place.

recs.q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the fifth heaven during Miraj?
recs.facts: He met Haroon A.S in the fifth heaven.
recs.rel: Haroon A.S was the elder brother of Musa A.S.

recs.q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the sixth heaven during Miraj?
recs.facts: He met Musa A.S in the sixth heaven; Musa advised him to ask Allah to reduce the number of prayers.
recs.rel: The prayers were reduced from fifty to five.

recs.q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the seventh heaven during Miraj?
recs.facts: He met Ibrahim A.S in the seventh heaven, leaning against Bait-ul-Mamoor.
recs.rel: Bait-ul-Mamoor is visited daily by seventy thousand angels.

recs.q: What was the name of the camel on which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) traveled during the Hijrah?
recs.facts: The Prophet's well-known she-camel was Al-Qaswa, and he rode her to Madina.
recs.rel: Duldul was his white mule.

recs.q: From whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) purchase the land for the mosque in Madina (Masjid-e-Nabawi)?
recs.facts: The land of Masjid-e-Nabawi belonged to two orphans, Sahl and Suhail, and the Prophet (PBUH) bought it from them.
recs.rel: The Prophet first stayed at the house of Abu Ayyub Ansari R.A.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the Charter of Madina (Meesaq-e-Madina) issued?
recs.facts: The Charter of Madina was made soon after the Hijrah, in 1 A.H, between Muslims, Jews and others of Madina.
recs.rel: It is often called the first written constitution of an Islamic state. The number of its articles differs in sources, so that part is not asked.

recs.q: In which Hijri year was the change of Qibla (from Baitul Maqdis to Kaaba) ordered?
recs.facts: The order to turn towards the Kaaba came in the 2nd year after Hijrah, during prayer at Masjid-e-Qiblatain.
recs.rel: The Battle of Badr took place in the same year.

recs.q: According to the common Seerah count, how many Ghazwat (expeditions led by the Prophet PBUH himself) are there?
recs.facts: Seerah books commonly count 27 Ghazwat, in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part himself; he actually fought in about nine of them.
recs.rel: Expeditions he did not lead are called Saraya, commonly counted as 56.

recs.q: Which was the first Ghazwa of Islam?
recs.facts: The first Ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH) was Abwa, also called Waddan, in 2 A.H, and no fighting took place.
recs.rel: The first major battle of Islam was Badr.

recs.q: Who was the first to compile Ahadith (Hadith) officially, on the order of Hazrat Umar bin Abdul Aziz?
recs.facts: Imam Ibn Shihab Zuhri is widely regarded as the first to compile Ahadith formally, at the order of Umar bin Abdul Aziz.
recs.rel: Imam Bukhari's Sahih Bukhari is the most authentic collection.

recs.q: How many Ahadith are reported from Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A?
recs.facts: Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A is credited with 5374 narrations, the highest among the Sahaba, according to Baqi bin Makhlad.
recs.rel: Abdullah bin Umar R.A and Anas bin Malik R.A follow him in the number of narrations.

recs.q: Which Prophet is known as Shaikh-ul-Anbiya?
recs.facts: Hazrat Nuh A.S is called Shaikh-ul-Anbiya (Elder of the Prophets) because of his very long life of preaching.
recs.rel: Ibrahim A.S is called Khalilullah and Abul Anbiya.

recs.q: Who was given the title Ameen-ul-Ummat?
opts: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah R.A
Hazrat Saad bin Abi Waqqas R.A
recs.facts: The Prophet (PBUH) gave Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah R.A the title Ameen-ul-Ummat (Trustworthy of the Ummah).
recs.rel: He was one of the ten Sahaba given the good news of Jannah.

recs.q: What is the dome over the sacred grave of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) known as?
recs.facts: The dome over the Prophet's tomb in Masjid-e-Nabawi is known as the Green Dome (Gumbad-e-Khizra).
recs.rel: Gumbad-e-Sakhra is the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem.

recs.q: Where is Bait-ul-Mamoor located?
recs.facts: Bait-ul-Mamoor is a house of worship of the angels in the seventh heaven, directly above the Kaaba.
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) saw it during Miraj.

recs.q: Which mosque was demolished on the order of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
recs.facts: The hypocrites built Masjid-e-Dirar to harm Muslims, and the Prophet (PBUH) had it destroyed after Surah At-Tawbah revealed its purpose.
recs.rel: Masjid-e-Quba was the first mosque built in Islam.

recs.q: Who conquered the fort of Qamus during the Battle of Khyber?
recs.facts: Hazrat Ali R.A, given the flag by the Prophet (PBUH), conquered the fort of Qamus and killed its champion Marhab.
recs.rel: Ali R.A is known by the title Asadullah (Lion of Allah).

recs.q: Which woman tried to poison the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at Khyber?
recs.facts: A Jewish woman, Zainab bint Harith, served poisoned roasted goat meat to the Prophet (PBUH) after the conquest of Khyber.
recs.rel: Bishr bin Bara R.A died from eating it.

recs.q: Which Surah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) recite at the conquest of Makkah?
recs.facts: On entering Makkah, the Prophet (PBUH) was reciting Surah Al-Fath while riding his camel.
recs.rel: Surah Al-Fath was revealed after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

recs.q: In which year of Prophethood did the first migration to Abyssinia (Habshah) take place?
recs.facts: In Rajab of the 5th year of Prophethood (615 A.D), a small group went to Abyssinia to escape persecution.
recs.rel: They were protected by the Christian king Najashi (Negus).

recs.q: How many people took part in the first migration to Abyssinia, according to Ibn Ishaq?
recs.facts: Ibn Ishaq's account gives 11 men and 4 women, in total 15.
recs.rel: Hazrat Usman R.A and his wife Ruqayyah R.A were among them.

recs.q: In which year A.D. did the second migration to Abyssinia take place, according to the common account?
recs.facts: The second, bigger migration took place about a year after the first, around 616 A.D.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib R.A led the second group.

recs.q: How many people in total took part in the second migration to Abyssinia?
recs.facts: The second migration had 83 men and 18 women, in total 101 people.
recs.rel: Hazrat Jafar R.A recited Surah Maryam before King Najashi.

recs.q: What does Harb-e-Fijar mean?
opts: A war fought in the prohibited (sacred) months
A war for the Kaaba key
recs.facts: Harb-e-Fijar was fought between Quraish and Banu Qais in the sacred months, in which fighting was forbidden, so it was called the sinful war.
recs.rel: The young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it by handing arrows to his uncles.

recs.q: Which year is called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)?
recs.facts: In the 10th year of Prophethood, Hazrat Khadija R.A and Abu Talib both passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.
recs.rel: Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) went to Taif.

recs.q: What was the original name of Abu Jahl?
recs.facts: Abu Jahl was Amr bin Hisham, called Abul Hakam by Quraish; the Prophet (PBUH) called him Abu Jahl (father of ignorance). The list writes Omar bin Hisham.
recs.rel: He was killed in the Battle of Badr.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did the conquest of Makkah take place?
recs.facts: Makkah was conquered peacefully in Ramadan of 8 A.H (630 A.D).
recs.rel: The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah.

recs.q: In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform his (Farewell) Hajj?
recs.facts: He performed the only Hajj of his life, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 A.H and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.
recs.rel: He passed away about three months later.

recs.q: Where was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) buried?
opts: In the room (Hujra) of Hazrat Ayesha R.A
recs.facts: He passed away in the room of Ayesha R.A and was buried at the same spot, as Prophets are buried where they die.
recs.rel: Abu Bakr R.A and Umar R.A were later buried beside him.

recs.q: Which king tore up the letter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) inviting him to Islam?
recs.facts: The Persian king Khusro Parvez tore the letter, and the Prophet (PBUH) said his kingdom would also be torn apart.
recs.rel: Heraclius received the letter politely and Muqawqis sent gifts.

recs.q: Who was the Byzantine (Roman) emperor in the 7th Hijri year, when the Prophet PBUH sent him a letter?
recs.facts: Heraclius ruled the Byzantine Empire from 610 to 641 A.D and received the Prophet's letter in 7 A.H.
recs.rel: Abu Sufyan was questioned by Heraclius about the Prophet.

recs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
recs.facts: He passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal 11 A.H at the age of 63 years.
recs.rel: Abu Bakr R.A, Umar R.A and Ali R.A also died at 63 years.

recs.q: The Constitution of 1956 was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on which date?
recs.facts: The Constituent Assembly adopted the first Constitution on 29 February 1956 (1956 was a leap year).
recs.rel: It came into force on 23 March 1956, later celebrated as Republic Day.

recs.q: Which Prime Minister played the leading role in framing the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the 1956 Constitution.
recs.rel: He also served as Finance Minister and Secretary General of the government earlier.

recs.q: On which date did the Constitution of 1956 come into force?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and Pakistan became an Islamic Republic.
recs.rel: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the 1940 Lahore Resolution.

recs.q: The Constitution of 1956 was framed by the Constituent Assembly in the name of whom?
recs.facts: The Constitution was adopted in the name of the people of Pakistan, as the preamble says.
recs.rel: The Objective Resolution of 1949 was made its preamble basis.

recs.q: The Constitution of 1956 received its assent from which office holder?
recs.facts: The Governor General (Iskander Mirza) gave assent to the Constitution passed by the Constituent Assembly. He became the first President on 23 March 1956.
recs.rel: The office of Governor General was replaced by the President.

recs.q: What name did the Constitution of 1956 give to the country?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic, the first in the world.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution first dropped the word Islamic from the name.

recs.q: Which part of the Constitution of 1956 dealt with Fundamental Rights?
recs.facts: Fundamental Rights were placed in Part II of the 1956 Constitution.
recs.rel: The Directive Principles of State Policy came in the following part.

recs.q: Which form of government was provided by the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution set up a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister and cabinet responsible to the National Assembly.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution changed this to a presidential system.

recs.q: According to the Constitution of 1956, who was the Head of State?
recs.facts: The President replaced the Governor General as constitutional Head of State.
recs.rel: Iskander Mirza was the first President of Pakistan.

recs.q: What was the minimum age to become President under the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be at least 40 years old and a Muslim.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution lowered the minimum age to 35.

recs.q: What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
recs.facts: It provided a single-house National Assembly of 300 members, equally divided between East and West Pakistan.
recs.rel: Pakistan's first bicameral legislature came with the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution created the Supreme Court of Pakistan, replacing the Federal Court that existed since 1948. The source marked Federal Court, which is wrong.
recs.rel: The Federal Shariat Court was created much later, in 1980.

recs.q: Which languages were made national languages by the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: Urdu and Bengali were declared the state languages in the 1956 Constitution, with English used officially for 20 years.
recs.rel: Bengali was recognised after the 1952 Language Movement.

recs.q: Which type of federal structure did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
recs.facts: It provided a federation of two wings, East and West Pakistan, with federal, provincial and concurrent lists.
recs.rel: Powers were distributed through three lists.

recs.q: How many Articles and Parts did the Constitution of 1956 contain?
recs.facts: The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles, 13 Parts and 6 Schedules.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution has 280 Articles.

recs.q: For about how long did the Constitution of 1956 remain in force?
recs.facts: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated on 7 October 1958, about two and a half years.
recs.rel: It was the shortest-lived of Pakistan's three constitutions.

recs.q: On which date was the Constitution of 1956 abrogated?
recs.facts: President Iskander Mirza abrogated it on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan became Chief Martial Law Administrator and removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.

recs.q: Which body enacted the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: The second Constituent Assembly passed it, as the first one had been dissolved in 1954.
recs.rel: Governor General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly in October 1954.

recs.q: What was the total strength of the National Assembly under the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: It had 300 members, 150 from each wing, plus 10 seats reserved for women, so 310. The Constitution also kept parity between the wings.
recs.rel: Today the National Assembly has 336 seats.

recs.q: How were members of the National Assembly elected under the Constitution of 1956?
recs.facts: The Constitution provided direct elections to the National Assembly, though no general election was held before it was abrogated.
recs.rel: The first direct adult-franchise general election was held in 1970.

recs.q: What type of citizenship did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
recs.facts: Pakistan had a single citizenship for all citizens, as in a federation like India but unlike the USA.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution also has a single citizenship.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of 1956, how were powers divided in the federation?
recs.facts: Powers were shared through a Federal List, a Provincial List and a Concurrent List.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution had only Central and Provincial subjects.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of 1956, to whom was the Cabinet collectively responsible?
recs.facts: In the parliamentary system the Cabinet led by the Prime Minister was answerable to the National Assembly.
recs.rel: The Prime Minister was the head of government.

recs.q: On which date was the Constitution of 1962 enforced?
recs.facts: President Ayub Khan promulgated it on 1 March 1962 and it came into force on 8 June 1962. Note the source gave 28 February, which is not the correct date.
recs.rel: Martial law was lifted when it came into force.

recs.q: In how many Parts was the Constitution of 1962 divided (it had 250 Articles)?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution had 250 Articles, 12 Parts and 3 Schedules.
recs.rel: The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles and 13 Parts.

recs.q: Which form of government did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
recs.facts: It created a strong presidential system with the President as Chief Executive.
recs.rel: There was no Prime Minister in the 1962 Constitution as originally framed.

recs.q: How was the President elected under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The President was elected indirectly by an electoral college of Basic Democrats.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan won the 1965 election against Fatima Jinnah this way.

recs.q: The electoral college under the Constitution of 1962 was originally formed of how many Basic Democrats?
recs.facts: Originally 80,000 Basic Democrats (40,000 per wing) formed the electoral college.
recs.rel: It was later raised to 120,000 before the 1965 election.

recs.q: What was the voting age under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution set the minimum voting age at 21 years.
recs.rel: The voting age was lowered to 18 in 1973 and is now 18.

recs.q: What was the minimum age for a person to be elected President under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution required the President to be at least 35 years of age and a Muslim.
recs.rel: Under the 1956 Constitution it was 40 years.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of 1962, who had the power to dissolve the National Assembly?
recs.facts: The President held the power to dissolve the Assembly, one of his wide powers. The source asked the Article number, which could not be verified.
recs.rel: Under the 1973 Constitution this power is in Article 58.

recs.q: Under the Constitution of 1962, who could be impeached by the National Assembly?
recs.facts: The Constitution provided a process for impeaching the President, though it was very difficult to use.
recs.rel: In the 1973 Constitution the President is removed under Article 47.

recs.q: The Constitution of 1962 provided a federation of the centre and how many provinces?
recs.facts: The federation consisted of two provinces, East Pakistan and West Pakistan.
recs.rel: West Pakistan was a single province created through One Unit in 1955.

recs.q: What was the original name of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution dropped the word Islamic and called the country the Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The word Islamic was restored by an amendment.

recs.q: In which month of 1963 did the National Assembly pass the amendment restoring the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The first Amendment Act was passed in December 1963 and restored the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The amendment was formally assented in January 1964.

recs.q: Who was the Chief Executive of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The President was both head of state and chief executive.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan was the first President under this Constitution.

recs.q: What was the term of office of the President under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The President held office for five years.
recs.rel: The 1973 Constitution also gives a five-year term.

recs.q: Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The Supreme Court remained the apex court of the country.
recs.rel: The Supreme Court was first created by the 1956 Constitution.

recs.q: What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
recs.facts: It provided a single-house National Assembly.
recs.rel: The Senate came only with the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: Up to which age could a Supreme Court judge serve under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution set retirement of Supreme Court judges at 65 years.
recs.rel: Under the 1973 Constitution it is also 65 years.

recs.q: Which languages were national languages under the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: Urdu and Bengali were national languages, while English remained in official use.
recs.rel: Bengali was first recognised in 1956.

recs.q: Which system of local government did Ayub Khan make the base of the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The Basic Democracies system of 1959 created union councils whose members formed the electoral college.
recs.rel: The Devolution Plan was introduced later, in 2001.

recs.q: Which city was named as the capital of Pakistan in the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution named the newly built city of Islamabad as the capital, with Rawalpindi serving as the interim capital while it was being built.
recs.rel: Ayub Khan chose the site of Islamabad near General Headquarters at Rawalpindi.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1962 Constitution could the President promulgate Ordinances when the National Assembly was not in session?
recs.facts: Article 29 of the 1962 Constitution allowed the President to make an Ordinance with the same force as an Act when the Assembly was dissolved or not in session and immediate legislation was needed.
recs.rel: Such an Ordinance covered only matters within the competence of the Central Legislature.

recs.q: Under Article 226 of the 1962 Constitution, who was treated as the first President of Pakistan under that Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 226 (transitional provisions) provided that, following the referendum of February 1960, Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan was to be the first President under the 1962 Constitution.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution came into force on 8 June 1962.

recs.q: Which Order, issued by General Yahya Khan on 30 March 1970, set the framework for the first general elections and for making a new constitution?
recs.facts: The Legal Framework Order of 30 March 1970 laid down the basis for the December 1970 elections and required the elected Assembly to frame a constitution within 120 days.
recs.rel: The LFO also ended the One Unit scheme of West Pakistan on 1 July 1970.

recs.q: In which month and year was the Constitution of 1962 abrogated?
recs.facts: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.
recs.rel: The 1962 Constitution had come into force on 8 June 1962.

recs.q: For approximately how many years did the Constitution of 1962 remain in force?
recs.facts: It was in force from 8 June 1962 until 25 March 1969, which is about seven years (nearly six years and nine months).
recs.rel: It was Pakistan's second constitution.

recs.q: Which system of government was introduced by the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: The 1962 Constitution concentrated executive power in the President, who was both head of state and head of government, so critics called it a one-man show.
recs.rel: The President was elected indirectly by Electoral College of Basic Democrats.

recs.q: Who abrogated the Constitution of 1962?
recs.facts: General Agha Muhammad Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.
recs.rel: Yahya Khan became President and Chief Martial Law Administrator.

recs.q: On which date was the Constitution of 1973 authenticated by the President of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973 and President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry authenticated it on 12 April 1973.
recs.rel: The President who authenticated it was Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.

recs.q: On which date did the Constitution of 1973 come into force?
recs.facts: The Constitution was enforced on 14 August 1973, the Independence Day, after being authenticated on 12 April 1973.
recs.rel: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister under it.

recs.q: How many Articles does the Constitution of 1973 contain?
recs.facts: The Constitution of 1973 has 280 Articles divided into 12 Parts.
recs.rel: Articles added by amendments carry letters, for example Article 140A and Article 10A.

recs.q: On which date was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
recs.facts: The Objectives Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949, moved by Liaquat Ali Khan.
recs.rel: It became the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to whom?
recs.facts: The Objectives Resolution states that sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone.
recs.rel: It adds that the authority is delegated to the State through its people as a sacred trust.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, the authority exercised by the people of Pakistan within limits set by Allah is a what?
recs.facts: The Resolution says the authority to be exercised by the people within the limits prescribed by Allah is a sacred trust.
recs.rel: The Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers through the chosen representatives of the people.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, through whom shall the State exercise its powers and authority?
opts: The chosen representatives of the people
recs.facts: The Objectives Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers and authority through the chosen representatives of the people.
recs.rel: It also promises democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice as enunciated by Islam.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, how shall Muslims be enabled to order their lives?
opts: In accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam
recs.facts: The Resolution says Muslims shall be enabled to order their lives in the individual and collective spheres in accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam as set out in the Quran and Sunnah.
recs.rel: The Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, what freedom shall be given to minorities?
opts: To profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures freely
To follow only the teachings of Islam
To live as decided by government policy
recs.facts: The Resolution says adequate provision shall be made for minorities freely to profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures.
recs.rel: It also promises to safeguard the legitimate interests of minorities and backward classes.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, the independence of the judiciary shall be what?
recs.facts: The Resolution states that the independence of the judiciary shall be fully secured.
recs.rel: It also says fundamental rights, including equality of status and opportunity, shall be guaranteed.

recs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, Pakistan will make its full contribution towards what?
opts: International peace and progress and the happiness of humanity
recs.facts: The Resolution says the people of Pakistan should attain their rightful place among nations and make their full contribution towards international peace and progress and the happiness of humanity.
recs.rel: This is the closing aim stated in the Resolution and in the Preamble.

recs.q: In what form was the Objectives Resolution placed in the Constitution of 1973 as originally enacted?
recs.facts: In the original 1973 Constitution the Objectives Resolution was the Preamble. It became a substantive part later through Article 2A.
recs.rel: Article 2A was inserted by the Eighth Amendment in 1985.

recs.q: What name does Article 1 of the Constitution of 1973 give to Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 1(1) says Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
recs.rel: The name Islamic Republic was first used in the 1956 Constitution.

recs.q: After the 25th Amendment of 2018, what do the territories of Pakistan under Article 1 comprise?
opts: Four provinces, FATA and the Federal Capital
The provinces of Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh, and the Islamabad Capital Territory (plus such other territories as may be included)
Four provinces, Azad Kashmir and Islamabad only
recs.facts: The 25th Amendment (2018) merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed it from Article 1, so Article 1(2) now lists four provinces and the Islamabad Capital Territory. The older answer with FATA is outdated.
recs.rel: Article 1(2)(c) also covers such States and territories as are or may be included in Pakistan.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is Islam declared the State religion of Pakistan?
recs.facts: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Article 2A makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution.

recs.q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 2A states that the principles and provisions of the Objectives Resolution (Annex) are made substantive part of the Constitution and have effect accordingly.
recs.rel: It was inserted in 1985 through the Eighth Amendment.

recs.q: Under Article 5(1) of the Constitution of 1973, loyalty to whom is the basic duty of every citizen?
recs.facts: Article 5(1) says loyalty to the State is the basic duty of every citizen.
recs.rel: Article 5 is in Part I of the Constitution.

recs.q: Article 5(2) of the Constitution of 1973 describes obedience to the Constitution and law as the what of every citizen?
recs.facts: Article 5(2) says obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen wherever he may be and of every other person within Pakistan.
recs.rel: Article 5(1) makes loyalty to the State the basic duty of every citizen.

recs.q: A person who abrogates, subverts, suspends or holds in abeyance the Constitution by force or unconstitutional means is guilty of what under Article 6?
recs.facts: Article 6(1) says any person who abrogates or subverts the Constitution by use of force or show of force or other unconstitutional means is guilty of high treason.
recs.rel: The words 'suspends or holds in abeyance' were added by the 18th Amendment in 2010.

recs.q: Under Article 6(3) of the Constitution, who is empowered to provide the punishment for persons found guilty of high treason?
recs.facts: Article 6(3) says the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) shall by law provide for the punishment of persons found guilty of high treason.
recs.rel: The High Treason (Punishment) Act 1973 was passed under this Article.

recs.q: In which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the State defined for the purposes of Fundamental Rights?
recs.facts: Article 7 defines the State as the Federal Government, Parliament, a Provincial Government, a Provincial Assembly and local authorities.
recs.rel: Article 8 follows and deals with laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.

recs.q: Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution contain the Principles of Policy?
recs.facts: Chapter 2 of Part II, Articles 29 to 40, sets out the Principles of Policy.
recs.rel: Principles of Policy are not enforceable in court, unlike the Fundamental Rights.

recs.q: Under Article 8 of the 1973 Constitution, a law that is inconsistent with the Fundamental Rights is what?
opts: Void to the extent of the inconsistency
recs.facts: Article 8 says any law inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
recs.rel: Article 8 itself falls in Chapter 1 of Part II.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law?
recs.facts: Article 9 (security of person) says no person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.
recs.rel: The Supreme Court has read the right to life broadly to include a healthy environment.

recs.q: Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution deal with the Fundamental Rights?
recs.facts: Chapter 1 of Part II, Articles 8 to 28, contains the Fundamental Rights.
recs.rel: Articles 29 to 40 contain the Principles of Policy.

recs.q: What is Chapter 1 of Part II of the 1973 Constitution (Articles 8 to 28) called?
recs.facts: Chapter 1 of Part II is titled Fundamental Rights, the rights guaranteed by the Constitution and enforceable in court.
recs.rel: Chapter 2 of Part II is titled Principles of Policy.

recs.q: Safeguards as to arrest and detention are provided in which Article of the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 10 gives safeguards on arrest and detention, including the right to be told the grounds and to appear before a magistrate within 24 hours.
recs.rel: Article 10A adds the right to a fair trial.

recs.q: Article 10A of the 1973 Constitution deals with which right?
opts: Right to fair trial and due process
recs.facts: Article 10A guarantees the right to fair trial and due process in the determination of civil rights and criminal charges.
recs.rel: Article 25A deals with free and compulsory education.

recs.q: Through which amendment was the right to fair trial (Article 10A) added to the Fundamental Rights?
recs.facts: Article 10A was inserted by the 18th Amendment of 2010.
recs.rel: The 18th Amendment also inserted Article 19A (right to information) and Article 25A (right to education).

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution are slavery and forced labour prohibited?
recs.facts: Article 11 prohibits slavery, forced labour and the employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous work.
recs.rel: Article 11 also forbids trafficking in human beings.

recs.q: Article 12 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
recs.facts: Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment, meaning no one can be punished for an act that was not an offence when it was done.
recs.rel: Article 13 protects against double punishment and self-incrimination.

recs.q: Article 13 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
recs.facts: Article 13 says no person shall be punished more than once for the same offence nor be compelled to be a witness against himself.
recs.rel: Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment.

recs.q: Under which provision of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be subjected to torture for extracting evidence?
recs.facts: Article 14(2) says no person shall be subjected to torture for the purpose of extracting evidence.
recs.rel: Article 14(1) says the dignity of man and the privacy of home shall be inviolable.

recs.q: Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 15 of the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 15 guarantees every citizen the right to remain in, enter and move freely throughout Pakistan and settle in any part of it, subject to law.
recs.rel: Freedom of speech is in Article 19.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is freedom of assembly guaranteed?
recs.facts: Article 16 gives every citizen the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.
recs.rel: Article 17 covers freedom of association.

recs.q: Which freedom is provided in Article 17 of the 1973 Constitution?
recs.facts: Article 17 gives every citizen the right to form associations or unions and to form or be a member of a political party, subject to restrictions in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of Pakistan.
recs.rel: Article 16 covers freedom of assembly.

recs.q: Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 18 of the 1973 Constitution?
opts: Freedom of trade, business or profession
recs.facts: Article 18 gives every citizen the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation and to conduct any lawful trade or business.
recs.rel: Article 20 covers freedom to profess religion.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution does every citizen have the right of access to information in matters of public importance?
recs.facts: Article 19A, inserted by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives every citizen the right of access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.
recs.rel: Article 19 itself covers freedom of speech.

recs.q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is there safeguard against taxation for the purposes of any particular religion?
recs.facts: Article 21 says no person shall be compelled to pay any special tax the proceeds of which are to be spent on the propagation or maintenance of any religion other than his own.
recs.rel: Article 20 gives freedom to profess religion and to manage religious institutions.

recs.q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: Yesterday Sunday means today is Monday; the day after tomorrow is Monday + 2 = Wednesday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 19 - 4 = 15 days; 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Friday + 1 = Saturday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: What is 90% of 90?
recs.rel: Shortcut: x% of y equals y% of x, so 90% of 90 is 9 x 9 = 81.

recs.q: What is one third of 10% of 90?
recs.facts: 10% of 90 = 9, and one third of 9 = 3.
recs.rel: 10% of a number: move the decimal point one place to the left.

recs.q: What is one third of 10% of 120?
recs.facts: 10% of 120 = 12, and one third of 12 = 4.
recs.rel: Work from the inside out: first the percentage, then the fraction.

recs.q: How many months of a year have 31 days?
recs.facts: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days, so there are seven.
recs.rel: Knuckle trick: every knuckle is a 31-day month and every gap is a shorter month (July and August are both 31).

recs.q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper?
recs.facts: 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, so he writes 1 paper per minute.
recs.rel: Rate = work divided by time; find the rate of one worker first.

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
recs.rel: Percentage = part / total x 100; for a part of 500, divide the part by 5.

recs.q: What is the value of 2 + 2/2?
recs.facts: Division comes first: 2/2 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.
recs.rel: BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, Division and Multiplication, then Addition and Subtraction.

recs.q: What is a quarter of one tenth of 120?
recs.facts: One tenth of 120 = 12, and a quarter of 12 = 3.
recs.rel: Quarter of a number is the number divided by 4; one tenth is divided by 10.

recs.q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
recs.rel: If 2/3 is one group, the rest is 1/3, which is 33.33%.

recs.q: Ali bought a pen for Rs 30 and sold it for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage?
recs.rel: Profit % is always calculated on the cost price, not the selling price.

recs.q: Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball?
recs.facts: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket; football is mainly played with the foot.
recs.rel: Look for the equipment or the way the game is played.

recs.q: Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley.
recs.facts: Wheat, rice and barley are food grains for humans; hay is dried grass used as animal fodder.
recs.rel: Group by use: grains for food versus fodder.

recs.q: Which one is different from the others: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda, Baboon?
recs.facts: Monkey, ape, chimpanzee and baboon are primates; the panda is a bear.
recs.rel: Primates include monkeys, apes, baboons and humans.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 26 - 4 = 22 days; 22 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. How many women are there?
recs.rel: Find the fraction of the other group as 1 minus the given fraction.

recs.q: A man walked towards the north, then turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
recs.facts: North, then left gives West, then right from West gives North.
recs.rel: Left turn: N to W to S to E. Right turn: N to E to S to W.

recs.q: Complete the series: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, ?
recs.facts: Two series are mixed: 115, 170, 235 (add 55, then 65) and 55, 65, 75 (add 10), so the missing term is 75.
recs.rel: If a series looks random, separate the alternate terms into two series.

recs.q: Complete the series: 66, 63, 57, 45, ?
recs.facts: The differences are 3, 6, 12 (doubling), so the next difference is 24 and 45 - 24 = 21.
recs.rel: Check differences first; if they double, the series is a doubling-difference series.

recs.q: Complete the series: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ?
recs.facts: Each term is double the previous plus 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.

recs.q: Complete the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
recs.facts: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.
recs.rel: Letter series: convert letters to numbers (A=1 ... Z=26) and study the gaps.

recs.q: Complete the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
recs.facts: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 (gaps 2, 3, 4, 5), so the next gap is 6 and 15 + 6 = 21 = U.
recs.rel: Gaps that increase by 1 are the triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21.

recs.q: Complete the series: L, M, N, ?
recs.facts: The letters are consecutive in the alphabet, so after N comes O.
recs.rel: Simple consecutive series go forward one letter at a time.

recs.q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 15 days; 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Sunday + 1 = Monday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 4th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 10 days backwards; 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday - 3 = Thursday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: Why do parents give education to their children?
recs.facts: Education develops and grooms a child into a capable and responsible person.
recs.rel: In such questions choose the most natural and purposeful answer.

recs.q: Why do we boil milk?
recs.facts: Boiling kills harmful germs (bacteria), making the milk safe to drink.
recs.rel: Pasteurisation is a similar heating process used for packaged milk.

recs.q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
recs.facts: Yesterday Friday means today is Saturday; the day after tomorrow is Saturday + 2 = Monday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h; in 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 60 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time; convert minutes into hours first.

recs.q: A bat cannot see; a snake cannot what?
recs.facts: A snake has no outer ears and cannot hear airborne sound well, so the answer is hear (note: in reality a bat can see; it also uses echolocation).
recs.rel: Snakes sense vibrations through the ground and use their tongue to smell.

recs.q: What is the sound made by an eagle called?
recs.facts: The call of an eagle is described as a scream.
recs.rel: Other animal sounds: lion roars, owl hoots, dog barks.

recs.q: What is half of 9/90?
recs.facts: 9/90 = 0.1, and half of 0.1 = 0.05 = 1/20 (so the source statement of 1/5 or 0.2 is wrong).
recs.rel: Simplify the fraction first: 9/90 = 1/10.

recs.q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.rel: Present % + absent % = 100%, so 80% present means 20% absent.

recs.q: My brother's sister is your mother. Taking me as a male, what am I to you?
recs.facts: My brother's sister is my own sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, that is, your maternal uncle.
recs.rel: Brother's sister means own sister (or oneself if female).

recs.q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 11 days; 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday + 4 = Friday (the source statement of Saturday is wrong).
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 page?
recs.facts: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 men write 5 pages in the same 5 minutes).
recs.rel: When workers and work are equal, each worker does one unit in the given time.

recs.q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
recs.facts: Train speed = 2 x 30 = 60 km/h; in half an hour it covers 30 km.
recs.rel: Distance = speed x time; 30 minutes is half an hour.

recs.q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
recs.facts: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 1.11 minutes (the source value 0.9 is wrong).
recs.rel: Minutes per km = total minutes / total km.

recs.q: What is 80% of 90?
In a classroom, out of 1500 students 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
recs.rel: Simplify first: 1200/1500 = 4/5 = 80%.

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 10 days; 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday (the source statement of Friday is wrong).
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks, so the day stays Sunday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: What is the value of (2 + 2)?
recs.facts: Adding the numbers in the bracket gives 2 + 2 = 4 (the source statement of 8 is wrong).
recs.rel: Brackets are solved first.

recs.q: What is one third of 120?
recs.rel: A third is the number divided by 3.

recs.q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils?
recs.facts: One dozen = 12 pencils; price of 1 pencil = 27 / 12 = 2.25; 4 pencils = Rs 9.
recs.rel: 4 pencils is a third of a dozen, so the price is a third of 27.

recs.q: Ali moves towards the north, after some time he turns left, then turns left again. What is his present direction?
recs.facts: North, then left gives West, then left again gives South.
recs.rel: Two left turns make a U-turn (opposite direction).

recs.q: Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
recs.rel: Present is 68%, so absent is 100 - 68 = 32%.

recs.q: A train is moving at a speed of 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
recs.facts: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour; 90 / 5 = 18 km.
recs.rel: Convert minutes to hours: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour.

recs.q: A man covers 20 km in one hour and 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
recs.facts: Total time is 100 minutes for 20 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 20 = 5 minutes (the source value 0.2 is wrong).
recs.rel: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes.

recs.q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 4th day be?
recs.facts: The gap is 11 days backwards; 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 = Thursday.
recs.rel: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

recs.q: In a class of 24 students, 1/4 are male. What is the percentage of females?
recs.rel: If 1/4 are male, then 3/4 = 75% are female.

recs.q: A man walks towards the north, then turns left, then turns right. What is his present direction?
recs.facts: North, left gives West, then right from West gives North again.
recs.rel: A left turn followed by a right turn returns to the original direction.

recs.q: An aeroplane flies in the air mainly because of which force?
recs.facts: The shape of the wings produces lift, which overcomes weight so the aeroplane flies.
recs.rel: Four forces on a plane: lift, weight, thrust and drag.

recs.q: Vehicle is to wheels as sound is to what?
recs.facts: A vehicle moves on wheels, and sound travels as waves.
recs.rel: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

recs.q: After how many years does a leap year normally come?
recs.facts: A leap year (366 days) comes every 4 years, for example 2024 and 2028.
recs.rel: Century years are leap years only if divisible by 400.

recs.q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes (at the same speed)?
recs.facts: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 120/100 = 1.2 km per minute; in 15 minutes: 1.2 x 15 = 18 km. The printed answer 30 km in the source is wrong.
recs.rel: Find the speed per minute first, then multiply by the minutes.

recs.q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will tomorrow be?
